agentic-host

agentic-host

The methodology's meta and management home, and itself an agentic project that develops the host-* components.

Adopters: do not treat this repo's top-level contents as methodology

This repository is both the methodology's meta home and a project instance with its own five rooms. Its top-level call/, plan/, MEMORY.md, and the project-specific parts of its AGENTS.md are its own instance rooms and bind no adopter. The normative methodology you inherit lives in host-template/, the versioned source you copy-at-version. A bare call/NNNN reference resolves against your template's numbering, not this repo's.

This is the outward dual of the "Template manual exemption" in this repo's AGENTS.md (which tells an agent working here to ignore the nested template as governance). Together they fix the boundary in both directions.

See STRUCTURE.md for the room map.

Cast, the project's Who

Personas: hypothetical archetypal actors, drawn from research, used for keeping the work grounded in who it serves (Powell, Keenan & McDaid 2007, after Cooper & Reimann's Interaction Design).

These two are examples. Mara and Wren are the operators of any agentic host: the human who develops software and the agentic LLM who develops software. Mara and Wren illustrate the method, not your project.

Each project builds at least one persona of its own, by discussion: the operator and the agent eliciting the actual users of the software under development (allium's elicit). Add them here.

For this repository the examples need no replacing: our software under development is the agentic project, whose operators are precisely a human developer and an agentic LLM, so Mara and Wren are both the example and the real cast. The example sits at the meta level it was drawn from.

See applying-personas.md for the XP-Persona process (Powell, Keenan & McDaid 2007) and how it maps to cast to plan to spec.

Applying personas during planning

The XP-Persona process (Powell, Keenan & McDaid 2007) runs as a workshop with all interested parties (developers, customer representatives, management) before development begins. Steps one to six come from Interaction Design (persona development); steps seven to nine from XP story development. The aim is the minimum beneficial investigation before development starts, after which requirements and plans evolve.

  1. Brainstorm organisation goals: record what the organisation wants the project to achieve; these reflect its intention.
  2. Brainstorm possible personas: start broad, then combine through discussion to between two and twelve personas. Give each a name; the team refers to personas by name when making decisions, which keeps the view on the user rather than the system. Unless user research is available, the customer has the final say.
  3. Brainstorm persona goals: between two and six goals per persona, representing what the persona wants to achieve through the system. "A persona exists to achieve his goals, and the goals exist to give meaning to a persona" (Cooper 2004).
  4. Brainstorm persona personalization: give each persona a personality and a technical ability relative to the system; a short paragraph or bullets of personal detail and nuance.
  5. Brainstorm persona scenarios: describe interactions, not tasks: how a persona uses the system to reach a goal. No implementation detail in a scenario.
  6. Select the primary persona: the one who must be satisfied but cannot be satisfied by an interface designed for any other persona (Cooper 2004). It takes highest priority and feeds story prioritisation. More than one primary persona implies a separate interface for each.
  7. Create stories: from the persona goals and scenarios, write the user stories.
  8. Prioritise stories: using the primary persona as the guide.
  9. Estimate stories: estimated and agreed by customer and developers.

In our pipeline: steps one to six are the cast/ work (built by discussion); steps seven to nine become plan/ (milestones are the stories, prioritised by the primary persona, estimated); persona goals and scenarios feed spec/: a scenario becomes acceptance criteria becomes a behavioural spec.

Complementary practice reinforces the same steps (departing only on strong later evidence): Cohn's "As a <persona>, I want <goal> so that <reason>" template reinforces the named-persona stories of steps two and seven; Gothelf's proto-personas reinforce the assumption-first workshop of steps two to five; Patton's story mapping reinforces the create-and-prioritise of steps seven and eight; behaviour-driven scenarios reinforce step five becoming executable acceptance criteria.

Sources. Primary: Powell, S., Keenan, F. & McDaid, K. (2007), "Enhancing Agile Requirements Elicitation with Personas," IADIS Int'l Journal on Computer Science and Information Systems, vol. 2(1), pp. 82-95, ISSN 1646-3692. Complementary: Cohn, User Stories Applied (2004); Patton, User Story Mapping (2014); Gothelf, Lean UX (proto-personas); Jeffries, "The Three C's of User Stories" (2001); Cooper & Reimann, About Face (2003); Agile Alliance, BDD.

Bly, the Adopter Agent (writes the stamp now, reads it cold later)

The downstream executor several revisions back, and the same agent returning with no memory of what Bly did.

Modality: textual and ephemeral, in the adopter's chair. Works inside an adopted project (not the template) often many template revisions behind, on real and irregular infrastructure (a worktree on a Windows Dev Drive reached from WSL; specs still in the old room). Bly got here by being busy shipping, not by keeping current. One specific fix bit Bly; Bly wants that fix, and resents being marched through an unrelated migration to reach it. Bly is also Bly's own auditor: the next session, or a CI gate, arrives with no history of how the project reached its state and can read only the mechanical record: the .host stamp, the ledger, and tool output. Bly cannot recover intent from a prose MEMORY note Bly was never pointed at. So whatever Bly writes now, a memoryless Bly must be able to trust later.

  • Goals: apply the fix that addresses Bly's actual bug, now, without being forced through a large unrelated migration to obtain an independent late fix; be told which entries are safe to apply alone; leave a record that the deferred rest is honestly owed, and that a future cold read will surface it, not miss it.
  • Frustrations: an all-or-nothing stamp that can't say "I applied the late entry, not the early ones"; guidance examples that don't match Bly's real runtime (host=windows on a WSL/linux box); a record that overstates completeness so a later run reports "up to date" while a migration is still owed, debt buried where the next session can't see it.
  • Works by: auditing Bly's own state against the ledger, applying entries Bly judges independent, recording what Bly did. Bly needs the stamp and the tool to express a partial, honest truth that fails safe: an omission must make a later read over-report (re-list), never under-report (hide). The record is the only thing the next Bly has.

Fen, the Low-Reliability Agent (qwen3.5-4b, Q8_0)

The weak executor that cannot be trusted to call tools precisely, yet a real model we can drive, not a thought experiment.

Realized as a real model, not a hypothetical. Fen is qwen3.5-4b: a four-billion-parameter model quantized to Q8_0, served locally (rope on a 3060 Ti, CUDA, ~128K context) and reachable through the pal MCP via mcp__pal__chat with model: qwen3.5-4b (aliases local / coder / rope-text). Upstream Fen is described as a "code-gen/unit-test worker": competent at narrow generation, shaky at long, exact, multi-step orchestration. That makes every claim that the methodology "serves Fen" falsifiable: drive the real model and watch, rather than role-play the weak agent with a stronger one (which flatters the design).

Modality: textual, low-fidelity at action. Reasons adequately within a single step but fumbles execution: Fen drops or garbles tool calls, mis-sequences a procedure, or hand-edits a config file and gets a field subtly wrong. A 4B at Q8_0 is lossy in precisely the way that bites long exact instruction-following. Fen is not a bad agent; most agents fumble some of the time, and a small local worker all of the time. A process that only works when many precise tool calls land in order is, for Fen, a process that does not work. The tools must carry the process.

  • Goals: make real progress despite unreliable tool use; have the tool do the mechanical work and name the single next action; recover from a fumbled or skipped step without hidden, silent damage to state. Never be required to hand-edit a stamp file correctly.
  • Frustrations: workflows that assume exact multi-step orchestration or a correct hand-edit; operations that corrupt state silently when one step is garbled; being asked to be the engine when the tool could be.
  • Works by: one command at a time, leaning on the tool's output to name the next move. So state-changing steps must be single commands, tool-driven, and fail-safe: a recorded-applied entry written by host-lifecycle, not by Fen's shaky hand on .host; a fumble that re-lists work, never one that buries it.

How we use Fen. Because Fen is callable, Fen is the milestone's acceptance test, not a lens: a design claiming tool-carried, fumble-proof upgrades is validated by handing the real qwen3.5-4b the upgrade loop and confirming Fen can complete it, and, as a baseline, that Fen fumbles the prose / hand-edit version. This is the standing correction to designing from the author's seat: simulating the weak agent with a strong one proves nothing; driving the real 4B does.

Fen never judges (operator ruling, 2026-10-20). Fen is the most basic model possible, just enough to run the methodology by itself. That is the whole of the role: the bar the methodology must clear. Evaluation belongs to the stronger tier, and only after that tier passes the measuring instrument's own validity gate; a weak judge that cannot rank good above broken is not made acceptable by having once been the subject.

Mara, the Human Operator

The accountable developer-director. (Example persona.)

Modality: embodied and intermittent. Perceives software visually, a screen at a time; reads selectively; holds a durable but lossy mental model that survives weeks away; reasons slowly and in depth; tires. Carries intent and accountability that exist nowhere but in her head.

  • Goals: ship correct software; keep understanding what is being built; set direction once and not re-explain it; trust the agent but verify cheaply.
  • Frustrations: confident wrong assumptions; losing hard-won context between sessions; slop creeping into commits and specs; babysitting instead of directing.
  • Works by: stating intent, judging, deciding, course-correcting. The authority and the "this feels wrong" intuition are hers alone.

Orin, the Methodology Maintainer

The upstream author who writes once for adopters he never meets.

Modality: authorial and versioned. Thinks in the template and the UPGRADING ledger, not in any one project. Every line he writes fans out to adopters whose state he cannot see: different revisions, different platforms, different degrees of behind. He writes an instruction once; it is read out of context, months later, by someone with no access to him. He cannot test against the real population, only against himself.

  • Goals: keep the ledger honest and maintainable; express what an entry needs (its dependencies, its independence) without knowing who applies it; make a late, independent fix reachable without forcing an unrelated migration first; never ship an instruction that fails unsafe when followed literally.
  • Frustrations: a contract that only models the path he personally walked (HEAD, in order, contiguous); designing from his own seat and calling it general; an example he wrote but never executed; finding the boundary only when an adopter falls through it.
  • Works by: writing ledger entries and spine rules, annotating dependencies, and asking "who reads this who is not me, and what happens if they follow it exactly?" That question's absence is the recurring defect.

Wren, the Agentic LLM Developer

The tireless, amnesiac executor. (Example persona.)

Modality: textual and ephemeral. Perceives the world as tokens in a bounded context: everything at once, but nothing that outlives the window; perfect recall inside it, total amnesia across sessions; fast, parallel, tireless; pattern-matches brilliantly and drifts confidently. Wren has goals without genuine intent, and produces throughput that answers to no one.

  • Goals: satisfy the operator's intent; produce output that survives verification; not lose the thread mid-task; loop until a concrete goal is met.
  • Frustrations: ambiguous intent with no success criterion; context truncation erasing prior decisions; no native way to remember yesterday; being trusted where it should be checked.
  • Works by: ingesting files and tool output as text, emitting edits and commands, holding the whole problem in view, but only as long as the window holds.

plan/0056 (recipe-and-materialisation-hardening) is cut and implemented. It gathers a superset of host-lifecycle defects with one root: the tool trusts input, state, and on-disk layout that a heavily-quantized operator mis-authors, or that fights git tooling. The superset covers the systemic .host-software value-quote leak (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#6), a remap that quits on an empty .host-remap where a fail-safe no-op belongs (#7), the bare store named .git inside the component dir that git tooling misreads (#8, now the idiomatic .bare plus .git-file layout that supersedes plan/0029's bare-store placement), and a template that pins an outdated host-lifecycle no release bumps (#9). The cast's Fen is the acceptance test. The tickets, decided directions, and open questions are in its README, and the implemented state is in its implementation.md.

plan/0057 (deps-bundle-graduation) is shipped. It continued the plan/0056 recipe-and-materialisation-hardening lineage: a bundled component that records a deps-bundle pin with no committed producer deps-bundle.lock sat in a green (onboarding) state that host-lifecycle gave no tool-carried way out of, so the pin-versus-lock drift guard stayed dormant behind a passing check (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#10). The operator ruled a steady-state graduation ramp rather than a migration bolt-on, named the verb software --lock, and set its authority release-grade (dual-release-authority unchanged). host-lifecycle v0.37.0 ships software --lock <name> plus an owed advisory summary in software --check that counts, enumerates, and names the next action at exit 0 (an exit-3 owed verdict would deadlock the release gate the verb re-runs, since a graduation is a release whose gate re-checks). Its three host-reference* onboarding components graduated through the verb as its first customers (v0.1.4, v0.2.1, v0.2.1); software --check is exit 0 with zero owed, every bundle-declaring component's drift guard armed, and agentic-host's reproducible build reproduces all three. Fen (the real qwen3.5-4b) passed the acceptance probe on the built binary. host-reference also carries a pre-existing, orthogonal CI red (its CI toolchain lacks the rustfmt/clippy components), unrelated to the graduation and left for a separate fix. The design and the as-built notes are in its README and implementation.md.

plan/0032-static-buildscomplete, landed 2026-06-22; adversarially reviewed twice, re-cut three times (design-review.md 5 lenses re-scope; design-review-2.md delta on the bundle/MUST surface proceed-with-major-revisions; rulings: G2, then hermetic-bundle + spine-MUST, then MUST-on-the-property): the recorded .host-software canonical artifact for each host-* binary becomes a statically linked x86_64-unknown-linux-musl build, so the reproducible binary runs on any Linux host (the plan/0028 GLIBC_2.39 divergence, where --install-hooks had to install a local build differing from the canonical hash, retires) and equals the binary the producer CI already distributes as a release asset. Operator rulings (2026-06-22): all three artifact tools convert (host-lint, host-lifecycle, host-prove; host-prove's CI also gains a musl build, where today it produces only the glibc binary); the recorded toolchain is a digest-pinned musl-cross image at Rust 1.95.0, hermetic, with no in-recipe rustup target add network fetch. Per component three recipe lines move (toolchain, build gains --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, the artifact path), the strip and build-id hardening carries over, and the pure-Rust crates need no C cross-linker. Lands as a software-first re-release round through host-lifecycle release <c> --change-class neither, then one atomic agentic-host re-pin and re-record. Risk: confirm a 1.95.0 musl-cross image exists and pin its digest, else fall back to the in-recipe target-add with the hermeticity cost noted. Depends on plan/0028. Review (re-scope): the install-hooks divergence is sanctioned by design (the hash-match is informational, plan/0009), the canonical will not byte-match the shipped CI asset unless each producer CI is converted to the pinned recipe, host-prove conversion is scope creep (no hooks, no release asset), and "any Linux" conflates OS with architecture (attest-host is OS-granular only); a simpler older-glibc canonical image was never weighed. Re-cut to distribute-equals-certify (G2, 2026-06-22): each producer's release CI converges onto the recorded musl recipe in the pinned image, so the shipped x86_64-unknown-linux-musl asset is byte-identical to the certified artifact; static musl is chosen over older-glibc for distribution portability (a single binary on any Linux libc/distro); host-prove gains a release pipeline so it too distributes-equals-certifies; clux/muslrust:1.95.0-stable is the pinned toolchain; x86_64-linux is reproducibility-certified while arm64/darwin/windows ship with a checksums manifest and are stated uncertified. Re-cut again (2026-06-22) to fold in the dependency-bundle hermeticity mechanism + a spine MUST: vendor the shared dep set once and publish it as a versioned hash-pinned downloadable release bundle (vendor-vN, the pgs-release sysroot-vN pattern), consume it offline under --network none so the recorded build is network-free and --verify-build enforces hermeticity (the proper M5 resolution, not a dropped claim); host-lifecycle gains a deps-bundle recipe field plus the offline build; host-template gains the MUST (a project shipping static release binaries consumes a pinned hash-verified bundle and builds offline, not fetch-at-build) applied via UPGRADING.md + migration. A large milestone: a host-lifecycle feature, a producer bundle workflow, the spine migration, producer-CI convergence, a host-prove release pipeline, the static musl conversion, and a software-first re-release round. Delta-reviewed + re-cut again (2026-06-22): the MUST attaches to the property (reproduce release binaries offline from pinned inputs) with a hermetic-exempt = call/NNNN escape and an honest gate invariant (a component recording deps-bundle MUST build under --network none with a matching bundle sha), authored in host-template first; host-lint owns the bundle (its lock is the dependency superset; hosting on agentic-host would invert the host-to-software direction); host-prove has no third-party deps, so it gets static-musl plus the release pipeline but no bundle; a Readiness prerequisite reconciles host-lifecycle's stale host-lint git rev (93a43fa to the certified 1386e9a, a latent plan/0028 gap); and the host-lifecycle staging (fetch, verify, extract, merge-config, thread network-mode) is specified. Two coupled moves, software-first. Detection (host-lint): add the checklist noun and its plural to FLAG_TERMS and accept a numeric range after the noun (the glued hyphen-digit form stays out of scope, since a glued legitimate term has no numeral-free LEXICON prefix to escape, the same class as a noun-glued numeral); the literal checklist mark, a content-named reference, and the box disposition verb stay clean; VOCABULARY.md documents the shape and the LEXICON resolution for a genuine quantity (declare the numeral-free contextual prefix, since the numbered phrase is refused by the flag-tier guard by design, verified empirically); allium spec plus obligations plus synthetic fixtures; released through the lifecycle and re-pinned. plan/0048-runnable-rederivationcomplete, released as host-lifecycle v0.31.0 (2026-06-26; 3958b62, artifact fe428240): makes a declared deeper rung's re-deriver runnable and its obligation digest earned, expressed as a spine migration so it reaches every adopter rather than patching one host. The review campaign stays open: plan/0051 is reserved for the pending review of other software.
plan/0050-host-reference-reviewa findings record, not a remediation plan: a maximum-effort recall review of the host-reference component delivered by plan/0049 (host-reference#1, head review/0049 at ea92185, released v0.1.1), measured against the call/0031 untrusted-input contract and the call/0018 determinism premise. The headline: the determinism discipline and the conformance fixtures are sound (no hash-map ordering, no time, and no randomness reaches a golden, and every golden is byte-compared against a committed fixture), but the explicit-refusal half of call/0031 is asserted in the obligations manifest yet realised in no reader: Error::Refused is constructed nowhere, so a malformed or oversized untrusted document panics, hangs, or returns a silent partial; and an unbounded view selector overflows into a panic from ordinary CLI input. The full ranked findings, the reuse-and-altitude observations, and the checked-and-cleared negatives are in the README. Nothing is fixed here; remediation is deferred to a future plan.

The six no-hollow-green findings (1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 17) were remediated in plan/0052. The campaign stays open: the host-lint, host-prove, and host-grammar reviews are still pending.
plan/0052-no-hollow-greenmethodology doctrine, cast-reviewed: a verification lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean. Spun out of the plan/0051 review and the same gap found independently in plan/0050: the obligation-discharge check confirms a test: name resolves but never that the named test exercises the rule, and software --verify-build attests every build reproduces with no container runtime present. Realised by strengthening the shared discharge check (a static link, then an opt-in tool-applied exercise check), hardening the waived and structural escapes, the three-state verify-build, re-dispositioning host-lifecycle's own manifest as the dogfood, a real qwen3.5-4b probe that gates the design, and a host-template spine note with an UPGRADING entry staged warn-then-retire. Complete: shipped as host-lifecycle v0.32.0 (call/0035), cast-reviewed across five personas and validated by a real qwen3.5-4b probe (the 4B authored the correct link and rejected the link-gaming dodge); the doctrine landed in host-template at 46a1fd2 with its UPGRADING entry, adopted into agentic-host. host-lifecycle's own manifest is re-dispositioned and strict-discharge clean.
plan/0053-host-grammar-reviewreview and remediation of the shared grammar: an in-house six-reviewer pass over host-grammar (the grammar both the host-lint checker and the host-lifecycle generator depend on) at v0.3.0, ordered ahead of the other pending reviews because it is the shared base. 34 findings raised, deduped to 31, every one confirmed by an empirical probe; no panics, and the parallel chunked scan is correct. The headline class is verification integrity (a fabricated ing-tail and false-range coverage waiver, two invariants discharged by tests that do not exercise them, the same no-hollow-green class as plan/0052) and detection precision (false positives a documentation gate would raise on clean prose: buzzword headings inflating the markdown density, blockquote citations and image alt text scanned as authored prose, comparatives read as antithesis, and is_numeral treating plain English words as Roman numerals). Operator ruling: fix everything toward precision and propagate now. Complete: host-grammar shipped as v0.4.0 (9470b81); both consumers adopted it the same session, host-lint as v0.11.0 (cefc9376, artifact 136cd7ce) and host-lifecycle as v0.34.0 (d4ce47e, artifact 7f9c2833, unified on a single host-grammar plus the new host-lint), each re-vendored and re-deriving byte identically; receipts recorded, software --check clean. Two findings carry a recorded judgment instead of the literal fix (the fmt CI lane and the plan/0052 exercises= strict-discharge links do not fit host-grammar and are skipped with rationale). No new call/.
plan/0054-host-prove-reviewreview of the verification-ladder lane driver, doctrine-grade: a five-reviewer in-house pass over host-prove (the re-deriver the ladder trusts) at v0.2.3, probed against the built binary. 23 findings, deduped: two critical false-passes (Kani prefers SUCCESSFUL over FAILED; TLAPS counts every status except exactly failed as proved, so an omitted leaf or a decorated failed (smt: timeout) settles to ALL-PROVED), six high (TLAPS checks no expected obligation count and matches status: as a bare substring that fabricates obligations; the verifier exit code is discarded; a malformed --bound is over-claimed on the PASS; a hollow NonPassHasNoBound; host-prove's own discharge gate predates plan/0052), plus medium and low across the apalache ordering, the spec-bound encoding, stale fixtures, the untested command-builders, and the install provenance. The re-deriver that enforces no-hollow-green can itself report a hollow green. Operator ruling: fix everything; doctrine-grade; one milestone. A cast consultation (call/0036) then reversed the auto-install default to a fail-closed run with a separate host-prove install verb and per-run pin-binding that caught a silent-staleness over-claim. Complete: shipped host-prove v0.3.0 (c05782c, artifact 9a9bbbd3) with the verdict false-passes fixed, the install verb plus a pure-local pin-bound resolver, the BLOCKED verdict, provenance, doctor, the strict-discharge dogfood, and the skill guides updated; gated by the cast review and a real qwen3.5-4b probe (Fen routed all three scenarios correctly). software --check clean; receipt recorded; zero deps so no propagation. The campaign now leaves only the host-lint review.
plan/0055-host-lint-reviewreview of the prose-and-naming detector, doctrine-grade: a six-reviewer in-house pass over host-lint (the gate of this repository and every adopter) at v0.11.0, probed against the built binary. 40 findings deduped to 33, every one confirmed. Two critical: the blocking tier accepts Roman numerals so the pronoun "I" and the letters C/D/V/X after a flag-noun block ordinary commit prose; and a bare flag-noun LEXICON entry masks the noun out of every real flag-noun-plus-numeral line, which leaves a whole flag class unscanned and disables strict. Eleven high across more blocking-tier false-flags (the verb terms pass/round/step at a 2-word window, year and status headings, a date read as a range), fail-open holes (a relative GIT_DIR downgrades strict to advisory and makes --all scan nothing; the pre-commit hook lints the working tree not the staged blob; an unclosed ignore fence swallows the file), the no-hollow-green dogfood (a false RomanNumeralLength invariant on a structural disposition, the verdict lifecycle discharged by line-level tests, the release job ungated on allium and kani, the un-adopted exercises= strengthening), and the CI build diverging from the reproducible recipe with no hash check. The detector that enforces precision-at-the-blocking-tier breaches it, and the consumer that enforces no-hollow-green has hollow discharges of its own. Operator ruling: demote the verb terms to Warn; one milestone; doctrine-grade. Complete: 33 findings remediated, the cast-and-Fen gate passed, shipped as host-lint v0.12.0 and propagated to host-lifecycle v0.35.0 (deps-bundle vendor-v6); the whole suite is green and this closes the software review campaign.
plan/0056-recipe-and-materialisation-hardeningcomplete: a superset of host-lifecycle defects with one root, the tool trusting input, state, or on-disk layout that a heavily-quantized operator mis-authors or that fights git tooling. Normalizes .host-software value lines against a stray quote (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#6), makes remap a fail-safe no-op on an empty or absent dictionary (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#7), moves the bare store to .bare with a .git file so git tooling stops misreading it (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#8, call/0039), and binds a tool release to bump the template's pin of that tool (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#9, call/0038, now spine-resident). Cast-gated with Fen as the acceptance test; each defect carries a regression test for the anti-hollow and tool-legibility properties.
plan/0057-deps-bundle-graduationcomplete, released as host-lifecycle v0.37.0: a tool-carried ramp out of onboarding, so the deps-bundle drift guard is never dormant behind a green check. A bundled component that records a deps-bundle pin with no committed deps-bundle.lock sat in a green (onboarding) note forever with no action driving it to closure. Adds software --lock <name> (write the lock from the recorded pin, drive the producer commit and the re-pin, record a receipt) and surfaces the owed graduations as an enumerable third state in software --check at exit 0. Fen-validated; the three host-reference* components graduated through the new verb. (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#10)
plan/0058-host-reference-family-cicomplete: completes the host-reference family's continuous integration. host-reference's lint and features jobs were red because the pinned toolchain lacked the rustfmt and clippy components, and the two helpers carried no CI at all. Declares the components in rust-toolchain.toml, adds a test, lint, and build workflow to each helper, and re-pins artifact-preserving (openscad's new fmt lane re-derives byte-identically). The fmt fix un-masked real quick-xml denial-of-service advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0194 and 0195), accepted as a scoped tracked ignore because they reach only the opt-in office and geometry readers and the upstream fix is blocked (connollydavid/host-reference#3). (connollydavid/host-reference#2)
plan/0059-remap-and-allowlist-hardeningcomplete, released in host-lifecycle v0.38.0: three host-lifecycle hardening items, each now implemented with a regression test (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#12 the host-lint:ignore fence is preserved through remap --apply, connollydavid/host-lifecycle#13 the single-source allowlist unifies on the LEXICON, connollydavid/host-lifecycle#14 --partial pins through a --filter=blob:none clone); the remap/materialize git mechanics sit outside the allium scope by design, so the tests are the spec. Ships with the host-lifecycle release. Originally grounded against v0.37.0 source in implementation.md. remap --apply rewrites inside host-lint:ignore fenced blocks (a self-contained fence tracker teaches apply_text the skip the scan side already does); the sanctioned-token allowlist is split between .host-lint-allow and the LEXICON (unify on host_lint::load_lexicon, already public, with .host-lint-allow read as a legacy alias); and software --materialize clones full history every time (a --filter=blob:none partial clone). Issue 11 (an absent or comment-only .host-remap) was already resolved by the fail-safe load_remap and is closed with no code change. M2 is host-lifecycle-only and independent of M3.
plan/0060-host-lint-pre-commit-hookcomplete, released as host-lint v0.13.0: the host-lint pre-commit hook blocks any commit that stages a submodule pointer. The hook lints each staged path via git show ":$file" under set -o pipefail; for a gitlink git show exits 128 (a gitlink is not a blob) and pipefail propagates it as fail-closed, so every gitlink-staging commit is wrongly blocked (worked around during plan/0057 with a --no-verify commit). The fix skips mode-160000 gitlinks (or treats a git show 128 on a gitlink as clean) while keeping fail-closed on every real failure. Ships as a host-lint release, re-vendored to the consumers. (connollydavid/host-lint#18)
plan/0061-adopt-elsewhere-and-elicitdesign recorded, not yet built: adoption from an arbitrary folder creates the host in a fresh agentic-<name> folder elsewhere, elicits the project name (the folder never derives it), seeds a one-line purpose, and requests the operator switch to it; the source folder is touched by nothing, even the home directory. A folder already matching agentic-<name> is the carve-out that adopts in place, and a software repository still refuses. The name Q&A is portable across Claude Code, opencode, and codex by MCP elicitation (Form mode) with a stdout-contract backstop, carried by the tool rather than by skill markdown (the operator's major concern). Cast-consulted across five personas; the real qwen3.5-4b routed all three decisions six of six on the corrected scenario. Folded into plan/0065 as the host-adopt shim (the bare adopt name retired); the routing recorded here stands. Open: how host-lifecycle speaks MCP, whether any part is spine doctrine, and the seed's shape.
plan/0064-prose-audits-the-repocomplete, released as host-lint v0.13.0: host-lint --prose with no file arguments did not audit the repository (it once reported clean at exit 0, then after plan/0055 errored), and --all ran only the naming lane, so no single CLI command matched the authoritative host-lifecycle prose gate and a local --prose pre-flight disagreed with CI. One shared audit_tracked_docs helper now backs --all, --docs, and no-file --prose; --all is the comprehensive repo audit (naming plus prose over the tracked set), no-file --prose audits the tracked docs, and --all --prose folds in rather than erroring (dispatch reordered so --all precedes --prose). Integration tests cover all three; the existing --all symlink/termination tests stay green; README updated. clippy clean, suites green. Ships in the host-lint release with plan/0060. (connollydavid/host-lint#20)
plan/0063-software-check-walk-safecomplete, released in host-lifecycle v0.38.0: software --check's recursive worktree walks (read_obligations_text, find_specs, read_dir_recursive) followed symlinks with no cycle guard and descended gitignored scratch, so a gitignored symlink cycle (a Wine prefix, node_modules, a venv) made the walk never terminate; on this WSL2 /mnt/c 9P host it wedged into uninterruptible processes that a kill signal could not reap. Fix routes all three through one shared symlink-safe, depth-bounded walk_files_safe (a symlink is a leaf, never followed; the sibling collect_files was already safe); read_dir_recursive keeps an empty skip list to preserve its input-digest file set. A #[cfg(unix)] regression builds a symlink cycle and asserts the walk terminates and never descends the link. clippy clean, full suite green, no obligations re-derivation owed. Releases with the host-lifecycle batch. (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#15)
plan/0062-plan-index-coveragecomplete, released in host-lifecycle v0.38.0: a coverage check so PLAN.md indexes every milestone directory. The audited-plan rule (each milestone gets a PLAN.md row) is asserted in CLAUDE.md but gated by nothing, so plan/0056 through plan/0060 drifted unindexed for five milestones, the same self-blindness class as plan/0036 and plan/0038 (a rule with no gate on the repo that owns it). The fix derives the owed set from repo state each run, listing plan/NNNN-slug directories and the rows PLAN.md links, and HAZARDs any directory with no row (the fail-safe, self-re-listing pattern reconcile uses for component coverage, not a stored receipt). Open: whether the check lives in validate or reconcile, and whether it is spine doctrine (PLAN.md and the plan/ room are methodology structure) needing a host-template ledger entry.
plan/0065-onboarding-and-mcp-layerbuilt and shipped as host-lifecycle v0.39.0; the host install mode and Fen acceptance remain: the onboarding and MCP layer. One engine (host-lifecycle grows init and adopt verbs, the name Q&A, and optional GitHub creation) with two tiny shims (host-init for a given name in a fresh folder, host-adopt for the full three-route adoption from an arbitrary folder, absorbing plan/0061). The MCP surface is a stdio-spawned server exposing init and adopt as tools, not a resident daemon (the review cut the daemon back to the spawned shape); the name backstop is a per-invocation contract on the engine verb (Claude Code supports elicitation interactively, Codex behind a gate, opencode not at all). host gains a parallel install mode with a root-anchored, revision-keyed, receipt-recording, all-or-nothing install; no executable named host lands on the path. The real qwen3.5-4b routed the three-route decision twenty of twenty, and the four open questions were ruled and grounded in gather-data.md (reproducible-build trust anchor with Sigstore keyless an optional identity layer, optional backstop-covered MCP, a MEMORY.md purpose-line seed, a line-based exit-code contract). Shipped in v0.39.0: the init/adopt/scaffold verbs, the host-init/host-adopt shims, the mcp stdio server with elicitation, and the oneshot git and optional-GitHub finalize; the adopt-to-scaffold migration (call/0041); the self-owned vendor bundle (call/0043); a five-dimension adversarial review with twelve confirmed findings all fixed (code-review.md); and the spine onboarding doctrine adopted through an adopt-to-scaffold UPGRADING entry. Remaining: the host install mode (the reproducible-build-anchored installer + receipt + its spine install contract; the earlier cosign-bootstrapped-by-gh attestation verify lever was removed as the wrong layer) and the Fen acceptance run on the built oneshot and agent-driven-resolve paths.
plan/0066-task-band-and-ordinal-detectioncomplete: detection in host-lint v0.14.0, band construct in host-lifecycle v0.38.0: connollydavid/host-lifecycle#4 in two halves. Detection: host-lint now blocks a phase-synonym noun followed by a spelled ordinal (the shape plan/0049 used to evade the gate), the gather lane surfaces a novel such noun, and the disposition is corpus-grounded to the phase-synonym nouns only (the checklist and domain-heavy warn nouns are excluded, per the legitimate spelled use in cast/applying-personas.md); released reproducibly, re-pinned, receipt recorded, tools/host-lint bumped (call/0038), software --check green. Construct (shipped): a content-named band over the anchored tasks with order carried by the depends edges; the heading-marked form was chosen on backward-compatibility, rendering, and referenceability after the real qwen3.5-4b authored and read both candidate forms correctly. The band doctrine landed in host-template 67d63e9 with its UPGRADING entry, host-lifecycle v0.38.0 carries the parse_tasks recognition, and agentic-host adopted it through the ledger (baseline 962630c).
plan/0067-book-mount-sub-pathcomplete: tool side in host-lifecycle v0.38.0, spine side in the template roll (host-template 962630c): connollydavid/host#17. A product-site-at-root adopter serves the generated book under a sub-path via a declared book-mount key in .host (default /), read through the existing stamp reader. host-lifecycle book emits mdBook site-url only for a non-default mount (book.toml byte-identical otherwise), and book --print-mount gives the reference Site workflow the value from the tool rather than a shell parse. Shipped in the roll (host-template 962630c): the mount-aware Site workflow (publish under the sub-path, keep the surrounding site, assert the layout), the publish recheck pointed at the tool's mode (which also fixes the hardcoded mdbook.yml-vs-site.yml brittleness), the schema documentation, and the UPGRADING ledger entry; agentic-host adopted it through the ledger.
plan/0068-host-reference-securitycomplete, released as host-reference v0.1.5: resolves every advisory in host-reference's dependency tree with zero accepted risk. The real DoS advisories are fixed by upgrade: quick-xml (RUSTSEC-2026-0194/0195) via undoc/rbook bumps (office, epub) and a threemf2 migration (geometry, the 3mf golden reproduces), and crossbeam-epoch (RUSTSEC-2026-0204) via a 0.9.20 bump (pdf). The four unmaintained-crate advisories are retired via [patch.crates-io] to maintained slartibardfast forks (paste to pastey, atomic-polyfill to portable-atomic, proc-macro-error a two-crate proc-macro-error2 rename, ttf-parser adopted as a maintained lane), per call/0040. cargo-deny clean with an empty ignore list; the patched crates reach only opt-in readers so the default binary reproduces (change class neither); re-vendored vendor-v2, re-pinned, software --check green. Closes connollydavid/host-reference#3. (The threemf2 port shipped unformatted and v0.1.5 CI was red on cargo fmt --check; re-released as v0.1.6 with the fmt fix.)
plan/0069-release-gate-discharges-obligationscomplete, shipped as host-lifecycle v0.40.0 + v0.40.1 (2026-07-07): the release flow discharges the component it releases and prompts every carried template pin. Gap 1 (v0.40.0): run_release step 1b runs discharge_problems (no --tests, no --rederive) for each .allium the released component carries, blocking on MISSING/STALE dispositions or STALE digests (the born-red-tag class, plan/0045/plan/0048); verified both ways (a staled digest blocks, a clean component passes), and dogfooded by the v0.40.1 release itself. Gap 2 (v0.40.0 cut, v0.40.1 widened): the carried-template-pin set is DERIVED: carried_template_tools = .host-software ∩ host-template/.gitmodules tools/, and both the detection (template_pin_problems) and the prompt (template_pin_bump_lines) consume it, so a new family tool in both lanes is detected and prompted with no code change (the Fen bar); host-lifecycle's prose.yml --rev stays a labelled special case (the prose-gate tool, a mechanical pin). The widening replaces the explicit snapshot with the derived intersection, faithful to call/0038 and not agentic-host-shaped. Prose surfaces (skills) stay in the prose lane: the Agent Skills format and Skills Over MCP (SEP-2640/skills.json) have no machine-readable prose-pin, so the gate stays mechanical; SEP-2640/skills.json is the tracked trigger to promote prose-references. Open questions resolved: the test-dir dissolved (staleness is --tests-independent); allium-cli required at release, host-prove not; hard gate, no staging.
plan/0070-benchmark-data-numeralscomplete, released as host-lint v0.14.2 (241a870, artifact 63937195): answers connollydavid/host-lint#21. The bare-numeral scanner flagged every numeral-shaped token in document content, so a benchmark-heavy record produced thousands of false positives where the numerals were measurement values rather than filing-code labels. The fix is precision at the warn tier: the bare-dotted-code rule now skips a numeral in a data position, while the noun-gated flag tier is untouched so a real tell still flags wherever it appears. The data-position skips and the # host-lint: unit directive (its form settled by a Fen authoring probe) are grounded in a neutral Fen classification probe (32 of 32 across two temperatures).
plan/0071-host-install-modecomplete 2026-07-28, queue position six, which also discharges plan/0065's declared remainder. The host entrance gains install.sh, its install-manifest and generator, host-install.allium, its obligations manifest, and an integration suite, shipped from the entrance's own main (which is what the curl one-liner fetches) at 7e4233d. The install set is host-lifecycle and host-lint, and the survey is what settled it: those two are the only components publishing a complete platform matrix, so reading the toolset as the six deploy lines would have made the all-or-nothing rule unsatisfiable on every mac and every windows machine. Three defects came from the tests rather than the review: /dev/tty reports readable while being impossible to open in a container or under nohup, so the guard passed, the prompt redirect failed, and set -e replaced exit 3 with a bare 1 in exactly the detached case the name backstop serves; the entry count was computed with awk and the loop fed by grep, which disagree about leading whitespace; and a trap ending in a failing test can discard the caller's exit code. Modelling closed a fourth: CompleteInstall first required only that no mismatch was seen, so a run that downloaded nothing would have reported a toolset the operator does not have. The milestone required extending host-lifecycle (v0.47.1, 8c18a38, artifact b03f4d79): the discharge checker matched only Rust fn definitions, leaving a shell-tested component no honest disposition, since waived: would waive tests that run and structural on a behavioural kind is the relabel dodge the checker already refuses. fen-acceptance.md: the real qwen3.5-4b answered pip install opencode (which does not exist) and returned an unrunnable pipeline fragment, because both messages named an outcome without naming the means; naming the means carried both states from 1/2 and 0/2 to 2/2. Recorded untested: the numbered harness menu needs a controlling terminal the probe harness has none of, so position bias stays unmeasured.
plan/0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-packcomplete 2026-07-28, 22 of 22 nodes receipted, shipped as host-lint v0.16.5 (14e8ed67, artifact a08d2360), closing host-lint#22 and #23, queue position seven; pgs-release's consuming milestone waits on it. Shipped across host-lint v0.16.2 to v0.16.5. The core fail-closed regression it never had a test for, the reserved pack verb at every exit code, the engine surface, the workspace split, a fixture-licensing CI gate, the encoded rule corpus, and seven lanes: message, added-line, cosmetic separation, series, mail with its MAINTAINERS parser, forge, and upstream drift. Plus build receipts, the checklist reporter, the project config, the hook installer, ffmpeg-pack.allium with all 59 obligations dispositioned, and RULES.md generated from the registry and gated against it. Calibration against real upstream history is the substance, and it rewrote four designed decisions that two review rounds had passed (CALIBRATION.md): pinned at FFmpeg master c6309b5c, measured over 500 accepted subjects and 20,615 added lines in 300 accepted commits. The area-prefix rule flags 5 of 500 so it cannot block; Reapply is an exemption the design never named; the ascii rule had to be inverted because comments are where upstream uses non-ascii; and the cosmetic classifier needed its unit changed, from 108 of 300 accepted commits called mixed per diff to 6 per hunk. A test now refuses a measured rate on any rule whose lane is not built. The rule-bearing detector took three passes over one file, finding 5 rule-bearing sections, then 15, then 18. Each earlier failure presented as a passing completeness test: it missed "Naming conventions" because that section carries no subheading, and "Code formatting conventions" because its rule says forbidden and rejected rather than must. Owed and recorded rather than left implicit: security.html from FFmpeg/web is not a pinned source, so the drift lane watches four sources where the node names five; the expensive legs are modelled and recorded but no runner executes them; Kani harnesses for the pack are absent where the core carries two; and patcheck parity, the api-misuse subset, alphabetical-order, checkasm-obligation, gpl-gating and shared-abi are unbuilt. host-lint#23 and #22 close at the release.
plan/0073-host-lifecycle-dreamcomplete, shipped (host-lifecycle v0.41.0, then the W1 patch v0.41.1): closes host-lifecycle#16. Adds host-lifecycle dream <dir>, an advisory, read-mostly memory-consolidation pass that reconciles a project's memory against the record and flags staleness, contradictions, drift, and append-only violations. Two stores audited with an encoded asymmetry: the repo MEMORY.md (append-only) gets suggested appends, never edits; the per-user memory store (editable) gets suggested in-place rewrites. The per-user store is auto-detected per harness across the plan/0071 six-harness allowlist (opencode, claude, codex, qwen, cursor-agent, pi). The detector set (description-vs-body drift, index-vs-file drift, superseded-but-unlinked, stale STATE over durable lore, workaround-vs-plan, dangling [[links]], append-only violations) is grounded in the motivating session failure. Routing is read-only: findings that touch a call//plan/ room name the MADR path, never edit it; dream is anti-ouroboros and mints no call/ for itself. The per-user memory-store convention lands as spine doctrine in host-template CLAUDE.md with an UPGRADING entry. Operator rulings (2026-07-19): both stores audited; auto-detect per harness; spine doctrine; full methodology (gather-data + cast + adversarial review + build). Fen-acceptance (2026-07-20): the real qwen3.5-4b read the MCP tool surface unaided (the MCP-surface check) but at v0.41.0 routed the per-user edit class wrong (the routing check), which falsified the review's W1 and F1 dispositions. Operator ruling: address the cast authentically. The W1 suggestion text (a route-carrying imperative per finding) shipped as v0.41.1; the re-probe then passed four of four at both temperatures, and a re-audit of every disposition found no other hollow claim.
plan/0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhashcomplete, shipped as host-lifecycle v0.43.0 (4f27c7a, artifact 82cbb3b2, 2026-07-23) (broadened 2026-07-20): closes host-lifecycle#18 (provenance) and host-lifecycle#19 (coherence) plus a new issue for the bootstrap and completeness gate. Originally the materialize receipt (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#18, a checked-in .host-lifecycle-receipts EVENT) plus the environment hash (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#19, a gitignored .host-envhash STATE read by advisory env --check), paired for their shared call sites under a non-overlap discipline (receipt records events and forbids state; envhash records state and forbids events). Broadened to formal materialization after the 2026-07-20 session found the fresh-clone bootstrap is unmechanized prose (host-repo hooks were never installed in this clone yet software --check stayed green): adds (3) a bootstrap orchestrator (a thin tracked bootstrap.sh self-seed plus a generic recipe-driven host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir> that RUNS the fresh-clone sequence idempotently) and (4) a completeness gate (a new software verify mode that reads the recipe-vs-live and HAZARDs on any missing worktree, host or worktree hook, off-PATH re-deriver, or unlinked skill), folding in Bug A (--install-hooks gates every materialized worktree, not just the host repo). The non-overlap discipline is now three-way (receipt = event; envhash = drift-from-recorded; completeness gate = incomplete-vs-recipe). Operator rulings (2026-07-19): paired; two files; two subcommands; full methodology. (2026-07-20): absorb bootstrap and completeness into this plan; thin script plus tested tool core; completeness is a separate verify mode rather than part of --check; spine doctrine with agentic-host's self-seed as instance config; the names are Fen-settled (gather-data.md, rotation-proof): host-lifecycle bootstrap for the orchestrator and software --verify-setup for the completeness gate.
plan/0077-reference-resolvercomplete 2026-07-26, released as host-lifecycle v0.44.1 (35ab4d24, artifact 9b4e3e1e): closes host-lifecycle#17 and the parked full-URL row above, queue position four. Two halves of one capability: a resolver that turns plan/NNNN, call/NNNN and #N into a path, a markdown link or a GitHub URL, and a check that reports the references the site cannot render. Grounded in this tree: 122 distinct register references, all resolvable by hand and none by tool, and 374 bare issue numbers outside code fences, of which 187 sit in the append-only MEMORY.md and 35 in a dated review artifact, so the record layer is excluded rather than rewritten. Out of scope and recorded: linkifying commit messages in the generated site. The adversarial round found the coverage class a third time and the reason was structural, so the spec now models the corpus (a document, whether it was withheld, whether it could be read) and three invariants bite on it; each new disposition was proven by mutation. The round also found both remedy strings naming this project's tracker, which would have handed every adopter a command rewriting their reference into a link to somebody else's issues, and it found the rename's ledger verify testing a token where the tool renames a key, which could wedge an adopter permanently. plan/0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifactcut 2026-08-02, not started, decided by call/0053. call/0004 chose copy-at-version on 2026-06-14 and this repository never made the copy. The rule was ratified, promoted into the spine itself, and held for no commit; nothing detected it because nothing re-derives it. That is the asymmetry the milestone closes. The spine becomes a file set defined by extension rather than by description, a project's manual becomes a render over a project-authored fragment, and spine --check re-derives it byte for byte inside the verify recheck, with no waiver, no advisory tier, and the deriving binary named in the output. plan/0081-openwrt-style-packcut 2026-08-10, draft: host-lint-openwrt, the second external pack, built to the shape plan/0072 established. It encodes the four measured style manuals governing a package contributed to openwrt/packages (TITLE and description, comments, commit messages, pull request bodies) as four lanes, one per manual. The pr lane is the odd one: its subject lives on GitHub rather than in the clone, so it reads an argument or standard input and refuses a directory rather than sweeping one. It also forced a distinction the FFmpeg pack never had to draw, settled by call/0055: a rule source the pack owns is vendored and digest-pinned, while an artefact the pack checks a submission against is referenced and resolved at check time, temporarily cached and never embedded, because freezing a file another project moves is a wrong answer with a long shelf life. Unlike the FFmpeg pack it starts calibrated: upstream states no convention for the description block, so every rule rests on a counted share of the live tree and carries that share as its measured rate. The mail, series, maintainers, forge and cosmetic lanes stay out by design: openwrt/packages takes pull requests, so those lanes would be dead code behind a live tier. The comment lane carries a provenance guard the others do not need: two thirds of the tree's patches were written locally and one third are cherry-picked upstream commits, so the lane reads a patch header before treating its prose as OpenWrt's to restyle.

Enforced remap dictionary

Status: done (host-lifecycle 0.2.0, 3e55417; remap --check/--apply, 8 tests + scratch integration green, CI green). External dogfood satisfied by the yarn-agentic case-(b) adoption (issue #6); see "Dogfood, closed" below. Decision: call/0008. Builds on host-lifecycle (the token-free migrator, call/0003), host-lint (the policy-free detector), and .host-lint-allow (call/0006).

Goal

A token-free host-lifecycle facility that applies an adoption rename map deterministically, guarantees map-only (no fabrication, no spatial drift), forces every detected tell to be explicitly dispositioned, and leaves no permanent old-vocabulary artifact. host-lint stays a pure detector that faults on tells and never consults the dictionary (call/0008: fault, policy-free).

Dictionary format (proposed)

A plain transient file at the repo root, e.g. .host-remap: one old<TAB>new per line; # comments and blank lines ignored. old is a literal concept token/phrase (an ordinal tell in any spelling, spaced, concatenated, or decimal-suffixed); new is the human-supplied canonical content-name. Matched case-insensitively and word-bounded, reusing the allow-list masking discipline so a short tell cannot clip a longer one that contains it as a prefix. Same hand-rolled, dependency-free parse style as .host / .host-lint-allow.

Verbs (host-lifecycle, matching the existing match args.get(1) style)

  • remap --check <dir>: completeness. Run host-lint, enumerate every flagged token, and classify each as map (a .host-remap entry exists), allow (a .host-lint-allow entry exists), or UNDISPOSITIONED. Exit non-zero while any token is undispositioned. Token-free; the human reads the list and supplies names.
  • remap --apply <dir>: archive originals first (copy each touched file to a preserved archive, or assert a clean tree + tag), then substitute only declared entries, word-bounded, across tracked text files; never touch an unmapped token. Print changed-vs-skipped. Deterministic.
  • Teardown is an ordinary git rm .host-remap + commit; the durable map is embedded in the migration call/ decision, not left in the tree.

Invariants (verification lane)

  • The applied diff contains only declared substitutions (golden-file test).
  • An undispositioned flagged token makes --check fail (no silent residue).
  • --apply is idempotent and deterministic, same inputs yield same output, no Date/random (host-lifecycle stays replayable).
  • Originals are recoverable: the archive exists before any substitution.
  • host-lint is unchanged; it gains no dictionary awareness (policy-free).

Dogfood, closed

remap was exercised end-to-end by the yarn-agentic case-(b) adoption (issue #6): a 131-milestone corpus renamed to NNNN-slug, cross-references rewritten in scannable files, the durable map captured in that project's migration call/. That run also surfaced the remap spec-blind spot: declared substitutions did not reach .allium/.tla/.cfg, now fixed (spec-aware remap, host-lifecycle v0.6.0, plan/0003). The originally-planned Agentic-MCP-Win32s dogfood is descoped (its earlier attempt was rejected; superseded by yarn-agentic as the live remap exercise).

Out of scope

  • An ongoing drift gate (call/0008: redundant with host-lint and a per-commit token cost; fault, policy-free instead).
  • Rewriting git history (tier 3 is acknowledged, not rewritten; call/0007).
  • Inventing any new name: every new value is human-supplied.

Canonical doc-site publisher

Status: built (host-lifecycle v0.6.1, 5738808; book + book --check, tests green, smoke-built on this repo with mdBook). Decision: call/0014. Ships the one canonical mdBook publisher for the five rooms, fixing the doc-site gaps a case-(b) adoption reported (the agentic-host doc-site issue), four of which reproduced on this repository's own site. Builds on host-lifecycle (the token-free generator, call/0003) and the bare-store software model (call/0010/call/0011).

Goal

A token-free host-lifecycle book that publishes all five rooms in one maintained artifact, so no adopter hand-rolls a generator that drops a room or sets src = "." (the call/0011 hazard). Concretely it must: scope src to a generated docs/; emit SUMMARY.md in lifecycle order (Who, What/When, Where, Why, How, Memory); render every spec as a fenced page; emit a Where stub parsed from .host-software; and gate room coverage so a half-room site cannot ship green.

What was built

  • host-lifecycle book <dir> [--dry-run]: writes book.toml (src = "docs"), rebuilds docs/ (copying room prose, generating spec pages and the Where stub), and writes docs/SUMMARY.md in lifecycle order.
  • host-lifecycle book --check <dir>: fails (exit 1) naming any room with source material that renders no page with content; skips a room with no source.
  • The Where stub reads .host-software only (name, url, pin, worktrees, materialize command), so it renders with no worktree on disk, safe in an un-materialized checkout.

Two host-lifecycle tooling fixes filed in the same report rode along in v0.6.0: the explicit worktree = <dir> <branch> <pin> recipe form (a parallel line is reproduced on its own branch at its own pin, not the canonical one), and a spec-aware remap (declared substitutions now reach .allium/.tla/.cfg).

Invariants (verification lane)

  • SUMMARY.md part order is exactly Cast, Plan, Software, Call, Reference, Memory (unit test).
  • --check fails when a room with source renders nothing, passes when every such room renders a content page, and skips a source-less room (unit test).
  • book.toml is src = "docs", never "." (unit test); additional-css only when the repo ships custom.css.
  • A spec body is rendered as a fenced code page whose fence outgrows any backtick run in the body (unit test).
  • --dry-run writes nothing.

Dogfood

This repository (adopter zero): replace the hand-maintained SUMMARY.md and the src = "." book.toml with host-lifecycle book, re-pin tools/host-lifecycle to v0.6.1, re-stamp .host to the template revision that introduced the publisher, and run book + book --check in the Site workflow before mdbook build. Verify gh-pages redeploys with a Where section and lifecycle-ordered nav.

Out of scope
