Lens C's other findings do not depend on this and remain valid.</p> <h2 id="blocking-design-gaps-to-resolve-in-the-re-cut"><a class="header" href="#blocking-design-gaps-to-resolve-in-the-re-cut">Blocking design gaps (to resolve in the re-cut)</a></h2> <p><strong>G1. host-prove has zero dependencies, so the "one reusable bundle for all three" is false.</strong> host-prove's lockfile is a single package (itself); host-lifecycle has 11; host-lint has 77 (the superset, and lifecycle's third-party set is a subset of it). The bundle is effectively host-lint's vendor set; host-lifecycle reuses it incidentally; host-prove vendors nothing and builds offline trivially against an empty source set. Reframe: name host-lint the bundle owner, drop the three-way-overlap claim, and state host-prove is in scope only for the static-musl plus <code>--network none</code> mechanism, not the bundle.</p> <p><strong>G2. host-lifecycle pins a stale host-lint git rev, so distribute-equals-certify is already broken inside it.</strong> host-lifecycle's <code>Cargo.toml</code> depends on <code>host-lint</code> at git rev <code>93a43fa</code> (the pre-version-bump commit), while the certified <code>.host-software</code> host-lint pin is now <code>1386e9a</code> (v0.8.1). host-lifecycle's binary therefore embeds an older host-lint than the one certified, and a combined bundle would carry two host-lint revisions. Reconcile host-lifecycle's <code>host-lint</code> git rev to the certified pin <strong>before</strong> any bundle is cut; this is a Readiness prerequisite, and it is a latent inconsistency carried over from the plan/0028 cutover.</p> <p><strong>G3. The host-lifecycle staging logic, the load-bearing part, is unspecified and not expressible today.</strong> <code>software_verify_build</code> checks out a throwaway <code>.host-verify</code> worktree at the pin and calls <code>run_build_in_container</code>, which mounts only <code>src:/src</code>. There is no step to extract the vendor tarball into the worktree and write the source-replacement config, so an in-container <code>cargo build --offline</code> resolves nothing. And <code>run_build_in_container</code> takes <code>(runtime, image, build, src)</code> with no component context and chooses the network only from the global <code>HOST_LIFECYCLE_DOCKER_NETWORK</code> env, so it cannot pass <code>--network none</code> per-component. The re-cut must specify: a host-side fetch-and-sha-verify, extraction into the build tree, a merge of the vendored-sources stanzas into the existing <code>.cargo/config.toml</code>, and a network-mode parameter threaded into <code>run_build_in_container</code> (bundle present implies <code>--network none</code>; absent keeps the env behaviour, so the change is additive for not-yet-converted components).</p> <p><strong>G4. The source-replacement config collides with the tracked <code>.cargo/config.toml</code>.</strong> All three tools already track a <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> carrying the reproducibility <code>--build-id=none</code> rustflag. The <code>cargo vendor</code> <code>[source.*]</code> stanzas must be <strong>merged into</strong> that file, not overwrite it, or the build-id flag is lost and the hash moves for the wrong reason. This also interacts with Readiness's existing note that the musl image may shadow the flag via a <code>CARGO_TARGET_*_RUSTFLAGS</code> env; the re-cut must reconcile all three edits to that one file and prove the double-build hash is unchanged.</p> <h2 id="bundle-specifics-to-tighten-in-the-re-cut"><a class="header" href="#bundle-specifics-to-tighten-in-the-re-cut">Bundle specifics (to tighten in the re-cut)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Two git sources, not one.</strong> <code>cargo vendor</code> must replace both <code>host-grammar</code> and (for host-lifecycle) the <code>host-lint</code> git source; the exact <code>[source."git+...?rev=..."]</code> keys must match the lockfile byte-for-byte. Capture <code>cargo vendor</code>'s full stdout and commit it; the plan names only host-grammar.</li> <li><strong>Exact commands.</strong> Multi-manifest vendoring needs <code>cargo vendor --locked --sync <manifest> ...</code>, not a bare <code>cargo vendor</code>; and <code>cargo vendor</code> must run <code>--locked</code> or it can silently update the lock and vendor a drifted set. The build flag is <code>--locked --offline</code> (or <code>--frozen</code>).</li> <li><strong>Bundle determinism is its own gate.</strong> The tarball sha must be reproducible (normalized tar: <code>--sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner</code>, gzip <code>-n</code>), proven by a double-produce on two machines, or the published sha is a trusted blob, not a verifiable input. Add this to Readiness.</li> <li><strong>Bundle home: host-lint, not agentic-host.</strong> Hosting the bundle on an agentic-host release would invert the dependency direction (the software's producer CI would build-depend on the host). Host it on host-lint's releases (it is the dep superset); host-lifecycle consumes host-lint's bundle (it already depends on host-lint); host-prove consumes nothing. Record this in Decisions, not as an execution detail.</li> <li><strong>One source of truth for the pin.</strong> The <code>deps-bundle</code> pin lives in <code>.host-software</code> (agentic-host), but each producer CI (in its own repo) also needs the URL and sha to converge. Avoid two hand-edited copies: either commit a <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> in the producer repo that <code>software --check</code> asserts equals <code>.host-software</code>, or generate the producer CI from <code>.host-software</code>.</li> <li><strong>Scope the bundle to <code>--release</code>.</strong> <code>cargo vendor</code> vendors the whole lockfile, including host-lint's <code>proptest</code> dev-dependency tree (60-plus crates, with proc-macros). Harmless for <code>cargo build --release</code>, but it bloats the bundle and, if offline <code>cargo test</code> is ever run, raises a host-target proc-macro question. State <code>--release</code>-only scope.</li> <li><strong>Release-build worktree hygiene.</strong> <code>release</code> builds in the live canonical worktree, not a throwaway, so a staged <code>vendor/</code> and a config edit land in the tree the operator commits. Revert the edit and gitignore <code>vendor/</code> after the build so the worktree is not left dirty against the pin.</li> <li><strong>Bound the hermeticity claim.</strong> The producer <code>cargo vendor</code> job and the gate-driver <code>cargo install --rev</code> seed are network-allowed by design; the MUST scopes only to the per-component container build. <code>install_hooks</code> only copies the artifact, so it stays bundle-unaware.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-spine-must-the-decision-the-review-forces"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-must-the-decision-the-review-forces">The spine MUST: the decision the review forces</a></h2> <p>The fourth lens argues the MUST, as drafted (mandate the bundle mechanism, verified by <code>--network none</code>), has four problems: (1) <code>--network none</code> proves no egress, not that the build consumed the pinned bundle, so the real proof is bundle-sha verification plus a clean <code>CARGO_HOME</code>; (2) it is too strong for a general adopter and has no escape, where the reproducible-build anchor it builds on ships a <code>repro-exempt = call/NNNN</code> escape; (3) it is enforceable only for a component that opts in by recording <code>deps-bundle</code>, so a static-shipping component that omits it is invisible to the gate, which makes the universal wording unverifiable; (4) authoring a spine MUST inside an agentic-host project plan and a project <code>call/</code> risks forking the spine, which the anti-ouroboros rule forbids.</p> <p>The review's recommended shape, which preserves the MUST strength where it belongs:</p> <ul> <li>The spine requirement is the <strong>property</strong>: a component distributing release binaries MUST be able to reproduce them offline from pinned inputs. The bundle is the <strong>recommended mechanism</strong>, documented in build guidance, not itself the MUST.</li> <li>Ship a <code>hermetic-exempt = call/NNNN</code> escape, mirroring <code>repro-exempt</code>, so a non-pure-Rust adopter is not trapped.</li> <li>The <strong>enforceable gate invariant</strong> is honest and specific: a component that records a <code>deps-bundle</code> MUST build offline under <code>--network none</code> and its staged bundle sha MUST match the recorded hash.</li> <li><strong>Author in <code>host-template</code> first</strong>, migrate onto agentic-host via the <code>UPGRADING.md</code> ledger and a <code>.host</code> baseline advance; the agentic-host <code>call/</code> records only the software decision (the <code>deps-bundle</code> production-anchor change, instance-scoped), never the methodology MUST.</li> </ul> <p>This keeps a MUST (on the property), makes it general and escapable, makes the gate's claim match what it checks, and respects copy-at-version. The operator chose a MUST; this refines where the MUST attaches rather than reversing it.</p> <h2 id="per-lens-verdicts"><a class="header" href="#per-lens-verdicts">Per-lens verdicts</a></h2> <ul> <li>cargo vendor and offline correctness: proceed-with-revisions (sound in principle; the offline contract, the two git sources, and the <code>--sync</code>/<code>--locked</code> commands must be specified and the config merge proven).</li> <li>host-lifecycle feature and bootstrap: blocking-incomplete (the staging logic and the <code>--network none</code> path do not exist yet and are the load-bearing work).</li> <li>bundle hosting, versioning, reuse: re-scope (host-prove has no deps, host-lifecycle pins a stale host-lint rev, the bundle home is a real dependency-inversion decision, and the pin has two sources of truth).</li> <li>spine MUST soundness and adopter impact: re-scope (attach the MUST to the property with an exemption and an honest gate invariant, author it in the template first).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0032-design-review"><a class="header" href="#plan0032-design-review">plan/0032 design-review</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Verdict: re-scope (proceed only with major revisions).</strong> Five independent adversarial lenses (reproducibility, bootstrap/self-cert, re-release ordering, scope/cross-platform, altitude/necessity) reviewed the plan. Three returned <em>re-scope</em>, one <em>blocking-incomplete</em>, one <em>proceed-with-revisions</em>. The musl-cross image the plan needs does exist and is digest-pinnable, and the re-release mechanics are sound, but three headline payoffs are over-claimed or false, two execution hazards are unstated, and the simplest alternative was never weighed. The kernel survives only once the actual goal is restated.</p> </blockquote> <p>This review is a frozen record. It captures the findings as of 2026-06-22; the plan is re-cut in response, and the re-cut supersedes the plan text the findings critique.</p> <h2 id="method"><a class="header" href="#method">Method</a></h2> <p>Five lenses, each an independent reviewer reading the plan plus the relevant source (<code>host-lifecycle</code> <code>run_release</code>/<code>software_verify_build</code>/<code>install_hooks</code>/<code>run_build_in_container</code>, <code>.host-software</code>, the producer CI workflows, and the <code>plan/0028</code> MEMORY lessons). Each returned up to six findings with evidence and a fix. The findings below are consolidated and de-duplicated across lenses; the per-lens verdicts are listed at the end.</p> <h2 id="blocking-findings"><a class="header" href="#blocking-findings">Blocking findings</a></h2> <p><strong>B1. The motivating breakage is sanctioned by design, not a defect (necessity).</strong> The canonical binary is <em>executed</em> in exactly one place, <code>install_hooks</code> copying it into <code>.git/hooks</code>; <code>--verify-build</code> and <code>--check</code> only <em>hash</em> it. The reproducibility anchor never needs the canonical binary to run on the dev host. The one place that runs it already has a designed fallback: the local build, whose hash-mismatch note is "informational, not a gate" (the comment at <code>install_hooks</code> ~line 1213, and the <code>plan/0009</code> decision that the install gate is worktree-at-pin, not byte-hash, recorded in MEMORY). So the concrete current breakage the switch removes is cosmetic: the recorded and runnable binaries become the same file. The plan must name a concrete non-cosmetic breakage or concede the motivation is aesthetic.</p> <p><strong>B2. "Certify the binary we distribute" is false against the producer CI.</strong> <code>--verify-build</code> reproduces the recipe inside the recorded digest-pinned <code>toolchain</code> container with <code>--locked</code> and the strip/build-id hardening. Each producer's release CI builds its musl assets with a different, non-hermetic recipe: <code>rustup target add</code> plus a plain <code>cargo build --release --target</code> on a stock <code>ubuntu-latest</code>, no <code>--locked</code>, no pinned image, no reproducible double-build (host-lint <code>ci.yml:42-47</code>, host-lifecycle likewise; host-prove has no musl build at all). Two different toolchains do not byte-match. So the recorded canonical artifact will not equal the shipped release asset, and the "distribute one, certify another" gap does not close, it moves. Delivering this claim requires converting each producer's release job to build the canonical in the same pinned image, which the plan never scopes.</p> <p><strong>B3. <code>--install-hooks</code> MISSes the musl artifact, and a premature recipe push reddens CI.</strong> After the recipe edit, <code>install_hooks</code> reads <code>worktree.join("target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/<bin>")</code> and exits 1 with <code>MISSING ... build the component first</code> unless that file is already in the canonical worktree. Nothing in the dev flow puts it there: <code>--verify-build</code> builds into a throwaway <code>.host-verify</code> worktree it removes immediately, and the <code>plan/0028</code> local-build workaround built the glibc path <code>target/release/<bin></code>, which no longer matches the recipe. Separately, if the musl-edited <code>.host-software</code> (new build/artifact path) is committed and pushed to main while the recorded hash is still the old glibc sha and the pin is still the old commit, the next push runs <code>reproducible-build.yml</code>, whose <code>--verify-build</code> rebuilds at the old pin in the new recipe and DRIFTs against the stale hash, RED. Both need explicit handling: a step that produces the musl binary at the new path before <code>--install-hooks</code>, and an atomic-sequence rule that the recipe edit, new hash, new pin, and receipts land in one commit and never split across a push.</p> <h2 id="major-findings"><a class="header" href="#major-findings">Major findings</a></h2> <p><strong>M1. The simpler alternative was never weighed (altitude).</strong> glibc is forward-compatible, so building the canonical glibc binary in an <em>older-glibc</em> base image (an older debian/rust image) yields a canonical binary that runs on the dev WSL by changing one field, the <code>toolchain</code> digest, with no target flag, no musl-cross image hunt, no host-prove work, and no allocator footnote. The plan weighs only musl-internal alternatives (pinned image versus in-recipe target-add) and never records why an older-glibc canonical is rejected. Per the spine's "describe the simpler approach," this must be weighed explicitly or adopted.</p> <p><strong>M2. Wrong altitude: two concerns folded into one file.</strong> The canonical reproducibility artifact (the thing <code>--verify-build</code> hashes, which wants the simplest deterministic build) and the portable runnable binary (needed only by the hook install, and already produced by CI as a release asset) are distinct. Folding portability into the anchor adds a static-musl constraint to a file whose job is byte-reproducibility and drags in the hermeticity worry the plan then has to defend. If hook portability is genuinely wanted, fix it at the layer that needs it (have the hook install consume the verified CI musl asset, or keep the local-build fallback) and leave the anchor the simplest build.</p> <p><strong>M3. host-prove conversion is scope creep.</strong> Only host-lint carries <code>hooks = pre-commit</code>; host-prove and host-lifecycle binaries are never installed as hooks, so the <code>GLIBC_2.39</code> motivation does not apply to them. host-prove additionally ships no release asset today (its CI is a single smoke job with no release pipeline), so "recorded artifact equals distributed asset" has nothing to match. Converting host-prove plus building out its musl CI is uniformity-only work smuggled under a hook-portability headline. Cut it from this plan, or decide and price it as its own line item.</p> <p><strong>M4. "Any Linux" conflates OS with architecture.</strong> A static musl x86_64 binary runs on any Linux with an x86_64 kernel, not on aarch64 Linux, darwin, or windows. <code>attest-host</code> gates on <code>std::env::consts::OS</code> only (linux/macos/windows), with no arch dimension, and the current flat stanza form (no <code>attest-host</code>) attests on <em>any</em> host. So on an aarch64 Linux dev or CI host the recorded x86_64-musl recipe would attempt an x86_64 build and DRIFT rather than skip, and the producer's shipped aarch64/darwin/windows assets are never reproducibility-certified. The plan must scope the anchor to x86_64 Linux explicitly and decide the fate of the other shipped assets (record per-platform builds with their own shas, or declare them uncertified at the release surface).</p> <p><strong>M5. The "hermetic / no network fetch" rationale for the image is largely false.</strong> The build already fetches the <code>host-grammar</code> git dependency and the crates.io deps over the network (no vendor dir, no <code>--offline</code>, and <code>run_build_in_container</code> deliberately omits <code>--network none</code> and exposes <code>HOST_LIFECYCLE_DOCKER_NETWORK</code> precisely because network is needed). Preinstalling the musl std removes only the <code>rustup target add</code> fetch, a tiny slice of the network surface. Either drop the hermeticity claim and pick the image on the honest grounds (it ships the musl target), or actually vendor the deps and assert <code>--network none</code>.</p> <p><strong>M6. musl reproducibility is asserted, not proven.</strong> <code>--build-id=none</code> is injected via <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> scoped to <code>cfg(target_os = "linux")</code> (which includes musl), but a musl-cross image can set <code>CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_RUSTFLAGS</code>, which fully <em>replaces</em> the config <code>target.*.rustflags</code> (cargo does not merge), silently dropping the flag; and static linking depends on <code>+crt-static</code> and static-PIE defaults that have varied by rustc version and image. The Readiness step must double-build in the candidate image and <code>readelf -n</code> the binary to confirm no build-id and a stable hash <em>before</em> recording it, and pin the full linking configuration, not just the target triple.</p> <h2 id="confirmed-what-survives"><a class="header" href="#confirmed-what-survives">Confirmed (what survives)</a></h2> <ul> <li>The image exists and is digest-pinnable: <code>clux/muslrust:1.95.0-stable</code> (last built 2026-05-27). <code>messense/rust-musl-cross</code> has no 1.95.0 tag (rolling stable), so it is not a co-equal candidate.</li> <li><code>--change-class neither</code> is the correct class for a build-recipe change; it yields patch bumps (host-lint 0.8.2, host-lifecycle 0.19.3, host-prove 0.2.1 to 0.2.2), and <code>current_version</code> reads the last tag, so a re-run is version-idempotent.</li> <li><code>run_release</code> reads the on-disk recipe, so editing <code>toolchain</code>/<code>build</code> first makes <code>release</code> build the musl artifact and compute the right hash; the per-component interleave (edit recipe in the working tree, release, push the producer tag, then re-pin) is sound.</li> <li>host-lifecycle re-releasing itself works (the container build is independent of the glibc-local driver); the gate driver must be reinstalled from the released commit before the final green.</li> <li>Adding a toolchain to the three artifact tools and not to repo-only <code>host</code>/<code>host-grammar</code> raises no gate inconsistency.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-pivotal-question-for-the-re-cut"><a class="header" href="#the-pivotal-question-for-the-re-cut">The pivotal question for the re-cut</a></h2> <p>The findings converge on one decision the plan never settles: <strong>what is the actual goal?</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>G1, hook portability only.</strong> Make the canonical binary run on the dev host so the hook install stops diverging. Then the cheapest correct move is an older-glibc canonical image (M1), a one-field change, or doing nothing (B1, the local-build path is green by design). musl, all-three, and host-prove are unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>G2, distribute-equals-certify.</strong> Make the shipped binary and the certified binary the same. The load-bearing work is converting each producer's release CI to build the canonical in the pinned image (B2); only then is musl-static the right choice, for distribution portability across any Linux x86_64. This is larger than the plan scoped and must be priced.</li> </ul> <h2 id="recommended-re-cut-decisions"><a class="header" href="#recommended-re-cut-decisions">Recommended re-cut decisions</a></h2> <ol> <li>State the goal (G1, G2, or both) before anything else; it determines the whole shape.</li> <li>If G1: prefer the older-glibc image (or status quo); drop musl, drop host-prove, drop the byte-match claim.</li> <li>If G2: scope in producer-CI convergence onto the recorded recipe; keep musl for portability; price the producer work.</li> <li>Either way, scope the anchor to x86_64 Linux explicitly (M4) and decide the other assets' fate.</li> <li>Cut host-prove unless G2 uniformity is chosen and priced (M3).</li> <li>Make the musl-image digest confirmation and a reproducible double-build (build-id <code>readelf</code> check) a blocking Readiness gate, not a risk bullet (M6); pin the full linking config.</li> <li>Fix or drop the hermeticity claim (M5).</li> <li>Document the atomic re-pin sequence: recipe edits stay uncommitted until the producer tag is pushed, and one host commit carries toolchain, build, artifact path and hash, pin, and receipts (B3); add the explicit step that places the musl binary at the new path before <code>--install-hooks</code>.</li> </ol> <h2 id="per-lens-verdicts-1"><a class="header" href="#per-lens-verdicts-1">Per-lens verdicts</a></h2> <ul> <li>Reproducibility and toolchain hermeticity: proceed-with-revisions (image confirmed; F1 hermeticity, F3 asset byte-match, and F4 build-id survival must be fixed before recording any hash).</li> <li>Bootstrap, self-cert, install-hooks: re-scope (install-hooks MISSes the musl path; the divergence-retires and asset-byte-match payoffs are over-claims).</li> <li>Re-release ordering: blocking-incomplete (the RED-window and the install-hooks musl-path precondition need explicit atomic sequencing).</li> <li>Scope and cross-platform: proceed only after scoping host-prove out, scoping to x86_64, and making the multi-platform trust boundary explicit.</li> <li>Altitude and necessity: re-scope (the breakage is sanctioned by design, the older-glibc fix was never weighed, and a second full re-release round the same day as the cutover is the wrong cost at the wrong time for a cosmetic benefit).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0033-the-generated-book-is-correct-and-obeys-the-prose-hygiene-rule"><a class="header" href="#plan0033-the-generated-book-is-correct-and-obeys-the-prose-hygiene-rule">plan/0033: the generated book is correct and obeys the prose-hygiene rule</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Goal:</strong> close <code>connollydavid/host#15</code>. The methodology's own published book has two defects. First, <code>host-lifecycle book</code> emits a generated home-page link to a room landing whose source is <code>README.md</code>, and mdBook serves that page at <code>index.html</code> while rewriting the in-content link to <code>README.html</code>, so the link is a 404. Second, the rendered book carries em-dashes that the prose-hygiene rule (<code>plan/0030</code>) forbids in authored docs: the five generated room separators and roughly 113 em-dashes in the spine (<code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>) that every adopter renders in the Reference section. Operator ruling: clean fully, so the book obeys the rule the methodology preaches.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="context-7"><a class="header" href="#context-7">Context</a></h2> <p><code>host#15</code> was observed building the mdBook for an adopted project. Two findings:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Dead room-landing link.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle book</code> generates the home page (<code>docs/index.md</code>) with a bullet per room linking the room's first page. For a room whose landing file is <code>README.md</code> (the Cast room is the example), the emitted link is <code>cast/README.md</code>. mdBook applies its README-to-index rule and serves that page at <code>cast/index.html</code>, but it rewrites the in-content link to <code>cast/README.html</code>, which is never generated. The home page (and the aggregated <code>print.html</code>) therefore carry a 404. The sidebar nav link works, because mdBook maps <code>SUMMARY</code> chapter links through the README-to-index rule; only the generated in-content link breaks.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The methodology breaks its own prose-hygiene rule.</strong> <code>plan/0030</code> shipped a rule: authored docs carry zero prose tropes, and a decoration em-dash is a flagged trope. The rendered book shows em-dashes anyway, from two tool-controlled sources: the generated nav separators that <code>host-lifecycle book</code> writes for the five room part-titles, and the spine prose (<code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>) that renders verbatim in every adopter's Reference section. <code>host-lint --prose</code> flags roughly 96 em-dashes in the spine <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and 17 in <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, plus a few other tropes (negative parallelism, a false range, a decoration arrow, an anaphora run).</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-operator-ruling-2026-06-22"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-ruling-2026-06-22">Decision (operator ruling, 2026-06-22)</a></h2> <p><strong>Clean fully.</strong> Both tool-generated sources move off the em-dash, and the spine prose is reworded to <code>host-lint --prose</code> clean with meaning preserved. The alternative (an explicit exemption for the spine and the generated nav) was weighed and rejected: the methodology should obey the rule it asks every adopter to obey, and the issue itself notes that cleaning is the fix that makes the methodology consistent.</p> <h2 id="part-a-the-host-lifecycle-book-generator"><a class="header" href="#part-a-the-host-lifecycle-book-generator">Part A: the <code>host-lifecycle book</code> generator</a></h2> <p>Two changes in the <code>book</code> generator, with unit tests:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Home-page room links resolve.</strong> When the generated home overview links a room landing whose destination basename is <code>README.md</code>, link the page mdBook actually serves (<code><dir>/index.md</code>, which mdBook rewrites to <code><dir>/index.html</code>) rather than <code><dir>/README.md</code>. The <code>SUMMARY</code> nav links already resolve through mdBook's README-to-index rule and stay as they are.</li> <li><strong>Nav separators carry no em-dash.</strong> The five room part-titles (Cast, Plan, Software, Call, Reference) use a colon separator ("Cast: who") in place of the em-dash, so the generated sidebar and home overview obey the prose-hygiene rule on every page.</li> </ul> <p>The change alters the generated book output, so it ships as a <code>host-lifecycle</code> release (a fix to the generator). The recorded musl artifact moves, so <code>.host-software</code> re-pins and the release receipt is back-filled.</p> <h2 id="part-b-the-spine-prose"><a class="header" href="#part-b-the-spine-prose">Part B: the spine prose</a></h2> <p><code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> are reworded so <code>host-lint --prose</code> reports zero on both. Em-dashes become commas, colons, parentheses, or sentence breaks; the few other flagged tropes are reworded in place. Meaning is preserved exactly: only flagged punctuation and phrasing change, and every identifier, version string, citation, and rule stays byte-for-byte. The spine commit is pushed in <code>host-template</code>, then the agentic-host submodule pointer is bumped to it so the rendered Reference section is clean. This is a prose-only spine revision with no new adopter action, so it carries no <code>UPGRADING.md</code> ledger entry.</p> <h2 id="lifecycle-run-software-first"><a class="header" href="#lifecycle-run-software-first">Lifecycle run (software-first)</a></h2> <ol> <li>Implement Part A in the <code>host-lifecycle</code> worktree, with unit tests; <code>cargo test</code> and clippy clean.</li> <li>Implement Part B in the <code>host-template</code> worktree; verify <code>host-lint --prose</code> is zero on both files; commit and push <code>host-template</code>.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle release host-lifecycle --change-class neither</code> (a generator fix), run its printed commit, push, and tag steps, and collect the new pin and musl artifact hash.</li> <li>One atomic agentic-host commit: re-pin <code>.host-software</code> <code>host-lifecycle</code>, back-fill the release receipt, and bump the <code>host-template</code> submodule pointer.</li> <li>Reinstall the gate driver from the released commit.</li> <li>Gate with the released binary: <code>software --check</code>, <code>software --verify-build</code> (the artifact reproduces), <code>book</code> then <code>book --check</code>, and a direct check that the generated <code>docs/index.md</code> no longer links a <code>README.md</code>, that the generated nav carries no em-dash, and that the rendered spine pages are prose-clean.</li> <li>CI rewire: move the agentic-host workflow <code>host-lifecycle</code> install pins to the released commit.</li> <li>Records: this plan, the <code>PLAN.md</code> row, <code>MEMORY.md</code>, and a close comment on <code>host#15</code>.</li> </ol> <h2 id="verification-whole-suite-green-1"><a class="header" href="#verification-whole-suite-green-1">Verification (whole-suite green)</a></h2> <ul> <li>A <code>cargo test</code> case proves the home overview links the served page for a <code>README.md</code> landing, and a case proves the generated nav part-titles carry no em-dash.</li> <li><code>host-lint --prose</code> is zero on <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>.</li> <li>The regenerated <code>docs/index.md</code> contains no <code>](</code>-link ending in <code>README.md</code>, and the generated <code>docs/SUMMARY.md</code> part-titles carry no em-dash.</li> <li><code>software --check</code>, <code>software --verify-build</code>, and <code>book --check</code> are green; the producer and agentic-host CI runs are green across every repo.</li> </ul> <h2 id="records-2"><a class="header" href="#records-2">Records</a></h2> <p>This plan, the <code>PLAN.md</code> row, <code>MEMORY.md</code>, and the <code>host#15</code> close comment. No <code>call/</code> decision is needed: Part A is a tool bugfix and Part B is a prose-clean of the spine, neither a methodology decision.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0034-the-hygiene-grammar-grows-by-reflective-practice-fixes-host16"><a class="header" href="#plan0034-the-hygiene-grammar-grows-by-reflective-practice-fixes-host16">plan/0034: the hygiene grammar grows by reflective practice (fixes host#16)</a></h1> <p>Resolves connollydavid/host#16 (positional checklist-item references evade the ordinal lane).</p> <h2 id="context-8"><a class="header" href="#context-8">Context</a></h2> <p>host#16 reports that host-lint does not catch positional references to milestone checklist items. The shapes, quoted as the lane would receive them:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">box 7 boxes 4-8 steps 3-5 step 3-5 </code></pre> <p>The meeting that produced this milestone established, against the adopter where the shape emerged (reviewed in a scratch checkout only, never referenced in tracked files):</p> <ul> <li><strong>The guard is blind to the shape.</strong> None of the positional references in that adopter's history or its two milestone READMEs were caught on the noun token; the only non-clean verdicts fired on an em-dash. Plural and range forms also evade, because <code>check_line</code> splits on whitespace and tests one token against a singular noun set.</li> <li><strong>Not a migration artifact.</strong> The shape first appears in milestones authored fresh, whose items already carried content titles. It is an emergent authoring habit, and it is not in our spine (host-template never defined a checklist convention).</li> <li><strong>The available content name was bypassed.</strong> A reference cited a sibling item by position even where a content name was at hand, so adding content anchors at the source would not have prevented it. The fix is detection plus doctrine, not a convention.</li> <li><strong>The deeper gap is methodological.</strong> The spine already forbade positional naming; an agent ignored a rule it had, and the lane stayed silent. We had detection as a refusal with no sanctioned positive path, and no stated account of how the shared grammar grows when a tell emerges in practice. That account is the real subject here.</li> </ul> <h2 id="where-the-rule-lives"><a class="header" href="#where-the-rule-lives">Where the rule lives</a></h2> <p>The naming noun set (<code>FLAG_TERMS</code>) and <code>VOCABULARY.md</code> are host-lint's own. host-lint consumes host-grammar only for the numeral helper and the prose-trope engine. A positional reference is a <strong>naming</strong> tell, so it graduates into host-lint, not host-grammar.</p> <h2 id="decision"><a class="header" href="#decision">Decision</a></h2> <p>Two coupled moves: fix the bug in host-lint, and author the growth doctrine in the spine. The operator practice the doctrine describes is runnable today, without new tooling.</p> <h3 id="the-doctrine-authored-in-host-template"><a class="header" href="#the-doctrine-authored-in-host-template">The doctrine (authored in host-template)</a></h3> <p>The hygiene grammar is a living, shared source that grows by reflective practice:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Two authorities, named distinctly.</strong> A project's local operator validates its <code>LEXICON</code> and decides what is worth proposing. The shared-grammar maintainer validates universality and releases the change. An adopter proposes a candidate upstream rather than editing software it consumes.</li> <li><strong>Discovery is mechanical-first, operator-judged, agent-assisted.</strong> The reliable path is a sweep of history and recent work for recurring shapes the lane misses, triaged by the operator. An agent rarely perceives its own register as a tell, so its reflection is the assist, prompted at the verify gate and at adoption, never the mechanism.</li> <li><strong>The asymmetry that routes a shape.</strong> Legitimacy is local, so it is declared in the per-project <code>LEXICON</code>. A tell recurs across projects and models, so a confirmed tell graduates into the shared grammar the lane enforces: a naming tell into host-lint, a prose trope into host-grammar.</li> <li><strong>The universality test.</strong> The operator asks whether the shape is a property of how models segment work, or of this domain's vocabulary. A candidate that fails the test is reworded, not graduated.</li> <li><strong>Disposition order is never inverted.</strong> Reword into content by default, because a name is almost always available. Box or declare an irreducible citation. Declare the legitimate contextual phrase when a shape is a genuine quantity rather than a position. Reserve a graduation for the residue that recurs once rewording is genuinely impossible.</li> <li><strong>Reflection has a concrete trigger.</strong> It is prompted at the verify gate before a milestone closes, and at adoption.</li> <li><strong>Growth looks forward and has a correction path.</strong> Harvesting proposes what to catch from now on, and does not retro-flag the immutable past, which migration disposes of by renaming live files, boxing frozen records, and path-excluding append-only logs. A grammar bump that newly flags existing live docs follows the disposition order: reword the live ones, box the frozen ones. A graduation that proves to over-flag is narrowed by a later grammar release.</li> </ol> <p>A software <code>call/</code> for harvest tooling is deferred until that tooling is built (see Follow-ups).</p> <h3 id="detection-host-lint"><a class="header" href="#detection-host-lint">Detection (host-lint)</a></h3> <p>A1. Add <code>box</code>, <code>boxes</code>, and <code>steps</code> to <code>FLAG_TERMS</code> and accept a numeric range (<code>N-M</code>) after the noun, in <code>src/lib.rs</code>. Severity stays a flag, like the existing ordinal nouns. The glued hyphen-digit form stays out of scope: a legitimate glued term has no numeral-free <code>LEXICON</code> prefix, so it could not be escaped, and it is the same class as a noun-glued numeral; a hyphenated reference is the minority shape, a documented residual. Verify by: synthetic fixtures for the box/boxes/steps and range shapes all flag. A2. Preserve the boundaries. The literal checklist mark stays clean (it carries no noun-plus-numeral), a content-named reference stays clean, and the <code>box</code> disposition verb stays clean (no trailing numeral). Verify by: the mark, a content reference, and the verb all clean; <code>phase</code>/<code>stage</code>/<code>step</code> behaviour unchanged (existing tests green). A3. <code>VOCABULARY.md</code>: document the shape, its rationale, the literal-mark boundary, the noun-versus-verb note, and the LEXICON resolution for a genuine quantity. Declare the <strong>numeral-free contextual prefix</strong> (the phrase without the number), because the numbered phrase is refused by the flag-tier guard by design. Verify by: host-lint self-lint clean on <code>VOCABULARY.md</code>. A4. Update <code>host-lint.allium</code> and <code>.obligations</code> for the rule; add unit and integration fixtures (synthetic, never adopter-derived). Verify by: <code>cargo test</code>, <code>./test-integration.sh</code>, clippy clean; allium lane green. A5. Gather weak-agent data. Drive Qwen-3.5-4B through the clear cases (a positional reference flags, a literal mark is clean, a genuine quantity is declared by its prefix) and confirm it reaches the correct verdict unaided. A6. Release host-lint through the lifecycle, re-pin <code>.host-software</code> with the re-derived artifact hash, and run <code>software --verify-build</code> and <code>software --check</code>. Verify by: release gate green, tag pushed, both checks clean, CI green.</p> <h3 id="doctrine-host-template-spine"><a class="header" href="#doctrine-host-template-spine">Doctrine (host-template spine)</a></h3> <p>B1. Author the doctrine in <code>CLAUDE.md</code> as the continuation of the Hygiene lane item, prose-clean, with no promise of an unbuilt local-ban surface. Verify by: host-lint prose mode clean on the edit; the existing UPGRADING verify phrases unchanged. B2. Add the <code>UPGRADING.md</code> ledger entry, <code>requires</code> pinned to the Part A host-lint version. Verify by: the entry parses and its verify-grep passes after the edit. B3. Push inside the submodule, bump the pointer, re-record <code>.host</code>, and run the migration so this repo applies its own new doctrine. Verify by: baseline advanced, zero pending; any of this repo's live docs that now flag are reworded or boxed.</p> <h3 id="records-and-close"><a class="header" href="#records-and-close">Records and close</a></h3> <p>C1. Update the <code>PLAN.md</code> row and this doc to reflect what landed; commit and push immediately as audited docs. C2. <code>MEMORY.md</code> entry: the routing fact (a naming tell lives in host-lint), the bypassed-content-name finding, the two-authority model, the verify-gate reflection trigger. Separate commit, pushed. C3. Close host#16 with the before-and-after numbers.</p> <h2 id="scope-boundaries"><a class="header" href="#scope-boundaries">Scope boundaries</a></h2> <ul> <li>Out: a project-local ban surface. Every tell seen so far is universal; building it is speculative.</li> <li>Out: mechanizing the harvest and the verify-gate reflection prompt in the skills. The doctrine is runnable today by the operator's manual sweep and an upstream proposal. Mechanizing it is a named follow-up.</li> <li>Out: host-grammar. The shape is a naming tell, owned by host-lint.</li> <li>Out: the adopter's residue. Their cleanup; immutable commits; never referenced in tracked files here.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-19"><a class="header" href="#verification-19">Verification</a></h2> <p>host-lint flags every synthetic positional shape and stays clean on the literal mark, content names, and the disposition verb; the existing ordinal nouns are unchanged; the weak-agent clear cases classify correctly; <code>software --check</code> and <code>--verify-build</code> are clean; the spine prose mode is clean with the existing verify phrases intact; <code>validate plan/ call/</code> passes; the book builds; a tell-commit is blocked by the hook; all repos are green; host#16 is closed.</p> <h2 id="risks-and-honesty"><a class="header" href="#risks-and-honesty">Risks and honesty</a></h2> <ul> <li>host-lint is a context-free shape matcher. It flags the positional shape; it does not, and cannot, spare an algorithmic phrase of the same shape on its own. The sanctioned escape is a <code>LEXICON</code> declaration of the numeral-free contextual prefix, human-validated, verified to mask the quantity while leaving genuine positional references flagged.</li> <li>That escape is correct but not frictionless for a weak agent, which must notice a blocking flag and declare the prefix rather than the numbered phrase. This is an honest cost of widening the noun set, and the reason the prefix pattern is documented in <code>VOCABULARY.md</code>.</li> <li>The detection move independently fixes the bug; the doctrine is the deliberate spine evolution. They are sequenced software-first, so a stall in the doctrine never blocks the shipped fix.</li> </ul> <h2 id="follow-ups"><a class="header" href="#follow-ups">Follow-ups</a></h2> <ul> <li>Mechanize the harvest and the verify-gate reflection prompt in the skills (a software milestone that would carry the deferred software <code>call/</code>). <strong>Closed by <code>plan/0035</code></strong> (host-lint <code>gather</code> + the verify/adopt reflection step shipped; the deferred software decision is <code>call/0022</code>).</li> <li>A constrained local-ban surface only if a genuinely non-universal tell is found. <strong>Dormant</strong>: none has appeared, so there is no trigger and nothing to build (reaffirmed in <code>plan/0035</code>).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0035-gather-emergent-tells"><a class="header" href="#plan0035-gather-emergent-tells">plan/0035: gather emergent tells</a></h1> <p>Mechanizes the candidate-tell discovery the plan/0034 doctrine defines (the named follow-up).</p> <h2 id="context-9"><a class="header" href="#context-9">Context</a></h2> <p>plan/0034 authored the reflective grammar-growth doctrine: the shared tell corpus is incomplete and grows by reflective practice, with discovery mechanical-first (sweep the history and recent work for a recurring shape the lane does not catch), operator-validated, prompted at the verify gate and at adoption. That sweep is currently run by hand, as it was over a downstream adopter and at the gate. This milestone gives the doctrine a tool rather than only a description.</p> <h2 id="where-it-lives"><a class="header" href="#where-it-lives">Where it lives</a></h2> <p>host-lint owns the gather: it already holds the grammar (<code>FLAG_TERMS</code>) and the legitimacy allowlists (<code>PREV_SKIP</code> for version and figure contexts, <code>UNITS</code> for quantities) that separate a real candidate from noise, and it already dispatches subcommands (<code>lexicon</code>). host-lifecycle owns the <code>verify</code>, <code>adopt</code>, and <code>classify</code> skills, where the reflection prompt is wired.</p> <h2 id="the-gather-subcommand-host-lint"><a class="header" href="#the-gather-subcommand-host-lint">The gather subcommand (host-lint)</a></h2> <p><code>host-lint gather [<paths>]</code> runs <code>git log</code> over the repository and scans the tracked docs and comments itself, one command and parse-free for a weak agent. It extracts a word followed by a numeral, a numeric range, or a glued numeral; drops every word already in <code>FLAG_TERMS</code> (the lane catches it) and every legitimate context the allowlists name; and reports the recurring residue: the candidate word, its count, and example lines, ranked by count. It is advisory and exits zero, so it never gates. A candidate must recur (default at least twice) to surface, so a one-off is not treated as noise.</p> <p>Verify by: a synthetic corpus where a novel recurring word-plus-numeral shape is surfaced, a one-off is not, and a legitimate <code>figure 3</code> or <code>v2.1</code> is not; <code>cargo test</code> and the integration suite green; released through the lifecycle and re-pinned.</p> <h2 id="reflection-wiring-host-lifecycle-skills"><a class="header" href="#reflection-wiring-host-lifecycle-skills">Reflection wiring (host-lifecycle skills)</a></h2> <p>The <code>verify</code> skill gains a step: run <code>host-lint gather</code>, then the operator triages each candidate (propose it upstream, declare it in the <code>LEXICON</code>, or leave it). The <code>adopt</code> skill gains the same at the migration moment, where a project's whole prior history is in view (the richest sweep). The step is advisory; it prompts reflection and does not block the gate.</p> <p>Verify by: the <code>verify</code> and <code>adopt</code> skills name the gather step; a dogfood run of <code>host-lint gather</code> on this repository surfaces a sensible candidate set (the lane already catches our own tells, so the residue is small).</p> <h2 id="the-deferred-decision"><a class="header" href="#the-deferred-decision">The deferred decision</a></h2> <p>The software <code>call/</code> deferred in plan/0034 is written here, scoped to host-lint and host-lifecycle: the gather surfaces candidates mechanically, the operator validates, and the tool never auto-graduates a tell nor auto-bans one. It cites the spine doctrine by revision.</p> <h2 id="scope-boundaries-1"><a class="header" href="#scope-boundaries-1">Scope boundaries</a></h2> <ul> <li>No project-local ban surface (still YAGNI; every tell seen so far is universal).</li> <li>The gather is advisory and never gates; graduation stays a manual upstream proposal, per the doctrine.</li> <li>The gather surfaces; it does not decide. The operator triages.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-20"><a class="header" href="#verification-20">Verification</a></h2> <p>host-lint gather unit and integration fixtures pass; a dogfood run on this repository is sensible; the weak-agent (Qwen-3.5-4B) correctly triages a gather candidate; <code>software --check</code> and <code>--verify-build</code> clean; whole-suite CI green.</p> <h2 id="records-3"><a class="header" href="#records-3">Records</a></h2> <p>PLAN.md row, this doc, a MEMORY entry, and the software <code>call/</code>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="reconcile-internal-contradictions"><a class="header" href="#reconcile-internal-contradictions">Reconcile internal contradictions</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: complete (landed 2026-06-24).</strong> The spine carries the widened doctrine (<code>host-template</code> <code>d5a0034</code>); host-lifecycle <code>v0.24.2</code> (<code>9a1a586</code>) ships the annotation-backed <code>reconcile</code> check, the <code>validate</code> host-template-scope check, and the <code>restates =</code> field, with reconcile wired into the verify recheck and the <code>upgrade</code>/<code>adopt</code>/<code>verify</code> skills; agentic-host adopted the doctrine and reconciled all seven symptoms below through the check; <code>validate</code>/<code>software --check</code>/<code>reconcile</code>/<code>prose</code>/ <code>book --check</code> are green and the whole-suite CI is green. See <code>PLAN.md</code> for the landed detail.</p> <h2 id="context-10"><a class="header" href="#context-10">Context</a></h2> <p>A deep audit found contradictions where the host's own docs restate methodology the spine has moved: the <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> room map, the <code>README.md</code> and <code>CLAUDE.md</code> tool list and verification model, the recorded Where layout. Each staled when a past spine change landed cleanly (specs-to-software in plan/0012, the nested layout in plan/0029, host-prove and the ladder in plan/0023) and nothing re-read the restatement.</p> <p>The contradictions are symptoms of one root cause: migration and upgrade propagate a spine change but never prompt a re-examination of the project's own restatements. Needing a deep manual audit to find this drift is itself the evidence that a reflective practice the methodology should carry is absent. This milestone closes the gap and reconciles the drift.</p> <p>A de-risk review (five lenses plus Qwen-3.5-4B, recorded in <code>design-review.md</code>) reshaped the doctrine: the draft's scope rule was inoperable (4B could not apply an abstract describes-versus-uses test), its blanket cadence was alarm fatigue, and its primary trigger was wrong for a development host. The settled design follows.</p> <h2 id="the-doctrine-the-root-cause-fix-in-the-spine"><a class="header" href="#the-doctrine-the-root-cause-fix-in-the-spine">The doctrine (the root-cause fix, in the spine)</a></h2> <p>Widen the existing "grows by reflective practice" doctrine to one principle: an agent perceives neither the register it emits nor the restatements its own change stales, so both are re-examined on purpose, prompted at the trust boundaries, mechanical-first, and operator-validated. Two arms under it:</p> <ul> <li><strong>gather</strong> (plan/0034, plan/0035): forward, emergent tells in the corpus, a confirmed tell graduates upstream, cadence-driven.</li> <li><strong>reconcile</strong> (new): backward, the project's own restatements of methodology, a confirmed drift fixed locally and never propagated, fired by a specific spine move.</li> </ul> <p>Settled rules:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Prefer pointing over paraphrasing.</strong> An instance doc should point at the spine, not restate it; a restatement that remains is a reconciliation liability reconcile maintains.</li> <li><strong>Scope is machine-checkable and annotation-backed, not a judgment</strong> (the <code>LEXICON</code> and obligations house style): a restatement that must stay carries a declared assertion the tool checks against a source of truth. That is what makes it operable at the weak-agent bar.</li> <li><strong>Trigger is conditional and host-aware.</strong> A new <code>restates =</code> field on the <code>UPGRADING</code> stanza marks a drift-capable entry, and reconcile fires on it, naming which restatement to re-read. For a development host that authors spine changes with no upgrade record, the <strong>verify gate</strong> is the binding trigger: it runs the check when a drift-capable change landed since the last reconcile receipt, and records <code>n-a</code> otherwise. Adoption runs the full reconcile once.</li> <li><strong>Disposition is three-way</strong> (reuse tell-disposition): reword a live restatement, box a frozen citation, forward-correct an immutable record (<code>call/</code>, a <code>Status: done</code> doc, <code>MEMORY.md</code>).</li> <li><strong>A sibling <code>validate</code> check</strong> HAZARDs an <code>accepted</code> <code>call/</code> decision whose <code>Scope:</code> names <code>host-template</code>, closing decision-status drift (the <code>call/0017</code> class) mechanically.</li> </ul> <p>Authority: this is methodology, so it lives in the spine (<code>host-template</code>), never a project <code>call/</code>. The count-versus-stanzas tool check is dropped as noise (the live family disagrees, 5 against 4 against 3); the tool check is a set-diff, and the verification-model check is a positive assertion that every rung-driver is named.</p> <h2 id="build-order"><a class="header" href="#build-order">Build order</a></h2> <ol> <li>Seed the two spine truth data the checks need: an explicit host-* tool-family list and a verification-model datum (the manifest carries neither today).</li> <li>host-lifecycle gains the annotation-backed reconcile check (a Where-root off <code>software/</code>, a spec path asserted under <code>plan/</code>, the host-* family set-diff, a verification-model omission), the <code>restates =</code> read, and the <code>validate</code> decision-scope check; released through the lifecycle and re-pinned.</li> <li>Spine: widen the doctrine and add the <code>UPGRADING</code> entry; wire the reconcile step into the <code>upgrade</code>, <code>adopt</code>, and <code>verify</code> skills (gather stays where it is).</li> <li>agentic-host adopts, then reconciles the symptom drift below as the doctrine's first dogfood run, through the new check rather than by hand.</li> </ol> <h2 id="the-symptom-drift-the-first-dogfood"><a class="header" href="#the-symptom-drift-the-first-dogfood">The symptom drift (the first dogfood)</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Finding</th><th>Evidence</th><th>Disposition</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Root <code>CLAUDE.md</code> contradicts itself and the spine on the verification model (three lanes, <code>host-prove</code> omitted, against the six-rung ladder).</td><td><code>CLAUDE.md:24</code> vs <code>:9</code>/<code>:11</code> and the spine ladder.</td><td>reword live</td></tr> <tr><td><code>STRUCTURE.md</code> is a stale room map: What at <code>plan/<NNNN>/spec/</code>, Where at <code>host-lint/</code>, only host-lint of five components named.</td><td><code>STRUCTURE.md:9</code>/<code>:11</code> vs <code>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</code> and the live <code>software/</code> tree.</td><td>reword live; also clears the orphan <code>plan/0001-foundation/spec/</code></td></tr> <tr><td>Root <code>CLAUDE.md</code> points a spine change at a redirect stub.</td><td><code>CLAUDE.md:26</code> vs <code>host-template/MIGRATION.md</code>.</td><td>reword live</td></tr> <tr><td><code>README.md</code> names only three host-* tools and omits <code>host-prove</code>.</td><td><code>README.md:4</code> vs <code>.host-software</code>.</td><td>reword live</td></tr> <tr><td><code>call/0017</code> authored a now-spine-resident rule yet stays <code>accepted</code>.</td><td><code>call/0017:5</code> (Scope names <code>host-template</code>); rule in <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code>, applied <code>617e420</code>.</td><td><code>Status: superseded by the spine</code>; review <code>call/0018</code>; <code>call/0021</code> clean</td></tr> <tr><td>The <code>host-prove</code> <code>.host-software</code> pin sits one CI-only commit past its <code>v0.2.2</code> tag.</td><td><code>pin = 5e01f58</code> (<code>v0.2.2-1-g5e01f58</code>); tag <code>3ca95fc</code>; the extra commit is <code>ci.yml</code> only.</td><td>re-pin to the tag, or record the rationale</td></tr> <tr><td>Two record-tidiness defects.</td><td>the empty orphan <code>plan/0001-foundation/spec/</code>; PLAN.md's Skill-Hardening box unchecked while <code>SKILL-HARDENING.md</code> is done.</td><td>remove the dir; check the box with the crates.io deferral noted</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Resolved already in the campaign: the prose-hygiene gate the spine asserted but <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> did not implement (plan/0030 D4, host-lifecycle v0.22.0). The session auto-memory staled the same way and is corrected directly as memory hygiene, not tracked here.</p> <h2 id="verification-21"><a class="header" href="#verification-21">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li>The spine carries the widened doctrine; an <code>UPGRADING</code> entry records it; the <code>upgrade</code>/<code>adopt</code>/<code>verify</code> skills prompt reconcile; agentic-host adopts it.</li> <li>The reconcile check flags a planted drift (a Where-root off <code>software/</code>, a missing rung-driver) and stays silent on a clean doc; <code>validate</code> HAZARDs a <code>host-template</code>-scoped <code>accepted</code> decision. A Fen (Qwen-3.5-4B) run reaches the reconcile action on a concrete flag unaided.</li> <li>The symptom drift above reconciles to clean: root <code>CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, <code>README.md</code> match the spine and the live layout; <code>call/0017</code> is superseded; the <code>host-prove</code> pin is at its tag or cited; the orphan dir is gone; the PLAN.md box is checked.</li> <li><code>software --check</code>, <code>validate plan/ call/</code>, the prose gate, and the doc-site build are green; whole-suite green across the affected repos at close.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="design-review-the-migration-reflective-practice-doctrine-2026-06-24"><a class="header" href="#design-review-the-migration-reflective-practice-doctrine-2026-06-24">Design review: the migration reflective-practice doctrine (2026-06-24)</a></h1> <p>De-risk pass before authoring the doctrine into the spine, per the established loop (adversarially review + weak-agent test, then implement). Five independent review lenses over the candidate doctrine plus Qwen-3.5-4B operability data. Verdict: <strong>proceed with major revisions</strong>; the candidate's intent is right and the observed drift is real, but its scope rule, its cadence, and its primary trigger are wrong, and two of its four mechanization shapes are unbuildable as drafted.</p> <h2 id="method-1"><a class="header" href="#method-1">Method</a></h2> <p>Candidate doctrine: a prompted reflection that, after a spine change, re-examines the project's own restatements of methodology for drift and reconciles them, sibling to the plan/0034 grammar reflection. Reviewed through five lenses (scope-boundary operability, prompt cadence, redundancy vs the grammar reflection, mechanization feasibility, effectiveness against the real drift) and tested against Qwen-3.5-4B.</p> <h2 id="qwen-35-4b-data"><a class="header" href="#qwen-35-4b-data">Qwen-3.5-4B data</a></h2> <ul> <li>Pick the in-scope doc: correct (re-check the project's own STRUCTURE.md; skip the upstream spine copy and a persona).</li> <li>Spot a specific drift and reach the reconcile action: correct.</li> <li>Apply the abstract "describes vs uses" scope rule: <strong>inconsistent</strong>. The model treated the STRUCTURE.md room map as in-scope in one prompt and as an out-of-scope "use doc" in another, and garbled the describe-vs-use classification. Conclusion: a weak agent performs the reflection when handed a <strong>concrete</strong> target, but cannot reliably apply the <strong>abstract</strong> scope rule. The scope must be mechanical, not a judgment.</li> </ul> <h2 id="convergent-findings"><a class="header" href="#convergent-findings">Convergent findings</a></h2> <ol> <li> <p><strong>The scope rule is inoperable</strong> (lens 1, lens 4, 4B). "Describes vs uses" is a false dichotomy (most governance docs do both in one line), and "the project paraphrases / the spine owns a copy" is unstable here: the root <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> are simultaneously spine-derived and instance prose, and the host-to-template sole-source is a deliberately deferred seam. Replace the judgment with a machine-checkable set.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The disposition is two-way but the docs need three</strong> (lens 1). "Reconcile in place" collides with the immutable rooms: a <code>call/</code> body, a <code>Status: done</code> milestone doc, and <code>MEMORY.md</code> cannot be edited. Reuse the settled tell-disposition: reword a live doc, box a frozen citation, exclude the append-only record.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Blanket cadence is alarm fatigue</strong> (lens 2). Of 30 ledger entries, only about 6 are drift-capable (they move a room/tool/layout/verification concept a restatement mirrors). A per-upgrade prompt is noise four times in five, which trains the operator to dismiss the prompt on the entry that matters. The trigger must be conditional.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The primary trigger is wrong for a development host</strong> (lens 5). agentic-host authors its spine changes as its own milestones, so <code>upgrade --record</code> never fired for the three structural drifts (plan/0012, plan/0023, plan/0029). The only trigger present at those moments was the <strong>verify gate</strong>. For a development host the verify gate is the binding trigger; the upgrade-record and adoption triggers serve a consuming adopter.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Two mechanization shapes are unbuildable as drafted</strong> (lens 4). The host-* tool count against <code>.host-software</code> is noise (5 stanzas vs the README's 3 vs CLAUDE's 4, all partly legitimate). The "N lanes" phrase has no truth source: the manifest is a phase journal with no rung count. The general restatement-vs-spine diff is an unsolved language problem, not deferred engineering, so the doctrine must not frame it as a follow-up tool.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>It is one principle with the grammar reflection, two arms</strong> (lens 3). The shared root is self-blindness: an agent perceives neither the register it emits nor the restatements its own change stales. Widen the existing doctrine rather than add a parallel one. Keep the arms distinct in mechanics: a tell graduates <strong>upstream</strong> and rides a cadence; a reconcile fix stays <strong>local</strong> and is fired by a specific spine move.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The reconcile arm belongs in the upgrade skill</strong> (lens 3, lens 5), which has no Reflect step today, plus adoption, plus a conditional re-check at the verify gate. Stapling it to the gather cadence in the verify step over-fires it.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A sibling gap: decision-status drift</strong> (lens 5). <code>call/0017</code> left <code>accepted</code> after its rule moved into the spine is not a doc restatement; it is a MADR status drift, governed by anti-ouroboros. Nothing prompts the <code>Status: superseded by the spine</code> transition. A <code>validate</code> check that HAZARDs an <code>accepted</code> decision whose <code>Scope:</code> names <code>host-template</code> closes it mechanically.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Anti-ouroboros grain</strong> (lens 1). A doctrine that institutionalizes keeping paraphrases in sync blesses the duplication the methodology is trying to remove. Invert the default: an instance doc should point at the spine, not paraphrase it; a paraphrase that exists is a reconciliation liability. Reflection is the fallback for the paraphrase that cannot be eliminated.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="the-revised-doctrine-settled-design"><a class="header" href="#the-revised-doctrine-settled-design">The revised doctrine (settled design)</a></h2> <p><strong>One reflective-practice principle, two named arms.</strong> Widen the spine's existing "grows by reflective practice" doctrine so its root is self-blindness in general: an agent perceives neither the register it emits nor the restatements its own change stales, so both are re-examined on purpose, prompted at the trust boundaries, mechanical-first, and operator -validated. Two arms under it:</p> <ul> <li><strong>gather</strong> (unchanged, plan/0034 and plan/0035): forward, emergent tells in the corpus, a confirmed tell graduates upstream, cadence-driven (every verify, adoption).</li> <li><strong>reconcile</strong> (new): backward, the project's own restatements of methodology, a confirmed drift is fixed locally and never propagates, fired by a specific spine move.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Prefer pointing over paraphrasing.</strong> The primary prescription: an instance doc should point at the spine rather than restate it; a restatement that remains is a reconciliation liability the project chooses to carry. Reconcile maintains the unavoidable residue.</p> <p><strong>Scope is a machine-checkable, annotation-backed set, not a judgment.</strong> A restatement that must stay carries a declared assertion the tool checks against a source of truth, the way the <code>LEXICON</code>, the obligations manifest, and <code>.host-software</code> already work. Seed the spine with the two missing truth data first: an explicit host-* tool-family list and a verification-model datum (the manifest has neither today). The checks:</p> <ul> <li>a spec path asserted under <code>plan/</code> (the existing <code>plan_spec_problems</code> covers the file case; add the prose-cell case),</li> <li>a Where-root asserted off <code>software/</code>,</li> <li>a host-* family <strong>set-diff</strong> against the declared family list (catches the README host-prove omission and the STRUCTURE.md "only host-lint of five" completeness drift in one shape; the raw stanza count is dropped as noise),</li> <li>a verification-model paragraph that omits a rung-driver the declared datum names (a positive-assertion check, replacing the unbuildable "N lanes" count). Drop the "general prose diff as a follow-up tool" framing: the annotated set is the whole mechanizable surface, and the residue is a prompted human reflection, not a deferred tool.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Three-way disposition</strong> (reuse tell-disposition): reword a live restatement to match the spine; box a frozen citation; for an immutable record (a <code>call/</code> body, a <code>Status: done</code> doc, <code>MEMORY.md</code>) record a forward-pointing correction rather than edit it.</p> <p><strong>Conditional, host-aware trigger.</strong> Add an optional <code>restates =</code> field to the <code>UPGRADING</code> <code>[upgrade ...]</code> stanza, set by the spine author when an entry moves a mirrorable concept (room map, tool set, Where layout, verification model). Reconcile fires when a recorded upgrade carries a non-empty <code>restates</code>, naming which restatement to re-read. For a <strong>development host</strong> that authors spine changes with no upgrade record, the <strong>verify gate</strong> is the binding trigger: it runs the reconcile check whenever a drift-capable spine change landed since the last reconcile receipt, and records <code>n-a</code> otherwise. Adoption runs the full reconcile once. Wire the reconcile step into the <code>upgrade</code> skill (new Reflect step), the <code>adopt</code> skill, and the <code>verify</code> skill (conditional re-check); keep gather where it is.</p> <p><strong>Sibling validate check.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle validate</code> HAZARDs an <code>accepted</code> <code>call/</code> decision whose <code>Scope:</code> names <code>host-template</code>, prompting the <code>Status: superseded by the spine</code> transition. This closes decision-status drift (<code>call/0017</code>) mechanically, the gap the doctrine itself does not cover.</p> <h2 id="consequence-for-plan0036"><a class="header" href="#consequence-for-plan0036">Consequence for plan/0036</a></h2> <p>The doctrine is a larger build than the candidate: a spine doctrine widening, two new spine truth data (the family list, the verification-model datum), the annotation-backed reconcile check in host-lifecycle, the <code>restates =</code> ledger field, the <code>validate</code> decision-scope check, and skill wiring across <code>upgrade</code>/<code>adopt</code>/<code>verify</code>. The symptom reconciliation (the stale STRUCTURE.md, README, CLAUDE.md, the pin, the tidiness items) then becomes the doctrine's first dogfood run, reconciled through the new check rather than by hand.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="re-home-the-receipts-family-entirely-tool-driven"><a class="header" href="#re-home-the-receipts-family-entirely-tool-driven">Re-home the receipts family, entirely tool-driven</a></h1> <h2 id="context-11"><a class="header" href="#context-11">Context</a></h2> <p><code>plan/0030</code> settled the receipts ontology with the operator but deferred the move to its own milestone, because the shipped binary reads the applied-set only from <code>.host</code> (<code>applied_ids</code>) and the lifecycle receipts only from a single <code>.host-receipts</code>. Moving or splitting those files by hand would silently un-apply every recorded upgrade and HAZARD the embed and release gate, and CI cold-installs a pinned binary that knows only the old layout. So the re-homing must be <strong>100% tool-driven</strong>: a host-lifecycle subcommand performs the move and the split mechanically, the binary auto-migrates on read, and no file is hand-edited. This milestone reuses none of the prose work; it is the deferred follow-up named in <code>plan/0030</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-settled-ontology-with-the-6-of-8-split-resolved"><a class="header" href="#the-settled-ontology-with-the-6-of-8-split-resolved">The settled ontology, with the 6-of-8 split resolved</a></h2> <p>The prior review flagged that two framings (everything host-lifecycle executed, versus a concern-based split) disagree on six of the eight phases. Resolve it by one rule: a receipt lives in <code>.host-receipts</code> only if it is a <strong>methodology-version event</strong>, the act of moving the project to a template revision. <code>adopt</code> sets the baseline and <code>upgrade</code> advances it (carrying the applied-set). Every other phase host-lifecycle runs is <strong>operational</strong>, a thing done to the project or its components, and lives in <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Records</th><th>Written by</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>.host</code></td><td>the stamp: template, adopted revision, name, baseline</td><td>host-lifecycle</td></tr> <tr><td><code>.host-receipts</code></td><td><code>adopt</code> and <code>upgrade</code>, plus the applied-set (which <strong>moves here</strong> from <code>.host</code>): the methodology-version trail</td><td>host-lifecycle</td></tr> <tr><td><code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code></td><td>the operational phases: <code>classify</code>, <code>embed</code>, <code>remap</code>, <code>verify</code>, <code>publish</code>, <code>release</code></td><td>host-lifecycle</td></tr> <tr><td><code>.host-prove-receipts</code></td><td>cut until host-prove emits receipts (no file for an absent consumer)</td><td>none</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The uniform rule stands: <code>.host-<tool>-receipts</code> holds what that tool executed, while the tool-less <code>.host-receipts</code> holds the project's methodology-version trail.</p> <h2 id="100-tool-driven-the-core-requirement"><a class="header" href="#100-tool-driven-the-core-requirement">100% tool-driven, the core requirement</a></h2> <ol> <li> <p><strong>A migration subcommand.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle migrate-receipts <dir></code> performs the whole re-homing mechanically and idempotently: it moves the applied-set out of <code>.host</code> into <code>.host-receipts</code>, splits the operational receipts out of <code>.host-receipts</code> into <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>, and leaves the <code>adopt</code> and <code>upgrade</code> receipts in <code>.host-receipts</code>. It writes atomically, reports what moved, and a second run is a no-op (the project is already on the new layout). The agent runs one command; nothing is hand-edited. Operating the move ad hoc (editing the files) is a defect by construction, the same stance the lifecycle takes on every phase.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Auto-migrate on read (permanent back-compat).</strong> Every read path tolerates <strong>both</strong> layouts: <code>applied_ids</code> reads the legacy <code>applied =</code> lines in <code>.host</code> or the new applied-set in <code>.host-receipts</code>; the receipt gate unions <code>.host-receipts</code> and <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>. So the gate stays green across the boundary, and an adopter that has not yet run <code>migrate-receipts</code> is still read correctly. The old-layout reader is permanent, retired only by a later decision once no supported adopter is on the old side. It mirrors the legacy single-<code>revision</code> <code>.host</code> stamp, which the binary still auto-migrates on read today.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Writes route by the ontology.</strong> After this lands, <code>upgrade --record</code> appends the applied record to <code>.host-receipts</code>, a new operational receipt is appended to <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>, and an <code>adopt</code> or <code>upgrade</code> receipt stays in <code>.host-receipts</code>. A project still on the old layout is migrated by the next <code>migrate-receipts</code>, never by a surprise rewrite mid-command.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="delivery-software-first"><a class="header" href="#delivery-software-first">Delivery (software-first)</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>host-lifecycle</strong> (a feature release): the dual-format reader, the <code>migrate-receipts</code> subcommand, and the ontology-routed writes. Tests: a round-trip (an old-layout fixture migrates to the new layout, with the gate green before and after), an idempotent re-run, and an auto-migrate-on-read of a legacy fixture with no migration run. Released through <code>host-lifecycle release</code>, re-pinned, CI install revs bumped.</li> <li><strong>Spine (host-template)</strong>: update the stamp and receipts description (the applied-set now lives in <code>.host-receipts</code>; the per-tool <code>.host-<tool>-receipts</code> rule), and add an <code>UPGRADING</code> entry whose action is to bump host-lifecycle and run <code>host-lifecycle migrate-receipts .</code>, with a machine-checkable state-check <code>verify</code>.</li> <li><strong>agentic-host</strong>: re-pin host-lifecycle, run <code>migrate-receipts</code> (the tool-driven dogfood, not a hand edit), bump the host-template pointer, record the applied entry, verify, CI green.</li> </ol> <h2 id="verification-22"><a class="header" href="#verification-22">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>migrate-receipts</code> on an old-layout fixture yields the new three-file layout; the receipt gate is green before and after; a second run is a no-op.</li> <li>A legacy-layout fixture (applied-set in <code>.host</code>, a single <code>.host-receipts</code>) is read correctly with no migration run (auto-migrate on read), gate green.</li> <li><code>software --check .</code> on agentic-host is green after the dogfood migration (the gate unions both receipt files; the applied-set is read from <code>.host-receipts</code>).</li> <li>The weak agent (Qwen-3.5-4B) reaches the single <code>migrate-receipts</code> command unaided.</li> <li>Whole-suite green (host-lifecycle CI, agentic-host Site and reproducible-build, the latter cold-installing the dual-format binary and reading the migrated layout).</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-and-honesty-1"><a class="header" href="#risks-and-honesty-1">Risks and honesty</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The dual-format reader ships before the move.</strong> Every read path must tolerate both layouts in the same release that adds <code>migrate-receipts</code>, or the move un-applies the upgrades and HAZARDs the gate. agentic-host migrates only after CI installs that release.</li> <li><strong>CI cold-install.</strong> The reproducible-build and Site jobs install host-lifecycle at the new pin, which carries the dual-format reader, so they read the migrated layout fine.</li> <li><strong>Ongoing, not a shim.</strong> The old-layout reader is permanent backward compatibility, not a one-time migration helper, because copy-at-version lets each adopter cross the boundary at its own pace.</li> <li><strong>Value is organizational.</strong> This is an ontology refinement, not a defect fix; the operator settled it in <code>plan/0030</code> and chose to execute it. It earns its risk by making the receipts model uniform and the applied-set live with the version trail it belongs to.</li> </ul> <h2 id="landed-2026-06-24"><a class="header" href="#landed-2026-06-24">Landed (2026-06-24)</a></h2> <p>Shipped 100% tool-driven in host-lifecycle <strong>v0.23.0</strong> (<code>6e15e01</code>, artifact <code>76be6d9e</code>): the <code>migrate-receipts</code> subcommand, the dual-format reader, and ontology-routed writes; 80 tests, clippy clean. The spine description update is <code>ac32d1c</code> and the <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry is <code>4d2ebe9</code>, adopted in agentic-host (<code>applied=ac32d1c</code>). agentic-host dogfooded the migration through the tool: the applied-set (8 entries) moved into <code>.host-receipts</code>, the 26 operational receipts split into <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>, and adopt and upgrade stayed in <code>.host-receipts</code>. <code>software --check</code> reports 0 HAZARDs on the migrated layout, <code>--verify-build</code> reproduces, and the whole suite is green (host-lifecycle CI main and tag, agentic-host Site and the reproducible-build cold-clone reading the migrated layout). Fen (Qwen-3.5-4B) reached <code>host-lifecycle migrate-receipts .</code> unaided. The verify gate from <code>plan/0030</code> D4 caught an <code>ing-tail</code> trope in this very README during the release, a live demonstration that the gate enforces prose hygiene.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="prose-gate-the-meta-repos"><a class="header" href="#prose-gate-the-meta-repos">Prose-gate the meta repos</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: complete (landed 2026-06-24).</strong> host-template (<code>9268d76</code>) and host (<code>1dc9cb9</code>) are prose-clean and each carries a <code>Prose</code> CI gate pinned to host-lifecycle v0.24.2 (host's is its first CI workflow); both gates are green in CI. The agentic-host pointer and host pin moved in <code>0813795</code>; whole-suite CI is green.
