The one apparent blocker, the <code>harness</code> ai-diction on <code>`kani:<harness>`</code>, was a density artifact (two occurrences crossed the gate; one is clean), cleared by rewording the second occurrence, so no engine change was needed.</p> <h2 id="context-12"><a class="header" href="#context-12">Context</a></h2> <p>plan/0036 stopped the <em>instance</em> docs (this repo's <code>README</code>/<code>CLAUDE</code>/<code>STRUCTURE</code>) drifting from the spine, and the verify gate already runs <code>host-lifecycle prose .</code> over agentic-host's own tracked markdown. But the two repos that <em>author</em> the methodology prose are not gated, so their docs carry slop the spine itself forbids:</p> <ul> <li><strong>host-template</strong> (the spine): 90 prose-trope warnings. plan/0033 cleaned <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, but the rest were never swept: <code>UPGRADING.md</code> 37, <code>cast/</code> 26, <code>README.md</code> 13, the example <code>plan/</code> 7, <code>MIGRATION.md</code> 3, <code>call/0000</code> 3, <code>CLAUDE.md</code> 1.</li> <li><strong>host</strong> (the single-file front-door): one <code>README.md</code>, 29 warnings, and no CI at all.</li> </ul> <p>The spine states "authored docs carry zero prose tropes, as an ongoing rule"; this milestone makes the spine and the front-door obey the rule they publish. It is the same drift root cause as plan/0036, one level up: a rule with no gate on the repo that owns it.</p> <h2 id="approach-1"><a class="header" href="#approach-1">Approach</a></h2> <p><strong>Clean, then gate</strong> (a gate over dirty docs is red on day one). Reword by default, the methodology's standing disposition. One care-point: <code>UPGRADING.md</code>'s <code>verify =</code> and <code>requires =</code> lines are machine-checked, so they stay <strong>byte-for-byte</strong> (the plan/0033 precedent); only surrounding prose is reworded. The <code>cast/</code> personas and example <code>plan/</code>/<code>call/</code> docs are ordinary reword-in-place. This milestone edits the <strong>host</strong> repo, which agentic-host otherwise treats read-only, an accepted boundary crossing for this work.</p> <p>No <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry: an adopted project already runs the prose gate through the verify phase, so adopters inherit nothing new. This brings the meta repos under the existing rule via their own CI; it is not a spine rule change.</p> <h2 id="build-order-1"><a class="header" href="#build-order-1">Build order</a></h2> <ol> <li>Clean <strong>host-template</strong> to zero prose warnings (<code>UPGRADING</code> preserving the machine-checked lines, <code>cast/</code>, <code>README</code>, <code>MIGRATION</code>, <code>CLAUDE</code>, the example <code>plan/</code>/<code>call/</code>), meaning preserved. Verify with <code>host-lifecycle prose host-template</code>.</li> <li>Add a <strong>prose-check CI job</strong> to host-template (install the pinned host-lifecycle, run <code>host-lifecycle prose .</code>, fail on any trope). Commit and push host-template; bump pointer.</li> <li>Clean <strong>host</strong>'s <code>README.md</code> to zero warnings and add host's <strong>first CI workflow</strong> with the same prose gate. Commit and push host; re-pin <code>.host-software</code>.</li> <li>Verify both gates green in CI; agentic-host's own gate stays green; whole-suite green.</li> </ol> <h2 id="verification-23"><a class="header" href="#verification-23">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>host-lifecycle prose host-template</code> and <code>host-lifecycle prose software/host/main</code> both report clean (zero flag and zero warning).</li> <li>The host-template prose CI job and the new host prose CI job both pass.</li> <li>agentic-host <code>software --check</code>, <code>validate</code>, <code>reconcile</code>, <code>prose</code>, and <code>book --check</code> stay green; whole-suite CI green across the affected repos at close.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0039-concepts-as-uris-reconcile-by-pointing-not-annotating"><a class="header" href="#plan0039-concepts-as-uris-reconcile-by-pointing-not-annotating">plan/0039: Concepts as URIs (reconcile by pointing, not annotating)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: designed and validated, not yet built (2026-06-24).</strong> The design is settled; the build is the next milestone of work. The <code>family</code> to <code>components</code> rename and the removal of agentic-host's inline annotations are uncommitted in the working tree, held for the build.</p> <h2 id="context-13"><a class="header" href="#context-13">Context</a></h2> <p>The reconcile arm (plan/0036) guards a project's own restatements of methodology against drift after a spine change, using an inline annotation: a doc line carries <code><!-- host-reconcile: KIND --></code> and the tool checks that line against a single source of truth (the component set, the verifiers, the layout). The operator rejected every inline-annotation form on aesthetic grounds: a comment trailing a sentence, a comment pair wrapping a span, a markdown link carrying the directive, and an out-of-line metadata block. The objection is structural rather than cosmetic: any inline annotation is checker machinery sitting in the prose, and prose that reads clean is the whole point.</p> <p>A replacement was explored and validated. Each methodology concept becomes a URI: one canonical definition at a stable address, and every mention points to it with a plain link rather than restating it. This is the single-source-of-truth principle (DRY, Hunt and Thomas) made concrete, and the reflection-on-action lineage the doctrine already borrows (Schon); the addressing is the first Linked Data principle (Berners-Lee), names for things made dereferenceable. The decision records carry these as outward citations, kind to predecessors and peers; the project holds itself to the same rule with rigor, which is the inward face of the one principle.</p> <h2 id="the-design-refined-b"><a class="header" href="#the-design-refined-b">The design (refined-B)</a></h2> <p>Each concept (the project's <code>components</code>, the <code>verifiers</code>, the <code>software-root</code>, the <code>spec-home</code>) has one canonical definition at a stable <code>{#id}</code> anchor in an authored doc, <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>. Everywhere else points to it with a relative-path link (<code>STRUCTURE.md#components</code>), which renders and resolves under stock mdBook with no custom generator pass. There is <strong>no generated <code>concepts.md</code></strong>: with all four definitions in one doc, a page of links back to them is pure redundancy (see "Refinements this session"). Drift is caught by the coverage check, which holds each project-local home to its full <code>.host-software</code> set; the tool carries the concept vocabulary, so no file enumerates it.</p> <p>reconcile stops scanning inline annotations and runs three checks instead:</p> <ul> <li><strong>link-integrity</strong>: every concept link resolves to a declared concept anchor.</li> <li><strong>declared-anchor</strong>: a link target must be a known concept id, not any resolving fragment, so a link cannot point at the wrong concept and pass.</li> <li><strong>coverage</strong>: every component and verifier the source of truth names must be referenced somewhere, so dropping a tool fails by absence. This restores the bite the inline check had and link-integrity alone loses.</li> </ul> <p>The concept formerly named <code>family</code> is renamed <code>components</code>: the methodology's own word for the set recorded in <code>.host-software</code>. "Family" was an agentic-host overfit, since the host-* tools happen to share a prefix while an adopter's components need not be related.</p> <h2 id="scaling-by-uri-authority"><a class="header" href="#scaling-by-uri-authority">Scaling by URI authority</a></h2> <p>The split the inline mechanism muddled is resolved by who owns each definition. Spine-universal concepts (<code>software-root</code>, <code>spec-home</code>) live at URIs in the spine's namespace, one shared vocabulary every adopter links to. Project concepts (<code>components</code>, <code>verifiers</code>) live in the project's own namespace, sourced from that project's <code>.host-software</code> and wired lanes, never a spine constant. An adopter without a book or <code>.host-software</code> skips the project-scoped checks rather than dangling or silently passing.</p> <h2 id="two-cast-reviews"><a class="header" href="#two-cast-reviews">Two cast reviews</a></h2> <p>The design was reviewed twice through the cast, recorded here for the build.</p> <p>The first reviewed the markdown forms. Verdict: reject every inline form. The published prose must read clean (Mara); one link syntax for three meanings invites confident drift, and a stray bracket breaks it silently so the gate passes falsely (Wren). The pointer link survived as the one place a link reads naturally.</p> <p>The second reviewed the fork (retire inline reconcile for concept-as-URI, or keep it renamed). Verdict: unanimous hybrid. The direction is right, but link-integrity alone is looser than the inline check, because a dropped tool is never linked so nothing catches the absence; hence the coverage and declared-anchor checks are required. The cutover must fail safe: a retired checker hard-fails on a surviving annotation rather than ignoring it silently (Bly). Retiring a mechanism shipped days earlier is its own churn, so the path is deprecate-then-retire (Orin).</p> <h2 id="the-transition-deprecate-then-retire"><a class="header" href="#the-transition-deprecate-then-retire">The transition: deprecate-then-retire</a></h2> <ol> <li>Rename <code>family</code> to <code>components</code> across the binary, its tests, and the spine manifest (done in the working tree, the suite green).</li> <li>Mark inline reconcile deprecated, naming the concept-as-URI successor, and keep it checking under the new name so the bite holds during the transition.</li> <li>Add the concept homes (<code>{#id}</code> anchors) to <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, and build the coverage, declared-anchor, and link-integrity checks.</li> <li>Convert the host's restatements to pointers.</li> <li>Retire the inline mechanism one spine revision later, via an <code>UPGRADING</code> entry that over-reports the owed migration and hard-fails any surviving annotation.</li> </ol> <p>agentic-host accepts running in the gap as the first mover: its inline annotations are already removed, so its restatements are briefly unguarded until the coverage check ships. The operator accepted this as a calculated risk; an adopter is not asked to take it, since the deprecate-then-retire path and the fail-safe cutover protect the adopter.</p> <h2 id="validation-already-in-hand"><a class="header" href="#validation-already-in-hand">Validation already in hand</a></h2> <ul> <li>The concept-as-URI scheme renders and resolves under stock mdBook v0.5.2: the <code>{#id}</code> heading anchors are honored, a relative <code>STRUCTURE.md#id</code> link rewrites to <code>STRUCTURE.html#id</code>, and every link resolves.</li> <li>The real weak agent (Qwen-3.5-4B) authored concept pointer links unaided and correct, three of three, the <code>verifiers</code> route among them, which the inline scheme's classification step had failed. The reason is structural: pointing carries no judgment of whether a span is a restatement, the step that exhausted the model before.</li> <li>The <code>family</code> to <code>components</code> rename builds clean with the whole suite green.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-for-the-build"><a class="header" href="#verification-for-the-build">Verification (for the build)</a></h2> <ul> <li>Each project-local concept's home in <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> names its full <code>.host-software</code> set (coverage), with no generated <code>concepts.md</code>.</li> <li>reconcile flags a dropped component (coverage), a link to an undeclared concept (declared-anchor), and a broken link (link-integrity), and stays silent on a clean set.</li> <li>A surviving inline annotation hard-fails once the mechanism is deprecated, and never silently passes.</li> <li>A weak-agent run reaches the right pointer on a concrete case unaided.</li> <li>An adopter without a book or <code>.host-software</code> skips the project-scoped checks rather than dangling.</li> <li>The host's verify gate (validate, reconcile, prose, book) is green, and the whole-suite CI is green across the affected repos.</li> </ul> <h2 id="refinements-this-session-the-design-as-it-now-stands"><a class="header" href="#refinements-this-session-the-design-as-it-now-stands">Refinements this session (the design as it now stands)</a></h2> <p>Settled in discussion, checked against the cast and the real Qwen-3.5-4B, and kept in plain words for the weak agent (<strong>spine, copy-at-version, point, front-door</strong>):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Project-local facts, enforced.</strong> <code>components</code> and <code>verifiers</code> come from the project's own <code>.host-software</code>, never the spine manifest. The manifest is hardened to <strong>phases only</strong> (<code>manifest --check</code> rejects any other stanza), so an overfit cannot creep back into the shared spine. <code>components</code> are the <code>.host-software</code> members; <code>verifiers</code> are a <code>[verification] drivers</code> stanza (absent means skipped, fail-safe). The cast and a real 4B run backed the move; the 4B's reliable failure is exact-format emission rather than the judgment, so the edit is tool-carried and the prose only points.</li> <li><strong><code>host</code> is the front door, not a component.</strong> Of the members, the four tools (host-lint, host-lifecycle, host-prove, host-grammar) are the <code>components</code>; the single-file <code>host</code> is the <strong>front door</strong>, the methodology's entry point, set apart by <code>front-door = true</code>. This corrects a stale comment that called it "repo-self": agentic-host, the dev environment, is not a member at all and stays invisible to adopters.</li> <li><strong>The principle reaches the front door.</strong> One <strong>spine</strong>; everything else is a <strong>copy-at-version</strong> of it or <strong>points</strong> at it, never a restatement. The front-door <code>host</code> and every adopter are both copies-at-version of the spine, so "an adopter becomes host" is just <em>a copy of the one source</em>. Seeding the front door from the spine, so it cannot drift, is the named next application; the doctrine states the rule here, the build follows.</li> </ul> <h2 id="records-4"><a class="header" href="#records-4">Records</a></h2> <p>This document, a MEMORY entry, and a software <code>call/</code> for the concept-as-URI decision authored at build time. The <code>host-lifecycle next</code> footgun surfaced while allocating this number is filed as connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0040-front-door-from-spine"><a class="header" href="#plan0040-front-door-from-spine">plan/0040: front-door from spine</a></h1> <p>Generate the front-door <code>host</code> repo from the spine, so its restated facts cannot drift. Named as a follow-on in plan/0039 (the front-door principle: one spine, everything else a copy-at-version of it or a pointer, never a restatement), now picked up.</p> <h2 id="problem"><a class="header" href="#problem">Problem</a></h2> <p>The front-door repo (<code>github.com/connollydavid/host</code>) is a single <code>README.md</code>, "the process": the adopt, migrate, and upgrade procedure an agent or a patient human follows to bring a repo under the methodology. About sixty percent of it is the unique procedure (the case a/b/c and mode preview/shallow/staged/deep matrices, the step-by-step, the selection rules). The rest <strong>restates the spine</strong>: the five-rooms table, the <code>.host</code> stamp format, the "Wire the tools" ladder and its pins, the lifecycle-phase list, and the lanes-are-mandatory rule.</p> <p>Those restatements are hand-authored and gated by nothing against <code>host-template</code>, so every spine move (the nested layout in plan/0029, host-prove in plan/0023, concept-as-URI in plan/0039) stales them silently. This is the self-blindness the reconcile arm closes inside a host (plan/0036, plan/0039), but the <code>host</code> repo is its own repo and sits outside any host's verify gate, so reconcile never sees it.</p> <h2 id="decision-operator-this-session"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-this-session">Decision (operator, this session)</a></h2> <p>Realize copy-at-version by <strong>generating</strong> the front-door README from the spine: the spine-derived sections are regenerated from a pinned template revision so they cannot drift, rather than re-authored as independent prose. Two alternatives were weighed and declined:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Gate only</strong>: keep the README hand-authored and add a drift check. It catches drift but leaves the restatements in place, against the stated principle (never a restatement).</li> <li><strong>Point by link</strong>: replace each restatement with a link to the spine's canonical definition (the concept-as-URI move of plan/0039). It breaks the front door's self-containedness, the "point an agent at one file, no checkout" requirement that is the whole reason the front door is a single file.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-design-proposed-for-adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#the-design-proposed-for-adversarial-review">The design (proposed, for adversarial review)</a></h2> <p>The adversarial review superseded the fragment mechanism below; see <code>design-review.md</code> and the "Settled" section. This records what was proposed.</p> <p>The README is assembled from two kinds of section:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Spine-derived</strong> sections (the rooms, the stamp format, the ladder and pins, the phase list, the lanes rule), whose canonical source is the template at a pinned revision.</li> <li><strong>Procedure</strong> sections (the case and mode matrices, the step-by-step, the selection rules), the front door's own content.</li> </ul> <p>A host-lifecycle generator named <code>front-door</code> (a sibling of <code>book</code>) stitches the pinned spine-derived sections and the procedure sections into the committed <code>README.md</code>. A <code>front-door --check</code> regenerates and fails on any drift, the <code>book --check</code> and reproducible-build re-derivation pattern (regenerate from the pin, diff the committed output). The front-door repo records the seed revision in a <code>.host</code>-style stamp, so the copy-at-version anchor is explicit and a later spine move regenerates against the new revision.</p> <p>The spine-derived sections are <strong>audience-adapted</strong> for the adopter-doing-migration reader, not byte-identical to <code>CLAUDE.md</code>. So the template carries a front-door-audience canonical fragment for each shared section, which the generator reads at the pinned revision. The coverage discipline from reconcile carries over: the components and verifiers come from <code>.host-software</code>, so a dropped or added tool flows through without a hand edit.</p> <h2 id="open-decisions-settle-by-review-before-building"><a class="header" href="#open-decisions-settle-by-review-before-building">Open decisions (settle by review before building)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Procedure home.</strong> The procedure sections live canonically in the <code>host</code> repo today, with the template pointing at them (<code>MIGRATION.md</code>). Generation can keep that split (template owns the spine-derived fragments, the host repo owns the procedure fragments, the generator stitches), or move the whole README source into the template. Recommendation: keep the procedure canonical in the host repo; the template owns only the spine-derived fragments. This preserves the <code>MIGRATION.md</code> direction and keeps the procedure with its audience.</li> <li><strong>Section granularity.</strong> Which blocks are spine-derived (regenerated) versus procedure (authored). A first cut: regenerate the rooms table, the <code>.host</code> stamp block, the Wire-the-tools ladder and pins, the lifecycle-phase list, and the lanes-mandatory paragraph; author the rest.</li> <li><strong>Check strictness.</strong> Byte-exact regeneration (the README is fully generated and the check fails on any change, like <code>book --check</code>) versus block-bounded (only the spine-derived blocks are checked for drift, so the procedure prose can be hand-edited between regenerations).</li> <li><strong>Scope.</strong> Keep this agentic-host-local maintenance of the one published <code>host</code> repo, with no adopter obligation and no <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry, since most adopters have no front door (the plan/0038 precedent for meta-repo work). The host-lifecycle <code>front-door</code> capability is generic tooling, exercised only by agentic-host for the published front door.</li> </ul> <h2 id="settled-design-review"><a class="header" href="#settled-design-review">Settled (design review)</a></h2> <p>The two-lens adversarial review (<code>design-review.md</code>) found the fragment mechanism flawed: a hand-authored template fragment is a second source of truth, so <code>front-door --check</code> would prove the README matches the fragment and never that the fragment matches <code>CLAUDE.md</code>. It relocates drift rather than removing it. The four decisions are settled as:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Procedure home.</strong> Keep the split; the host repo owns the procedure (the <code>MIGRATION.md</code> pointer is live and assigns the procedure there).</li> <li><strong>Section granularity.</strong> Split by structured source, not by spine-derived. Coverage-check the phases against <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> and the wired tools against the <code>.host-software</code> <code>[verification]</code> drivers plus the lifecycle engine; generate the <code>.host</code> stamp block from the tool's format. The version pins, the lanes-mandatory rule, and the tool descriptions have no structured home and stay authored. A structured pin home is a named follow-up.</li> <li><strong>Check strictness.</strong> Byte-exact on the generated stamp block, coverage on the structured fact-sets, run on every gate sweep. The procedure prose stays authored, so the front door's teaching quality is preserved.</li> <li><strong>Scope.</strong> agentic-host-local, no <code>UPGRADING</code> entry. The binding check runs as a step in agentic-host's CI (the reproducible-build job), where the spine sources are materialized; it is a separate step, not the shared spine recheck, so no adopter without a front door runs it. The front-door repo keeps its plan/0038 prose gate and cannot run the coverage check itself.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The build sequence as a task graph (plan/0042). Each entry is an anchored task, the chain is linear, and each task carries a receipt in <code>.host-task-receipts</code>.</p> <h3 id="settle-open-decisions"><a class="header" href="#settle-open-decisions">Settle the open decisions by review</a></h3> <p>Settle the open decisions by adversarial review, recorded in a design-review subdoc with a proceed verdict.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="add-front-door-generator"><a class="header" href="#add-front-door-generator">Add the front-door generator</a></h3> <p>Add the <code>front-door</code> and <code>front-door --check</code> subcommands to host-lifecycle: phase coverage against <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>, tool coverage against the <code>.host-software</code> <code>[verification]</code> drivers plus the lifecycle engine, and byte-exact generation of the <code>.host</code> stamp block. No template fragments (the review rejected them as a second source). The unit tests pass.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #settle-open-decisions</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="section-and-regenerate"><a class="header" href="#section-and-regenerate">Bring the front door in line</a></h3> <p>Add the omitted <code>release</code> phase, confirm every wired tool is named, regenerate the <code>.host</code> stamp block, and write the seed stamp, so <code>front-door --check</code> is clean, the README reads unchanged in meaning, and <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> is clean.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #add-front-door-generator</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="wire-the-check"><a class="header" href="#wire-the-check">Wire the front-door check</a></h3> <p>Wire <code>front-door --check</code> as a step in the agentic-host CI (the reproducible-build job), where the spine sources are materialized, so a spine move that stales the front door is caught (a deliberately staled section fails the check). It is a separate step, not the shared spine recheck, so no adopter without a front door runs it. The front-door repo keeps its plan/0038 prose gate; it cannot run the coverage check itself, since it does not carry the sources. The whole-suite CI is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #section-and-regenerate</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <p>Release host-lifecycle, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, and record the receipt and a <code>call/</code> decision. The released binary gates green, and <code>software --check</code> and <code>--verify-build</code> are clean.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #wire-the-check</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks"><a class="header" href="#risks">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The spine-derived sections are audience-adapted, so the template fragments must be written for the migration reader, not transcluded verbatim from <code>CLAUDE.md</code>. Getting the boundary wrong duplicates prose instead of removing it.</li> <li>Generation must preserve the README's teaching quality. It is a document a human or a weak agent follows literally, so a mechanically-stitched README that reads worse is a regression, not a fix.</li> <li>Bootstrap: the generator lives in host-lifecycle, which the methodology materializes, so regenerating the front door depends on a built host-lifecycle at the pinned revision.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-1"><a class="header" href="#status-1">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lifecycle v0.27.0 (2026-06-25; <code>302e87f8</code>, artifact <code>0f63d960</code>). The <code>front-door</code> and <code>front-door --check</code> subcommands hold the single-file front door (the <code>.host-software</code> member marked <code>front-door = true</code>) to the spine's structured facts: coverage of the lifecycle phases (the manifest) and the wired tools (the <code>.host-software</code> verifier drivers plus the lifecycle engine), and byte-exact generation of the <code>.host</code> stamp block. A two-lens adversarial review (design-review.md) rejected the original template-fragment mechanism as a second source of truth, so the design was re-scoped to generate only from structured data; the version pins, the lanes rule, and the tool prose have no structured home and stay authored, with a structured pin home as a named follow-up. The check found and the milestone fixed a live drift (the front door had dropped the <code>release</code> phase). The binding check runs as a step in agentic-host's CI (the reproducible-build job); the front-door repo keeps its plan/0038 prose gate and cannot run the coverage check itself. <code>call/0026</code> records the decision; the build sequence is dogfooded as an anchored receipted task graph (each of the five tasks carries a <code>.host-task-receipts</code> receipt). Whole-suite CI green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0040-design-review-front-door-from-spine"><a class="header" href="#plan0040-design-review-front-door-from-spine">plan/0040 design review: front-door from spine</a></h1> <p>Two independent adversarial reviewers read the milestone, the front-door <code>README.md</code>, the spine (<code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>), and <code>.host-software</code>. One reviewed with a simplicity bias (is this over-engineered?), the other with an integrity bias (does generation actually stop the drift?). They converged on the same blocking finding and the same verdict, so this records the result and settles the four open decisions.</p> <p>The operator ruling that generation realizes copy-at-version stands; the review did not relitigate generate-against-gate. It interrogated the proposed mechanism and the four open decisions, and found the mechanism flawed as written.</p> <h2 id="the-convergent-blocking-finding"><a class="header" href="#the-convergent-blocking-finding">The convergent blocking finding</a></h2> <p>The proposed design carries a front-door-audience canonical fragment for each shared section in the template, and the generator stitches those fragments into the README. A hand-authored fragment in the template is a second source of truth. <code>front-door --check</code> would prove <code>README == regenerate(fragment)</code>, and never prove <code>fragment == CLAUDE.md</code>. A spine edit that misses the fragment passes every check and ships a stale front door. The mechanism relocates the drift from one pair of files to another inside the template; it does not remove it. This is the self-blindness the reconcile arm closes (plan/0036), reintroduced one level up.</p> <p>Both reviewers proved the point with live drift that the design would not catch:</p> <ul> <li>The front-door phase list (<code>README.md</code> line 155) names <code>classify</code>, <code>adopt</code>, <code>embed</code>, <code>remap</code>, <code>verify</code>, <code>publish</code>, <code>upgrade</code> and omits <code>release</code>, which the manifest carries as a phase with its own skill. The restatement is already stale by one concept.</li> <li>The tool-ladder version pins (Rust <code>1.95.0</code>, <code>allium-cli 3.4.2</code>, <code>tla2tools v1.8.0</code>, Temurin <code>21</code>) have no single structured home. Rust lives in <code>.host-software</code> as a per-component digest-pinned container tag (a different image from the front-door's <code>rust:1.95.0</code> prose, with the digest dropped); the other three live only inside component CI workflows in materialized worktrees, which a fresh clone of the template or the front-door repo does not have. There is nothing for a generator to read, so a pin fragment would be a third unstructured copy of values that already disagree.</li> </ul> <p>The shared correction: generate only from the structured data the tooling already reads, and for a fact-set with no structured home, do not pretend a prose fragment makes it drift-proof.</p> <h2 id="the-four-open-decisions-settled"><a class="header" href="#the-four-open-decisions-settled">The four open decisions, settled</a></h2> <h3 id="procedure-home-keep-the-split"><a class="header" href="#procedure-home-keep-the-split">Procedure home: keep the split</a></h3> <p>The template owns the spine-derived material; the front-door repo owns the procedure as its own content. <code>host-template/MIGRATION.md</code> is a live pointer that already assigns the procedure to the <code>host</code> repo, so the split matches the spine. Moving the whole README into the template would drag the case and mode matrices, the front door's genuine unique content, into the spine for no drift-protection gain.</p> <h3 id="section-granularity-split-by-structured-source-not-by-spine-derived"><a class="header" href="#section-granularity-split-by-structured-source-not-by-spine-derived">Section granularity: split by structured source, not by spine-derived</a></h3> <p>A section is drift-proof through the tool only when its fact has a canonical home the tool reads. The split:</p> <ul> <li>The lifecycle phases have a home: <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>. A coverage check holds the front-door to it, so a phase added or removed in the manifest fails by absence. This catches the live <code>release</code> omission.</li> <li>The wired tools have a home: <code>.host-software</code>, the <code>[verification]</code> drivers plus the lifecycle engine. A coverage check holds the front-door to that set, so a dropped or added tool fails by absence (the dropped-tool class plan/0036 found in this same README).</li> <li>The <code>.host</code> stamp format is a fixed format the tool already writes. The generator emits it, so the stamp block cannot be restated wrong.</li> <li>The version pins, the lanes-mandatory rule, and the per-tool descriptions have no structured home, and the lanes rule is a teaching paraphrase rather than a datum. They stay authored. The pins are deliberately the generic versions the methodology targets for an adopter, not this host's internal per-component digests, which is a further reason they do not derive from <code>.host-software</code>. A structured pin home is a named follow-up, not this milestone.</li> </ul> <h3 id="check-strictness-byte-exact-on-the-generated-block-coverage-on-the-fact-sets-run-unconditionally"><a class="header" href="#check-strictness-byte-exact-on-the-generated-block-coverage-on-the-fact-sets-run-unconditionally">Check strictness: byte-exact on the generated block, coverage on the fact-sets, run unconditionally</a></h3> <p>Byte-exact whole-file regeneration would make the entire teaching README a generated artifact, against the milestone's own risk that a mechanically stitched README reads worse. Block-bounded generation that runs only when someone chooses to regenerate reopens the silent staling the milestone set out to close. The resolution takes the safe part of each: the generated stamp block is byte-exact, the structured fact-sets (phases, tools) are coverage-checked, and the whole check runs on every gate sweep so nothing waits on a manual regeneration. The procedure prose stays hand-authored and untouched.</p> <h3 id="scope-agentic-host-local-and-the-bite-lives-in-the-development-host"><a class="header" href="#scope-agentic-host-local-and-the-bite-lives-in-the-development-host">Scope: agentic-host-local, and the bite lives in the development host</a></h3> <p>No adopter obligation and no <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry: most adopters have no front door, and the plan/0038 precedent for meta-repo work applies. The check needs the spine sources (the manifest and <code>.host-software</code>), which live in agentic-host, not in the front-door repo. So the binding check runs in agentic-host's CI (the reproducible-build job), where the front-door is a materialized component and the sources are present. It is a separate CI step rather than the shared spine recheck, so no adopter without a front door runs it and no <code>UPGRADING</code> entry is owed. The front-door repo keeps the prose gate it gained in plan/0038; it cannot run the coverage check itself, because it does not carry the sources, and that asymmetry is recorded rather than papered over. A <code>call/</code> decision records the capability.</p> <h2 id="the-re-scoped-design"><a class="header" href="#the-re-scoped-design">The re-scoped design</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle front-door <dir></code> and <code>front-door --check <dir></code>, a sibling of <code>reconcile</code>:</p> <ul> <li>Coverage of the phases against <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>, and of the wired tools against the <code>.host-software</code> <code>[verification]</code> drivers plus the lifecycle engine.</li> <li>Generation of the <code>.host</code> stamp block from the tool's canonical format, checked byte-exact.</li> <li>A clear report of any missing phase or tool and any stamp drift, exiting non-zero so the gate is red until the front-door is brought back in line.</li> </ul> <p>The pins, the lanes rule, and the tool descriptions stay authored, and the milestone says so plainly rather than claiming a drift-proofing it cannot deliver.</p> <h2 id="verdict"><a class="header" href="#verdict">Verdict</a></h2> <p>Proceed with changes. The generation surface narrows to the stamp block; the phases and tools move from prose fragments to coverage against their real homes; the pins are de-scoped to authored with a pin-home follow-up; and the binding check runs as a step in agentic-host's CI. The milestone then delivers its stated goal for every fact that has a home, and is honest about the facts that do not.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0041-next-fails-closed"><a class="header" href="#plan0041-next-fails-closed">plan/0041: next fails closed</a></h1> <p>Make <code>host-lifecycle next <dir></code> fail closed when it is pointed at a directory with no numbered entries, instead of silently yielding <code>0000</code>. Closes connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1, the footgun surfaced during plan/0039.</p> <h2 id="problem-1"><a class="header" href="#problem-1">Problem</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle next <dir></code> prints the next free <code>NNNN-slug</code> number as the maximum of the directory's numbered entries plus one, and falls back to <code>0000</code> when there are no numbered entries. So <code>next .</code> (the host root), a typo'd path, or any non-room path silently yields a valid-looking <code>0000</code>, and an agent can go on to create a colliding <code>0000-slug</code> in the wrong place. The repro is exact:</p> <pre><code>host-lifecycle next plan -> 0040 # correct host-lifecycle next call -> 0024 # correct host-lifecycle next . -> 0000 # the host root has no numbered entries </code></pre> <p>At the weak-agent bar this is fail-unsafe: a garbled argument returns a plausible wrong answer rather than an error.</p> <h2 id="decision-operator-this-session-1"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-this-session-1">Decision (operator, this session)</a></h2> <p><code>next</code> <strong>fails closed</strong>. A directory with no <code>NNNN-slug</code> entries (the host root, a typo, a non-room path, or a freshly-scaffolded empty room) exits non-zero rather than printing <code>0000</code>. The fresh-empty-room case is folded into fail-closed rather than special-cased, because rooms gain a first entry quickly (the worked-example <code>call/0000</code>, the first milestone) and fail-safe beats fail-unsafe.</p> <p>The exact failure form (a usage message versus a distinct error message, the exit code, and whether a did-you-mean hint helps) is settled by a <strong>Qwen-3.5-4B ergonomics check</strong>: the form the weak agent recovers from correctly (re-points at a real room, or recognizes the first-entry case and proceeds with an explicit number) is the one shipped. If the data shows the empty-room path needs a hand, an explicit affordance is added then, not pre-emptively.</p> <h2 id="the-change-host-lifecycle"><a class="header" href="#the-change-host-lifecycle">The change (host-lifecycle)</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>next</code> distinguishes a missing or non-directory path from an existing directory with no numbered entries, and exits non-zero in both, with a message that names the likely fix (point at a room such as <code>plan/</code> or <code>call/</code>). The precise wording and exit code follow the 4B check.</li> <li>A unit test covers: a populated room returns the maximum plus one (unchanged); an empty existing directory exits non-zero; a missing path exits non-zero; the host root exits non-zero.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-1"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-1">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The build sequence as a task graph (plan/0042): each entry is an anchored task. The chain is linear, and each task carries a receipt in <code>.host-task-receipts</code>.</p> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">Gather the failure-form data</a></h3> <p>Show the 4B the footgun and the candidate failure forms (usage to stderr with a non-zero exit, a distinct error message, with and without the did-you-mean hint), and record which form it recovers from. The recorded data note names the chosen form.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-fail-closed"><a class="header" href="#implement-fail-closed">Implement the fail-closed next</a></h3> <p>Implement the fail-closed <code>next</code> with the chosen form and the unit test, so <code>next .</code> exits non-zero while <code>next plan</code> still prints the correct next number.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="record-the-call-decision"><a class="header" href="#record-the-call-decision">Record the call decision</a></h3> <p>Record a small <code>call/</code> decision (fail-closed <code>next</code>, the 4B-validated form).</p> <ul> <li>depends: #implement-fail-closed</li> <li>verify: host-lifecycle validate call/</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <p>Release host-lifecycle (<code>--change-class neither</code>, a patch bump), re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the receipt, and bump the CI install pins. The released binary gates green, <code>software --check</code> and <code>--verify-build</code> are clean, and the whole-suite CI is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #record-the-call-decision</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="close-the-issue"><a class="header" href="#close-the-issue">Close the issue</a></h3> <p>Close connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 with the release reference.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #release-and-re-pin</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-1"><a class="header" href="#risks-1">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>A freshly-scaffolded empty room now errors. If that path is more common than assumed, the 4B data surfaces it and an explicit affordance (a clear create-the-first-entry message, or a <code>--first</code> flag) is added. The blast radius is low: the change is localized to the <code>next</code> function.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-2"><a class="header" href="#status-2">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lifecycle v0.26.1 (2026-06-25; <code>2f606e29</code>, artifact <code>adf5c10a</code>). <code>next</code> fails closed: a non-directory or a directory with no <code>NNNN-slug</code> entries exits non-zero (code <code>2</code>) with a diagnostic and a did-you-mean drawn from the known rooms, instead of the silent <code>0000</code> fallback that returned a plausible wrong number for a typo'd or non-room path. The fresh-empty-room case folds into fail-closed with no special flag. The form was settled by a Qwen-3.5-4B (Fen) ergonomics check (gather-data.md): the weak agent recovered the intended room from the diagnostic and recognized the empty room as a first-entry case. <code>call/0025</code> records the decision; a unit test covers a populated room (unchanged), an empty directory, a missing path, and the host root. Re-pinned, release receipt recorded, CI install pins bumped; <code>software --check</code> and <code>--verify-build</code> green; connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 closed. The build sequence is dogfooded as an anchored receipted task graph (each of the five tasks carries a <code>.host-task-receipts</code> receipt).</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0041-gather-the-next-failure-form-set-by-qwen-35-4b"><a class="header" href="#plan0041-gather-the-next-failure-form-set-by-qwen-35-4b">plan/0041 gather: the next failure form, set by Qwen-3.5-4B</a></h1> <p>The fail-closed <code>next</code> error form is the one a weak agent recovers from. A recorded Qwen-3.5-4B (Fen) run settled it, the bar the methodology applies to ergonomics.</p> <h2 id="how-the-run-was-reached"><a class="header" href="#how-the-run-was-reached">How the run was reached</a></h2> <p>The rope HTTPS front-end rejected the host-only bearer (the token had rotated), so the run went through the pal front-end to the same <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> backend. pal frames a scenario as user content rather than a true system message, a weaker framing than rope. The result held on a clean re-run, so the weaker framing did not change it.</p> <h2 id="what-fen-was-shown"><a class="header" href="#what-fen-was-shown">What Fen was shown</a></h2> <p>Two recovery scenarios. The first ran <code>next .</code> (the repository root) meaning to run <code>next plan</code>, and saw each candidate form:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">Form A — terse usage, exit 2, stderr: host-lifecycle next <dir> Form B — diagnostic error, exit 1, stderr: host-lifecycle: '.' has no numbered (NNNN-slug) entries; point `next` at a room such as plan/ or call/ Form C — diagnostic error and a suggestion, exit 1, stderr: host-lifecycle: '.' has no numbered (NNNN-slug) entries did you mean a room? try: host-lifecycle next plan </code></pre> <p>The second ran <code>next call</code> against a freshly created, empty <code>call/</code> room, to test whether the error blocks an agent on a genuine first entry.</p> <h2 id="what-fen-did"><a class="header" href="#what-fen-did">What Fen did</a></h2> <p>For the wrong-path scenario, Fen produced the correct recovery command for every form. It judged the form with a suggestion line the most reliable, because the line carries the exact command and removes the step of constructing it; the terse usage form was the weakest. The exit value did not gate recovery: Fen recovered at every code shown, and its stated preference for a <code>1</code> rested on reading a <code>2</code> as non-standard, which a usage error does not warrant.</p> <p>For the empty-room scenario, Fen recognized <code>call/</code> as the intended room and the case as its first entry, and named the first filename <code>call/0000-...</code> rather than treating the empty room as a dead end. So the fresh-empty-room case needs no special affordance.</p> <h2 id="the-chosen-form"><a class="header" href="#the-chosen-form">The chosen form</a></h2> <p>A distinct diagnostic error that names the likely fix and carries a did-you-mean line with an exact command:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">host-lifecycle: '.' has no numbered (NNNN-slug) entries did you mean a room? try: host-lifecycle next plan </code></pre> <p>It exits non-zero with <code>2</code>, the code the tool already returns for its sibling path and argument errors (a missing argument, a non-directory), so one convention holds across the tool. The empty-room path stays folded into fail-closed, with no <code>--first</code> flag, because the agent recovers from it unaided.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0042-receipted-task-graph"><a class="header" href="#plan0042-receipted-task-graph">plan/0042: receipted task graph</a></h1> <p>The numbered tasks inside a milestone become first-class: each is an anchored node with a stable identity, each emits a receipt when discharged, and a prerequisite edge (within a milestone or across milestones) turns the project's build sequences into one schedulable graph a coordinator can fan out to parallel sub-agents. Adopter-facing and mandatory. The design was settled by operator ruling after a five-lens adversarial review (see design-review.md).</p> <h2 id="problem-2"><a class="header" href="#problem-2">Problem</a></h2> <p>A milestone's <code>Build sequence</code> is a numbered prose list, where each step pairs an action with a verification check. Three gaps:</p> <ul> <li><strong>No receipt.</strong> Each lifecycle phase emits a receipt (done with re-derivable evidence, skip with a cited reason, HAZARD if missing), so a phase claim is audited. The in-plan tasks have no such discipline: a step marked done in prose is an unverifiable claim, the same defect the phase receipts close, one level down.</li> <li><strong>A task has no stable identity.</strong> A position renumbers when a plan is re-cut, so neither a receipt nor a dependency edge can key on it. A receipt that points at "step three" breaks the moment a step is inserted above it. The fix is a content-named anchor, the stable URI a receipt and an edge hang on.</li> <li><strong>The sequence is implicitly serial.</strong> A prose list cannot say which steps are independent or which depend on a task in another milestone. An arbitrary-complexity project (the methodology's real audience, not this repo's own linear history) has genuinely independent and cross-milestone tasks, and the list cannot express the graph a coordinator would schedule.</li> </ul> <p>A separate matter is the bare <code>#N</code> GitHub issue reference, which is a fragment rather than a full URL. It is real and out of scope here: a future plan will enforce full URLs for <code>#N</code> references. plan/0042's task references already use a full relative-path anchor (<code>plan/NNNN/README.md#anchor</code>), so this milestone does not depend on that future one.</p> <h2 id="decision-operator-this-session-after-the-adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-this-session-after-the-adversarial-review">Decision (operator, this session, after the adversarial review)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Anchored task nodes, for stable identity.</strong> A task is a <code>### </code> step-heading under the <code>## Build sequence</code> section whose anchor sits at the heading end (<code>### Gather data {#gather-data}</code>, the placement stock mdBook honors). A <code>### </code> heading elsewhere is ordinary prose; the parser rejects an anchored task outside the build-sequence section and a build-sequence task heading without an anchor. References use the plan/0039 anchored form (<code>[text](plan/NNNN/README.md#anchor)</code>).</li> <li><strong>A receipt per task, in a new <code>.host-task-receipts</code> ledger.</strong> Tool-written, keyed by <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code>, never a hand-edited inline status. This is a deliberate third receipt kind beside the plan/0037 two-file ontology, recorded in a <code>call/</code> decision and a short ontology note; the review flagged the ontology cost and the operator accepted it for the physical separation.</li> <li><strong>A project-wide dependency graph, built now.</strong> A task may declare <code>depends</code>, a local <code>#anchor</code> or a cross-milestone <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code>. A task with no <code>depends</code> depends on the previous task, so the default is linear. The tool resolves the edges into one project-wide graph and derives the ready frontier (the tasks whose <code>depends</code> all carry a done receipt); a coordinator may dispatch the frontier to parallel sub-agents. Built as forward infrastructure for arbitrary-complexity adopters, not gated on this repo's own linear milestones.</li> <li><strong>Adopter-facing and mandatory.</strong> The spine carries the task model and an <code>UPGRADING</code> entry; the receipt-per-task gate is a hard rule, the strongest discipline. agentic-host implements the capability and migrates its own plans (plan/0040 and plan/0041) as the dogfood.</li> </ul> <h3 id="the-authoring-rule-and-why-it-holds-at-the-weak-agent-bar"><a class="header" href="#the-authoring-rule-and-why-it-holds-at-the-weak-agent-bar">The authoring rule, and why it holds at the weak-agent bar</a></h3> <p>The dependency graph was gated on a Qwen-3.5-4B investigation and passed: six of six on within-milestone authoring and reading (including the serialize-when-unsure instinct), and four of four on cross-milestone references (read a <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code> dependency, and author a mixed local-plus-cross-plan <code>depends</code> from a menu). A free-form probe confirmed the danger boundary: asked to find what can run in parallel, the 4B invents false independence to increase parallelism, which races two sub-agents, while a missing edge only over-serializes. So the rule is: <strong>an author declares each task's prerequisites (what must finish before it), and the tool derives parallelism.</strong> The prerequisite question is local and conservative; the parallelism is the tool's to compute.</p> <h2 id="the-design-settled-the-reviews-fixes-folded-in"><a class="header" href="#the-design-settled-the-reviews-fixes-folded-in">The design (settled, the review's fixes folded in)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>One global graph.</strong> Because an anchor is a project-wide URI and the ledger is keyed globally, the graph spans milestones. Cycle detection and the dangling-dependency check run over the whole resolved edge set, not one milestone, so a cross-plan cycle or a <code>depends</code> on a removed cross-plan anchor is a HAZARD.</li> <li><strong>Per-task gating, not per-milestone-complete.</strong> The review found that a milestone's completeness is prose with no structured referent. So the gate fires per task: a declared anchored task with no receipt is a HAZARD, exactly as the receipt gate already HAZARDs a manifest phase with no receipt. There is no new milestone-status surface.</li> <li><strong>The verify field, mechanical or attested.</strong> A task's check is a first-class field, either mechanical (a command the gate re-runs) or attested (an operator confirmation or a <code>call/NNNN</code> citation the gate resolves). A mechanical <code>done</code> with no command is a HAZARD; an attested <code>done</code> is discharged by the citation resolving, which is weaker than re-derivation and labeled as such. The command runs through a guarded runner (no recursion into the gate, a decided cross-platform path), which reuses the existing recheck mechanism rather than a new grammar.</li> <li><strong>Staleness, both halves of call/0018.</strong> A task records the input set its verify covers; <code>--record-digests</code> fingerprints them into the ledger, and a later offline run raises a STALE HAZARD if those inputs drift without a fresh re-derivation, with full re-derivation in the verify lane. This is the obligations digest mechanism applied to task receipts, the half the first draft dropped.</li> <li><strong>A separate task-anchor link checker.</strong> Resolving a <code>[text](plan/NNNN/README.md#anchor)</code> reference is a new checker, path-shape gated, in a namespace disjoint from the reconcile concept ids (a task heading must never shadow a concept home). Only link-integrity transfers; the declared-anchor and coverage bites do not apply to an open per-milestone anchor set. The parser also enforces the heading-end placement directly, so a misplaced anchor is caught before it can 404.</li> <li><strong>Skip is cited, drift is caught.</strong> A substantive <code>skip</code> carries a resolvable <code>call/NNNN</code> citation (parity with call/0017); the gate is non-omission assurance for declared work, not a completeness proof, and the doctrine says so. A reverse check holds every ledger key to a live anchor, so a renamed or removed task cannot leave a stale done behind.</li> <li><strong>Two task systems, one of record.</strong> The durable ledger is the audit record the tool writes after re-derivation; the agent's own ephemeral session task list is scratch scheduling and is never the source of a <code>done</code>.</li> <li><strong>Resource isolation is the parallel-dispatch precondition.</strong> A <code>depends</code> is an ordering constraint, not a mutual-exclusion lock, so a coordinator fans a frontier out to parallel sub-agents only when they are resource-isolated (separate worktrees); two tasks with disjoint prerequisites that write the same file are not safe to parallelize, and the doctrine states the assumption.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-2"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-2">Build sequence</a></h2> <ol> <li>Record the <code>call/</code> decision for the third receipt ledger and the ontology note, and settle the <code>depends</code> syntax (a host-lint-clean grammar, the first-task base case, the insertion semantics of the linear default). Verify: <code>validate call/</code> ok; the syntax is lint-clean by <code>host-lint --all</code>.</li> <li>Implement in host-lifecycle: parse the anchored tasks and <code>depends</code> (with the heading disambiguation and the end-placement check), build and validate the global graph (cross-plan resolution, cycle detection, dangling-dependency HAZARD), the <code>.host-task-receipts</code> ledger with input-digest staleness, the per-task gate, the verify-field runner, the status read, and the task-anchor link checker. Verify: unit tests, and a synthetic fixture that exercises a cross-milestone diamond and a broken reference.</li> <li>Add the spine doctrine (the anchored receipted task model, the prerequisite-not-parallelism rule, the resource-isolation precondition, the mandatory gate) and an <code>UPGRADING</code> entry. Verify: host-template prose clean; the entry's verify post-condition holds.</li> <li>Validate the full task form at the weak-agent bar (author a task with an anchor, a verify field, a local and a cross-plan <code>depends</code>, and its receipt). Verify: a recorded Qwen-3.5-4B run authors them correctly.</li> <li>Migrate agentic-host: re-express plan/0040 and plan/0041 as anchored receipted tasks and back-fill their receipts through the tool. Verify: <code>validate plan/</code>, the per-task gate, and the link checker clean; the two milestones read unchanged in meaning.</li> <li>Release host-lifecycle, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the receipt and the <code>call/</code> decision, and bump the CI install pins. Verify: the released binary gates green; <code>software --check</code>, <code>--verify-build</code>, and the whole-suite CI green.</li> </ol> <h2 id="risks-2"><a class="header" href="#risks-2">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The mandatory per-task gate raises the bar for every adopter, so the line between a task worth a receipt and a trivial step must stay crisp (an anchored <code>### </code> under <code>## Build sequence</code> is a task, a trivial step's receipt is a cheap attested or skip entry) or the gate becomes ritual.</li> <li>The global graph spans milestones, so a cross-plan edge couples two milestones' lifecycles; the dangling-dependency check must run on every gate so a re-cut in one milestone cannot silently wedge another.</li> <li>Author-written verify commands run during the gate, so the guarded runner and the no-recursion rule are load-bearing for safety.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-3"><a class="header" href="#status-3">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lifecycle v0.26.0 (2026-06-25). The <code>tasks</code> subcommand, the <code>.host-task-receipts</code> ledger (call/0024), the completion-aware per-task gate in <code>software --check</code>, the task-anchor link checker, and the <code>tasks --new</code> scaffolding shipped; the spine doctrine is in host-template (<code>2229dbb</code>) and adopted. plan/0040 and plan/0041 are dogfooded (their build sequences re-expressed as anchored task graphs). Whole-suite CI green across all three repos.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0042-design-review"><a class="header" href="#plan0042-design-review">plan/0042 design review</a></h1> <p>Five independent adversarial lenses ran against the plan: methodology coherence, weak-agent followability, mechanism soundness, simplicity, and failure modes. Verdicts: three re-scope, two proceed-with-revisions. Net: re-scope to a minimal evidenced core, defer the speculative machinery until a consumer exists, and close several soundness holes before building.</p> <h2 id="verdicts-by-lens"><a class="header" href="#verdicts-by-lens">Verdicts by lens</a></h2> <ul> <li>Methodology coherence: re-scope</li> <li>Weak-agent followability: proceed-with-revisions</li> <li>Mechanism soundness: proceed-with-revisions</li> <li>Simplicity and YAGNI: re-scope</li> <li>Failure modes: re-scope</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-the-lenses-converged-on-highest-confidence"><a class="header" href="#what-the-lenses-converged-on-highest-confidence">What the lenses converged on (highest confidence)</a></h2> <h3 id="the-n-collision-premise-is-not-in-the-corpus"><a class="header" href="#the-n-collision-premise-is-not-in-the-corpus">The <code>#N</code>-collision premise is not in the corpus</a></h3> <p>(failure-modes, simplicity, followability) A grep of every plan, PLAN.md, <code>call/</code>, and MEMORY.md found that every <code>#N</code> is a GitHub issue reference; no plan references another's build step by number. The "name the milestone, not the step" convention already prevents the collision, and host-lint does not gate an intra-doc step number. So anchoring a task to remove the <code>#N</code> collision solves a hypothetical. The evidenced need is the receipt, an auditable record of task completion.</p> <h3 id="the-optional-graph-has-no-consumer"><a class="header" href="#the-optional-graph-has-no-consumer">The optional graph has no consumer</a></h3> <p>(simplicity, failure-modes, coherence) No milestone in the project's history has carried independent tasks, and both named consumers (plan/0040, plan/0041) are linear. The Qwen-3.5-4B investigation proved the graph is safe to author, which is not the same as needed. The graph is inert until declared, so deferring it costs nothing, and re-adding it is a one-field addition to an already-anchored node when a real parallel milestone exists.</p> <h3 id="the-third-receipt-file-breaks-the-plan0037-ontology"><a class="header" href="#the-third-receipt-file-breaks-the-plan0037-ontology">The third receipt file breaks the plan/0037 ontology</a></h3> <p>(coherence, mechanism, simplicity) plan/0037 partitions receipts by one rule: a methodology-version event lives in <code>.host-receipts</code>, everything host-lifecycle executes lives in <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>. A task receipt is host-lifecycle executing a discharge, so it is operational by that rule and belongs in the operational ledger, distinguished by a key shape (<code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code>), not a third top-level file. The operator requirement (tool-written, never a hand-edited inline status) is met by the operational ledger keyspace.</p> <h3 id="the-completion-trigger-is-unbuildable-as-written"><a class="header" href="#the-completion-trigger-is-unbuildable-as-written">The completion trigger is unbuildable as written</a></h3> <p>(mechanism, the crux risk; coherence; failure-modes) The gate fires on "a milestone marked complete", but a milestone's status is prose with no structured referent the tool reads. The fix every mechanism reviewer reached: drop the per-milestone predicate. Gate per task, where a declared anchored task with no receipt is a HAZARD exactly as the existing receipt gate HAZARDs a manifest phase with no receipt; or fire on the verify or release act and let the absence of a clean run be the not-complete signal.</p> <h3 id="link-integrity-over-task-anchors-is-a-new-subsystem-not-an-extension"><a class="header" href="#link-integrity-over-task-anchors-is-a-new-subsystem-not-an-extension">Link-integrity over task anchors is a new subsystem, not an extension</a></h3> <p>(coherence, mechanism, simplicity, failure-modes) reconcile is built on a closed four-concept vocabulary (<code>CONCEPT_IDS</code>) with one-home and coverage semantics. Task anchors are open-ended, per-milestone, and multi-home. So it needs a separate checker, path-shape gated on <code>plan/NNNN/README.md#anchor</code>, in a namespace disjoint from the concept ids (or a task heading <code>{#components}</code> shadows the concept home), and only link-integrity transfers; the declared-anchor and coverage bites do not.</p> <h2 id="soundness-holes-to-close-before-building"><a class="header" href="#soundness-holes-to-close-before-building">Soundness holes to close before building</a></h2> <h3 id="staleness-takes-only-half-of-call0018-the-single-worst-failure"><a class="header" href="#staleness-takes-only-half-of-call0018-the-single-worst-failure">Staleness takes only half of call/0018 (the single worst failure)</a></h3> <p>(failure-modes) call/0018 is re-derivation plus input-digest staleness. The plan records the command to re-run but not the inputs the receipt covers, so a <code>done</code> receipt goes stale silently, or the gate re-runs every command on every check, which is too expensive and so gets skipped in practice. Either way a milestone ships a <code>done</code> that no longer holds, the unverifiable-claim defect one level down, now wearing an audited badge. Fix: adopt the obligations digest-ledger that the project already ships (record per-task input digests, raise a cheap offline drift HAZARD, re-derive in the verify lane).</p> <h3 id="task-heading-versus-prose-heading-is-undefined"><a class="header" href="#task-heading-versus-prose-heading-is-undefined">Task heading versus prose heading is undefined</a></h3> <p>(followability, the blocking finding; coherence) The <code>### </code> level is already the ordinary subsection across the corpus, including this plan's own <code>### The graph passes the weak-agent bar</code> heading. The tool cannot tell a task from a prose heading, and neither can the weak agent. Fix: a task is a <code>### </code> heading that carries an anchor under the one <code>## Build sequence</code> section; a <code>### </code> elsewhere is prose; the parser rejects the ambiguous forms.</p> <h3 id="the-verify-fields-attested-branch-cannot-re-derive-and-a-mechanical-one-is-arbitrary-code"><a class="header" href="#the-verify-fields-attested-branch-cannot-re-derive-and-a-mechanical-one-is-arbitrary-code">The verify field's attested branch cannot re-derive, and a mechanical one is arbitrary code</a></h3> <p>(mechanism, followability) "A done re-derives its verify" is false for an attested verify, which has nothing to run; define attested discharge as cite-resolution, weaker than the re-derivation the plan claims. A mechanical verify is author prose run as a shell command on every check, so guard it (the recursion and the POSIX-only path are real), and make a mechanical <code>done</code> with no command a HAZARD.</p> <h3 id="skip-to-green-and-under-writing"><a class="header" href="#skip-to-green-and-under-writing">Skip-to-green and under-writing</a></h3> <p>(failure-modes, followability) A task marked <code>skip</code> clears the gate, and the gate counts only declared tasks, so under-writing the hard tasks games it. Fix: a substantive skip carries a resolvable <code>call/NNNN</code> citation (parity with call/0017), and the doctrine states plainly that the gate is non-omission assurance for declared work, not a completeness proof.</p> <h3 id="ledger-drift-and-orphan-receipts"><a class="header" href="#ledger-drift-and-orphan-receipts">Ledger drift and orphan receipts</a></h3> <p>(mechanism, failure-modes) A renamed or deleted anchor orphans its receipt, and a renamed task re-does work while the old receipt lingers claiming done. Fix: a reverse check, where every ledger key resolves to a live anchor, mirroring the existing obligations stale-id rule.</p> <h3 id="two-task-systems"><a class="header" href="#two-task-systems">Two task systems</a></h3> <p>(failure-modes) The agent harness has its own ephemeral task list. State the relationship: the durable ledger is the audit record the tool writes after re-derivation; the harness list is scratch and never the source of a <code>done</code>.</p> <h3 id="resource-exclusion-if-the-graph-stays"><a class="header" href="#resource-exclusion-if-the-graph-stays">Resource exclusion, if the graph stays</a></h3> <p>(failure-modes) A <code>depends</code> models ordering, not mutual exclusion, so two tasks with disjoint prerequisites can still race on a shared file. Parallel dispatch is safe only when sub-agents are resource-isolated (separate worktrees); state the assumption.</p> <h3 id="anchor-end-placement-has-no-pre-ship-catch"><a class="header" href="#anchor-end-placement-has-no-pre-ship-catch">Anchor-end placement has no pre-ship catch</a></h3> <p>(followability, failure-modes) A start-placed task anchor renders a different id and the cross-reference 404s, and link-integrity fires only when something else references it. Fix: the parser enforces heading-end placement directly.</p> <h2 id="recommended-re-cut-the-minimal-evidenced-core"><a class="header" href="#recommended-re-cut-the-minimal-evidenced-core">Recommended re-cut (the minimal evidenced core)</a></h2> <p>Ship first, the evidenced need:</p> <ol> <li>Anchored task nodes, disambiguated: an anchor-carrying <code>### </code> heading under <code>## Build sequence</code>, the anchor at the heading end, both enforced by the parser.</li> <li>A per-task receipt in the operational ledger keyspace, with input-digest staleness (both halves of call/0018), gated per task rather than per milestone-complete.</li> <li>A separate task-anchor link checker (path-shape gated), so a cross-task reference that breaks fails the gate.</li> </ol> <p>Defer until a consumer exists:</p> <ul> <li>The dependency graph, the frontier derivation, the cycle check, and the coordinator fan-out. Keep the node design graph-ready (a later one-field add).</li> </ul> <p>Drop:</p> <ul> <li>The third receipt file (use the operational keyspace).</li> <li>A general verify-disposition grammar (a mechanical verify is a command string; everything else is attested and cite-resolved).</li> <li>The per-milestone-complete trigger.</li> </ul> <h2 id="decisions-for-the-operator-the-review-touches-three-rulings"><a class="header" href="#decisions-for-the-operator-the-review-touches-three-rulings">Decisions for the operator (the review touches three rulings)</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The graph.</strong> Defer until a real parallel milestone, or build it now as a forward capability for parallel sub-agents? The reviewers find no consumer and recommend defer; the original rationale was forward-looking. The node design stays graph-ready either way.</li> <li><strong>The ledger.</strong> Honor "separate tool-written" as a keyspace inside the operational <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> (ontology-clean) rather than a third top-level file?</li> <li><strong>Scope.</strong> Dogfood meta-repo-only first (the plan/0038 test for an adopter obligation), or stay adopter-facing with the receipt obligation made opt-in per milestone (the inert-until-declared ladder pattern)? A blanket mandatory receipt-per-task gate taxes adopters who write small linear plans.</li> </ol> <h2 id="resolution-operator-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#resolution-operator-2026-06-25">Resolution (operator, 2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p>The operator settled the three decisions, overriding the re-scope on the first and third with a stated rationale, and confirmed the cross-plan capability:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The graph: build now.</strong> The methodology serves projects of arbitrary complexity, not this repo's own linear history, so "no consumer in agentic-host" is the wrong lens; the consumer is the arbitrary-complexity adopter. The graph is built now as forward infrastructure, with cross-milestone <code>depends</code> confirmed at the 4B bar (four of four: read a <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code> dependency, author a mixed local-plus-cross-plan <code>depends</code>).</li> <li><strong>The ledger: a new top-level <code>.host-task-receipts</code>.</strong> The operator accepted the ontology cost for the physical separation; it is recorded as a deliberate third receipt kind in the build's <code>call/</code> decision.</li> <li><strong>Scope: adopter-facing and mandatory.</strong> The receipt-per-task gate is a hard rule for every adopter.</li> </ul> <p>The <code>#N</code> GitHub reference matter is acknowledged (a bare <code>#N</code> is not a safe full URL) and deferred to a future plan that enforces full URLs; plan/0042's task references use full relative-path anchors and never the <code>#N</code> form. The review's soundness findings (both halves of call/0018, the per-task trigger, the heading disambiguation, the separate link checker, the skip-citation, the drift reverse check, and the resource-isolation precondition) are folded into the re-cut README.</p> <h2 id="status-4"><a class="header" href="#status-4">Status</a></h2> <p>Resolved. The plan/0042 README is re-cut to the settled design; ready to build.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0043-the-entrance-check-a-reusable-standalone-document-check"><a class="header" href="#plan0043-the-entrance-check-a-reusable-standalone-document-check">plan/0043: the entrance check (a reusable standalone-document check)</a></h1> <p>The front-door check (plan/0040, host-lifecycle v0.27.0) holds the one published entrance of agentic-host to the spine. The same problem recurs wherever a project keeps a self-contained document that restates the methodology and cannot link to it: an adopter-authored standalone <code>SKILL.md</code>, or any project's operator-and-agent landing page. This milestone is the whole effort: it generalizes the check into an opt-in, reusable capability declared by a single <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, builds the document and concept machinery the generalization needs, and reconciles the spine flag the standalone rename left diverged. It supersedes the agentic-host-local scope set in plan/0040.</p> <h2 id="problem-3"><a class="header" href="#problem-3">Problem</a></h2> <p>A self-contained document is read out of context (a single-file entry point, a skill loaded on its own), so it cannot point at a canonical definition with a link the way an in-host doc does (the reconcile arm). It restates, and the restatement stales silently when the spine moves. plan/0040 solved this for one document, hardwired: the tool finds the <code>.host-software</code> member marked <code>entrance = true</code> and checks its <code>README.md</code> against the manifest phases, the <code>.host-software</code> tools, and the <code>.host</code> stamp format. Nothing lets another document, or another project, opt in, and the marker is wired to a member's <code>README.md</code> by filename, so a differently-named document cannot be pointed at.</p> <p>Two facts the pre-generalization audit and the design review surfaced shape the work:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The marker is a spine concept.</strong> host-template (<code>CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>UPGRADING.md</code>) documents the marker as the adopter-facing way reconcile sets a single-file front door apart from <code>components</code>. The standalone rename (<code>call/0027</code>) moved the tool to <code>entrance = true</code> and left the spine on <code>front-door = true</code>, a divergence the deprecation shim absorbs. The generalization owes the spine reconciliation.</li> <li><strong>The per-member marker was overloaded.</strong> When the marker was a per-member value, the same predicate set the entrance and defined <code>components</code> (members minus the entrance), so a richer value form could un-mark the front door and re-demote it into <code>components</code>. The declaration below moves the marker to its own stanza, which names the member outright, so that overload dissolves by construction.</li> </ul> <h2 id="decision-operator"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator">Decision (operator)</a></h2> <p>plan/0043 expands to encompass every aspect of the entrance work, rather than narrowing to the spine reconciliation the design review recommended. The review's blocking findings become requirements the design meets, not reasons to defer. The declaration is a single <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, a global singleton among the <code>.host-software</code> members, so one entrance reaches any document by path while the marker-break is designed out at the parse layer. The standalone sibling framing (reconcile holds linkable docs honest with pointers; entrance holds self-contained docs honest with coverage and generation, because they cannot link) stands. The name <code>entrance</code> stands, settled by the Qwen-3.5-4B run in <code>gather-data.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-design"><a class="header" href="#the-design">The design</a></h2> <h3 id="the-declaration-a-singleton-entrance-stanza"><a class="header" href="#the-declaration-a-singleton-entrance-stanza">The declaration: a singleton <code>[entrance]</code> stanza</a></h3> <p>A project declares its entrance in one <code>[entrance]</code> stanza in <code>.host-software</code>, a global singleton among the member stanzas (a second stanza is a loud error). It names the member the entrance belongs to, the document within that member's worktree, and the concepts the document keeps complete:</p> <pre><code>[entrance] member = host document = README.md restates = phases tools </code></pre> <p><code>document</code> defaults to <code>README.md</code> and reaches any file in the member's worktree, so a <code>SKILL.md</code> or a landing page is declared by path rather than excluded by a hardwired filename. <code>restates = true</code> keeps the document complete against every concept (the front-door case), so a full front door never types an enumeration; a concept list keeps it complete against that subset. The concept names are a closed vocabulary the tool validates at parse time, so an unknown concept is a loud error rather than a silently ignored word.</p> <p>The named <code>member</code> is set apart from <code>components</code>, the one member singled out among the rest, exactly as the front door is today, so reconcile holds the component set to the others. Because the stanza names the member outright, there is no per-member value to misparse, and no value form can demote the entrance into the component set: the marker-break the review found dissolves. The Qwen-3.5-4B runs (<code>gather-data.md</code>) leaned to a member-level value for the member-and-README case and to a self-documenting <code>[entrance "…"]</code> stanza for clarity; the full-reach requirement (a document path the member flag cannot carry) and the singleton constraint settle the form on the dedicated stanza.</p> <h3 id="the-migration"><a class="header" href="#the-migration">The migration</a></h3> <p>The legacy per-member marker, both <code>front-door = true</code> and the <code>entrance = true</code> that agentic-host adopted in <code>call/0027</code>, is accepted by the deprecation shim as the front-door entrance during the transition, mapped to the equivalent stanza. The shim warns and names the stanza form. Its retirement landed in this milestone as host-lifecycle v0.30.0 (the operator chose to retire now, rather than a release later): a surviving per-member marker is a loud problem in every consumer, never the entrance, and the spine and agentic-host carry no legacy marker.</p> <h3 id="the-concept-set-checked-against-its-homes"><a class="header" href="#the-concept-set-checked-against-its-homes">The concept set, checked against its homes</a></h3> <p>The <code>restates</code> concepts select what the check holds, each against the structured home it already reads: the lifecycle phases against the manifest, the wired tools against the <code>.host-software</code> drivers, the <code>.host</code> stamp against the tool's canonical format, and the other <code>.host-software</code> concepts reconcile already names (<code>components</code>, <code>verifiers</code>, <code>software-root</code>, <code>spec-home</code>).
