The check holds the document complete against the declared set only, so a front door declaring <code>true</code> is held to every concept and a partial entrance is held to its subset. The concept vocabulary is the reconcile vocabulary plus the phases and the stamp, named once, so an adopter learns one set of words.</p> <h3 id="the-honest-scope"><a class="header" href="#the-honest-scope">The honest scope</a></h3> <p>The entrance check holds any document that restates a concept with a structured home. A document that restates only home-less teaching doctrine (a disposition rule, the conditional-lane MUST) declares no checkable concept, and its <code>restates</code> set says so plainly. This is plan/0040's settled principle carried forward: a fact is drift-proof through the tool only when the tool reads its home, and the milestone says so rather than claiming a coverage it cannot deliver. The generality earns itself as real entrances that restate home-backed concepts appear; the machinery is built now so they can opt in.</p> <h3 id="the-routing-rule"><a class="header" href="#the-routing-rule">The routing rule</a></h3> <p>Generate what is naturally a format or data block (the <code>.host</code> stamp), coverage-check what is naturally prose (a phase name, a tool name), and never put a generation marker in teaching prose (plan/0039). The declaration stays out of the document, in the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, so the document reads clean.</p> <h3 id="the-reconcile-relationship"><a class="header" href="#the-reconcile-relationship">The reconcile relationship</a></h3> <p><code>entrance</code> stays a separate subcommand, the sibling of <code>reconcile</code>, settled by plan/0040 and confirmed by the review. reconcile resolves links and checks anchors over tracked markdown; entrance reads a materialized document, covers the manifest phases, and generates the stamp byte-exact. They share only the parsed <code>[entrance]</code> stanza (the entrance and the set-apart member), kept a single tested source so a change serves both consumers at once.</p> <h3 id="the-spine-reconciliation"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-reconciliation">The spine reconciliation</a></h3> <p>host-template replaces the <code>front-door = true</code> prose with the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza in <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>UPGRADING.md</code>, documents the stanza and its <code>document</code> and <code>restates</code> fields, and ships an adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry that migrates a legacy per-member marker to the stanza, whose verify post-condition holds <code>entrance --check</code>, <code>reconcile</code>, and <code>software --check</code> green so a misapplied migration shows loudly at apply time. The exit-code convention comment (exit <code>1</code> for the issues a command finds, exit <code>2</code> when it cannot proceed on its input), refined by the code review in <code>code-review.md</code>, folds into the same release.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-3"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-3">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The build sequence as a task graph (plan/0042), each entry an anchored task carrying a receipt. The tool gains the stanza first, then the spine documents it, then agentic-host moves to it, so no state is half-migrated.</p> <h3 id="settle-open-decisions"><a class="header" href="#settle-open-decisions">Settle the open decisions by review</a></h3> <p>Settle the declaration form, the concept-set model, the reconcile relationship, and the spine reconciliation by adversarial review, recorded in <code>design-review.md</code> with the operator re-cut that expands the milestone, designs out the marker-break with the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, and reaches any document by path under a global-singleton constraint.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-entrance"><a class="header" href="#implement-entrance">Implement the entrance generalization</a></h3> <p>Parse the singleton <code>[entrance]</code> stanza (one per project, the member, the <code>document</code> path defaulting to <code>README.md</code>, the <code>restates</code> concept set with a <code>true</code> sentinel and a closed vocabulary), resolve the document within the member's worktree, route the declared concepts through the check against their homes, set the named member apart from <code>components</code>, accept the legacy per-member marker by the shim, and fold in the exit-code convention comment. Regression tests pin the new parse: the stanza yields the entrance member and keeps it out of <code>components</code>, the document path resolves within the worktree, and a declared subset checks only its concepts. A second <code>[entrance]</code> stanza fails loudly, and so does an unknown concept name.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #settle-open-decisions</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-doctrine"><a class="header" href="#spine-doctrine">Add the spine doctrine and the ledger entry</a></h3> <p>Replace the <code>front-door = true</code> prose in host-template (<code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>UPGRADING.md</code>) with the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, document its <code>document</code> and <code>restates</code> fields, add the entrance doctrine (an entrance is a declared self-contained document held to the spine, the standalone sibling of reconcile), and add the adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry that migrates a legacy per-member marker to the stanza, whose verify post-condition holds <code>entrance --check</code>, <code>reconcile</code>, and <code>software --check</code>. host-template prose stays clean.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #implement-entrance</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="migrate-agentic-host"><a class="header" href="#migrate-agentic-host">Move agentic-host to the stanza</a></h3> <p>Migrate agentic-host's <code>.host-software</code> from <code>entrance = true</code> to the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza, adopt the host-template revision, and confirm <code>entrance --check</code>, <code>reconcile</code>, and <code>software --check</code> stay green on the new declaration.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #spine-doctrine</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="validate-4b"><a class="header" href="#validate-4b">Validate at the weak-agent bar</a></h3> <p>Validate the stanza ergonomics and an entrance use case (a member that declares a concept subset and a non-README document) with a recorded Qwen-3.5-4B run that confirms the singleton, the <code>document</code> path, and the sentinel-and-vocabulary guards.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #migrate-agentic-host</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release, re-pin, and record</a></h3> <p>Release host-lifecycle, bump the host-template pointer, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the receipts and a <code>call/</code> decision that supersedes the scope of <code>call/0026</code> and carries <code>call/0027</code> to completion, and bump the CI install pins. The released binary gates green and the whole suite is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #validate-4b</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="retire-shim"><a class="header" href="#retire-shim">Retire the legacy per-member marker</a></h3> <p>Retire the deprecate-then-retire shim: a surviving per-member <code>front-door = true</code> or <code>entrance = true</code> becomes a loud problem in every consumer, never the entrance. Add the spine retirement doctrine and an adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> entry, gated so the live spine no longer teaches the legacy marker. Ship a host-lifecycle release, then re-pin and adopt.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #release-and-re-pin</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-3"><a class="header" href="#risks-3">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The milestone touches the spine, the tool, and the agentic-host declaration at once. The tool gains the stanza before the spine documents it and agentic-host moves to it, and the shim accepts the legacy marker throughout, so no state is half-migrated.</li> <li>The declaration adds a surface every adopter could meet, so it stays one stanza: a member, a document path, a closed concept set with a <code>true</code> sentinel, validated loudly, a single entrance per project.</li> <li>The generality is built ahead of a second real entrance. The honest scope keeps the claim true to what the tool reads, so the machinery is ready without over-claiming a coverage it cannot yet exercise.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-5"><a class="header" href="#status-5">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lifecycle v0.29.0 (2026-06-25; <code>dbeb3db</code>, artifact <code>01171b92</code>). The entrance check reads a singleton <code>[entrance]</code> stanza in <code>.host-software</code> that names the member and the document within it (default <code>README.md</code>), held complete against the concepts it <code>restates</code>, reaching any document by path, the standalone sibling of reconcile. A three-reviewer adversarial design review returned a re-scope verdict; the operator re-cut it to expand the milestone, folding the review's blocking findings in as design requirements. A three-reviewer adversarial code review (<code>code-review.md</code>) then found and fixed two blocking defects before release: the parse <code>problems</code> reached only the entrance command, so a typo'd member re-demoted the front door through reconcile; and an empty <code>restates</code> checked nothing yet reported clean. A Qwen-3.5-4B run validated the declaration form and the stanza ergonomics (<code>gather-data.md</code>). host-template <code>ba86125</code> carries the doctrine and the adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> entry; agentic-host migrated its <code>.host-software</code> to the stanza and adopted the revision. Supersedes the agentic-host-local scope of plan/0040 and the scope half of <code>call/0026</code>, carries <code>call/0027</code> to completion, and is recorded in <code>call/0028</code>. The legacy per-member marker was then retired (host-lifecycle v0.30.0, host-template <code>de8a517</code>): a surviving one is a loud problem in every consumer, which completes the deprecate-then-retire path. The whole suite is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0043-code-review-the-entrance-stanza-implementation"><a class="header" href="#plan0043-code-review-the-entrance-stanza-implementation">plan/0043 code review: the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza implementation</a></h1> <p>Three independent adversarial reviewers read the uncommitted <code>#implement-entrance</code> diff (the <code>[entrance]</code> stanza in <code>parse_project_facts</code>, the routed <code>entrance</code> check, the document resolution, the legacy shim) against the milestone, the design review, and <code>call/0027</code>. One read for parser correctness and edge cases, one for the reconcile coupling and regressions, one for fail-safe behavior and the exit codes. They converged on two blocking defects and a cluster of parser holes, all of which shipped green because no test exercised them. The verdict was fix-first; the fixes are below, and the suite now covers each.</p> <h2 id="the-blocking-defects"><a class="header" href="#the-blocking-defects">The blocking defects</a></h2> <h3 id="the-problems-guard-reached-only-one-consumer"><a class="header" href="#the-problems-guard-reached-only-one-consumer">The <code>problems</code> guard reached only one consumer</a></h3> <p>The <code>[entrance]</code> value form is parsed once, and the same parse sets the entrance member apart from <code>components</code>, the set reconcile holds <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> to. A malformed stanza (a typo in <code>member</code>) recorded a <code>problems</code> entry but still computed <code>components</code> by excluding the typo'd name, so the real front door stayed in <code>components</code>. The <code>entrance</code> command surfaced <code>problems</code>; reconcile did not, so it took the corrupted set and would demand <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> name the front door a component, the exact <code>call/0027</code> silent demotion, relocated to a different consumer. The integrity reviewer proved it from a one-character typo; the correctness and fail-safe reviewers reached the same seam.</p> <p>Fix: reconcile now surfaces <code>facts.problems</code> and exits before it trusts <code>components</code>, so a malformed stanza is loud in every consumer. (<code>software --check</code> was confirmed never to read <code>ProjectFacts</code>, so the seam was reconcile alone.)</p> <h3 id="an-empty-restates-value-checked-nothing-and-reported-clean"><a class="header" href="#an-empty-restates-value-checked-nothing-and-reported-clean">An empty <code>restates</code> value checked nothing and reported clean</a></h3> <p><code>restates =</code> with an empty value missed the <code>true</code> sentinel arm and parsed to an empty concept set, which <code>checks</code> answers false for every concept. The entrance check then ran nothing and printed clean, a fail-open inversion of the milestone's fail-safe stance. All three reviewers found it.</p> <p>Fix: an empty <code>restates</code> value is now a problem (exit <code>2</code>), the same as an unknown concept.</p> <h2 id="the-parser-holes"><a class="header" href="#the-parser-holes">The parser holes</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A sub-named <code>[entrance "x"]</code> was silently ignored.</strong> The match was on the literal <code>[entrance]</code>, so the self-documenting form the Fen runs leaned toward dropped to no entrance with no problem. Now it parses and flags the wrong form.</li> <li><strong><code>document</code> could escape the worktree.</strong> A <code>..</code> or absolute <code>document</code> resolved outside the member's worktree, and write mode could rewrite an external file. Now an escaping <code>document</code> is a problem.</li> <li><strong>The <code>true</code> sentinel was case-sensitive.</strong> A legacy <code>entrance = True</code> did not match, so the member silently lost its entrance status and fell into <code>components</code>, a <code>call/0027</code>-class demotion over a capital letter. The legacy marker and the <code>restates</code> sentinel are both case-insensitive now.</li> <li><strong>A duplicate <code>member</code> key last-wrote silently.</strong> A repeated <code>member</code> in one stanza is now a problem.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-exit-code-framing"><a class="header" href="#the-exit-code-framing">The exit-code framing</a></h2> <p>The review found that the exit-code comment this milestone folds in contradicted the code it sits beside: it claimed an expected logic error exits <code>2</code>, while a <code>--check</code> drift, the most expected logic outcome, exits <code>1</code>, as it does across the tool's many check sites. The codebase convention is the standard one and was kept: <code>0</code> clean, <code>1</code> the red outcome a command surfaces (a drift, a HAZARD, a failed gate), <code>2</code> a command that cannot proceed on its input (a missing, unreadable, or malformed input the user named; <code>next</code> on a numberless directory). The comment, <code>gather-data.md</code>, and the build-sequence task are corrected to that wording rather than the code changed across the tool.</p> <h2 id="a-noted-boundary-not-a-defect"><a class="header" href="#a-noted-boundary-not-a-defect">A noted boundary, not a defect</a></h2> <p>A reviewer observed that a partial entrance (a <code>restates</code> subset) declared on a real component member would exclude that member from <code>components</code>. The entrance is the single set-apart entry point by design (a non-component member: the front door, or a standalone document with its own member), so this is a misuse outside the model rather than a code defect. The boundary is recorded; a document inside a tool component is not the singleton entrance.</p> <h2 id="verdict-1"><a class="header" href="#verdict-1">Verdict</a></h2> <p>Ship, after the fixes. The two blocking defects are closed and covered by tests, the parser holes are loud rather than silent, and the exit-code wording matches the tool. <code>cargo test</code> is green and <code>cargo clippy</code> is clean; reconcile exits <code>2</code> on a typo'd member and the entrance exits <code>2</code> on an empty <code>restates</code>, both verified on the built binary.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0043-design-review-the-entrance-check"><a class="header" href="#plan0043-design-review-the-entrance-check">plan/0043 design review: the entrance check</a></h1> <p>Three independent adversarial reviewers read the milestone, <code>gather-data.md</code>, the spine (<code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code>, <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md</code>, <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>), the reconcile and entrance code in <code>software/host-lifecycle/main/src/main.rs</code>, and <code>call/0023</code> and <code>call/0027</code>. One read with a simplicity bias (is this premature and over-built?), one with an integrity bias (does coverage actually hold the new documents complete?), and one with a weak-agent-ergonomics bias (can an adopter and a weak agent author and apply it without a silent break?). They converged on the same core findings and a re-scope.</p> <p>The operator decisions recorded so far stand: the capability is opt-in and reusable in principle, the name is <code>entrance</code>, and it is the standalone sibling of reconcile. The review interrogated the declaration form, the concept-set model, the reconcile relationship, and the spine reconciliation, and found the generalization premature and one mechanism broken as drawn.</p> <h2 id="the-convergent-blocking-finding-the-value-form-breaks-the-shared-marker"><a class="header" href="#the-convergent-blocking-finding-the-value-form-breaks-the-shared-marker">The convergent blocking finding: the value form breaks the shared marker</a></h2> <p>The <code>entrance</code> marker is overloaded. <code>parse_project_facts</code> sets a member apart as the entrance only when the value is exactly <code>true</code> (<code>main.rs:1352</code>, <code>val.trim() == "true"</code>). That one predicate feeds two checks at once: <code>facts.entrance</code> is the entrance check's target, and <code>facts.components</code> is every member except the entrance, the set reconcile holds the <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> components home to (<code>main.rs:1362</code>, the coverage bite at <code>main.rs:1607</code>).</p> <p>So the gathered Style A value, <code>entrance = phases tools</code>, does not generalize the flag. It silently un-marks the entrance: the value is not <code>true</code>, the <code>host</code> member loses its set-apart status, <code>facts.entrance</code> goes empty, and <code>host</code> falls back into <code>facts.components</code>. The next reconcile run then demands the <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> components home name <code>host</code>, the exact silent demotion <code>call/0027</code> was written to forbid, reintroduced through the value rather than the key. No test covers a non-boolean <code>entrance</code> value, so the regression would ship green. The integrity and ergonomics reviews both proved this from the code.</p> <p>The lesson is plan/0040's, one rung along: a fact is only safe through the tool when the tool actually reads it. The concept list in <code>entrance = phases tools</code> is read by nothing today (<code>entrance_problems</code> checks all phases and all tools and the stamp unconditionally, <code>main.rs:1750</code>), so the declared set is unverifiable sugar that also breaks the marker.</p> <h2 id="the-generality-is-unfounded-the-new-documents-restate-doctrine-with-no-home"><a class="header" href="#the-generality-is-unfounded-the-new-documents-restate-doctrine-with-no-home">The generality is unfounded: the new documents restate doctrine with no home</a></h2> <p>The milestone's headline is that the check generalizes to a standalone <code>SKILL.md</code> and an operator-and-agent landing page. The entrance check holds three facts: the lifecycle phases (home: the manifest), the wired tools (home: <code>.host-software</code>), and the <code>.host</code> stamp block (a fixed format). <code>entrance_spine_facts</code> returns the full manifest and the full driver set every time (<code>main.rs:1795</code>); <code>entrance_problems</code> looks for the phases, the tools, and a <code>## The stamp</code> block (<code>main.rs:1750</code>).</p> <p>A standalone skill or a landing page restates teaching doctrine: the disposition rules, the point-over-restate principle, the conditional-lane MUST. None of that has a structured home the tool reads, so the check cannot hold it complete. plan/0040 settled exactly this class: the lanes rule and the tool prose have no structured home and stay authored, and the milestone says so plainly rather than claiming a drift-proofing it cannot deliver (<code>plan/0040/design-review.md:69</code>, <code>:112</code>). The simplicity review also found that the one concrete candidate, <code>software/host-lint/main/SKILL.md</code>, restates neither the phases nor the tools, so the motivating second user does not exist in the repo, and the check resolves a member's <code>README.md</code> by filename (<code>main.rs:1809</code>), so a differently-named skill doc could not even be declared.</p> <p>So the entrance check holds, honestly, any document that restates the phase, tool, and stamp facts, which in practice is the front-door <code>README.md</code> and little else. The broader pitch is not delivered by the design.</p> <h2 id="the-real-finishable-payload-the-spine-reconciliation"><a class="header" href="#the-real-finishable-payload-the-spine-reconciliation">The real, finishable payload: the spine reconciliation</a></h2> <p>The one part with a real, non-speculative obligation is the spine reconciliation that the pre-generalization audit surfaced. The spine still teaches the old spelling: <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md:281</code> and <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md:207</code> both document <code>front-door = true</code>, while the tool prefers <code>entrance = true</code> and a deprecation shim absorbs the gap (<code>call/0027</code>). This is live debt <code>call/0027</code> deferred, fixable now, and it needs none of the declaration-form or concept-set machinery.</p> <p>The integrity review added a sharp constraint: the shim retirement adds a hard fail on a surviving <code>front-door = true</code>, but the spine prose that teaches <code>front-door = true</code> has no structured home and nothing gates it. Retire the shim while the spine still teaches the old spelling, and the spine teaches the very spelling the tool now rejects. So a <code>front-door</code> grep over host-template is a release gate of the retirement, not an afterthought. The ergonomics review added that the adopter ledger entry is a pure boolean rename (<code>front-door = true</code> to <code>entrance = true</code>), which stays a safe literal substitution precisely because <code>entrance = true</code> still parses, and its verify post-condition must hold reconcile and <code>software --check</code> green, not only <code>entrance --check</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-decisions-settled"><a class="header" href="#the-decisions-settled">The decisions, settled</a></h2> <h3 id="the-declaration-form-keep-entrance--true-defer-the-value-form"><a class="header" href="#the-declaration-form-keep-entrance--true-defer-the-value-form">The declaration form: keep <code>entrance = true</code>, defer the value form</a></h3> <p><code>entrance = true</code> stands. It marks the front door, which restates every concept, and it already parses, so the spine rename stays a safe no-op substitution. The concept-list value (Style A) is deferred with the generalization: introducing it now breaks the shared marker for a feature no document needs yet. The Fen leaning to a member-level concept list is recorded in <code>gather-data.md</code> for that future decision, with the caveats the review added: a <code>true</code> or <code>all</code> sentinel for the restates-everything case so the full front door never types an enumeration, a closed concept vocabulary the tool validates at parse time, and the marker keyed on presence with a non-empty value rather than on <code>== "true"</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-concept-set-model-deferred-with-its-homes-named"><a class="header" href="#the-concept-set-model-deferred-with-its-homes-named">The concept-set model: deferred, with its homes named</a></h3> <p>Deferred with the declaration form. The only concepts with a structured home are the phases and the tools, and the front door restates both, which <code>entrance = true</code> already covers in full. A partial entrance (a document restating a subset) has no consumer yet, and a routed concept set is unimplemented (<code>entrance_problems</code> checks all concepts unconditionally). When a real partial entrance exists, the set must be a closed vocabulary aligned with reconcile's concept names, rather than a third overlapping word list.</p> <h3 id="the-reconcile-relationship-settled-a-separate-subcommand"><a class="header" href="#the-reconcile-relationship-settled-a-separate-subcommand">The reconcile relationship: settled, a separate subcommand</a></h3> <p>Already settled by plan/0040 (the entrance check ships as a sibling of reconcile) and confirmed in every review here. reconcile resolves links and checks anchors over tracked markdown; entrance reads a materialized README, covers the manifest phases, and generates the stamp byte-exact. Folding entrance into reconcile would put a generator inside a checker. They share only <code>parse_project_facts</code>, and that shared marker is the real coupling point, to be kept a single, tested primitive. This leaves the open list.</p> <h3 id="the-spine-reconciliation-the-milestones-core-do-it-now"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-reconciliation-the-milestones-core-do-it-now">The spine reconciliation: the milestone's core, do it now</a></h3> <p>Rename <code>front-door = true</code> to <code>entrance = true</code> in <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md</code>, ship an adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> ledger entry for the rename, and retire the deprecate-then-retire shim with a hard fail on a surviving <code>front-door = true</code>. Gate the retirement on a <code>front-door</code> grep over host-template, so the spine never teaches the spelling the tool rejects, and gate the ledger entry's verify post-condition on reconcile and <code>software --check</code> green, not only <code>entrance --check</code>. Fold in the exit-code convention comment that <code>gather-data.md</code> validated.</p> <h2 id="verdict-2"><a class="header" href="#verdict-2">Verdict</a></h2> <p>Re-scope. The opt-in generalization for documents unlike the front door is deferred until a real second entrance exists, one that restates a concept with a structured home, since the headline <code>SKILL.md</code> and landing-page use cases restate doctrine the tool cannot hold complete, and the gathered value form breaks the shared marker for a feature no document needs yet. The milestone's deliverable becomes the spine reconciliation it already owes: rename the spine flag, ship the adopter ledger entry, retire the shim behind a host-template <code>front-door</code> grep gate, and fold in the exit-code comment, with the marker parse left on <code>entrance = true</code> so reconcile's component model stays intact. The entrance check's honest scope is recorded: it holds any document that restates the phase, tool, and stamp facts, which today is the front door.</p> <h2 id="operator-re-cut"><a class="header" href="#operator-re-cut">Operator re-cut</a></h2> <p>The operator overruled the re-scope. plan/0043 is the effort for the whole entrance work, so it expands to encompass every aspect rather than narrowing to the spine reconciliation. The review's blocking findings become design requirements the milestone must meet, not reasons to defer:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The marker-break is designed out.</strong> The entrance marker keys on the <code>entrance</code> key present with a non-empty value, parsed once into the concept set, with <code>true</code> meaning the full set. A member stays set apart whatever its value form, so the value never demotes the front door into reconcile's components. Good design closes the seam; it is not a reason to wait. A regression test pins both <code>facts.entrance</code> and <code>facts.components</code> for the value form.</li> <li><strong>The concept set is wired, not decorative.</strong> The declared concepts select what the check holds, each against its structured home, so the value is verified rather than ignored.</li> <li><strong>The scope is stated, not over-claimed.</strong> The entrance check holds any document that restates a concept with a structured home. A document that restates only home-less doctrine declares no checkable concept, and the per-document declaration says so plainly, rather than the tool pretending a coverage it cannot deliver.</li> <li><strong>The spine reconciliation lands inside this milestone,</strong> beside the marker work, so the value form and the spine rename ship together and no state is half-renamed.</li> </ul> <p>The expanded design and its build sequence are in <code>README.md</code>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0043-gather-data-the-declaration-form-and-the-exit-code-convention-qwen-35-4b"><a class="header" href="#plan0043-gather-data-the-declaration-form-and-the-exit-code-convention-qwen-35-4b">plan/0043 gather-data: the declaration form and the exit-code convention (Qwen-3.5-4B)</a></h1> <p>Two pre-generalization questions put to Fen (Qwen-3.5-4B) through pal, the way the name and the front-door coverage call were settled. The probes were short, and each is judged on the converged reasoning.</p> <h2 id="the-declaration-form-finding-1"><a class="header" href="#the-declaration-form-finding-1">The declaration form (finding 1)</a></h2> <p>How a project declares an entrance and the concepts it must keep complete. Three candidate <code>.host-software</code> styles, put to Fen across three runs:</p> <ul> <li>Style A, a concept list on the member: <code>entrance = phases tools</code> under <code>[software "host"]</code>.</li> <li>Style B, a boolean with a restates line: <code>entrance = true</code> and <code>restates = phases tools</code>.</li> <li>Style C, a dedicated stanza: <code>[entrance "host"]</code> with <code>restates = phases tools</code>.</li> </ul> <p>The picks were C, then A, then C (the host with two concepts, the host judged on first-try authoring, and a skill with one concept).</p> <ul> <li><strong>Style B is rejected in every run.</strong> <code>entrance = true</code> reads as ambiguous (is an entrance, or entrance is enabled), and the boolean with a separate restates line is redundant and verbose for the same fact.</li> <li><strong>Style C wins in isolation</strong> (the <code>[entrance "host"]</code> header self-documents the purpose), <strong>and both the C runs and the A run raised the same caveat unprompted</strong>: when the entrance is an existing <code>[software]</code> member carrying <code>url</code> and <code>pin</code>, a member-level form is wanted, since a separate <code>[entrance]</code> stanza splits the declaration off from the member it describes.</li> <li><strong>agentic-host's entrance is the <code>[software "host"]</code> member</strong> (it carries <code>url</code> and <code>pin</code>), so the caveat applies and the data resolves to <strong>Style A</strong>: a concept list on the member, <code>entrance = <concepts></code>, which both marks the member and names what it keeps complete. So <code>entrance = true</code> generalizes to <code>entrance = phases tools</code>, or an all-concepts value for a full front door. One caveat carried forward: a bare single value such as <code>entrance = phases</code> reads cryptic, so the value wants a clear list shape.</li> </ul> <p>The leaning for the generalization review: the declaration form is a concept-list value on the member (<code>entrance = <concepts></code>), rather than the boolean-with-restates pair or a separate stanza. The review confirms it.</p> <h2 id="the-exit-code-convention-finding-3"><a class="header" href="#the-exit-code-convention-finding-3">The exit-code convention (finding 3)</a></h2> <p>The convention set in the plan/0040 and plan/0041 decision review: exit <code>1</code> is an unexpected or internal fault, exit <code>2</code> is an expected logic or usage error. Put to Fen as a routing task over two scenario sets.</p> <ul> <li>The first set: a missing named <code>.host-software</code> exits <code>2</code>; a disk-full write exits <code>1</code>; a directory with no numbered entries exits <code>2</code>.</li> <li>The second set (the converged reasoning, before a pal format-loop): a named missing config stanza exits <code>2</code>; a kernel socket drop mid-read exits <code>1</code>; a <code>--check</code> on a document missing a required heading exits <code>2</code>.</li> </ul> <p>Every scenario routed correctly, including the no-entries case to <code>2</code>, which matches the fail-closed <code>next</code> decision (plan/0041). The convention wording is clear enough for a weak agent to route a new error, so the one-line comment is safe to write into the generalization release. The second run hit the documented pal format-loop after it converged, so the reasoning before the loop is what counts here.</p> <p>The code review of the implementation (<code>code-review.md</code>) refined the framing: the tool's established convention is issues-found versus cannot-proceed, so a <code>--check</code> drift exits <code>1</code> (the issue the check finds) and a cannot-proceed input exits <code>2</code> (the no-entries case above). The probe still shows a weak agent routes a stated convention correctly; the comment shipped is worded to the established convention.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0044-lexicon-masking-reaches-the-prose-lane"><a class="header" href="#plan0044-lexicon-masking-reaches-the-prose-lane">plan/0044: LEXICON masking reaches the prose lane</a></h1> <p>The LEXICON allowlist (host-lint issue #13) masks a sanctioned phrase before the naming lane classifies a line, so a legitimate tell-shaped token a project declares stops flagging. The prose lane, the host-grammar density engine behind <code>--prose</code> and <code>--docs</code>, never consulted that allowlist, so a legitimate domain word the prose grammar reads as an ai-diction trope had no sanctioned escape. host-lint issue #16 reports the divergence. This milestone extends the existing pre-detection mask to the prose lane, so one declaration serves both lanes.</p> <h2 id="problem-4"><a class="header" href="#problem-4">Problem</a></h2> <p>The two lanes take different paths. The naming lane masks each line with the sanctioned phrases before it classifies; the prose lane hands the raw document to the host-grammar engine and never sees the allowlist. So a project that legitimately uses a domain noun the grammar over-reads (the reporter's case is the noun <code>harness</code>, the name of a <code>rehost harness</code> used identically across its codebase) is left with two options, rename the term or carry the warning, while the naming lane would have honoured a declaration.</p> <p>This contradicts the living-grammar doctrine, which names the per-project LEXICON as the home for a token the shared grammar flags but the project judges legitimate. For a prose trope that home did not exist: the only inline-source escape is the block-level <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fence, and there is no per-project prose allowlist. The README also overclaims. It says a declared phrase never flags "in any mode", though the enumerated modes are the naming modes alone.</p> <h2 id="decision-operator-1"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-1">Decision (operator)</a></h2> <p>Of the three options the issue lists, the operator chose the first, extend the mask, and set aside a separate prose allowlist and documenting the gap as intentional. One declaration in the existing LEXICON serves both lanes; the prose lane reuses the same pre-detection blank-out the naming lane already performs. The decision and its alternatives are recorded in <code>call/0029</code>, validated at the weak-agent bar in <code>gather-data.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-design-1"><a class="header" href="#the-design-1">The design</a></h2> <h3 id="the-mask-before-both-the-per-tell-scan-and-the-density-score"><a class="header" href="#the-mask-before-both-the-per-tell-scan-and-the-density-score">The mask, before both the per-tell scan and the density score</a></h3> <p><code>scan_prose_text</code> masks the whole document with <code>mask_allowed</code>, the naming lane's blank-out (byte-length-preserving, word-boundaried, case-insensitive), before the host-grammar pass. The masked text feeds both the per-tell scan and the document density score, so a declared phrase contributes to neither. Because the mask preserves byte length, the offsets that locate each surviving tell still index the original document, and the reported excerpt stays the author's own text.</p> <h3 id="surgical-not-blanket"><a class="header" href="#surgical-not-blanket">Surgical, not blanket</a></h3> <p>A declared multi-word phrase clears the trope only within that phrase; a standalone occurrence of the same word still flags. Declaring <code>rehost harness</code> clears <code>harness</code> inside that phrase and leaves a later standalone <code>harness</code> reported, the same word-boundary specificity the naming lane already carries.</p> <h3 id="no-new-abuse-surface"><a class="header" href="#no-new-abuse-surface">No new abuse surface</a></h3> <p>The prose lane reuses the same provenance-gated entries the naming lane masks with: an entry must hold a letter, may not launder a flag-tier tell, and a tracker reference must carry a URL. So the prose lane grants no muting power the naming lane lacked. The density gate divides the weighted tell count by the sentence count, so masking a phrase removes only its own weight from the numerator and cannot inflate the denominator to push other, undeclared tells under the threshold. A weak-agent run confirmed this reading: handed honest options, including holding for a separate stricter allowlist, the model judged the reuse adequately bounded on the no-new-power argument.</p> <h3 id="the-readme-reconciliation"><a class="header" href="#the-readme-reconciliation">The README reconciliation</a></h3> <p>The masked-modes wording adds <code>--prose</code> and <code>--docs</code>, so the "in any mode" claim becomes true rather than narrowed to the naming modes.</p> <h3 id="no-spine-change"><a class="header" href="#no-spine-change">No spine change</a></h3> <p>Extending the mask makes the existing doctrine, that a legitimate tell-shaped token stays in the per-project LEXICON, hold for the prose lane. The doctrine is met, not changed, so host-template carries no new UPGRADING entry; an adopter reads the corrected behaviour on the next host-lint bump.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-4"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-4">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="settle-by-data"><a class="header" href="#settle-by-data">Settle the approach with data</a></h3> <p>Settle the lane-consistency reading, the surgical word-boundary semantics, and the abuse question with a recorded Qwen-3.5-4B run, in <code>gather-data.md</code>, run direct against rope with a real system prompt and non-contaminated options.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="extend-mask"><a class="header" href="#extend-mask">Extend the mask to the prose lane</a></h3> <p>Thread the sanctioned phrases into <code>scan_prose_text</code> and <code>run_docs</code>, mask the document before the per-tell scan and the density score, and report each surviving tell from the original text. Regression tests pin the behaviour: a declared phrase clears the trope within the phrase, a standalone occurrence of the same word still flags, an empty allowlist leaves the scan unchanged, and the density score drops by the masked phrase alone.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #settle-by-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="readme-claim"><a class="header" href="#readme-claim">Reconcile the README claim</a></h3> <p>Add <code>--prose</code> and <code>--docs</code> to the masked-modes wording so the "in any mode" claim holds. host-lint prose stays clean.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #extend-mask</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-close"><a class="header" href="#release-and-close">Release, re-pin, and close</a></h3> <p>Release host-lint with the change class that removes findings, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, bump the CI install revisions, and close issue #16. The released binary gates green and the whole suite is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #readme-claim</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-4"><a class="header" href="#risks-4">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The mask now feeds the density engine, so a mis-scoped entry could hide a real trope. The provenance guards and the per-occurrence word boundary keep the mask specific, and the sentence-count denominator stops a mask from diluting the other tells.</li> <li>The change removes prose findings when a phrase is declared, so it ships under the removes-findings change class, and an adopter reads the masked-modes wording to learn the new reach.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-6"><a class="header" href="#status-6">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lint v0.10.1 (2026-06-25; <code>0c2bfc3</code>, artifact <code>941126c9</code>). The <code>--prose</code> and <code>--docs</code> lanes consult the per-repo LEXICON: <code>scan_prose_text</code> masks a declared phrase with the naming lane's <code>mask_allowed</code> before both the per-tell scan and the document density score, so a declared <code>rehost harness</code> clears the trope on <code>harness</code> within that phrase and a standalone occurrence still flags. The README masked-modes wording adds <code>--prose</code> and <code>--docs</code>. Validated at the Qwen-3.5-4B bar (<code>gather-data.md</code>): lane consistency, the surgical word boundary, and the abuse-bounding confirmed, with the dissent option available and not chosen. The first abuse-guard probe was contaminated by an option asserting a multi-word rule the tool does not enforce; it was recorded and discarded, then re-run with honest options. <code>call/0029</code> records the decision. No spine change, since the doctrine is met rather than changed. The <code>src/lib.rs</code> edit staled two Kani-backed obligations (<code>DetectInternalCodeAsName</code>), which host-lint's own obligations lane caught after the first tag; the feature shipped as v0.10.0, then v0.10.1 re-derived the obligation digests through host-prove and is the pinned release. host-lint issue #16 is closed. The whole suite is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-the-prose-lane-lexicon-approach-at-the-weak-agent-bar"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-the-prose-lane-lexicon-approach-at-the-weak-agent-bar">gather-data: the prose-lane LEXICON approach at the weak-agent bar</a></h1> <p>The <code>#settle-by-data</code> task. The questions were whether extending the LEXICON mask to the prose lane is the least-surprising reading, whether the mask should be surgical at the word boundary, and whether reusing the allowlist opens an abuse surface. The run went direct against the rope HTTPS endpoint (the OpenAI-compatible front-end to Fen, <code>qwen3.5-4b</code>) with a real system prompt, the sampler at the Qwen thinking-precise values (<code>temperature</code> 0.6, <code>top_p</code> 0.95, <code>top_k</code> 20, <code>min_p</code> 0). The model thinks before it answers, so the judgement is read off the converged reasoning, the way Fen is always read.</p> <h2 id="the-system-prompt"><a class="header" href="#the-system-prompt">The system prompt</a></h2> <p>A senior-engineer reviewer of host-lint, asked to judge a self-contained multiple-choice design question and answer with the single best option and a short justification.</p> <h2 id="probe-one-lane-consistency"><a class="header" href="#probe-one-lane-consistency">Probe one: lane consistency</a></h2> <p>Given that the naming lane masks a LEXICON phrase and the prose lane does not, what is the least-surprising prose-lane behaviour for a declared <code>rehost harness</code>? The model chose <strong>(A)</strong>, the prose lane consults the same LEXICON, and rejected the blanket-mute option as over-permissive and inconsistent with the naming lane's scope logic. So the model expects both lane consistency and the surgical word boundary.</p> <h2 id="probe-two-the-abuse-guard-and-a-contamination-correction"><a class="header" href="#probe-two-the-abuse-guard-and-a-contamination-correction">Probe two: the abuse guard, and a contamination correction</a></h2> <p>The first abuse-guard probe offered an option that asserted LEXICON requires multi-word phrases. The real <code>validate_lexicon_entry</code> enforces no such rule: a single legitimate word is a valid entry, and the guards are a letter requirement, a refusal to launder a flag-tier tell, and a URL for a tracker reference. The model accepted that false premise, so that pass was discarded as contaminated.</p> <p>The re-run offered honest options: two sound "adequately bounded" rationales (the sentence-count denominator; the provenance guards plus naming-lane symmetry) and one genuine dissent (hold for a separate stricter prose allowlist). With the dissent on the table, the model chose <strong>(b)</strong>: the prose lane reuses the same provenance-gated entries the naming lane already masks with, so it grants no muting power the naming lane lacked. It reconfirmed the surgical semantics, <strong>(ii)</strong>: after the declared phrase is blanked, only a standalone occurrence of the word still flags.</p> <h2 id="verdict-3"><a class="header" href="#verdict-3">Verdict</a></h2> <p>The direction and the surgical semantics are confirmed, and the dissent option was available and not chosen. The abuse concern is real and bounded by two facts the model and the code agree on: the provenance guards make a declaration a visible, enumerated act, and the density denominator is the sentence count, so a mask removes only its own weight and cannot dilute the other tells. The recorded rope responses are the evidence trail.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0045-the-embedded-prose-engine-catches-up"><a class="header" href="#plan0045-the-embedded-prose-engine-catches-up">plan/0045: The embedded prose engine catches up</a></h1> <p>plan/0044 taught host-lint's prose lane to honor the per-repo LEXICON, so a legitimate domain noun a project declares stops reading as an ai-diction trope. host-lifecycle runs that same lane in-process for its verify-phase prose recheck (<code>host-lifecycle prose</code>, the <code>--docs</code> engine via the linked <code>host_lint</code> crate), so the gate needs no host-lint on PATH. But host-lifecycle embedded the crate at an older revision, before the mask existed, so the recheck ignored the LEXICON the standalone binary already honored. connollydavid/host-lifecycle#2 reports the divergence. This milestone shares host-lint's docs engine into its library, so the binary and the embedded copy run one engine and cannot drift, then bumps host-lifecycle onto it.</p> <h2 id="problem-5"><a class="header" href="#problem-5">Problem</a></h2> <p>The prose mask (<code>mask_allowed</code>) lived in the <code>host_lint</code> library and was current. But host-lifecycle's <code>prose_audit</code> reimplemented the <code>--docs</code> walk and called <code>scan_prose_text</code> at the crate revision it pinned, host-lint v0.8.1, whose signature had no allowlist parameter. The embedded engine could not consult the LEXICON even in principle: it received no phrases to mask. Because <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> exits non-zero on any warning, an adopter with a legitimate flagged domain noun on a governed surface, the case the issue names, had a permanently failing verify recheck and no remedy, since the sanctioned escape (declare the phrase in LEXICON) was the one path the embedded engine never took.</p> <p>The loader (<code>load_lexicon</code>) and the walk (<code>run_docs</code>) lived in host-lint's binary; the library held only the parsing primitives, so host-lifecycle had no shared entry point to call. The reimplemented walk was itself the drift surface: even with the crate bumped, an embedder that re-derives the loader and walk by hand stays one edit away from lagging again.</p> <h2 id="decision-operator-2"><a class="header" href="#decision-operator-2">Decision (operator)</a></h2> <p>Share the engine into the library, rather than replicate the loader inside host-lifecycle. <code>Lexicon</code>, <code>load_lexicon</code>, and <code>run_docs</code> move into the <code>host_lint</code> library as public functions; host-lint's binary calls them; host-lifecycle calls the same functions. The embedded prose recheck becomes a thin call into the shared engine, so a future host-lint change to the loader, the walk, or the mask reaches the embedder on the next bump with no hand re-derivation. The operator chose the shared-library path over the one-release replicate-in-host-lifecycle path precisely because the bug is an instance of embedded-engine drift, and the fix should close the class, not the instance.</p> <h2 id="the-design-2"><a class="header" href="#the-design-2">The design</a></h2> <h3 id="loader-and-walk-in-the-shared-library"><a class="header" href="#loader-and-walk-in-the-shared-library">Loader and walk in the shared library</a></h3> <p><code>Lexicon</code> plus <code>load_lexicon</code> and <code>run_docs</code> become public in <code>host_lint</code>'s lib. <code>run_docs</code> returns a <code>Result</code> instead of exiting the process, so host-lint's binary prints the error and exits while an in-process embedder surfaces it as it chooses. host-lint's CLI behavior is unchanged, confirmed against the fixture: a LEXICON-declared phrase clears the trope (exit 0), an undeclared occurrence still warns (exit 3), and the git-failure message and exit code are byte-identical to before.</p> <h3 id="host-lifecycle-calls-the-engine"><a class="header" href="#host-lifecycle-calls-the-engine">host-lifecycle calls the engine</a></h3> <p><code>prose_audit</code> shrinks to <code>host_lint::load_lexicon(root).phrases_lc</code> plus <code>host_lint::run_docs(root, &allow, &ignore)</code>. The reimplemented walk is gone, so the walk, the loader, and the mask are all shared with the standalone binary. A regression test pins the fix: a declared phrase clears the trope in the in-process audit, and an undeclared occurrence of the same word still warns.</p> <h3 id="the-moved-dependency-needs-a-fresh-bundle"><a class="header" href="#the-moved-dependency-needs-a-fresh-bundle">The moved dependency needs a fresh bundle</a></h3> <p>host-lifecycle pins host-lint by git revision and builds offline from a hash-pinned vendor bundle (plan/0032). Bumping the revision is the first dependency move since the bundle was cut, so the shared bundle is regenerated as <code>vendor-v2</code>, covering host-lint v0.10.2's source, and host-lifecycle's <code>deps-bundle</code> is re-pinned in <code>.host-software</code> and <code>deps-bundle.lock</code>. host-lint stays on <code>vendor-v1</code>: its own closure is unchanged, and its build ignores the host-lint-crate entry the bundle also carries.</p> <h3 id="no-spine-change-1"><a class="header" href="#no-spine-change-1">No spine change</a></h3> <p>The doctrine, that a legitimate tell-shaped token stays in the per-project LEXICON for both lanes, is met rather than changed, so host-template carries no new UPGRADING entry; an adopter reads the corrected behaviour on the next host-lifecycle bump. The meta-repo prose CI pins (host-template, host) move to v0.30.1 so their own prose gate runs the same engine.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-5"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-5">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="reproduce"><a class="header" href="#reproduce">Diagnose and reproduce</a></h3> <p>Build a minimal fixture (a tracked doc whose ai-diction noun is declared in a sibling LEXICON) and confirm the divergence: standalone <code>host-lint --docs</code> masks the phrase and exits clean, while <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> warns and exits non-zero on the same repo. Trace the root cause to the embedded crate revision whose <code>scan_prose_text</code> takes no allowlist.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="share-engine"><a class="header" href="#share-engine">Share host-lint's docs engine into the library</a></h3> <p>Move <code>Lexicon</code>, <code>load_lexicon</code>, and <code>run_docs</code> into the <code>host_lint</code> library as public items; have the binary call them; make <code>run_docs</code> return a <code>Result</code>. Regression tests pin the loader and the masked walk. host-lint's CLI behavior stays identical, and clippy is clean.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #reproduce</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="consume-engine"><a class="header" href="#consume-engine">host-lifecycle consumes the shared engine</a></h3> <p>Bump the host-lint dependency to v0.10.2, rewrite <code>prose_audit</code> to call the shared loader and walk, and add the LEXICON-masking regression test. The rebuilt binary clears the fixture: a declared phrase exits clean, an undeclared occurrence still warns.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #share-engine</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="vendor-v2"><a class="header" href="#vendor-v2">Regenerate the vendor bundle for the moved dependency</a></h3> <p>Produce <code>vendor-v2</code> from host-lint's manifest synced with host-lifecycle's, covering host-lint v0.10.2's source, publish it, and re-pin host-lifecycle's <code>deps-bundle</code>. The offline <code>--network none</code> release build reproduces the canonical hash.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #consume-engine</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-close"><a class="header" href="#release-and-close">Re-pin, bump CI, and close</a></h3> <p>Release host-lint v0.10.2 and host-lifecycle v0.30.1, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, bump the five CI install revisions, record the release receipts, and close the issue. <code>software --check</code> is clean and the whole suite is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #vendor-v2</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-5"><a class="header" href="#risks-5">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The loader and walk now live in the library, so an embedder and the CLI share one code path. A bug in <code>run_docs</code> would reach both, but a single shared path is the point: it removes the drift this milestone fixes, and the path is covered by tests on both sides.</li> <li>Regenerating the vendor bundle is the documented cost of moving a pinned dependency. The new bundle is hash-pinned and its offline build is verified by the release gate, so a wrong bundle fails the gate rather than shipping.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-7"><a class="header" href="#status-7">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lint v0.10.3 (<code>63348a6</code>, artifact <code>753ac4f6</code>) and host-lifecycle v0.30.1 (<code>46d481c</code>, artifact <code>23c27bff</code>, on <code>vendor-v2</code> sha <code>4e49536b</code>); host-lifecycle embeds the host-lint library at v0.10.2 (<code>5a9d2c5</code>), which is engine-identical to v0.10.3. host-lint's <code>Lexicon</code>, <code>load_lexicon</code>, and <code>run_docs</code> are public library items; its binary and host-lifecycle's <code>prose_audit</code> call the same engine, so the embedded prose recheck cannot lag a future host-lint change. The fixture confirms the fix end to end: with the LEXICON the recheck exits clean, without it the trope still warns. host-lint's standalone <code>--docs</code> behavior is byte-identical across the refactor. The shared bundle was regenerated as <code>vendor-v2</code> so the offline release build sees host-lint v0.10.2; host-lint stays on <code>vendor-v1</code>. The five CI install pins (agentic-host reproducible-build and mdbook, host-template and host prose) move to v0.30.1. No spine change, since the doctrine is met rather than changed. <code>software --check</code> and the fixture are green; connollydavid/host-lifecycle#2 is closed.</p> <p>host-lint was first tagged v0.10.2 at <code>5a9d2c5</code>, but the <code>src/lib.rs</code> edit staled its two kani obligation digests (<code>DetectInternalCodeAsName</code>), so that tag's CI failed the obligations staleness lint (the kani proofs and all six binaries passed). The digests were re-derived by fingerprinting the new source (<code>git hash-object src/lib.rs</code> into <code>host-lint.obligations.digests</code>), which is artifact-preserving because the ledger is not compiled, and promoted into a clean v0.10.3 tag, the pinned release. v0.10.2 stays a superseded tag. host-lifecycle keeps embedding the host-lint library at <code>5a9d2c5</code> (engine-identical to v0.10.3), so no vendor regeneration or host-lifecycle re-release was needed.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0046-the-generated-book-moves-to-mdbook-freeing-docs"><a class="header" href="#plan0046-the-generated-book-moves-to-mdbook-freeing-docs">plan/0046: the generated book moves to mdBook/, freeing docs/</a></h1> <p><code>host-lifecycle book</code> generates a browsable mdBook site from a project's rooms. It writes the generated mdBook source into a top-level <code>docs/</code> folder and clears that folder on every run. connollydavid/host-lifecycle#3 reported this as a destructive <code>book</code> bug. The real defect is narrower and deeper: <code>docs/</code> is a generic name, and a project brought under the methodology that already keeps hand-written documentation in <code>docs/</code> loses it on the first <code>book</code> run. This milestone moves the generated source and built HTML under a tool-named <code>mdBook/</code> folder, which frees <code>docs/</code> for authored content and removes the collision at its root.</p> <h2 id="problem-6"><a class="header" href="#problem-6">Problem</a></h2> <p>The generator reserves <code>docs/</code> as its output and wipes it each run (<code>fs::remove_dir_all</code>). For a greenfield project adopted from the template that is safe, because <code>docs/</code> is gitignored generated output from the start. For a migration it is a footgun: <code>classify</code> and <code>adopt</code> never inspect a pre-existing <code>docs/</code>, so a project that keeps a tracked research record or hand-written guides in <code>docs/</code> has them deleted the first time the doc site is generated. The reporter's suggested fixes (stop defaulting to <code>docs/</code>, make the source dir configurable) point at the generator, but the underlying choice is a location decision: where should generated output live so it never collides with the one folder name projects most commonly use for authored docs.</p> <h2 id="decision-settled-with-data-and-the-cast"><a class="header" href="#decision-settled-with-data-and-the-cast">Decision, settled with data and the cast</a></h2> <p>The generated mdBook source and built HTML move under one gitignored top-level folder named <code>mdBook/</code>: <code>mdBook/src/</code> for the generated source and <code>mdBook/out/</code> for the built HTML. The config <code>book.toml</code> stays at the repository root, so mdBook is still invoked exactly as before (<code>mdbook build</code> from the root, no arguments). <code>docs/</code> is freed for authored content.</p> <pre><code class="language-toml"># book.toml (repo root, gitignored) [book] src = "mdBook/src" [build] build-dir = "mdBook/out" </code></pre> <p>This holds to mdBook's own conventions. <code>src</code> and <code>build-dir</code> are first-class config keys that accept any relative path, and the generator already set a non-default <code>src = "docs"</code>, so re-pointing them is ordinary use of the tool rather than a fight with it. The folder name <code>mdBook/</code> makes it self-evident that the tree is the tool's generated workspace, so a migrating project never mistakes it for authored content.</p> <h3 id="the-data-fen-the-real-qwen35-4b"><a class="header" href="#the-data-fen-the-real-qwen35-4b">The data (Fen, the real qwen3.5-4b)</a></h3> <p>The decision was settled against the project's weak-agent persona, driven directly through the rope API with a true system prompt. A first probe fed the model mdBook's own idiom and it preferred the standard source-folder name 4 of 5 times. A fair head-to-head that also stated the ensemble's conventions favoured consolidating everything under one folder. The deciding fact is that mdBook's <code>src</code> is configurable, so the consolidated layout keeps the root-level invocation while tucking the generated trees under <code>mdBook/</code>. The locked layout then passed an acceptance test: handed the same scenario of a project with hand-written <code>docs/</code>, the real model judged <code>docs/</code> safe under the new layout 5 of 5 times, and judged the old <code>docs/</code>-as-output layout dangerous 3 of 3 times. The weak agent perceives the footgun, and perceives it gone.</p> <h3 id="the-cast"><a class="header" href="#the-cast">The cast</a></h3> <p>Consulting the five personas confirmed the layout and added four requirements for shipping it. Mara and Wren are served by a loud generated-versus-authored boundary that even a small model reads correctly. Fen requires the migration to stay a single tool-driven command rather than a hand-edit. Bly, the adopter several revisions behind, requires the change to apply as an independent ledger entry and the cleanup of the old generated trees to fail safe, so a skipped step re-lists rather than hides. Orin, the maintainer, requires the ledger entry to be version-gated on the new host-lifecycle and safe when followed literally on old infrastructure.</p> <h2 id="the-design-3"><a class="header" href="#the-design-3">The design</a></h2> <h3 id="the-generator"><a class="header" href="#the-generator">The generator</a></h3> <p><code>write_book</code> writes the SUMMARY and room pages into <code>mdBook/src/</code> instead of <code>docs/</code>. <code>book_toml</code> sets <code>src = "mdBook/src"</code> and adds <code>build-dir = "mdBook/out"</code>. The user-facing strings and the tests follow the rename. The build still runs from the root.</p> <h3 id="the-spine-and-the-gitignore"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-and-the-gitignore">The spine and the gitignore</a></h3> <p>The generated trees are gitignored as one entry. <code>host-template/.gitignore</code> and agentic-host's <code>.gitignore</code> carry <code>/book.toml</code> and <code>/mdBook/</code> in place of <code>/docs/</code> and <code>/book/</code>. The doctrine in <code>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</code> states that generated output lives under <code>mdBook/</code> and that <code>docs/</code> is available for authored content, which retires the earlier reserved-<code>docs/</code> reading. <code>call/0014</code> is already superseded by the spine, so this is a spine change propagated through <code>UPGRADING</code>, not a new project decision.</p> <h3 id="the-adopter-ledger"><a class="header" href="#the-adopter-ledger">The adopter ledger</a></h3> <p><code>UPGRADING.md</code> gains one entry that is independent (it needs no earlier unrelated migration), declares <code>requires</code> the new host-lifecycle version (an adopter on the old binary still writes <code>docs/</code>), and carries a machine-checkable verify. The migration swaps the two gitignore lines and removes the stale generated <code>docs/</code> and <code>book/</code> trees. An adopter records it with <code>host-lifecycle upgrade --record</code>, so the step is tool-carried and the stamp is never hand-edited.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-6"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-6">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="decide-layout"><a class="header" href="#decide-layout">Decide the layout with data and the cast</a></h3> <p>Settle where generated output lives, against the real qwen3.5-4b (rope, true system prompt) and the five personas. The acceptance test confirms the weak agent sees <code>docs/</code> safe under the new layout and endangered under the old one.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="book-generator"><a class="header" href="#book-generator">Move the book generator to mdBook/</a></h3> <p>Re-point <code>write_book</code> and <code>book_toml</code> to <code>mdBook/src</code> and <code>mdBook/out</code>, and follow the rename through the user-facing strings and the tests. The build runs from the root unchanged.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #decide-layout</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-and-ledger"><a class="header" href="#spine-and-ledger">Update the spine and the adopter ledger</a></h3> <p>Update <code>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</code> doctrine and <code>.gitignore</code>, and add the independent, version-gated, fail-safe <code>UPGRADING</code> entry with a machine-checkable verify.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #book-generator</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="repoint-agentic-host"><a class="header" href="#repoint-agentic-host">Re-point agentic-host and clean the old trees</a></h3> <p>Swap agentic-host's <code>.gitignore</code> to <code>/book.toml</code> and <code>/mdBook/</code>, point <code>mdbook.yml</code> publishing at <code>mdBook/out</code>, remove the stale generated <code>docs/</code> and <code>book/</code>, and regenerate the site locally to confirm it builds.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #book-generator</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-verify"><a class="header" href="#release-and-verify">Release, adopt, and verify the whole suite</a></h3> <p>Release host-lifecycle, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the release receipt, bump the CI install pins, adopt the new spine revision on agentic-host through the ledger, and confirm the whole suite is green and that the Site workflow serves <code>mdBook/out</code>.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #spine-and-ledger</li> <li>depends: #repoint-agentic-host</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-6"><a class="header" href="#risks-6">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>An adopter that runs the new host-lifecycle without applying the gitignore swap would see the old generated <code>docs/</code> and <code>book/</code> linger as untracked clutter. The ledger entry handles the swap and the cleanup, and is version-gated so it pairs with the binary that changes the output.</li> <li>A migrating project that already tracks content in <code>docs/</code> is now safe by construction, since the generator no longer writes there. The classify-time guard discussed under #3 is no longer needed, because the reserved name is gone.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-8"><a class="header" href="#status-8">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lifecycle v0.30.2 (<code>f2b4607</code>, artifact <code>3a9e59ce</code>). <code>host-lifecycle book</code> writes its generated source to <code>mdBook/src/</code> and the built HTML to <code>mdBook/out/</code>, with <code>book.toml</code> kept at the repo root, so <code>mdbook build</code> runs from the root unchanged. <code>docs/</code> is freed for authored content, which closes connollydavid/host-lifecycle#3 at its root: the generator no longer reserves <code>docs/</code>, so the migration footgun cannot recur and the classify-time guard is unnecessary. The spine carries the doctrine and the gitignore (host-template <code>e068828</code>) plus an independent, version-gated, fail-safe <code>UPGRADING</code> entry (<code>e068828</code>, requires host-lifecycle v0.30.2); agentic-host adopted it through the ledger (<code>upgrade --record e068828</code>). The decision was settled against the real qwen3.5-4b, which read <code>docs/</code> as out of harm's way under the new layout in every run and reproduced the footgun on the old layout in every run, and the five cast personas confirmed it. A regression test pins the generator to <code>mdBook/src</code> and proves an authored <code>docs/</code> is left intact. <code>software --check</code> is clean and the Site workflow serves <code>mdBook/out</code>. The whole suite is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0047-the-prose-lane-audits-the-authored-working-tree-not-just-the-tracked-subset"><a class="header" href="#plan0047-the-prose-lane-audits-the-authored-working-tree-not-just-the-tracked-subset">plan/0047: the prose lane audits the authored working tree, not just the tracked subset</a></h1> <p><code>host-lint --docs</code> and the <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> recheck that embeds it audit authored markdown by walking <code>git ls-files</code>, which lists tracked and staged files only. A brand-new authored doc that has not been staged yet is silently skipped, so a pre-commit <code>prose</code> run reads clean over it and then the same doc fails the <code>verify</code> recheck once committed, with no content change. connollydavid/host-lint#17 reports it. This milestone widens the walk to the authored working tree, so a new doc is audited before it is staged and a clean result is never silently partial.</p> <h2 id="problem-and-investigation"><a class="header" href="#problem-and-investigation">Problem and investigation</a></h2> <p>The skip is real and partly intentional. The walk uses <code>git ls-files</code> precisely to exclude gitignored output, vendored deps, un-materialized worktrees, and submodules, which is why the prose lane never trips over generated content. Skipping an untracked authored file is a side effect of that choice. Two facts narrow the gap: staging closes it, because <code>git ls-files</code> includes staged files (a <code>git add</code> makes the new doc scanned), so the window is only the moment between creating a file and staging it; and the workaround (stage before checking) is documented. So the question is whether a pre-commit check should cover the unstaged case at all.</p> <p>The cast answers it. A <code>prose: clean</code> that silently skipped a new file is the record that <strong>overstates completeness</strong> Bly is built to catch, the <strong>silent trap</strong> Fen fumbles into (clean pre-commit, HAZARD post-commit), and the instruction that <strong>fails unsafe when followed literally</strong> that Orin guards against. By the methodology's own fail-safe principles a silent partial-clean is a defect, even where the scan scope is intentional. The operator chose to widen the walk.</p> <h2 id="the-design-4"><a class="header" href="#the-design-4">The design</a></h2> <p><code>run_docs</code>, the shared engine (host-lint library, used by both <code>host-lint --docs</code> and <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> since plan/0045), walks two sets: <code>git ls-files</code> (tracked and staged) and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard</code> (untracked files git would offer to add). The two sets are disjoint, so no dedup is needed. <code>--exclude-standard</code> keeps gitignored output, vendored deps, and un-materialized worktrees out, exactly as the bare <code>git ls-files</code> walk did, so only authored markdown that is or is about to be in the repo is audited. The per-file logic is unchanged: <code>.md</code> only, <code>.host-lintignore</code> honored, symlinks skipped.</p> <p>The walk scope is a host-lint implementation detail, not spine doctrine (the spine never states the mechanism), so this milestone needs no doctrine change and no adopter <code>UPGRADING</code> entry. A fresh CI checkout carries no untracked authored files, so CI behaviour is unchanged; only a local pre-commit or working-tree run gains the new coverage.</p> <h2 id="validation"><a class="header" href="#validation">Validation</a></h2> <p>Confirmed end to end before release. The <code>#17</code> reproduction now flags an untracked authored doc while the gitignored generated tree stays excluded. On agentic-host, <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard</code> finds no markdown (the generated <code>mdBook/</code> and <code>book.toml</code> are gitignored), so <code>--docs</code> stays clean and the verify recheck is unchanged. A unit test pins all three cases: a tracked doc scanned, a new untracked doc scanned, a gitignored generated doc excluded.</p> <p>The real qwen3.5-4b judged the fix at the weak-agent bar (rope, true system prompt): handed a new unstaged doc with an error, it said the new working-tree walk catches it in every run, and the old tracked-only walk misses it in every run. The five cast personas confirmed the change serves them.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-7"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-7">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="investigate-decide"><a class="header" href="#investigate-decide">Investigate and decide</a></h3> <p>Reproduce the skip, confirm it is intentional and that staging closes it, and weigh fix against the documented workaround through the cast. Operator chose to widen the walk.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="scan-working-tree"><a class="header" href="#scan-working-tree">Scan the authored working tree</a></h3> <p>Widen <code>run_docs</code> to <code>git ls-files</code> plus <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard</code>; the per-file logic and the gitignore exclusion are unchanged. A unit test pins the three cases.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #investigate-decide</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="validate"><a class="header" href="#validate">Validate with Fen and the cast</a></h3> <p>Confirm the fix end to end (untracked caught, generated excluded, CI unchanged) and at the weak-agent bar with the real qwen3.5-4b, and consult the cast.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #scan-working-tree</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-cascade"><a class="header" href="#release-cascade">Release host-lint and cascade host-lifecycle</a></h3> <p>Re-derive the kani digests before tagging (the <code>src/lib.rs</code> edit stales them), release host-lint, bump host-lifecycle's host-lint dependency, regenerate the offline bundle as <code>vendor-v3</code>, release host-lifecycle, and re-pin <code>.host-software</code>.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #validate</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="close-and-verify"><a class="header" href="#close-and-verify">Re-pin, close, and verify the suite</a></h3> <p>Bump the CI install pins, record the receipts, close the issue, and confirm the whole suite is green.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #release-cascade</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-7"><a class="header" href="#risks-7">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The walk now reads untracked authored markdown, so a working-tree draft a developer has not chosen to commit is audited. That is the intended coverage, and a genuine scratch file is gitignored, which the <code>--exclude-standard</code> filter excludes.</li> <li>The change is in the shared <code>run_docs</code>, so it cascades through a host-lint release and a host-lifecycle release with a regenerated bundle, the same shape as plan/0045.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-9"><a class="header" href="#status-9">Status</a></h2> <p>complete, released as host-lint v0.10.4 (<code>ce683be</code>, artifact <code>a9ef0865</code>) and host-lifecycle v0.30.3 (<code>0de2843</code>, artifact <code>cf59cc16</code>, on <code>vendor-v3</code> sha <code>817a71d9</code>). The shared <code>run_docs</code> walks <code>git ls-files</code> (tracked and staged) plus <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard</code> (untracked non-ignored), so a new authored doc is audited before it is staged and a pre-commit run is never silently clean over a file it skipped. <code>--exclude-standard</code> holds generated output, vendored deps, and un-materialized worktrees out, so a fresh CI checkout is unchanged. connollydavid/host-lint#17 is closed. Validated end to end and at the weak-agent bar: the real qwen3.5-4b judged the new walk catches a new unstaged doc in every run and judged the old walk misses it in every run; a unit test pins a tracked doc scanned, an untracked doc scanned, a gitignored generated doc excluded; on agentic-host the new walk finds no untracked markdown, so the verify recheck stays clean. No spine change, since the walk scope is a host-lint implementation detail rather than spine doctrine. The <code>src/lib.rs</code> edit staled the kani obligation digests, which were re-derived before tagging (the plan/0045 lesson applied first try, so the v0.10.4 tag is green). <code>software --check</code> is clean and the whole suite is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0048-a-declared-rungs-re-deriver-must-be-runnable-and-its-digest-earned"><a class="header" href="#plan0048-a-declared-rungs-re-deriver-must-be-runnable-and-its-digest-earned">plan/0048: a declared rung's re-deriver must be runnable, and its digest earned</a></h1> <p>A host-lint <code>src/lib.rs</code> change stales the kani obligation digests, and the tag is born red on the obligations staleness lint while the proof itself is fine. This kept recurring, and the standing workaround was to hand-edit the digest ledger. This milestone traces that to its root, which is not a release-tooling decision at all, and fixes it as a methodology migration rather than a patch to one host.</p> <h2 id="how-the-scope-arrived-here"><a class="header" href="#how-the-scope-arrived-here">How the scope arrived here</a></h2> <p>The milestone opened as a release-time guard: should <code>host-lifecycle release</code> block, auto-record, or attest when it finds a stale digest. Driving the real qwen3.5-4b cold (no leading framing) showed the weak agent cannot reason about the underlying soundness, conflating "recompute the fingerprint" with "re-run the proof," so a preference poll on that guard was the wrong instrument. Consulting the cast reframed it: the fingerprint is a proxy for "is the proof current," and the born-red exists because the proxy is refreshed by hand, no longer tied to the proof it claims to track. The principle the cast settled on: a cheap proxy may stand in for an expensive check only while it stays mechanically coupled to it, refreshed by the thing that runs the real proof and by nothing else.</p> <p>Asking why the coupled path was abandoned uncovered the actual defect. The sanctioned <code>host-lifecycle obligations <spec> --rederive --record-digests</code> re-runs the proof through host-prove and records the digest only on a pass. It had been recorded in memory as failing with <code>ENOENT</code> on the <code>/mnt/c</code> WSL mount, a host-prove invocation gap blamed on the filesystem. That diagnosis was wrong. The proof runs fine on <code>/mnt/c</code>.
