The real causes were that <strong>host-prove was never installed on PATH</strong> by the local setup (host-lint's CI installs it; the fresh-clone discipline never did), and that it was handed <code>src/</code> rather than the crate root. Once host-prove is installed and pointed at the crate root, the full chain re-derives both rungs and exits clean, locally, on <code>/mnt/c</code>.</p> <p>So the re-deriver was referenced and materialized, its CI lane present, and yet not runnable on the box that needed it. It was available but never discharged, the very <code>call/0018</code> distinction, turned on the re-deriver itself. Nobody noticed for two weeks because the kani proof is verified by another path (CI runs <code>cargo kani</code> directly and re-derives there), so the local re-derivation's brokenness was invisible, and a <code>command not found</code> reads as a filesystem fault, so it was filed as a WSL problem and never re-opened.</p> <h2 id="the-decision-express-it-as-a-migration-not-a-host-fix"><a class="header" href="#the-decision-express-it-as-a-migration-not-a-host-fix">The decision: express it as a migration, not a host fix</a></h2> <p>A one-off <code>cargo install host-prove</code> in this host's setup would re-bury the gap for the next adopter. The fix generalizes an invariant the spine already has. The spine enforces "declare a deeper rung, oblige its lane": <code>software --check</code> HAZARDs a <code>kani:</code>/<code>apalache:</code>/<code>tlaps:</code> obligation with no matching CI workflow. But "the workflow is present in CI config" is weaker than "the re-derivation actually runs," and the gap between them is exactly where this hid. The migration is one clause longer:</p> <blockquote> <p>A declared rung obliges its lane to be runnable, not merely present. Re-derivation that cannot run is not discharged. Available is not present-in-CI is not runnable is not discharged.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="the-validated-design-fen-hard-evidence-non-leading"><a class="header" href="#the-validated-design-fen-hard-evidence-non-leading">The validated design (Fen, hard evidence, non-leading)</a></h2> <p>Two questions were put to the real qwen3.5-4b with neutral framing, after an earlier leading round was discarded.</p> <p>A check that the re-deriver resolves on PATH falls short on its own. Asked cold whether a gate that confirms the tool is on PATH could still pass while the verification does not work, six of eight runs said yes, naming version mismatch, wrong arguments, missing dependencies, and a stand-in executable that returns success. So a PATH probe alone is recognized as too weak even at the weak-agent bar.</p> <p>Asked which check best ensures the claim is real, given the gate must stay cheap, eight of eight runs chose a recorded result showing the proof was run on the current code and passed, over both an on-PATH check and a one-off smoke run. That recorded-pass-on-current-code is the digest ledger earned by a passing re-derivation, with the staleness check guaranteeing it is current. The weak agent reconstructed <code>call/0018</code> from first principles.</p> <p>So the gate does not gain a PATH probe. It gains two coupled things:</p> <ul> <li>A <strong>runnability</strong> check that the re-deriver <strong>executes</strong> (a cheap version probe), not merely resolves, since on-PATH is not works.</li> <li>The digest stays <strong>earned</strong>: recorded only by <code>--rederive --record-digests</code> (now runnable), never hand-edited, so the existing staleness check soundly means a passing re-derivation on the current code.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-fix"><a class="header" href="#the-fix">The fix</a></h2> <h3 id="host-lifecycle"><a class="header" href="#host-lifecycle">host-lifecycle</a></h3> <p><code>software --check</code>, for a materialized component that declares a deeper rung, probes that the rung's re-deriver executes (host-prove runs, the verifier is reachable) and HAZARDs when it cannot, beside the existing "no CI lane" HAZARD. The probe is cheap and never runs the proof; the real re-derivation stays the pluggable <code>call/0018</code> enforcement.</p> <h3 id="host-template-doctrine-and-the-ledger"><a class="header" href="#host-template-doctrine-and-the-ledger">host-template doctrine and the ledger</a></h3> <p>The "Mandatory when used" and <code>call/0018</code> text widens the "obliges its CI lane" rule into "obliges a runnable lane driver," with the available-is-not-runnable-is-not-discharged line and the earn-the-digest rule (discharge through <code>--rederive --record-digests</code>, never a hand edit). One independent, version-gated <code>UPGRADING</code> entry carries it; every adopter who upgrades gets the runnability gate, so the first time their own declared rung is not runnable, the gate says so.</p> <h3 id="agentic-host-adopts-it"><a class="header" href="#agentic-host-adopts-it">agentic-host adopts it</a></h3> <p>Like any adopter: record the ledger entry, install host-prove in the fresh-clone setup and in the CI that runs <code>software --check</code>, and the gate goes green by being runnable. The CLAUDE.md setup line is the project-local instance of the spine rule, not the fix.</p> <h3 id="the-record-is-corrected"><a class="header" href="#the-record-is-corrected">the record is corrected</a></h3> <p>The WSL-ENOENT entries in MEMORY were a misdiagnosis and are struck with a correcting entry: the re-derivation runs on <code>/mnt/c</code>; the causes were host-prove not on PATH and the wrong directory. This stays local, since it is this host's own record, not methodology.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-8"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-8">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="diagnose-audit"><a class="header" href="#diagnose-audit">Diagnose, audit, and decide</a></h3> <p>Reproduce the false ENOENT, prove the local re-derivation runs once host-prove is on PATH and pointed at the crate root, audit the missed install step and the misdiagnosis, and settle the migration shape with the cast.</p> <ul> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="validate-strictness"><a class="header" href="#validate-strictness">Validate the gate strictness with Fen</a></h3> <p>Put the gate check to the real qwen3.5-4b with neutral framing: a PATH probe is insufficient (six of eight), a recorded pass on the current code is best (eight of eight). The gate checks runnability that executes plus an earned, current digest.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #diagnose-audit</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="runnability-gate"><a class="header" href="#runnability-gate">The runnability gate in host-lifecycle</a></h3> <p><code>software --check</code> probes that a declared rung's re-deriver executes and HAZARDs when it cannot. Unit tests cover a declared rung with a runnable driver, with a missing driver, and with no declared rung.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #validate-strictness</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-and-release"><a class="header" href="#spine-and-release">Spine doctrine, ledger, and release</a></h3> <p>Generalize the host-template doctrine and add the independent, version-gated <code>UPGRADING</code> entry. Release host-lifecycle, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, advance the host-template pointer so the entry is PENDING, and correct the memory. The migration is now built and published; adopting it on this host is its own step.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #runnability-gate</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="adopt"><a class="header" href="#adopt">agentic-host adopts the entry</a></h3> <p>On the operator's trigger, "Read and follow https://github.com/connollydavid/host to keep this repository an agentic project," adopt like any project: record the ledger entry, install host-prove in the fresh-clone setup and the CI that runs <code>software --check</code>, bump the CI host-lifecycle pins, and confirm the whole suite is green. The gate goes green by being runnable.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #spine-and-release</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="risks-8"><a class="header" href="#risks-8">Risks</a></h2> <ul> <li>The runnability probe runs in every <code>software --check</code>, including CI, so the CI that runs the gate must install the re-deriver. That install is part of the adoption, and its absence is precisely the HAZARD the migration adds.</li> <li>A probe that the re-deriver executes is stronger than on-PATH but still not a proof that the rung passes; the earned digest and the pluggable re-derivation carry that, as <code>call/0018</code> intends.</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-10"><a class="header" href="#status-10">Status</a></h2> <p>complete. The runnability gate ships in host-lifecycle v0.31.0 (<code>software --check</code> HAZARDs a declared rung whose re-deriver does not execute). The spine doctrine and the version-gated <code>UPGRADING</code> entry <code>6174996</code> ("a re-deriver that runs") are pushed; <code>.host-software</code> is re-pinned to v0.31.0. The memory misdiagnosis is corrected. On the operator's trigger, "Read and follow https://github.com/connollydavid/host to keep this repository an agentic project," agentic-host adopted the entry the case-(c) way: <code>upgrade --record 6174996</code> passed its verify and recorded the applied claim, host-prove is installed in the fresh-clone setup and in the CI that runs <code>software --check</code>, and both CI host-lifecycle pins are at v0.31.0. <code>software --check</code> is green (the gate reports the re-deriver runnable for both declaring components), and the whole suite is green across agentic-host, host-lifecycle, and host-template.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0049-external-reference-corpus"><a class="header" href="#plan0049-external-reference-corpus">plan/0049: external reference corpus</a></h1> <p>This milestone adds a new component, <code>host-reference</code>, that reads external documentation an agentic project depends on but does not author, and normalises it into a token-lean form an agent can interpret in context. The material arrives in many shapes, such as Markdown, HTML, PDF, Office documents, images, structured data, electronic design files, and mechanical CAD. <code>host-reference</code> reads each shape and produces a normalised representation chosen for low token cost and faithful meaning.</p> <p>The milestone is in design. This README records the direction and the open questions; the settled decisions land in <code>call/0030</code> and its siblings once the weak-agent probes and the cast review return. The probe set and its adversarial review live in <code>gather-data.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="why-9"><a class="header" href="#why-9">Why</a></h2> <p>An agentic project already applies rigour to what it produces. The build is reproducible, the authored prose is linted, the specifications are checked. The material it consumes has none of that treatment. External reference knowledge enters an agent's context raw and unpinned. It is heavy in tokens, and nothing records where it came from. The <code>reference</code> memory kind records only a pointer to the content. There is no inbound counterpart to the outbound discipline, and <code>host-reference</code> is that counterpart.</p> <p>The primary goal is in-context interpretation: let an agent understand external material inside its context window at low token cost, and act on it and cite it with a provenance trail. Token reduction is the means; correct interpretation is the end. The impact is measured rather than asserted, since each ingest records the raw token count against the normalised token count, so the saving is a number a reader can check.</p> <h2 id="direction"><a class="header" href="#direction">Direction</a></h2> <p><code>host-reference</code> is a reference compiler with a two-layer model.</p> <ul> <li>The immutable normalised layer holds the normalised corpus, a semantic skeleton, and a content-addressed source map. It is re-derived from the source bytes in a pinned toolchain, so it is reproducible and attestable the same way a binary is.</li> <li>The mutable overlay layer holds annotations, edits, and agent notes. It is collaborative and anchored into the immutable layer by standard selectors, so it survives a re-derivation.</li> </ul> <p>Four properties carry the design:</p> <ul> <li>Semantic normalisation to tokens. Each content kind maps to its token-optimal target, and the semantic structure that aids interpretation (headings, reading order, tables, entities, cross references) is preserved rather than discarded.</li> <li>Deterministic re-derivation and attestation. The immutable layer is a reproducible artifact that <code>software --check</code> and host-prove verify.</li> <li>Bidirectional provenance and editing. The source map resolves both directions, round-trip fidelity is a declared per-kind property, an editable view writes back where a well-behaved lens exists, and a hard-to-edit kind such as PDF carries edits in a standard sidecar rather than a mutated original.</li> <li>Tiered, range-addressable views. A cheap skeleton is always resident; a full slice is fetched on demand by page range, section, offset, or token budget, so a large document costs only the slice a task needs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="format-coverage"><a class="header" href="#format-coverage">Format coverage</a></h2> <p>The specification is closed over the superset of content kinds; the build lands one kind at a time, each with a conformance fixture that re-derives byte for byte. The modality families are prose, structured data, office documents, fixed-layout documents, raster images, vector graphics, electronic mail, electronic design, engineering geometry, and audio-visual media. Each family holds several kinds. Prose covers Markdown and HTML and the documentation markups, the TeX family and reStructuredText and AsciiDoc and Org-mode among them, along with RTF and EPUB and the manual page. Structured data covers JSON and CSV and YAML and XML, the config and tabular kinds (TOML, the INI family, JSON Lines, the calendar and contact kinds, the Jupyter notebook), and the columnar Parquet and Arrow. Electronic design covers the SPICE netlist alongside KiCad and Gerber and Eagle. Engineering geometry covers mechanical CAD and the 3D-printing kinds (mesh, the container kinds, the toolpath kind, and the parametric source kind).</p> <p>Many kinds share a reader, so the breadth collapses to a small set of mechanisms: a zip reader for the Office and EPUB and 3D-printing containers, a compound-file reader for legacy Office and Outlook mail, an XML reader for vector graphics and several design kinds, fixed-layout extraction, optical character recognition, columnar decoding, media-container metadata, and the engineering parsers.</p> <p>Audio-visual media follows the recognition split of <code>call/0030</code>. The attested layer holds what re-derives deterministically, the container metadata such as duration and codec and stream layout. The transcript and the description are machine-learning output, so they live in the overlay through the provider-agnostic adapter, the same way the text inside an image does. The columnar kinds re-derive deterministically and stay in the attested layer, since a schema and its statistics are a parse rather than an inference.</p> <p>The component's remit is external reference material, not code. Source code and the interface and schema definition kinds, an API description or a protocol schema, are software; they belong to the <em>Where</em> room and the <code>host-*</code> tooling rather than to a reference reader, and they are out of scope here. Archives are out of scope as well, since a container of arbitrary files is a packaging concern rather than a content kind. The pluggable model of <code>call/0033</code> carries the superset as the menu, and an adopting project enables the subset its corpus needs.</p> <h2 id="decisions"><a class="header" href="#decisions">Decisions</a></h2> <p>The design is settled across four records.</p> <ul> <li><code>call/0030</code> fixes the component shape and these mechanism choices: the overlay is a Loro document, recognition is hybrid (a deterministic engine for the attested layer and a provider-agnostic vision adapter for the overlay), the semantic layer is a sidecar in JSON-LD bound to the <code>plan/0039</code> vocabulary, the round-trip law is a per-kind lens law in the property-based lane, and an undeclared capability defaults to the most restrictive setting.</li> <li><code>call/0031</code> fixes the untrusted-input threat model: ingested material is untrusted, met by defensive parsing with hard bounds, a legible untrusted boundary, and a fail-safe recorded refusal.</li> <li><code>call/0032</code> fixes the engineering-geometry token target, taken to the cast since the summary target has no settled industry answer: a deterministic structure-and-metadata summary keyed on the model tree, with a parsed-against-computed reproducibility split and an extensible per-format default.</li> <li><code>call/0033</code> fixes the reader architecture: each format is a pluggable Cargo feature, every reader is pure-Rust with no C dependency, the best reader per format is chosen on merit, the dependency licences are per plugin with AGPL banned and GPL flagged, and the in-scope set is the adopting project's choice.</li> </ul> <p>The canonicalisation rules, the reference tokenizer the token accounting reports against, and the query surface a running project calls are build-time details settled inside the milestone.</p> <h2 id="readers-and-dependencies"><a class="header" href="#readers-and-dependencies">Readers and dependencies</a></h2> <p>Each kind binds the best maintained pure-Rust reader, pinned with its version and licence in <a href="plan/0049-external-reference-corpus/readers.html"><code>readers.md</code></a>, which also carries the licence watch-list and the pure-Rust feature discipline. Almost every pick is permissive. The GPL <code>openscad-rs</code> runs out-of-process under <code>call/0033</code>, which doubles as the first real test of the plugin API, since the OpenSCAD plugin drives that helper through the same <code>Normalizer</code> interface as every in-process reader. The manual page and TeX and IGES have no pure-Rust library, so they are deferred rather than hand-rolled or bound to a C library. A <code>cargo-deny</code> lane denies AGPL and flags GPL.</p> <h2 id="validation-1"><a class="header" href="#validation-1">Validation</a></h2> <p>The agent-facing surfaces are validated at the weak-agent bar before the design locks, the way plan/0042 and plan/0039 were. The probe set, its adversarial review, and the recorded run live in <code>gather-data.md</code>. A design judgement with no settled answer, such as the engineering-geometry summary fields, goes to the cast rather than a pass rate.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-9"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-9">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The build runs as an anchored task graph (plan/0042): each task carries a receipt in <code>.host-task-receipts</code>, and a downstream task stays pending until its prerequisites carry receipts. The order lives in the <code>depends</code> edges rather than the names. The scaffold and the embed are done.</p> <h3 id="scaffold-workspace"><a class="header" href="#scaffold-workspace">Scaffold the workspace</a></h3> <p>Author the Cargo workspace on the pinned toolchain. The <code>host-reference-core</code> library carries the <code>Normalizer</code> trait and the two-layer types, and a thin CLI sits over it.</p> <ul> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="embed-component"><a class="header" href="#embed-component">Embed the component</a></h3> <p>Create the public repo and push the scaffold. Pin it source-only in <code>.host-software</code> and materialize the bare store and worktree. Record the embed and release receipts.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #scaffold-workspace</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="text-cheap-kinds"><a class="header" href="#text-cheap-kinds">The text-cheap kinds</a></h3> <p>Land the text-cheap normalisers that <code>call/0030</code> groups under the text and data and XML mechanisms, each with a conformance fixture that re-derives byte for byte.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #embed-component</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="pluggable-foundation"><a class="header" href="#pluggable-foundation">The pluggable foundation</a></h3> <p>Retrofit the text-cheap readers behind Cargo features in the CLI, the text-cheap set on by default and the heavier readers reserved for their own opt-in features (call/0033). Add the <code>cargo-deny</code> lane that denies AGPL and flags GPL. A build with no features compiles to an empty registry.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #text-cheap-kinds</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test && cargo deny check licenses advisories</li> </ul> <h3 id="expand-prose-and-structured-readers"><a class="header" href="#expand-prose-and-structured-readers">The expanded prose and structured readers</a></h3> <p>Land the documentation markups and the extra config and tabular kinds behind their features, each with a conformance fixture. The prose readers are reStructuredText and AsciiDoc and Org-mode and RTF and EPUB and BibTeX; the structured readers are TOML and the INI family and JSON Lines and the calendar and contact kinds and the Jupyter notebook and the columnar Parquet and Arrow. The pins live in <code>readers.md</code>.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #pluggable-foundation</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="office-mail-fixed-layout"><a class="header" href="#office-mail-fixed-layout">Office and mail and fixed-layout</a></h3> <p>Land the office and mail normalisers over the shared container readers, and add the born-digital PDF. Each carries its fixture.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #pluggable-foundation</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="recognition-and-engineering"><a class="header" href="#recognition-and-engineering">Recognition and engineering</a></h3> <p>Land the recognition path for scanned PDF and image and audio-visual media. Add the EDA layout normalisers and the engineering geometry of <code>call/0032</code>. Each carries its fixture.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #office-mail-fixed-layout</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="overlay"><a class="header" href="#overlay">The overlay</a></h3> <p>Land the Loro overlay and the write-back path over the W3C Web Annotation selectors, with the round-trip law proptested per kind.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #recognition-and-engineering</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="spec-and-release"><a class="header" href="#spec-and-release">The spec and the release</a></h3> <p>Add the <code>.allium</code> spec with its lanes and obligations, and wire the CI. Establish the reproducible build with its deps-bundle, and release through <code>host-lifecycle</code>.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #overlay</li> <li>verify: host-lifecycle software --verify-build .</li> </ul> <h3 id="harden-untrusted-input"><a class="header" href="#harden-untrusted-input">Harden untrusted input and remediate the review</a></h3> <p>Fold the <code>plan/0050</code> review findings back into this milestone rather than deferring them to a separate plan (the operator's call: a review finding is a requirement, not a descope). The must-fix cluster is the <code>call/0031</code> refusal contract, which the obligations manifest asserts but no reader keeps: bound the <code>view</code> selector at its source so an oversized length returns <code>Error::Parse</code> instead of overflowing into a panic (finding 1), and make readers return <code>Error::Refused</code> on a resource bound or a hostile structure instead of panicking, hanging, or silently zeroing (findings 2 through 4 and the office, EPUB, and audio-visual instances). The determinism holes in the two out-of-process helpers, the overlay re-anchoring, the lens-law proptests, and the CI feature-compile gap follow. <code>plan/0051</code> is reserved for the other review cluster.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #spec-and-release</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h3 id="consolidate-reuse"><a class="header" href="#consolidate-reuse">Consolidate the reuse findings</a></h3> <p>Fold in the review's reuse and altitude observations and the view-ignores-selector deviation (the residuals deferred from the harden-untrusted-input pass, on the operator's call to fold both in). Move the duplicated reader boilerplate into shared <code>core</code> helpers: one <code>raw_tokens</code> policy for a comparable saving ratio, a <code>Tier0::whole</code> constructor, a <code>char_offset_view</code> body, a fence-aware <code>markdown_heading_outline</code> for prose and HTML, a default <code>Normalizer::view</code> that returns the skeleton (so the metadata readers drop their boilerplate view), and a declared <code>extensions()</code> with a default hint-matching <code>detect</code>. Share the conformance bless-or-compare protocol through a <code>host-reference -testkit</code> dev-dependency crate. Behaviour-preserving (only the image, av, and OCR raw-token counts move, the documented basis change); released as a follow-on host-reference version.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #harden-untrusted-input</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-reference/main && cargo test</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-11"><a class="header" href="#status-11">Status</a></h2> <p>The design is settled and the build is under way. The scaffold and the embed are done, and so is the text-cheap-kinds task: its normalisers and conformance fixtures have landed behind the <code>host-reference-core</code> contract and the CLI (prose, structured data, markup, vector, and the SPICE netlist). The component is pinned source-only in <code>.host-software</code>, and <code>software --check</code> is green. The build sequence above is an anchored receipted task graph (plan/0042). The pluggable foundation and the expanded prose and structured readers have landed, each reader a feature-gated crate, and the per-kind pins live in <code>readers.md</code>; the library-less kinds stay deferred. Office and mail and fixed-layout have landed (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX over undoc; EML over mail-parser; born-digital PDF over lopdf and pdf-extract), and so has recognition-and-engineering: the attested deterministic readers of the recognition split, image and audio-visual container metadata alongside the EDA and engineering-geometry parsers. OCR is delivered too, as the first out-of-process plugin (<code>call/0034</code>): a helper binary carries the ocrs engine and its CC-BY-SA-4.0 models, the permissive plugin runs it at arm's length, and the recognised text re-derives deterministically into the attested layer. OpenSCAD followed as the second out-of-process plugin, the GPL <code>openscad-rs</code> parser in its own repo, and STEP, 3MF, and AMF completed the engineering geometry, so only IGES stays deferred. The overlay has landed too: the mutable Loro layer, anchored to the immutable layer by W3C Web Annotation selectors, with the write-back path and the per-kind round-trip lens law proptested. Audio-visual transcription rides that overlay's provider-agnostic adapter by the <code>call/0030</code> split. The spec and the release, the last node, have landed: <code>host-reference.allium</code> distils the Normalizer contract (<code>allium check</code> and <code>analyse</code> clean), the <code>.obligations</code> manifest dispositions every obligation, the CI workflow runs the build and the conformance, lens-law, clippy, cargo-deny, and allium lanes, and the reproducible build is established. host-reference is released as v0.1.1 through the tool-carried sequence: the canonical default-feature binary re-derives byte-identically in the pinned muslrust toolchain from the vendored deps-bundle, proven by <code>software --verify-build</code>. Releasing the first workspace component took a host-lifecycle fix (v0.31.2): it reads and bumps the version in <code>[workspace.package]</code> and syncs every member's lock entry. Every node through the release carries a receipt.</p> <p>The milestone then re-opened to absorb the <code>plan/0050</code> review. A maximum-recall audit of the released host-reference found the determinism discipline and the conformance fixtures sound, but the <code>call/0031</code> explicit-refusal contract asserted yet kept by no reader, and an unbounded <code>view</code> selector overflowing into a panic. Rather than defer that to a separate plan, the harden-untrusted-input node folds the remediation back in; <code>plan/0051</code> is reserved for the other review cluster.</p> <p>The harden-untrusted-input node has landed. Every <code>plan/0050</code> finding is remediated: the <code>call/0031</code> refusal contract is realised across the readers and is now test-backed rather than falsely waived (<code>core::char_offset_window</code> saturates the selector window, <code>guard_panic</code> contains the pdf-extract and mp4 panics, the calendar and the archive readers refuse malformed and bomb input, and a <code>GuardedReader</code> contract test plus per-reader hostile-input tests discharge the obligation); the overlay refuses an ambiguous or empty anchor and its lens-law proptests exercise the real read and write sides; the correctness findings (the image and OCR collision, the case-sensitive hint, the fenced-code outline, the reStructuredText markup, the SPICE net arity, the canonical-form escaping, and the rest) are fixed; CI compiles the CLI with every reader feature and gates <code>cargo fmt --check</code>; and the out-of-process plugins stage input at a random temporary path and record the helper version into the attestation. It shipped as host-reference v0.1.2 with the two helpers at v0.2.0, each re-deriving byte-identically in the pinned toolchain, with the release receipts and the node receipt recorded.</p> <p>The consolidate-reuse node then folded in the review's reuse and altitude observations and the view-ignores-selector deviation (the residuals the operator chose to fold in rather than leave). The duplicated reader boilerplate moved into shared <code>core</code> helpers (one <code>raw_tokens</code> policy, <code>Tier0::whole</code>, <code>char_offset_view</code>, a fence-aware <code>markdown_heading_outline</code>, a default <code>view</code>, and a declared <code>extensions()</code>), and a <code>host-reference-testkit</code> crate now owns the conformance protocol the readers copy-pasted. It is behaviour-preserving apart from the documented <code>raw_tokens</code> basis change, and shipped as host-reference v0.1.3 (the helpers unchanged at v0.2.0), re-deriving byte-identically. The broader review campaign stays open: <code>plan/0051</code> is held for the pending review of other software.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0049-reviewers-guide-the-external-reference-corpus"><a class="header" href="#plan0049-reviewers-guide-the-external-reference-corpus">plan/0049 reviewer's guide: the external reference corpus</a></h1> <p>This guide orients a review of the milestone. It says what to read in each repository and what is worth scrutiny. The milestone's code spans five repositories; review <code>host-reference</code> first, since it is the bulk.</p> <h2 id="what-the-milestone-delivers"><a class="header" href="#what-the-milestone-delivers">What the milestone delivers</a></h2> <p><code>host-reference</code> is a reference compiler. It normalises external documentation that an agentic project consumes but does not author, turning it into a token-lean, attestable form. It carries a two-layer model: an immutable attested layer that re-derives deterministically from the source bytes, and a mutable overlay layer for annotations and edits, anchored into the attested layer by standard selectors.</p> <p>The design is settled across the <code>call/</code> decisions:</p> <ul> <li><code>call/0030</code>: the component shape and the immutable-against-overlay split.</li> <li><code>call/0031</code>: the untrusted-input threat model (defensive parsing, a recorded refusal).</li> <li><code>call/0032</code>: the engineering-geometry token target (a deterministic structure summary).</li> <li><code>call/0033</code>: the reader architecture (pluggable by feature, pure-Rust, the licence policy, and the out-of-process boundary).</li> <li><code>call/0034</code>: OCR as the first out-of-process plugin.</li> </ul> <p>The build ran as an anchored task graph (<code>README.md</code> in this folder). Every node carries a receipt in <code>.host-task-receipts</code>, and <code>readers.md</code> records the pinned reader for each content kind alongside the licence watch-list.</p> <h2 id="host-reference-released-v011"><a class="header" href="#host-reference-released-v011">host-reference (released v0.1.1)</a></h2> <p>The component, a Cargo workspace. <code>crates/core</code> holds the contract, <code>crates/cli</code> is a thin CLI over the registered readers, and each reader is its own crate behind a Cargo feature.</p> <p>The contract lives in <code>crates/core/src/lib.rs</code>:</p> <ul> <li>the <code>Normalizer</code> trait, with <code>modality</code>, <code>capabilities</code>, <code>detect</code>, <code>skeleton</code>, <code>view</code>, and <code>put</code>.</li> <li><code>Caps</code>, whose <code>Default</code> is the most restrictive setting, so an undeclared capability cannot over-claim editability.</li> <li>the bidirectional <code>SourceMap</code>, the <code>Tier0</code> skeleton, and the <code>Tier1</code> windowed view.</li> </ul> <p>Worth checking here: the fail-safe default, and that <code>put</code> refuses unless a reader declares a well-behaved lens.</p> <p>The readers are feature-gated crates, each with byte-for-byte conformance fixtures under <code>crates/<name>/fixtures/</code>:</p> <ul> <li>the text-cheap default set: prose, structured data, config, HTML, vector, and the SPICE netlist.</li> <li>opt-in markup and structured kinds: reStructuredText, AsciiDoc, Org, RTF, EPUB, BibTeX, the calendar and contact kinds, the Jupyter notebook, Parquet, and Arrow.</li> <li>office, mail, and fixed-layout: the office documents through undoc, internet mail through mail-parser, and born-digital PDF through lopdf with pdf-extract.</li> <li>recognition and engineering: image metadata and EXIF; audio-visual container metadata under a new <code>AudioVisual</code> modality; the EDA tallies for KiCad, Eagle, and Gerber; and the engineering geometry kinds (STL, glTF, DXF, OBJ, PLY, G-code, 3MF, AMF, STEP).</li> <li>out-of-process: the <code>ocr</code> and <code>openscad</code> plugins, which spawn helper binaries reviewed in their own repositories.</li> </ul> <p>What to scrutinise:</p> <ul> <li>Determinism. Each conformance golden is compared byte-for-byte, and the fixtures are static committed files, so a golden is independent of the build configuration. Confirm that no reader folds in nondeterministic state such as a timestamp, a hash-map iteration order, or a re-encoded container.</li> <li>The overlay (<code>crates/overlay</code>). It is a Loro CRDT document holding annotations anchored by W3C Web Annotation selectors. A <code>TextQuote</code> selector re-locates by content, so an annotation survives a re-derivation that shifts offsets. The per-kind round-trip lens law (GetPut and PutGet) is proptested for the write-back kinds in <code>crates/overlay/tests/lens_law.rs</code>.</li> <li>The licence lane (<code>deny.toml</code>). AGPL is banned and GPL is flagged. Confirm the allow-list matches the dependency tree and that no copyleft code reached the permissive crates.</li> <li>The specification. <code>host-reference.allium</code> distils the Normalizer contract, and <code>host-reference.obligations</code> dispositions every <code>allium plan</code> obligation. The trait rules map to named contract tests in <code>crates/core/tests/contract.rs</code>; the rules realised outside the trait are waived with stated reasons. The CI workflow runs the build, the conformance fixtures, the lens-law proptests, clippy, cargo-deny, and the allium lane.</li> </ul> <h2 id="host-reference-ocr-released-v011"><a class="header" href="#host-reference-ocr-released-v011">host-reference-ocr (released v0.1.1)</a></h2> <p>The out-of-process OCR helper. It carries the <code>ocrs</code> engine over the <code>rten</code> runtime, with the OCR models embedded in the binary.</p> <p>It is a separate program because the models are CC-BY-SA-4.0, a content-copyleft licence. The permissive <code>host-reference-ocr</code> plugin runs this binary at arm's length and reads the recognised text from stdout, so the plugin and its dependents are an aggregation with the helper rather than a derivative of it. This is the <code>call/0033</code> boundary built for GPL, applied to a content licence, and the first real exercise of the out-of-process plugin API.</p> <p>What to scrutinise: the licence confinement (the README states the split upfront and <code>NOTICE.md</code> attributes the models), and that the helper honours the simple contract the plugin expects, an image path argument in and the recognised text on stdout.</p> <h2 id="host-reference-openscad-released-v011"><a class="header" href="#host-reference-openscad-released-v011">host-reference-openscad (released v0.1.1)</a></h2> <p>The out-of-process OpenSCAD helper. It links the GPL-3.0 <code>openscad-rs</code> parser, so the binary is GPL. It prints the kind of each top-level statement, which the permissive <code>openscad</code> plugin tallies into the structure skeleton.</p> <p>What to scrutinise: that the GPL stays confined, since the helper binary is GPL while <code>host-reference</code> carries no <code>openscad-rs</code>, and that the helper repository's <code>cargo-deny</code> names <code>openscad-rs</code> and the binary as the flagged GPL exceptions while banning AGPL.</p> <h2 id="host-lifecycle-v0312"><a class="header" href="#host-lifecycle-v0312">host-lifecycle (v0.31.2)</a></h2> <p>Two patches, both to let a workspace component release through the tool-carried sequence, since host-reference is the first such component:</p> <ul> <li><code>cargo_version</code> and <code>set_cargo_version</code> fall back to <code>[workspace.package]</code> when a virtual workspace root carries no <code>[package]</code> version.</li> <li>the lock sync bumps every workspace member that inherits the workspace version, not only the deploy crate, so the pinned <code>--locked</code> rebuild does not fail on a stale member.</li> </ul> <p>What to scrutinise: the two functions and their unit tests, and that a single-crate component still releases unchanged, since a root <code>[package]</code> wins over <code>[workspace.package]</code>.</p> <h2 id="agentic-host-the-host-repository"><a class="header" href="#agentic-host-the-host-repository">agentic-host (the host repository)</a></h2> <p>The milestone's prose and provenance, rather than code:</p> <ul> <li><code>plan/0049-external-reference-corpus/</code>: this README task graph, <code>readers.md</code>, and <code>gather-data.md</code>.</li> <li><code>call/0034</code>: the decision that OCR ships out-of-process.</li> <li><code>.host-software</code>: the reproducible-build provenance for host-reference and the two helpers, naming the toolchain, the build, the artifact digest, and the deps-bundle.</li> <li><code>.host-task-receipts</code> and <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>: the anchored task receipts and the per-component embed and release receipts.</li> </ul> <p>What to scrutinise: that each receipt's evidence matches the work, and that the recorded artifact digests are the ones <code>software --verify-build</code> reproduces.</p> <h2 id="reproducibility-and-the-verification-lanes"><a class="header" href="#reproducibility-and-the-verification-lanes">Reproducibility and the verification lanes</a></h2> <p>Every artifact component builds offline in a pinned muslrust container from a vendored deps-bundle, and re-derives byte-identically. <code>host-lifecycle software --verify-build</code> is green across all six artifact components. The recorded digest is the container build at the <code>/src</code> mount path, the reproducibility anchor; a build at any other path embeds different crate paths and drifts.</p> <h2 id="known-deferrals-intentional-rather-than-gaps"><a class="header" href="#known-deferrals-intentional-rather-than-gaps">Known deferrals, intentional rather than gaps</a></h2> <ul> <li>Transcription of audio-visual media: non-deterministic inference, deferred to the overlay's provider-agnostic adapter.</li> <li>IGES: no pure-Rust reader exists.</li> <li>Compressed AMF, the zip variant: the reader refuses it with a clear message, and uncompressed AMF is delivered.</li> <li>Outlook MSG: skipped, its OLE2 fixture disproportionate for a niche format, and internet mail covers the common case.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-host-reference-agent-surfaces-at-the-weak-agent-bar"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-host-reference-agent-surfaces-at-the-weak-agent-bar">gather-data: host-reference agent surfaces at the weak-agent bar</a></h1> <p>This records the weak-agent probe work for plan/0049. The probes test whether a weak agent (Fen, the <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> model reached through the rope HTTPS endpoint) can use the agent-facing surfaces the design proposes: a windowed retrieval selector, a templated semantic sidecar, a capability declaration, the data-against-instruction posture for ingested content, and the deterministic boundary for engineering geometry. The set was reviewed adversarially and revised before any run, so the recorded run measures the surfaces and not the artefacts of a leaky question.</p> <p>The run and the cast review are pending. The results are appended below once they return.</p> <h2 id="the-adversarial-review-that-shaped-the-set"><a class="header" href="#the-adversarial-review-that-shaped-the-set">The adversarial review that shaped the set</a></h2> <p>A first draft of five probes was reviewed against the contamination rules plan/0044 and plan/0042 already follow. The review found flaws that would let the model pass or fail for a reason other than the one under test, and each was fixed:</p> <ul> <li>A surface cue. The first retrieval probe placed the exact token budget on the correct option alone, so the model could match a number rather than reason. The fix repeats the budget on a wrong option, so the budget no longer points at the answer.</li> <li>A contestable key. The retrieval probe also let a page selector stand as a defensible answer beside the section selector. The fix makes the section straddle two shared pages, so the page selector over-includes a neighbour and the section selector is the clean choice.</li> <li>An unanswerable blank. The sidecar probe asked the model to supply a concept identifier and a selector it had never seen, which tests recall of an unseen vocabulary. The fix supplies the context block and a menu, so each blank is a choice among shown values.</li> <li>An undecidable key. The capability probe left the OCR output unspecified, so the semantic flag could read either way. The fix states the output, so the flag is determinable.</li> <li>A self-perturbing payload. The data-against-instruction probe embedded a literal instruction-like string, which can influence the model answering the probe. The fix references the string rather than embedding it, and drops the option no reasoner would pick in favour of two genuine ways to get it wrong.</li> <li>A judgement with no answer. The geometry probe graded a design choice the project itself has not settled. The fix splits it: a graded part tests the deterministic boundary, which has a real answer, and an open part elicits the design opinion for the cast and is unscored.</li> </ul> <p>The revised set adds an abstain option to every probe, pins the system prompt, and randomises the option order across runs. The cast reviews the authoring probe and the open part, since the same author wrote the design and the probes.</p> <h2 id="cast-review-before-the-run"><a class="header" href="#cast-review-before-the-run">Cast review, before the run</a></h2> <p>The review lenses are the four cast personas, named in the findings below. Fen is the run itself, the acceptance test, so it is not a lens. Four findings changed the instrument before the run.</p> <ul> <li>Wren and Mara asked for a stated success bar, since a result with no pre-registered threshold is read after the fact and flatters the design. The bar is pre-registered below.</li> <li>Orin asked what happens when Fen fails a probe, and required the answer to be written before the run, so a failure cannot be waved away. The response to a failure is pre-registered below.</li> <li>Mara warned against over-reading a pass: a pass shows the surface is legible to a weak agent, and says nothing about whether the surface is the right design. The pass criteria say so.</li> <li>Bly required two fail-safe rules. The capability model defaults an absent or unknown flag to the most restrictive setting (no round-trip, no write-back), so a normaliser that forgets to declare cannot over-claim editability. The result record marks an unsettled question as owed rather than implying it is settled, so a cold read over-reports the remaining work rather than hiding it. Both fold into call/0030.</li> </ul> <h2 id="pass-criteria-and-the-response-to-a-failure"><a class="header" href="#pass-criteria-and-the-response-to-a-failure">Pass criteria and the response to a failure</a></h2> <p>The graded probes are probe one, probe three, probe four, and probe five part one. Probe two and probe five part two are cast judgements and are unscored.</p> <p>A graded probe passes when the intended option is chosen in all three runs. A run that chooses the abstain option does not count as a wrong answer. A probe that abstains across the runs is read as a framing gap to fix in the probe, or a context gap to fix in the surface, and is not a pass. A run that chooses a wrong option is a failure signal.</p> <p>When a graded probe fails, the surface is read as illegible to a weak agent, and the design of that surface is revised rather than the result set aside. This is written before the run so a failure cannot be reinterpreted after it.</p> <h2 id="the-system-prompt-1"><a class="header" href="#the-system-prompt-1">The system prompt</a></h2> <p>A senior engineer reviewing the host-reference design, answering a self-contained multiple-choice question with the single best option and a short justification, and choosing the abstain option when the question lacks enough to decide. Each probe supplies the definitions it needs, such as the meaning of the capability flags and the two layers.</p> <h2 id="the-sampler"><a class="header" href="#the-sampler">The sampler</a></h2> <p>Direct against the rope endpoint with the Qwen thinking-precise values: <code>temperature</code> 0.6, <code>top_p</code> 0.95, <code>top_k</code> 20, <code>min_p</code> 0. The model reasons before it answers, so the judgement is read off the converged reasoning.</p> <h2 id="probe-one-windowed-retrieval"><a class="header" href="#probe-one-windowed-retrieval">Probe one: windowed retrieval</a></h2> <p>The skeleton shows a section titled Electrical Characteristics that begins partway down page 41 and ends partway down page 43, so it shares page 41 with the prior section and page 43 with the next. A task needs only that section, within a budget of 2000 tokens. The choices:</p> <ul> <li>(A) <code>view --select section:"Electrical Characteristics" --max-tokens 2000</code></li> <li>(B) <code>view --select page:41-43 --max-tokens 2000</code></li> <li>(C) load the full document view, then read the section</li> <li>(D) abstain, the skeleton gives too little to choose</li> </ul> <p>The intended answer is (A): the section selector respects the budget and avoids the neighbours on the shared pages. Option (B) carries the same budget yet pulls the two adjacent sections. Option (C) is the load-everything instinct. This tests budgeted retrieval over bulk loading.</p> <h2 id="probe-two-templated-semantic-sidecar"><a class="header" href="#probe-two-templated-semantic-sidecar">Probe two: templated semantic sidecar</a></h2> <p>Given a fixed context block and a menu of concept identifiers and selectors, the model fills three slots of a JSON-LD sidecar entry for the fact that one span states the absolute-maximum ratings of part 2N2222A. Each slot is a choice from the menu rather than free composition. This tests whether the model can place known pieces into a template, the form plan/0042 found a weak agent handles. This probe is unscored and goes to the cast, since authoring is a judgement.</p> <h2 id="probe-three-capability-flags"><a class="header" href="#probe-three-capability-flags">Probe three: capability flags</a></h2> <p>A scanned, image-only PDF is read by a deterministic OCR engine that yields text with reading order and no tagged headings or tables. The model chooses the capability set over the four flags round-trip, write-back, semantic, and ocr:</p> <ul> <li>(A) round-trip no, write-back no, semantic partial, ocr yes</li> <li>(B) round-trip yes, write-back yes, semantic full, ocr yes</li> <li>(C) round-trip no, write-back no, semantic none, ocr yes</li> <li>(D) abstain</li> </ul> <p>The intended answer is (A): reading order is partial semantic structure, and the conversion is lossy, so it has no round-trip. Option (B) over-claims a round-trip on a lossy kind. Option (C) under-claims the reading order. This tests the lossy-against- lossless instinct against a stated output.</p> <h2 id="probe-four-ingested-content-is-data"><a class="header" href="#probe-four-ingested-content-is-data">Probe four: ingested content is data</a></h2> <p>An ingested HTML source contains a string that reads like an instruction to the reader to delete files. The source is external, so the manifest already marks the whole source untrusted. How the skeleton should hold that string:</p> <ul> <li>(A) quote it verbatim within a data span, preserving it, since the source already carries the untrusted mark</li> <li>(B) rewrite it into a summary of its intent</li> <li>(C) remove it from the normalised output</li> <li>(D) abstain</li> </ul> <p>The intended answer is (A). Option (B) editorialises and loses fidelity and the provenance trail. Option (C) sanitises by deletion and loses the same. There is no act-on-it option, since the tension worth testing is fidelity against sanitising, and the string is referenced rather than embedded so it cannot perturb the model.</p> <h2 id="probe-five-part-one-the-deterministic-boundary"><a class="header" href="#probe-five-part-one-the-deterministic-boundary">Probe five, part one: the deterministic boundary</a></h2> <p>For a STEP assembly, which candidate cannot be re-derived byte for byte from the source in a pinned toolchain, and so belongs in the overlay rather than the attested layer:</p> <ul> <li>(A) a description produced by a vision model from a rendered image</li> <li>(B) the assembly tree with units and bounding boxes</li> <li>(C) the count of solids and faces and edges</li> <li>(D) abstain</li> </ul> <p>The intended answer is (A): a model reading is not reproducible, so it sits in the overlay with its provenance recorded. Options (B) and (C) are deterministic and belong in the attested layer. This tests the boundary between the two layers, which has a real answer.</p> <h2 id="probe-five-part-two-the-geometry-summary-for-the-cast"><a class="header" href="#probe-five-part-two-the-geometry-summary-for-the-cast">Probe five, part two: the geometry summary, for the cast</a></h2> <p>An open question, unscored: which fields make the most useful compact summary of a large assembly for an agent reading it in context, and why. The answer is recorded for the cast, since the project has no settled target for engineering geometry.</p> <h2 id="run-plan"><a class="header" href="#run-plan">Run plan</a></h2> <p>At least three runs per probe, with the option order randomised across runs. The record reports both the choice and its consistency across runs, since a choice that varies is a guess. Probe two and probe five part two go to the cast.</p> <h2 id="results"><a class="header" href="#results">Results</a></h2> <p>The run went against <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> on rope with the recorded sampler, three runs per graded probe, the option order rotated each run so the correct content sat at a different letter each time.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Probe</th><th>Surface tested</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Probe one</td><td>windowed retrieval selector</td><td>pass, three of three</td></tr> <tr><td>Probe three</td><td>capability flags</td><td>pass, three of three</td></tr> <tr><td>Probe four</td><td>ingested content is data</td><td>pass, three of three</td></tr> <tr><td>Probe five part one</td><td>the deterministic boundary</td><td>pass, three of three</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The rotation is the signal. Across the three runs the model chose the letters A, then D, then C, each mapping back to the same correct content, so it answered by content rather than by position. Every run finished cleanly rather than at the token cap, and the abstain option was available and went unchosen on every graded probe.</p> <p>The reasoning matched the intended logic. On probe three the model derived each flag: text from an image carries no round-trip, reading order is partial semantic structure, and the image-only source takes no write-back. On probe five part one it separated the assembly tree and the counts, re-derivable from the STEP source, from the vision-model description, an inference that is not intrinsic to the source. On probe four it reached the preserve-verbatim answer through the byte-for-byte integrity rule, so the data-against-instruction posture held as a consequence of integrity rather than as a rule of its own, a stronger anchor than the probe had assumed.</p> <p>The cast probes:</p> <ul> <li>Probe two. One run filled all three slots correctly from the menu (<code>@type</code> Table, <code>about</code> the absolute-maximum-ratings concept, <code>derivedFrom</code> the section selector). A second run spent its budget on reasoning and was cut off before the answer. The completed run shows the templated sidecar is fillable from a menu at the weak-agent bar, and the cut-off run is a thinking-length artefact rather than an authoring failure.</li> <li>Probe five part two. Re-run with an open prompt, since the batch system prompt had assumed a multiple-choice shape and collided with the open question. The model proposed an assembly hierarchy, a critical-component list, interface topology, an assembly sequence, and constraint boundaries. These fields carry the dependencies an agent needs without reading every part record. Recorded for the cast.</li> </ul> <p>The raw responses are saved as the evidence trail.</p> <h2 id="cast-review-after-the-run"><a class="header" href="#cast-review-after-the-run">Cast review, after the run</a></h2> <p>The same four lenses read the results.</p> <ul> <li>Mara accepts the surfaces as legible to a weak agent and holds her earlier line: a pass shows legibility, and the correctness of the capability taxonomy and the geometry target still rests on the design and the cast rather than on this run.</li> <li>Wren reads the rotation result as the de-biased signal he asked for. The model moved its letter with the options and kept its content, so there is no position artefact, and it did not drift into a confident wrong answer.</li> <li>Bly notes the two cut-off runs are recorded as cut-offs rather than passed off as answers, and that probe five part two stays owed to the cast. He asks call/0030 to confirm the capability default he set before the run, so a normaliser that omits a flag falls to the restrictive setting.</li> <li>Orin draws one process lesson: a batch that mixes a multiple-choice instruction in the system prompt with an open elicitation made the open probe fail to complete, so a future run separates the two shapes. The pre-registered response to a failure went unused, since no graded probe failed.</li> </ul> <p>Verdict: the four agent-facing surfaces pass at the weak-agent bar and carry into call/0030 as designed. The templated semantic sidecar is fillable by the weak agent. The engineering-geometry target is the one open design judgement and goes to the cast, with the weak agent's field list recorded as input. The capability fail-safe default and the security decision remain for call/0030 and its security sibling.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0049-reader-and-dependency-pins"><a class="header" href="#plan0049-reader-and-dependency-pins">plan/0049: reader and dependency pins</a></h1> <p>This records the pinned reader for each content kind of <code>host-reference</code>, under the <code>call/0033</code> policy. Each reader is a pure-Rust plugin behind a Cargo feature and the best maintained library for its format. Its licence is clear of AGPL, and any GPL dependency is flagged. The versions below are current as of the 2026-06-27 research pass, and the exact Cargo pins land when each reader is built. A few kinds have no pure-Rust library, so they take a scoped in-house parser, listed at the end.</p> <h2 id="prose"><a class="header" href="#prose">Prose</a></h2> <div Apache-2.0</td><td>a generic XML read, since Eagle 6 and later is XML; no dedicated crate</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="engineering-geometry"><a class="header" It pulls the unmaintained <code>proc-macro-error</code> (RUSTSEC-2024-0370) through <code>ruststep-derive</code>, accepted on the same footing as <code>paste</code></td></tr> <tr><td>IGES</td><td>deferred</td><td>n/a</td><td>no pure-Rust reader exists, every working reader is C++</td></tr> <tr><td>DXF</td><td><code>dxf</code> 0.6.1</td><td>MIT</td><td>ASCII, binary, and the legacy DXB</td></tr> <tr><td>STL</td><td><code>stl_io</code> 0.11.0</td><td>MIT</td><td>binary and ASCII, with zero runtime dependencies</td></tr> <tr><td>OBJ</td><td><code>tobj</code> 4.0.4</td><td>MIT</td><td>a Rust port rather than a tinyobjloader binding</td></tr> <tr><td>3MF</td><td><code>threemf</code> 0.8.0</td><td>0BSD</td><td>delivered: <code>read</code> gives the mesh, vertex, and triangle counts; pure-Rust on the deflate path</td></tr> <tr><td>AMF</td><td><code>roxmltree</code> 0.20</td><td>MIT OR Apache-2.0</td><td>delivered for the uncompressed XML: object, mesh, vertex, and triangle counts. A compressed AMF (zip) is refused with a clear message for now</td></tr> <tr><td>G-code</td><td><code>gcode</code> 0.7.0</td><td>MIT OR Apache-2.0</td><td>a tokenizer that does not interpret machine state</td></tr> <tr><td>OpenSCAD</td><td><code>openscad-rs</code> 0.1, out-of-process</td><td>GPL-3.0, flagged</td><td>delivered (call/0034): the GPL parser lives in the separate <code>host-reference-openscad</code> repo, and the permissive <code>openscad</code> plugin runs it at arm's length and tallies the statement kinds; opt-in</td></tr> <tr><td>glTF, GLB</td><td><code>gltf</code> 1.4.1</td><td>MIT OR Apache-2.0</td><td>both the JSON and the binary container</td></tr> <tr><td>PLY</td><td><code>ply-rs-bw</code> 4.0.0</td><td>MIT</td><td>the maintained fork; the original carries a security advisory</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="recognition-and-engineering-what-landed"><a class="header" href="#recognition-and-engineering-what-landed">Recognition-and-engineering: what landed</a></h2> <p>The <code>#recognition-and-engineering</code> wave landed the attested, deterministic readers of the recognition split. Each is a feature-gated <code>Normalizer</code> with byte-for-byte conformance fixtures, built and pinned on its own lifecycle pass.</p> <ul> <li>Image (<code>image</code> feature): format, pixel dimensions, and EXIF.</li> <li>Audio-visual (<code>av</code> feature, the new <code>AudioVisual</code> modality): audio codec, sample rate, channels, and duration through symphonia; video per-track type, dimensions, and duration through <code>mp4</code>.</li> <li>Electronic design (<code>eda</code> feature): KiCad form tally, Eagle element tally, Gerber command count.</li> <li>Engineering geometry (<code>geometry</code> feature): STL, glTF, DXF, OBJ, PLY, G-code, 3MF, AMF, and STEP.</li> </ul> <p>OCR is delivered too, as the first out-of-process plugin (<code>call/0034</code>). The only pure-Rust OCR engine, <code>ocrs</code> over <code>rten</code>, carries CC-BY-SA-4.0 model weights, so the <code>call/0033</code> arms-length rule built for GPL applies: the <code>host-reference-ocr-helper</code> binary carries the engine and the embedded models, and the permissive <code>ocr</code> plugin runs it as a separate process and reads the recognised text back. The recognised text of a fixed engine over fixed bytes is a deterministic parse, run-to-run identical on a host, so it sits in the attested layer with a byte-for-byte golden, the same contract the in-process readers carry. The transcript of audio-visual media stays non-deterministic provider output and rides the <code>call/0030</code> overlay adapter in <code>#overlay</code>; the audio-visual reader here declares <code>ocr: false</code>.</p> <p>OpenSCAD is delivered too, as the second out-of-process plugin (<code>call/0033</code>, <code>call/0034</code>), the same shape as OCR: the GPL-3.0 <code>openscad-rs</code> parser lives in its own repo, <code>host-reference-openscad</code>, and the permissive <code>openscad</code> plugin runs that helper at arm's length and tallies the statement kinds it prints. STEP, 3MF, and AMF are in too, in-process in the geometry crate: 3MF through <code>threemf</code>, AMF through <code>roxmltree</code> over the uncompressed XML, and STEP through <code>ruststep</code>'s schema-agnostic parser, which earned an accepted unmaintained advisory (<code>proc-macro-error</code> through <code>ruststep-derive</code>) rather than the deferral the maturity rule had reserved for it. The engineering-geometry modality is now complete bar IGES, which stays deferred because every working reader is C++.</p> <h2 id="licence-watch-list"><a class="header" href="#licence-watch-list">Licence watch-list</a></h2> <ul> <li>AGPL is banned, and the pinned set carries none. The one risk was <code>gerber_parser</code>, which was AGPL through its 0.1 line and relicensed to MIT or Apache at 0.2, so the pin sits at or above 0.2.</li> <li>GPL is avoided and flagged. The <code>epub</code> crate is GPL and a permissive equal exists, so EPUB reads through the Apache-licensed <code>rbook</code> and the GPL crate never enters the build. <code>openscad-rs</code> is GPL and has no permissive equal, so OpenSCAD takes the out-of-process route of <code>call/0033</code>, described below. These are the only two GPL crates in view.</li> <li>Weak copyleft is allowed and noted. The <code>symphonia</code> and <code>mp4parse</code> media readers are MPL-2.0, a file-level copyleft that binds only their own files. The dormant <code>tex-parser</code> is LGPL, and it is passed over for the in-house tokenizer on maturity grounds rather than licence.</li> <li>Content copyleft is confined behind the boundary. The ocrs models are CC-BY-SA-4.0, the first content-copyleft dependency. They are not a cargo dependency, so <code>cargo-deny</code> does not see them; they are vendored data. The <code>call/0034</code> out-of-process boundary keeps them in the separate <code>host-reference-ocr</code> repo (the helper binary embeds them), attributed in its <code>NOTICE.md</code> and stated upfront in its <code>README.md</code>, so the <code>host-reference</code> repo carries none of it and the permissive plugin and its dependents are an aggregation with the models rather than a derivative.</li> <li>A <code>cargo-deny</code> lane denies AGPL and surfaces GPL, so the line holds as readers are added. The ocrs and rten code is permissive (MIT or Apache-2.0) and clears the lane.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-openscad-out-of-process-boundary"><a class="header" href="#the-openscad-out-of-process-boundary">The OpenSCAD out-of-process boundary</a></h2> <p>OpenSCAD is the one kind that takes a GPL reader. <code>openscad-rs</code> is a real tested <code>.scad</code> parser and the strongest reader for the kind, so the build uses it through the out-of-process rule of <code>call/0033</code>. The GPL-3.0 parser lives in its own repo, <code>host-reference-openscad</code>, whose helper binary depends on <code>openscad-rs</code> and is therefore GPL too. It reads a <code>.scad</code> file and prints the kind of each top-level statement, one per line. The host-reference OpenSCAD plugin stays permissive: it runs the helper at arm's length over the command line and tallies those kinds into the structure skeleton, so the two are aggregated rather than linked. The plugin is feature-gated and opt-in, and it depends on the helper binary being installed, which is the cost the <code>call/0033</code> consequence names. The helper repo's own <code>cargo-deny</code> lane treats <code>openscad-rs</code> and the helper binary as the expressly-flagged GPL exceptions rather than a violation, and the host-reference workspace carries no <code>openscad-rs</code> at all. OCR (<code>call/0034</code>) reached the out-of-process rule first, for a CC-BY-SA content licence rather than GPL; OpenSCAD is the second, for GPL. Both plugins implement the same <code>Normalizer</code> interface as every in-process reader, so the interface is general enough to drive an out-of-process helper with no special case.</p> <h2 id="pure-rust-feature-discipline"><a class="header" href="#pure-rust-feature-discipline">Pure-Rust feature discipline</a></h2> <p>Some readers are pure-Rust only with the right features. The <code>parquet</code> reader builds with default features off and the pure-Rust codecs on, which drops the C <code>zstd</code> codec and with it the ability to read zstd-compressed Parquet. The <code>arrow</code> reader keeps <code>ipc_compression</code> off for the same reason. The <code>lopdf</code> reader keeps its default <code>flate2</code> backend, the pure-Rust <code>miniz_oxide</code> rather than C zlib. The <code>threemf</code> reader and the other zip-backed readers stay on the pure-Rust deflate path. The <code>cargo-deny</code> lane and the pure-Rust build both run in the verification lanes.</p> <h2 id="deferred-kinds"><a class="header" href="#deferred-kinds">Deferred kinds</a></h2> <p>Three kinds have no maintained pure-Rust library and no composition over the existing pure-Rust readers, so normalising one would mean a substantial from-scratch parser. Rather than hand-roll a parser or reach for a C library, the build defers them until a pure-Rust library appears.</p> <ul> <li>Manual page and troff: only generator crates exist, with no parser.</li> <li>TeX and LaTeX: no maintained permissive pure-Rust document parser exists, and <code>pulldown-latex</code> covers the math alone.</li> <li>IGES: every working reader is C++.</li> </ul> <p>This keeps the pure-Rust line and the scope discipline together. A kind earns a reader when a pure-Rust library can carry it, and it waits otherwise. STEP sat just inside the line on <code>ruststep</code>, and it cleared it: the crate parses, so STEP is delivered rather than deferred, at the cost of one accepted unmaintained advisory.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0050-host-reference-review-findings-from-the-reference-compiler-audit"><a class="header" href="#plan0050-host-reference-review-findings-from-the-reference-compiler-audit">plan/0050 host-reference review: findings from the reference-compiler audit</a></h1> <p>This milestone records a maximum-effort review of <code>host-reference</code>, the reference compiler delivered by plan/0049. It is a findings record, not a remediation plan: nothing here is fixed in this milestone. Each finding carries its file, its mechanism, and the concrete input that triggers it, so a later remediation plan can pick the work up cold. The disposition for every finding below is the same (<em>recorded, remediation deferred</em>) and is not repeated per entry.</p> <h2 id="what-was-reviewed"><a class="header" href="#what-was-reviewed">What was reviewed</a></h2> <ul> <li>Repository: <code>connollydavid/host-reference</code>, pull request #1, "host-reference: external reference compiler".</li> <li>Head: <code>review/0049</code> at <code>ea92185</code> (identical to <code>host-reference</code> <code>main</code>, released v0.1.1).</li> <li>Base: <code>review-base/scaffold</code> at <code>88c6bcf</code>.</li> <li>Diff: 174 files, about 11,219 insertions and 38 deletions: roughly forty feature-gated normaliser crates plus the shared <code>core</code>, the <code>cli</code>, the <code>overlay</code> crate, the <code>.allium</code> specification with its obligations manifest, the <code>deny.toml</code> licence lane, and the CI workflow.</li> </ul> <p>The review ran locally at maximum recall (the cloud <code>code-review ultra</code> lane was unavailable, so its local fallback ran). Ten independent finder angles ran in parallel: five correctness groups across the crates, plus the overlay lens laws, a cross-cutting determinism audit, the CLI and core dispatch, the conformance fixtures and removed-behaviour audit, the specification and CI coverage, and a reuse and altitude pass. Targeted verification followed (several findings were confirmed by executing the code at the reviewed revision), then one gap sweep. Findings were deduped and ranked.</p> <h2 id="the-contract-the-findings-test-against"><a class="header" href="#the-contract-the-findings-test-against">The contract the findings test against</a></h2> <p>Every reader implements one trait, <code>Normalizer</code> (<code>crates/core/src/lib.rs</code>): <code>skeleton</code> returns the <code>Tier0</code> skeleton, <code>view</code> a windowed <code>Tier1</code> slice, <code>put</code> a write-back patch. The invariants the findings measure against:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Determinism is the premise.</strong> A <code>skeleton</code> output is serialized by <code>core::serialize_tier0</code> and compared byte for byte against a committed golden fixture in each crate's <code>tests/conformance.rs</code>. The component's whole claim is that output is "a pure function of the source bytes and the pinned toolchain" (call/0018, call/0030). Any non-determinism that reaches serialized output is a real defect.</li> <li><strong>Refusals are explicit (call/0031).</strong> A parse that hits a resource bound or a hostile structure must return <code>Error::Refused</code> (or <code>Error::Parse</code>). A panic, a hang, or a silent partial on malformed input is forbidden.</li> <li><strong>The source map is faithful.</strong> Each <code>Span.origin</code> is a byte range into the source; it must satisfy <code>start <= end <= len</code> and point at the true origin of the region it labels.</li> <li><strong>String slicing in Rust panics</strong> on a non-char-boundary or out-of-range index, so any <code>view</code> or <code>skeleton</code> that slices a <code>&str</code> by a computed offset on arbitrary input is a panic candidate.</li> </ul> <h2 id="correctness-findings-ranked"><a class="header" href="#correctness-findings-ranked">Correctness findings, ranked</a></h2> <p>The fifteen most severe, in order. The line numbers are at the reviewed revision.</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>A <code>view</code> selector with a large length overflows and panics instead of refusing.</strong> <code>crates/cli/src/main.rs</code> <code>parse_selector</code> (the root) and every <code>view</code> <code>CharOffset</code> arm (<code>crates/data/src/lib.rs:75</code>, <code>config:59</code>, <code>prose:123</code>, <code>asciidoc:54</code>, <code>bibtex:52</code>, <code>org:51</code>, <code>rst:54</code>, <code>html:92</code>, <code>netlist:110</code>, <code>vector:106</code>, and <code>calendar</code>). <code>parse_selector</code> accepts an unbounded <code>len</code>; each <code>view</code> computes <code>s + *len</code> <em>before</em> <code>floor_boundary</code> clamps it. <code>host-reference view notes.txt --select offset:1:18446744073709551615</code> panics with "attempt to add with overflow" in a debug build; in release the sum wraps below <code>s</code>, <code>floor_boundary</code> returns <code>end < start</code>, and <code>text[start..end]</code> panics "slice index starts at 1 but ends at 0". Confirmed by execution. The contract demands a clean <code>Error::Parse</code>. Fix belongs at the source, in <code>parse_selector</code> (a <code>checked_add</code> or an explicit bound).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>No reader ever constructs <code>Error::Refused</code>; the hostile-input obligation is waived but unrealised.</strong> <code>host-reference.obligations</code> (the <code>RefuseHostileInput</code> disposition). A grep for <code>Error::Refused</code> across <code>crates/**/lib.rs</code> matches only the <code>core</code> enum definition; no reader builds it, and <code>Source</code> carries no size or trust field. The obligations manifest waives <code>RefuseHostileInput</code> as "realised per reader as <code>Error::Refused</code> where a bound is hit," but that realisation does not exist, and the obligations check only verifies that test <em>names</em> resolve, so CI stays green. Every malformed or oversized untrusted document therefore hits a panic, a hang, or a silent partial, the exact call/0031 failure the spec forbids. Findings 3, 4, and the further findings on the office, EPUB, and audio-visual readers are concrete instances of this systemic gap.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The PDF reader aborts the process on many loadable PDFs.</strong> <code>crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:60</code> (and the <code>view</code> path at <code>:42</code>). <code>pdf_extract::extract_text_from_mem</code> carries roughly twenty <code>panic!</code>/<code>todo!</code> sites for structures <code>lopdf</code> loads but <code>pdf-extract</code> 0.12 does not handle (an unsupported CMap, an image soft mask, a missing glyph width). The call site maps <code>Err</code>, not an unwind, so a single crafted-but-loadable PDF aborts the CLI instead of returning <code>Error::Refused</code>. (Mechanism certain; the trigger is a specific PDF.)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The calendar reader returns success on malformed input.</strong> <code>crates/calendar/src/lib.rs:94</code>. <code>calendar_shape</code> (and <code>vcard_shape</code>) match only <code>Entry::ICalendar</code>/<code>Entry::VCard</code>; calcard's error variants (<code>InvalidLine</code>, <code>UnterminatedComponent</code>, <code>UnexpectedComponentEnd</code>) are dropped. A truncated <code>.ics</code> (a <code>BEGIN:VCALENDAR</code> with no matching <code>END</code>), or pure garbage, returns <code>Ok("calendar: 0 components")</code>, a silent partial the contract bans. (The parser terminates, so this is a silent-success bug, not a hang.)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>An overlay <code>TextQuote</code> selector silently re-anchors to the wrong occurrence.</strong> <code>crates/overlay/src/lib.rs:54</code>. When the <code>prefix + exact + suffix</code> context no longer matches (for example after a re-derivation drops surrounding text), resolution falls back to <code>text.find(exact)</code>, the <em>first</em> bare occurrence. For <code>"on the cat, off the cat"</code> with <code>prefix:"off "</code>, the annotation re-anchors to offset 0 instead of 12, and <code>write_back</code> then splices the edit into the wrong span with no ambiguity error, the opposite of the "survives re-derivation" property selectors exist to provide. Confirmed by execution.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The image and OCR readers claim the same extensions; the image reader wins and OCR is dead.</strong> <code>crates/cli/src/main.rs:95</code> and <code>:99</code>. Both <code>detect</code> exactly <code>png|jpg|jpeg|gif|bmp|tif|tiff|webp</code>, and <code>pick</code> returns the first reader whose <code>detect</code> is true, in registry-push order; <code>image</code> is pushed first. A build with both features (<code>--features "image ocr"</code>) routes every raster to image metadata, so the OCR reader never runs. The recognised-text path is silently unreachable in that configuration.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A format hint is not lowercased, so an uppercase extension is reported unsupported.</strong> <code>crates/cli/src/main.rs:124</code>. Every <code>detect</code> matches lowercase tokens only. <code>host-reference skeleton README.MD</code> (or <code>PHOTO.JPG</code>, <code>data.JSON</code>) yields "unsupported: no normaliser is registered for this kind" even with the relevant feature enabled. Common, legitimate input is rejected.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The prose and HTML heading outlines ignore fenced code blocks.</strong> <code>crates/prose/src/lib.rs:89</code> and <code>crates/html/src/lib.rs:38</code>. A line beginning with <code>#</code> then a space is treated as an ATX heading with no fence awareness, so a <code>#</code> line inside a triple-backtick block is emitted as a spurious outline entry, with a source-map span pointing at the code line. Wrong skeleton on very ordinary Markdown.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The out-of-process helpers are resolved by PATH or an environment variable and are not pinned.</strong> <code>crates/ocr/src/lib.rs:74</code> and <code>crates/openscad/src/lib.rs:82</code>. The skeleton body and token counts of these two readers are the stdout of <code>host-reference-ocr-helper</code> / <code>host-reference-openscad-helper</code>, selected from <code>HOST_REFERENCE_OCR_HELPER</code> / <code>HOST_REFERENCE_OPENSCAD_HELPER</code> or a bare PATH lookup, neither of which is in <code>Cargo.lock</code>. The same source bytes yield different attested skeletons across machines or helper versions, directly against the "pure function of the source bytes and the pinned toolchain" premise. The goldens stay green only because the conformance tests stub the helper.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Both out-of-process helpers stage input at a predictable shared temp path.</strong> <code>crates/ocr/src/lib.rs:80</code> and <code>crates/openscad/src/lib.rs:89</code>. The path is <code>temp_dir()/host-reference-ocr-<content_id>.<ext></code> (and the OpenSCAD analogue), fully predictable from the bytes, opened with <code>File::create</code> (follows symlinks, truncates) and removed unconditionally. A pre-planted symlink at that path is followed and its target truncated (a local symlink attack); two concurrent calls on the same bytes collide, with one's truncate or <code>remove_file</code> racing the other's helper read. That race is non-deterministic and surfaces as an intermittent "helper failed". An <code>O_EXCL</code> temp file with a random suffix is the fix.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The overlay lens is not very-well-behaved, and the proptests do not test the law they name.</strong> <code>crates/overlay/tests/lens_law.rs:45</code> (and <code>:6</code>).
