The fixed-offset splice lens violates PutPut whenever a replacement's length differs from the span it replaces: for <code>"abcdef"</code>, origin <code>2..4</code>, <code>v="X"</code> then <code>w="QQ"</code>, <code>put(put(s,v),w)</code> is <code>"abQQf"</code> but <code>put(s,w)</code> is <code>"abQQef"</code> (confirmed by execution), so the "well-behaved lens" claim in <code>src/lib.rs:5</code> is only partly true. The PutPut law is neither stated nor tested, and the <code>put_get</code> test re-implements the splice formula as its own oracle rather than composing a read-back through <code>get</code>, so it cannot catch a <code>get</code>/<code>put</code> mismatch.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>CI never compiles the CLI with any non-default reader feature.</strong> <code>.github/workflows/ci.yml</code> (the <code>build</code>, <code>test</code>, and <code>lint</code> jobs). The build uses default (<code>text</code>) features; <code>cargo test --workspace</code> and <code>cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets</code> build the <code>host-reference</code> crate with default features too. Each reader crate is exercised as a workspace <em>member</em>, but the CLI's <code>#[cfg(feature = "office")]</code> (and the other sixteen non-default) <code>reg.push(...)</code> arms and their <code>use</code> imports are compiled by no job. Rename a type in a heavy reader and forget the CLI: CI is green, but <code>cargo build --features office</code> breaks for a consumer. A <code>--all-features</code> (or per-feature) compile job closes it.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A reStructuredText section title drops all inline markup.</strong> <code>crates/rst/src/lib.rs:108</code>. <code>inline_text</code> collects only <code>TextOrInlineElement::String</code> children, so a title with emphasis, strong, or literal markup renders with those portions silently omitted: <code>Install </code>pip<code> </code> yields <code>Install </code>, and a title that is entirely markup (<code>*Important*</code>) yields an empty or <code>(untitled)</code> entry. Wrong outline in the attested skeleton.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The SPICE net heuristic counts comments and value tokens as nets.</strong> <code>crates/netlist/src/lib.rs:73</code>. Every token between the first and the last on a line is treated as a net, so <code>R1 in out 1k ; load resistor</code> yields nets <code>{in, out, 1k, ;, load}</code> (five) rather than <code>{in, out}</code>, and <code>V1 in 0 DC 5</code> yields <code>{in, 0, DC}</code>. The wrong (but stable) net set is baked into the conformance golden.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The canonical serialized form has no delimiter escaping, so document content can inject a section break.</strong> <code>crates/core/src/lib.rs:199</code> together with the data reader's <code>field</code>/<code>shape</code> (<code>crates/data/src/lib.rs</code>). <code>serialize_tier0</code> emits the markdown body verbatim between the literal lines <code>== markdown ==</code>, <code>== source-map ==</code>, and <code>== tokens ==</code>. The data reader interpolates JSON object keys (and CSV headers) into the body unescaped, and a JSON key may contain a real newline. A document <code>{"x\n== source-map ==\ny": 1}</code> injects a second literal <code>== source-map ==</code> line into the markdown section, so any consumer that parses the canonical attested form mis-splits it. The form needs an escape or a length-prefixed framing.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="further-correctness-findings"><a class="header" href="#further-correctness-findings">Further correctness findings</a></h2> <p>Beyond the ranked fifteen, all real, cut only by the output cap:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>The HTML <code>view</code> reports the wrong source-map origin.</strong> <code>crates/html/src/lib.rs:99</code>. <code>view</code> returns a slice of the <em>converted</em> markdown (<code>md[start..end]</code>) but reports <code>origin: 0..bytes.len()</code>, the raw-HTML byte length. The span neither reflects the returned window nor points at the true origin of the returned text, so it breaks the bidirectional source map. (The <code>data</code> <code>view</code> is correct because its text is the source bytes; the HTML conversion makes the offsets incomparable.)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The PDF title is decoded as UTF-8 when PDF strings are commonly UTF-16BE.</strong> <code>crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:76</code>. <code>pdf_title</code> runs <code>from_utf8_lossy</code> over the Info <code>/Title</code> bytes; a Word- or Acrobat-exported title carried as UTF-16BE (BOM <code>0xFEFF</code>) decodes to mojibake. Wrong, but deterministic, skeleton output.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The Parquet conformance golden is pinned to the <code>parquet-rs</code> patch version.</strong> <code>crates/columnar/tests/conformance.rs</code> and its golden. The test generates the Parquet buffer in memory; the bytes embed <code>created_by = "parquet-rs version X.Y.Z"</code>, so the golden's content id (<code>e9b68265a677</code>) and <code>raw_tokens</code> (721) are a function of the dependency version, not the source. <code>Cargo.toml</code> pins <code>parquet = "59"</code> (a caret range), so a routine <code>cargo update</code> within the range changes the golden and the test fails with a confusing "tier-0 drifted" message unrelated to any source change. The Arrow golden is immune (Arrow IPC embeds no version string), which makes the asymmetry concrete. <code>--locked</code> CI does not flake; a maintainer bumping the lock would.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The audio reader fabricates a duration from a hostile chunk size.</strong> <code>crates/av/src/lib.rs:92</code>. <code>audio_shape</code> trusts the declared data-chunk count; a WAV with a bogus <code>data</code> size (<code>0xFFFFFFFF</code>) yields an "attested" duration that is a lie derived from the header, where the contract wants a refusal.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The audio-visual reader can panic on a malformed MP4 box.</strong> <code>crates/av/src/lib.rs:103</code>. An MP4 whose 32-bit box size is smaller than the 8-byte header, or larger than the file, can drive an under/overflow in <code>mp4</code> 0.14's box parsing; the panic propagates out of <code>skeleton</code> (no <code>catch_unwind</code>) instead of refusing. A concrete instance of finding 2.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The office and EPUB readers have no resource bound.</strong> <code>crates/office/src/lib.rs:53</code> and <code>crates/epub/src/lib.rs:55</code>. Raw bytes go straight to <code>undoc</code> / <code>rbook</code>, whose zip layer decompresses parts without a cap, so a small deflate-bomb archive expands to multiple gigabytes and OOMs or hangs rather than refusing. Concrete instances of finding 2.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A degenerate overlay <code>TextQuote</code> resolves to an empty span rather than <code>None</code>.</strong> <code>crates/overlay/src/lib.rs:50</code>. An empty <code>exact</code> makes <code>str::find("")</code> return <code>Some(0)</code>, so a meaningless selector resolves to <code>0..0</code> and <code>write_back</code> builds an empty-span insertion at byte 0 instead of refusing.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A dotless path routes by its whole filename.</strong> <code>crates/cli/src/main.rs:124</code>. <code>hint</code> is <code>path.rsplit('.').next()</code>, so a file literally named <code>net</code> (or <code>org</code>, <code>obj</code>, <code>step</code>, <code>env</code>) has hint <code>net</code> and is parsed as a SPICE netlist. Unusual input, real misroute.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The <code>view</code> of most metadata readers ignores its selector.</strong> <code>crates/rtf/src/lib.rs:50</code>, and similarly <code>av</code>, <code>columnar</code>, <code>eda</code>, <code>geometry</code>, <code>image</code>, <code>office</code>, <code>epub</code>, <code>mail</code>, <code>openscad</code>, <code>pdf</code>. A windowed or token-budgeted request silently returns the whole document and blows any token budget the caller relied on. For the tiny engineering tallies this is harmless; for the RTF de-styled text it is a real deviation from the trait's documented windowed slice.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>An obligation is discharged by the wrong test.</strong> <code>host-reference.obligations:35</code>. <code>rule-failure.Window.1</code> is the hostile-input branch of the Window rule (<code>not source.hostile</code>), but it is mapped to <code>window_refuses_an_unsupported_selector</code>, which exercises selector refusal, a different concern. With no <code>hostile</code> field on <code>Source</code>, the failure path is discharged in name only.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>No <code>cargo fmt --check</code> runs in CI.</strong> <code>.github/workflows/ci.yml</code> (the <code>lint</code> job). The job gates clippy with <code>-D warnings</code> and <code>cargo-deny</code>, but never checks formatting, so source-format drift can land on a repo whose premise is reproducible artifacts. Low severity (style, not correctness).</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="overlay-lens-laws-and-proptest-integrity"><a class="header" href="#overlay-lens-laws-and-proptest-integrity">Overlay lens laws and proptest integrity</a></h2> <p>The overlay's "lens law" proptests are the weakest verification in the PR; findings 11 and the empty <code>TextQuote</code> above are the substantive bugs, and these are the test-integrity gaps around them (<code>crates/overlay/tests/lens_law.rs</code> and <code>tests/overlay.rs</code>):</p> <ul> <li>The law tests construct the <code>Edit</code> by hand from pre-clamped, pre-sorted offsets and call <code>normalizer.put</code> directly, so neither <code>resolve</code> (selector to range, with its bounds and boundary checks) nor <code>write_back</code> (selector to <code>Edit</code>) is ever property-tested for any law.</li> <li>The text generators are <code>".{0,80}"</code>, which excludes newlines, the one character that makes the prose normaliser's structure non-trivial, so the prose lens law never sees multi-line input.</li> <li>The reversed-range guards (<code>end.max(start)</code> in <code>put</code>, the <code>start <= end</code> branch in <code>resolve</code>) are never exercised, because every test pre-sorts its offsets.</li> <li>The CRDT merge test (<code>tests/overlay.rs:31</code>) asserts only one merge direction and set membership, not convergence or deterministic ordering, and <code>Overlay::new</code> carries a random peer id, so a non-convergent or order-divergent merge would still pass.</li> </ul> <h2 id="reuse-simplification-and-altitude"><a class="header" href="#reuse-simplification-and-altitude">Reuse, simplification, and altitude</a></h2> <p>Quality observations on the new code, in descending value. These are not defects in behaviour; the cost named is duplication or a metric that does not mean what it claims.</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>The golden-test scaffolding is copy-pasted across roughly twenty-three <code>conformance.rs</code> files</strong> (<code>crates/*/tests/conformance.rs</code>) and differs only by the normaliser type name. A shared <code>testkit::check_fixture::<N: Normalizer></code> in a dev-dependency crate would own the bless protocol, the golden filename, and the drift message once instead of in twenty-three places.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>floor_boundary</code> and the UTF-8 decode helper are each defined identically in eleven-to-thirteen crates</strong> (<code>prose</code>, <code>data</code>, <code>config</code>, <code>rst</code>, <code>asciidoc</code>, <code>org</code>, <code>rtf</code>, <code>bibtex</code>, <code>calendar</code>, <code>netlist</code>, <code>vector</code>). They belong in <code>core</code>; a fix to boundary handling currently has to be applied in every copy and can drift between them.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Every reader hand-builds the <code>Tier0</code></strong> (content id, two token counts, a whole-document span), and the text readers repeat an identical <code>CharOffset</code> <code>view</code> body. A <code>Tier0::whole(source, outline)</code> constructor and a <code>core::char_offset_view</code> helper would collapse both.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>raw_tokens</code> is computed three incompatible ways:</strong> <code>count_tokens(text)</code> (text readers), <code>count_tokens(&from_utf8_lossy(bytes))</code> (<code>pdf</code>, <code>geometry</code>, <code>columnar</code>, <code>eda</code>, <code>epub</code>, <code>mail</code>, <code>office</code>, <code>openscad</code>), and bare <code>bytes.len()</code> (<code>image</code>, <code>av</code>, <code>ocr</code>). The headline savings ratio the <code>Tier0</code> design exists to report is therefore measured on different bases across modalities and is not comparable. The basis decision belongs in one <code>core</code> policy.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The <code>view</code> boilerplate that ignores its selector</strong> (the further-finding above) would disappear behind a default trait method on <code>Normalizer</code> that returns the skeleton's markdown when no windowing is supported.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The registry dispatches by first match in insertion order, with no collision check</strong> (<code>crates/cli/src/main.rs</code>). The order is load-bearing but unenforced; a registry keyed by extension would make dispatch explicit and surface the image/OCR collision (finding 6) at construction instead of as a silent wrong pick.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The ATX-heading outline is implemented twice</strong> (<code>prose</code> and <code>html</code>). A <code>core::markdown_heading_outline</code> would serve both and any future Markdown-targeting reader.</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="what-was-checked-and-cleared"><a class="header" href="#what-was-checked-and-cleared">What was checked and cleared</a></h2> <p>The negative results matter as much as the findings: they say what a remediation plan does not need to re-examine. All confirmed at the reviewed revision.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Determinism is otherwise clean.</strong> No <code>HashMap</code> or <code>HashSet</code> reaches serialized output anywhere in <code>crates/*/src</code>; every tally is a <code>Vec</code> or <code>BTreeMap</code>/<code>BTreeSet</code> and is sorted before emission. <code>serde_json</code> is at its default (sorted <code>BTreeMap</code>, no <code>preserve_order</code> anywhere), and the data reader sorts object keys regardless. <code>ply-rs-bw</code> is backed by <code>indexmap</code> (file order), EXIF fields are sorted, MP4 tracks are sorted by id, config keys are sorted. No float is formatted into any golden (every numeric output is an integer count or the exif crate's exact rational display). No time, randomness, environment, or threading reaches output, with the sole exception of the two out-of-process helpers (findings 9 and 10).</li> <li><strong>The conformance fixtures are sound.</strong> Every normaliser crate ships a <code>tests/conformance.rs</code> on one correct pattern: load or generate the input, <code>serialize_tier0(skeleton)</code>, and <code>assert_eq!</code> against a committed golden. The golden is rewritten only under <code>HOST_REFERENCE_BLESS=1</code>, which returns immediately, so a normal run never writes the file it then reads. All golden files are tracked and non-empty; <code>cargo test --workspace --locked</code> runs the assertions; no <code>#[ignore]</code>, no <code>assert!(true)</code>, no self-comparison, no early return. The OCR test golden encodes a stub helper's fixed output (finding 9), which is correctly scoped to this crate rather than the engine that lives out of process.</li> <li><strong>The removed-behaviour audit is clean.</strong> The only deletions in the diff are the version bump, the expanded members list, the regenerated <code>Cargo.lock</code>, and the old CLI placeholder stub (a blanket refusal) replaced by real registry dispatch. Every error path from the stub is re-established (missing path, unknown command, unknown kind all exit 2 with a clean error); <code>deny.toml</code> and <code>.gitignore</code> are new files, not edits.</li> <li><strong>Workspace coverage is consistent.</strong> Every crate directory is in the workspace <code>members</code>; every reader has a matching CLI feature and a <code>registry()</code> push; <code>overlay</code> is correctly not a CLI reader.</li> <li><strong>The licence lane is complete.</strong> Every otherwise-unallowed SPDX token in the tree appears only as an OR alternative beside an allowed licence; the three advisory ignores are unmaintained-only and mask no vulnerability; AGPL is banned and GPL flagged, with the GPL confined to the OpenSCAD helper's own repository.</li> <li><strong>The core helpers hold.</strong> <code>serialize_tier0</code>'s span sort key <code>(start, end, source)</code> is a total, stable order; <code>count_tokens</code>'s <code>expect</code> loads the vocab embedded in the crate, so it cannot fail at runtime; <code>content_id</code>'s six-byte prefix is fine for keying a single source's map. The CLI's argv handling is panic-free (missing arguments and a directory path map to an <code>Error</code>).</li> <li><strong>The named library panics did not reproduce.</strong> <code>stl_io</code> streams triangles and does not preallocate from a declared count, <code>ply-rs-bw</code> caps preallocation, and the G-code and SPICE paths return <code>Error::Parse</code> rather than indexing into absent coordinates.</li> </ul> <h2 id="disposition"><a class="header" href="#disposition">Disposition</a></h2> <p>Everything above is recorded for a future remediation plan and is not actioned in this milestone. The must-fix cluster, when that plan is cut, is findings 1 through 4: bound the selector at its source, and make the readers return <code>Error::Refused</code> on a resource bound or a hostile structure instead of panicking, hanging, or silently zeroing. That is the call/0031 contract the component asserts but does not yet keep. The determinism discipline and the conformance fixtures are sound foundations to build that on.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0051-host-lifecycle-review-findings-and-component-remediation"><a class="header" href="#plan0051-host-lifecycle-review-findings-and-component-remediation">plan/0051 host-lifecycle review: findings and component remediation</a></h1> <p>This milestone records a maximum-effort review of <code>host-lifecycle</code>, the lifecycle gate, generator, and migrator, and remediates its component-local findings. It is the first review in the campaign reserved for software other than <code>host-reference</code> (whose review is plan/0050).</p> <p>The review was driven inside our own tooling rather than by the external lane that produced plan/0050: a multi-agent pass of nine reviewers across the functional surfaces, then adversarial verification of every raised finding, then synthesis. That was a deliberate test of whether an in-house review is as effective as the external pass. It found a genuine headline defect and the adversarial layer culled a large fraction of the raised findings, so the answer for our own components is yes.</p> <h2 id="the-cross-cutting-result-is-split-out"><a class="header" href="#the-cross-cutting-result-is-split-out">The cross-cutting result is split out</a></h2> <p>The review found that a verification lane can report clean without performing its check. The obligation-discharge check confirms only that a test name resolves, never that the named test exercises the rule; and <code>software --verify-build</code> attests "every non-exempt build reproduces its recorded artifact" even when no build was rebuilt (no container runtime present). The same discharge gap appeared independently in the host-reference review (plan/0050), which makes it methodology-level, not a host-lifecycle bug.</p> <p><strong>plan/0052 (no-hollow-green)</strong> owns that cross-cutting doctrine and its cast-reviewed design. The findings that belong to it (findings 1, 3, 4, 5, 10, and 17 below) are recorded here for the audit trail and dispositioned <em>remediated in plan/0052</em>. Everything else is component-local and fixed in this milestone.</p> <h2 id="what-was-reviewed-1"><a class="header" href="#what-was-reviewed-1">What was reviewed</a></h2> <ul> <li>Component: <code>host-lifecycle</code> at its pinned release (<code>cbe72e6</code>, v0.31.2): the single <code>src/main.rs</code> (about 9,557 lines, 356 functions, 115 inline tests), its <code>host-lifecycle.allium</code> spec, and its <code>host-lifecycle.obligations</code> manifest.</li> <li>Method: nine reviewers, one per functional surface (subprocess handling, path safety, reproducibility, receipts, manifest parsing, doc gates, fail-safe discipline, reuse, test adequacy), each over the real code. An adversarial verifier then tried to refute every raised finding against the source; a finding it could not substantiate defaulted to refuted. A synthesis pass deduped and ranked the survivors.</li> <li>Result: 44 findings raised, 17 refuted by verification, 27 surviving, deduped to 24 ranked. Zero critical, zero high, 6 medium, 18 low. The verification pass corrected several severities and rejected several reviewer exploits as self-defeating or factually wrong.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-contract-the-findings-test-against-1"><a class="header" href="#the-contract-the-findings-test-against-1">The contract the findings test against</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Fail-safe gates.</strong> Every gate subcommand (<code>software --check</code>, the <code>release</code> verify gate, <code>prose</code>, <code>reconcile</code>, <code>entrance --check</code>, <code>obligations</code>) must fail closed: HAZARD or non-zero on doubt, no silent skip, no partial mutation. A gate that passes when it should HAZARD, or that attests a guarantee it did not establish, is the most severe class.</li> <li><strong>Determinism (call/0018, call/0030).</strong> Discharge is byte-identical re-derivation in a pinned toolchain. The artifact-hash comparison, the deps-bundle drift check, and toolchain-pin enforcement must be sound.</li> <li><strong>Receipts (call/0042).</strong> The task graph is gated by receipts, latest-receipt-wins, and staleness detected on an input change; a milestone reads complete only once its task receipts land.</li> <li><strong>Host-root escape (DetectOffPin).</strong> No worktree or path may escape the host root, and a tracked symlink into an un-materialized worktree is rejected.</li> <li><strong>Subprocess hygiene.</strong> Its external tools include git, curl, tar, sh, a container runtime, sha256sum, host-prove, allium. Unchecked exit status, a missing-tool fail-open, argument injection, and download-without-integrity are in scope.</li> </ul> <h2 id="findings-remediated-in-plan0052"><a class="header" href="#findings-remediated-in-plan0052">Findings remediated in plan/0052</a></h2> <p>These six are the no-hollow-green cluster. They are listed here for completeness, with the same line references the review cited; their remediation, doctrine, and the cast review live in plan/0052.</p> <ol> <li><strong><code>software --verify-build</code> attests "every build reproduces" with no container runtime.</strong> <code>src/main.rs:3450</code> skips each build when <code>container_runtime()</code> returns <code>None</code> without incrementing the failure count, then <code>:3510</code> prints the clean guarantee and exits 0 having rebuilt and compared nothing. The sibling <code>release</code> path at <code>:7290</code> blocks on the identical condition, so the correct fail-closed behaviour already exists one lane over. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Seven hazarded-verdict and DetectOffPin obligations are dispositioned to a pure-function test.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle.obligations:22,24,40,41,42,45,51</code> all point at <code>host_root_escape_is_detected</code> (<code>src/main.rs:8416</code>), which asserts only the helper <code>escapes_root</code> and never calls <code>software_check</code>, produces a Finding, settles a verdict, or observes an exit. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>DetectUnreproducedArtifact is dispositioned to a test that proves the rule does not bite.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle.obligations:28</code> names <code>provenance_attestation_and_exemption</code>, which exercises the benign-note path and sets <code>build: None</code> so the rule's precondition is never satisfied. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Receipt re-derivation obligations are mapped to tests that do not exercise re-derivation.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle.obligations:32,50</code> name a book-layout test and a parse test (a name collision on the word "record"); the genuine staleness enforcement is tested elsewhere but not by the named obligations. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>software --check</code> under-enforces DetectArtifactNotReproducible.</strong> <code>provenance_problems</code> (<code>src/main.rs:4439</code>) fires on artifact plus no-toolchain, but never on the rule's second disjunct (artifact plus no build recipe), which is caught only in the heavy <code>--verify-build</code> lane. (confirmed, latent)</li> <li><strong>The plan/0048 re-deriver-runnability gate lacks an automated test for its HAZARD branch.</strong> <code>tier_rederiver_problems</code> (<code>src/main.rs:4607</code>) HAZARDs when a declared deep rung cannot run, but the only test asserts the green path; the HAZARD branch, added because a missing host-prove install hid for two weeks, has no coverage. (confirmed, low)</li> </ol> <h2 id="component-findings-remediated-in-this-milestone"><a class="header" href="#component-findings-remediated-in-this-milestone">Component findings, remediated in this milestone</a></h2> <p>The eighteen component-local findings, in the review's rank order.</p> <ol start="2"> <li><strong><code>software --materialize</code> does not enforce the host-root-escape guard that <code>--check</code> enforces.</strong> <code>escapes_root</code> runs only in <code>software_check</code>; the mutating <code>software_materialize</code> (<code>src/main.rs:3831</code>) never calls it, so a <code>.host-software</code> name or branch containing <code>..</code> could place a bare store or worktree above the host root, and the fresh-clone flow runs <code>--materialize</code> before <code>--check</code>. The realistic blast radius is litter in the wrong location, because the manifest is trusted operator config and git refuses a non-empty target, but the defensive asymmetry is real. Fix: call <code>escapes_root</code> on the name, branch, and worktree entries at the top of <code>software_materialize</code> (and reject in the parser), reusing the exact checks <code>software_check</code> runs so the two paths cannot diverge. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The deps-bundle provenance cross-check silently no-ops when the lock is absent.</strong> <code>provenance_problems</code> (<code>src/main.rs:4464</code>) prints a note and does not fault when it cannot read <code>deps-bundle.lock</code>. The reviewer's framing (absence equals corruption, HAZARD always) is wrong: the live recipe has legitimately-onboarding components that declare a bundle and have no lock yet, and that fix would turn <code>--check</code> red for them. The real, narrow gap is that deleting a tracked lock in a materialized worktree leaves the cross-check bypassed while the pin reads clean. <strong>Engineered, not applied verbatim:</strong> gate the lenient note on an explicit not-yet-locked condition and HAZARD a missing lock only for a materialized component that declares a bundle. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong>The task skip gate accepts an arbitrary free-text reason, weaker than the recorder.</strong> <code>task_verdict</code> (<code>src/main.rs:2474</code>) validates the reason only when it begins with <code>call/</code>; a non-citation reason such as <code>wip</code> falls through to a pass, where the recorder <code>tasks_record</code> requires a valid citation and exits non-zero. The gate is the fail-safe authority over hand-edited receipt files, so the asymmetry lets work through with an unaccountable justification. Fix: require a valid cited decision in the skip arm and HAZARD otherwise. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>tasks --rederive</code> reports success when the verify passes but the receipt cannot be written.</strong> <code>tasks_rederive</code> (<code>src/main.rs:2846</code>) prints a cannot-write note and increments neither the failure nor the refreshed count, so a run where every verify passed but every write failed exits 0 having persisted nothing. The manual-record path treats the same error as fatal. Fix: treat the write error as a failure so the exit code reflects the unpersisted state. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>migrate-receipts</code> writes three files with per-file atomicity only; the set of three has none.</strong> <code>migrate_receipts</code> (<code>src/main.rs:6789</code>) writes the stamp (which strips the applied lines) before the receipts file (which should receive them), so an I/O fault between the two strips the applied set out of the stamp while the receipts file never receives it, recoverable only through git. Fix: write the data-receiving file before the data-shedding file, or stage all three and rename in dependency order. (confirmed, low)</li> <li><strong><code>milestone_complete</code> reads raw markdown while <code>parse_tasks</code> masks fenced code.</strong> Within the task gate the two plan-README sub-parsers disagree on fences (<code>src/main.rs:2497</code> versus <code>:2141</code>), so a fenced <code>## Status</code> example flips the receipt-gating completeness verdict. This weakens the gate whose purpose is to refuse a complete milestone whose receipts have not landed. Fix: run <code>milestone_complete</code> over the fence-masked view, or factor one fence-aware document scan shared by every plan-doc check. (confirmed, latent)</li> <li><strong>The reconcile concept and link-integrity gate has no fence masking.</strong> <code>scan_concept_anchors</code> and <code>concept_links_on</code> (<code>src/main.rs:1583</code>) scan raw lines with only a per-line backtick guard, so a heading or link inside a fenced example is treated as a live concept home or link; the result is a false duplicate-home HAZARD or a dead-anchor link that passes. The sibling task gate already tracks fence state, so the two markdown gates disagree on identical input. Fix: thread the fence-masked view through the concept and reconcile scans. (confirmed, latent)</li> <li><strong>Two divergent readers decide whether a deep rung is declared.</strong> The tier gate uses a raw substring <code>contains("kani:")</code> over concatenated obligation bodies (<code>src/main.rs:4532</code>) while the obligations engine parses dispositions and requires <code>parse_rung</code> to see the prefix as a real token (<code>:4857</code>), so a comment line or a non-rung disposition makes the gate demand a CI lane and a re-deriver for a tier the engine does not treat as a rung. Fix: have the lane gate parse manifests with the same parser the engine uses. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>[verification]</code> is not a singleton and <code>drivers</code> is last-wins.</strong> <code>parse_project_facts</code> guards <code>[entrance]</code> against duplicates and emptiness but not <code>[verification]</code> (<code>src/main.rs:1398</code>), so a second stanza, a repeated key, or an empty <code>drivers</code> silently disarms the reconcile verifier-coverage check. Fix: mirror the <code>[entrance]</code> handling (count stanzas, flag a repeated key, treat an empty <code>drivers</code> as a problem). (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The software-root and spec-home concepts have only link-integrity, no content bite.</strong> <code>concept_checks</code> (<code>src/main.rs:1702</code>) runs the content check only for components and verifiers; the single-value homes get anchor and link checks but no content verification, and the old predicate that checked their content runs only over the deprecated inline annotations agentic-host has deleted. <strong>Engineered, not applied verbatim:</strong> the reviewer's lift-the-old-predicate fix is unsound (the real spec-home text "never under plan/" would false-positive); add a content assertion correct against the canonical wording instead. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>A duplicate <code>[software "<name>"]</code> stanza is silently accepted.</strong> <code>parse_software</code> (<code>src/main.rs:3537</code>) pushes a fresh entry per header with no duplicate-name detection; materialize and release act on the first, so the second's url is ignored. The project-facts parser already flags duplicates, so this is an inconsistency. Fix: reject duplicate component names with a precise error. (confirmed, low)</li> <li><strong><code>milestone_complete</code> reads a narrow completion lexicon only from the milestone README.</strong> Completion is recognised only when the first line under <code>## Status</code> begins with complete, done, or landed (<code>src/main.rs:2497</code>); a synonym, a markdown bullet, or completion marked only in PLAN.md reads as open. Every live plan uses the recognised words today, so this is a missed nudge, not a false complete. Fix: broaden the lexicon and strip list markers. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong>The reconcile coverage check uses substring rather than token matching.</strong> <code>cover</code> (<code>src/main.rs:1697</code>) tests membership with <code>str::contains</code>, and <code>host-reference</code> is a substring of the longer helper names. The reviewer's cited exploit is self-defeating (the example still contains the token as a delimited word), and STRUCTURE.md names all members today, so it is a precision gap in a recall-biased heuristic, not currently triggered. Fix: match on token boundaries. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong>The entrance tools coverage is an un-anchored substring search over the whole document.</strong> <code>entrance_problems</code> (<code>src/main.rs:1860</code>) checks each wired tool with a whole-document substring, so a tool named only inside a URL or a fence satisfies the restatement. The doc-comment marks this as an intentional lenient-presence choice and a test asserts it, so it is a genuine bug-versus-intent ambiguity. Fix, if treated as a defect: require the token at a word boundary in masked prose; otherwise record the intent. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong>Recorded artifact, hooks, and deps paths bypass the escapes_root guard.</strong> These paths feed <code>Path::join</code> without the lexical guard applied to name and branch (<code>src/main.rs:3652</code>), and an absolute artifact path replaces the base so <code>--verify-build</code> would hash a file outside the throwaway worktree. The manifest is trusted operator config and the footgun is largely self-detecting, so this is defence-in-depth. Fix: reject an absolute or escaping artifact, hooks, or deps path in the parser. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong><code>release</code> stages the deps-bundle into the live canonical worktree.</strong> An abnormal termination between staging and restore (<code>src/main.rs:7352</code>) leaves vendored deps and an edited <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> behind, with no Drop guard. The vendored files are gitignored and the tool never commits, so the operator sees the modified tracked file in git status before any commit. Fix: stage in a throwaway detached worktree as <code>--verify-build</code> does, or register the restore on a Drop guard, or refuse to proceed when a prior staged snippet is detected. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong>There is no single shared markdown document view.</strong> The heading and anchor primitives are already shared functions, so the headline is overstated; the genuine kernel is that the inline backtick guard is hand-copied at several sites and two block-fence loops exist. No correctness defect follows directly; the fence divergences in findings 11 and 12 are the concrete cost. Fix: consolidate the duplicated inline-backtick guard and unify the two block-fence loops. (uncertain)</li> <li><strong><code>collect_files</code> follows symlinks.</strong> It classifies entries with <code>is_dir</code>/<code>is_file</code> (which follow symlinks) with no guard, unlike the sibling <code>tracked_markdown</code> which skips symlinks (<code>src/main.rs:864</code>). <code>remap</code> is an operator-run self-targeting migration that refuses on a dirty tree and acts only on the operator's own dictionary, so there is no untrusted-input vector; this is the lowest-ranked finding (verdict uncertain, reachable false). Fix: take the type from the DirEntry without following, and skip symlinks as the sibling <code>tracked_markdown</code> does. (uncertain)</li> </ol> <h2 id="what-was-checked-and-cleared-1"><a class="header" href="#what-was-checked-and-cleared-1">What was checked and cleared</a></h2> <p>The negatives bound the work. The review confirmed the verification ladder's deep rungs already discharge correctly (the <code>--rederive</code> path runs the verifier through host-prove and requires a PASS, and a missing re-deriver returns UNPROVEN and exits non-zero), so the no-hollow-green work in plan/0052 finishes an uneven application of a pattern the codebase already trusts, rather than inventing one. Determinism in the gate output, the receipt parse and latest-wins logic, and the manifest validation for url and pin presence are sound. The path-safety and manifest findings are bounded by <code>.host-software</code> being trusted, gitignored, operator-authored config.</p> <h2 id="disposition-1"><a class="header" href="#disposition-1">Disposition</a></h2> <p>The eighteen component findings are remediated in this milestone and shipped as host-lifecycle v0.33.0. Findings 6 and 15 are engineered rather than applied as the reviewers suggested. Finding 6 distinguishes a deleted tracked <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> (a HAZARD: the pin cross-check is bypassed) from a lock git never tracked (an onboarding note), so onboarding does not turn the check red. Finding 15 asserts the canonical wording of the software-root and spec-home homes (<code>software/</code>; co-location) rather than lifting the old inline predicate, whose <code>plan/</code>-and-<code>spec</code> form would have misfired on the real spec-home text "co-located ... never under <code>plan/</code>". Finding 20 is resolved by recording the entrance tool-presence leniency as deliberate: that check performs a real test, so it is not hollow green, and a word-boundary rule would still miss a token in a bare URL and could flag a legitimate phrasing. The six no-hollow-green findings (1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 17) are remediated in plan/0052 under its cast-reviewed doctrine. The review campaign stays open: the reviews of host-lint, host-prove, and host-grammar are still pending, each to be cut under its own milestone.</p> <h2 id="status-12"><a class="header" href="#status-12">Status</a></h2> <p>Complete. Shipped as host-lifecycle <strong>v0.33.0</strong> (commit <code>08ba98b</code>, artifact <code>cffe14ba10c8ada02ad1d3e5c3c003d9d0c392ae5001225cf025c4ce5cdc9fab</code>), re-deriving byte-identically in the recorded <code>clux/muslrust</code> toolchain. The change is classed <code>removes-flag</code> because several gates now reject inputs they previously accepted (a duplicate <code>[software]</code> stanza, a free-text task skip reason, a deleted tracked lock, a second <code>[verification]</code> stanza). The release receipt is recorded, <code>software --check</code> is clean at the new pin, and the suite (118 tests, clippy, allium check and analyse, obligations discharge) is green. This milestone records no new <code>call/</code> decision; the only cross-cutting decision is plan/0052's <code>call/0035</code>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0052-no-hollow-green-a-lane-that-cannot-check-must-not-report-clean"><a class="header" href="#plan0052-no-hollow-green-a-lane-that-cannot-check-must-not-report-clean">plan/0052 no-hollow-green: a lane that cannot check must not report clean</a></h1> <p>This milestone states one doctrine and realises it: <strong>a verification lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean.</strong> A gate that reports clean without having run its check is worse than no gate, because it lies to the reader who cannot catch the lie: the cold auditor with no memory of intent, and the executor that reads the green as a signal to stop.</p> <h2 id="where-it-came-from"><a class="header" href="#where-it-came-from">Where it came from</a></h2> <p>The plan/0051 review of host-lifecycle found the doctrine violated in two lanes, and the plan/0050 review of host-reference found the same shape independently. Two independent components showing the same gap make it methodology-level, not a single component's bug.</p> <ul> <li><strong>The obligation-discharge lane.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle obligations</code> confirms only that a <code>test:<name></code> disposition names a test that exists (a substring check), never that the named test exercises the rule it discharges. Seven hazarded-verdict obligations in host-lifecycle's own manifest are dispositioned to a test that asserts a pure helper and never drives the gate, and the ladder stays green. The same pattern appeared in host-reference, where a hostile-input obligation was waived but unrealised with green CI.</li> <li><strong>The reproducible-build lane.</strong> <code>software --verify-build</code> skips every build when no container runtime is present and then prints "every non-exempt build reproduces its recorded artifact" and exits 0, attesting a guarantee it never checked.</li> </ul> <p>The deep rungs (<code>kani</code>, <code>apalache</code>, <code>tlaps</code>) already discharge correctly: the <code>--rederive</code> path runs the verifier through host-prove and requires a PASS, and a missing re-deriver returns UNPROVEN and exits non-zero (plan/0048). So this milestone finishes an uneven application of a pattern the codebase already trusts; it does not invent one.</p> <h2 id="the-cast-review"><a class="header" href="#the-cast-review">The cast review</a></h2> <p>A spine change is gated on a cast review (cast/applying-personas.md). All five personas reviewed both realisations. The converged verdict:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Reuse the rung lane.</strong> Strengthen the <code>test:</code> disposition the way the deep rungs already work, not with mutation rigs or coverage instrumentation (Mara, Wren: a flaky gate trains the reader to ignore red, which is hollow green wearing the opposite mask).</li> <li><strong>Auditable link, not proven behaviour</strong> (Orin). The always-on check verifies a static link: the named test resolves to exactly one test and names the rule's observable (its Finding kind or verdict transition). The heavier claim, that the test truly drives the rule, is an opt-in tool-applied check, and the residue the machine cannot prove is labelled <em>attested</em>, never written as if the machine proved it. A doctrine sentence the adopter cannot mechanically obey recreates hollow green one level up.</li> <li><strong>Three states, not two</strong> (all five). A lane distinguishes verified, legitimately-not-checked-here (a declared attest-host or a cited repro-exempt, an honest neutral skip), and could-not-check (a HAZARD). Only the third may never be rendered as the first. The verb is "report exactly what you established", not "HAZARD whenever you cannot check", so legitimate by-design skips do not turn adopter suites into hollow red.</li> <li><strong>Shut the escapes in the same change</strong> (Fen). Hardening <code>test:</code> without hardening the <code>waived:</code> and <code>structural</code> dispositions only moves the hole: a weak agent under a hard gate routes around it by relabelling. So <code>waived:</code> must cite a real <code>call/</code> decision (reusing the existing <code>cited_decision_exists</code> check, which today gates repro-exempt but not waived), and <code>structural</code> is cross-checked against the analyse lane.</li> <li><strong>Propagation is a breaking change</strong> (Orin, Bly). Tightening a shared gate turns every adopter's green <code>test:</code> dispositions red the instant they bump the tool, often as a transitive install decoupled from the upgrade ledger. So the tightening ships warn-then-retire, keyed at a revision, and the reject line self-references its own UPGRADING entry by revision key, with the entry marked <code>independent = true</code> so it can be applied alone.</li> </ul> <p>The weak agent (Fen, the real qwen3.5-4b) is the acceptance test for the discharge change, not a lens: the design's weak-agent claim is falsifiable and is to be falsified before the doctrine ships.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-10"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-10">Build sequence</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>#strengthen-discharge.</strong> Replace the substring check with: resolve to exactly one test (else AMBIGUOUS) and a static linkage check that the test names the rule's observable. Crisp HOLLOW reject that self-references its UPGRADING revision key. Harden the <code>waived:</code> and <code>structural</code> escapes in the same change. Ship as a warning first (deprecate-then-retire).</li> <li><strong>#three-state-verify-build.</strong> Never print the clean guarantee unless at least one in-scope build was actually rebuilt and matched. An in-scope build that could not run (no runtime, no pin) is UNVERIFIABLE, a distinct token from a real drift, exits non-zero, and carries its remedy inline. The declared attest-host and cited repro-exempt skips stay neutral.</li> <li><strong>#exercise-check.</strong> Extend <code>--rederive</code> to the <code>test:</code> rung: run the named test and require a PASS, and as an opt-in heavy check neutralise the rule and require the verdict to flip to FAIL, with the neutralisation applied by the tool, never authored by the weak agent.</li> <li><strong>#dogfood-redisposition.</strong> Re-disposition host-lifecycle's own manifest so the strengthened check turns its hollow green honest (the plan/0051 findings 3, 4, 5, 10, 17); this proves the check bites on the dogfood.</li> <li><strong>#probe.</strong> Drive the real qwen3.5-4b against the strengthened gate: can it author passing dispositions unaided, and on a red does it author an exercising test or route to mass-waive. This gates the doctrine and the release.</li> <li><strong>#spine-doctrine.</strong> Author the doctrine in host-template (the discharge link and the three-state reporting rule), with an UPGRADING entry staged warn-then-retire and marked <code>independent = true</code>, then adopt it into agentic-host through the revision-keyed upgrade ledger (copy-at-version).</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-13"><a class="header" href="#status-13">Status</a></h2> <p>Complete. The tool shipped as host-lifecycle <strong>v0.32.0</strong> (<code>call/0035</code>), re-deriving byte-identically: the obligation-discharge <code>exercises=</code> link escalated under <code>--strict-discharge</code>, the structural and waived escape checks, and the three-state verify-build. The cast review and the real qwen3.5-4b probe both passed; the 4B authored the correct link and rejected the link-gaming dodge on semantic grounds. The doctrine landed in host-template at <code>46a1fd2</code> with UPGRADING entry <code>46a1fd2</code>, recorded applied in agentic-host through its verify grep. host-lifecycle's own manifest is re-dispositioned, and <code>obligations --strict-discharge</code> over it is clean where it was hollow. The plan/0051 component remediation proceeds independently.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0053-host-grammar-review-findings-and-remediation"><a class="header" href="#plan0053-host-grammar-review-findings-and-remediation">plan/0053 host-grammar review: findings and remediation</a></h1> <p>This milestone records a maximum-effort review of <code>host-grammar</code>, the shared grammar both <code>host-lint</code> (the checker) and <code>host-lifecycle</code> (the generator) depend on as a git dependency, and remediates its findings. It is the next review in the campaign after <code>host-lifecycle</code> (plan/0051, plan/0052). The operator ordered it ahead of <code>host-lint</code> and <code>host-prove</code> because it is the shared base: fixing the dependency before its consumers means the consumer reviews build on a corrected foundation.</p> <h2 id="what-was-reviewed-2"><a class="header" href="#what-was-reviewed-2">What was reviewed</a></h2> <ul> <li>Component: <code>host-grammar</code> at its pinned release (<code>9d51468</code>, v0.3.0): the naming and number grammar (<code>src/lib.rs</code>, about 102 lines), the token-free agentic-tell prose engine (<code>src/tells.rs</code>, about 792 lines), the <code>host-grammar.allium</code> spec and its <code>host-grammar.obligations</code> manifest, the property tests (<code>tests/prose_properties.rs</code>), the three <code>spec/*.tla</code> deep-verification specs and their <code>spec/ParallelScan.obligations</code>, and the four CI workflows.</li> <li>Method: six independent reviewers, one per functional surface (the naming grammar and the generator-equals-checker symmetry; the lexical and per-sentence tells; the cross-sentence run equations and the parallel chunked scan; the markdown-aware path; the density scoring and the allium spec fidelity; the obligation-discharge honesty and CI integrity under the no-hollow-green doctrine). Each reviewer probed its own claims empirically against the built crate, marked every finding confirmed or speculative, and defaulted to speculative on doubt. Cross-reviewer duplicates were merged and the load-bearing findings were independently reproduced before remediation.</li> <li>Result: 34 findings raised, deduped to 31 (three were found by two reviewers each: the markdown heading-diction density inflation, the anaphora-plus-listicle double count, and the stale triad comment). Every finding was confirmed by an empirical probe; none survived as speculative only. Zero critical, zero high in the sense of a memory-safety or data-loss defect: the prose engine has no panics and the parallel scan is correct. The headline class is verification integrity (a fabricated test-coverage waiver, two invariants discharged by tests that do not exercise them) and detection precision (false positives a documentation gate would raise on clean prose).</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-contract-the-findings-test-against-2"><a class="header" href="#the-contract-the-findings-test-against-2">The contract the findings test against</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Generator equals checker.</strong> <code>host-grammar</code> exists so that what <code>host-lifecycle</code> emits is exactly what <code>host-lint</code> accepts. Any divergence between <code>format_number</code>, <code>is_valid_name</code>, <code>is_valid_slug</code>, and <code>is_numeral</code> and the producible set is the cardinal-invariant class.</li> <li><strong>The prose engine is advisory by density.</strong> An individual tell is advisory; the per-document density gate is what escalates. The engine must not panic (it gates commits and docs), must not raise a false positive on clean prose, and must not silently miss what it claims to catch.</li> <li><strong>Parallel equals sequential.</strong> <code>scan_chunked(text, k)</code> must equal <code>scan_prose(text)</code> for every chunk count, the property the allium and property-based lanes check and the three <code>.tla</code> specs model across worker interleavings.</li> <li><strong>No hollow green (plan/0052).</strong> A verification lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean. An obligation discharged by a test whose name resolves but which does not exercise the rule is the canonical violation; a waiver is the sanctioned escape only when it carries a real structural reason, never deferred backlog dressed as discharge.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-operator-decision"><a class="header" href="#the-operator-decision">The operator decision</a></h2> <p>The operator ruled <strong>fix everything toward precision</strong> and <strong>propagate now</strong>. The verification integrity, CI, and spec fidelity findings change no detection output and are fixed outright. The detection-behavior findings are tuned toward precision: every false positive a clean document would raise is pruned, and the clear bugs are engineered. After release, the new <code>host-grammar</code> is adopted by both consumers in this same session (each pins it by exact git rev), with the whole suite green across all three components.</p> <h2 id="findings-verification-integrity-ci-and-spec-fidelity"><a class="header" href="#findings-verification-integrity-ci-and-spec-fidelity">Findings: verification integrity, CI, and spec fidelity</a></h2> <p>These change no detection output. They are fixed in this milestone.</p> <ol> <li><strong>The ing-tail and false-range waivers claim coverage that does not exist.</strong> <code>host-grammar.obligations:39-44</code> waives all six <code>DetectIngTail</code> and <code>DetectFalseRange</code> obligations as "covered by the tells.rs scan unit tests." No test in the crate exercises <code>ing_tail</code> or <code>false_ranges</code>; the only references are the implementation sites. The justification is false and the two rules ship with zero coverage. This is the canonical no-hollow-green violation, the same class plan/0052 was cut for. Fix: add real positive and negative property tests for both rules and remap the six obligations to them. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>DensityIsWeightedOverSentences</code> is mapped to a test that never asserts the density formula.</strong> <code>host-grammar.obligations:48</code> points at <code>density_gate_requires_both</code>, which asserts the gate conjunction (the sibling invariant), never <code>density = weighted / sentences</code>. Fix: add a property asserting the formula and remap. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>RunTellsAreSuperlinear</code> is verified for anaphora but not listicle.</strong> The invariant quantifies over both ids; the mapped test (<code>host-grammar.obligations:50</code>) filters only anaphora, and the sole listicle test asserts firing, not weight. Fix: assert the listicle weight too. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The countdown negative-case waiver cites a test with no negated run.</strong> <code>host-grammar.obligations:35</code> waives the unclosed-run negative as covered by <code>clean_technical_prose_is_silent</code>, whose fixture contains no negated sentence at all. Fix: add a real negative test (a negated run with no closer raises no countdown) and remap. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The listicle negative-case waiver points at the wrong discriminator.</strong> <code>host-grammar.obligations:32</code> waives the non-ordinal-run negative as covered by <code>anaphora_pair_is_free</code>, which tests a run-length floor, not the ordinal discriminator. Fix: add a negative test (a long non-ordinal run raises no listicle) and remap. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>CI runs <code>cargo test</code> only; the pinned code fails clippy.</strong> <code>test.yml</code> has no clippy or format lane, unlike the sibling components, and the pinned code fails <code>cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings</code> on the recorded 1.95.0 toolchain with six lints (<code>manual_range_contains</code> at <code>tells.rs:193</code>, <code>manual_div_ceil</code> at <code>:476</code>, three <code>collapsible_match</code> at <code>:554</code>, <code>:559</code>, <code>:571</code>, and a <code>manual_repeat_n</code> in the tests). Fix: clear the six lints and add clippy and format-check CI lanes. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>A stale <code>host-lifecycle</code> pin runs the obligations gate from an old checker.</strong> <code>allium.yml</code> installs <code>host-lifecycle --rev d91dae3</code> while <code>.host-software</code> pins a newer release. Fix: bump the workflow pin to the recorded release. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The Apalache obligation claims a scope wider than it checks.</strong> <code>spec/ParallelScan.obligations</code> and <code>ParallelScanSymbolic.tla</code> say the reconstruction holds for every <code>(N,K)</code> with <code>1<=K<=N</code>, but <code>CInit</code> admits only <code>N</code> in <code>2..8</code>. Fix: reword the obligation and spec comments to the bound that is actually discharged. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The TLAPS gate does not bind to the named theorem.</strong> <code>host-prove.yml</code> greps the generic proof status, so a rename or deletion of <code>WorkerIndexInBounds</code> would pass vacuously. Fix: add a static check that the declared theorem is present in the spec file before the proof runs. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The allium spec omits every lexical-corpus and shape tell the engine emits.</strong> The spec models only the eight per-sentence and run rules; the seven corpus diction tells and the two shape tells (<code>punchy-fragments</code>, <code>bold-first-bullets</code>) have no rule, so the spec reasons about a smaller score than ships, and the <code>lexical</code> enum variant is declared but never produced. Fix: add rules for the two shape tells with their weights and tests, and an explicit scope statement declaring the corpus a data-driven phrase layer modeled as the <code>lexical</code> kind rather than enumerated as rules. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Listicle emits one aggregate tell summing all runs; the spec emits one per run.</strong> <code>listicle</code> sums <code>(L-2)^2</code> across every ordinal run and <code>run_tells</code> emits a single tell, so the tell count undercounts and the single weight matches no run when two or more runs exist. Fix: emit one listicle tell per run, mirroring <code>anaphora_runs</code>. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The cite strings diverge between spec and code for all eight rules.</strong> The spec uses a path form and the anaphora cite uses a different prefix entirely; the code uses a prose form. Fix: align the spec cites to the shipped strings. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Spec fidelity nits.</strong> The spec types weights and gates as exact <code>Decimal</code> while the implementation uses <code>f32</code>; the <code>max(1, sentences)</code> clamp is in the code and README but not the spec; the <code>is_triad</code> doc comment says four words while the code and spec say five; the TLA model spawns exactly <code>K</code> workers (with empty trailing chunks) while the implementation spawns at most <code>K</code> non-empty chunks. Fix: a Decimal-abstracts-f32 note, the clamp in the spec, the corrected comment, and a worker-count fidelity note. (confirmed)</li> </ol> <h2 id="findings-detection-behavior-tuned-toward-precision"><a class="header" href="#findings-detection-behavior-tuned-toward-precision">Findings: detection behavior, tuned toward precision</a></h2> <p>These change what the engine flags. They ripple to <code>host-lint</code>'s prose lane (the gate on every repository's commits and documents) and are tuned toward fewer false positives.</p> <ol start="14"> <li><strong><code>is_numeral</code> accepts plain English words as Roman numerals.</strong> The Roman arm is a bare charset-and-length gate, so <code>is_numeral</code> returns true for <code>lid</code>, <code>mid</code>, <code>mild</code>, and for non-canonical forms such as <code>IIII</code> and <code>VV</code>; the result contradicts its own doc comment. Fix: validate a canonical Roman numeral (a value round-trip) so only real numerals qualify. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>format_number</code> can emit a number <code>is_valid_name</code> rejects.</strong> The pad width is a minimum, so a register at or past ten thousand formats to more than four digits while the checker enforces exactly four, a silent generator-checker divergence. Fix: accept the natural overflow form (four digits, or more than four with no leading zero) so the checker accepts exactly what the generator produces, while still rejecting an over-padded number. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong><code>is_triad</code> flags four-or-more-item lists as a tricolon.</strong> The gate accepts three or more comma-spans with no upper bound, so an ordinary enumeration is mislabeled a tricolon and adds weight. A tricolon is three. Fix: require exactly three spans. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The em-dash pivot in the negative-parallelism config is dead code.</strong> The word tokenizer drops punctuation, so the dash entry in the pivot set can never match. Fix: remove the dead entry and note that punctuation pivots are outside the word-based equation, the precision-preserving resolution (the alternative, detecting it on the raw text, would add a false-positive-prone path, and the dash already earns a decoration tell). (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Negative parallelism fires on comparatives.</strong> The <code>than</code> pivot makes a comparison such as <code>no faster than light</code> register as antithesis. Fix: drop <code>than</code> from the pivot set; the genuine <code>not X but Y</code> form keeps its pivot. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Countdown fires on a plain sentence-initial negation.</strong> The countdown opener set includes the bare <code>no</code>, so an ordinary clause opening with <code>No ...</code> is read as a countdown fragment. Fix: require the <code>not</code> opener only. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>A repeated-ordinal run is counted as both an anaphora and a listicle.</strong> The spec models a run as classified by <code>ordinal_led</code> into one of the two, with anaphora requiring <code>not ordinal_led</code>; the code computes them in independent passes and double-counts a same-ordinal run. Fix: suppress the anaphora run when its opener is an ordinal, matching the spec. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The markdown density numerator counts heading diction while the denominator excludes headings.</strong> <code>scan_prose_markdown</code> scans heading diction (by design, headings can read as a pedagogical hook), but <code>tell_score_markdown</code> divides the resulting weight by a heading-excluded sentence count, so a clean-body document with buzzword headings crosses the gate, and the doc comment falsely claims headings are excluded. Fix: score the density over body blocks only so heading diction stays advisory and does not escalate the gate, and correct the doc comment. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Loose multi-paragraph list items fuse word boundaries.</strong> A list item with two paragraphs concatenates their text with no separator, so the last word of one paragraph and the first of the next merge into one token; a word-boundaried tell is then destroyed or fabricated. Fix: insert a separator when a paragraph continues a list item. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Blockquote content is scanned as the author's own prose.</strong> A quoted block (commonly an external citation, the very text that is trope-dense) is run through every tell as if authored. Fix: exclude blockquote text from the scan, mirroring the code-block exclusion. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>Image alt text is scanned for diction.</strong> Descriptive alt text naturally uses words such as <code>landscape</code> and <code>harness</code>, so good accessibility text raises diction tells. Fix: suppress text capture inside an image, matching the URLs-are-not-prose intent. (confirmed)</li> <li><strong>The lexical word-boundary test uses ASCII bytes.</strong> A corpus stem adjacent to a non-ASCII letter reads as a boundary and fires, an unsound general boundary test. Fix: decide boundaries on character classification, not raw ASCII bytes. (confirmed)</li> </ol> <h2 id="findings-recorded-as-intended-no-clean-text-false-positive"><a class="header" href="#findings-recorded-as-intended-no-clean-text-false-positive">Findings recorded as intended (no clean-text false positive)</a></h2> <p>These are double-attributions on genuinely trope-dense text, not false positives a clean document would raise, and the documented behavior is to count adjacencies. They are recorded as intended rather than coordinated away, which would add stateful complexity and risk missing a real tell.</p> <ul> <li><strong>A negated countdown run is also an anaphora.</strong> A run of negated sentences closed by a <code>Just</code> fragment earns both the countdown and the anaphora tell. The text is genuinely heavy; the anaphora is real (a repeated opener) and the countdown is real (the closed run).</li> <li><strong>A chain of terse questions overcounts self-answered adjacencies.</strong> The engine counts adjacencies by design; a chain such as a question followed by a one-word question followed by a one-word answer is a self-answered-question-dense passage, and each adjacency is a real instance.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-was-checked-and-cleared-2"><a class="header" href="#what-was-checked-and-cleared-2">What was checked and cleared</a></h2> <p>The negatives bound the work. The parallel chunked scan is correct: <code>scan_chunked</code> equals <code>scan_prose</code> for every chunk count (verified for a wide range including the degenerate counts), the merge folds partials in chunk order, run detection runs once over the concatenated metadata so a boundary-straddling run rejoins, and the float sum is computed in identical order so the gate is bit-deterministic across worker counts. No function on any surface panics: every slice and unwrap is guarded. The naming grammar round-trips for every register inside the pad width, the slug validity is byte-safe, and the decimal arm of <code>is_numeral</code> rejects its edge cases. The gate constants match the spec, the both-gates logic is exact, and all eight structural weights and ids agree between code and spec. The three deep-verification lanes (the bounded TLC model, the Apalache symbolic check, and the TLAPS proof) genuinely run and gate, and the anaphora obligations, the positive cases, and the structural spec-shape dispositions are honestly discharged.</p> <h2 id="status-14"><a class="header" href="#status-14">Status</a></h2> <p>Complete. host-grammar shipped as <strong>v0.4.0</strong> (commit <code>9470b81</code>), a pin-only component with no artifact. The change is a minor bump because the detection output moves: <code>is_numeral</code> now validates canonical Roman numerals, the prose engine is tuned toward precision, and the markdown density score covers the body alone. The local gate is green (25 unit tests, 25 property tests, clippy under <code>-D warnings</code>, the three <code>allium</code> lanes, and the obligations discharge); a new clippy CI lane plus the corrected obligation mappings guard against regression.</p> <p>Two findings carry a recorded judgment rather than the literal fix. The fmt CI lane of finding 6 is deliberately not added: host-grammar's detection tables are hand-formatted compactly, so a <code>cargo fmt --check</code> gate would force a sweeping reformat out of proportion to this review. The plan/0052 <code>exercises=</code> strict-discharge links are not added either: host-grammar's property tests are black-box over the public API by design, so a white-box containment link does not fit, and the substantive no-hollow-green fix is already in place (every obligation maps to a test that genuinely exercises its rule, which the discharge check confirms).</p> <p>Propagation (operator ruling: propagate now): both consumers adopted the new host-grammar this session. host-lint shipped as <strong>v0.11.0</strong> (commit <code>cefc9376</code>, artifact <code>136cd7ce</code>) with its deps-bundle re-vendored to <code>vendor-v4</code>, and its one affected property test moved to the corrected canonical-Roman contract. host-lifecycle shipped as <strong>v0.34.0</strong> (commit <code>d4ce47e</code>, artifact <code>7f9c2833</code>) with its deps-bundle re-vendored to <code>vendor-v5</code>; it bumped both its host-grammar and its host-lint dependency so the tree unifies on a single host-grammar v0.4.0 and its prose lane runs the fixed engine. Both re-derive byte identically, the release receipts are recorded, and <code>software --check</code> is clean at the new pins. This milestone records no new <code>call/</code> decision.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0054-host-prove-review-findings-and-the-on-demand-verifier-plugin-design"><a class="header" href="#plan0054-host-prove-review-findings-and-the-on-demand-verifier-plugin-design">plan/0054 host-prove review: findings, and the on-demand verifier-plugin design</a></h1> <p>This milestone records a maximum-effort review of <code>host-prove</code>, the verification-ladder lane driver (the re-deriver the ladder trusts), and the design decided for its remediation. It is the next review in the campaign after <code>host-grammar</code> (plan/0053). It is treated as doctrine-grade (operator ruling) because host-prove is the no-hollow-green enforcement tool, and the review found that host-prove can itself report a hollow green: it has several paths that settle a PASS over a real failure.</p> <h2 id="what-was-reviewed-3"><a class="header" href="#what-was-reviewed-3">What was reviewed</a></h2> <ul> <li>Component: <code>host-prove</code> at its pinned release (<code>3d1bba79</code>, v0.2.3): the single <code>src/main.rs</code> (333 lines), the <code>host-prove.allium</code> spec and its <code>host-prove.obligations</code> manifest, <code>tools.lock</code>, the <code>install/*.sh</code> scripts, the three skill guides, the <code>tests/</code> fixtures and runner, and the CI.</li> <li>Method: five independent reviewers, one per surface (verdict-parsing soundness; the fail-closed CLI, subprocess, and exit-code path; the allium spec and obligation discharge under the no-hollow-green lens; the <code>install/*.sh</code> and <code>tools.lock</code> provenance; CI, the reproducible build, tests, and the weak-model skill guides). Each probed its claims empirically against the built binary; the load-bearing false-passes were independently reproduced before write-up.</li> <li>Result: 23 findings, deduped. Two critical false-passes, six high, eleven medium, four low. No function panics, and the reproducible-build recipe matches <code>.host-software</code> byte for byte.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-contract-the-findings-test-against-3"><a class="header" href="#the-contract-the-findings-test-against-3">The contract the findings test against</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Verdict soundness (the cardinal rule).</strong> host-prove is the re-deriver the ladder trusts (<code>call/0018</code>: discharge is the verifier passing on re-derivation). A PASS verdict (<code>SUCCESSFUL</code> / <code>PROVEN</code> / <code>ALL-PROVED</code> / <code>TYPECHECK-OK</code>, exit 0) must never be reported over a real failure, a refutation, a crash, or an incomplete run. Ambiguity must fail closed (exit 2). A false PASS silently defeats the whole ladder; a false FAIL or false ERROR is far less dangerous.</li> <li><strong>No hollow green (plan/0052).</strong> A lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean, and an obligation must be discharged by a test that exercises the rule. host-prove must hold itself to the doctrine it drives for others.</li> <li><strong>Provenance.</strong> Each verifier is pinned by version and SHA256 in <code>tools.lock</code> and verified before use; the host-prove binary builds offline and re-derives byte-identically.</li> </ul> <h2 id="findings"><a class="header" href="#findings">Findings</a></h2> <p>Critical (false-pass):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Kani prefers SUCCESSFUL over FAILED</strong> and ignores the <code>Complete - <n> failures</code> summary, so a refuted <code>harness</code> is reported as a clean proof when both verdict tokens appear.</li> <li><strong>TLAPS treats every status except exactly <code>failed</code> as proved</strong>, so an <code>omitted</code> leaf, a <code>missing</code> or <code>interrupted</code> obligation, and even a decorated <code>failed (smt: timeout)</code> all settle to <code>ALL-PROVED</code> at the top, unbounded rung.</li> </ol> <p>High:</p> <ol start="3"> <li><strong>TLAPS never checks the expected obligation count or theorem</strong>, so a truncated or killed run reports <code>ALL-PROVED</code> on whatever subset it emitted.</li> <li><strong>TLAPS matches <code>status:</code> and <code>loc:</code> as a bare substring on any line</strong>, so echoed spec content (<code>ASSUME msg.status: proved</code>) fabricates a proved obligation.</li> <li><strong>The verifier process exit code is discarded.</strong> The verdict rests only on output text, so a tool that prints a clean line then exits non-zero is reported as a pass.</li> <li><strong>A malformed <code>--bound</code></strong> (with no <code>unwind=</code> or <code>length=</code> prefix) is dropped at the verifier yet stamped verbatim into the PASS verdict, so the recorded bound can over-claim the coverage the run explored; the <code>unspecified</code> safety net catches only an absent bound, not a malformed one.</li> <li><strong><code>kani_failed</code> discharges the <code>NonPassHasNoBound</code> invariant without asserting</strong> that the FAILED line carries no bound; the property the invariant exists to enforce is asserted by no test.</li> <li><strong>host-prove's own discharge gate cannot catch that.</strong> Its CI pins a host-lifecycle predating plan/0052, runs the discharge check advisory-only (no <code>--strict-discharge</code>), and the manifest declares no <code>exercises=</code> link, so host-prove has not adopted the discharge strengthening it drives for others. Its tests are white-box (they call the parsers directly), so the links fit.</li> </ol> <p>Medium:</p> <ol start="9"> <li><strong>Apalache prefers <code>NoError</code> over <code>Error</code></strong>, so a co-occurrence reports PROVEN.</li> <li><strong>Apalache <code>Deadlock</code> and <code>RuntimeError</code></strong> fall through to ERROR (exit 2), mislabeling a real negative result as could-not-run.</li> <li><strong>An unrecognized <code>--mode</code> value silently means <code>check</code></strong> rather than a rejection.</li> <li><strong>The spec models a <code>Verdict.bound</code> field the code does not represent</strong>, and the three <code>Bound</code> values use two incompatible verdict-line encodings (<code>[bound=<x>]</code> versus a separate <code>[unbounded]</code>).</li> <li><strong><code>BoundedToolsNeverUnbounded</code> is discharged by a presence-only assertion</strong> that never checks the unbounded form is absent, and only for the with-bound case.</li> <li><strong><code>NonPassHasNoBound</code> and the unusable transition are tested for one representative each</strong>; the apalache check-mode ERROR path and the tlaps zero-status ERROR path have no test at all.</li> <li><strong>The Apalache fixtures were captured from version 0.47.2</strong> while <code>tools.lock</code> pins 0.58.0, so the parser contract is validated against a version that is never shipped.</li> <li><strong>The <code>run_*</code> command-builders</strong> (flag assembly, bound-prefix stripping, the live dispatch) are exercised by no test.</li> <li><strong>The kani skill guide calls the soundness <code>--bound</code> optional</strong> and never tells the model that a <code>[bound=unspecified]</code> PASS must be flagged. The omission contradicts the bound design.</li> <li><strong><code>cargo kani setup</code> fetches an unverified, undocumented backend.</strong> The lockfile pins the crate, not the backend binary the setup step downloads.</li> <li><strong>CI never runs the installers or the SHA-verification path</strong> (only a syntax check), and the README advertises a CI matrix that does not exist, so the provenance anchor is asserted but never machine-verified.</li> </ol> <p>Low:</p> <ol start="20"> <li><strong>The apalache PROVEN label trusts <code>--inv</code></strong> rather than confirming the checked invariant from output (sound in direct-run, where the flag and the run share a source).</li> <li><strong><code>get(flag)</code> returns the next token unconditionally</strong>, so a value-flag placed before another flag swallows it (fail-closed in practice, but a misleading verdict).</li> <li><strong>The release job publishes the asset without re-deriving and comparing its hash</strong> in the same run, so a reproducibility regression would publish silently.</li> <li><strong><code>verify_sha</code>'s <code>[0-9a-f]*</code> guard is a weak validator</strong> (it rejects a valid uppercase digest and admits a hex-prefixed non-digest); the exact comparison is the real gate, so there is no bypass.</li> </ol> <h2 id="what-was-checked-and-cleared-3"><a class="header" href="#what-was-checked-and-cleared-3">What was checked and cleared</a></h2> <p>No function panics, on any surface. The reproducible-build recipe (the image digest, the build line, <code>strip = true</code>, and the linux-scoped <code>--build-id=none</code>) matches <code>.host-software</code> byte for byte. <code>verify_sha</code> is fail-closed: it refuses an empty or <code>n/a</code> expected hash, and the exact <code>sha256sum</code> comparison admits no wrong value, so no bypass exists. The verdict vocabulary is consistent across the spec, the source, and the three guides, and the guides are procedural for a weak model (one wrapper command per step, a fixed verdict word matched, explicit STOP conditions, authoring handed to a strong model). <code>TlapsPassIsUnbounded</code>, <code>PassCarriesBound</code>, the three transition edges, and the <code>StartRun</code> waiver are genuinely discharged. The <code>--stdin</code> parse path runs no subprocess and touches no network.</p> <h2 id="the-operator-decision-1"><a class="header" href="#the-operator-decision-1">The operator decision</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Fix everything.</strong> The verdict-parsing, bound, and discharge findings are clear fail-closed soundness fixes, not recall or precision tradeoffs.</li> <li><strong>The verifiers become on-demand, tool-carried plugins</strong>, modeled on host-reference's out-of-process helpers (<code>call/0033</code>, <code>call/0034</code>). The <code>install/*.sh</code> scripts fold into a <code>host-prove install <tool></code> Rust subcommand that reads <code>tools.lock</code>, verifies the SHA256 before use, and exposes the binary, orchestrated in one process (shelling only <code>curl</code>, <code>sha256sum</code>, and <code>tar</code>, so host-prove keeps its zero-dependency offline-reproducible build). A verifier that is absent at run time is auto-installed (SHA-verified) and then run, so a weak agent issues one command. A <code>call/</code> decision will record the architecture when the work lands.</li> <li><strong>Doctrine-grade.</strong> The design is cast-reviewed and gated on a real qwen3.5-4b probe, as plan/0052 was, because host-prove is the no-hollow-green tool and the guide and auto-install changes are weak-agent-facing.</li> <li><strong>One milestone</strong> carries the soundness fixes, the plugin rework, the decision record, the cast review, and the probe gate.</li> </ul> <h2 id="network-aspects"><a class="header" href="#network-aspects">Network aspects</a></h2> <p>host-prove's network behaviour splits into contexts.
