The on-demand auto-install decision adds one new context, recorded here before it is built so its terms are explicit.</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Build time stays offline.</strong> The binary has zero third-party dependencies and builds with <code>--network none</code> in the pinned muslrust container; the artifact <code>.host-software</code> records is produced with no network. Auto-install changes nothing here: the binary fetches nothing at build time, and the build stays hermetic.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The <code>--stdin</code> parse path touches no network and spawns no subprocess.</strong> The parser, its unit tests, and <code>tests/run.sh</code> validate the verdict mapping fully offline, so the discharge-trust logic is testable with no network and no verifier installed.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Running a verifier is a local subprocess.</strong> Once a verifier is installed, host-prove runs it as a local process and parses its output; host-prove itself opens no socket. apalache and tlaps are local provers (a JVM tool and a prebuilt installer); kani runs locally once set up. The one residual exception is <code>cargo kani setup</code>, which fetches a backend on first use (finding 18).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Auto-install on demand is the single place host-prove reaches the network, under pinned, verified, fail-closed terms.</strong></p> <ul> <li>When a declared verifier is absent at run time, host-prove fetches the pinned asset named in <code>tools.lock</code> (a github release asset for apalache and tlaps; the crates.io crate plus <code>cargo kani setup</code> for kani), verifies its SHA256 against <code>tools.lock</code> before the artifact is extracted or executed, and only then runs it. A mismatch fails closed (exit 2). The fetch is of a pinned, hash-verified tool, never of untrusted input, so it is consistent with the spirit of the no-reach-out rule (<code>call/0031</code>): that rule forbids fetching untrusted content while processing untrusted data, whereas here the fetched artifact is the verifier itself, pinned and verified, and the trigger is an explicit verifier invocation.</li> <li>The fetch happens once per host, at first activation; later runs use the installed binary and touch no network. The network cost is a one-time activation, not a per-run dependency.</li> <li>The verdict is reproducible from the pinned tool version, but the auto-install fetch is not part of the reproducible-build attestation, which covers only the host-prove binary. Tool provenance (the <code>tools.lock</code> pin plus its SHA) is a runtime concern, separate from the build provenance <code>.host-software</code> records.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><strong>Offline and air-gapped operation degrades closed.</strong> Because auto-install needs the network, host-prove in an offline or <code>--network none</code> environment cannot install an absent verifier. The design requires this to fail closed: an absent verifier that cannot be fetched yields a could-not-run verdict (exit 2) with a precise message, never a silent pass; a verifier already on PATH is used with no fetch. An air-gapped operator pre-installs the pinned verifiers (the same <code>host-prove install</code> path against a local mirror, or a pre-seeded PATH), so auto-install is a convenience for the connected case, not a hard dependency for a run whose verifier is already present.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>CI keeps the two contexts apart.</strong> The hermetic build and the parser tests run offline (<code>--network none</code>); they need no verifier and no network. The provenance check the review asks for (finding 19) is a distinct, network-enabled lane that runs <code>host-prove install <tool></code>, confirms the SHA against <code>tools.lock</code>, and runs a smoke verdict; a periodic re-fetch detects an upstream asset re-published under the same name with a different hash (a supply-chain drift alarm). That lane is the machine-verification the current syntax-only CI lacks.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Supply-chain posture.</strong> Every fetch is pinned by exact version and asset and verified by SHA256 before use, so the untrusted transport (the network, the github CDN, crates.io) cannot substitute a different artifact without detection. The open edge is the <code>cargo kani setup</code> backend (finding 18), which the lockfile does not cover; the milestone will pin it or, failing a clean pin, document the residual on the kani plugin. The reachable hosts are the github release CDN and crates.io, and the underlying <code>curl</code> honours a standard proxy environment.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="cast-consultation-and-the-revised-install-design-supersedes-the-auto-install-plan-above"><a class="header" href="#cast-consultation-and-the-revised-install-design-supersedes-the-auto-install-plan-above">Cast consultation, and the revised install design (supersedes the auto-install plan above)</a></h2> <p>The operator flagged three worries about auto-install-on-demand (silent failures, updates, sandbox restrictions) and asked the cast to weigh in. All five personas were consulted. The result reversed the auto-install-on-demand default and surfaced the true defect.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Unanimous (all five): per-run pin-binding is the real fix.</strong> Every run must bind the verifier to the embedded <code>tools.lock</code> pin by version and hash before executing it; an absent, wrong-version, or unverifiable verifier yields exit 2 and no verdict, never folded into a pass or a fail. A verdict comes from the exact pinned tool or it does not come. The first sketch reused whatever was installed or on PATH with no version check, the silent-staleness defect the operator sensed: after a pin bump a host keeps using the old verifier and still reports a clean pass.</li> <li><strong>Majority (Mara, Orin, Fen, Wren): fail closed by default, install as a separate explicit verb.</strong> Fen reframed the weak-agent case: its rule is one tool-driven command at a time with the tool naming the next move, not collapsing an install side effect into a run, so a fail-closed verdict that prints <code>run: host-prove install <tool></code> is the tool carrying the process. Wren required a hard split: the run path is pure-local and structurally cannot install, so a sandbox or air-gapped host is never surprised, and <code>host-prove install</code> is the only verb that touches the network or filesystem. Orin required the resolver to bind to the embedded pin (a version-stamped install dir keyed to the pin, so a bump moves the lookup path and the old version is never glanced at) and that re-install always be an explicit operator act, because the host may be air-gapped and the operator must learn the pin moved. Mara required that no verdict ever issue from a tool not verified against the pin, with a cheap check (<code>host-prove doctor</code>).</li> </ul> <p><strong>The decided design (operator-confirmed, to be recorded in <code>call/0036</code>):</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong>Per-run pin-binding.</strong> The run path resolves the verifier only from a version-stamped install keyed to the embedded pin, with an install-time SHA marker that must match the embedded pin; absent, mismatched, or unverifiable resolves to a distinct <strong>BLOCKED</strong> verdict at exit 2 that names <code>host-prove install <tool></code>. No pass or fail issues from an unbound verifier. A PATH binary of unverifiable provenance counts as not-pinned.</li> <li><strong>Hard split, fail closed.</strong> The run and parse path is pure-local (it works under <code>--network none</code> and air-gapped) and never installs. <code>host-prove install <tool></code> is the sole verb that fetches, SHA-verifies, and installs, into a version-stamped directory; a CI provisioning lane runs it.</li> <li><strong>Update-safe.</strong> The version-stamped directory is keyed to the embedded pinned version, so a pin bump cannot be silently ignored: the next run resolves to a path that does not exist and reports BLOCKED, so the operator runs install and learns the pin moved.</li> <li><strong>Provenance and doctor.</strong> A PASS verdict carries the resolved tool version and its pin-bound marker, so a glance or a cold read confirms the pinned tool produced it; <code>host-prove doctor</code> prints each declared verifier's installed version and pin status without running a proof.</li> </ol> <p>This updates the network-aspects section above: auto-install is not a run-path side effect. Installation is a separate, explicit, network-touching verb, and the run path is pure-local and fail closed, so a sandbox cannot be surprised and an air-gapped host degrades to BLOCKED rather than a silent or surprising failure.</p> <h2 id="status-15"><a class="header" href="#status-15">Status</a></h2> <p>In progress, and CI-green at host-prove <code>8607932</code>. Landed: the soundness false-pass fixes and the discharge dogfood (<code>NonPassHasNoBound</code> asserts bound-absence, <code>exercises=</code> links, <code>--strict-discharge</code>); the cast consultation and <code>call/0036</code>; and the fail-closed install design (the pure-local pin-bound resolver, the <code>host-prove install</code> and <code>host-prove doctor</code> verbs with version-stamped SHA-verified installs, the distinct BLOCKED verdict, and the PASS provenance suffix). The shell installers are retired for the verb, and a CI <code>install-smoke</code> lane machine-verifies the install path on a clean runner (it installs the pinned apalache and confirms <code>doctor</code> reports it pin-bound). 24 unit tests, 9 fixtures, clippy, the strict discharge of 27 obligations, and all three CI jobs (verdict-parser, install-smoke, allium) are green.</p> <p>A correction is recorded for the audit trail: the soundness commit <code>f4736e9</code> carried a step name whose colon-space was invalid workflow YAML, so the remote CI failed to parse from that commit until the fix at <code>8607932</code>, even though the local gate was green throughout. Verifying the local gate is not verifying CI; a <code>python yaml</code> parse check now precedes relying on the workflow.</p> <p>The kani skill-guide fix landed (the bound is mandatory for a trustworthy PASS, and a <code>[bound=unspecified]</code> PASS must be flagged), with all three guides covering the BLOCKED verdict.</p> <h2 id="the-doctrine-gate"><a class="header" href="#the-doctrine-gate">The doctrine gate</a></h2> <p>Cast-reviewed across the personas and gated on a real qwen3.5-4b (Fen) probe, as plan/0052 was.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Fen probe (passed).</strong> The real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> was driven on the changed weak-agent surface (the decision-table routing). It routed all three scenarios correctly: a BLOCKED verdict to <code>run: host-prove install <tool></code>; a <code>SUCCESSFUL … [bound=unspecified]</code> PASS to <em>not trustworthy as-is, supply the bound or flag it</em> (it did not take the SUCCESSFUL word at face value); and a FAILED to report the counterexample without weakening the assertion. Decision-table routing held at the 4B.</li> <li><strong>Cast review (passed after fixes).</strong> Mara, Bly, and Orin each confirmed the fail-closed, pin-bound design satisfies their non-negotiable for apalache and tlaps, and converged on three over-claims: (1) a kani PASS stamped <code>pinned</code> like the hash-verified tools though kani is version-only bound with an unverified <code>cargo kani setup</code> backend; (2) the apalache/tlaps pin marker was an install-time stamp of the asset sha, not a per-run check of the executed binary; (3) the end-to-end guarantee needs the consumer to reject an unsuffixed or <code>--stdin</code> PASS. Fixes: kani's verdict and <code>doctor</code> now say <code>version-pinned, backend unverified</code> and never claim it is <code>pinned</code>; the marker now records the extracted binary's own sha and <code>resolve</code> re-hashes it every run (a content bind, not a stamp); and <code>tools.lock</code> names the unpinned backend precisely. The third is a consumer-side requirement recorded below.</li> </ul> <h2 id="residual-notes"><a class="header" href="#residual-notes">Residual notes</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Consumer must require the pinned suffix.</strong> A live PASS carries <code>[<tool>=<version> …]</code>; a <code>--stdin</code> or hand-fed PASS does not. The end-to-end no-hollow-green guarantee depends on the consumer (<code>host-lifecycle obligations --prove</code>) accepting only a suffixed, pin-bound PASS, never a bare <code>SUCCESSFUL</code>/<code>PROVEN</code> line. This is a host-lifecycle obligation-check requirement, a follow-on.</li> <li><strong>kani backend.</strong> <code>cargo kani setup</code> fetches the verdict-producing backend unpinned; this is inherent to kani's distribution, confined to the explicit install verb (an air-gapped host fails the install rather than fetching unverified), and now named honestly in the verdict, <code>doctor</code>, and <code>tools.lock</code>. Not a release blocker.</li> <li><strong>Apalache fixtures.</strong> The static fixtures were captured from 0.47.2; the parser keys on version-stable outcome strings, and the CI <code>install-smoke</code> lane now provisions the pinned 0.58.0. A fixture refresh (or a real-tool end-to-end smoke) is a low-risk follow-on.</li> </ul> <h2 id="released"><a class="header" href="#released">Released</a></h2> <p>Complete. Shipped as host-prove <strong>v0.3.0</strong> (commit <code>c05782c</code>, artifact <code>9a9bbbd36edc072cfe5518a408211fabf8c78cff63ed3cb89d25129b8ff9f03f</code>), re-deriving byte-identically in the recorded <code>clux/muslrust</code> toolchain. The change is classed <code>removes-flag</code> because the verdict vocabulary and run behaviour change: a run is now fail-closed and pin-bound, an absent or wrong-version verifier is <code>BLOCKED</code> rather than run, and the verdict lines carry provenance and the corrected tlaps form. The release receipt is recorded, <code>.host-software</code> is re-pinned, the PATH binary is reinstalled (the plan/0048 runnability gate's re-deriver is live), and <code>software --check</code> is clean at the new pin. host-prove has zero dependencies, so no consumer propagation is owed. This milestone adds one decision, <code>call/0036</code>. The review campaign now leaves only the host-lint review.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0055-host-lint-review-findings-the-blocking-tier-precision-recut-and-the-no-hollow-green-dogfood"><a class="header" href="#plan0055-host-lint-review-findings-the-blocking-tier-precision-recut-and-the-no-hollow-green-dogfood">plan/0055 host-lint review: findings, the blocking-tier precision recut, and the no-hollow-green dogfood</a></h1> <p>This milestone records a maximum-effort review of <code>host-lint</code>, the prose-and-naming detector that gates this repository and every adopter project, and the remediation decided for it. It is the last review in the campaign, after <code>host-grammar</code> (plan/0053) and <code>host-prove</code> (plan/0054). It is treated as doctrine-grade (operator ruling) on two counts: the review changes the blocking detection contract, and it closes a no-hollow-green gap in the very tool whose grammar consumer enforces that doctrine for the suite.</p> <h2 id="what-was-reviewed-4"><a class="header" href="#what-was-reviewed-4">What was reviewed</a></h2> <ul> <li>Component: <code>host-lint</code> at its pinned release (<code>cefc9376</code>, v0.11.0): the detector core <code>src/lib.rs</code> (1077 lines), the CLI <code>src/main.rs</code> (554 lines), the <code>host-lint.allium</code> spec with its <code>host-lint.obligations</code> manifest and <code>.obligations.digests</code> ledger, <code>VOCABULARY.md</code> (the rule source), the <code>pre-commit</code>/<code>commit-msg</code> hook script, <code>test-integration.sh</code>, <code>lint-skill.sh</code>, the skill guides, <code>Cargo.toml</code>, and the CI workflow. The detector consumes <code>host-grammar</code> at <code>9470b81</code> (v0.4.0) for the prose lane.</li> <li>Method: six independent reviewers, one per surface (naming-tell detection; the LEXICON allowlist and masking; the prose lane and the ignore-fence engine; the CLI, git-root resolution, and exit-code dispatch; the allium spec and obligation discharge under the no-hollow-green lens; and VOCABULARY, the hooks, CI, and the integration suite). Each probed its claims empirically against the built binary; the load-bearing findings were reproduced independently before write-up.</li> <li>Result: 40 raw findings, deduped to 33 distinct, every one confirmed against the built v0.11.0 binary. Two critical, eleven high, fourteen medium, six low. The audited source matches the pin digest (<code>cc31f540</code>), so the findings hold against the released artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-contract-the-findings-test-against-4"><a class="header" href="#the-contract-the-findings-test-against-4">The contract the findings test against</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Precision at the blocking tier.</strong> host-lint has three tiers: a blocking Flag (exit 1) for a confirmed tell, an advisory Warn (exit 3, recall-biased) for an ambiguous one, and a Note (exit 0). The recall bias is sanctioned only at Warn. A Flag blocks a commit, so the blocking tier must fire only on a confirmed tell; a false Flag there trains users to bypass the hook, which destroys the gate. The review measured the blocking tier against ordinary English and source.</li> <li><strong>No fail-open.</strong> The detector must never silently pass a real tell. A masking allowlist, a git-root miss, an unclosed ignore fence, or a hook that reads the wrong bytes must fail closed or fail loud, never settle to a clean exit over content it did not scan.</li> <li><strong>No hollow green (plan/0052).</strong> A lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean, and an obligation must be discharged by a test that exercises the rule. host-lint must hold itself to the doctrine its grammar lane enforces for the suite.</li> <li><strong>Reproducible build.</strong> The release artifact must re-derive byte-identically from the recorded toolchain, and CI must prove it against the <code>.host-software</code> hash.</li> </ul> <h2 id="findings-1"><a class="header" href="#findings-1">Findings</a></h2> <p>The concrete trigger strings are boxed below so the doc gate does not read them as authored tells.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">A. blocking-tier false-flags (the gate over-blocks legitimate text): "in this pass I fixed the parser bug" blocked (the pronoun "I" parses as Roman 1) "port the lexer pass to C" blocked (the language letter "C" parses as Roman 100) "pass 2 arguments to the helper" blocked "round 2 decimal places before display" blocked "step into 3 dimensions of design" blocked "## 2024" / "## 404" (markdown heading) blocked "release wave 2024-01 shipped" blocked (a date read as a numeric range) "// 200: OK response handler" (comment) blocked (a status code read as a label prefix) B. fail-open holes (the gate silently passes real tells): a bare LEXICON entry of a flag-noun masks the noun out of every real flag-noun-plus-numeral line an unclosed host-lint:ignore fence swallows the rest of the file a relative GIT_DIR collapses the repo root, dropping the LEXICON and downgrading strict to advisory </code></pre> <h3 id="a-blocking-tier-false-flags-precision"><a class="header" href="#a-blocking-tier-false-flags-precision">A. Blocking-tier false-flags (precision)</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Sev</th><th>Finding</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>N1</td><td><strong>critical</strong></td><td><code>is_numeral</code> accepts canonical Roman numerals, so the pronoun "I" and the single letters C/D/V/X after any flag-noun settle to a blocking Flag. Ordinary commit-body prose blocks.</td></tr> <tr><td>N2 / V1</td><td>high</td><td>The verb and measurement nouns (<code>pass</code>, <code>round</code>, <code>step</code>, <code>level</code>, <code>part</code>) flag within a 2-word window, so ordinary English blocks. The <code>i+2</code> lookahead widens the collision. VOCABULARY.md documents immediate adjacency in comments, headers, and subjects; the code matches any line at a 2-word gap, so the rule source misdescribes the contract.</td></tr> <tr><td>N3</td><td>medium</td><td><code>check_bare_numeral_header</code> flags any all-digit markdown heading, including a changelog year and a status-code reference, with no year guard. <code>gather_candidates</code> already skips a 4-digit year; this lane does not.</td></tr> <tr><td>N4</td><td>medium</td><td><code>is_num_range</code> accepts a <code>YYYY-MM</code> date and a year range, so a date-stamped label flags.</td></tr> <tr><td>N5</td><td>medium</td><td><code>check_label_prefix</code> flags a numeric-key comment such as an HTTP status line.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The structural root: the blocking lane lacks the year and length guards <code>gather_candidates</code> already has, accepts Roman numerals in a lane where single letters collide with English, and reaches a numeral two words away rather than adjacent.</p> <h3 id="b-fail-open-holes-recall-more-dangerous-for-a-gate"><a class="header" href="#b-fail-open-holes-recall-more-dangerous-for-a-gate">B. Fail-open holes (recall, more dangerous for a gate)</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Sev</th><th>Finding</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>L1</td><td><strong>critical</strong></td><td>LEXICON laundering: a bare flag-noun entry, or a multiword entry whose tokens stop short of a numeral, passes the G2 no-laundering guard, then masks the flag-noun out of a real line. The whole flag class then goes unscanned repo-wide, and strict mode no longer escalates it. G2 checks only the phrase's own class. It never checks whether masking the phrase would clear a flag elsewhere.</td></tr> <tr><td>C1</td><td>high</td><td>A relative <code>GIT_DIR</code> (which <code>git --git-dir=.git commit</code> exports) makes <code>repo_root()</code> return empty, so the LEXICON is dropped and a blocking strict Flag downgrades to an advisory Warn.</td></tr> <tr><td>C2</td><td>high</td><td>With an empty root, <code>--all</code> and <code>--docs</code> exit clean having scanned nothing, so a repository audit passes vacuously.</td></tr> <tr><td>V4</td><td>high</td><td>The pre-commit hook lints the working-tree file, not the staged blob, so a tell staged then edited out of the working tree commits unseen.</td></tr> <tr><td>P2</td><td>high</td><td>An unclosed <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fence leaves the ignore state set to end of file, so every later line is skipped and tells after a forgotten close are never seen.</td></tr> <tr><td>V5</td><td>medium</td><td>The hook acts only on exit 1 and exit 3, so an exit 2 (a usage error or a git failure) lets the commit through. On an error the gate becomes a no-op for that file, and the commit proceeds.</td></tr> <tr><td>P4</td><td>medium</td><td>A bare fence inside an ignore block closes it early, with no nesting awareness, so a quarantined citation leaks back to the linter.</td></tr> <tr><td>L2</td><td>medium</td><td>A phantom tracker reference cited to any unrelated URL masks a real review-code flag offline; the URL is never parsed or correlated, and the liveness lane is a separate non-default subcommand.</td></tr> <tr><td>C4</td><td>medium</td><td><code>--prose</code> with no file arguments exits clean silently, so a script that trusts the exit code reads a vacuous pass.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="c-hollow-green-in-host-lints-own-ladder-the-plan0052-doctrine-dogfooded"><a class="header" href="#c-hollow-green-in-host-lints-own-ladder-the-plan0052-doctrine-dogfooded">C. Hollow green in host-lint's own ladder (the plan/0052 doctrine, dogfooded)</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Sev</th><th>Finding</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>S1</td><td>high</td><td>The <code>RomanNumeralLength</code> invariant (cap 4) contradicts the pinned host-grammar, which has no length cap, and a <code>structural</code> disposition cannot test the invariant at all. A decorative green, on the same Roman acceptance that drives N1.</td></tr> <tr><td>S2</td><td>high</td><td>The verdict-lifecycle obligation block is discharged by single-line classifier tests, not by the matches-to-exit-code aggregation in <code>main.rs</code>. The negative <code>rule-failure.RecordFlag.1</code> maps to an always-positive test, so it is non-falsifiable.</td></tr> <tr><td>V6</td><td>high</td><td>The release CI job omits <code>allium</code> and <code>kani</code> from its <code>needs</code>, so a tag can ship with a red spec or a red proof. A hollow-green release path.</td></tr> <tr><td>S3</td><td>medium</td><td>The <code>exercises=</code> strengthening from plan/0052 is un-adopted: no <code>exercises=</code> links, no <code>--strict-discharge</code>. The gate confirms a test name resolves, never that the test exercises the rule, though host-lint's property tests are fully white-box and ready for the link.</td></tr> <tr><td>S4</td><td>medium</td><td>An unmodeled flag-tier rule (a review-noun plus a code), and a kani proof dispositioned to a rule whose code path it cannot reach.</td></tr> <tr><td>S5</td><td>medium</td><td>The spec under-models its own engine: the Note severity, the prose occurrence-mapping, the LEXICON guards, masking, gather, and the ignore-fence quarantine are tested but neither modeled nor obligated.</td></tr> <tr><td>S6</td><td>low</td><td>The entity-creation obligations assert only that a detector returned a match, never the modeled <code>Match</code> fields, and the spec rule names do not map to the code function names.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="d-reproducible-build-and-ci-integrity"><a class="header" href="#d-reproducible-build-and-ci-integrity">D. Reproducible build and CI integrity</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Sev</th><th>Finding</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>V7</td><td>high</td><td>CI builds on the stock runner with apt musl-tools, without <code>--locked</code> or <code>--offline</code> and ignoring the deps-bundle, and never verifies the artifact against the <code>.host-software</code> hash. The Cargo.toml comment claiming CI proves the byte-identical artifact is false; no such step exists.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="e-test-and-coverage-gaps"><a class="header" href="#e-test-and-coverage-gaps">E. Test and coverage gaps</a></h3> <p>V2 (medium): the VOCABULARY core regex omits nine enforced terms, and the documented header restriction for the machine-learning term is unimplemented. V3 (medium): nothing keeps VOCABULARY.md in sync with the code constants, and thirteen of twenty-five flag terms have no test. V8 (medium): the ignore-fence exemption has no integration test, and the hook script itself is exercised nowhere. V9 (medium): the should-flag integration cases assert a nonzero exit, conflating Flag and Warn, so a Flag-to-Warn regression stays green.</p> <h3 id="f-robustness-and-lower-severity"><a class="header" href="#f-robustness-and-lower-severity">F. Robustness and lower severity</a></h3> <p>L3 and P1 are the same bug (high): <code>escalate_subject_decoration</code> over-escalates a body decoration to a Flag whenever the subject contains the same character, because it tests substring containment of the match text rather than the match line. P3 (high): a second, markdown-normalised occurrence of a repeated prose tell is silently dropped, under-reporting. P5 (medium): the occurrence mapping lacks a word boundary, so a short tell mislocates onto a longer word. C3 (medium): <code>escape_json</code> emits raw control bytes, producing invalid JSON. C5 (low): the per-file path follows symlinks while <code>--all</code> skips them. P6 and L4 (low, speculative): a char-boundary panic on a masked multibyte phrase, and a non-ASCII mask boundary. N6 (low): a typographic dash range is missed. N7 (low): <code>milestone</code> and <code>tier</code> are absent from the terms, and a review-noun plus a bare numeral does not flag (a vocabulary judgment). N8 (low): the co-author exemption is position-agnostic. N9 (low): a strict decimal Warn cannot be escaped through the LEXICON.</p> <h3 id="checked-and-cleared"><a class="header" href="#checked-and-cleared">Checked and cleared</a></h3> <p>The reviewers confirmed several load-bearing negatives. The G1 master-key guard holds (a lettered phrase never masks a bare numeral). The masking offset arithmetic is byte-safe for the ASCII case. The ignore fence is honored only in markdown, so a code file or a commit message cannot open one, and an ordinary code fence stays linted so a tell cannot be laundered by inline quoting. The kani tier is re-run for real through host-prove with a fresh digest ledger, and the detection rules whose tests genuinely exercise the mapped function are honestly discharged. No naming-lane panics were found.</p> <h2 id="operator-decisions-1"><a class="header" href="#operator-decisions-1">Operator decisions</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The blocking tier holds only the high-centrality work-unit words; the disposition is grounded in corpus data, not assertion.</strong> The operator's first ruling demoted the verb and measurement terms (<code>pass</code>, <code>round</code>, <code>step</code>, <code>level</code>, <code>part</code>). The operator then asked to ground the rest in data rather than assert a noun is collision-prone. Measuring the <code><noun> <numeral></code> shape across roughly 35,500 real <code>.rs</code> files (a proxy for adopter code) showed six more nouns I had kept blocking are overwhelmingly domain usage with zero in-project tells: <code>section</code> (the single largest source), <code>chapter</code>, <code>epoch</code>, <code>batch</code>, <code>era</code>, <code>period</code>. The operator ruled to demote all six. The blocking tier now holds the work-unit words (<code>phase</code>, <code>stage</code>, <code>sprint</code>, <code>iteration</code>, <code>cycle</code>, <code>increment</code>, <code>wave</code>) plus the near-zero-exposure synonyms and the host#16 checklist terms (<code>steps</code> stays blocking by operator decision). The clear-bug part of class A (the Roman acceptance, the two-word window, the year and status guards) is fixed regardless of tier. The contract change is recorded in <code>call/0037</code> and reflected in VOCABULARY.md, the rule source.</li> <li><strong>One milestone.</strong> plan/0055 carries both the component fixes and the no-hollow-green dogfood (class C), released together, rather than the plan/0051-plus-0052 split host-lifecycle used.</li> <li><strong>Doctrine-grade.</strong> The remediation is gated by a cast review and a real qwen3.5-4b probe before release, the same bar as plan/0052 and plan/0054, because it changes the contract and closes the dogfood gap.</li> </ol> <h2 id="remediation-plan"><a class="header" href="#remediation-plan">Remediation plan</a></h2> <p>Fix everything toward the contract above. The blocking tier is recut for precision (drop Roman in the blocking lane, require immediate adjacency, add the year and status guards, demote the verb terms to Warn). The fail-open holes are closed (the LEXICON guard tests the masking effect; the empty root fails closed; the unclosed fence fails loud; the hook lints the staged blob and treats an unexpected exit as a block). The no-hollow-green gap is closed (the false invariant corrected and re-dispositioned, the verdict aggregation given white-box coverage, the <code>exercises=</code> links and <code>--strict-discharge</code> adopted, the release job gated on allium and kani). The reproducible build is wired in CI against the recorded hash. The coverage gaps are filled. Then host-lint is released, re-pinned, and propagated to host-lifecycle (host-lint is a library dependency of the in-process prose lane, so a host-lint change obliges a re-vendor and re-release of host-lifecycle, as in plan/0053). The whole suite must be green.</p> <h2 id="process-note"><a class="header" href="#process-note">Process note</a></h2> <p>One reviewer ran without worktree isolation and committed two probe fixtures into the shared host-lint worktree, which then sat two unpushed commits ahead of the pin with stray tracked files. The audited source was untouched (the digest matches the pin), so the findings stand. The worktree is reset to the pin before remediation. The lesson: run probing reviewers under worktree isolation. This is recorded in MEMORY.</p> <h2 id="in-house-remediation"><a class="header" href="#in-house-remediation">In-house remediation</a></h2> <p>The whole in-house layer is complete, tested, and committed in the host-lint worktree on top of the v0.11.0 pin. Every finding above is fixed or dispositioned.</p> <ul> <li>Detector and lexicon: the blocking-tier recut (N1, N2, N3, N4, N5, N6), the lexicon anti-laundering guard (L1), the corpus-grounded demotion of the domain-heavy nouns, and the citation-gate number correlation (L2). The verb-and-domain-noun demotion contract is recorded in <code>call/0037</code>.</li> <li>Fail-opens and prose lane: the CLI fail-opens (C1, C2, C3, C4), the prose lane and ignore-fence engine (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6), and the hook's staged-blob scan with fail-closed exit handling (V4, V5).</li> <li>Rule source and coverage: VOCABULARY.md rewritten to the two-tier contract with a doc-to-code sync test (V1, V2, V3); the integration suite asserts exact exit codes and covers the ignore fence and the hook end to end (V8, V9).</li> <li>No-hollow-green dogfood in host-lint's own ladder: the false <code>RomanNumeralLength</code> invariant removed (S1), the verdict aggregation given a <code>verdict_code</code> helper and a real test (S2), <code>exercises=</code> links on every test disposition with <code>--strict-discharge</code> in CI (S3), the review-code flag rule modelled and the Kani harnesses re-attributed (S4), an auditable scope note for the unmodelled engine (S5), an entity-creation test that asserts the Match shape (S6), and the release CI gated on allium and kani (V6). The reproducible-build CI builds the published linux asset by the pinned recipe and the false Cargo.toml claim is corrected (V7).</li> <li>Low-severity, recorded rather than changed: C5 (an explicit file argument is followed by design, unlike the <code>--all</code>/<code>--docs</code> tree walk; the hook no longer scans by path, so it is unaffected); N7 (<code>tier</code> measured domain-heavy at 91 corpus hits, so it stays out of the blocking set; <code>milestone</code> has zero corpus hits and adding it is left to the operator, not widened here); N8 (the co-author exemption is intentionally lenient per its attribution rationale); N9 (the bare-decimal warn is recall-biased by design; a strict escalation of it is the intended cost of a declarable lexicon).</li> <li>Self-consistency dogfood (operator-caught, beyond the review findings): host-lint's own internals named constructs by ordinal position, the exact tell it detects and the methodology forbids. The conformance gates, the lexicon guards, the warn-rule labels, and the severity tiers are renamed after their content; the bare review finding-code citations are dropped from the shipping artifact (the milestone is cited by its content-slugged name, the review record keeps its finding labels). Separately, the name-format conformance gate read the skill name from the directory holding SKILL.md, which is the worktree line <code>main</code> in the materialized layout, so it failed when run in the worktree; it now reads the parent directory's name, so the gate passes in the worktree as well as on an installed skill and a repo-named CI checkout.</li> </ul> <h2 id="doctrine-gate"><a class="header" href="#doctrine-gate">Doctrine gate</a></h2> <p>Gated like plan/0052 and plan/0054: a cast review across four lenses (Mara, Orin, Wren, Bly) and a real qwen3.5-4b (Fen) probe. It earned its keep: it caught defects the in-house pass had missed, one of which my own fix had introduced.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Fen probe (the real 4B): passed.</strong> Three weak-agent-facing scenarios, routed correctly across three trials with sound reasoning and no miss: an advisory warn lets the commit proceed; a blocking flag is reworded, not bypassed; a refused lexicon entry is renamed, not hand-edited. The two-tier contract and the refusal UX hold at the 4B bar.</li> <li><strong>Cast review findings, all fixed (commit <code>5d6eb6a</code>):</strong> a HIGH fail-open the V4 staged-blob fix had reopened (a non-ASCII filename is C-quoted, so <code>git show</code> failed and, without <code>pipefail</code>, fed empty input to the linter, committing a tell in <code>café.md</code> clean; fixed with NUL-delimited listing, <code>pipefail</code>, <code>.exe</code>, and a fail-closed read of an undecodable scannable blob); the Roman-acronym false-flag class (an uppercase abbreviation like <code>DC</code>, <code>XL</code>, or <code>MM</code> standing after a flag noun, fixed by bounding a blocking Roman to ordinal value <code><= XXXIX</code>); a review-code laundering hole (a bare review code such as <code>F1</code> registered in the lexicon launders the review-code flag, fixed by refusing a standalone review code); a date/degenerate range (<code>12-07</code>, <code>1-1</code>, fixed by requiring an ascending range); and the <code>## 404</code> status-code header (fixed by skipping a 3+-digit bare integer).</li> <li><strong>Operator review during the gate</strong> raised three sharp questions, each resolved with evidence. (1) Does the recut let Roman smuggle a phase tell? My first answer (drop Roman) did; reversed to the value bound, so an ordinal-roman phase up to <code>XXXIX</code> still blocks and cannot smuggle while the abbreviations do not false-flag. (2) Is the evidence enough? The <code>.rs</code> corpus grounds the demotions but is register-limited, so the gap was measured directly: <code>phase <UPPERCASE></code> occurs zero times in 35.5k <code>.rs</code> files, and <code>box</code>/<code>boxes</code>/<code>steps</code> + numeral occurs once in markdown, so the roman-acronym false-flag and the retained doc-register terms both carry low real exposure. (3) Does the LEXICON support a domain term like this? No, by design (<code>call/0006</code>, <code>call/0019</code>): the LEXICON registers genuine vocabulary and refuses a tell, an irreducible domain tell goes in a <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fence or is reworded; the no-laundering guard is what makes the LEXICON "not an escape".</li> </ul> <h2 id="status-16"><a class="header" href="#status-16">Status</a></h2> <p>Complete. The recut shipped as host-lint <strong>v0.12.0</strong> (commit <code>78bd526</code>, artifact <code>ecbf2c1d</code>), re-pinned in <code>.host-software</code>, with the agentic-host hook binary reinstalled to the canonical static build. host-lifecycle adopted it as <strong>v0.35.0</strong> (commit <code>f925317</code>, artifact <code>d0cd4aed</code>), its deps-bundle re-vendored to <code>vendor-v6</code>, so the in-process prose lane runs the recut detector. The worktree carried the remediation on top of the v0.11.0 pin (the recut and lexicon guard, the fail-opens and prose lane, the rule-source rewrite and coverage, the no-hollow-green dogfood, the ordinal-naming self-consistency fix, and the cast-gate fixes). Verification: 85 unit and property tests, clippy clean, 128 integration cases, the strict-discharge gate clean across all 51 obligations with the kani rungs re-derived, <code>allium check</code> clean, and <code>lint-skill.sh</code> passing in full (in the materialized worktree and on a repo-named checkout).</p> <p>The whole suite is green: the host-lint and host-lifecycle release CI both pass at their tags, and the agentic-host reproducible-build job re-derives both artifacts byte-identically inside the recorded toolchain container with <code>software --check</code> clean and no HAZARD. This closes the software review campaign: every host-* component has been reviewed, remediated, and released, and host-lint was the last.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0056-recipe-and-materialisation-hardening-host-lifecycle-legible-and-fail-safe-to-a-heavily-quantized-operator"><a class="header" href="#plan0056-recipe-and-materialisation-hardening-host-lifecycle-legible-and-fail-safe-to-a-heavily-quantized-operator">plan/0056 recipe-and-materialisation-hardening: host-lifecycle legible and fail-safe to a heavily-quantized operator</a></h1> <p>This milestone gathers a superset of host-lifecycle defects that share one root: <strong>the tool trusts input, state, and on-disk layout that a heavily-quantized operator mis-authors, or that fights git tooling and its own docs.</strong> Each is a place where host-lifecycle should normalize the input, fail safe on a degenerate state, or present a layout that neither git nor a cold reader can misread. The cast's Fen (the real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code>) is the acceptance test.</p> <h2 id="where-it-came-from-1"><a class="header" href="#where-it-came-from-1">Where it came from</a></h2> <p>A cross-project read-only audit for a single quote-leak class (opened as <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/6">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#6</a>) found the reported <code>worktrees = "main"</code> leak was one symptom of a systemic raw-value read across the whole <code>.host-software</code> parser, and the same class recurring fail-safe in host-lint and latent in host-prove. Probing that result, the operator surfaced three more defects of the same family: <code>remap</code> bailing on an empty dictionary rather than a fail-safe no-op (<a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/7">#7</a>), and the bare-store layout naming a bare repo <code>.git</code> inside the component dir, which git tooling misreads as a working tree (<a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/8">#8</a>), and the template pinning an outdated host-lifecycle that no release bumps (<a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/9">#9</a>). Four defects, one root: the tool does not yet withstand the weak-agent author, the degenerate state, or the release drift the methodology explicitly serves.</p> <h2 id="the-superset"><a class="header" href="#the-superset">The superset</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Defect</th><th>Decided direction</th><th>Class</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/6">#6</a></td><td><code>.host-software</code> value lines read raw; ordinary ASCII quotes leak into refs, paths, hashes, URLs</td><td>Normalize value lines on the existing <code>stamp_value_after_eq</code> model (unquote a <code>"…"</code> wrapper, reject a stray quote); cover every value field and both parsers; regression fixture</td><td>recipe parsing</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/7">#7</a></td><td><code>remap</code> exits 2 on an empty or absent <code>.host-remap</code></td><td>Fail-safe no-op: <code>--apply</code> no-op exit 0; <code>--check</code> still scans with zero rules and exits on the tells; informational status lines, not error; keep malformed-dictionary errors; anti-hollow test</td><td>control-flow fail-safe</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/8">#8</a></td><td>Bare store named <code>.git</code> inside <code>software/<name>/</code> fights git tooling; docs describe a third layout</td><td>Adopt <code>.bare</code> + <code>.git</code>-file per component; reconcile the stale docs; re-materialize; supersede plan/0029's bare-store placement</td><td>on-disk layout + doc reconcile</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/9">#9</a></td><td>Template pins an outdated host-lifecycle that no release bumps</td><td>A tool release bumps the template's pin, and a gate fails on a stale pin (durable policy <code>call/0038</code>)</td><td>release process</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The detailed per-defect implementation plan is in <a href="plan/0056-recipe-and-materialisation-hardening/implementation.html">implementation.md</a>; the durable policy for #9 is recorded in <code>call/0038</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-casts-throughline"><a class="header" href="#the-casts-throughline">The cast's throughline</a></h2> <p>Fen (qwen3.5-4b, Q8_0) is the milestone's acceptance test, not a lens: the design is validated by driving the real 4B to author a <code>.host-software</code> value, operate <code>remap</code> on an empty dictionary, and read the materialized layout, and confirming it succeeds where the un-hardened forms fumble it. Two persona demands run across all three defects:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Fen:</strong> the tool must carry the process and name the single next action; silence and a red-error-on-benign both fail it. This shapes #7's status lines and #6's split between a loud error on a malformed value and a benign no-op on a merely-empty one.</li> <li><strong>Bly (writes now, reads cold; its own auditor):</strong> the record and the layout must fail safe and never over-report. An empty remap says "nothing to do", not "done" (#7); the docs must match the code so a cold read is not misled (#8); a normalized value must not silently launder a corrupt pin (#6).</li> </ul> <p>Because these touch tool behaviour the spine relies on, the milestone is gated on a cast review (<code>cast/applying-personas.md</code>).</p> <h2 id="supersedes-and-owes"><a class="header" href="#supersedes-and-owes">Supersedes and owes</a></h2> <ul> <li>#8 supersedes plan/0029's bare-store placement (<code>software/<name>/.git</code> becomes <code>software/<name>/.bare</code> plus a <code>.git</code> file). <code>call/0039</code> records the change, its migration, and the rationale.</li> <li>#8 also surfaces a reconcile gap: the reconcile pass does not cover the recipe's on-disk layout, so the plan/0029 doc drift stood undetected. Whether reconcile should is an open question, out of scope here.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-24"><a class="header" href="#verification-24">Verification</a></h2> <p>Ships as one host-lifecycle release, then re-vendor and propagate to consumers, with the whole-suite verify gate green across host-lifecycle and every consumer, and the Fen probe passing on the three flows. Each defect carries its own regression test; #7 and #8 additionally assert the anti-hollow and the tool-legibility properties.</p> <h2 id="open-questions"><a class="header" href="#open-questions">Open questions</a></h2> <ul> <li>Whether #6, #7, #8 ship as one release or a small series (they are independent fixes with a shared root; one release is simpler for the pin bookkeeping).</li> <li>The migration path for already-materialized components under #8 (re-materialize from <code>url</code> + <code>pin</code>, or an in-place move of <code>.git</code> to <code>.bare</code> plus writing the <code>.git</code> file).</li> <li>Whether the <code>--check</code> empty-dictionary scan (#7) should honor <code>.host-lintignore</code> for <code>MEMORY.md</code> the way the full <code>--all</code> path does (it already collects via <code>is_target</code> / <code>path_ignored</code>, so likely yes; confirm).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0056-implementation-addressing-6-7-8-9"><a class="header" href="#plan0056-implementation-addressing-6-7-8-9">plan/0056 implementation: addressing #6, #7, #8, #9</a></h1> <p>A detailed plan for each defect in the superset. Line citations are anchors into the current <code>software/host-lifecycle/main/src/main.rs</code>; confirm them at edit time.</p> <h2 id="ordering-and-release"><a class="header" href="#ordering-and-release">Ordering and release</a></h2> <p>Address the defects in the order #7, #6, #8, #9. <code>#7</code> is fully designed and self-contained; <code>#6</code> is mechanical and well-scoped; <code>#8</code> carries a layout migration and a <code>call/</code> decision; <code>#9</code> changes the release command and adds a gate, and is recorded as <code>call/0038</code>.</p> <p>Recommendation: one host-lifecycle release carries the <code>#6</code>, <code>#7</code>, <code>#8</code> code, and <code>#9</code> folds into that release's own outward instructions. One pin bump, one re-vendor, one propagate. Split <code>#8</code> into its own release only if the layout migration proves large enough to warrant it.</p> <h2 id="7-remap-a-fail-safe-no-op-that-still-audits"><a class="header" href="#7-remap-a-fail-safe-no-op-that-still-audits">#7 remap: a fail-safe no-op that still audits</a></h2> <p>Goal: <code>remap</code> treats an empty or absent <code>.host-remap</code> as a fail-safe no-op with an informational line; a malformed dictionary still errors; the <code>--check</code> case still audits, so an empty dictionary never yields a clean verdict without a scan.</p> <p>Changes:</p> <ul> <li><code>remap</code> (<code>main.rs:714</code>): remove the <code>rules.is_empty()</code> guard, so an empty dictionary reaches the <code>--check</code> / <code>--apply</code> dispatch.</li> <li><code>load_remap</code> (<code>main.rs:731</code>): an absent file (a NotFound read error) yields an empty rule set; any other read error keeps the loud exit. The malformed-line errors (<code>main.rs:744</code>, <code>749</code>) stay.</li> <li><code>remap_apply</code> (<code>main.rs:974</code>): when the rule set is empty, print <code>remap --apply: no rules in .host-remap; nothing to rename (0 files changed)</code> and return, ahead of the clean-tree guard, because a no-op writes nothing and needs no clean tree.</li> <li><code>remap_check</code> (<code>main.rs:926</code>): count the targets scanned, and give the summary line a rule count and an outcome clause: <code>; clean</code> when zero tells remain, or <code>; author a .host-remap or allow entry</code> when any remain. Keep the exit code keyed on the remaining tells.</li> </ul> <p>Tests (<code>remap_tests</code>, <code>main.rs:7982</code>):</p> <ul> <li>an empty <code>--apply</code> writes nothing and prints the no-op line.</li> <li>a <code>--check</code> over an empty and over an absent <code>.host-remap</code>, against a target holding a tell, still reports the tell and exits non-zero. This is the anti-hollow guard.</li> <li><code>load_remap</code> on a directory with no <code>.host-remap</code> returns an empty set.</li> </ul> <p>Testability note: <code>remap_check</code> and <code>remap_apply</code> end in <code>process::exit</code>. Extract the scan-and-decide core into a function returning an exit code, and keep the <code>process::exit</code> at the boundary, so a test asserts the code directly.</p> <p>Verify: <code>cargo test</code>, plus a manual <code>remap --check</code> on a tree with no dictionary, which exits 0 when the tree is clean.</p> <h2 id="6-recipe-value-normalization"><a class="header" href="#6-recipe-value-normalization">#6 recipe value normalization</a></h2> <p>Goal: every <code>.host-software</code> value line is normalized (a <code>"..."</code> wrapper stripped, a stray quote rejected) before it reaches git, curl, the filesystem, or a hash compare, matching the <code>.host</code> stamp reader that already does this.</p> <p>Changes:</p> <ul> <li>Add a shared helper, or reuse <code>stamp_value_after_eq</code> (<code>main.rs:437</code>), that strips a single surrounding double-quote pair, else takes the trimmed token, and rejects an unbalanced quote with a line error.</li> <li>Apply at <code>parse_software</code> (<code>main.rs:3825</code>) for every field: <code>url</code>, <code>pin</code>, <code>branch</code>, <code>worktrees</code>, <code>toolchain</code>, <code>deploy</code>, <code>artifact</code> (both whitespace tokens), <code>hooks</code>, <code>deps-bundle</code> (both tokens), and the <code>worktree</code> line <code>store=</code> token.</li> <li>Apply at <code>parse_project_facts</code> (<code>main.rs:1400</code>) for <code>document</code>, <code>member</code>, <code>drivers</code>.</li> <li>Apply at <code>parse_rung</code> and the obligation manifest (<code>main.rs:5340</code>, <code>5606</code>) for the <code>spec=</code>, <code>bound=</code>, and name tokens.</li> <li>A stray or unbalanced quote in a value is a loud line error (exit 2), the same malformed-line discipline <code>parse_software</code> already uses.</li> </ul> <p>Tests:</p> <ul> <li>helper units: a wrapped value, a bare value, an unbalanced value, an empty value.</li> <li>a stanza with <code>worktrees = "main"</code>, <code>pin = "<sha>"</code>, and <code>artifact = "path" "<sha>"</code> parses to unquoted values.</li> <li>an unbalanced <code>pin = "abc</code> exits 2.</li> </ul> <p>Verify: <code>cargo test</code>, plus the audit flow, where a quoted value no longer reaches git.</p> <h2 id="8-git-layout-bare-plus-a-git-file"><a class="header" href="#8-git-layout-bare-plus-a-git-file">#8 git layout: <code>.bare</code> plus a <code>.git</code> file</a></h2> <p>Goal: materialisation produces <code>software/<name>/</code> holding <code>.bare/</code>, a <code>.git</code> file (<code>gitdir: ./.bare</code>), and the <code><branch>/</code> worktrees; git tooling resolves the container through the <code>.git</code> file; the docs match; existing components re-materialize.</p> <p>Changes:</p> <ul> <li><code>store_dir</code> (<code>main.rs:4051</code>) returns <code>component_dir(root, name).join(".bare")</code>. The existing callers (<code>main.rs:3619</code>, <code>4133</code>, <code>4255</code>, <code>4367</code>) keep operating on the returned path.</li> <li>Materialize (<code>main.rs:4133</code>): after the bare clone (now into <code>.bare</code>), write the <code>.git</code> file at <code>component_dir(root, name).join(".git")</code> with <code>gitdir: ./.bare</code> and a trailing newline. Confirm <code>git -C software/<name> worktree add</code> and <code>worktree list</code> resolve through it.</li> <li><code>--check</code> (<code>main.rs:4367</code>): keep the bare-store existence check on <code>.bare</code>, and assert the <code>.git</code> file exists and points at <code>.bare</code>, so a half-migrated component is caught.</li> <li><code>collect_files</code> skip set (<code>main.rs:880</code>): add <code>.bare</code> beside <code>.git</code>, as a guard if the walker ever descends into a component directory.</li> <li>Docs and reconcile: update the <code>.host-software</code> header, the materialize doc comment (<code>main.rs:1201</code>), the <code>store_dir</code> doc (<code>main.rs:4049</code>), the <code>plan/0029</code> comment (<code>main.rs:4001</code>), and the <code>.gitignore</code> note, so no stale <code><name>.git</code> or <code><name>/.git</code> bare-store reference remains.</li> <li>Tests (<code>main.rs:9171</code>, <code>9132</code>): assert <code>.bare</code> plus the <code>.git</code> file, in place of a <code>.git</code> directory.</li> </ul> <p>Migration of already-materialized components: re-materialize from <code>url</code> and <code>pin</code> (a teardown then a materialize), which the recorded pin reproduces deterministically. The milestone documents the one-time operator action.</p> <p>Decision: <code>call/0039</code> records superseding <code>plan/0029</code>'s bare-store placement: the layout, the migration, and the rationale that a bare repo named <code>.git</code> fights git tooling.</p> <p>Verify: <code>cargo test</code>; an end-to-end re-materialize with a clean <code>--check</code>; a <code>git status</code> inside <code>software/<name>/</code> that no longer errors on a bare repo, and an IDE that no longer flags the directory as a stray repo.</p> <h2 id="9-template-pin-on-release-call0038"><a class="header" href="#9-template-pin-on-release-call0038">#9 template pin on release (call/0038)</a></h2> <p>Goal: a tool release leaves the template's pin of that tool equal to the released version, carried by the release command and enforced by a gate. The durable policy is <code>call/0038</code>.</p> <p>Changes:</p> <ul> <li>The release sequence for a tool the template pins bumps the template's pin (the <code>prose.yml</code> revision today), commits and pushes it inside the template, then bumps the submodule pointer in the host.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle release</code> prints the template-pin bump as an explicit outward instruction, beside the re-pin and re-vendor instructions.</li> <li>A release gate reads the template's pinned tool versions and fails when any is older than the latest release of that tool.</li> </ul> <p>Tests:</p> <ul> <li>a gate unit over a fixture template whose pin sits behind the released version fails; an equal pin passes.</li> </ul> <p>Verify: a dry release confirms the outward instruction is printed and the gate fires on a stale pin.</p> <h2 id="cross-cutting-verification-and-release"><a class="header" href="#cross-cutting-verification-and-release">Cross-cutting verification and release</a></h2> <ul> <li>Build and test in the host-lifecycle worktree (<code>cargo test</code>, the integration script).</li> <li>Cut one host-lifecycle release carrying the <code>#6</code>, <code>#7</code>, <code>#8</code> code, with <code>#9</code> changing the release command and gate. Determine the change-class at release: <code>#6</code> and <code>#7</code> add no detector flags, and a new <code>--</code> output line or gate may set it.</li> <li>Re-vendor and propagate to the consumers that pin host-lifecycle (<code>plan/0032</code>, <code>call/0021</code>), and bump the template pin per <code>call/0038</code>.</li> <li>The whole-suite verify gate is green across host-lifecycle and every consumer.</li> <li>The Fen acceptance probe drives the real 4B through the four flows (author a quoted <code>.host-software</code> value, run <code>remap</code> on an empty dictionary, read the materialized layout, and run a release), and confirms each is legible and fail-safe where the un-hardened forms fumble it.</li> </ul> <h2 id="implemented-with-review-refinements"><a class="header" href="#implemented-with-review-refinements">Implemented, with review refinements</a></h2> <p>All four defects are implemented in <code>software/host-lifecycle/main/src/main.rs</code>, with 130 unit tests green (stable across repeated parallel runs) and clippy clean. An adversarial review (six dimensions, each finding verified by an independent refutation pass) raised fifteen confirmed findings; the substantive ones changed the shipped design:</p> <ul> <li><code>#8</code> migration is carried by <code>--materialize</code> itself, as a self-heal, not a manual teardown. An existing plan/0029-layout component (a bare repo named <code>.git</code>) is renamed to <code>.bare</code> in place at the top of the materialize loop, and <code>git worktree repair</code> re-points the existing worktrees' gitdir links. The recorded pin reproduces either way, so the migration needs no network and preserves local state. The original plan's teardown-then-materialize is no longer required; the <code>MISSING software/<name>/.bare (run --materialize)</code> message is the accurate remedy. The stray case (both <code>.git</code> and <code>.bare</code> present) fails closed with a clear message rather than an EISDIR fault. The empirical <code>git</code> behaviour (rename breaks the worktree links, <code>worktree repair</code> restores them) is verified, and a regression test builds the old layout and asserts the migrated end state.</li> <li><code>#6</code> exempts the free-form <code>build</code> command from the fail-closed unquote. A <code>build</code> value is passed verbatim to a shell where interior quotes are meaningful (<code>CFLAGS="-O2" make</code>), so it uses the tolerant <code>unq_cmd</code> (strip a clean wrapper, else pass through) rather than the strict <code>unq</code> that fails closed on a bare ref, path, hash, or URL. Every other value field stays strict.</li> <li><code>#9</code> hardens the gate: the prose-CI reader is three-state (<code>Rev</code> / <code>InstallNoRev</code> / <code>NoInstall</code>) so a host-lifecycle install whose <code>--rev</code> cannot be parsed still HAZARDs, and the pin compare is a case-insensitive hex-prefix match (floored at seven) so an abbreviated <code>--rev</code> for the same commit counts as equal. The release-time template-pin-bump instruction is a pure, unit-tested helper that names each step as a concrete command.</li> <li><code>#9</code> scope was too narrow, a serious gap found by auditing every pin: host-template pins host-lifecycle in <code>prose.yml</code> AND the <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> submodule (built by <code>reproducible-build.yml</code> and <code>site.yml</code>), and host-lint in the <code>tools/host-lint</code> submodule. The submodules were the most stale (host-lifecycle at v0.15.1, host-lint at v0.2.0, versus prose.yml's v0.30.1). The gate now reads every pin site (<code>template_submodule_pin</code> via <code>git rev-parse HEAD:<subpath></code>) and HAZARDs each that does not match the recorded <code>.host-software</code> pin of that tool. <code>call/0038</code> is rewritten to record the full pin surface.</li> <li>The <code>collect_files</code> skip-set <code>.bare</code> entry the plan specified is not added: the walker already skips the whole <code>software/</code> subtree, so it never reaches the store. This is a deliberate deviation, recorded here rather than left as a silent omission.</li> <li>The <code>parse_software</code> reject path ends in <code>process::exit(2)</code>; its decision logic is the pure <code>unquote_recipe_token</code> returning <code>None</code>, which is unit-tested for every malformed case. The exit glue is left untested, consistent with the file's other <code>process::exit(2)</code> value-error sites.</li> </ul> <p>Test coverage added for the review's no-hollow findings: the migration and self-heal paths, the <code>--check</code> gitdir-link gate firing, the twin <code>parse_project_facts</code> quote-strip, a present-but-blank <code>.host-remap</code>, the three-state prose reader, the prefix SHA compare, and the release instruction.</p> <p>Not yet done (the outward rollout, operator-run): cut the host-lifecycle release, re-pin <code>.host-software</code> and reconcile its header to the <code>.bare</code> layout (<code>call/0039</code>), migrate the materialized components by re-running <code>--materialize</code>, and <strong>fully upgrade host-template</strong> so every pin site is current (<code>call/0038</code>): the <code>prose.yml</code> <code>--rev</code> and the <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> submodule to the released host-lifecycle commit, and the <code>tools/host-lint</code> submodule to the recorded host-lint commit, then bump the agentic-host submodule pointer to that host-template commit. Shipping the <code>#9</code> gate turns the existing template drift into three live HAZARDs (one per stale pin), so the full template upgrade is part of the same release; this red window is deliberate and self-resolves once every pin matches.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0057-deps-bundle-graduation-a-tool-carried-ramp-out-of-onboarding-so-the-drift-guard-is-never-dormant-behind-a-green-check"><a class="header" href="#plan0057-deps-bundle-graduation-a-tool-carried-ramp-out-of-onboarding-so-the-drift-guard-is-never-dormant-behind-a-green-check">plan/0057 deps-bundle-graduation: a tool-carried ramp out of onboarding, so the drift guard is never dormant behind a green check</a></h1> <p>This milestone continues the recipe-and-materialisation-hardening lineage (plan/0056): the tool should fail safe on a degenerate state and present a state that neither git nor a cold reader can misread. Here the degenerate state is a bundled component that records a <code>deps-bundle</code> pin with no committed producer <code>deps-bundle.lock</code>. The tool tolerates it as a green <code>note</code> <code>(onboarding)</code> forever, with no action that ever drives it to closure, so the pin-versus-lock drift guard the methodology advertises sits dormant behind a passing check.</p> <p>The cast's Fen (the real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code>) is the acceptance test.</p> <h2 id="where-it-came-from-2"><a class="header" href="#where-it-came-from-2">Where it came from</a></h2> <p>The <code>host</code> upgrade flow left agentic-host up to date, but <code>software --check</code> carried three standing <code>(onboarding)</code> notes: <code>host-reference</code>, <code>host-reference-ocr</code>, and <code>host-reference-openscad</code> declare a <code>deps-bundle</code> yet commit no lock. The operator asked whether to commit those locks. Consulting the cast reframed the question: the missing locks are the symptom; the defect is that host-lifecycle ships no way out of onboarding, and reports the owed work as green.</p> <p>Filed as <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/10">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#10</a>.</p> <h2 id="the-defect-two-facets"><a class="header" href="#the-defect-two-facets">The defect (two facets)</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>No graduation path.</strong> <code>embed</code> names the entry (record the pin) but nothing names the exit (commit the lock, arm the guard). Followed literally, <code>embed</code> then <code>software --check</code> then a green result leaves an adopter believing the component is finished while the advertised guarantee is off. A later re-point of that component's bundle hash in <code>.host-software</code> then passes <code>--check</code> clean, the exact drift the lock exists to catch.</li> <li><strong>Verdict-layer under-report.</strong> The onboarding line re-prints every run (over-reports at stdout, which is correct), but the exit code is <code>0</code>. A cold-read auditor or a CI gate reads the verdict, not the prose, so at the verdict layer the owed lock under-reports: the gate says up to date while a graduation is owed, and the word <code>(onboarding)</code> frames a debt as a stable resting state.</li> </ol> <p>The never-tracked lock staying green is not the defect; plan/0051 decided that correctly, and a tracked-then-deleted lock is already a HAZARD. The defect is the absent exit and the green verdict over an owed transition.</p> <h2 id="why-it-is-universal"><a class="header" href="#why-it-is-universal">Why it is universal</a></h2> <p>The shape is a property of the lifecycle contract, not of any component: record a bundle pin, tolerate the missing lock as green, name no next action, and a bundled component sits in onboarding indefinitely with the guard dormant. Any adopter who brings a reproducibly-built component under the methodology in the natural order lands there. The fix belongs in host-lifecycle and the shared docs, not in a downstream cleanup. The operator's universality call stands (cast unanimous).</p> <h2 id="decided-direction-operator-ruling-a-steady-state-ramp-not-a-migration-bolt-on"><a class="header" href="#decided-direction-operator-ruling-a-steady-state-ramp-not-a-migration-bolt-on">Decided direction (operator ruling: a steady-state ramp, not a migration bolt-on)</a></h2> <p>The exit is a standing lifecycle operation reachable at any time, not a step wired onto the migration or upgrade flow. The fix must:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Ship a standalone, tool-carried, receipted graduation</strong> (the <code>software --lock <name></code> verb the operator later ruled): write the <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> from the recorded pin, drive the producer commit and the re-pin, and record a receipt. One command a weak agent can run, never a manual git dance.</li> <li><strong>Be reachable late and independently</strong>: order-free, with no unrelated migration or full release cascade replayed to reach it. Onboarding is entered at arbitrary times, so its exit is a standing operation.</li> <li><strong>Surface onboarding as a distinct, enumerable, owed third state</strong> (the no-hollow-green three-state model, plan/0052): a countable owed-list a cold read sees as owed graduations, queryable apart from clean, held in the tool's mechanical record rather than a prose note.</li> <li><strong>Be idempotent and self-re-listing</strong>: derive the owed-set from repo state each run (declares a <code>deps-bundle</code> and has no committed lock), so a truncated partial graduation re-lists the remainder and never buries it.</li> <li><strong>Fail loud on mismatch</strong>: one green terminal (lock committed and equal to the pin); refuse a lock that disagrees with the pin.</li> </ul> <p>The fix must not: re-color the note into a HAZARD before the graduation ships; couple graduation to an unrelated migration; silence the note; or mutate state inside <code>--check</code> (graduation is a separate, explicit, receipted action).</p> <h2 id="the-casts-throughline-1"><a class="header" href="#the-casts-throughline-1">The cast's throughline</a></h2> <p>Fen is the acceptance test, not a lens: the design is validated by driving the real 4B to graduate a bundled component in one command, and confirming it fumbles the manual multi-step git form. Four seats returned the same verdict and shaped the requirements:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Orin</strong> (maintainer): the graduation must be a standalone, late-reachable action, not a version-keyed migration step; the spine already states the drift guard as if automatic while the tool leaves it un-armed. The tool lands first; the three onboarding components are its first customer.</li> <li><strong>Bly</strong> (writes now, reads cold; its own auditor): the exit-code <code>0</code> under-reports the owed lock; onboarding must read as owed and enumerable, and each graduation must drop a receipt a cold session can trust.</li> <li><strong>Mara</strong> (operator, final say): universal and worth a small milestone; the defect is a steady-state lifecycle gap that merely surfaces during migration, so build the general ramp. A release-grade path would mint no-op version bumps for a byte-identical re-derivation.</li> <li><strong>Wren</strong> (amnesiac executor): the done predicate exists (the <code>ok</code> branch) but nothing asserts a bundled component must reach it, so there is no goal to loop against; the graduation must be idempotent and self-re-listing across a truncated window.</li> </ul> <p>Because this touches tool behaviour the spine relies on, the milestone is gated on a cast review (<code>cast/applying-personas.md</code>) and the Fen probe.</p> <h2 id="open-questions-1"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-1">Open questions</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Which authority the graduation commit answers to.</strong> Committing the lock advances the producer HEAD, and <code>.host-software</code> pins a released commit with its re-derived artifact hash (dual-release-authority). A release-grade graduation mints a no-op version bump for a byte-identical re-derivation; a lighter graduation that re-pins to an untagged commit breaks dual-release-authority. The milestone must decide which holds, or whether a bundled-lock commit is a sanctioned exception.</li> <li><strong>Whether the owed third state reuses <code>next</code> or extends <code>software --check</code>.</strong> The owed-list could surface through the existing <code>next</code> action or as a new disposition in <code>--check</code>; both must avoid the gate mutating state.</li> <li><strong>The first-customer cleanup.</strong> agentic-host's three <code>host-reference*</code> components graduate through the new tool once it ships, not by a hand-rolled release cascade. That cleanup is downstream of the tool, not a substitute for it.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-25"><a class="header" href="#verification-25">Verification</a></h2> <p>Ships as one host-lifecycle release, then re-vendor and propagate to consumers, with the whole-suite verify gate green across host-lifecycle and every consumer and the Fen probe passing on the graduation flow. The cheap-verification bar (Mara): every bundle-declaring component reads <code>ok pin matches deps-bundle.lock</code>, zero onboarding notes, and a recorded receipt per graduated component, so nothing is silently owed after the fix.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0057-implementation"><a class="header" href="#plan0057-implementation">plan/0057 implementation</a></h1> <p>The two operator rulings settled the design fork: the verb is <code>software --lock <name></code>, and the graduation commit answers to <strong>release-grade</strong> authority (it drives a normal producer release, so <code>.host-software</code> keeps pinning a released, tagged commit; dual-release-authority is unchanged and no gate is loosened).</p> <h2 id="the-owed-advisory-summary-software---check"><a class="header" href="#the-owed-advisory-summary-software---check">The owed advisory summary (<code>software --check</code>)</a></h2> <p><code>provenance_problems</code> already prints the onboarding <code>note</code> and returns it as a non-fault (it does not add to <code>bad</code>, so onboarding stays green). It gains a <code>&mut Vec<String> owed</code> out-parameter, and the onboarding branch pushes the component name. <code>software_check</code> threads the <code>owed</code> list through, and the <code>software --check</code> caller prints a counted, enumerated summary that names the next action:</p> <pre><code>-- N deps-bundle graduation(s) owed: <names>; run: host-lifecycle software --lock <name> <dir> </code></pre> <p>Owed stays <strong>exit 0</strong>, deliberately. Turning onboarding into a fault is the retro-red trap plan/0051 rejected, and it would deadlock the graduation: <code>--lock</code> drives a release whose verify gate re-runs <code>software --check</code> (a <code>HOST_LIFECYCLE_IN_CHECK</code> re-entrancy guard sits on exactly that path), so a non-zero owed exit would block graduating one component while the others are still legitimately owed. The fix for the under-report is loudness, not a fault: a counted, enumerated line, re-listed every run, derived from repo state (declares a <code>deps-bundle</code>, no matching lock on disk). That makes it idempotent and self-re-listing, so a partial graduation re-lists the remainder, and a cold read surfaces the debt rather than a green that hides it (Bly's over-report direction).</p> <h2 id="the-graduation-verb-software---lock-name"><a class="header" href="#the-graduation-verb-software---lock-name">The graduation verb (<code>software --lock <name></code>)</a></h2> <p>The component name is the flag's value rather than a positional, so it never collides with <code><dir></code>. The verb:</p> <ol> <li>Resolves the component. If it declares no <code>deps-bundle</code>, it errors (exit 2). The worktree must be materialized at its pin.</li> <li>Reads the on-disk lock and fails loud on the wrong state: <ul> <li>a lock equal to the pin is already locked, a no-op success (exit 0), so the verb is idempotent.</li> <li>a lock that differs from the pin is producer drift; the verb refuses (exit 1) rather than overwrite a disagreeing lock.</li> <li>no lock is the onboarding case, which proceeds.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Writes <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> as the recorded <code><url> <sha></code> (so the content is never hand-typed) and stages it.</li> <li>Drives <code>run_release(root, name, Some("neither"), false)</code>: the verify gate, the tool-computed fix-only version bump, the container rebuild that re-derives the byte-identical artifact hash (the lock is provenance, never compiled in), and the operator-run outward steps (commit the staged lock and the bump, tag, push, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the receipt). The outward steps stay operator-run, consistent with the existing <code>release</code> verb, so the local mechanical work is tool-carried and the single next action is named at each step (the Fen bar).</li> </ol> <p>Writing the lock before the gate is safe: the check reads the lock from disk, so the just-written lock reads <code>ok</code> (not owed) during the gate.</p> <h2 id="spec-obligations-tests"><a class="header" href="#spec-obligations-tests">Spec, obligations, tests</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>host-lifecycle.allium</code>: the owed state is a first-class advisory <code>Owed</code> entity, a <code>DetectOwedGraduation</code> rule (<code>bundle_owed</code> implies an <code>Owed</code> record, never a <code>Finding</code>), and an <code>OwedNeverHazards</code> invariant (an owed component's pin vacuously matches, so onboarding never hazards). The <code>--lock</code> verb is a mutation at the altitude of <code>materialize</code>/<code>release</code>, so the check-spec models the owed state it surfaces, not the verb. Five new obligations dispositioned.</li> <li>Rust unit tests: owed detection (a bundled component with no lock is owed; a matching lock is not; a differing lock is a fault, not owed). The <code>--lock</code> fail-loud branches are exercised by the actual graduation and the Fen probe.</li> </ul> <h2 id="as-built-status-local-green"><a class="header" href="#as-built-status-local-green">As-built status (local, green)</a></h2> <p>The code and spec are implemented and green locally: <code>software --check</code> prints the counted owed summary at exit 0; <code>--lock</code> guards resolve, refuse a non-bundle component, refuse a drift, and drive <code>run_release</code>; <code>allium check</code>/<code>analyse</code> clean; all 41 obligations dispositioned; 132 tests pass; clippy clean. What remains is outward: the Fen acceptance probe, then the release cascade (release host-lifecycle, re-vendor, propagate, graduate the three components), each pushing to a producer repo.</p> <h2 id="cascade-after-the-code-is-green"><a class="header" href="#cascade-after-the-code-is-green">Cascade (after the code is green)</a></h2> <ol> <li>Release host-lifecycle (the new verb plus the owed summary is a feature; change class likely <code>adds-flag</code>). Re-derive the artifact, tag, re-pin, record the receipt.</li> <li>Re-vendor and propagate to consumers per the recorded recipe.</li> <li>Graduate the three onboarding components with the new verb (<code>software --lock host-reference</code>, <code>host-reference-ocr</code>, <code>host-reference-openscad</code>), each a <code>neither</code> producer release, then re-pin. They are the ramp's first customer.</li> <li>Whole-suite verify green, <code>software --check</code> at exit 0 with zero owed, receipts recorded.</li> </ol> <h2 id="acceptance"><a class="header" href="#acceptance">Acceptance</a></h2> <p>Fen (the real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code>) is handed the one-command graduation and must complete it, and, as the baseline, must fumble the manual hand-write-and-release form. The cast review gates the design.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0058-host-reference-family-ci-complete-the-reference-familys-continuous-integration"><a class="header" href="#plan0058-host-reference-family-ci-complete-the-reference-familys-continuous-integration">plan/0058 host-reference-family-ci: complete the reference family's continuous integration</a></h1> <p>The host-reference family's CI is incomplete. host-reference itself is red, and its two helpers carry no CI at all, so a third of the family is unverified by any per-repo lane.
