The fix makes the book's mount point a declared, machine-readable key rather than a hand-authored workflow exception, so a product-site-at-root adopter needs configuration, not a durable workaround the next template upgrade silently drops.</p> <h2 id="the-tool-side-shipped-in-host-lifecycle-v0380"><a class="header" href="#the-tool-side-shipped-in-host-lifecycle-v0380">The tool side (shipped in host-lifecycle v0.38.0)</a></h2> <p>The mount point is an optional flat <code>book-mount</code> key in the <code>.host</code> stamp, with <code>/</code> as the default. It is read through the existing stamp reader, so it needs no new parser and survives a baseline re-stamp. <code>host-lifecycle book</code> emits mdBook's <code>[output.html] site-url</code> from it, and only for a non-default mount, so <code>book.toml</code> stays byte-identical for every project that publishes at the root; a sub-path mount then resolves the book's absolute links (the 404 and print pages) correctly. A <code>book --print-mount</code> mode prints the normalized mount for the reference Site workflow to consume, so the workflow reads the value from the tool rather than shell-parsing the stamp (the internalise-tool-orchestration doctrine). A unit test covers both the default (no <code>site-url</code>) and a declared sub-path.</p> <h2 id="the-spine-side-shipped-in-the-template-roll"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-side-shipped-in-the-template-roll">The spine side (shipped in the template roll)</a></h2> <p>The reference Site workflow the template ships is made mount-aware: it publishes the book under the declared sub-path with the surrounding site kept, and asserts the layout after the build. The publish recheck in <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> points at the tool's mount-aware mode rather than testing a hardcoded workflow filename, which also fixes a latent brittleness where the recheck named <code>mdbook.yml</code> while the template ships <code>site.yml</code>. The <code>book-mount</code> key, its default, and the sub-path boundary are documented in the spine, and an UPGRADING.md ledger entry keyed to that doctrine commit carries it to adopters, with a <code>requires</code> on the host-lifecycle release above. This half shipped as host-template <code>962630c</code> (the mount-aware Site workflow, the <code>book --print-mount</code> publish recheck, and the <code>book-mount</code> doctrine, with the UPGRADING ledger entry keyed to it), and agentic-host adopted it through the ledger; its own doc-site workflow is now mount-aware, though it still publishes at the root.</p> <h2 id="verification-36"><a class="header" href="#verification-36">Verification</a></h2> <p>Tool side: the unit test asserts a default mount emits no <code>site-url</code> and a declared sub-path emits it, and <code>book --print-mount</code> returns the declared value; shipped reproducibly in host-lifecycle v0.38.0. Spine side: a mount-aware Site workflow publishes the book under the sub-path without overwriting the surrounding site, and the publish recheck passes against the tool's mode. Both land with the whole-suite verify gate green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0068-host-reference-security-fix-the-dos-advisories-and-retire-every-unmaintained-crate-advisory"><a class="header" href="#plan0068-host-reference-security-fix-the-dos-advisories-and-retire-every-unmaintained-crate-advisory">plan/0068 host-reference-security: fix the DoS advisories and retire every unmaintained-crate advisory</a></h1> <p>Completing the CI lint lane (plan/0058) un-masked real and informational advisories in host-reference's dependency tree. This milestone resolves all of them, so the advisory lane is clean with no accepted risk. Shipped as host-reference v0.1.5.</p> <h2 id="the-real-vulnerabilities-fixed-by-upgrade"><a class="header" href="#the-real-vulnerabilities-fixed-by-upgrade">The real vulnerabilities, fixed by upgrade</a></h2> <p>Two denial-of-service advisories are genuine and are fixed by moving to the patched lines:</p> <ul> <li>quick-xml (RUSTSEC-2026-0194 quadratic start-tag parsing, RUSTSEC-2026-0195 unbounded namespace allocation) reached three opt-in readers. The premise had gone stale: undoc 0.5.3 and rbook 0.7.10 now require quick-xml at version 0.41, so a lockfile-only bump cleared the office and epub paths. The geometry reader now uses threemf2 in place of threemf, which drops quick-xml entirely (it reads with instant-xml), a ten-line port whose 3mf golden reproduces byte for byte.</li> <li>crossbeam-epoch (RUSTSEC-2026-0204, an invalid pointer dereference in the pointer formatter), freshly published and reaching the opt-in pdf reader through rayon, is fixed by a bump to 0.9.20.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-unmaintained-advisories-retired-by-maintained-forks"><a class="header" href="#the-unmaintained-advisories-retired-by-maintained-forks">The unmaintained advisories, retired by maintained forks</a></h2> <p>The four unmaintained-crate advisories are retired through <code>[patch.crates-io]</code> redirects to maintained slartibardfast forks, per call/0040: paste to pastey, atomic-polyfill to portable-atomic, proc-macro-error to a two-crate rename of proc-macro-error2, and ttf-parser adopted as a maintained lane (it has no successor). cargo-deny does not advisory-check a git source, so each redirect retires the advisory genuinely rather than by a blanket ignore. ttf-parser forbids unsafe code, so the lane's obligation is a fuzzing pass over its untrusted-input surface, not a memory-safety audit.</p> <h2 id="release-and-reproducibility"><a class="header" href="#release-and-reproducibility">Release and reproducibility</a></h2> <p>The patched crates and the migrated readers are all opt-in, absent from the default <code>text</code> binary that is built and deployed, so the release is change-class neither and the default binary reproduces (its hash moves only with the version string). Re-vendored offline as vendor-v2, re-pinned, receipt recorded, and the whole-suite <code>software --check</code> is green with the deny.toml ignore list empty.</p> <h2 id="verification-37"><a class="header" href="#verification-37">Verification</a></h2> <p><code>cargo deny check advisories</code> is clean with an empty ignore list and no accepted risk. The geometry 3mf golden reproduces under threemf2. <code>cargo build --all-features</code> compiles every opt-in reader against the forks. The default binary re-derives its recorded hash offline against vendor-v2. Closes connollydavid/host-reference#3.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0069-release-gate-discharges-obligations-the-release-discharges-the-component-it-releases-and-prompts-every-carried-pin"><a class="header" href="#plan0069-release-gate-discharges-obligations-the-release-discharges-the-component-it-releases-and-prompts-every-carried-pin">plan/0069 release-gate-discharges-obligations: the release discharges the component it releases and prompts every carried pin</a></h1> <h2 id="build-status-2026-07-07-1"><a class="header" href="#build-status-2026-07-07-1">Build status (2026-07-07)</a></h2> <p>Shipped across two host-lifecycle releases; both gaps closed; the whole-suite verify gate is green.</p> <ul> <li> <p>v0.40.0 (<code>49b64b4</code>, artifact <code>414496cd</code>): Gap 1 + the first Gap 2 cut.</p> </li> <li> <p>v0.40.1 (<code>9092416</code>, artifact <code>09707ff2</code>): Gap 2 widened to the derived intersection (below). v0.40.1 was the first release to exercise Gap 1's own gate: <code>host-lifecycle release</code> ran "discharging host-lifecycle.allium …" and passed, so the gate now covers the tool that ships it.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Gap 1</strong>: <code>run_release</code> step 1b runs <code>discharge_problems</code> (<code>allium plan</code> + <code>obligation_gaps</code> with no <code>--tests</code> + <code>manifest_staleness_problems</code>) for each <code>.allium</code> the released component carries, after the verify recheck and before the version bump; a non-empty result blocks the release. Verified both ways: a staled digest blocks <code>host-lifecycle release</code> at the gate (<code>STALE … release blocked</code>, exit 1), and a clean component passes (host-lifecycle, 41/41 dispositioned).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Gap 2</strong>: the carried-template-pin set is <strong>derived</strong>: <code>carried_template_tools</code> = <code>.host-software</code> ∩ <code>host-template/.gitmodules tools/</code> names, and both <code>template_pin_problems</code> (detection) and <code>template_pin_bump_lines</code> (prompt) consume it, so they cannot skew. A new family tool that lands in both lanes is detected and prompted with no code change (the Fen bar: a fixture <code>host-foo</code> in both lanes is carried). host-lifecycle carries a second surface (the prose-CI <code>--rev</code> install), kept as a labelled special case (it is the prose-gate tool, a methodology fact, and a mechanical <code>--rev</code>, not prose). External referenced tools (allium, specula) are excluded by the intersection.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Open questions resolved: the test-dir question dissolved (the gate runs with no <code>--tests</code>, since <code>staleness_problems</code> is independent of it); allium-cli is required at release time, host-prove is not (no <code>--rederive</code>); a hard gate at release, no staging. The carried set is derived, not hardcoded, so the detection and prompt serve any producer (not only agentic-host's two tools).</p> <h2 id="scope-and-what-this-plan-does-not-fix"><a class="header" href="#scope-and-what-this-plan-does-not-fix">Scope, and what this plan does not fix</a></h2> <p>This plan closes two release-flow gaps that surfaced when host-lint v0.14.0 shipped with stale obligation digests: the release gate does not discharge the component it releases, and the release tool prompts the carried-template pin bump only for host-lifecycle.</p> <p>It does not guarantee a release ships green. A sibling incident, host-reference v0.1.5 (unformatted code, <code>cargo fmt --check</code> red), is a different lane this plan leaves to a follow-up. And component release-CI triggers on the tag, so lanes that only run in CI (the multi-platform build matrix, GitHub-hosted kani, <code>cargo test</code>) remain the final gate; a local pre-flight can only catch the lanes it can reproduce locally.</p> <h2 id="the-incident-and-root-cause"><a class="header" href="#the-incident-and-root-cause">The incident and root cause</a></h2> <p>host-lint v0.14.0 shipped with its own CI red on the tag: its release commit bundled feature code that changed <code>src/lib.rs</code> without re-recording the two <code>DetectReviewCodeAsName</code> obligation digests, so the <code>--strict-discharge</code> lane failed on the tag. The verify gate's discharge reported STALE, but only after the release had tagged and pushed. This is the recurring born-red-tag class (plan/0045, plan/0048).</p> <p>Two gaps in <code>run_release</code>:</p> <p><strong>Gap 1: the release gate does not discharge the component it releases.</strong> Step 1 runs the manifest verify phase's <code>recheck =</code> (host-template <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>), which is <code>validate plan/ call/ && prose . && reconcile .</code>, a project-level prose-and-drift check. It does not run the obligations check against the released component's <code><spec>.obligations</code> ledger, so a stale digest or an undispositioned obligation in that component is invisible at release time. The discharge runs only in the component's own CI, after the tag.</p> <p><strong>Gap 2: the release tool prompts the carried-template pin bump only for host-lifecycle.</strong> <code>template_pin_bump_lines</code> returns the host-template pin-bump steps only when the released component is host-lifecycle. host-lint is also carried as <code>host-template/tools/host-lint</code>, so releasing it leaves the template pin behind; <code>software --check</code>'s call/0038 HAZARD catches it after the fact, but the release flow does not prompt the operator. The call/0038 rule is spine-resident (host-template <code>CLAUDE.md</code>); only the tool prompt is missing.</p> <h2 id="decided-direction-6"><a class="header" href="#decided-direction-6">Decided direction</a></h2> <p>Both gaps close in one host-lifecycle release; both live in <code>run_release</code>.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Gap 1</strong>: <code>run_release</code> gains a component-scoped obligations check as a gate step, after the manifest recheck and before the version bump. It runs <code>host-lifecycle obligations <spec></code> (no <code>--tests</code>, no <code>--rederive</code>) for each <code>.allium</code> the released component carries; a component with no spec is skipped, the way <code>software --check</code> already detects lanes. The offline check catches MISSING and STALE dispositions and STALE input digests (<code>staleness_problems</code> runs whenever <code>--rederive</code> is absent, independent of <code>--tests</code>), which is exactly the born-red class. Test-name resolution and proof re-derivation stay in component CI, where the test sources and heavy verifiers live. A non-zero check blocks the release the way a red verify recheck already does.</li> <li><strong>Gap 2</strong>: <code>template_pin_bump_lines</code> generalizes to every component the carried template pins. It reads the template's <code>.gitmodules</code> against the recorded pointer (so a partially-initialized submodule is handled, not silently skipped) and emits the bump steps for any released component that appears there, not only host-lifecycle. No spine change (the rule is spine-resident); the tool catches up to the rule.</li> </ul> <h2 id="open-design-questions"><a class="header" href="#open-design-questions">Open design questions</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>allium-cli dependency.</strong> <code>obligations</code> shells out to <code>allium plan</code> to derive the obligation set, so allium-cli must be on PATH at release time. It is on this host; a fresh-clone release environment must install it. host-prove is not needed (the gate runs no <code>--rederive</code>). Flag, don't hide.</li> <li><strong>Hard gate vs staged warn-then-retire.</strong> A release-time gate is not the same as reddening an adopter's <code>software --check</code>: a release that ships its own component red should block. Proposal: hard gate at release, no staging. Operator confirm.</li> </ol> <h2 id="build-sequence-11"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-11">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="add-discharge-gate"><a class="header" href="#add-discharge-gate">Add the component-scoped obligations gate</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test manifest_staleness</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lifecycle/main/src/main.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="generalize-pin-bump"><a class="header" href="#generalize-pin-bump">Generalize the carried-pin prompt</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: cd software/host-lifecycle/main && cargo test template_pin_bump</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lifecycle/main/src/main.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-repin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-repin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #add-discharge-gate, #generalize-pin-bump</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="follow-ups-not-this-plan"><a class="header" href="#follow-ups-not-this-plan">Follow-ups (not this plan)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The general release pre-flight.</strong> Step 3 runs only <code>cargo build --release</code>; the component's other CI lanes (fmt, clippy, test, allium, kani, deny) do not run locally before tagging. <code>cargo fmt --check</code> is the cheapest and would have caught host-reference v0.1.5; a follow-up could add the cheap local lanes (fmt, and clippy where CI runs it) to the release container step. The heavier lanes and the multi-platform matrix stay in tag-CI by necessity.</li> <li><strong>Prose surfaces (skills) when a standard lands.</strong> The pin gate is deliberately mechanical: skills and other authored prose that <em>reference</em> a tool version are not pin surfaces, because there is no standard machine-readable form for such a reference. The Agent Skills open format (agentskills.io) and the Skills Over MCP Working Group (SEP-2640, a Resources-based Skills Extension; a <code>skills.json</code> registry with dependency metadata is in progress) are moving toward machine-readable skill metadata. Track SEP-2640 / skills.json: when a skill's tool-version reference becomes a declared, machine-readable field, the pin gate can promote it (the derived-carried-set mechanism already routes by surface kind, so the addition is a new kind, not a rework).</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-38"><a class="header" href="#verification-38">Verification</a></h2> <p>A constructed stale-digest worktree blocks <code>host-lifecycle release <component></code> with the same STALE line the verify gate surfaces, before any version bump or tag. Releasing host-lint prints the host-template <code>tools/host-lint</code> bump steps; releasing host-reference prints none (it is not carried). clippy clean, the inline suite passes, and the whole-suite verify gate is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0070-benchmark-data-numerals-the-bare-numeral-lane-stops-flagging-measurement-data"><a class="header" href="#plan0070-benchmark-data-numerals-the-bare-numeral-lane-stops-flagging-measurement-data">plan/0070 benchmark-data-numerals: the bare-numeral lane stops flagging measurement data</a></h1> <p>Answers <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/21">host-lint#21</a>. The bare-numeral scanner flags every numeral-shaped token in document content as a potential naming tell, so a benchmark-heavy engineering record produces thousands of false positives where the numerals are measurement values, not filing-code labels. The <code>host-lifecycle remap --check</code> gate cannot close with them present, and declaring each value in the LEXICON does not scale: one such record carries 829 once-only measurement values. The naming and prose lanes are clean on these records; only the bare-numeral advisory fires on data.</p> <p>The fix is precision at the warn tier, not a new escape. The bare-dotted-code rule (VOCABULARY.md §4) gains the context it was missing: a numeral that sits in a data position is skipped. The noun-gated flag tier is untouched, so a real tell still flags wherever it appears.</p> <h2 id="the-false-positive-classes-grounded-in-a-fen-run"><a class="header" href="#the-false-positive-classes-grounded-in-a-fen-run">The false-positive classes, grounded in a Fen run</a></h2> <p>A neutral classification probe on the real qwen3.5-4b (see gather-data.md) returned 32 of 32 correct across two temperatures and a shuffled order. The boundary Fen drew is the boundary the rule will encode. The false-positive classes are a table cell, an approximation or comparison operator, and a compound or domain unit. The label controls stayed label, including the load-bearing precision case: a real tell placed inside a table cell still reads as a label, because the flag tier is location-independent.</p> <h2 id="decided-direction-7"><a class="header" href="#decided-direction-7">Decided direction</a></h2> <p>Four additions to the warn rule, each narrowing it only:</p> <ul> <li>Table cells. A bare numeral whose neighbours are pipe delimiters is a data cell; the column header that carries the unit sits on another line the token-local rule cannot see.</li> <li>Prose operators. A numeral preceded by an approximation or comparison operator, or followed by the multiplication sign, is a quantity.</li> <li>Compound units. A numeral followed by a slashed unit token is a quantity; the slash is a structural signal in the same way the pipe is.</li> <li>Domain units, declared. A non-structural domain unit after the numeral is declared in the LEXICON and consulted alongside the built-in unit set. An all-caps unit before the numeral is already skipped by the all-caps designator rule; the gap is a domain unit that follows.</li> </ul> <h2 id="open-design-questions-1"><a class="header" href="#open-design-questions-1">Open design questions</a></h2> <ul> <li>The unit-declaration form. Whether the LEXICON carries a dedicated block for units or a per-entry marker is an authoring-ergonomics call. A second Fen run settles it the way plan/0066 settled the band form, rather than the author guessing.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-12"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-12">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">Gather the Fen data</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the classification table in gather-data.md is 32 of 32 at two temperatures</li> </ul> <h3 id="skip-table-cells"><a class="header" href="#skip-table-cells">Skip table-cell numerals</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test table_cell</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="prose-quantity-operators"><a class="header" href="#prose-quantity-operators">Add prose-quantity operators</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test quantity_operators</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="compound-units"><a class="header" href="#compound-units">Recognise slashed compound units</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test compound_units</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="lexicon-domain-units"><a class="header" href="#lexicon-domain-units">Declare domain units in the LEXICON</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test declared_units</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs, software/host-lint/main/src/main.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="update-vocabulary"><a class="header" href="#update-vocabulary">Document the shapes in VOCABULARY.md</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #skip-table-cells, #prose-quantity-operators, #compound-units, #lexicon-domain-units</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && cargo test vocabulary</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/VOCABULARY.md</li> </ul> <h3 id="spec-and-obligations"><a class="header" href="#spec-and-obligations">Update the spec and obligations</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #update-vocabulary</li> <li>verify: cd software/host-lint/main && host-lifecycle obligations host-lint.allium --tests tests</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/host-lint.allium, software/host-lint/main/host-lint.obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-repin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-repin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #spec-and-obligations</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h3 id="close-issue"><a class="header" href="#close-issue">Close host-lint#21</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #release-and-repin</li> <li>verify: attested operator</li> </ul> <h2 id="follow-ups-not-this-plan-1"><a class="header" href="#follow-ups-not-this-plan-1">Follow-ups (not this plan)</a></h2> <ul> <li>The density advisory. The issue's third option, a single advisory when a document carries very many bare numerals, is out of scope; the precision fix removes the mass of false positives directly, so the density signal is no longer needed to close the gate.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-39"><a class="header" href="#verification-39">Verification</a></h2> <p>The released host-lint binary reproduces its recorded hash. The unit and integration suites cover each new skip and its controls, with a real tell still flagging inside a table cell. The obligations manifest is fully dispositioned, and the whole-suite verify gate is green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0070-gather-data-the-datalabel-boundary-measured-on-the-real-qwen35-4b"><a class="header" href="#plan0070-gather-data-the-datalabel-boundary-measured-on-the-real-qwen35-4b">plan/0070 gather-data: the data/label boundary, measured on the real qwen3.5-4b</a></h1> <p>The decision rests on data, not assertion. A neutral classification probe confirms where a weak model draws the data-versus-label line, so the rule encodes the natural boundary rather than an author's judgment. Fen is qwen3.5-4b at Q8_0, driven through the pal MCP with model <code>qwen3.5-4b</code>, parsed after the thinking block. Two full passes were run: the first in authored order, the second with the items shuffled.</p> <h2 id="the-probe"><a class="header" href="#the-probe">The probe</a></h2> <p>Sixteen snippets from a benchmark report, each with one token highlighted. Fen classifies the token as DATA (a measurement or result value) or LABEL (an identifier or name reference). The framing is neutral and names no structural cue as decisive.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">passes: temperature 0 (authored order), temperature 0.3 (shuffled) DATA classes (the false positives this plan fixes): | A100 | 11.34 | 10.00 | 11.34 table cell | latency_ms | 25.27 | 25.27 table cell NMSE ≈ 1.0 1.0 approx operator speedup ~2.2× over baseline 2.2 tilde and multiplier accuracy > 67.5% 67.5 comparison operator throughput 11.34 t/s 11.34 compound unit cost 3.2 ms/token 3.2 slashed unit LABEL controls (true tells, must still warn or flag): ## 5.5 error handling 5.5 bare-numeral header (flag) Phase 2.1: auth refactor 2.1 noun-gated (flag) Sprint 3 backlog 3 noun-gated (flag) exec tools (5.5) 5.5 parenthetical code-as-name (warn) as decided in 2.1 2.1 bare dotted code (warn) see section 3 of the spec 3 advisory ordinal noun (warn) upgrade to 2.1 2.1 recall-biased warn </code></pre> <h2 id="result"><a class="header" href="#result">Result</a></h2> <p>32 of 32 correct, identical across both passes. Fen drew the line exactly where the rule will encode it: every table cell, operator, and unit-bearing numeral is DATA; every header, noun-gated, and bare-as-name numeral is LABEL. The shuffled order and the higher temperature changed no verdict, so the result is not a first-option or ordering artifact.</p> <p>The load-bearing precision case is a real tell placed inside a table cell. It still read LABEL, because the flag tier is location-independent. Skipping a table-cell bare numeral opens no hole.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">| Phase 2.1: auth | status: done | LABEL (the flag rule catches it, pipes or not) </code></pre> <h2 id="the-framing-sensitivity-note"><a class="header" href="#the-framing-sensitivity-note">The framing-sensitivity note</a></h2> <p>An earlier leading prompt that named version as a DATA cue made Fen call the canonical bare dotted code DATA. Under the neutral framing it is consistently LABEL. A weak model's read of a bare dotted code is framing-sensitive. That is independent support for keeping that form a recall-biased warn with the LEXICON as the declared escape, rather than promoting it to a flag.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0071-host-install-mode-the-curl-one-liner-the-manifest-the-receipt-the-handoff"><a class="header" href="#plan0071-host-install-mode-the-curl-one-liner-the-manifest-the-receipt-the-handoff">plan/0071 host-install-mode: the curl one-liner, the manifest, the receipt, the handoff</a></h1> <p>This milestone completes plan/0065's remaining <code>host</code> install mode. The <code>host</code> repo gains <code>install.sh</code>, a <code>curl -fsSL ... | bash</code> entry point that downloads the host-* binaries with verified provenance, scaffolds a new <code>agentic-<name></code> project, detects the operator's agent harness, and launches it to continue the bringup Q&A. The install manifest, the local receipt, the platform/shell detection, and the harness allowlist are the substance; the curl script is the surface.</p> <h2 id="scope-what-this-completes"><a class="header" href="#scope-what-this-completes">Scope: what this completes</a></h2> <p>plan/0065 shipped the onboarding engine (<code>host-lifecycle init</code>/<code>adopt</code>, the MCP server, the shims) as v0.39.0 and locked the install-mode contract in its README (lines 109-280). What remained was the install mode itself: the manifest, the verified binary download, the receipt, the platform/shell detection, the harness handoff, and the <code>install.sh</code> surface. This plan delivers all of it.</p> <p>The mechanical decisions below are grounded in a documented survey recorded in <a href="plan/0071-host-install-mode/gather-data.html">gather-data.md</a>: the installer patterns, the harness names and star ordering, and the release assets each component actually publishes. The UX conditionals are <strong>not</strong> yet grounded. Probing them needs the real script output rather than a mock, so the Fen probe runs at the <code>#fen-acceptance</code> node and this README's UX choices stand as proposals until it does.</p> <h2 id="the-one-liner"><a class="header" href="#the-one-liner">The one-liner</a></h2> <pre><code>curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/host/main/install.sh | bash </code></pre> <p>Named:</p> <pre><code>curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/host/main/install.sh | bash -s -- agentic-acme </code></pre> <p>A short URL (<code>https://host.david.connol.ly/install.sh</code>) may redirect here in due course; the script assumes nothing about it.</p> <h2 id="the-installcreate-separation"><a class="header" href="#the-installcreate-separation">The install/create separation</a></h2> <p>plan/0065 line 170: "Install and create are two failure domains, so the one-command form does not fold them into one atomic step." The script honours this as two phases with a clean seam:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Install phase</strong>: detect platform, fetch the install manifest, verify its authenticity against the trust root, download each binary in the install set, verify each against its recorded hash, install all-or-nothing to the path, write the local receipt. A partial install records the missing binaries and exits non-zero; nothing lands silently.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Create phase</strong>: prompt for the project name (or accept <code>$1</code>), run <code>host-lifecycle init <name></code> to scaffold, detect the operator's installed agent harnesses, present a menu (or auto-select if one), and <code>exec</code> the chosen harness inside the project directory so the bringup Q&A continues interactively.</p> </li> </ol> <p>A first-run does both phases in sequence, but the install verifies the whole install set landed before create begins. "A bootstrap never runs against a partial toolchain" (plan/0065:173).</p> <h2 id="the-install-set"><a class="header" href="#the-install-set">The install set</a></h2> <p><strong><code>host-lifecycle</code> and <code>host-lint</code>, and nothing else.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle</code> does the mechanical work of scaffolding and <code>host-lint</code> is the artifact whose absence the bootstrap gate reports by name, which is why <code>software/host/main</code>'s README already asks an adopter for exactly this pair.</p> <p>The set is not the six <code>deploy</code> lines in <code>.host-software</code>, and the survey is what settles that: those two are the only components publishing a complete platform matrix. <code>host-prove</code> publishes a single linux musl binary, and the two reference helpers publish a vendor bundle and no binary at all, so an all-or-nothing install over the six would fail on every mac and every windows machine. Holding the set at two means the install works on every target it claims without any component having to cut a release first. Widening it later is a manifest change and a release in the widened component, not a change to this script.</p> <h2 id="the-manifest-and-the-trust-root"><a class="header" href="#the-manifest-and-the-trust-root">The manifest and the trust root</a></h2> <p>plan/0065 lines 121-132 and 234-243 locked the contract:</p> <ul> <li>An install manifest records each binary's version and canonical SHA256 hash.</li> <li>The hashes are single-sourced from the public per-component release receipts (the GitHub release asset digests), never from agentic-host's <code>.host-software</code>.</li> <li>The manifest is keyed to the template revision, because <code>host</code> install is also the upgrade route: an adopter on a given revision receives the binaries that revision pins.</li> <li>The trust root is the reproducible build itself: every host-* binary is reproducibly built from pinned source plus a recorded toolchain, so <code>software --verify_build</code> re-derives its recorded hash anywhere. The installer treats that hash as the root. No external signer, no bootstrap problem, offline by construction. Sigstore keyless is an optional identity layer, not the load-bearing root.</li> <li>The manifest and the install script are themselves authenticated before they run, so a corrupted or substituted manifest cannot present a self-consistent set that the leaf hash-check would pass. The trust-anchor material travels into the local install receipt so a later verification does not depend on refetching a moving remote.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Manifest authentication: settled.</strong> HTTPS to GitHub is the transport-layer trust root, identical to every curl|bash installer used by rustup, homebrew, bun, deno, Claude Code, Codex CLI all trust HTTPS for first-run). The manifest is served from the same repo over the same TLS as <code>install.sh</code> itself, so the trust boundary for the manifest is the same boundary the user already crossed to run the script. The reproducible build is the independent verification path: an adopter can always rebuild any binary from pinned source + toolchain (<code>software --verify_build</code>) and compare hashes, offline, with no external signer. plan/0065:234 already removed cosign as "the wrong layer"; this confirms that ruling. No bootstrap paradox: first-run trust is HTTPS, durable trust is the reproducible build.</p> <h2 id="the-local-receipt"><a class="header" href="#the-local-receipt">The local receipt</a></h2> <p>plan/0065 lines 134-143: the install writes a durable machine-side receipt recording each installed binary, its version, its verified hash, and the trust anchor used. It is persisted locally (not in the project's <code>.host</code> stamp, which describes a project, not the machine's binaries) and is re-verifiable offline. A partial install records the missing binaries as absent or pending and never leaves a silently-missing tool untraceable.</p> <p><strong>Receipt location: settled.</strong> <code>$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentic-<name>/install-receipt</code> (defaulting to <code>~/.local/share/agentic-<name>/install-receipt</code> when <code>XDG_DATA_HOME</code> is unset). Each project gets its own machine-side receipt; multiple projects on the same machine can be on different template revisions with different binary versions. XDG-conformant, namespaced by the project name (not a generic <code>host/</code> dir), and distinct from the per-project <code>.host-receipts</code> that plan/0037 established for applied-set receipts.</p> <p><strong>Self-update is never an install.sh concern.</strong> plan/0065:142 mentions a self-update that rewrites the receipt in the same step it swaps the binary, but that is a function of the agentic harness (the agent running <code>host-lifecycle upgrade</code> inside the project), not of this install script. <code>install.sh</code> does first-run install only. Re-running it scaffolds a new project, not an update.</p> <h2 id="platform-and-shell-detection"><a class="header" href="#platform-and-shell-detection">Platform and shell detection</a></h2> <p>Three OS families, two architectures, and the user's login shell for PATH configuration:</p> <p><strong>OS detection</strong> (the proven pattern from the opencode installer, verified against the release asset names):</p> <pre><code>darwin macOS -> host-lifecycle-darwin-{amd64,arm64} linux Linux -> host-lifecycle-linux-{amd64,arm64} windows MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN -> host-lifecycle-windows-{amd64,arm64}.exe </code></pre> <p><code>uname -s</code> distinguishes the three; <code>uname -m</code> maps <code>x86_64</code> to amd64 and <code>aarch64</code> to arm64.</p> <p><strong>Shell detection</strong> (for PATH config modification, since the script runs as bash via curl|bash but writes to the user's login shell config):</p> <p>The script reads <code>$SHELL</code> and writes the idiomatic PATH line to the right config file: <code>~/.zshrc</code> (zsh, macOS default since Catalina), <code>~/.bashrc</code> (bash), <code>~/.config/fish/config.fish</code> (fish, using <code>fish_add_path</code>), or <code>~/.profile</code> (fallback). The opencode installer's <code>current_shell</code> case block is the proven reference pattern.</p> <p><strong>Git Bash on Win32</strong> (git-scm): <code>uname -s</code> returns <code>MINGW*</code> or <code>MSYS*</code>, which maps to the windows platform. The script downloads the <code>.exe</code> binary, installs to the MSYS2 bin dir, and <code>command -v</code> in Git Bash resolves <code>.exe</code>-suffixed binaries transparently, so the harness allowlist needs no platform-specific logic.</p> <h2 id="prerequisite-checks-fail-early-fail-loudly"><a class="header" href="#prerequisite-checks-fail-early-fail-loudly">Prerequisite checks: fail early, fail loudly</a></h2> <p>Before any work, the script checks its own prerequisites and exits with an actionable message if any is missing:</p> <ul> <li><code>git</code>: host-lifecycle clones the template during scaffold</li> <li>SHA256 verifier: <code>sha256sum</code> (Linux/Git Bash), <code>shasum -a 256</code> (macOS), or <code>certutil</code> (native Windows). Detected before the verify step, not at it.</li> <li><code>curl</code>: inherently present (<code>curl | bash</code>), but checked if re-run from a local file.</li> </ul> <p><code>cargo</code> and <code>rustup</code> are NOT prerequisites of the install script (it downloads pre-built binaries), but the harness-driven bringup inside the scaffolded project will eventually need them. The script notes this in its final handoff block, not as a gate.</p> <h2 id="harness-detection-and-the-allowlist"><a class="header" href="#harness-detection-and-the-allowlist">Harness detection and the allowlist</a></h2> <p>After scaffolding, the script detects installed agent harnesses and offers to launch one so the bringup Q&A continues interactively inside the project. The allowlist is strict: only known harness binaries are probed, ordered by GitHub star count (a data signal, not an opinion), not alphabetically and not by PATH order (which varies by machine).</p> <p>The 6-harness allowlist (star-ordered, binary names confirmed from official docs and the harnesscli unified meta-tool):</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Binary</th><th>Harness</th><th>Stars</th><th>Confidence</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>1</td><td><code>opencode</code></td><td>opencode</td><td>184k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>2</td><td><code>claude</code></td><td>Claude Code</td><td>137k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>3</td><td><code>codex</code></td><td>Codex CLI</td><td>96.5k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>4</td><td><code>qwen</code></td><td>Qwen Code</td><td>25.9k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>5</td><td><code>cursor-agent</code></td><td>Cursor Agent</td><td>unquantified</td><td>confirmed binary; <code>agent</code> fallback too generic for a strict allowlist, skip</td></tr> <tr><td>6</td><td><code>pi</code></td><td>Pi Agent</td><td>unquantified</td><td>confirmed binary</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Dropped from consideration:</p> <ul> <li><code>cheetahclaws</code>: PyPI package name confirmed, but the console-script entry point is unconfirmed. Re-evaluate when the binary invocation is documented.</li> <li><code>zcode</code>: no official CLI binary; only a third-party wrapper (zCode-CLI-X). The official distribution is a GUI installer.</li> </ul> <p>No <code>HARNESS</code> environment variable: research confirmed no cross-vendor standard exists (each tool self-identifies via its own native var, e.g. <code>CLAUDECODE</code>). The closest to a standard is the third-party <code>detect-coding-agent</code> crate reading native vars, which is for detecting a <em>running</em> harness, not an <em>installed</em> one. Our script detects installed harnesses via <code>command -v</code>, which is correct regardless.</p> <p><strong>Selection logic:</strong></p> <ul> <li><code>$1</code> is the project name, not the harness. The harness is never a positional arg.</li> <li>Zero harnesses detected: scaffold anyway, print "install opencode or claude, then <code>cd <name></code>." The project is ready regardless.</li> <li>One harness detected: auto-select, no menu.</li> <li>Multiple detected: numbered menu via <code>read -rp ... < /dev/tty</code> (curl owns stdin). The numbering follows the order above (deterministic across machines). The menu lists only names and numbers, no star counts, no popularity labels. The ordering is the star ordering, but the numbers are not shown to the user.</li> <li><code>exec <harness></code> in the project dir replaces the script process; the harness reads the scaffolded CLAUDE.md as its entrance and continues the bringup Q&A. Because <code>curl | bash</code> runs bash as a child of the user's shell, <code>exec</code> replaces that child, not the parent shell. When the harness exits, the user is back in their original directory. The script prints <code>cd <name></code> as its final line before <code>exec</code> so the command is in scrollback. This is the curl-pipe-bash pattern's natural behavior, not a workaround.</li> </ul> <h2 id="name-resolution"><a class="header" href="#name-resolution">Name resolution</a></h2> <p>plan/0065 lines 99-107 locked the name backstop: the verb accepts the name by flag or environment, else prompts on a controlling terminal, else exits with code 3 and a machine-parseable stderr line naming the missing field.</p> <p>For <code>install.sh</code>, the name resolves in this order:</p> <ol> <li><code>$1</code> if provided (<code>bash -s -- agentic-acme</code>)</li> <li><code>read -rp 'Project name (agentic-<name>): ' name < /dev/tty</code> if no arg and a TTY is available</li> <li>Exit 3 with a machine-parseable message if neither</li> </ol> <p>The name is validated: it must match <code>^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$</code> and is prefixed with <code>agentic-</code> if it does not already start with it. Path traversal (<code>../</code>), shell metacharacters, and empty strings are rejected before reaching <code>host-lifecycle init</code>. <code>agentic-host</code> is reserved (it is the name of this project's own development host) and refused with an actionable message; the script exits non-zero and suggests choosing a different name.</p> <h2 id="the-allium-specification"><a class="header" href="#the-allium-specification">The Allium specification</a></h2> <p>The install state machine is genuinely complex (platform detect, manifest fetch, trust verify, per-binary download and hash-check, all-or-nothing, receipt, then name prompt, scaffold, harness detect, launch), so it earns a spec, not just tests.</p> <p>The spec lives in the <code>host</code> repo (specs-live-with-software, plan/0012) and models the surface <code>InstallRun</code> with states and transitions:</p> <ul> <li><code>Prerequisites</code> -> <code>Detecting</code> (all met) | <code>MissingPrereq</code> (any absent, exit 1)</li> <li><code>Detecting</code> -> <code>FetchingManifest</code> (platform identified) | <code>UnsupportedPlatform</code> (exit 1)</li> <li><code>FetchingManifest</code> -> <code>VerifyingManifest</code> (fetched) | <code>FetchFailed</code> (exit 5)</li> <li><code>VerifyingManifest</code> -> <code>Downloading</code> (trust root verified) | <code>ManifestUntrusted</code> (exit 1)</li> <li><code>Downloading</code> -> <code>VerifyingBinary</code> (per-binary) | <code>DownloadFailed</code> (exit 5)</li> <li><code>VerifyingBinary</code> -> <code>Downloading</code> (hash matches, next binary) | <code>HashMismatch</code> (exit 1, all-or-nothing) | <code>AllVerified</code> (last binary matches)</li> <li><code>AllVerified</code> -> <code>WritingReceipt</code> -> <code>InstallDone</code></li> <li><code>InstallDone</code> -> <code>NamePrompt</code> (create phase begins)</li> <li><code>NamePrompt</code> -> <code>Scaffolding</code> (name resolved) | <code>NameRequired</code> (no TTY, exit 3) | <code>NameReserved</code> (<code>agentic-host</code>, exit 4)</li> <li><code>Scaffolding</code> -> <code>HarnessDetect</code> (project created) | <code>TargetExists</code> (exit 4)</li> <li><code>HarnessDetect</code> -> <code>Launching</code> (resolved) | <code>NoHarness</code> (print message, exit 0)</li> <li><code>Launching</code> -> <code>Done</code> (<code>exec harness</code>)</li> </ul> <p>Invariants:</p> <ul> <li>Each binary's hash is verified before the binary lands on PATH.</li> <li>No project is scaffolded before the whole install set is installed and verified.</li> <li>The receipt is written before the create phase begins.</li> <li>The name is never empty when it reaches <code>Scaffolding</code>.</li> <li>The name is never <code>agentic-host</code> (reserved).</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-40"><a class="header" href="#verification-40">Verification</a></h2> <p><strong>Integration tests</strong> exercise every branch:</p> <ul> <li>Prerequisites: missing <code>git</code> -> exit 1 with actionable message</li> <li>Platform: darwin/linux/windows detection from mocked <code>uname</code></li> <li>Manifest: trust-root failure -> exit 1 before any download</li> <li>Binary: hash mismatch -> exit 1, nothing on PATH, receipt records the failure</li> <li>Binary: all match -> receipt written, all binaries on PATH</li> <li>Name: from arg, from TTY prompt, from neither (exit 3)</li> <li>Name: path-traversal rejected, shell-metacharacter rejected, empty rejected</li> <li>Name: <code>agentic-host</code> refused (reserved), actionable message, exit 4</li> <li>Harness: zero detected (print + exit 0), one detected (auto-select), multiple (menu), invalid menu selection (re-prompt)</li> <li>Scaffold: existing target -> exit 4</li> <li>Shell config: correct file written for zsh/bash/fish/profile</li> </ul> <p><strong>Fen probe</strong> (gather-data.md) validates the UX conditionals:</p> <ul> <li>Name prompt legibility: does <code>(agentic-<name>)</code> produce <code>agentic-acme</code>, not <code>acme</code>?</li> <li>No-harness message: does the print-and-exit read as actionable to a weak agent?</li> <li>Manifest authentication pattern: which of the surveyed installer patterns reads as trustworthy to a cold read?</li> <li>Ordered menu: does a weak agent read a numbered ordered menu (names only, no star counts) without position bias?</li> </ul> <p><strong>Installer survey</strong> (gather-data.md) grounds the mechanical patterns:</p> <ul> <li>The hash-check-and-verify pattern (opencode, rustup, homebrew, deno, bun, Claude Code, Codex CLI): what do the shipping majority do?</li> <li>The manifest format: TOML (host-lifecycle's idiom) vs JSON vs plain text</li> <li>The trust-root mechanism: reproducible build hash vs external signer vs GitHub-digest-only</li> <li>The receipt location: <code>~/.host-receipts</code> vs XDG vs home-dir dotfile</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-13"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-13">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The tasks are anchored receipted nodes (plan/0042), built as a forward graph:</p> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">gather-data</a></h3> <p>Grounds every conditional in data: the Fen probe (UX), the installer survey (mechanical patterns), and the binary-name/harness survey confirmation.</p> <ul> <li>verify: every conditional in this README traces to a gather-data.md row</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-install-sh"><a class="header" href="#write-install-sh">write-install-sh</a></h3> <p>The tight bash script, zero third-party deps. Implements the full state machine: prerequisites, platform/shell detection, manifest fetch, trust verify, per-binary download and hash-check, all-or-nothing, receipt, name resolution, scaffold, harness detect, launch.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>bash -n install.sh</code> (syntax), <code>shellcheck install.sh</code> (lint; requires adding a shellcheck job to the host repo's CI, which currently has only a prose gate per plan/0038), integration tests pass</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-manifest"><a class="header" href="#write-manifest">write-manifest</a></h3> <p>The install manifest keyed to the template revision, single-sourced from public release receipts. Generated or declared; its format settled by the installer survey.</p> <ul> <li>verify: manifest hashes match the public release asset digests for every binary in the install set</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-allium-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-allium-spec">write-allium-spec</a></h3> <p>The <code>InstallRun</code> surface with states, transitions, and invariants as specified above.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>allium check</code> + <code>allium analyse</code> exit 0, zero findings</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">write-obligations</a></h3> <p>Every <code>allium plan</code> obligation dispositioned in a <code><spec>.obligations</code> manifest, discharged by the integration tests.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle obligations <spec> --tests tests --strict-discharge</code> clean</li> <li>depends: #write-allium-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">write-tests</a></h3> <p>Integration tests covering every branch listed in Verification above. The test harness mocks <code>uname</code>, <code>command -v</code>, <code>/dev/tty</code>, and the network (manifest fetch, binary download) so tests run offline and deterministic.</p> <ul> <li>verify: full test suite green, every spec obligation exercised</li> <li>depends: #write-install-sh, #write-allium-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="host-repo-release"><a class="header" href="#host-repo-release">host-repo-release</a></h3> <p>Ship <code>install.sh</code>, the manifest, the spec, and the tests in the <code>host</code> repo. The entrance ships through its own release authority (plan/0065:192-194).</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle entrance --check</code> green, <code>software --check</code> clean, CI green</li> <li>depends: #write-install-sh, #write-manifest, #write-obligations, #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="re-pin-and-receipt"><a class="header" href="#re-pin-and-receipt">re-pin-and-receipt</a></h3> <p>Re-pin <code>host</code> in agentic-host's <code>.host-software</code>, record the release receipt.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>software --check .</code> clean at the new pin</li> <li>depends: #host-repo-release</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">fen-acceptance</a></h3> <p>The real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> runs the one-liner end-to-end (or as close as the sandbox allows) and the harness-detection menu, confirming the UX conditionals hold at the weak-agent bar.</p> <ul> <li>verify: Fen routes the install flow and the harness selection correctly</li> <li>depends: #host-repo-release</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0071-fen-acceptance-installsh-output-read-by-the-real-qwen35-4b"><a class="header" href="#plan0071-fen-acceptance-installsh-output-read-by-the-real-qwen35-4b">plan/0071 fen-acceptance: install.sh output, read by the real qwen3.5-4b</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-28</li> <li>Model and parameters: as in <a href="plan/0071-host-install-mode/../0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/fen-acceptance.html">plan/0078</a>, the model card's thinking settings, two repeats per state.</li> <li>Protocol: every state was captured from a real run of the built <code>install.sh</code> inside the test suite's own sandbox, never hand-written. Between the rounds the only thing that changed was the message text; the probe framing is the earlier rounds' word for word. Probes and transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/install-mode/</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-this-round-had-to-decide"><a class="header" href="#what-this-round-had-to-decide">What this round had to decide</a></h2> <p>The README's UX conditionals were the part of this milestone that no survey could settle. gather-data grounded the mechanical choices in how the shipping installers behave and then said plainly that the UX half was <strong>not</strong> grounded, because probing it needs real script output rather than a mock. This is that probe.</p> <p>Three states were put in front of the model, each as the complete output of a run, with the exit code stated and one question: what is your single next action.</p> <h2 id="round-one"><a class="header" href="#round-one">Round one</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">no harness installed repeat 1: ACTION: Install opencode framework by running pip install opencode repeat 2: ACTION: cd agentic-acme several harnesses, no controlling terminal repeat 1: ACTION: cd agentic-acme repeat 2: ACTION: cd agentic-acme no name, and no controlling terminal to ask on repeat 1: ACTION: bash -s -- acme repeat 2: ACTION: ./install.sh acme </code></pre> <p><strong>The deferral held, 2 of 2.</strong> Told that several harnesses are installed and that it should start one itself, the model went to the project rather than picking one. That is the state where the script refuses to choose for the operator, and the refusal reads as intended.</p> <p><strong>Naming a harness without naming where to get it leaked, 1 of 2.</strong> The message said "Install one (opencode or claude, for example)". The model produced <code>pip install opencode</code>, which is not how opencode is distributed and does not exist. Nothing in the output suggested pip; the model filled a gap the message left open.</p> <p><strong>The missing-name remedy failed, 2 of 2.</strong> Neither answer was runnable. The message offered <code>for example | bash -s -- acme</code>, a fragment of a pipeline, and both repeats returned a fragment: one echoed it verbatim, the other invented a local <code>./install.sh</code> that a <code>curl | bash</code> run does not leave behind.</p> <p>The two failures are one failure. <strong>An instruction that names an outcome without naming the means leaves the means to be invented</strong>, and a four-billion-parameter model invents confidently. This is the finding <a href="plan/0071-host-install-mode/../../call/0049-the-unattended-charter.html">call/0049</a> recorded from the charter probe, arriving from the other direction: there it was a prohibition phrased against a method leaking, here it is an instruction omitting the method.</p> <h2 id="what-changed"><a class="header" href="#what-changed">What changed</a></h2> <p>Two messages, and nothing else. The harness line now names where each harness comes from, because a URL cannot be invented:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">Install an agent harness, then run it inside the project: opencode https://opencode.ai Claude Code https://claude.com/claude-code cd agentic-acme </code></pre> <p>The name remedy now quotes a whole command rather than the tail of one:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">install.sh: name required: pass one as an argument. Complete command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/host/main/install.sh | bash -s -- acme </code></pre> <h2 id="round-two"><a class="header" href="#round-two">Round two</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">no harness installed repeat 1: ACTION: cd agentic-acme repeat 2: ACTION: cd agentic-acme no name, and no controlling terminal to ask on repeat 1: ACTION: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/host/main/install.sh | bash -s -- acme repeat 2: ACTION: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/host/main/install.sh | bash -s -- acme </code></pre> <p>Both states now hold 2 of 2, and the missing-name repeats return the command byte for byte rather than a paraphrase of it. One thing changed between the rounds, which is the constraint this project's memory records after a probe that changed two things and measured neither.</p> <h2 id="what-this-did-not-test"><a class="header" href="#what-this-did-not-test">What this did not test</a></h2> <p>The menu. The branch that numbers several harnesses and reads a choice needs a controlling terminal, and the probe harness has none; what was measured is the no-terminal branch beside it, where the script declines to choose. Position bias in the numbered menu therefore remains unmeasured, and the ordering it would present is the star ordering from gather-data, which no probe here has exercised.</p> <p>Also untested: the install phase's own failure messages. The digest mismatch, the unsupported platform and the missing prerequisite were read by the integration suite for their exit codes, not by a weak agent for their legibility.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-installer-survey-and-harness-names"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-installer-survey-and-harness-names">gather-data: installer survey and harness names</a></h1> <p>Grounds every mechanical conditional in plan/0071's README in how the shipping majority actually do it. Each row traces a conditional in the README to its evidence here.</p> <h2 id="installer-survey"><a class="header" href="#installer-survey">Installer survey</a></h2> <p>Surveyed: <strong>rustup</strong> (<code>sh.rustup.rs</code>), <strong>opencode</strong> (<code>opencode.ai/install</code>), <strong>deno</strong> (<code>deno.land/install.sh</code>), <strong>bun</strong> (<code>bun.sh/install</code>). Fetched 2026-07-09.</p> <h3 id="platform-and-architecture-detection"><a class="header" href="#platform-and-architecture-detection">Platform and architecture detection</a></h3> <p>All four use <code>uname -s</code> (OS) and <code>uname -m</code> (CPU). The patterns:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Installer</th><th>Detection</th><th>Edge cases handled</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>rustup</td><td><code>uname -s</code> + <code>uname -m</code></td><td>Rosetta (x86_64 to arm64 via <code>sysctl</code>), ELF bitness (32-bit userland on 64-bit kernel), LoongArch UAPI, Android, illumos</td></tr> <tr><td>opencode</td><td><code>uname -s</code> + <code>uname -m</code></td><td>Rosetta, musl/Alpine, AVX2 baseline</td></tr> <tr><td>deno</td><td><code>uname -sm</code> combined</td><td>none beyond the combined check</td></tr> <tr><td>bun</td><td><code>uname -ms</code> combined</td><td>Rosetta, musl/Alpine, AVX2 baseline</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> <code>uname -s</code> + <code>uname -m</code> with Rosetta detection on Darwin (the minimum all four agree on). No ELF bitness, no AVX2 baseline, no LoongArch; our targets are darwin/linux/windows on amd64/arm64 only, which matches the 6 release assets host-lifecycle publishes.</p> <h3 id="hash-verification"><a class="header" href="#hash-verification">Hash verification</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Installer</th><th>SHA256 in script</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>rustup</td><td>no (delegates to binary)</td><td>the <code>rustup-init</code> binary does its own verification</td></tr> <tr><td>opencode</td><td>no</td><td>HTTPS-only trust</td></tr> <tr><td>deno</td><td>no</td><td>HTTPS-only trust</td></tr> <tr><td>bun</td><td>no</td><td>HTTPS-only trust</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><strong>The shipping majority do not verify hashes in the install script.</strong> They rely on HTTPS as the transport-layer trust root. Our install.sh strengthens beyond the majority by verifying SHA256 digests from the host-lifecycle release manifest. This is justified because: (1) host-lifecycle already publishes per-platform digests on the GitHub releases API, (2) we install multiple binaries and the all-or-nothing invariant requires confirming each landed correctly, (3) the reproducible-build anchor (plan/0032) makes the digest a meaningful identity check, not just a transport check.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> Verify SHA256 after download, before moving any binary to PATH. Grounded as a strengthening, not as following the majority.</p> <h3 id="manifest"><a class="header" href="#manifest">Manifest</a></h3> <p>None of the four uses a manifest. They download from URL patterns:</p> <ul> <li>rustup: <code>${ROOT}/dist/${arch}/rustup-init</code></li> <li>opencode: GitHub <code>releases/latest/download/${filename}</code>, version from API</li> <li>deno: <code>dl.deno.land/release/${version}/deno-${target}.zip</code>, version from <code>release-latest.txt</code></li> <li>bun: GitHub <code>releases/latest/download/bun-${target}.zip</code></li> </ul> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> We need a manifest because we coordinate binaries across multiple repos. The format is plain text, one line per binary <strong>per platform</strong>, because each platform variant has its own URL and its own digest: <code>binary <name> <version> <platform> <url> <sha256></code>, above a <code>template-revision</code> line. That is twelve lines for the install set settled in the release-asset survey below. Plain text is simpler than TOML or JSON and parses in pure bash with <code>while read</code>, so <code>install.sh</code> needs neither <code>jq</code> nor a TOML reader.</p> <h3 id="trust-root"><a class="header" href="#trust-root">Trust root</a></h3> <p>All four use HTTPS to their download origin. None uses GPG, cosign, or an external signer. rustup additionally enforces TLS 1.2+ and negotiates strong cipher suites (with graceful fallback for older curl/wget).</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> HTTPS to GitHub (<code>raw.githubusercontent.com</code> for the script, <code>api.github.com</code> for the manifest/digests, <code>github.com</code> for release assets). Enforce <code>curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2</code>. No GPG, no cosign (settled in plan/0065:234, the wrong layer for a reproducible-build project).</p> <h3 id="shell-configuration"><a class="header" href="#shell-configuration">Shell configuration</a></h3> <p>All four detect <code>$SHELL</code> and write export commands to the appropriate config file. The pattern is uniform:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Shell</th><th>Config file</th><th>Line written</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>zsh</td><td><code>~/.zshrc</code></td><td><code>export PATH=$DIR:$PATH</code></td></tr> <tr><td>bash</td><td><code>~/.bashrc</code> or <code>~/.bash_profile</code></td><td><code>export PATH=$DIR:$PATH</code></td></tr> <tr><td>fish</td><td><code>~/.config/fish/config.fish</code></td><td><code>fish_add_path $DIR</code></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>bun is the most thorough: it also checks <code>$XDG_CONFIG_HOME</code> variants and handles <code>.profile</code> fallback. opencode writes to <code>$GITHUB_PATH</code> in CI.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> Detect <code>$SHELL</code>, write the export to the appropriate config file. Support zsh/bash/fish/profile. Check <code>$XDG_CONFIG_HOME</code>. Write to <code>$GITHUB_PATH</code> in CI. All match the majority pattern.</p> <h3 id="install-location"><a class="header" href="#install-location">Install location</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Installer</th><th>Location</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>rustup</td><td><code>~/.cargo/bin</code> (via the binary)</td></tr> <tr><td>opencode</td><td><code>~/.opencode/bin</code></td></tr> <tr><td>deno</td><td><code>~/.deno/bin</code> (or <code>$DENO_INSTALL/bin</code>)</td></tr> <tr><td>bun</td><td><code>~/.bun/bin</code> (or <code>$BUN_INSTALL/bin</code>)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Pattern: <code>~/.<app>/bin</code>. Our install.sh uses <code>~/.local/bin</code> (XDG data dir for receipt, local bin for binaries) because the tools are shared across projects, not per-project.</p> <h3 id="receipt"><a class="header" href="#receipt">Receipt</a></h3> <p>None of the four writes a receipt. This is unique to our approach.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> Write <code>$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentic-<name>/install-receipt</code> (default <code>~/.local/share/agentic-<name>/install-receipt</code>). Justified by idempotency: the receipt records what landed, when, at what version, so re-running the script is deterministic (skip what's installed, install what's missing, fail if a hash diverged).</p> <h3 id="tty-handling-for-curl-pipe-bash"><a class="header" href="#tty-handling-for-curl-pipe-bash">TTY handling for curl-pipe-bash</a></h3> <p>rustup and deno both use <code>< /dev/tty</code> to read interactive input when the script is piped (stdin is owned by curl). This is the standard pattern.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> All interactive reads go through <code>< /dev/tty</code>. Grounded in the rustup and deno precedent.</p> <h3 id="shell-dialect"><a class="header" href="#shell-dialect">Shell dialect</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Installer</th><th>Dialect</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>rustup</td><td>POSIX <code>sh</code> (dash-compatible)</td><td>maximum portability</td></tr> <tr><td>opencode</td><td>bash (<code>set -euo pipefail</code>)</td><td>progress bar needs bash</td></tr> <tr><td>deno</td><td>POSIX <code>sh</code></td><td>maximum portability</td></tr> <tr><td>bun</td><td>bash (<code>set -euo pipefail</code>)</td><td>arrays for config-file list</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> bash with <code>set -euo pipefail</code>. The harness allowlist, menu logic, and string manipulation are cleaner in bash. We require <code>bash</code> explicitly in the shebang (<code>#!/usr/bin/env bash</code>). The opencode and bun precedent justifies this.</p> <p><strong>Critical constraint: macOS bash 3.2 compatibility.</strong> macOS ships bash 3.2.57 at <code>/bin/bash</code>, the last GPLv2 release. Apple froze it when bash 4.0 switched to GPLv3, and has never updated it. Every macOS user has bash 3.2 and only 3.2 unless they installed a newer one via Homebrew. Confirmed via Apple TN2065: <code>/bin/sh</code> on macOS is bash in POSIX mode. Since Catalina (10.15, 2019), zsh is the default interactive shell, but <code>/bin/bash</code> is present on every macOS release including current Tahoe (26) and Golden Gate (27 beta).</p> <p>This pins install.sh to <strong>bash 3.2-safe constructs only</strong>:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Safe in 3.2 (use these)</th><th>bash 4+ only (avoid these)</th><th>Replacement</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>set -euo pipefail</code></td><td><code>mapfile</code> / <code>readarray</code> (4.0)</td><td><code>while read -r line; do ...</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>[[ ]]</code> test</td><td><code>declare -A</code> assoc arrays (4.0)</td><td>parallel arrays + <code>case</code> dispatch</td></tr> <tr><td><code>read -rp</code></td><td><code>${var^^}</code> / <code>${var,,}</code> (4.0)</td><td><code>tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>${var//pattern/replacement}</code></td><td><code>|&</code> pipe shorthand (4.0)</td><td><code>2>&1 |</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>local</code> variables</td><td><code>coproc</code> (4.0)</td><td>named pipes or <code>&</code> + <code>wait</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>case</code> / <code>select</code></td><td><code>${var:i:n}</code> substring (4.2)</td><td><code>cut -c</code> or <code>expr substr</code></td></tr> <tr><td>arrays <code>arr=(a b c)</code> <code>${arr[@]}</code></td><td><code>${!name@}</code> indirect (4.3)</td><td><code>eval</code> or <code>case</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>printf '%s'</code></td><td><code>declare -g</code> (4.2)</td><td>avoid global declaration in functions</td></tr> <tr><td><code>< /dev/tty</code> redirect</td><td></td><td></td></tr> <tr><td><code>trap</code> / <code>exit</code> / <code>return</code></td><td></td><td></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The constructs we need (the state machine, harness allowlist, name validation, menu, SHA256 verification, manifest parsing) are all expressible in 3.2-safe bash: <code>case</code> dispatch, indexed arrays, <code>while read</code> loops, <code>[[ ]]</code> tests, and string operators. No associative arrays or <code>mapfile</code> required.</p> <h3 id="downloader"><a class="header" href="#downloader">Downloader</a></h3> <p>All four prefer curl, with wget as a fallback. rustup additionally detects the broken snap-curl and handles it.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> Prefer <code>curl</code>, fail with a clear message if neither curl nor wget is available (but do not implement wget fallback; curl is ubiquitous on the platforms we target, and the complexity is not justified for 6 platforms).</p> <h3 id="two-stage-vs-fat-script"><a class="header" href="#two-stage-vs-fat-script">Two-stage vs fat script</a></h3> <p>rustup is thin: the shell script detects platform, downloads the <code>rustup-init</code> binary, and execs it. The binary does the real work (installing toolchains, configuring PATH, etc.). The others are fat: the shell script does everything (download, extract, configure PATH, print success message).</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh:</strong> Fat script. We install multiple binaries (not one self-installing binary like rustup), and the scaffold step runs <code>host-lifecycle init</code> after the binaries are on PATH. The fat approach matches opencode, deno and bun.</p> <h2 id="release-asset-survey"><a class="header" href="#release-asset-survey">Release-asset survey</a></h2> <p>The README's install phase says "download each host-* binary", and its invariant says no project is scaffolded before "the full toolset is installed and verified". Neither names the set. <code>.host-software</code> carries six <code>deploy</code> lines, and reading the toolset as those six makes the invariant unsatisfiable on most platforms. Surveyed 2026-07-28 against the live releases:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Latest</th><th>Assets</th><th>Platform coverage</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>host-lifecycle</td><td>v0.47.0</td><td>6</td><td>complete: darwin, linux and windows on amd64 and arm64</td></tr> <tr><td>host-lint</td><td>v0.16.1</td><td>12</td><td>complete, plus six <code>host-lint-ffmpeg-*</code> pack assets</td></tr> <tr><td>host-reference</td><td>v0.1.6</td><td>5</td><td>windows-arm64 absent</td></tr> <tr><td>host-prove</td><td>v0.3.0</td><td>1</td><td><code>host-prove-linux-x86_64-musl</code> alone, under a different naming scheme</td></tr> <tr><td>host-reference-ocr</td><td>vendor-v1</td><td>1</td><td><code>vendor.tar.gz</code>; no binary published</td></tr> <tr><td>host-reference-openscad</td><td>vendor-v1</td><td>1</td><td><code>vendor.tar.gz</code>; no binary published</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Every asset in all six carries a <code>digest</code> field on the releases API (<code>sha256:...</code>), so the manifest's single source holds wherever a binary is published at all. The gap is coverage, not provenance.</p> <p><strong>Decision for install.sh: the install set is <code>host-lifecycle</code> and <code>host-lint</code>.</strong> These are the two with a complete platform matrix, so all-or-nothing is satisfiable on every target the script claims. They are also the two the entrance already asks for: <code>software/host/main</code>'s README names exactly this pair under <em>What you need</em>, and the bootstrap gate reports host-lint by name as the artifact whose absence blocks a clone. Nothing new has to be released for the install to work, which is the reason to prefer this reading over any other.</p> <p>What this excludes, and why it is not a deferral to fix later:</p> <ul> <li><code>host-prove</code> cannot enter a cross-platform install set today. It publishes a linux musl binary alone, so an all-or-nothing install including it would fail on every mac and every windows machine. Adding it means publishing five more assets from its release workflow.</li> <li><code>host-reference</code> is one asset short (windows-arm64). It is a near miss rather than a structural gap, and it is document tooling that a fresh agentic project does not need to scaffold.</li> <li><code>host-reference-ocr</code> and <code>host-reference-openscad</code> publish a vendor bundle and no binary, so there is nothing for a manifest to point at.</li> <li><code>host-lint</code>'s six <code>host-lint-ffmpeg-*</code> assets are the pack, not the core binary. The manifest names assets, never "every asset of the release", so the pack is out by construction and plan/0072 decides whether it is ever installed by default.</li> </ul> <p>This also fixes the <code>host-prove</code> naming assumption. The manifest records each asset's URL rather than deriving it from a platform template, so a component whose names do not follow <code><name>-<os>-<arch></code> costs nothing at parse time; only the platform gap keeps it out.</p> <h2 id="harness-name-survey"><a class="header" href="#harness-name-survey">Harness-name survey</a></h2> <p>The allowlist (6 harnesses, star-ordered) was confirmed during planning and re-verified here:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Binary</th><th>Harness</th><th>Stars</th><th>Confidence</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>1</td><td><code>opencode</code></td><td>opencode</td><td>184k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>2</td><td><code>claude</code></td><td>Claude Code</td><td>137k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>3</td><td><code>codex</code></td><td>Codex CLI</td><td>96.5k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>4</td><td><code>qwen</code></td><td>Qwen Code</td><td>25.9k</td><td>confirmed</td></tr> <tr><td>5</td><td><code>cursor-agent</code></td><td>Cursor Agent</td><td>unquantified</td><td>confirmed binary</td></tr> <tr><td>6</td><td><code>pi</code></td><td>Pi Agent</td><td>unquantified</td><td>confirmed binary</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Dropped: <code>zcode</code> (no CLI binary), <code>cheetahclaws</code> (entry point unconfirmed).</p> <p>The ordering is the star ordering. The menu shows names and numbers only, no star counts, no popularity labels. This keeps the menu clean and avoids implying a recommendation beyond ordering.</p> <p>No <code>HARNESS</code> environment variable: research confirmed no cross-vendor standard exists. Detection is via <code>command -v <binary></code>.</p> <h2 id="fen-probe"><a class="header" href="#fen-probe">Fen probe</a></h2> <p>The Fen probe (weak-model UX validation) runs at the <code>fen-acceptance</code> build step (the last task in the build sequence), where the real install.sh output is available to probe against. The probe validates:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Name prompt</strong>: does <code>(agentic-<name>)</code> produce <code>agentic-acme</code>, not <code>acme</code>?</li> <li><strong>No-harness message</strong>: does the print-and-exit read as actionable?</li> <li><strong>Ordered menu</strong>: does a weak agent read a numbered ordered menu (names only) without position bias?</li> <li><strong>Manifest trust</strong>: does the trust message read as trustworthy to a cold read?</li> </ol> <p>Deferred until fen-acceptance, because probing requires the actual script output, not a mock.</p> <h2 id="conditional-traceability"><a class="header" href="#conditional-traceability">Conditional traceability</a></h2> <p>Every conditional in the README traces to a gather-data row:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>README conditional</th><th>gather-data row</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Platform: <code>uname -s</code>/<code>uname -m</code> + Rosetta</td><td>Platform detection table</td></tr> <tr><td>SHA256 verification after download</td><td>Hash verification (strengthening)</td></tr> <tr><td>Manifest: plain text, one line per binary</td><td>Manifest (none use one; we need one)</td></tr> <tr><td>Trust root: HTTPS to GitHub</td><td>Trust root (all four use HTTPS)</td></tr> <tr><td>Shell config: zsh/bash/fish/profile</td><td>Shell configuration table</td></tr> <tr><td>Install location: <code>~/.local/bin</code></td><td>Install location (XDG vs <code>~/.<app>/bin</code>)</td></tr> <tr><td>Receipt: per-project XDG</td><td>Receipt (unique to us; justified by idempotency)</td></tr> <tr><td>TTY: <code>< /dev/tty</code> for interactive reads</td><td>TTY handling (rustup, deno precedent)</td></tr> <tr><td>Dialect: bash, <code>set -euo pipefail</code></td><td>Shell dialect (opencode, bun precedent)</td></tr> <tr><td>bash 3.2-safe constructs only</td><td>macOS ships 3.2.57 (last GPLv2; never updated)</td></tr> <tr><td>Downloader: curl, no wget fallback</td><td>Downloader (curl ubiquitous on 6 targets)</td></tr> <tr><td>Fat script, not two-stage</td><td>Two-stage vs fat (opencode/deno/bun precedent)</td></tr> <tr><td>Harness allowlist: 6 binaries, ordered</td><td>Harness-name survey table</td></tr> <tr><td>No <code>HARNESS</code> env var</td><td>Harness-name survey (no standard exists)</td></tr> <tr><td>Menu: names and numbers only</td><td>Harness-name survey (ordering without star counts)</td></tr> <tr><td>Install set: <code>host-lifecycle</code> and <code>host-lint</code></td><td>Release-asset survey (the two with a complete matrix)</td></tr> <tr><td>All-or-nothing over the install set</td><td>Release-asset survey (unsatisfiable over all six deploy lines)</td></tr> <tr><td>Manifest records a URL per asset, not a template</td><td>Release-asset survey (host-prove's naming diverges)</td></tr> <tr><td>Digests read from the releases API</td><td>Release-asset survey (every asset carries <code>digest</code>)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div><div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack-pack-dispatch-in-the-core-and-the-first-external-pack"><a class="header" href="#plan0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack-pack-dispatch-in-the-core-and-the-first-external-pack">plan/0072 ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack: pack dispatch in the core and the first external pack</a></h1> <p>This milestone delivers the FFmpeg commit-rule checker as host-lint's first external pack: a reserved <code>pack</code> dispatch verb in the core, a new <code>host-lint-ffmpeg</code> binary built on the <code>host_lint</code> library, and a rule registry that encodes every FFmpeg commit and patch rule with an honest enforcement tier. The consuming project is pgs-release (the FFmpeg subtitle upstreaming programme); the consuming milestone lives there, not here.</p> <p>The design record is <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/22">host-lint#22</a> (the opening design, the pgs9-review addendum, the consolidated revision that supersedes both, and the public-signals addendum of 2026-07-17), adversarially reviewed in <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/23">host-lint#23</a>.
