Every design-level finding of #23 is folded into #22's consolidated build sequence, task by task, with each task naming the findings it absorbs; the public-signals addendum then verified the design against the live upstream state and amended the sequence again (the review below). This README does not restate the rule tables or the finding bodies; the issues are the record, and RULES.md (the docs-and-release task) becomes the in-repo human form of the corpus. What lives here is the milestone: scope, the settled architecture, the open operator decisions, and the receipted task graph, which merges the consolidated revision and the public-signals deltas into one final sequence.</p> <h2 id="scope-1"><a class="header" href="#scope-1">Scope</a></h2> <p>Delivered by this milestone, all in the host-lint repository except the final re-pin:</p> <ul> <li>The core fix for the live defect #23 verified: an explicit nonexistent file argument exits 0 clean on v0.14.2 where the tool fails closed everywhere else.</li> <li>The reserved <code>pack</code> dispatch verb (<code>host-lint pack ffmpeg ...</code>), sibling to <code>lexicon</code> and <code>gather</code>, with a <code>packs</code> listing and a strict core/pack version handshake.</li> <li>The <code>host-lint-ffmpeg</code> pack: rule registry with completeness-as-a-test, message, diff, series, mail, and forge lanes, the cosmetic/functional classifier, receipted expensive legs, the checklist reporter, the project-pack config layer, and the hook installer.</li> <li>The security-path routing rules (exploitable issues route to ffmpeg-security, never to the public patch paths) and the mailing-list mechanics from the FAQ, MAINTAINERS, and fate.texi sources the public-signals review surfaced.</li> <li>Corpus calibration over accepted upstream history before any severity tier freezes.</li> <li>The network-having upstream-drift CI lane against every acknowledged source, ffmpeg.org and the FFmpeg/web-carried security page included.</li> <li>The pack's spec discipline at the repo bar (<code>ffmpeg-pack.allium</code>, obligations, Kani, proptest), RULES.md, and the release.</li> </ul> <p>Out of scope, recorded so the boundary is explicit:</p> <ul> <li>host-adoption: the pgs project pack TOML, <code>install-hooks</code> into the pgs FFmpeg worktrees, and the acceptance runs (the live pgs9 series, plus the frozen pgs8-wip series as a known-findings regression fixture whose recorded mechanical findings the pack must reproduce). That is a pgs-release milestone, cut there once the release exists.</li> <li>Full patcheck parity (typo lists, micro-optimization hints): deferred, and the registry marks those entries deferred rather than silently absent.</li> <li>FFmpeg's release-manager process and maintainer push-timing etiquette: excluded, and the completeness fixture carries the exclusions as explicit entries.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-settled-architecture"><a class="header" href="#the-settled-architecture">The settled architecture</a></h2> <p>The consolidated revision on #22 settled these after #23's review; they are constraints on every task below, not open questions:</p> <ul> <li>Dispatch is a reserved verb, never a bare name. A bare argument stays what it always was, a file path; <code>host-lint pack ffmpeg</code> dispatches while <code>host-lint ffmpeg</code> scans a file named <code>ffmpeg</code> (or fails closed when it is not scannable).</li> <li>The version handshake is strict: the pack refuses to run on a major or minor mismatch with the core, exit 2 with both versions named; the installer stamps and re-stamps core and pack together.</li> <li>Enforcement is three honest tiers: mechanical (the pack asserts it), expensive (a receipted re-derivable run; the cheap lane reports receipt presence and staleness, never a pass it did not run), attested (listed for the human, never auto-greened). This is the no-hollow-green rule (plan/0052) applied to a rule corpus.</li> <li>Severity tiers freeze only after calibration against accepted upstream history, and the registry records each mechanical rule's measured false-positive rate. Intuition proposes; measurement disposes.</li> <li>Completeness is a test, not a claim: a fixture enumerates every rule-bearing section of the pinned developer.texi (Coding Rules and Code behaviour included) and the test fails when any entry lacks a registry mapping. Source digests are scoped per rule-bearing section, so unrelated texi edits do not raise drift, and a separate network-having lane fails when ffmpeg.org drifts from what the corpus acknowledges.</li> <li>Nothing the pack needs is ever committed into the target FFmpeg clone; config resolves worktree-first (the worktree's private gitdir, then the git common dir, then defaults), so a submission-mode worktree and a wip-mode worktree coexist. Receipts live in the git common dir with an export form the consuming host can ledger.</li> <li>The project pack is data, not code: a TOML declaring branch grammar, tag grammar, and frozen-branch derivation, authored in the consuming host.</li> <li>The installed commit-msg hook chains the core <code>--stdin</code> naming scan with the pack msg lane and aggregates verdicts, so an agentic naming tell in a target-clone commit message is still caught.</li> <li>The corpus baseline is a genuine upstream master SHA. The revision the opening post recorded is a pgs-release fork commit, not an upstream one (the public-signals review's finding), so every drift claim keyed to it was unsound; the registry pins upstream and carries a corpus-freshness check at encode time.</li> <li>Submission is dual-path and the pack checks both: the mail lane covers the ffmpeg-devel path and the forge lane covers code.ffmpeg.org, whose landing mechanics (rebase and fast-forward only, per-commit messages landing verbatim) make the msg, diff, and series lanes apply to a pull request exactly as to a mailed series.</li> <li>AI-policy honesty: FFmpeg has no adopted AI/LLM contribution policy, so the pack encodes none. What it encodes instead is the operative text that does exist (the security page's automated-submissions ban, the optional Forgejo Fairy reviewer) and the community-enforced human-review norm as an attested leg grounded in the primary review record, never as an invented mechanical rule.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-public-signals-review-2026-07-17"><a class="header" href="#the-public-signals-review-2026-07-17">The public-signals review (2026-07-17)</a></h2> <p>Before this milestone was cut, a fanned-out research pass (four angles, adversarial primary-source verification of every load-bearing claim, a completeness critic, and a targeted second round) verified the design against the live upstream state. The full findings are the public-signals addendum on <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/22">host-lint#22</a>; the headlines:</p> <ul> <li>The corpus baseline was a fork SHA (the provenance defect above), and exactly five upstream developer.texi commits post-date the pinned content, three of them substantive rules the corpus lacked: narrow variable scope in loops (2026-04-22, advisory), bug fixes intended for backporting stay focused (2026-06-24), and the reviews-section rewrite adding the official optional Forgejo Fairy LLM reviewer (2026-07-13). The SI-units item became written rule text and promotes from attested to advisory. All five changes were live in the developer.html fetch the opening post records, so the misses were encoding gaps, not staleness: a second, independent argument for the completeness-as-a-test discipline.</li> <li>FFmpeg's LLM rules as they stand: no adopted policy (the July 2025 RFC remained discussion-only), per-maintainer discretion in practice, an official optional LLM reviewer on the forge path, a hard "Automated submissions are not accepted" plus named-human-reviewer requirement on the security path, and kernel-DCO sign-off semantics, so the responsible human signs off and certifies provenance of agent-drafted code. The January 2026 review of the AMD HIP-SDK pull request grounds the enforced human-review norm in primary quotes and names the concrete reviewer-recognized tells (end-user setup instructions in a commit message, a self-describing AVOption constant, duplicated documentation, untested configure targets).</li> <li>Four operative rule sources were never encoded: ffmpeg.org/security.html (three-way submission routing, the 10-item report contents), doc/mailing-list-faq.texi (per-message size cap, plain-text MIME, threading and etiquette mechanics, the DMARC bounce trap), MAINTAINERS (the CC routing rule and the parser realities), and doc/fate.texi (sample sequencing and immutability). The issue tracker also moved (Forgejo primary, Trac legacy), which changes the ticket-reference shapes.</li> <li>The Forgejo landing mechanics were established empirically from the live repo settings and observed merges (the API answers anonymous non-browser reads): no squash, no merge commits, verbatim per-commit landings, PR title as the relayed list subject, the PR description never entering history, and resubmission as force-push to the same PR.</li> </ul> <h2 id="open-decisions-for-the-operator"><a class="header" href="#open-decisions-for-the-operator">Open decisions for the operator</a></h2> <p>Five, carried from #22's consolidated revision. The build sequence proceeds on the recommendations until the operator rules otherwise; each ruling lands in the registry or config as data, not as a redesign.</p> <ol> <li>Pack residence. Recommended: the host-lint cargo workspace, extraction reconsidered when a second pack appears.</li> <li>The pgs branch grammar versus the live <code>-wip</code> branch name. The ruling belongs in a pgs-release decision record; the pack encodes whichever grammar is ruled.</li> <li>patcheck depth. Recommended: the correctness-adjacent subset; the rest deferred with deferred registry entries.</li> <li>Sign-off default. Recommended: <code>wip</code> mode default, <code>submission</code> mode set by hook config in pgs worktrees and by CI for series checks.</li> <li>The calibration threshold: the agreed false-positive rate above which a mechanical rule may not hold flag tier. This one has no recommendation; it is set when the calibration report exists.</li> </ol> <h2 id="issue-disposition"><a class="header" href="#issue-disposition">Issue disposition</a></h2> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/23">host-lint#23</a> stays open for the one live code defect and closes when the core-fix release ships. The fix travels first and does not wait on the pack build.</li> <li><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/22">host-lint#22</a> is the design record and closes when docs-and-release ships the pack.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-14"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-14">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The tasks are anchored receipted nodes (plan/0042), transplanted from #22's consolidated revision, merged with the public-signals deltas, and with the release seams made explicit for this host. Tasks with no stated dependency follow the previous task; stated dependencies override. Each pack task names the #23 findings it absorbs in the issue text; the verify lines here are the receipts' checks.</p> <h3 id="core-fail-closed-file-args"><a class="header" href="#core-fail-closed-file-args">core-fail-closed-file-args</a></h3> <p>An explicit file argument that is not a scannable file exits 2 with a diagnostic naming the path, in line with the tool's fail-closed pattern everywhere else.</p> <ul> <li>depends: none</li> <li>verify: regression test; <code>host-lint no-such-file.md</code> exits 2 and names the path</li> </ul> <h3 id="core-fix-release"><a class="header" href="#core-fix-release">core-fix-release</a></h3> <p>The live-defect fix ships as its own patch release ahead of the pack, so #23 does not wait on the pack build: <code>host-lifecycle release host-lint --change-class neither</code>, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the release receipt, close #23 with the release named.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #core-fail-closed-file-args</li> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> clean at the new pin; #23 closed</li> </ul> <h3 id="pack-dispatch"><a class="header" href="#pack-dispatch">pack-dispatch</a></h3> <p>The reserved <code>pack</code> verb: resolution beside the binary then on PATH, arg and exit-code passthrough, <code>packs</code> listing, strict version handshake with refusal on skew, exit 2 with an install hint when the pack is absent.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #core-fail-closed-file-args</li> <li>verify: stub-pack integration tests covering passthrough of each exit code, the collision case (a file named <code>ffmpeg</code> in cwd: <code>pack ffmpeg</code> dispatches, bare <code>ffmpeg</code> scans the file), skew refusal, and the missing-pack hint</li> </ul> <h3 id="engine-surface"><a class="header" href="#engine-surface">engine-surface</a></h3> <p>The reporting surface (<code>output_text</code>, <code>output_json</code>, <code>fix_hint</code>) moves from <code>main.rs</code> into the <code>host_lint</code> lib; the stable embedding surface is documented.</p> <ul> <li>depends: none</li> <li>verify: <code>cargo build</code> and <code>cargo test</code> green with <code>main.rs</code> consuming only the lib surface; host-lifecycle's embedding compiles unchanged</li> </ul> <h3 id="workspace-split"><a class="header" href="#workspace-split">workspace-split</a></h3> <p>The repository becomes a cargo workspace: the existing crate unchanged plus the <code>host-lint-ffmpeg</code> bin crate; release assets per platform; <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> regenerated.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #engine-surface</li> <li>verify: <code>cargo build --workspace --release</code> offline from the vendored bundle; both binaries produced on all release targets in CI</li> </ul> <h3 id="fixture-licensing"><a class="header" href="#fixture-licensing">fixture-licensing</a></h3> <p>The licensing policy decided before any fixture lands: synthesized fixtures by default; a real upstream excerpt only where synthesis cannot reproduce the case, isolated with explicit provenance and licensing notes.</p> <ul> <li>depends: none</li> <li>verify: the fixtures directory ships its provenance README; a CI check requires it wherever real excerpts sit</li> </ul> <h3 id="rule-registry"><a class="header" href="#rule-registry">rule-registry</a></h3> <p>The encoded corpus, widened per #23 and re-grounded per the public-signals review: the baseline re-pins to a genuine upstream master SHA with a corpus-freshness check at encode time; the five-commit developer.texi drift set is absorbed (narrow-scope, backport-minimal, SI-units promotion, reviews/Fairy, tracker transition); the source set widens to security.html (pinned by FFmpeg/web commit plus fetch date, since no SECURITY file exists in the FFmpeg tree), mailing-list-faq.texi, MAINTAINERS (snapshot pinned by SHA plus content hash), and fate.texi; every rule-bearing chapter sits in the completeness fixture; a measured-rate field per mechanical rule (empty until calibration); per-section source digests. <code>rules</code>, <code>rules --json</code>, and <code>rules --verify-source <tree></code>.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #workspace-split</li> <li>verify: the completeness test fails when any rule-bearing chapter entry lacks a registry mapping; a doctored section raises drift while an edit elsewhere does not; the freshness check fails on a pin older than the newest developer.texi commit</li> </ul> <h3 id="msg-lane"><a class="header" href="#msg-lane">msg-lane</a></h3> <p>The message checks corrected against measured ground truth: the widened area grammar, the <code>Revert</code>/<code>fixup!</code>/<code>squash!</code> exemptions, the enumerated exact-string vague list, ascii-clean, mode-aware sign-off, no-end-user-setup-instructions (commit bodies are why-and-what, never install walkthroughs; grounded in the January 2026 review record), and ticket-ref accepting Forgejo issue references alongside legacy Trac shapes and CVE ids now that the primary tracker moved.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #rule-registry</li> <li>verify: the measured ground-truth subjects from #23 join the fixtures as a must-pass corpus; synthetic violations fire each rule exactly once; proptest over the grammar</li> </ul> <h3 id="diff-lane"><a class="header" href="#diff-lane">diff-lane</a></h3> <p>The added-line checks with scope drawn precisely: the full Makefile-class and golden-output whitespace exemptions, library-trees-only naming scope, the lexical VLA rule retired in favour of a <code>-Wvla</code> build leg, ascii-comments, the api-misuse patcheck subset, the narrow-variable-scope advisory heuristic (a loop counter declared immediately before the for loop that uses it), and the self-describing AVOption constant heuristic (name equals value, the reviewer-named tell).</p> <ul> <li>depends: #rule-registry, #fixture-licensing</li> <li>verify: per-rule positive and negative fixtures, with a <code>*.mak</code> tab, a <code>tests/ref</code> golden file, and an fftools identifier all passing; patcheck parity cases</li> </ul> <h3 id="cosmetic-separation"><a class="header" href="#cosmetic-separation">cosmetic-separation</a></h3> <p>The mixed cosmetic/functional classifier, fully specified: <code>diff -w -b</code> per git-howto, blank-line handling defined, the brace allowance and the 2026-03-25 whitespace-only relaxation encoded as fixtures.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #diff-lane</li> <li>verify: six fixture commits (mixed flags; pure re-indent, pure functional, brace allowance, whitespace-only relaxation, and blank-line-only all pass)</li> </ul> <h3 id="corpus-calibration"><a class="header" href="#corpus-calibration">corpus-calibration</a></h3> <p>The tier freeze: every mechanical rule runs over several thousand recent accepted upstream commits; a rule flagging above the agreed rate is demoted or refined; the registry's measured-rate fields are populated. Tiers freeze here and nowhere earlier.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #msg-lane, #diff-lane</li> <li>verify: the calibration report is committed beside the registry; a gate test asserts no flag-tier mechanical rule exceeds the agreed rate on the calibration corpus</li> </ul> <h3 id="series-lane"><a class="header" href="#series-lane">series-lane</a></h3> <p>The per-commit walk and series-order checks, corrected and widened: the generated-header allowlist and dual-root include resolution, provider-before-consumer extended to Makefile object references, registration triggers over every table (filters and bitstream filters included), the version-bump check reading the split version headers and Makefile HEADERS variables, plus alphabetical-order, maintainers-coverage, checkasm-obligation, gpl-gating, doc-updated, and shared-abi with its false-positive mode documented. The public-signals additions land here too: the backport-fix focus warn (a ticket- or CVE-referencing fix carrying hunks the fix does not need warns to split), the fate-sample checks (a FATE test referencing a sample absent from fate-suite requires a samples-request note, an existing fate-suite path is never repurposed, sample minimality attested), and the security three-way routing classifier (exploitable to ffmpeg-security, non-exploitable UB or leak to a Forgejo PR, everything else the normal path).</p> <ul> <li>depends: #cosmetic-separation, #corpus-calibration</li> <li>verify: the synthetic-repo suite extends per rule; a series including <code>config_components.h</code> passes; a Makefile object reference ahead of its source flags; a filter registration with no Changelog, doc, or MAINTAINERS hunk fires each obligation; an avpriv move without a minor bump flags; a crash-fix commit with a new fate sample and no samples-request note fires both the routing note and the sample check</li> </ul> <h3 id="build-receipts"><a class="header" href="#build-receipts">build-receipts</a></h3> <p>The expensive lane with home and legs settled: per-commit compile, <code>--enable-shared</code>, <code>-Wvla</code>, standalone-compile, <code>--disable-x86asm</code> when assembly is added, an out-of-tree configure-and-make leg when the series touches Makefiles or ffbuild (a reviewer-enforced expectation from the January 2026 record), optional FATE. Receipts in the git common dir with the export form, carrying base and head SHAs, toolchain identity, config digest, and the legs run; missing receipt notes, stale receipt warns (exit 3), an unrun leg renders unrun, never passed.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #series-lane</li> <li>verify: toy-repo run producing a receipt with legs recorded; a rewritten head reads stale (warn); a missing leg renders unrun; the export form round-trips</li> </ul> <h3 id="mail-lane"><a class="header" href="#mail-lane">mail-lane</a></h3> <p>The format-patch directory checks, widened by the mailing-list-faq and MAINTAINERS sources: parseability, subject-prefix coherence, cover-letter warn, the per-message 1000 kB flag (oversize mail stalls silently in an unwatched moderation queue), plain-text MIME, the 70-character prose-wrap advisory (composed prose only, never the diff payload), the uncompressed-attachment advisory, single-list To/Cc addressing, the thread-targeting check (an <code>--in-reply-to</code> target must belong to the same series' prior-version thread), maintainer-cc (a CC-marked MAINTAINERS entry matching a touched path must appear in the Cc list, with the section-scoped glob matcher and all three observed CC syntaxes), the DMARC pre-send warn (a From: domain publishing reject or quarantine bounces off ffmpeg-devel), and patchwork post-send verification (the series appears, prior versions marked superseded). Attested: the subscription precondition and interleaved-reply style.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #msg-lane</li> <li>verify: fixtures generated by <code>git format-patch</code>, with a broken numbering case, a missing cover letter case, an oversize-mail case, an HTML-only case, a wrong-list case, a hijacked-thread case, and a missing-CC case among them; the MAINTAINERS parser passes the live-syntax fixture set (three CC forms, the non-CC parenthesized address, the section-scoped duplicate globs)</li> </ul> <h3 id="forge-lane"><a class="header" href="#forge-lane">forge-lane</a></h3> <p>The code.ffmpeg.org path checks, empirically grounded in the live repo settings and observed landings and re-checkable via the anonymous API: the PR title satisfies the area-prefix subject grammar (it becomes the relayed list subject), <code>WIP:</code> as the draft marker, the description-as-cover-letter advisory plus the rationale-lands-in-commits check (the description never enters git history), and force-push resubmit discipline (same PR per revision, no [PATCH vN] title, a delta comment on each push). The msg, diff, and series lanes already apply per commit since landings are rebase or fast-forward with verbatim messages; this lane adds only the forge-specific surface.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #msg-lane</li> <li>verify: fixture PR metadata cases (a bare-branch-name title flags, an area-prefixed title passes, a WIP title notes, a versioned title flags); the empirical-grounding note names the API endpoints a re-check reads</li> </ul> <h3 id="checklist-reporter"><a class="header" href="#checklist-reporter">checklist-reporter</a></h3> <p><code>checklist</code> renders the full registry over a series: mechanical results from the lanes, expensive results from receipts, the widened attested set listed with citations, measured rates alongside each mechanical result, the tier boundary visible (checked, receipted, attested). The attested set gains the human-review leg (grounded in the January 2026 primary quotes and enumerating the reviewer-named tells), the post-land fate.ffmpeg.org monitoring leg, and the security-path attested items (named human reviewer, finder credit, reproducible-with-existing-applications).</p> <ul> <li>depends: #series-lane, #build-receipts</li> <li>verify: golden-output test; a grep asserts no attested item ever renders as checked and no unrun leg renders as passed</li> </ul> <h3 id="project-pack-config"><a class="header" href="#project-pack-config">project-pack-config</a></h3> <p>The config layer with worktree-first resolution: TOML schema (upstream ref, mode, branch grammar, tag grammar, frozen derivation from history tags), the loader, a documented example, and the branch and tag checks.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #rule-registry</li> <li>verify: precedence tests including a two-worktree clone holding different modes; branch, tag, and frozen-branch checks against a synthetic repo with history tags</li> </ul> <h3 id="hook-installer"><a class="header" href="#hook-installer">hook-installer</a></h3> <p><code>install-hooks</code> lands hooks per worktree with config in the worktree's private gitdir; the installed commit-msg hook runs the core <code>--stdin</code> scan and the pack msg lane with aggregated verdicts; core and pack versions stamped together, a skewed pair refused; nothing tracked or untracked lands in the target tree.</p> <ul> <li>depends: #msg-lane, #diff-lane, #project-pack-config</li> <li>verify: a two-worktree install with differing modes; a phase-tell commit message in the target clone is blocked by the chained core scan; a staged tab is blocked; the skew case refuses; <code>git status</code> in the target shows nothing new</li> </ul> <h3 id="upstream-drift-lane"><a class="header" href="#upstream-drift-lane">upstream-drift-lane</a></h3> <p>The network-having CI lane, watching every acknowledged source: developer.html and git-howto as designed, plus security.html (keyed to FFmpeg/web commits, since the page changed five times in 2026 alone), mailing-list-faq.html, the MAINTAINERS snapshot, and fate.texi. Normalize, compare each rule-bearing section against the digest the corpus acknowledges, fail on unacknowledged drift; drift audits use a recursive tree diff, never a flat listing or a capped compare API. The tier rule: if two competent runs must agree, it is a tool (mechanical or expensive); if they may reasonably differ, it is <code>delegated</code> — a new tier: a model call with a rubric, a structured verdict, a receipt, advisory-only, unrun never passed; if it certifies responsibility, it is human-attested — a model may assist, never discharge.</p> <ul> <li>The tier enum becomes <code>mechanical | expensive | delegated | attested</code>. Harness seams: <code>claude -p --output-format json --json-schema <schema></code> and <code>opencode run -m <provider/model> --format json --agent <name></code>; both verified on the originating dev host — re-verify availability on a new host. plan-doc commits push immediately; MEMORY.md entries are separate commits.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="angle-ffmpeg-ai-policy"><a class="header" href="#angle-ffmpeg-ai-policy">ANGLE: ffmpeg-ai-policy</a></h1> <p>SUMMARY: Searched ffmpeg.org developer docs (developer.html live 2026-07-17; doc/developer.texi at master via GitHub mirror and at the corpus-pinned rev a7ffc46c), the ffmpeg-devel archives (pipermail and mail-archive.com, 2025-2026), FFmpeg community/governance page, the FFmpeg/FFmpeg commit history for doc/developer.texi, and 2026 press coverage of the AMD incident. Headline state as of 2026-07-17: FFmpeg has NO adopted AI/LLM contribution policy — no ban, no disclosure requirement, no GA vote or TC decision. A July 2025 RFC ("[RFC] Introducing policies regarding 'AI' contributions", Alexander Strasser, 2025-07-01) proposed creating one and produced disclosure/responsibility proposals (all PROPOSED, none adopted). The operative regime is per-maintainer discretion under ordinary review standards, enforced in practice: a Feb 2026 AMD patch was publicly rejected as unreviewed "AI slop", with the demand of "thorough manual review of all AI-generated code before submission". Sign-off carries Linux-kernel DCO semantics (the checklist links kernel submitting-patches.rst "Sign your work"), so a human submitter certifies origin of agent-drafted code; one core maintainer (Rémi Denis-Courmont, 2025-11-11) has argued DNN-generated patches are LGPL-incompatible, contested by Niedermayer and not policy. Limitation: code.ffmpeg.org pages (Forgejo_Fairy profile, michaelni/Fairies repo) are Anubis-bot-blocked and could not be fetched; no evidence anywhere suggests a policy is hosted there. But the sweep treated developer.texi + developer.html + git-howto + patcheck as the whole rule universe and only byte-diffed the sibling docs without encoding them. Four official, currently-operative rule sources were never read for content, and each contains submitter-facing rules the corpus lacks: (1) ffmpeg.org/security.html — fetched live today, it routes exploitable bugs to ffmpeg-security@ffmpeg.org, requires "Name(s) or alias(es) of the human reviewer(s) who verified the report", and states "Automated submissions are not accepted"; this is operative AI-relevant text that directly qualifies the ai-policy agent's headline claim that the Fairy sentence is FFmpeg's only AI-related official text, and it changes submission routing for the crash/overflow fixes a subtitle-decoder programme will plausibly produce. (2) doc/mailing-list-faq.texi — verified byte-identical by the drift agent but never encoded; it imposes mechanical mail-lane constraints (1000 kB message cap with moderation hold, no HTML-only mail, no top-posting, ~70-char client line wrap, uncompressed attachments, no cross-posting). (3) MAINTAINERS — read only for the Trac [X] flag; its header defines an operative routing rule ("A (CC <address>) after the name means that the maintainer prefers to be CC-ed on patches") and names the subtitle-area maintainers pgs-release will interact with (pgssubdec.c: Reimar Doeffinger; text subtitles: Clément Bœsch). (4) doc/fate.texi — imposes sample-handling obligations (samples-request channel, never replace/remove existing samples, samples uploaded ~24h before push, monitor fate.ffmpeg.org after landing) that refine the corpus's fate-obligation and sample-provenance legs. Two claims were repeated without primary grounding: Forgejo PR merge/versioning mechanics (whether commit messages land verbatim and how vN resubmission works — this decides whether the msg/series lanes fully apply on the Forgejo path; a 30-commit GitHub-API sample today shows all-linear single-parent history with no Reviewed-on trailers, but no one confirmed a PR-origin commit), and the Feb-2026 AMD enforcement precedent, which every agent cites from press coverage only while the pack is about to derive an attested rule from it. Trac wiki, FOSDEM talks, and social accounts were also unswept but are unlikely to change the pack (Trac is legacy; the X post is part of the AMD story). Not complete: six gaps.</p> <p>GAP: The security submission path is a missed modality with operative, AI-relevant text: ffmpeg.org/security.html (live 2026-07-17) routes exploitable bugs to ffmpeg-security@ffmpeg.org, requires named human reviewers ('Name(s) or alias(es) of the human reviewer(s) who verified the report'), states 'Automated submissions are not accepted', directs non-exploitable UB/leak fixes to a Forgejo PR instead, and gives ffmpeg-cve@ffmpeg.org for CVE-ID additions. This changes how an agent-drafted crash/overflow fix in a subtitle decoder may be submitted, and it contradicts the ai-policy agent's claim that the Forgejo Fairy sentence is the only AI-relevant official text. close: Fetch https://ffmpeg.org/security.html and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/SECURITY.md (if present), plus the ffmpeg-web repo commit history for security.html to date the automated-submissions ban. Encode a series-lane routing rule: a commit fixing an exploitable issue must not go to ffmpeg-devel/Forgejo as an ordinary patch — it goes to ffmpeg-security@ffmpeg.org with a named human reviewer, reproducible test case, stack trace, and commit hash; non-exploitable UB/leak fixes go to a Forgejo PR; CVE-ID contributions go to ffmpeg-cve@ffmpeg.org.</p> <p>GAP: doc/mailing-list-faq.texi was byte-diffed for drift but never encoded as a rule source; it imposes mechanical mail-lane constraints absent from the corpus: 1000 kB message size limit (oversize mail is held for moderation), no HTML-only messages, avoid top-posting (trimmed interleaved replies), configure the mail client to wrap at ~70 chars, do not compress small attachments, do not cross-post to multiple lists. close: Fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/doc/mailing-list-faq.texi and https://ffmpeg.org/mailing-list-faq.html, extract every operative sentence, and add mail-lane checks: total generated mail size < 1000 kB (else split the series or link samples), plain-text MIME only, uncompressed attachments, ~70-char reply wrapping, and interleaved-reply style on vN resubmission threads.</p> <p>GAP: The MAINTAINERS file was read only for the Trac [X] flag, not as a rule source. Its header defines an operative submitter-facing routing rule — '(CC <address>) after the name means that the maintainer prefers to be CC-ed on patches and related discussions' — and it names the maintainers pgs-release's series will touch (pgssubdec.c: Reimar Doeffinger; text subtitles in lavc/lavf: Clément Bœsch; srt/ass/microdvd: Aurelien Jacobs). No corpus rule CCs path-matched maintainers. close: Fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/MAINTAINERS, parse entries whose file globs match paths touched by the series, and add a mail-lane check: any matched entry carrying a '(CC <address>)' marker must appear in the outgoing Cc list; record the subtitle-area maintainer set and each entry's activity flag ([X]/[0]/[1]/[2]) in the pack's project config for pgs-release.</p> <p>GAP: Forgejo PR landing mechanics are ungrounded: no agent established the merge style (rebase/fast-forward vs merge vs squash), whether per-commit messages land on master verbatim (which decides whether the msg and series lanes fully apply on the Forgejo path), where cover-letter content goes (PR description is lost or kept?), or how vN resubmission is expressed (force-push to the same PR vs a new PR, and whether [PATCH vN] numbering has a Forgejo analog). A 30-commit sample of master via api.github.com today is all single-parent with no Reviewed-on trailers — consistent with rebase landing — but no commit was traced to a PR origin. close: With an authenticated code.ffmpeg.org session or API token (Anubis blocks anonymous access, including /api/v1), fetch a recently merged PR via /api/v1/repos/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls?state=closed and its commits; alternatively, pick a relayed '[PR] <title> (PR #NNNNN)' subject from https://www.mail-archive.com/ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org/ whose PR is now merged and locate the resulting commits on master via https://api.github.com/repos/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commits?path=<file>. Record: merge style, verbatim-message preservation, cover-letter fate, and the resubmission convention; then scope the msg/mail lanes accordingly (e.g. PR title = subject grammar, PR description = cover letter, force-push = vN).</p> <p>GAP: The Feb-2026 AMD 'AI slop' enforcement precedent — the basis for the pack's proposed attested human-review leg — is grounded only in secondary press (videocardz.com, opensourceforu.com, HN); no agent fetched the primary ffmpeg-devel thread or Forgejo PR. Press accounts add a concrete msg-lane detail nobody encoded: reviewers objected to end-user setup instructions (pacman steps) stuffed into the commit message, and the submitter denied AI use — so the operative objections (verbatim reviewer quotes, which tells were named) are unverified. close: Search https://www.mail-archive.com/ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org/ and https://ffmpeg.org/pipermail/ffmpeg-devel/2026-February/ for the AMD HIP SDK on Windows thread (author from amd.com, reviewer Zhao Zhili); fetch the actual review messages, quote the exact objections, and use them to (a) ground the attested line-by-line human-review leg in primary text and (b) add a msg-lane check that commit bodies contain no end-user setup/install instructions (why-and-what only).</p> <p>GAP: doc/fate.texi and fate.ffmpeg.org were never read; fate.texi imposes sample obligations that refine the corpus's fate-obligation and sample-provenance legs: new samples are requested via a mail to samples-request, existing fate-suite files must never be replaced/removed/overwritten, all samples needed by a commit should be uploaded ~24h before push, and contributors are expected to monitor fate.ffmpeg.org after landing for cross-platform breakage. page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0072-source-pins-the-upstream-corpus-the-registry-encodes"><a class="header" href="#plan0072-source-pins-the-upstream-corpus-the-registry-encodes">plan/0072 source pins: the upstream corpus the registry encodes</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-28</li> <li>Fetched over HTTPS from <code>raw.githubusercontent.com</code> at the FFmpeg master commit below, and digested on arrival.</li> </ul> <p>The <code>#rule-registry</code> node requires the encoded corpus to be pinned to a genuine upstream master SHA with per-section digests, so that drift in a rule-bearing section is detectable and an edit elsewhere is not. This file records the pins that fetch produced, so the work begins from verified bytes rather than from a second fetch that may differ.</p> <h2 id="the-commit"><a class="header" href="#the-commit">The commit</a></h2> <pre><code>FFmpeg/FFmpeg master c6309b5c63add7ad0ec221fafefc32bdcd6f8b91 </code></pre> <h2 id="the-files-and-what-each-is-for"><a class="header" href="#the-files-and-what-each-is-for">The files, and what each is for</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Upstream path</th><th>sha256</th><th>Bytes</th><th>Why the registry needs it</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>doc/developer.texi</code></td><td><code>26549522babfb7af744059d68077440064de6693ee6ff8c41b53ea3c36534e4c</code></td><td>45328</td><td>The commit and patch rules themselves</td></tr> <tr><td><code>doc/mailing-list-faq.texi</code></td><td><code>7ba38b8b16e6b94d6054d64da6dfa17738c874b693d85fe8ee9f62b36b7ac0f6</code></td><td>13148</td><td>The mailing-list mechanics the mail lane checks</td></tr> <tr><td><code>MAINTAINERS</code></td><td><code>55e05c3c17d7909886cbdd563154ff2d7a43bc5d0866bddb63df2adbc5aa0f58</code></td><td>31632</td><td>Area ownership, for the area-prefix and routing rules</td></tr> <tr><td><code>doc/fate.texi</code></td><td><code>07b49cf2c33b20d04b828166ce569f6d7d57e4b2791b113bcd6b134e7960ecba</code></td><td>9855</td><td>The FATE obligations the testing rules refer to</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Not yet fetched: <code>security.html</code> from the <code>FFmpeg/web</code> repository, which the node pins by that repository's commit plus a fetch date because no <code>SECURITY</code> file exists in the FFmpeg tree. It is the source for the security-path routing rules, and it is the one source whose pin is a fetch rather than a tree path.</p> <h2 id="what-the-structure-looks-like"><a class="header" href="#what-the-structure-looks-like">What the structure looks like</a></h2> <p><code>doc/developer.texi</code> carries 35 headings at chapter, section and subsection level. The rule-bearing density is not uniform: <code>Patches/Committing</code> alone carries ten <code>@subheading</code> rules, and they are the ones the message and diff lanes turn on.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">Licenses for patches must be compatible with FFmpeg. You must not commit code which breaks FFmpeg! Commit messages Testing must be adequate but not excessive. Do not commit unrelated changes together. Bug fixes intended for backporting should stay focused. Cosmetic changes should be kept in separate patches. Credit the author of the patch. Credit any researchers Always wait long enough before pushing changes </code></pre> <p>The commit-message format the message lane encodes is stated in that section verbatim:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">area changed: short 1 line description details describing what and why and giving references. </code></pre> <p>Three of those subheadings are the ones the milestone's harder nodes exist for, and reading them together is what shows why. "Do not commit unrelated changes together" and "Cosmetic changes should be kept in separate patches" are the pair the <code>#cosmetic-separation</code> classifier has to tell apart, and "Bug fixes intended for backporting should stay focused" is a third scope rule that overlaps both without being either. A registry that flattened them into one "keep patches focused" entry would lose exactly the distinction the lane is being built to make.</p> <h2 id="what-this-record-does-not-settle"><a class="header" href="#what-this-record-does-not-settle">What this record does not settle</a></h2> <p>The enforcement tier per rule. A tier is a claim about how reliably a rule can be detected mechanically, and the <code>#corpus-calibration</code> node measures that against accepted upstream history before any tier freezes. The <code>measured-rate</code> field stays empty until then, which is the design's own sequencing and not an omission here.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0073-host-lifecycle-dream-own-the-per-user-memory-store-then-audit-it"><a class="header" href="#plan0073-host-lifecycle-dream-own-the-per-user-memory-store-then-audit-it">plan/0073 host-lifecycle-dream: own the per-user memory store, then audit it</a></h1> <p>Closes <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/16">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#16</a>.</p> <h2 id="why-10"><a class="header" href="#why-10">Why</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle validate</code> checks room structure and naming; it has no notion of memory-content staleness. A recalled memory that a later decision silently superseded is invisible until an agent anchors on it. The motivating failure (in the issue) was exactly that: a session anchored a megakernel base on a recalled note that was a one-day-later <em>workaround</em> description, and missed the standing operator decision that locked the base to F16-ssm_out.</p> <p>The original plan was to audit each vendor's per-user memory store. The gather-data survey (2026-07-19) showed that path is not worth it: the closed harnesses are encrypting their stores, opencode has no native store at all, and fighting encryption is a moving target with no durable win. The clean play is to <strong>own the store</strong>: ship an optional opencode plugin that implements the host-* per-user store format, and let <code>dream</code> audit <em>that</em>. Vendor stores become explicitly out of scope.</p> <h2 id="scope-2"><a class="header" href="#scope-2">Scope</a></h2> <p>Three deliverables, in one milestone:</p> <ol> <li><em><em>The host-</em> per-user memory store</em>* (the format and the storage layer). A markdown-per-entry store at <code>~/.host-memory/<project>/</code>, with a <code>MEMORY.md</code> index, <code>description:</code> + free-form body per entry, and <code>[[slug]]</code> cross-entry links. The format is the methodology's own, named in the spine.</li> <li><strong>Memory tools added to the existing <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> server</strong> (shipped in v0.39.0 per plan/0065 with <code>init</code> and <code>adopt</code>). The plan/0073 work adds <code>memory_list</code> / <code>memory_read</code> / <code>memory_write</code> / <code>memory_consolidate</code> to that server. The reference implementation of the format; the plugin opencode already loads gains a per-user memory tier alongside the onboarding tools.</li> <li><strong><code>host-lifecycle dream <dir></code></strong>: the advisory, read-mostly audit over both stores (the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> and the host-* per-user store), flagging staleness, contradictions, drift, and append-only violations. Read-only by default; emits findings, never auto-rewrites.</li> </ol> <h3 id="operator-rulings-2026-07-19"><a class="header" href="#operator-rulings-2026-07-19">Operator rulings (2026-07-19)</a></h3> <ol> <li><strong>Own the store; do not read vendor stores.</strong> The closed harnesses encrypt their stores; opencode has none. We ship an optional opencode plugin that implements the host-* format. Other harnesses are out of scope; an operator on a closed harness uses only the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> tier.</li> <li><strong>Both stores audited.</strong> The repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> (append-only) and the host-* per-user store (editable) are both in <code>dream</code>'s scope. The asymmetry is encoded in what <code>dream</code> suggests: an <em>append</em> for repo-store findings, an in-place edit suggestion for editable-store findings.</li> <li><strong>Memory tools added to the existing <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> (stdio), not a new server.</strong> Plan/0065 shipped <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> (v0.39.0) with <code>init</code> and <code>adopt</code>. plan/0073 extends that server with <code>memory_list</code> / <code>memory_read</code> / <code>memory_write</code> / <code>memory_consolidate</code>. Same stdio JSON-RPC pattern; one server, two concerns (onboarding + memory), each tool independently invocable. Matches the existing opencode MCP config (pal is configured the same way); portable to any harness that speaks MCP.</li> <li><strong>One plan, not split.</strong> Doctrine + plugin + dream ship together. The plugin and the audit co-evolve against the same format.</li> <li><strong>Full methodology.</strong> Gather-data (done), cast consultation, adversarial review, then build.</li> </ol> <h3 id="what-is-descoped-explicitly"><a class="header" href="#what-is-descoped-explicitly">What is descoped (explicitly)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Reading any closed/encrypted vendor memory store (Codex, Cursor, Pi, etc.). Closed harnesses get the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> tier only.</li> <li>Reading Claude's or Qwen's native store, even though both are plain markdown. Convergent formats are noted empirically in the survey; nothing is adopted from them. The host-* store is its own thing.</li> <li>Auto-detecting which harness is running. <code>dream</code> reads <code>~/.host-memory/</code> regardless of harness; an operator who installed the plugin gets audited, an operator who did not gets only the repo-store findings.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-two-store-asymmetry-load-bearing"><a class="header" href="#the-two-store-asymmetry-load-bearing">The two-store asymmetry (load-bearing)</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>Repo <code>MEMORY.md</code></strong>: append-only (CLAUDE.md §6). <code>dream</code>: <ul> <li>never proposes an in-place edit;</li> <li>suggests an <em>append</em> with the correction text and a forward <code>[[link]]</code> from the superseded entry;</li> <li><strong>detects</strong> any edit to an existing entry as an append-only violation (the one and only sanctioned §6 escape is the archive-first map-only rename; every other in-place edit is a violation).</li> </ul> </li> <li><em><em>Host-</em> per-user store</em>* (editable). <code>dream</code>: <ul> <li>may propose in-place rewrites, prunes, relinks;</li> <li>reconciles the index one-liner with the corrected entry <code>description</code>;</li> <li>keeps durable measured lore even inside a stale entry (mark the state superseded, do not delete the facts).</li> </ul> </li> </ol> <h2 id="detectors-candidate-dream-checks"><a class="header" href="#detectors-candidate-dream-checks">Detectors (candidate <code>dream</code> checks)</a></h2> <p>Each is grounded in a real failure mode observed in the motivating run. The gather-data Fen probe (2026-07-19) showed the simpler detectors read clearly at the weak-agent bar and the methodology-discipline ones do not; the build does not start until the detector naming is sharpened (three options recorded in <code>gather-data.md</code>: rename, lean on routing, or accept partial coverage at the 4B bar).</p> <ul> <li><strong>description-vs-body drift.</strong> An entry's <code>description:</code> (what recall keys on) contradicts its own self-corrected body. (Fen PASS both temps.)</li> <li><strong>index-vs-file drift.</strong> The <code>MEMORY.md</code> index pointer is staler than the file it points to.</li> <li><strong>superseded-but-unlinked.</strong> A conclusion that a later memory overturns, with no forward <code>[[link]]</code> between them. (Fen PASS both temps.)</li> <li><strong>stale STATE markers over durable lore.</strong> A snapshot memory whose state is done but whose measured lore is still valid.</li> <li><strong>workaround-vs-plan conflation.</strong> Two entries asserting contradictory current facts, neither referencing the other.</li> <li><strong>dangling <code>[[link]]</code></strong> on either store.</li> <li><strong>append-only violations</strong> on the repo store. (Fen conflated with stale-state-over-lore; the build sharpens the naming before this detector ships.)</li> <li><strong>room-touching findings</strong> routed to MADR. (Fen conflated with superseded-but-unlinked; same sharpening.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="routing-the-cross-harness-discipline-now-narrower"><a class="header" href="#routing-the-cross-harness-discipline-now-narrower">Routing (the cross-harness discipline, now narrower)</a></h2> <p><code>dream</code> is read-only and routes findings; it never writes.</p> <ul> <li><strong>editable-store hygiene</strong>: suggested edits, printed verbatim.</li> <li><strong>repo-store staleness</strong>: suggested <strong>append</strong> with the correction text and the forward <code>[[link]]</code> to add, printed verbatim.</li> <li>a finding that touches a <code>call/</code> or <code>plan/</code> <strong>room</strong>: route to the MADR path (<code>Status: superseded</code> on the immutable record + audited commit), <strong>not</strong> a memory edit. <code>dream</code> names the room and the record; it does not touch them.</li> <li><strong>anti-ouroboros</strong>: <code>dream</code> is methodology hygiene, not a software decision. It must <strong>not</strong> propose minting a <code>call/</code> for the audit itself. The durable output is the corrected store plus a <code>feedback</code>-type memory capturing the lesson.</li> </ul> <p><code>dream</code> also sits at the intersection of:</p> <ul> <li><strong>the two memory stores</strong> (different rules),</li> <li><strong>the recall injector</strong> (which per-user descriptions get surfaced into context; the MCP server is the recall surface),</li> <li><strong><code>host-lint</code></strong> (which gates any repo-store commit; the suggested appends must be lint-clean),</li> <li><strong>the room discipline</strong> (findings that touch <code>call/</code>/<code>plan/</code> route to <code>validate</code>/MADR, not to a memory edit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-cli-shape"><a class="header" href="#the-cli-shape">The CLI shape</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>host-lifecycle dream <dir></code>: read-mostly. Print findings, do not write.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle dream <dir> --fix</code>: apply <strong>only</strong> the mechanical, safe class (index/description reconciliation, dangling-link repair) on the <strong>editable</strong> host-* store, never the repo store. Refuses the repo store even with <code>--fix</code>.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle dream <dir> --json</code>: machine-readable findings.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle mcp</code>: the stdio MCP server (shipped v0.39.0). Plan/0073 adds the memory tools (<code>memory_list</code>, <code>memory_read</code>, <code>memory_write</code>, <code>memory_consolidate</code>) alongside the existing <code>init</code> and <code>adopt</code>. Loaded by opencode (or any MCP-speaking harness) via the standard stdio-MCP config.</li> <li>Exit codes follow the host-lint convention: <code>0</code> clean, <code>1</code> findings, <code>2</code> cannot-proceed-on-input (no repo, no host-* store found).</li> </ul> <p>The <code>--fix</code> set is conservative and grows one class at a time. Anything that touches meaning (the workaround-vs-plan class, the supersession class) is report-only forever; only structure (the index one-liner, the dangling link) is <code>--fix</code>-able.</p> <h2 id="the-store-format-the-spine-names-it"><a class="header" href="#the-store-format-the-spine-names-it">The store format (the spine names it)</a></h2> <p>The host-* per-user memory store at <code>~/.host-memory/<project>/</code>:</p> <pre><code>~/.host-memory/ <project>/ # one dir per project (encoded cwd, claude-style) MEMORY.md # the index: one bullet per entry <slug>.md # one markdown file per memory entry ... </code></pre> <p>Each entry file:</p> <pre><code class="language-markdown">--- description: <one-line summary; what recall keys on> type: feedback | fact | workaround | state # the entry's class created: <YYYY-MM-DD> --- <free-form markdown body> <optional [[slug]] cross-references to other entries> </code></pre> <p>The <code>MEMORY.md</code> index:</p> <pre><code class="language-markdown">- [<Title>](<slug>.md) — <one-line summary, same as the description: line> </code></pre> <p>The format is the methodology's own. The opencode plugin implements it; the <code>dream</code> audit reads it. Convergence with other harnesses' formats is empirical, not load-bearing.</p> <h2 id="open-design-questions-2"><a class="header" href="#open-design-questions-2">Open design questions</a></h2> <p>The cast pass and adversarial review rule on these:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Detector naming.</strong> The gather-data probe showed <code>append-only-violation</code> and <code>room-touching</code> do not read clearly at the 4B bar. Three options on the table (rename, lean on routing, accept partial coverage); a fourth is now viable since we own the store: <strong>emit the route as the primary finding and the class as secondary metadata</strong>, so the operator-facing surface is always actionable ("append this", "edit that", "file this MADR") even when the class name is fuzzy.</li> <li><strong>The MCP tool surface.</strong> Four new tools (<code>memory_list</code> / <code>memory_read</code> / <code>memory_write</code> / <code>memory_consolidate</code>) join the existing <code>init</code> and <code>adopt</code> on the <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> server (plan/0065). The cast review confirms whether <code>memory_search</code> (a semantic query) is needed at MVP or is a follow-up.</li> <li><strong>The store's project-encoding.</strong> Claude uses <code>/</code>-to-<code>-</code> cwd mangling; opencode uses a SQLite-keyed project id. The host-* format names its own project-encoding (the cwd with <code>/</code> to <code>-</code>, plus a project-name override for the harness-agnostic case), documented in the spine.</li> <li><strong>The Allium spec scope.</strong> Per plan/0014, a stateful feature earns an Allium spec. The detector state machine + the MCP tool surface are the natural model. The spec lives in the host-lifecycle repo.</li> <li><strong>The cast-consultation frame.</strong> Bly, Fen, Orin each see a different failure mode. The cast review shapes the <code>--fix</code> set, the MCP tool naming, and the report format.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-spine-doctrine-host-template-claudemd"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-doctrine-host-template-claudemd">The spine doctrine (host-template CLAUDE.md)</a></h2> <p>The spine gains:</p> <ul> <li>the <em><em>host-</em> per-user memory store convention</em>*: the path (<code>~/.host-memory/<project>/</code>), the format (markdown per entry, <code>MEMORY.md</code> index, <code>description:</code> + free-form body, <code>[[slug]]</code> cross-refs), and the editable rule;</li> <li>a restatement of the <strong>append-only asymmetry</strong> at the per-user level: the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> is append-only; the per-user store is editable; <code>dream</code> is the gate that holds both;</li> <li>a <code>dream</code> cadence: when to run it (e.g. at the start of a session that will rely on recall, at the end of a session that superseded a decision);</li> <li>a note that <em><em>the host-</em> per-user store is the reference tier</em>*; vendor stores are not read. An operator on a harness without the MCP plugin gets only the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> tier.</li> </ul> <p>An adopter UPGRADING entry keys the new revision and requires the host-lifecycle release that carries <code>dream</code> and <code>mcp</code>.</p> <h2 id="verification-41"><a class="header" href="#verification-41">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Unit tests</strong> for every detector: each fires on a constructed fixture and is silent on a clean fixture. The append-only-violation detector fires on a hand-edited repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> and is silent on the append-only one.</li> <li><strong>Integration tests</strong> for the routing: a repo-store finding suggests an append; an editable-store finding suggests an edit; a finding that touches a <code>call/</code> record names the room and does not propose an edit.</li> <li><strong>Integration tests for the MCP server</strong>: <code>memory_list</code> returns the index; <code>memory_read</code> returns an entry; <code>memory_write</code> creates a new entry with the right frontmatter and updates the index; <code>memory_consolidate</code> runs a <code>dream</code> pass and reports findings. Tool calls exercised over stdio JSON-RPC. The existing <code>init</code>/<code>adopt</code> tools (plan/0065) stay green unchanged.</li> <li><strong>Allium spec</strong> models the detector state machine and the MCP tool surface; <code>allium check</code> + <code>analyse</code> + <code>plan</code> exit 0; obligations discharged by tests; Kani for the structural invariants (e.g. the <code>--fix</code> set never touches the repo store).</li> <li><strong>Fen probe</strong> (gather-data.md): the detector phrasing reads as a finding to a 4B at both temps for the simpler detectors; the methodology-discipline detectors are either sharpened to pass at the 4B bar or surface the route as the primary finding.</li> <li><strong>Cast consultation</strong> (cast/*.md): the <code>--fix</code> set, the MCP tool naming, and the report format clear Bly (overstates-completeness), Fen (weak-agent -trap), Orin (fails-unsafe).</li> <li><strong>Adversarial design review</strong> (design-review.md): five independent lenses, with the duplication risk (vs. plan/0074's envhash) and the auto-detect reversal as named lenses.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> clean at the new pin; the host-lifecycle release receipt recorded; #16 closed.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-15"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-15">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The tasks are anchored receipted nodes (plan/0042), built as a forward graph:</p> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">gather-data</a></h3> <p>Grounds every conditional in data: the six-harness memory-store survey, the auto-detect reversal (closed harnesses encrypt; opencode has no native store), and the Fen probe on detector phrasing and routing legibility.</p> <ul> <li>verify: every conditional in this README traces to a gather-data.md row</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">write-spec</a></h3> <p>The <code>DreamRun</code> and <code>MemoryStore</code> Allium surface with the detector state machine, the MCP tool surface, the routing rules, and the append-only-violation invariant. Lives in the host-lifecycle repo.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>allium check</code> + <code>allium analyse</code> exit 0, zero findings</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">write-obligations</a></h3> <p>Every <code>allium plan</code> obligation dispositioned in a <code><spec>.obligations</code> manifest, discharged by the unit and integration tests.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle obligations <spec> --tests tests --strict-discharge</code> clean</li> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-store"><a class="header" href="#implement-store">implement-store</a></h3> <p>The storage layer: read/write markdown entries at <code>~/.host-memory/<project>/</code>, the <code>MEMORY.md</code> index manager, the <code>[[slug]]</code> link resolver, the project-encoding helper.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a round-trip write-then-read returns the entry; the index stays in sync after every write</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-dream"><a class="header" href="#implement-dream">implement-dream</a></h3> <p>The <code>dream</code> subcommand and the detector set, built on the storage layer plus the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> reader. <code>--fix</code> is the conservative structural-only set on the editable store, refusing the repo store. dream and the MCP <code>memory_consolidate</code> tool share the detector engine. The initial pass implements the structural detectors precisely (superseded-but-unlinked, dangling-link, room-touching) and stubs the semantic ones (stale-state-over-lore, workaround-vs-plan, append-only-violation) with documented TODOs; the deferred detectors land at #implement-remaining.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; <code>dream <fixture></code> emits the expected findings; <code>--fix</code> refuses a repo-store fixture</li> <li>depends: #implement-store</li> </ul> <h3 id="weed-and-tend"><a class="header" href="#weed-and-tend">weed-and-tend</a></h3> <p>Run the <code>weed</code> skill in check mode to enumerate every spec↔code divergence (plan/0015: weed catches hand-authored spec drift the implementation passes clean on; the host-lint spec bug <code>DetectInternalCodeAsName</code> flag-vs-warn is the precedent). Then run the <code>tend</code> skill to reconcile each divergence into one of three buckets: (a) spec over-promises (e.g. the MemoryWrite surface not needed for dream-only): trim the spec; (b) code under-delivers (e.g. the deferred detectors): record for #implement-remaining; (c) they agree: no change. The tended spec is the new baseline; the manifest is rewritten to match what the post-tend spec + the current Rust surface can discharge.</p> <ul> <li>verify: the weed check report and the tend reconciliation table are recorded in <code>weed-and-tend.md</code>; the tended spec parses + analyses clean; the trimmed manifest's <code>--tests src</code> check passes non-strict with zero STALE entries</li> <li>depends: #implement-dream</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">write-tests</a></h3> <p>The test suite against the tended spec. Each unignored test from #write-tests goes green.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test --release</code> green (no <code>#[ignore]</code> remaining); the previously-deferred Kani proofs pass</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="extend-mcp"><a class="header" href="#extend-mcp">extend-mcp</a></h3> <p>Add <code>memory_list</code>, <code>memory_read</code>, <code>memory_write</code>, <code>memory_consolidate</code> tools to the existing <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> server (shipped v0.39.0 per plan/0065). Same stdio JSON-RPC pattern; the <code>tool_defs</code> registry grows, the dispatch arm gains the memory tools, the existing <code>init</code>/<code>adopt</code> tools stay byte-identical. Built on the implementation that #implement-remaining just landed.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; an integration test drives the server over stdio and exercises each memory tool; the <code>init</code>/<code>adopt</code> tools still pass their existing tests unchanged</li> <li>depends: #implement-remaining</li> </ul> <h3 id="wire-opencode-plugin"><a class="header" href="#wire-opencode-plugin">wire-opencode-plugin</a></h3> <p>The opencode configuration entry for the <code>host-lifecycle mcp</code> stdio server is already in place for <code>init</code>/<code>adopt</code> (plan/0065); plan/0073 confirms it loads the new memory tools. My recommendation: keep the spec dream-only for plan/0073; the MCP surface gets its own spec (or spec section) at a follow-up milestone if the adversarial review confirms the need.</p> <p><strong>Disposition:</strong> O1 deferred to #write-spine-doctrine (name as MVP-grade). O2 deferred to #write-spine-doctrine (name the boundary). O3 deferred to #adversarial-review.</p> <h2 id="fen-weak-agent-qwen35-4b-q8_0"><a class="header" href="#fen-weak-agent-qwen35-4b-q8_0">Fen (weak agent, qwen3.5-4b Q8_0)</a></h2> <p><strong>Concern:</strong> can a 4B read the new detectors and route correctly?</p> <p><strong>Finding F1 (routing intuition differs from spec):</strong> the Fen probe on the three new detectors showed the model routes by FINDING CLASS (some findings are "edit", some "append", some "report") rather than by STORE (per-user → edit, repo → append). The spec encodes routing by store; the model's intuition is class-based. The mismatch is not a design flaw — the store -based routing is the correct methodology rule (the asymmetry is load-bearing) — but the report format should make the route explicit so the model doesn't need to infer it.</p> <p><strong>Finding F2 (three new detectors readable):</strong> the model correctly identified the three new detector classes when given a constructed fixture (the probe above). The naming (stale-state-over-lore, workaround-vs-plan, append-only-violation) reads clearly to a 4B when presented in context.</p> <p><strong>Disposition:</strong> F1 addressed: the dream report already prints <code>route=edit</code> or <code>route=append</code> explicitly in the text output, so the model doesn't infer. F2 addressed: the detectors read at the 4B bar.</p> <h2 id="summary-of-dispositions"><a class="header" href="#summary-of-dispositions">Summary of dispositions</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Finding</th><th>Disposition</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>M1 (cadence)</td><td>deferred to #write-spine-doctrine</td></tr> <tr><td>M2 (--fix no-op)</td><td>recorded; first class at follow-up or flag marked reserved</td></tr> <tr><td>W1 (no suggested fix text)</td><td>named follow-up: add suggestion field to Finding</td></tr> <tr><td>W2 (MCP schema clear)</td><td>addressed</td></tr> <tr><td>B1 (path-sensitivity)</td><td>recorded; envhash (plan/0074) catches the move</td></tr> <tr><td>B2 (no cross-machine)</td><td>deferred to #write-spine-doctrine</td></tr> <tr><td>O1 (heuristic MVP-grade)</td><td>deferred to #write-spine-doctrine</td></tr> <tr><td>O2 (boundary in spine)</td><td>deferred to #write-spine-doctrine</td></tr> <tr><td>O3 (spec scope)</td><td>deferred to #adversarial-review</td></tr> <tr><td>F1 (routing by class vs store)</td><td>addressed (route printed in report)</td></tr> <tr><td>F2 (new detectors readable)</td><td>addressed</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Five findings deferred to #write-spine-doctrine, one to #adversarial-review, one named follow-up (suggestion text), and three addressed. No blocking findings for the current implementation.</p> <h2 id="adversarial-review-2026-07-19"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review-2026-07-19">Adversarial review (2026-07-19)</a></h2> <p>Three named lenses plus a cast-completeness audit. Each lens examines a load-bearing design decision the cast consultation surfaced or skirted. Findings classified: <strong>blocking</strong> (must fix before release), <strong>major</strong> (should fix or explicitly defer), <strong>minor</strong> (note and move on).</p> <h3 id="lens-1-duplication-risk-vs-plan0074s-envhash"><a class="header" href="#lens-1-duplication-risk-vs-plan0074s-envhash">Lens 1: Duplication risk vs. plan/0074's envhash</a></h3> <p><strong>Focus:</strong> do dream's per-user store audit and plan/0074's envhash overlap on the move-detection signal? Bly's finding B1 raised the path-sensitivity concern.</p> <p><strong>Analysis:</strong> envhash fingerprints the local environment (repo abspath, worktree paths, hook binary hash, image digest, submodule init state). Its job is coherence: "is my tree still what I hashed?" dream audits memory content for staleness: "is my recall stale?" The overlap point is the CWD: if the project moves, dream's per-user store path changes and dream silently reads an empty store (B1).</p> <p><strong>Finding L1-1 (minor): dream must NOT try to detect moves.</strong> Move detection is envhash's job (plan/0074). dream should run over whatever store is present and report what it finds. If the store is empty because the project moved, that's envhash's signal to surface, not dream's. The two tools are complementary, not duplicative: envhash says "your environment moved"; dream says "your memory is stale." Confirming the non-overlap.</p> <p><strong>Finding L1-2 (minor, deferred): the per-user store encoding uses CWD.</strong> A project-name key (from <code>.host</code> stamp) would survive a move. This is a deeper change; for MVP, the CWD encoding is the bar. Named follow-up for a future revision.</p> <h3 id="lens-2-the-spec-scope-question-auto-detect-reversal--o3"><a class="header" href="#lens-2-the-spec-scope-question-auto-detect-reversal--o3">Lens 2: The spec scope question (auto-detect reversal + O3)</a></h3> <p><strong>Focus:</strong> the weed+tend decision trimmed the spec to dream-only, removing MemoryWrite/Suggestion/LinkRef entities. Orin's finding O3 deferred the ruling to this review. Is the trim correct?</p> <p><strong>Analysis:</strong> the MCP surface IS tested (4 integration tests over stdio JSON-RPC). The MemoryWrite safety property ("memory_write never writes to the repo store") is enforced by code (no code path exists) and tested (memory_write doesn't accept a store parameter). But it's not asserted in the spec.</p> <p><strong>Finding L2-1 (major, ruled): accept the code-level enforcement for plan/0073 MVP.</strong> The spec stays dream-only. Rationale: the dream feature's load-bearing semantics (detector set, routing, verdict lifecycle, invariants) are fully modeled. The MCP surface is a transport layer over the dream engine; it's tested behaviourally. A formal spec for the MCP surface would add modelling weight without changing runtime behaviour. If the methodology later needs the formal contract (e.g. a second consumer of memory_write, or a Kani proof of the repo-refusal invariant), a follow-up milestone restores the entity.</p> <p><strong>Finding L2-2 (major): the Finding entity lacks a suggestion field.</strong> Wren's finding W1 noted the dream report says WHAT is wrong but not HOW to fix it. The code's Finding has <code>explanation</code> (prose) but no <code>suggestion</code> (verbatim fix text). For MVP this is acceptable (the operator reads the explanation and constructs the fix), but it limits the <code>--fix</code> surface's future. The adversarial review rules: <strong>defer to a named follow-up plan</strong> (not plan/0073). The suggestion text is a UX refinement, not a correctness gap.</p> <h3 id="lens-3-mcp-surface-shape"><a class="header" href="#lens-3-mcp-surface-shape">Lens 3: MCP surface shape</a></h3> <p><strong>Focus:</strong> are the four memory tools the right shape? Does memory_write's safety property hold? Are there gaps?</p> <p><strong>Finding L3-1 (minor): the <code>op</code> schema conflates create and update.</strong> The MCP schema exposes <code>op: write | delete</code>; the original spec had <code>MemoryWriteOp = create | update | delete</code>. The code's <code>write</code> is an idempotent create-or-update (MemoryStore::write checks if the slug exists and preserves <code>created</code> on update). This is simpler and matches the operator's mental model. Acceptable for MVP; the three-value form is a follow-up if the distinction becomes load-bearing (e.g. refusing to update a Fact entry without confirmation).</p> <p><strong>Finding L3-2 (minor): no scoping on memory_consolidate.</strong> The tool audits both stores unconditionally. For MVP this is correct (dream's job is to catch staleness everywhere). A <code>--scope per-user|repo|both</code> flag is a future refinement if the operator needs to isolate.</p> <p><strong>Finding L3-3 (addressed): memory_write preserves <code>created</code> on updates, sets <code>last_edited</code> to today.</strong> Correct behaviour; verified by the integration test <code>memory_write_then_list_then_read_round_trips</code>.</p> <h3 id="lens-4-cast-consultation-completeness-audit"><a class="header" href="#lens-4-cast-consultation-completeness-audit">Lens 4: Cast consultation completeness audit</a></h3> <p><strong>Focus:</strong> ensure every cast finding has a clear owner, timeline, and disposition. A follow-up milestone restores the spec entity if the methodology needs the formal contract.</p> <p><strong>Finding C2: W1 deferred to a follow-up plan.</strong> The suggestion text is a UX refinement, not a correctness gap for MVP.</p> <p><strong>Finding C3: M2 ruled.</strong> <code>--fix</code> is documented as "reserved" in the spine; the first safe class (dangling-link repair) lands at a follow-up with cast-review sign-off.</p> <h3 id="verdict-4"><a class="header" href="#verdict-4">Verdict</a></h3> <p>No blocking findings. Two major findings ruled:</p> <ul> <li>L2-1: spec stays dream-only (MVP; MCP surface is code-tested)</li> <li>L2-2: suggestion text deferred to a follow-up plan</li> </ul> <p>Three minor findings noted and deferred:</p> <ul> <li>L1-2: per-user store encoding by project-name (follow-up)</li> <li>L3-1: three-value MemoryWriteOp (follow-up)</li> <li>L3-2: memory_consolidate scoping (follow-up)</li> </ul> <p>The plan/0073 implementation proceeds to #write-spine-doctrine with the ruled dispositions folded into the spine text.</p> <h2 id="post-acceptance-correction-2026-07-20-two-hollow-dispositions"><a class="header" href="#post-acceptance-correction-2026-07-20-two-hollow-dispositions">Post-acceptance correction (2026-07-20): two hollow dispositions</a></h2> <p>The #fen-acceptance run against the real qwen3.5-4b falsified two of the dispositions above. This section records the correction so the epistemic trail stays honest.</p> <p><strong>W1 and L2-2 were not a UX refinement.</strong> The review deferred the suggestion text as "a UX refinement, not a correctness gap for MVP" (C2, L2-2). The acceptance probe showed the opposite: without the verbatim imperative, the 4B routes the per-user edit class wrong at both temperatures, so the acceptance criterion "Fen routes each finding class correctly" was not met. The suggestion text is load-bearing at the weak-agent bar, not cosmetic.</p> <p><strong>F1 was recorded "addressed" when it was not.</strong> F1's disposition read "addressed: the dream report already prints route=edit or route=append explicitly, so the model does not infer." The probe transcripts show the model does not read the <code>route=</code> token at all; it follows the explanation prose. For the per-user store the prose and the printed route diverge, and the model follows the prose. Printing the route was necessary but not sufficient.</p> <p><strong>Resolution (host-lifecycle v0.41.1).</strong> Both are the same root cause and both are fixed by promoting the W1 suggestion text into the report surface: each finding gains a route-carrying imperative in the natural language the model reads. The routing re-probe then passed four of four at both temperatures (recorded in fen-acceptance.md).</p> <p><strong>Re-audit.</strong> Because F1 was hollow, every disposition in this document was re-verified against the code, spec, spine, and tests. W1, F1, and L2-2 (one root cause) were the only hollow ones. Every other disposition verified authentic: implemented, honestly documented as a no-op or MVP-grade, or a follow-up the acceptance does not contradict. The re-audit table is in fen-acceptance.md.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="fen-acceptance-the-4b-bar-on-routing-and-the-mcp-surface-2026-07-20"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance-the-4b-bar-on-routing-and-the-mcp-surface-2026-07-20">fen-acceptance: the 4B bar on routing and the MCP surface (2026-07-20)</a></h1> <p>The task's verify: the real qwen3.5-4b routes each finding class correctly (suggested append vs suggested edit vs the MADR route) on a constructed fixture, and uses the MCP <code>memory_list</code> tool unaided.</p> <h2 id="fixture"><a class="header" href="#fixture">Fixture</a></h2> <p><code>/tmp/plan0073-accept/</code> (idempotent, rebuildable):</p> <ul> <li>repo tier <code>repo/MEMORY.md</code>: two sections, one linking a missing <code>[[q8-kernel-brief]]</code> (dangling-link, repo), one citing <code>call/0007</code> (room-touching, repo).</li> <li>per-user tier <code>home/.host-memory/-tmp-plan0073-accept-repo/</code>: three entries; <code>kv-cache-f16</code> carries <code>superseded_by: kv-cache-q8</code> with no forward link in the body (superseded-but-unlinked, per-user); <code>build-notes</code> links a missing <code>[[megakernel-base]]</code> (dangling-link, per-user); <code>kv-cache-q8</code> is clean.</li> </ul> <p>The real audit (<code>HOME=/tmp/plan0073-accept/home host-lifecycle dream /tmp/plan0073-accept/repo</code>, v0.41.0) emitted exactly the four designed findings, exit 1:</p> <pre><code class="language-text">kv-cache-f16 (per-user) [superseded-but-unlinked] route=edit -- superseded by `kv-cache-q8` but no forward link `[[kv-cache-q8]]` in the body build-notes (per-user) [dangling-link] route=edit -- body links `[[megakernel-base]]` but no entry `megakernel-base` exists in the per-user store 2026-07-10-kv-cache-stays-at-f16 (repo) [dangling-link] route=append -- body links `[[q8-kernel-brief]]` but no entry `q8-kernel-brief` exists in the repo store 2026-07-15-release-checklist-follows-call-0007 (repo) [room-touching] route=append -- body cites `call/0007`; confirm the record is not superseded by the spine </code></pre> <h2 id="probe-channel"><a class="header" href="#probe-channel">Probe channel</a></h2> <p>Same as gather-data: <code>~/.local/bin/fen-probe</code> (Unsloth direct, <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code>), <code>top_p</code> 0.8, <code>enable_thinking</code> false, <code>max_tokens</code> 800.
