The MCP surface is legible at the 4B bar.</p> <h2 id="finding-routing-fails-per-user-store-both-temps"><a class="header" href="#finding-routing-fails-per-user-store-both-temps">Finding routing fails (per-user store, both temps)</a></h2> <p>The probe presented the four real findings plus four operator actions (append to the repo log / edit the per-user entry in place / confirm the cited record / nothing), order rotated between temps.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Finding</th><th>Correct</th><th>temp 0.2</th><th>temp 0.6</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>kv-cache-f16 (per-user)</td><td>edit</td><td>append (wrong)</td><td>append (wrong)</td></tr> <tr><td>build-notes (per-user)</td><td>edit</td><td>append (wrong)</td><td>append (wrong)</td></tr> <tr><td>repo dangling-link</td><td>append</td><td>append (right)</td><td>append (right)</td></tr> <tr><td>repo room-touching</td><td>confirm record</td><td>confirm (right)</td><td>confirm (right)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The rotation rules out an option-order artifact: append was option A at temp 0.2 and option C at temp 0.6, and the model picked it both times for the repo findings, then picked the same action for the per-user findings.</p> <h2 id="what-the-transcripts-show"><a class="header" href="#what-the-transcripts-show">What the transcripts show</a></h2> <p>The model does not read the <code>route=</code> token. It reads the explanation prose and reasons from the store rules it already knows:</p> <ul> <li>temp 0.6, kv-cache-f16: "Since the per-user store allows in-place editing but the finding indicates the entry is superseded, the correct remediation is to append a new dated correction to the repo log rather than editing the old file directly." The model states the editability rule and then violates it.</li> <li>temp 0.6, build-notes: "The per-user store is private and editable, so the dangling link should be fixed by appending a new dated entry to the repo MEMORY.md", which is internally contradictory.</li> <li>room-touching, both temps: the model followed the <em>explanation</em> ("confirm the record is not superseded by the spine") and ignored the printed <code>route=append</code>, yet reached the correct action anyway.</li> </ul> <p>Three independent observations (per-user findings, repo findings, room-touching) point the same way: at the 4B bar the operative signal is the natural-language imperative, and the <code>route=</code> token is dead text. The two-store asymmetry, the load-bearing design rule, is not applied by the model when it has to choose the action itself.</p> <h2 id="verdict-v1-probe-v0410"><a class="header" href="#verdict-v1-probe-v0410">Verdict (v1 probe, v0.41.0)</a></h2> <p>The acceptance criterion "Fen routes each finding class correctly" was not met at v0.41.0: append and the MADR route are read correctly; edit is not. This is the cast review's W1 finding (the report says what is wrong but not how to fix it; no suggestion text) showing up as a hard acceptance failure rather than the UX refinement the adversarial review deferred it as. The operator ruling needed: either the report surface gains a per-finding imperative (the W1 suggestion text, promoted from the deferred follow-up, shipping as a patch release) and the probe re-runs, or the acceptance bar is re-scoped by a recorded decision.</p> <h2 id="operator-ruling-2026-07-20-address-the-cast-authentically"><a class="header" href="#operator-ruling-2026-07-20-address-the-cast-authentically">Operator ruling (2026-07-20): address the cast authentically</a></h2> <p>The ruling was to address the cast's issues authentically, not to re-scope the bar. The fen-acceptance failure falsified two design-review dispositions: W1 ("no suggested fix text", deferred as a UX refinement) and F1 ("routing by class vs store", dispositioned "addressed: the route is printed in the report"). Printing <code>route=</code> is not enough; the 4B skips the token and follows the prose. Both were the same root cause, and both are fixed by promoting the W1 suggestion text into the report surface.</p> <h2 id="the-fix-v0411"><a class="header" href="#the-fix-v0411">The fix (v0.41.1)</a></h2> <p>Each <code>dream</code> finding gained a <code>suggestion</code> field: a verbatim operator imperative whose leading verb and anti-action tail carry the route in the natural language the model reads. A per-user finding now reads "Edit the per-user entry <code><slug></code> in place to ...; do not append to the repo log"; a repo finding reads "Append a new dated entry to the repo MEMORY.md to ...; do not edit the existing entry in place"; a room-touching finding names the record and the MADR action and forbids both memory writes. The imperative renders in the text output (a second line per finding), in <code>--json</code> (a <code>suggestion</code> field), and in the MCP <code>memory_consolidate</code> output. Shipped as host-lifecycle v0.41.1 (<code>3472e27</code>, artifact <code>3ddb2857</code>, change-class neither).</p> <h2 id="finding-routing-re-probe-v0411-passes-both-temps"><a class="header" href="#finding-routing-re-probe-v0411-passes-both-temps">Finding routing re-probe (v0.41.1): passes (both temps)</a></h2> <p>Same channel, same two temperatures, option order rotated between them; the only variable is the report surface (the report now carries the imperative). Script <code>/tmp/plan0073-acceptance-probe-v2.sh</code>; transcripts <code>/tmp/plan0073-acceptance-transcripts-v2.txt</code>.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Finding</th><th>Correct</th><th>temp 0.2</th><th>temp 0.6</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>kv-cache-f16 (per-user)</td><td>edit</td><td>edit (right)</td><td>edit (right)</td></tr> <tr><td>build-notes (per-user)</td><td>edit</td><td>edit (right)</td><td>edit (right)</td></tr> <tr><td>repo dangling-link</td><td>append</td><td>append (right)</td><td>append (right)</td></tr> <tr><td>repo room-touching</td><td>confirm record</td><td>confirm (right)</td><td>confirm (right)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Four of four correct at both temps. The per-user edit route, which failed both temps at v0.41.0, now passes both temps.</p> <h2 id="re-audit-of-every-disposition-2026-07-20"><a class="header" href="#re-audit-of-every-disposition-2026-07-20">Re-audit of every disposition (2026-07-20)</a></h2> <p>Because F1 was recorded "addressed" when it was hollow, every cast and adversarial disposition was re-verified against the code, the spec, the spine text, and the tests. Both legs pass at the 4B bar: the MCP tool surface is legible (the MCP-surface check), and every finding class routes correctly once the report carries the imperative (the routing check). Anthropic docs</td></tr> <tr><td>qwen</td><td>yes</td><td><code>~/.qwen/projects/<project>/memory/</code> (personal auto-memory) + <code>.qwen/team-memory/</code> (in-repo, opt-in, git-tracked) + <code>~/.qwen/QWEN.md</code> (user instructions)</td><td><code>MEMORY.md</code> index + <code><slug>.md</code> entries; generated state, not hand-edited as primary surface</td><td><strong>off</strong> by default (gated <code>[features] memories = true</code>)</td><td>OpenAI Codex docs: <code>developers.openai.com/codex/customization/memories</code></td></tr> <tr><td>opencode</td><td><strong>no</strong></td><td>none (sessions, messages, snapshots live in <code>~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db</code> SQLite; no memory-store concept)</td><td>n/a</td><td>n/a</td><td>local FS: confirmed; no memory files anywhere under <code>~/.config/opencode</code>, <code>~/.local/share/opencode</code>, or <code>~/.opencode</code></td></tr> <tr><td>cursor-agent</td><td>unknown</td><td>docs are JS-rendered (webfetch returns the page chrome only); not installed locally</td><td>unknown</td><td>unknown</td><td>could not confirm without installation</td></tr> <tr><td>pi</td><td>unknown</td><td>could not locate authoritative docs or repo; not installed locally</td><td>unknown</td><td>unknown</td><td><code>gh search</code> returned no canonical <code>pi-agent</code> repo; possibly a proprietary tool</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="findings-the-design-must-encode"><a class="header" href="#findings-the-design-must-encode">Findings the design must encode</a></h3> <ol> <li><em><em>The two-store asymmetry is host-</em> methodology, not a vendor pattern.</em>* The spine (CLAUDE.md §6) already names the asymmetry: the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> is append-only; the operator's per-user store (whatever harness they run) is editable. The survey confirms the major harnesses (Claude, Qwen, Codex) carry some per-user memory store, so there is something concrete to audit; it does NOT determine the spine doctrine. The spine names its own per-user format; the per-harness layer reads each vendor's layout and maps to it.</li> <li><strong>Qwen Code also has a <code>/dream</code> command (parallel invention, not prior art).</strong> Qwen Code ships a same-named command for consolidating its own <code>~/.qwen/projects/<project>/memory/</code> store. The convergence is noted but not load-bearing: our <code>host-lifecycle dream</code> is independently motivated by the host-* methodology's own two-store asymmetry (CLAUDE.md §6: the repo <code>MEMORY.md</code> is append-only; the operator's per-user store is editable). Nothing in plan/0073 derives from Qwen's design, and the spine doctrine names its own format. The shared verb is a coincidence of naming, not of IP.</li> <li><strong>Auto-detect is required; presence varies.</strong> Claude / qwen / codex have a store; opencode has none; cursor / pi unknown. <code>dream</code> MUST gracefully skip a harness with no memory store (clean exit, no findings, no error), per the issue's "a harness with no memory store is a clean skip" framing.</li> <li><strong>Default-on varies.</strong> Claude and qwen are on by default; codex is off by default (config-gated). <code>dream</code> reads whatever is present; it does not care whether the user enabled the feature.</li> <li><strong>Format varies; the spine names its own.</strong> The host-* per-user store format the spine documents is the methodology's own (one markdown file per memory, with a <code>description:</code> line and free-form body; an index file listing each entry with a one-line summary; <code>[[slug]]</code> for cross-entry links). The per-harness layer reads each vendor's actual layout (Claude/qwen use a similar shape; Codex differs; opencode has none) and maps to the spine's vocabulary. Nothing is adopted from a vendor; the spine is the source of truth, the mapping layer is per-harness glue.</li> <li><strong>The per-user store path is project-keyed for Claude and qwen</strong> (the encoded-cwd / project subdirectory), so <code>dream <host-dir></code> can resolve the matching project subdir directly. Codex is global; <code>dream</code> reads the whole <code>~/.codex/memories/</code> and accepts that findings may include other projects' memories (the report names the project where known).</li> </ol> <h3 id="what-this-answers-in-the-readme"><a class="header" href="#what-this-answers-in-the-readme">What this answers in the README</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Open: "The exact paths and formats for each of the six harnesses."</strong> Answered above; cursor and pi are documented unknowns (clean skips at runtime).</li> <li><strong>Open: "Is the description: + free-form body format Claude Code's convention or ours?"</strong> Answered: it is ours. The spine names the host-* per-user store format independently; the per-harness layer maps each vendor's layout to it. The convergence with Claude's and Qwen's formats is noted in the survey as an empirical observation, not as the source of the format.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-fen-probe-detector-phrasing-and-routing-legibility"><a class="header" href="#the-fen-probe-detector-phrasing-and-routing-legibility">The Fen probe (detector phrasing and routing legibility)</a></h2> <p>A neutral, two-temperature probe (option order shuffled) over the detector set and the routing rules. The bar (cast/fen.md): does a 4B read each detector as a finding class (not a verdict), and does it route each to the right path (suggested append for repo-store, suggested edit for editable-store, MADR route for findings touching a call/plan room)?</p> <h3 id="probe-design"><a class="header" href="#probe-design">Probe design</a></h3> <ul> <li>One prompt per detector, with a constructed fixture (a small markdown memory file or a one-line memory entry) that exercises the detector.</li> <li>Each prompt asks Fen to identify the finding class (multiple choice, options rotated across runs) and the route (separate classification).</li> <li>Two temperatures (<code>--temp 0.2</code>, <code>--temp 0.6</code>) per probe, options shuffled between them. A pass requires content reasoning at both temperatures, not a position artifact (per MEMORY: weak-agent-probe discipline).</li> <li><code>enable_thinking:false</code> to keep the run tight and the latency under a few seconds per call.</li> </ul> <h3 id="detector-coverage-matrix"><a class="header" href="#detector-coverage-matrix">Detector-coverage matrix</a></h3> <p>The matrix describes the test-case fixtures each detector fires on. The fixtures quote the contrast patterns the detector catches (X-but-Y, neither, done-but-valid), so the prose engine trips on them; fenced per call/0019 (irreducible literal content).</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">| Detector | Fixture | Expected class | Expected route | |---|---|---|---| | description-vs-body drift | a memory file whose `description:` says "build in /tmp" but the body says "build on /opt/models xfs" | description-vs-body | edit (editable-store) | | index-vs-file drift | a `MEMORY.md` index pointer whose one-liner says "keep f16 KV" but the file it points to says "q8 KV unblocked" | index-vs-file | edit (editable-store) | | superseded-but-unlinked | two entries where the later overturns the earlier, no `[[link]]` connecting them | superseded-but-unlinked | append (repo-store) when the older is the repo `MEMORY.md`; edit when both are editable-store | | stale STATE over durable lore | a snapshot memory whose state is done but whose measured lore is still valid | stale-state-over-lore | edit (editable-store) with the dated current-state block | | workaround-vs-plan | two entries asserting contradictory current facts, neither referencing the other | workaround-vs-plan | append (repo-store) when one is repo `MEMORY.md`; edit when both editable | | dangling `[[link]]` | a `[[some-slug]]` reference whose target does not exist | dangling-link | edit (either store) | | append-only violation | an in-place edit to an existing repo `MEMORY.md` entry (detected via git diff) | append-only-violation | MADR route (room: `call/`); the violation is recorded, not auto-repaired | | room-touching finding | a memory that references a `call/0017` decision since superseded by the spine | room-touching | MADR route (room: `call/`); name the record, do not edit | </code></pre> <h3 id="results-1"><a class="header" href="#results-1">Results</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Detector</th><th>Temp 0.2</th><th>Temp 0.6</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>description-vs-body drift</td><td>A (PASS)</td><td>C (PASS)</td><td>clear at the 4B bar</td></tr> <tr><td>superseded-but-unlinked</td><td>A (PASS)</td><td>C (PASS)</td><td>clear at the 4B bar</td></tr> <tr><td>append-only violation</td><td>C (FAIL, picked stale-state-over-lore)</td><td>A (FAIL, picked stale-state-over-lore)</td><td>conflated</td></tr> <tr><td>room-touching</td><td>D (FAIL, picked superseded-but-unlinked)</td><td>B (FAIL, picked dangling-link)</td><td>conflated</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>(Option order rotated between the two temps; PASS at both means the verdict is content reasoning, not position. See the run log for the full transcript.)</p> <p><strong>The honest finding:</strong> 2 of 4 detectors read clearly at the weak-agent bar; 2 do not. The model consistently reads an in-place edit to a date-stamped entry as "stale state over lore" rather than "append-only violation", and consistently reads a memory citing a superseded <code>call/</code> decision as "superseded-but-unlinked" rather than "room-touching". The simpler detectors (drift, supersession) are clear; the methodology-discipline ones are not.</p> <p><strong>Implication for the design (feeds back into the README):</strong> the detector naming or framing needs sharpening before the build. Three concrete options the cast consultation and adversarial review should rule on:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Rename.</strong> <code>append-only-violation</code> reads to a 4B as "the entry is stale"; it is actually "the entry was hand-edited in violation of the append-only rule". A name like <code>append-only-edit-detected</code> (a mechanical observation, not a state description) might separate it from the state-vs-lore frame. Similarly <code>room-touching</code> reads as "it touches a room"; the model defaults to the closer-sounding class. Renaming to <code>madar-route-required</code> (the routing decision, not the symptom) might help.</li> <li><strong>Lean on routing, not class.</strong> The load-bearing question for the operator is "what do I do with this finding" (the route), not the class name. Routing may be the better weak-agent surface: "this finding wants an append / an edit / a MADR record" is more actionable than "this is an append-only violation".</li> <li><strong>Accept partial detector coverage at the 4B bar.</strong> Some detectors are inherently review-grade (the append-only violation requires git-diff evidence; the room-touching requires reading the room). The probe documents which detectors are weak-agent-clear and which require the operator's eye, mirroring the honest-tier enforcement in plan/0072.</li> </ol> <p>The build does not start until this is resolved.</p> <h2 id="run-log"><a class="header" href="#run-log">Run log</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-07-19</li> <li><strong>Model:</strong> <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code> (Fen, Q8_0)</li> <li><strong>Channel:</strong> Unsloth direct, <code>http://api.d07yx58.net:8888/v1</code>, via <code>~/.local/bin/fen-probe</code> (token at <code>~/.unsloth-api-d07yx58-net</code>).</li> <li><strong>Agentic params:</strong> <code>temperature</code> 0.2 and 0.6 (option order rotated between them), <code>top_p</code> 0.8, <code>enable_thinking</code> false, <code>max_tokens</code> 600.</li> <li><strong>Probe script:</strong> <code>/tmp/plan0073-probe.sh</code> (idempotent; reproduces the matrix above; writes one line per (detector, temp) with the model letter and a PASS / FAIL verdict).</li> </ul> <h3 id="transcript-excerpts"><a class="header" href="#transcript-excerpts">Transcript excerpts</a></h3> <p>The model's reasoning (reproduced here so the verdicts are auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>drift, temp 0.2 (PASS, A):</strong> "The entry contains a contradiction between the description ('build in /tmp') and the body text ('build on /opt/models xfs'). … ANSWER: A".</li> <li><strong>superseded, temp 0.6 (PASS, C):</strong> "entry A from June 2026 recommends keeping f16 KV, while entry B from July 2026 states that q8 KV is unblocked and beats f16. … However, there is no explicit link connecting A to B … ANSWER: C".</li> <li><strong>append-violation, temp 0.2 (FAIL, picked stale-state-over-lore):</strong> "the entry describes a situation where a memory record was edited in place … the date field itself was not updated to reflect the new edit … This aligns with the concept of 'stale-state-over-lore'". The model reads the date mismatch as state staleness, not as an append-only violation.</li> <li><strong>room-touching, temp 0.2 (FAIL, picked superseded-but-unlinked):</strong> "the old rule is still being cited as a 'live rule'. This indicates that the old entry has not been properly retired or linked as obsolete … ANSWER: D (superseded-but-unlinked)". The model collapses the room-routing case into the closer-named detector.</li> </ul> <h3 id="reproducibility"><a class="header" href="#reproducibility">Reproducibility</a></h3> <pre><code class="language-sh"># From a host with the fen-probe script on PATH and the Unsloth token at # ~/.unsloth-api-d07yx58-net: bash /tmp/plan0073-probe.sh </code></pre> <p>Latency: ~1 s per call at temp 0.2; ~1.5 s at temp 0.6. Total run ~10 s.</p> <h2 id="non-overlap-confirmation-dream-vs-upgrade-2026-07-19"><a class="header" href="#non-overlap-confirmation-dream-vs-upgrade-2026-07-19">Non-overlap confirmation: dream vs upgrade (2026-07-19)</a></h2> <p>The operator raised the discipline concern: dream must not proxy for upgrade. The two tools have non-overlapping surfaces (dream = memory; upgrade = template revisions + applied set). Confirmation from two angles.</p> <h3 id="modeling-formal-disjointness"><a class="header" href="#modeling-formal-disjointness">Modeling (formal disjointness)</a></h3> <p>Cross-reference lint of the dream spec (<code>software/host-lifecycle/main/host-lifecycle-dream.allium</code>) for upgrade -surface tokens:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">grep -nE "upgrade|applied|baseline|ledger|host-receipts|host-lifecycle-receipts|host-task-receipts" \ software/host-lifecycle/main/host-lifecycle-dream.allium </code></pre> <p>Two hits, both in the explicit non-overlap comment (lines 31, 33): the comment that documents the discipline. None in entities or rules. Every entity in the spec is memory-domain (<code>MemoryStore</code>, <code>MemoryEntry</code>, <code>LinkRef</code>, <code>Finding</code>, <code>Suggestion</code>, <code>Dream</code>, <code>MemoryWrite</code>); no applied-set, baseline, or receipt-ledger entities appear. Formal disjointness confirmed by inspection.</p> <h3 id="ergonomic-weak-agent-routing-probe"><a class="header" href="#ergonomic-weak-agent-routing-probe">Ergonomic (weak-agent routing probe)</a></h3> <p>A second Fen probe (<code>/tmp/plan0073-routing-probe.sh</code>, same model and channel as the detector-class probe) over six scenarios: three memory-staleness (the correct tool is dream) and three spine-revision (the correct tool is upgrade). Two temperatures, option order rotated.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Scenario group</th><th>temp 0.2</th><th>temp 0.6</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Memory -> dream (3 scenarios)</td><td>3/3 routed correctly</td><td>3/3 routed correctly</td></tr> <tr><td>Spine -> upgrade (3 scenarios)</td><td>3/3 routed correctly (prose-form)</td><td>2/3 routed correctly</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>11 of 12 routed correctly. The one "fail" is <code>spine-tool-bump</code> (a new ledger entry requires host-lifecycle v0.41.0 but the project pins v0.40.1): genuinely ambiguous, because the memory entry about the version is stale and the project needs an upgrade. The model picked the memory reading at temp 0.6. The scenario conflates the two surfaces itself; the design does not. The temp 0.2 spine rows did not always emit the demanded <code>ANSWER: X</code> line; the prose answer routed correctly in every case.</p> <h3 id="verdict-5"><a class="header" href="#verdict-5">Verdict</a></h3> <p>Non-overlap holds: confirmed formally (spec disjointness) and at the weak-agent bar (routing). The cast-consult and adversarial-review tasks already in the build sequence will sharpen the spine docs and the SKILL.md trigger conditions; the spec's <code>Route</code> enum simplifies to <code>{edit, append}</code> (no <code>madar</code>), since dream never proposes a MADR action.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><p>The file write wasn't permitted, so I'll deliver the review here in full. (The empty <code>spec-review-fable.md</code> placeholder is still there if you want me to write this into it later — say the word and grant the write.)</p> <p>One note on provenance before the findings: the spec text you pasted matches <code>software/host-lifecycle/main/host-lifecycle-dream.allium</code> in the materialized worktree line-for-line (286 lines), so all line numbers below cite that file. I also cross-checked the plan records: the non-overlap confirmation in <code>plan/0073-host-lifecycle-dream/gather-data.md</code> ends with "the spec's <code>Route</code> enum simplifies to <code>{edit, append}</code> (no <code>madar</code>), since dream never proposes a MADR action" — which is decisive for several findings below.</p> <p><strong>Headline: the spec cannot pass its own write-spec gate as it stands.</strong> Two rules emit <code>route: madar</code> (lines 174, 183), a value the <code>Route</code> enum does not contain — and per the recorded non-overlap ruling, must not contain. Independently, <code>DetectDanglingLink</code> (162–166) violates <code>RepoFindingsNeverEdit</code>, and <code>DreamIsReadOnly</code> is falsified by every run that records a finding.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="1-the-five-invariants-soundness-and-completeness"><a class="header" href="#1-the-five-invariants-soundness-and-completeness">1. The five invariants: soundness and completeness</a></h2> <p><strong><code>DreamIsReadOnly</code> (251–254) — unsound, and not about read-only-ness.</strong> The expression says "if <code>saw_finding</code> then the status is terminal." Two defects. First, it is violated in every reachable run with at least one finding: <code>RecordFinding</code> (204–207) sets <code>saw_finding = true</code> while <code>status</code> is still <code>dreaming</code>, and <code>DreamCompletes</code> is a separate external stimulus that arrives later. The state between the first finding and the verdict falsifies the disjunction — and that state is quiescent (the detector cascade has settled), so it fails under any invariant-checking granularity. Second, it <em>accepts</em> the actually dangerous state: a <code>Finding</code> created after a <code>clean</code> verdict (nothing guards <code>RecordFinding</code> on <code>dream.status = dreaming</code>) yields <code>saw_finding = true, status = clean</code> — a verdict that lied — and the third disjunct makes the invariant hold there. It rejects the benign mid-scan state and blesses the harmful one. The prose property (247–250: the audit never mutates; all writes come from the MCP surface) is not encoded anywhere and cannot be in the current model: <code>MemoryWrite</code> (228–231) has no origin/caller attribution, so "the audit never writes" is a frame condition with no state to check. Fix: add <code>origin: audit | mcp_tool | consolidation</code> to <code>MemoryWrite</code>, assert <code>for w in MemoryWrites: w.origin != audit</code>, and delete or rename the current expression.</p> <p><strong><code>RepoStoreAppendOnly</code> (260–263) — sound, but narrower than its name.</strong> It is discharged by <code>MemoryWriteRefusesRepo</code> (233–237), and what it encodes is "the MCP tool refuses every repo write" — the repo store is MCP-<em>read-only</em>, not append-only. The actual append-only property (an existing entry's text never changes) has no state to range over: the spec has no entry-mutation action; <code>is_append_only_violation</code> (60) is an observation input from the analysis pass, not a modeled write. Acceptable at this altitude (the mutation surface is git, out of scope), but the name over-claims what is proved.</p> <p><strong><code>FixNeverTouchesRepo</code> (268–271) — sound, leaning on an unstated binding.</strong> It quantifies over <code>s.target_store</code>, a <em>copy</em> denormalized by <code>ScopeSuggestion</code> (193). It holds today only because <code>ScopeSuggestion</code> is the sole Suggestion creator and copies faithfully. Nothing asserts <code>s.target_store = s.finding.entry.store</code>, so a future Suggestion creator (the consolidate path is the obvious candidate) that mis-copies <code>target_store</code> bypasses the repo protection while this invariant stays green. See M3 below.</p> <p><strong><code>RepoFindingsNeverEdit</code> (276–279) — the property is right; the spec violates it.</strong> <code>DetectDanglingLink</code> (162–166) has no store guard and emits <code>route: edit</code> unconditionally. Counterexample in three steps: a <code>MemoryEntry</code> with <code>store.loc = repo</code>; a <code>LinkRef</code> with that entry as <code>src</code> and <code>resolves = false</code>; the rule creates a Finding with a repo-store entry and <code>route = edit</code>. <code>allium analyse</code> should surface exactly this trace. The comment at 161 ("editable on either store") asserts the violation as intent, contradicting both the <code>Route</code> comment (29–30) and CLAUDE.md section 6. Fix: split by store — per_user → edit, repo → append (a suggested correcting entry with the forward <code>[[link]]</code>).</p> <p><strong><code>EveryFindingHasARoute</code> (283–286) — vacuous.</strong> <code>Finding.route</code> is typed <code>Route</code> (76) and <code>Route</code> = {edit, append} (36–39), so the disjunction is a tautology the type system already guarantees; it can never fail and does no analytic work. The defect it presumably targets — the <code>madar</code> emissions — is a checker-level failure caught before any invariant runs (<code>madar</code> resolves to neither a binding nor a <code>Route</code> literal). And if <code>Route</code> ever legitimately grew a member, this invariant would start rejecting it: it hardcodes the enum's contents a second time. Delete it, or re-aim it at something the type system cannot see (M2).</p> <p><strong>Missing invariants:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>M1 — <code>VerdictMatchesFindings</code>.</strong> Prose line 6: "settles to exactly one terminal verdict: clean (0) or findings (1)" — the exit code is the tool's entire contract, and nothing encodes <code>d.status = clean implies not d.saw_finding</code>. It is also not provable today: (a) <code>saw_finding</code> is never initialized — <code>StartDream</code> (199–202) sets only <code>status</code>, so a run may begin with a stale latch and report <code>findings</code> on a clean store; (b) <code>RecordFinding</code> lacks a dreaming-guard, so a late Finding flips the latch under a settled <code>clean</code> verdict. Fix: <code>StartDream</code> also ensures <code>saw_finding = false</code>; guard <code>RecordFinding</code>; add the invariant.</li> <li><strong>M2 — Detector completeness.</strong> Prose lines 3–5 promise both stores are scanned for staleness, contradictions, drift. The rule set silently drops two repo cases: <code>is_stale_state</code> and <code>is_workaround_not_plan</code> fire only for <code>per_user</code> (149–159). A stale repo entry produces no Finding, no route, exit 0 — and no invariant notices, because nothing connects a raised precondition flag to Finding existence. Add per-detector completeness invariants (<code>for e in MemoryEntries where e.is_stale_state: exists f in Findings where f.entry = e</code>).</li> <li><strong>M3 — <code>SuggestionTargetsItsFinding</code></strong>: <code>for s in Suggestions: s.target_store = s.finding.entry.store</code>. Without it, <code>FixNeverTouchesRepo</code> protects a copy, not the store the fix actually hits.</li> <li><strong>M4 — Audit-never-writes.</strong> The real content of <code>DreamIsReadOnly</code>; needs <code>MemoryWrite.origin</code> first. Until then, "read-only" (6–7, 247) is asserted nowhere in the model.</li> <li><strong>M5 (minor) — acceptance biconditional</strong> <code>w.accepted iff w.target_store.loc = per_user</code>. The invariant set encodes only the refuse direction; the accept direction exists only as rule <code>MemoryWriteAcceptsPerUser</code> (239–243), so a regression there — or a third <code>StoreLoc</code> later — is invisible.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2-paired-detectors-vs-post-creation-route-rewrite"><a class="header" href="#2-paired-detectors-vs-post-creation-route-rewrite">2. Paired detectors vs post-creation route rewrite</a></h2> <p><strong>Creation-time routing is the right call; the pairing is the weaker of the two creation-time encodings.</strong></p> <p>Why creation-time beats a rewrite rule: Allium invariants are state assertions with no temporal operators. A rewrite rule (<code>when: f: Finding.created, requires: repo and route = edit, ensures: f.route = append</code>) manufactures a transient state where <code>RepoFindingsNeverEdit</code> is false; the invariant would have to be weakened to settled states only — exactly the "eventually correct" shape the language cannot check cleanly, and which the stale comment at 273–274 still half-describes. There is also a rule-ordering race: <code>ScopeSuggestion</code> fires on the same <code>Finding.created</code> trigger (191–195), and with a rewrite rule in play, whether a Suggestion is scoped before or after the route settles is unspecified. Creation-time routing removes the race class rather than adjudicating it, and keeps every invariant inductive (check each creation rule once) instead of forcing the analyser to reason about interleavings.</p> <p>The cost — demonstrated in this very spec — is that pairing turns store-coverage into a by-hand exhaustiveness obligation with no checker backstop. Three of six detectors have already drifted: stale-state and workaround-vs-plan lost their repo halves (149–159), and dangling-link (162–166) skipped pairing entirely and broke the invariant. Nothing forces "per detector, the per_user and repo <code>requires</code> are jointly exhaustive."</p> <p>Recommended encoding — same semantics, half the rules, no silent-drop failure mode. Allium ensures blocks compose with <code>if</code>/<code>else</code>:</p> <pre><code>rule DetectDescriptionBodyDrift { when: entry: MemoryEntry.created requires: entry.has_description_body_drift ensures: if entry.store.loc = per_user: Finding.created(entry: entry, kind: "description-body-drift", route: edit) else: Finding.created(entry: entry, kind: "description-body-drift", route: append) } </code></pre> <p>One <code>requires</code> per detector means the store split cannot eat a case; routing stays creation-time; <code>RepoFindingsNeverEdit</code> stays inductive. If the pairs are kept instead, add the M2 completeness invariants so a missing half is a caught defect rather than a silent coverage hole. Either way, delete the sentence at 122–123 ("The route emitted here is the detector's <em>default</em>; the invariant below constrains the actual verdict") — it documents the rejected rewrite design, and spec comments are contract prose.</p> <h2 id="3-mcp-surface-gaps"><a class="header" href="#3-mcp-surface-gaps">3. MCP-surface gaps</a></h2> <p><code>MemoryWrite</code> is two fields (228–231): a store pointer and an accept bit. Everything below is invisible to it.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Update vs create — missing.</strong> No operation kind, no target entry. Risk: the end-to-end property the plan exists for — "consolidation applies finding F's suggested edit to entry E" — is unstatable; a consolidation that writes the right store but the wrong entry, or creates a duplicate instead of editing, satisfies every invariant. Deletion is real on the per-user store (consolidation prunes), and deleting an entry that others <code>[[link]]</code> to manufactures dangling links — the audit's own defect class; no invariant says a fix does not create findings. Minimum: <code>op: create | update | delete</code>, <code>entry: MemoryEntry?</code>, and a rule tying an applied Suggestion to the write that discharges it.</li> <li><strong>Idempotency — missing.</strong> No request identity, no at-most-once tie to a Suggestion. Risk: an MCP transport retry or harness re-invocation double-applies; for append-shaped writes that means duplicate entries, which the next dream flags as contradiction/drift — the fixer becomes a finding generator. Cheap fix: <code>write.suggestion: Suggestion?</code> plus "at most one accepted write per suggestion."</li> <li><strong><code>memory_consolidate</code> — absent entirely.</strong> It exists only in the comment at 225–227 ("calls memory_write on the per-user store only") — the strongest safety claim on the mutation side, and it is a frame condition with no state behind it. Risk: nothing constrains a consolidation to apply only Suggestions with <code>applies = true</code>; a consolidation writing arbitrary content, or "fixing" a repo-store finding by writing a shadow copy into the per-user store (accepted — it is per_user), is fully invariant-clean. Also unmodeled: whether consolidate re-runs the detectors, and which Dream run's Suggestion set it consumes.</li> <li><strong>Concurrency / atomicity — unmodeled.</strong> (i) TOCTOU verdict staleness: a write lands between the analysis pass populating the precondition booleans (47–51) and <code>DreamCompletes</code>; the verdict describes a store that no longer exists. Tolerable for an advisory tool, but say it — a <code>@guarantee</code> on <code>DreamRun</code> scoping the verdict to a snapshot. (ii) In fix mode, the Suggestion's verbatim text (79) was computed against content a concurrent write may have changed; <code>MemoryWrite</code> has no expected-version field, so compare-and-swap is inexpressible and lost updates are unmodeled. (iii) A multi-write consolidation (edit A + append B) has no transaction; partial application can leave A's new <code>[[link]]</code> pointing at a B never created.</li> <li><strong>Partial failure — <code>accepted</code> conflates authorization with effect.</strong> The per-user store is physically two writes (entry file + <code>MEMORY.md</code> index line); a crash between them is index/entry divergence — adjacent to the drift class the audit detects, and the index-points-at-missing-file case is a dangling reference <code>LinkRef</code> cannot even represent (it models entry-to-entry links only, 64–65). Risk: <code>accepted = true</code> reported over a half-applied write. Minimum: split <code>accepted</code> (policy) from <code>completed</code> (durable effect) and hang the guarantees off <code>completed</code>.</li> </ul> <p>One deliberate gap worth a line in the spec: no modeled actor can execute an <code>append</code>-routed repo suggestion — memory_write refuses the store and <code>applies</code> is pinned false. The executor is the operator via a linted git commit, outside the model. State that next to the <code>Route</code> enum, or a reader will hunt for the missing repo-append path and conclude the spec is incomplete rather than advisory.</p> <h2 id="4-reviewer-raised-findings"><a class="header" href="#4-reviewer-raised-findings">4. Reviewer-raised findings</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>F1 — <code>route: madar</code> (174, 183) does not exist, and must not.</strong> <code>madar</code> resolves to neither a binding nor a <code>Route</code> literal, so <code>allium check</code> cannot exit 0 — the plan's write-spec gate ("check + analyse exit 0, zero findings") fails before analysis begins. This is not merely a typo for "madr": the non-overlap verdict in gather-data.md explicitly retired it. The enum and its comment (26–35) carry the post-confirmation design; the two rules and the header (line 5: "edit / append / MADR") still carry the pre-confirmation design from the gather-data detector table. The spec is caught mid-migration, self-inconsistent in exactly the direction the non-overlap ruling closes off. Under the confirmed decision: append-only-violation → <code>append</code> (repo; the suggested correcting entry — matching CLAUDE.md section 6's own convention that corrections are new entries); room-touching → store-split like the others (per_user → edit, repo → append), naming the superseded room record as <em>context in the finding text</em>, never as a route. <code>DetectRoomTouching</code> (180–184) also needs the store guard it currently lacks.</li> <li><strong>F2 — the run lifecycle cannot be re-entered, and the graph knows it.</strong> The transition graph (94–98) is authoritative in Allium 3 — rules producing transitions outside it are validation errors — and it has no <code>-> dreaming</code> edge. <code>StartDream</code> (199–202) carries no <code>requires</code>, so it can produce <code>clean -> dreaming</code> on a second <code>DreamStarts</code> (the surface's <code>provides</code> has no when-guard, 105–110): at minimum a checker question, likely a validation error. Combined with <code>saw_finding</code> never being initialized or reset, the model supports exactly one run per universe without saying so. Either declare single-shot (guard <code>DreamStarts</code>) or add re-run edges plus the <code>saw_finding = false</code> reset. Related: <code>Finding</code> has no reference to its Dream (73–77), so under any multi-run reading, verdicts bleed across runs through the single given <code>dream</code>.</li> <li><strong>F3 — stale identifier in a comment.</strong> Line 121 names "RouteRepoFindingsNeverEdit"; the invariant is <code>RepoFindingsNeverEdit</code> (276). A dangling name reference — in the spec whose flagship detector is dangling links.</li> <li><strong>F4 — <code>Finding.kind</code> is a String (75).</strong> The six kind names are convention, not checked; a typo'd kind in a future rule is invisible, and completeness invariants cannot quantify per kind. An open String may be deliberate while detector naming is under cast review (13–15), but once naming settles it should become an enum.</li> <li><strong>F5 — <code>fix_mode</code> (93) is never assigned.</strong> As an unbound input, the analyser may flip it mid-run between Finding creations, scoping some suggestions applicable and others not within one run. It is a per-run CLI flag: bind it at <code>DreamStarts</code>.</li> <li><strong>F6 — no failure verdict.</strong> <code>status: dreaming | clean | findings</code> (91) gives a crashed scan (unreadable store, malformed entry) no modeled outcome, while the header pins the exit contract to 0/1. CLI strings are out of scope, but the verdict machine is in scope; an <code>error</code> terminal keeps <code>findings</code> from becoming the dumping ground for "crashed."</li> <li><strong>F7 — cross-store links unmodeled.</strong> LinkRef resolution is defined same-store (64–65). If <code>[[slug]]</code>s may cross stores — and the per-user tier's value is precisely that it references repo lore — same-store resolution makes every cross-store link a false-positive dangling-link finding. Either record "links are same-store by format definition" as a spine/format decision, or resolve across both stores.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Priority order:</strong> (1) F1 — fails the gate and contradicts the recorded ruling; (2) the <code>DetectDanglingLink</code> store split — an analyser-findable invariant violation; (3) <code>DreamIsReadOnly</code> → replace with M4 (needs <code>MemoryWrite.origin</code>) and add M1 with the <code>saw_finding</code> init/guard fixes; (4) M2 completeness, ideally via the single-rule <code>if</code>/<code>else</code> encoding; (5) the MCP-surface gaps (op/entry, consolidate as a modeled Suggestion consumer, accepted vs completed); (6) comment hygiene (F3, 122–123, line 5) — cheap, and in a spec, comments are contract prose.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="weed-and-tend-for-plan0073-2026-07-19"><a class="header" href="#weed-and-tend-for-plan0073-2026-07-19">weed-and-tend for plan/0073 (2026-07-19)</a></h1> <p>The lifecycle gap (operator catch): weed and tend were skipped between implement-dream and write-tests. Per MEMORY plan/0015, weed is the spec↔code alignment check that catches hand-authored spec drift the implementation passes clean on (the host-lint <code>DetectInternalCodeAsName</code> flag-vs-warn bug is the precedent). The fable review caught the spec's INTERNAL inconsistencies but could not see spec↔code drift.</p> <h2 id="weed-check-enumerated-divergences"><a class="header" href="#weed-check-enumerated-divergences">weed check: enumerated divergences</a></h2> <p>Grouped by spec construct. The dangling-link detector uses a <code>known_slugs: &BTreeSet<String></code> resolver against the store; it does not materialise LinkRef entities.</li> <li>Classification: <strong>spec-bug.</strong> The entity adds modelling weight without easing the analyser; a boolean field <code>has_dangling_link</code> on MemoryEntry is the same shape as the other detector preconditions. The repo store is read-only in dream by construction.</li> <li>Classification: <strong>spec-bug for the current scope.</strong> The invariants reference the removed MemoryWrite type. The dream-side property is enforced by the <code>--fix</code> exit code; the MCP/consolidation property lands at #extend-mcp.</li> </ul> <h4 id="acceptancebiconditional--completedimpliesaccepted--idempotentsuggestiondischarge"><a class="header" href="#acceptancebiconditional--completedimpliesaccepted--idempotentsuggestiondischarge">AcceptanceBiconditional / CompletedImpliesAccepted / IdempotentSuggestionDischarge</a></h4> <ul> <li>Spec: keys on MemoryWrite.</li> <li>Code: <strong>absent.</strong></li> <li>Classification: <strong>spec-bug for the current scope; aspirational.</strong> Tend action: remove; restore at #extend-mcp.</li> </ul> <h4 id="repofindingsneveredit"><a class="header" href="#repofindingsneveredit">RepoFindingsNeverEdit</a></h4> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>for f in Findings where f.entry.store.loc = repo: f.route != edit</code>.</li> <li>Code: enforced by <code>DetectorInput::route_for(StoreLoc::Repo) == Route::Append</code>.</li> <li>Classification: <strong>intentional</strong> (aligned; load-bearing, Kani-provable).
