<code>Finding.dream</code> field</td><td>remove from spec; restore at #extend-mcp with the MCP surface</td></tr> <tr><td>(b) code catches up</td><td>DetectStaleStateOverLore, DetectWorkaroundVsPlan, DetectAppendOnlyViolation</td><td>keep in spec; record for #implement-remaining</td></tr> <tr><td>(c) intentional gap</td><td>Dream entity (conceptual model vs procedural code); MemoryEntry precondition booleans (spec-stored vs code-computed); MemoryStore.loc vs .dir; Finding field naming (modulo the dropped <code>dream</code>)</td><td>no change</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="post-tend-spec-shape"><a class="header" href="#post-tend-spec-shape">Post-tend spec shape</a></h2> <ul> <li>2 enums (StoreLoc, Route) — MemoryWriteOp and MemoryWriteOrigin removed.</li> <li>5 entities (MemoryStore, MemoryEntry, Finding, Dream, Project) — LinkRef, Suggestion, MemoryWrite removed.</li> <li>7 detector rules — all kept (3 are bucket-b for #implement-remaining).</li> <li>DetectDanglingLink rephrased to key on <code>MemoryEntry.has_dangling_link</code> (the field already exists) instead of LinkRef.</li> <li>5 verdict-lifecycle rules (StartDream, RecordFinding, VerdictFindings, VerdictClean, VerdictError) — unchanged.</li> <li>2 invariants (RepoFindingsNeverEdit, VerdictMatchesFindings) — the MemoryWrite/Suggestion-flavoured ones removed.</li> </ul> <h2 id="post-tend-manifest-shape"><a class="header" href="#post-tend-manifest-shape">Post-tend manifest shape</a></h2> <p>The MemoryWrite/Suggestion-flavoured obligation IDs disappear (those constructs are gone from the spec). The deferred-detector obligations stay, dispositioned <code>waived: pending #implement-remaining</code> (the tests land with the implementation, not ahead of it). The remaining structural + detector + verdict + invariant obligations keep their <code>test:</code> / <code>structural</code> dispositions; the <code>test:</code> names are still forward refs until #write-tests.</p> <h2 id="verification-42"><a class="header" href="#verification-42">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>allium check host-lifecycle-dream.allium</code> rc=0, zero errors / warnings.</li> <li><code>allium analyse host-lifecycle-dream.allium</code> rc=0.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle obligations host-lifecycle-dream.allium --tests src</code> rc=0, zero STALE entries (every disposition's obligation ID still exists in the trimmed spec).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0074-formal-materialization-provenance-coherence-bootstrap-and-completeness-for-the-where-room"><a class="header" href="#plan0074-formal-materialization-provenance-coherence-bootstrap-and-completeness-for-the-where-room">plan/0074 formal materialization: provenance, coherence, bootstrap, and completeness for the Where room</a></h1> <p>Closes <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/18">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#18</a> and <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/19">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#19</a>, plus <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/20">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#20</a> for the formal bootstrap and completeness gate (filed at #gather-data). Paired by operator ruling (2026-07-19), then broadened by operator ruling (2026-07-20): the receipt, the envhash, the bootstrap orchestrator, and the completeness gate all share the same materialize / install-hooks call sites and the same Where-room state, so building them together under one explicit non-overlap discipline avoids the duplication that separate plans would risk.</p> <h2 id="why-11"><a class="header" href="#why-11">Why</a></h2> <p>The fresh-clone materialization of an agentic project is currently unmechanized prose. The spine (host-template CLAUDE.md) and this host's CLAUDE.md describe a sequence of manual steps an agent hand-executes in order: seed the materializer, init submodules, <code>software --materialize</code>, link skills, build the gating binary, <code>--install-hooks</code>, install the PATH re-derivers, then <code>software --check</code>. Prose is not a gate. Steps get skipped silently, and nothing catches it.</p> <p>The evidence is this repository. During the 2026-07-20 session the host-repo commit hooks were found absent: <code>--install-hooks</code> had never been run in the clone, and <code>software --check</code> stayed green the whole time, because it verifies pins and receipts but is blind to whether the local environment was actually set up. Four gaps, one root (materialization is realized but neither driven nor verified as a whole):</p> <ul> <li><strong>#18 (provenance).</strong> After a clone plus materialize, an operator cannot tell from the audit trail when, where, or by whom the worktrees were last realized, even though the gating binary they then trust was produced by that materialization.</li> <li><strong>#19 (coherence).</strong> After a repo move, a partial <code>submodule</code> re-init, an image bump, or an ambient rebuild of the gating binary, the local tree differs from what the operator last touched, with no signal that it moved.</li> <li><strong>Bootstrap (new).</strong> There is no single entrypoint that RUNS the fresh-clone sequence. Each step is prose an agent executes by hand, so a step is skipped and the tree is silently half-materialized.</li> <li><strong>Completeness (new).</strong> There is no gate that asserts the setup COMPLETED. <code>software --check</code> passes on a clone whose hooks were never installed, whose PATH re-derivers are absent, or whose skills are unlinked. A companion bug: <code>--install-hooks</code> gates only the host repo, leaving every materialized worktree (a real commit surface) with no local tell-gate.</li> </ul> <h2 id="scope-3"><a class="header" href="#scope-3">Scope</a></h2> <p>Four host-lifecycle concerns, one release, one non-overlap discipline:</p> <ol> <li><strong>The materialize receipt (#18).</strong> An operational receipt in <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> written on <code>software --materialize</code> (and on a recorded <code>git submodule update</code> / checkout that touches the Where room), in the same append-only shape as the <code>embed</code> receipt. Records the EVENT.</li> <li><strong>The environment hash (#19).</strong> A gitignored <code>.host-envhash</code>, recomputed on demand, compared by <code>host-lifecycle env --check</code>. Records the recorded STATE; advisory, never fails the gate.</li> <li><strong>The bootstrap orchestrator (new).</strong> A thin, tracked <code>bootstrap.sh</code> that does only the self-seed (read the host-lifecycle pin from <code>.host-software</code>, <code>cargo install</code> it) then delegates to a new, generic, recipe-driven <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> subcommand that RUNS the rest of the sequence idempotently. Drives the sequence.</li> <li><strong>The completeness gate (new).</strong> A new <code>software --verify-setup</code> verify mode (name settled by the Fen probe, gather-data.md) that reads the RECIPE plus the live tree and HAZARDs when the setup is incomplete: a worktree unmaterialized, a hook uninstalled (host or worktree), a declared re-deriver off PATH, a skill unlinked, host-role-aware. Gates COMPLETENESS. Folds in the worktree-hook fix (Bug A): <code>--install-hooks</code> gates every materialized worktree, not just the host repo.</li> </ol> <h3 id="not-overfit-to-agentic-host-operator-ruling-2026-07-20"><a class="header" href="#not-overfit-to-agentic-host-operator-ruling-2026-07-20">Not overfit to agentic-host (operator ruling, 2026-07-20)</a></h3> <p><code>bootstrap</code> and the completeness gate are <strong>generic host-lifecycle capabilities driven by <code>.host-software</code></strong> and the declared rungs, and they serve any adopter with a materialized Where room. The one agentic-host-specific piece is the self-seed: because this host materializes <code>host-lifecycle</code> itself (the materializer cannot be served from what it materializes), its <code>bootstrap.sh</code> seeds host-lifecycle from the pin before delegating. A normal adopter installs a released host-lifecycle and runs <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> directly, with no self-seed wrapper. Nothing about agentic-host's component set, its musl target, or its host-prove rung is hardcoded; all of it comes from the recipe.</p> <h3 id="operator-rulings"><a class="header" href="#operator-rulings">Operator rulings</a></h3> <p><strong>2026-07-19 (original pair):</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong>Paired in one plan.</strong> The shared call sites are wired once.</li> <li><strong>Two distinct files.</strong> <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> (checked-in provenance) and <code>.host-envhash</code> (gitignored coherence). Never the same file.</li> <li><strong>Two distinct subcommands.</strong> The receipt writes via <code>software --materialize</code> (automatic); the envhash reads via <code>host-lifecycle env --check</code> (advisory, explicit).</li> <li><strong>Full methodology.</strong> Gather-data, cast consultation, adversarial review, then build.</li> </ol> <p><strong>2026-07-20 (the broadening):</strong> 5. <strong>Absorb the bootstrap and completeness gate into this plan.</strong> They share the materialize / install-hooks call sites and the Where-room state; building them here under one discipline avoids the third-feature duplication a separate plan would risk. 6. <strong>Thin script plus tool core.</strong> <code>bootstrap.sh</code> does only the self-seed; the mechanized sequence is a tested <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap</code> subcommand, not untested shell (the "one command, internalise for weak agents" idiom that folded host-prove's wrappers into its binary). 7. <strong>The completeness gate is a separate verify mode, not folded into <code>--check</code>.</strong> It reads the recipe-vs-live completeness question, distinct from the pin-vs-recorded question <code>--check</code> already answers and the state-vs-recorded question <code>env --check</code> answers. 8. <strong>Spine-aware, do not overfit.</strong> The bootstrap and completeness pattern is spine doctrine (every adopter with a Where room has this problem); agentic-host's self-seed is instance config. 9. <strong>Fen decides the names (settled).</strong> The Fen naming probe (gather-data.md) settled both, rotation-proof at both temperatures: the orchestrator is <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> and the completeness gate is <code>host-lifecycle software --verify-setup <dir></code>.</p> <h2 id="the-non-overlap-discipline-load-bearing-now-three-way"><a class="header" href="#the-non-overlap-discipline-load-bearing-now-three-way">The non-overlap discipline (load-bearing, now three-way)</a></h2> <p>Four concerns touch the same call sites and the same state. What keeps them from duplicating is that each answers a different question against a different reference point, and defers on every fact another owns:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>Question</th><th>Reference point</th><th>Result kind</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Receipt (#18)</td><td>What happened, by what authority, when?</td><td>the event</td><td>append-only provenance line</td></tr> <tr><td>Envhash (#19)</td><td>Did the tree drift from what I last recorded?</td><td><code>.host-envhash</code> (recorded state)</td><td>advisory delta, exit 0</td></tr> <tr><td>Completeness gate (new)</td><td>Is the setup complete per the recipe?</td><td><code>.host-software</code> (required state)</td><td>HAZARD / clean gate</td></tr> <tr><td>Bootstrap (new)</td><td>(does not verify) it MAKES the state</td><td>the recipe</td><td>side effects, then defers verification to the gate</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The event-vs-state field table (receipt vs envhash) stays exactly as designed:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Fact</th><th>Receipt (#18)</th><th>Envhash (#19)</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Materialization happened</td><td>yes (the event)</td><td>no</td></tr> <tr><td>Disposition (done/skip)</td><td>yes</td><td><strong>forbidden</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>Evidence (e.g. "git submodule update --init")</td><td>yes</td><td><strong>forbidden</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>Timestamp</td><td>yes</td><td><strong>forbidden</strong> (a digest has no time)</td></tr> <tr><td>Component realized</td><td>yes (by name)</td><td>yes (by worktree presence)</td></tr> <tr><td>Pin SHA</td><td><strong>reference only</strong></td><td><strong>never</strong> (pin adherence is <code>software --check</code>'s job)</td></tr> <tr><td>Toolchain image reference</td><td>yes</td><td>no</td></tr> <tr><td>Toolchain image digest</td><td><strong>never</strong></td><td>yes</td></tr> <tr><td>Hook binary hash</td><td><strong>never</strong></td><td>yes</td></tr> <tr><td>Repo abspath</td><td><strong>never</strong></td><td>yes</td></tr> <tr><td>Submodule init state</td><td><strong>never</strong></td><td>yes</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>And the completeness gate defers cleanly to all three: it never writes a receipt (it verifies, it does not act), never recomputes the envhash (it reads the recipe and the live tree, not the recorded fingerprint), and never checks pin adherence (that is <code>software --check</code>'s row). It owns exactly one question no other concern answers: <strong>is every required local artifact present?</strong></p> <h2 id="the-call-site-wiring"><a class="header" href="#the-call-site-wiring">The call-site wiring</a></h2> <p>Every state-changing op writes the receipt and/or the envhash, but the two record orthogonal facts:</p> <ul> <li><code>software --materialize</code>: writes a materialize receipt (event, components realized, pin-by-reference, image reference, timestamp) and writes <code>.host-envhash</code> (worktree paths, hook binary hash, image digest, submodule init state, repo abspath).</li> <li><code>software --install-hooks</code>: writes <code>.host-envhash</code> (new hook binary hash) and writes <strong>no</strong> receipt. Now gates the host repo AND every materialized worktree (Bug A).</li> <li><code>software --verify_build</code>: writes <code>.host-envhash</code> (image digest confirmed), no receipt.</li> <li>image pull: writes <code>.host-envhash</code> only.</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code>: calls the above ops in sequence, so the receipt and envhash are written by the ops it drives, not by bootstrap itself. Bootstrap adds no new writer.</li> </ul> <p><code>host-lifecycle env --check</code> recomputes the envhash from current state, diffs against the stored one, prints only the delta (advisory). The completeness gate recomputes required-vs-present from the recipe and HAZARDs on any gap. <code>software --check</code> reports the envhash state alongside the gate result, never as part of pass/fail; whether <code>--check</code> also runs the completeness gate, or the completeness gate stays a separate invocation, is a gather-data question.</p> <h2 id="the-bootstrap-sequence-generic-recipe-driven"><a class="header" href="#the-bootstrap-sequence-generic-recipe-driven">The bootstrap sequence (generic, recipe-driven)</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> runs, idempotently, whatever the recipe implies (each step a no-op if already satisfied):</p> <ol> <li><code>git submodule update --init</code> for the declared tool/template submodules (read from <code>.gitmodules</code>).</li> <li><code>software --materialize <dir></code> for every <code>.host-software</code> component (writes the receipt and envhash).</li> <li>link the skill symlinks (the generic form of this host's <code>link-skills.sh</code>).</li> <li>build each artifact-bearing component this host is a build host for, at its recorded target.</li> <li><code>software --install-hooks <dir></code> (host repo plus every worktree, Bug A).</li> <li>install each declared PATH re-deriver (a component the recipe or the declared rungs mark as needing PATH presence for the gate, plan/0048).</li> <li>run the completeness gate as the final self-check.</li> </ol> <p>The thin <code>bootstrap.sh</code> (this host only) does the self-seed alone, then <code>exec host-lifecycle bootstrap .</code>.</p> <h2 id="open-design-questions-3"><a class="header" href="#open-design-questions-3">Open design questions</a></h2> <p>The gather-data and cast pass rule on these:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The names (Fen probe, settled).</strong> Settled in gather-data.md, rotation-proof at both temperatures: <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> for the orchestrator (over setup / provision / realize; <code>materialize</code> is taken and is a subset) and <code>host-lifecycle software --verify-setup <dir></code> for the completeness gate (over <code>--verify-env</code> / <code>--verify-host</code>; "env" collides with the sibling <code>env</code> subcommand). Both read at the 4B bar as "runs the setup" and "checks the setup is complete", distinct from <code>materialize</code> (clone worktrees), <code>--check</code> (pins/receipts), and <code>env --check</code> (drift).</li> <li><strong>The receipt kind.</strong> #18's open question: its own kind vs re-opening the <code>embed</code> recheck. Our read is its own kind.</li> <li><strong>The envhash format.</strong> TOML (host-lifecycle's idiom) vs flat key:value.</li> <li><strong>The <code>env --check</code> exit code.</strong> Advisory: <code>0</code> clean, <code>0</code> with delta, <code>2</code> cannot-proceed (no envhash on disk).</li> <li><strong>The completeness-gate exit code.</strong> A gate: <code>0</code> complete, non-zero HAZARD on any missing required artifact (matching the <code>software --check</code> HAZARD convention), host-role-aware so a non-build host does not HAZARD on an absent build artifact.</li> <li><strong>Does <code>--check</code> run the completeness gate?</strong> Fold it into the existing gate sweep, or keep it a distinct invocation the bootstrap runs and an operator can run explicitly.</li> <li><strong>The image-digest probe.</strong> Reading the locally pulled image digest shells out to docker / podman inspect; with no runtime the envhash records "no runtime" and stays silent on the image dimension.</li> <li><strong>The spine change.</strong> #18 (receipt) and the bootstrap-plus-completeness doctrine are methodology-level. #19 (envhash) is tooling-only.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verification-43"><a class="header" href="#verification-43">Verification</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Unit tests</strong> for the receipt writer (every field, append-only, no-state-fields), the envhash writer (every dimension, per-input sub-hash, no-event-fields), the bootstrap step planner (each step derived from the recipe, each idempotent), and the completeness gate (each required-artifact class detected present and absent, host-role-aware).</li> <li><strong>Integration tests</strong> for the non-overlap discipline: a single <code>software --materialize</code> writes both files sharing no data field by name; the completeness gate writes neither. A test asserts the schema disjointness directly.</li> <li><strong>Integration tests</strong> for <code>env --check</code> (a move, a hook rebuild, a submodule toggle, a missing envhash each produce the expected advisory and exit 0) and for the completeness gate (an unmaterialized worktree, an uninstalled host hook, an uninstalled worktree hook, an off-PATH re-deriver, an unlinked skill each HAZARD; a fully bootstrapped tree is clean; a non-build host does not HAZARD on the absent build artifact).</li> <li><strong>Integration test</strong> for bootstrap: on a fixture missing hooks and skills, <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap</code> makes the completeness gate go clean, and a second run is a no-op.</li> <li><strong>Allium spec</strong> for the <code>MaterializeRun</code>, <code>EnvHash</code>, <code>BootstrapRun</code>, and <code>Completeness</code> entities, the no-overlap invariant (a <code>Reads</code> field on one is a <code>NeverReads</code> field on the others), the append-only receipt rule, and the worktree-hook coverage invariant (a materialized worktree implies an installed worktree hook after bootstrap). <code>allium check</code> + <code>analyse</code> + <code>plan</code> exit 0; obligations discharged by tests; Kani for the schema disjointness and the worktree-hook coverage invariants.</li> <li><strong>Fen probe</strong> (gather-data.md): the naming probe (above); the <code>env --check</code> delta reads as a route (which dimension moved); the completeness-gate HAZARD reads as "install the missing thing", not "your tree drifted"; the receipt, envhash, and completeness gate read as three different concerns, not three names for one.</li> <li><strong>Cast consultation</strong> (cast/*.md): Bly (overstates-completeness; the envhash is NOT an audit and the completeness gate is NOT provenance), Orin (fails-unsafe; a missing envhash is a prompt, the completeness gate is the actual gate, the bootstrap must be idempotent), Fen (weak-agent-trap; <code>env --check</code> must not read as a gate, and the completeness gate must not read as drift).</li> <li><strong>Adversarial design review</strong> (design-review.md): five independent lenses, with the duplication risk as a named lens (a reviewer whose sole job is to find overlap among receipt, envhash, and completeness gate) and the overfit risk as a named lens (a reviewer whose job is to find any agentic-host specific baked into the generic bootstrap or gate).</li> <li><code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> clean at the new pin; the host-lifecycle release receipt recorded; #18, #19, and #20 closed.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-16"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-16">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>The tasks are anchored receipted nodes (plan/0042), built as a forward graph:</p> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">gather-data</a></h3> <p>Grounds the conditionals: the Fen naming probe (bootstrap name, completeness-gate name), the receipt-kind question (#18), the envhash file format, the env-check and completeness-gate exit codes, whether <code>--check</code> runs the completeness gate, and the image-digest probe. Files the new issue (#20) for the bootstrap plus completeness gate.</p> <ul> <li>verify: every conditional in this README traces to a gather-data.md row; the Fen naming probe transcript is recorded</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">write-spec</a></h3> <p>The <code>MaterializeRun</code>, <code>EnvHash</code>, <code>BootstrapRun</code>, and <code>Completeness</code> Allium surface, the no-overlap invariant, the append-only receipt rule, the envhash-is-not-a-receipt rule, the completeness-gate-is-not-drift rule, and the worktree-hook coverage invariant. Lives in the host-lifecycle repo.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>allium check</code> + <code>allium analyse</code> exit 0, zero findings</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">write-obligations</a></h3> <p>Every <code>allium plan</code> obligation dispositioned in a <code><spec>.obligations</code> manifest. The schema-disjointness and worktree-hook-coverage obligations are Kani harnesses.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle obligations <spec> --tests tests --strict-discharge</code> clean</li> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> </ul> <p>The manifest landed with the spec (<code>host-lifecycle-materialize.obligations</code>, 5a1121c: 38 structural, 68 behavioural forward refs). Its receipt waits for #write-tests: the obligations gate reads a named test that does not yet exist as ABSENT, so a manifest of forward refs cannot discharge (at any strictness) until the tests it names are written. The node's deliverable exists; its verify becomes satisfiable at the end of the build.</p> <h3 id="implement-receipt"><a class="header" href="#implement-receipt">implement-receipt</a></h3> <p>The materialize receipt writer: a new entry in <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> on <code>software --materialize</code>, event-level fields only.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a materialize run appends exactly one receipt with no state-level data</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-envhash"><a class="header" href="#implement-envhash">implement-envhash</a></h3> <p>The envhash writer and the <code>env --check</code> reader: <code>.host-envhash</code> (gitignored), written by <code>--materialize</code> / <code>--install-hooks</code> / <code>--verify_build</code> / image pull, read by <code>env --check</code>. Per-input sub-hash; advisory exit codes.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; each state-changing op refreshes the envhash; <code>env --check</code> prints the delta and exits 0</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="fix-worktree-hooks"><a class="header" href="#fix-worktree-hooks">fix-worktree-hooks</a></h3> <p>Bug A: <code>software --install-hooks</code> gates every materialized worktree (the dispatch script plus the binary into each worktree's hooks dir), not just the host repo, gating on each worktree at its pin, host-role-aware.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; after <code>--install-hooks</code>, a tell-laden commit in a worktree is blocked; a fresh fixture's worktrees are all gated</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-completeness-gate"><a class="header" href="#implement-completeness-gate">implement-completeness-gate</a></h3> <p>The completeness gate <code>software --verify-setup</code>: reads the recipe plus the live tree, HAZARDs on any missing required artifact (worktree, host hook, worktree hook, PATH re-deriver, linked skill), host-role-aware. Writes nothing.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; each missing-artifact class HAZARDs; a bootstrapped tree is clean; a non-build host does not HAZARD on the absent build artifact</li> <li>depends: #fix-worktree-hooks, #implement-envhash</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-bootstrap"><a class="header" href="#implement-bootstrap">implement-bootstrap</a></h3> <p>The generic <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code> subcommand: the recipe-driven step planner running submodules / materialize / link-skills / build / install-hooks / install-re-derivers / <code>--verify-setup</code>, idempotently. The thin <code>bootstrap.sh</code> (this host) self-seeds then delegates.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; on a fixture missing hooks and skills, <code>bootstrap</code> makes the completeness gate clean; a second run is a no-op; <code>bootstrap.sh</code> seeds then delegates</li> <li>depends: #implement-completeness-gate</li> </ul> <h3 id="wire-shared-call-sites"><a class="header" href="#wire-shared-call-sites">wire-shared-call-sites</a></h3> <p>Wire <code>software --materialize</code> to write both files in one call; <code>--install-hooks</code> / <code>--verify_build</code> / image-pull to write <code>.host-envhash</code> only. Assert the call-site-level non-overlap: one call site, orthogonal writers, no shared data field; the completeness gate and bootstrap write no data files.</p> <ul> <li>verify: a <code>software --materialize</code> run produces both artifacts; <code>--install-hooks</code> produces only the envhash; a test asserts the wiring writes each file exactly when the design says to</li> <li>depends: #implement-receipt, #implement-bootstrap</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">write-tests</a></h3> <p>Integration tests covering every call site, every envhash dimension, every env-check delta path, every completeness-gate HAZARD class, the bootstrap idempotence, and the schema-disjointness and worktree-hook-coverage properties.</p> <ul> <li>verify: full test suite green; Kani proofs of schema disjointness and worktree-hook coverage</li> <li>depends: #wire-shared-call-sites</li> </ul> <h3 id="cast-consult"><a class="header" href="#cast-consult">cast-consult</a></h3> <p>Cast consultation across Mara, Wren, Bly, Orin, Fen on the three-way non-overlap discipline, the bootstrap idempotence, and the overfit boundary. Recorded in design-review.md.</p> <ul> <li>verify: each cast persona's concern addressed or recorded as a follow-up</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review">adversarial-review</a></h3> <p>A multi-lens adversarial review with one lens dedicated to overlap among receipt / envhash / completeness gate, and one lens dedicated to any agentic-host specific baked into the generic bootstrap or gate. Findings recorded in design-review.md; the re-cut staged there.</p> <ul> <li>verify: every blocking finding fixed or recorded; the re-cut executed</li> <li>depends: #cast-consult</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spine-doctrine"><a class="header" href="#write-spine-doctrine">write-spine-doctrine</a></h3> <p>The host-template CLAUDE.md gains the materialize-receipt doctrine (a fourth receipt kind), the bootstrap doctrine (a fresh clone runs <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code>, or a thin self-seed wrapper that delegates to it), and the completeness-gate doctrine (setup completeness is gated, not assumed). No spine doctrine for the envhash (tooling-only, local). An UPGRADING entry keys the new revision.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle upgrade</code> lists the entry on a pre-revision host; <code>upgrade --record</code> clears it</li> <li>depends: #adversarial-review</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">release-and-re-pin</a></h3> <p><code>host-lifecycle release host-lifecycle --change-class adds-flag</code>, re-pin <code>.host-software</code>, record the release receipt, close #18, #19, and #20.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> clean at the new pin; the issues closed</li> <li>depends: #write-spine-doctrine, #fen-acceptance</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">fen-acceptance</a></h3> <p>The real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> runs <code>env --check</code> on a moved repo and a rebuilt hook binary (the delta reads as a route), runs the completeness gate on a half-bootstrapped tree (the HAZARD reads as "install the missing thing"), and distinguishes the receipt, the envhash, and the completeness gate given a one-line description of each. Separately, it drives <code>bootstrap</code> on a fresh fixture and confirms the tree goes clean.</p> <ul> <li>verify: Fen routes each delta correctly, reads each HAZARD as an install action, distinguishes the three artifacts, and bootstraps a fixture clean</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <p>Re-cut 2026-07-23 (operator ruling): this node depended on #release-and-re-pin, which put the weak-agent acceptance downstream of the tag. The probes need a BUILT binary, not a released one, and plan/0076 had already shown why the distinction matters: its Fen pass ran twice, the second time only because the cast-acceptance fixes had reworded the very remedy strings the probe reads. An acceptance that cannot change what ships is a postscript, so both acceptances now gate the release instead of following it.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0074-design-review-the-cast-reads-the-built-diff"><a class="header" href="#plan0074-design-review-the-cast-reads-the-built-diff">plan/0074 design-review: the cast reads the built diff</a></h1> <p>Date: 2026-07-23. Subject: <code>fd7c632..d3848f2</code> in host-lifecycle (the materialize receipt, the environment fingerprint, the worktree gate fix, the completeness gate, the orchestrator, the test matrix and the proof).</p> <h2 id="who-read-it"><a class="header" href="#who-read-it">Who read it</a></h2> <p>Mara, Bly, Orin and Wren each read the plan README, the built diff and the sources their own lens calls for, and returned findings with file and line evidence. <strong>Fen was not simulated</strong>: <code>cast/fen.md</code> makes Fen a real model rather than a hypothetical, so Fen's consultation is the weak-agent acceptance recorded in <a href="plan/0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/fen-acceptance.html">fen-acceptance.md</a>, which ran the real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> against the built output and caught a real defect (the drift delta read as nothing-to-do). That probe is Fen's contribution to this review.</p> <h2 id="what-they-converged-on"><a class="header" href="#what-they-converged-on">What they converged on</a></h2> <p>Three findings arrived independently from more than one chair, and those are the ones that matter most.</p> <p><strong>The completeness gate fails open on any probe it cannot run.</strong> Bly (1, 3), Orin (1). <code>setup.rs</code> drops a requirement with <code>let Some(..) else { continue }</code> in three places: a hooks-declaring component with no artifact stanza, an unresolvable host hooks directory, an unresolvable worktree hooks directory. A requirement that is never constructed can never be a gap, and the run then prints "setup complete: every artifact the recipe requires of this host is present". Bly reproduced it on a fixture: the installer said it could gate nothing, and the gate said the setup was complete. This is the plan's own founding evidence (hooks absent for two weeks under a green check) reappearing inside the gate built to catch it.</p> <p><strong>The gate is blind to work the orchestrator performs.</strong> Bly (2), Orin (12), Wren (3). Bootstrap links skills from worktrees <em>and</em> submodules and inits submodules; the gate reads only worktree <code>skills/</code> directories and has no submodule requirement at all. On this repo the gate lists ten skill requirements while the tree carries twenty-seven links, and de-initializing every submodule leaves the gate clean. Wren found the sharper edge: <code>link-skills.sh</code> also links a component that ships a single root <code>SKILL.md</code> (this is how <code>.claude/skills/host-lint</code> exists), which bootstrap never creates and the gate never misses, so replacing the script with bootstrap would silently drop that link.</p> <p><strong>Bootstrap builds the commit gate with ambient cargo.</strong> Mara (1), Wren (4). The build step shells the recorded <code>build</code> string through <code>sh -c</code> in the worktree, while the same tool states, seven hundred lines away, that a build is only meaningful inside the digest-pinned toolchain container. On a genuine fresh clone the recorded recipe (musl target, <code>--offline</code>, vendored deps) fails and the run dies with no remedy; on a warm machine it succeeds and installs a binary that is not the canonical one, which is the plan/0032-retired workaround reintroduced by an orchestrator.</p> <h2 id="the-rest-of-the-blocking-set"><a class="header" href="#the-rest-of-the-blocking-set">The rest of the blocking set</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The gate and the orchestrator read the recipe through different accessors</strong> (Orin 2). The gate expands per-platform <code>[build]</code> subsections; bootstrap reads the flat fields. For an adopter on the form the upgrade ledger tells them to migrate to, bootstrap reports the build step satisfied, the gate hazards on the missing artifact, and re-running never converges.</li> <li><strong>Remedies are not runnable</strong> (Wren 1, 2). Six gate remedies print a literal <code><dir></code>, and the four drift routes drop the <code>host-lifecycle</code> prefix, so they name a subcommand as if it were a binary. The weak-agent transcript shows the model faithfully mirroring both defects.</li> <li><strong>Agentic-host is baked into generic code</strong> (Mara 2, 5, 9; Orin 17; Bly 5; Wren 14). The re-deriver step matches the literal string <code>host-prove</code> against <code>deploy</code>, which is the deployed-line field rather than the component name, so an adopter who writes <code>deploy = main</code> gets the step silently skipped and then hazarded. The fingerprint reads only a binary literally named <code>host-lint</code>. The remedies name <code>link-skills.sh</code> and <code>software/host-prove/main</code>, neither of which exists in an adopter's tree.</li> <li><strong>The materialize receipt dirties a shared tracked file on every clone</strong> (Orin 3). <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> is committed; materialize appends to it; bootstrap runs materialize. The instruction the doctrine is about to give every adopter leaves a modified tracked file behind, once per contributor per clone, recording a purely local event.</li> <li><strong>The host's own CLAUDE.md is not a deliverable of any node</strong> (Wren 5). Only the template's spine doctrine is. On release day a cold session reads the seven-step hand sequence and runs it, which is now the wrong sequence.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-finding-that-explains-the-others"><a class="header" href="#the-finding-that-explains-the-others">The finding that explains the others</a></h2> <p>Bly (7): <code>CompleteSetupCoversWorktreeHooks</code> is dispositioned to a test of the <code>hooks_installed</code> helper, which never constructs a run, never calls <code>verify_setup</code> and never calls <code>setup_requirements</code>. No test anywhere passes a recipe with a hooks-declaring component into <code>setup_requirements</code>, so the entire host-and-worktree hook requirement generator, which carries the two blocking gate findings, is uncovered. The strict-discharge check passes because the token appears in the body; body containment cannot tell a helper from the surface under test. Writing the missing test makes both gate findings fail immediately.</p> <h2 id="dispositions"><a class="header" href="#dispositions">Dispositions</a></h2> <p>Every blocking finding above is fixed at <a href="plan/0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/README.html#adversarial-review">#adversarial-review</a>, which re-reads the fixed diff, except where noted:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Finding</th><th>Disposition</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Gate fails open on unreadable probes</td><td>Fix: an unreadable probe constructs a requirement that is absent, never omits one</td></tr> <tr><td>Gate blind to submodules and to root-<code>SKILL.md</code> skills</td><td>Fix: the gate reads the same sources the orchestrator writes</td></tr> <tr><td>Ambient build of the gating binary</td><td>Fix: bootstrap does not shell the recorded recipe; it reports the gap with the documented local build</td></tr> <tr><td>Two recipe accessors</td><td>Fix: both read through <code>builds_view()</code></td></tr> <tr><td>Remedies not runnable</td><td>Fix: interpolate the real root, prefix the binary name</td></tr> <tr><td>Overfit leaks (re-deriver name and field, gate binary name, remedy paths)</td><td>Fix: derive from the recipe</td></tr> <tr><td>Materialize receipt dirties a tracked file</td><td>Operator decision, carried to the end of this document</td></tr> <tr><td>Host CLAUDE.md not owned by any node</td><td>Fix: folded into #write-spine-doctrine, whose scope now includes the host's own manual</td></tr> <tr><td>Hollow discharge of the coverage invariant</td><td>Fix: repoint at a test that runs <code>setup_requirements</code> over a hooks-declaring recipe</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Should-fix findings carried into the same pass: the <code>n-a</code> line's false reason (Mara 3, Bly 6, Wren 8), the silent <code>.gitignore</code> write (Mara 7, Bly 10, Orin 11, Wren 12), the clean-verdict overstatement when dimensions went unread (Bly 4, Orin 4), a recorded dimension that becomes unreadable never reporting moved (Orin 4), one toolchain image per fingerprint (Mara 6), no route from <code>--check</code> to <code>--verify-setup</code> (Mara 4, Wren 6), unevaluable hedges in two drift remedies (Wren 7), absolute skill links where the script writes relative ones (Wren 11), the missing subcommands in the usage line (Wren 10), and the manifest's overclaim about what the proof establishes (Bly 8, 9).</p> <p>Deferred with a reason: <code>sha256sum</code> portability (Orin 5) is a real narrowing of the fingerprint on non-GNU machines and is filed rather than fixed here, because it touches the pre-existing <code>sha256_file</code> used by the artifact attestation. The <code>.host-lintignore</code> breadth (Mara 8, Bly 14, Wren 15) is recorded as owed narrowing, with the remap-fixture split named as its exit.</p> <h2 id="the-operator-decision-this-review-surfaced"><a class="header" href="#the-operator-decision-this-review-surfaced">The operator decision this review surfaced</a></h2> <p>Orin's finding 3 is not a defect to fix in code without a ruling. The materialize receipt was designed as checked-in provenance (#18, operator ruling 2, 2026-07-19), and the review shows what that means once bootstrap runs materialize on every clone: one appended stanza per contributor per clone, in a shared append-only file, recording an event that is purely local. The options are to keep it as designed and accept the accretion, to record only authoritative materializations, to deduplicate by content so a repeat realization appends nothing, or to move the record to the local tier and revisit the checked-in ruling. Carried to the operator.</p> <h2 id="the-adversarial-round-2026-07-23-on-the-fixed-diff"><a class="header" href="#the-adversarial-round-2026-07-23-on-the-fixed-diff">The adversarial round (2026-07-23, on the fixed diff)</a></h2> <p>Five lenses re-read the diff after the cast's blocking set was fixed: duplication, overfit, fail-open, and discharge-integrity (the weak-agent lens is the acceptance). Three of them reproduced their findings against the built binary; the discharge lens proved its findings by mutation, editing a scratch copy and re-running the whole suite to see whether anything caught the change.</p> <h3 id="what-survived-probing"><a class="header" href="#what-survived-probing">What survived probing</a></h3> <p>The receipt-versus-fingerprint split holds under attack: no cross-artifact reads, correct write attribution at every call site, and the receipt provably carries no state fact. The gate writes nothing, and the verifying-ops assertion is real. Three of the gate's requirement classes have no counterpart anywhere else. The minimal-adopter path is exercised end to end.</p> <h3 id="what-did-not"><a class="header" href="#what-did-not">What did not</a></h3> <p><strong>The verification is thinner than its numbers.</strong> Four obligations are discharged by a test whose own doc comment describes the opposite behaviour; two invariants survive mutation of the exact code they name (deleting host-role awareness, or blanking every worktree hook target, leaves all 277 tests green); one invariant is discharged by a test of <code>.gitignore</code>. The mechanism is systemic: test names were fitted to obligation ids while their bodies tested something else, and the strict-discharge check is a substring match that cannot tell.</p> <p><strong>The proof proves less than the manifest says.</strong> Two of its three assertions are tautologies over a two-variant enum. The third restates the function it checks, 550 lines away in the same file. The quantification runs over a hand-maintained array rather than the enum, so a new fact mapped to the wrong artifact verifies clean; and the writer's real dependency, the positional pairing of stanza name to value, is neither proved nor tested (swapping two entries records the repo path under the submodule stanza with everything green).</p> <p><strong>Two fresh fail-opens, both reproduced.</strong> Hooks are checked by filename alone, so a tree whose hooks are present, non-executable and byte-wrong reads "setup complete" while git ignores them and the commit lands. And a requirement whose source directory is empty or unreadable ceases to exist rather than becoming a gap, so gutting a submodule's working tree turns two required skills into no requirement at all.</p> <p><strong>Bootstrap leaves a false drift on every fresh clone.</strong> Its hooks step calls the counting loop rather than the op that refreshes the fingerprint, so the first <code>env --check</code> after a successful bootstrap reports the gate binary as moved and hands the operator a no-op remedy. That is the one dimension this work was founded on, and the weak-agent acceptance passed on exactly that output.</p> <p><strong>A receipt survives an aborted materialize.</strong> The append is inside the per-component loop and the abort exits mid-loop, so a two-component recipe whose second component fails leaves provenance for a run that never realized.</p> <p><strong>Declared parallel worktrees are invisible to the gate and to bootstrap's materialize step</strong>, while the installer gates them: removing a declared <code>worktrees =</code> line leaves the gate clean and bootstrap declining to re-create it.</p> <p><strong>One boundary was broken to make a fix work.</strong> Reporting a recorded-then-unreadable dimension as moved (the fix that stopped the fingerprint staying silent about a deleted gate binary) contradicts two spec invariants, and the test written for it asserts the counterexample of the invariant it discharges. The <code>env --check</code> and <code>--verify-setup</code> remedies for that state are now byte-identical, which is the overlap the whole plan is organized against.</p> <p><strong>Bootstrap re-implements the gate's predicates</strong> rather than deferring to them, and the two have already drifted: a gate provider with an artifact and no build line makes the gate hazard while bootstrap reports the step satisfied.</p> <h3 id="disposition-2"><a class="header" href="#disposition-2">Disposition</a></h3> <p>Recorded here, carried to the operator: the blocking set above is a second round of work of the same size as the first, and one of its findings (the requirement set deriving from directory listings rather than from the recipe and the pin) is a structural change to how the gate enumerates. The release waits on it.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0074-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-built-output"><a class="header" href="#plan0074-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-built-output">plan/0074 fen-acceptance: the real qwen3.5-4b reads the built output</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-23</li> <li>Model: <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code> (Fen), the gateway's OpenAI-compatible surface (token out of band, never recorded).</li> <li>Params: the model card's thinking-general settings, identical to the plan/0076 matrix recorded in <a href="plan/0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/../0076-dream-store-model/gather-data.html">that plan's gather-data</a> (thinking enabled through the chat template).</li> <li>Protocol: the built binary produced the real output for each surface on real fixtures: a materialized, gated tree that was then moved with its gate binary rebuilt; a half-bootstrapped tree that was never gated and never linked; a fresh clone. Each probe hands the model the verbatim output and asks for its single next action. Two repeats per probe check stability; the three-way distinguishing probe rotates the option order instead. Probes, fixtures and raw transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/materialize-surface/</code> on the operator's machine.</li> </ul> <h2 id="pass-criteria"><a class="header" href="#pass-criteria">Pass criteria</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The drift delta reads as a route.</strong> The model names what moved and acts only where a line says to act, and never treats the check as a gate.</li> <li><strong>The completeness HAZARD reads as "install the missing thing".</strong> The action installs a missing artifact; it is not a drift reconciliation and not a record edit.</li> <li><strong>The bootstrap output reads as complete.</strong> The model moves on rather than re-running steps.</li> <li><strong>The three concerns are distinguishable</strong> from one-line descriptions, rotation-stable.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-first-pass-found-a-real-defect"><a class="header" href="#the-first-pass-found-a-real-defect">The first pass found a real defect</a></h2> <p>The completeness gate, the bootstrap run and the three-way distinction all passed on the first attempt. The drift delta did not:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">envcheck repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle env --check . envcheck repeat 2: ACTION: Proceed with task execution since environment check succeeded without blockers </code></pre> <p>Both repeats are consistent about the one thing the design most wanted (the check is not a gate, and nothing is blocked), and both miss the other half: the output named two moved dimensions and neither response routed to either. The summary line led with "advisory, nothing is gated", and at the 4B bar that sentence dominated the two lines above it. A delta that a reader treats as noise is a delta that hides a rebuilt gate binary.</p> <p><strong>The fix went into the output, not the criterion.</strong> Each moved dimension now says what changed and whether it implies an action: a moved hook binary says to re-install the hooks if the reader did not rebuild it, a moved repo path says there is nothing to fix, and the summary tells the reader to act only where a line says to.</p> <h2 id="results-after-the-fix-four-of-four"><a class="header" href="#results-after-the-fix-four-of-four">Results after the fix: four of four</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">envcheck repeat 1: ACTION: software --install-hooks . envcheck repeat 2: ACTION: software --install-hooks . gate repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --install-hooks . gate repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --install-hooks . bootstrap repeat 1: ACTION: inspect software/gate/main bootstrap repeat 2: ACTION: begin development work on software/gate distinguish order 1 (receipts=A, envhash=B, verify-setup=C): Q1: A Q2: C Q3: B distinguish order 2 (verify-setup=A, envhash=B, receipts=C): Q1: C Q2: A Q3: B </code></pre> <p>Both drift repeats now act on the dimension whose line says to act, and neither acts on the repo path, whose line says there is nothing to fix. The gate's hazard reads as an install in both repeats, over a listing that also contained an unlinked skill, so the model took one safe action rather than a batch. The bootstrap output reads as finished work in both repeats: neither response re-ran a step. The three-way distinction is correct in both rotations, so the mapping is a reading of the descriptions rather than a position artefact.</p> <h2 id="what-this-did-not-test-1"><a class="header" href="#what-this-did-not-test-1">What this did not test</a></h2> <p>The probe machine has no container runtime, so the image-digest dimension stayed silent throughout. How a moved image digest reads at the 4B bar is therefore untested. The <code>--install-hooks</code> remedy was accepted as an action rather than executed, so the probe establishes that the route is legible; whether the remedy works is what the integration tests assert.</p> <h2 id="re-run-after-the-review-rounds-four-of-four-and-the-routes-changed-under-it"><a class="header" href="#re-run-after-the-review-rounds-four-of-four-and-the-routes-changed-under-it">Re-run after the review rounds: four of four, and the routes changed under it</a></h2> <p>The cast and adversarial rounds reworked most of the strings these probes read: the gate's remedies interpolate the real root, the drift routes name the binary rather than a subcommand, a vanished dimension is no longer called drift, and the unread line routes to the gate instead of reassuring. The probes re-ran against the rebuilt output, same parameters, same fixtures:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">envcheck repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --verify-setup /home/…/fix/b envcheck repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --verify-setup /home/…/fix/b gate repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --install-hooks /home/…/fix/c gate repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle software --install-hooks /home/…/fix/c bootstrap repeat 1: ACTION: Begin development tasks in the software/gate/main worktree bootstrap repeat 2: ACTION: execute smoke tests distinguish order 1 (receipts=A, envhash=B, verify-setup=C): Q1: A Q2: C Q3: B distinguish order 2 (verify-setup=A, envhash=B, receipts=C): Q1: C Q2: A Q3: B </code></pre> <p>Two things improved measurably. The drift repeats now emit a <strong>runnable</strong> command with this tree's real path: the earlier pass was scored on intent over <code>software --install-hooks .</code>, a string that names a subcommand as a binary and a directory the model supplied itself, which the discharge review flagged. And the drift action now follows the line that says to act to the command that answers it, rather than acting on a dimension whose line says there is nothing to fix.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-naming-probe-and-settled-conditionals-2026-07-20--2026-07-21"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-naming-probe-and-settled-conditionals-2026-07-20--2026-07-21">gather-data: naming probe and settled conditionals (2026-07-20 / 2026-07-21)</a></h1> <p>This records the #gather-data task. The Fen naming probe (2026-07-20) settled the two names; the remaining conditionals (the receipt kind, the envhash file format, the env-check and verify-setup exit codes, whether <code>--check</code> runs the completeness gate, the image-digest probe, the spine-change split) are settled below (2026-07-21), each traced to a row so every conditional in the README has a grounding. The new issue was filed and #18 reconciled as part of this task.</p> <h2 id="channel"><a class="header" href="#channel">Channel</a></h2> <p><code>~/.local/bin/fen-probe</code> (Unsloth direct, <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code>), <code>max_tokens</code> 400. Two temperatures (0.2, 0.6) with the option order rotated between them, so a first-option artifact is detectable. Script <code>/tmp/plan0074-naming-probe.sh</code>; transcripts <code>/tmp/plan0074-naming-transcripts.txt</code>.</p> <h2 id="decision-1-the-orchestrator-that-runs-the-whole-fresh-clone-setup"><a class="header" href="#decision-1-the-orchestrator-that-runs-the-whole-fresh-clone-setup">Decision 1: the orchestrator that runs the whole fresh-clone setup</a></h2> <p>Given the sibling commands (<code>--materialize</code> clones worktrees, <code>--install-hooks</code> installs hooks, <code>--check</code> verifies pins) and a description of a new all-in-one command that runs the complete setup, the model chose:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Candidate</th><th>temp 0.2 (order)</th><th>temp 0.6 (order)</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><strong>bootstrap</strong></td><td><strong>A, chosen</strong></td><td><strong>D, chosen</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>setup</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr> <tr><td>provision</td><td>C</td><td>B</td></tr> <tr><td>realize</td><td>D</td><td>A</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><code>bootstrap</code> at both temps. Rotation-proof: it was option A at temp 0.2 and option D at temp 0.6, chosen both times. The model's reason: "bootstrap is the standard technical term for initializing a system by running a comprehensive sequence of setup tasks to make it ready for use."</p> <p><strong>Settled: <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code>.</strong></p> <h2 id="decision-2-the-gate-that-checks-the-setup-is-complete"><a class="header" href="#decision-2-the-gate-that-checks-the-setup-is-complete">Decision 2: the gate that checks the setup is complete</a></h2> <p>Given the sibling checks (<code>software --check</code> for pins, <code>env --check</code> for drift) and a description of a new check that fails if any required piece of the setup is missing, the model chose:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Candidate</th><th>temp 0.2 (order)</th><th>temp 0.6 (order)</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><strong>--verify-setup</strong></td><td><strong>A, chosen</strong></td><td><strong>C, chosen</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>--verify-env</td><td>B</td><td>B</td></tr> <tr><td>--verify-host</td><td>C</td><td>A</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><code>--verify-setup</code> at both temps. Rotation-proof: it was option A at temp 0.2 and option C at temp 0.6, chosen both times. It reads as "verify the setup is complete", distinct from <code>env --check</code> (drift) and <code>--check</code> (pins). The operator had leaned toward <code>--verify-env</code> / <code>--verify-host</code>; the 4B bar prefers <code>--verify-setup</code>, and "env" collides with the sibling <code>env</code> subcommand.</p> <p><strong>Settled: <code>host-lifecycle software --verify-setup <dir></code>.</strong></p> <h2 id="the-remaining-conditionals-settled-2026-07-21"><a class="header" href="#the-remaining-conditionals-settled-2026-07-21">The remaining conditionals (settled 2026-07-21)</a></h2> <p>Each README "Open design questions" bullet, grounded and settled. Two were operator decisions (2026-07-21): the envhash format and whether <code>--check</code> runs the completeness gate.</p> <h3 id="the-receipt-kind-18"><a class="header" href="#the-receipt-kind-18">The receipt kind (#18)</a></h3> <p>Its own kind. Grounded in the existing writer: <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> stanzas are keyed <code>[receipt "<phase>" "<component>"]</code> (see <code>receipt_stanza</code>, src/main.rs), so the materialize receipt is a new phase value, <code>[receipt "materialize" "<component>"]</code>, not a re-opening of the <code>embed</code> recheck. Event-level fields only (disposition, evidence, pin-by-reference, image reference, tool, recorded), in the same append-only shape the <code>embed</code> receipt already uses.</p> <h3 id="the-envhash-file-format-operator-decision-2026-07-21"><a class="header" href="#the-envhash-file-format-operator-decision-2026-07-21">The envhash file format (operator decision, 2026-07-21)</a></h3> <p><strong>TOML stanzas.</strong> Matches host-lifecycle's state-file idiom (<code>.host-software</code>, <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> are both TOML-stanza). Per-input sub-hash as <code>[envhash "<dimension>"]</code> stanzas (worktree paths, hook binary hash, image digest, submodule init state, repo abspath), so <code>env --check</code> diffs dimension-by-dimension and prints only the moved rows. Rejected: flat key:value, which would diverge from the idiom for no gain.</p> <h3 id="the-env---check-exit-code"><a class="header" href="#the-env---check-exit-code">The <code>env --check</code> exit code</a></h3> <p>Advisory, three outcomes: <code>0</code> clean (envhash present, no delta), <code>0</code> with delta (envhash present, dimensions moved, prints the route, never fails), <code>2</code> cannot-proceed (no <code>.host-envhash</code> on disk, a prompt to materialize, not a gate failure). Never exit 1; <code>env --check</code> is a sanity aid, never a gate (#19's framing, and Fen's weak-agent trap: it must not read as a gate).</p> <h3 id="the-completeness-gate-exit-code"><a class="header" href="#the-completeness-gate-exit-code">The completeness-gate exit code</a></h3> <p>A gate: <code>0</code> complete, non-zero HAZARD on any missing required artifact, matching the <code>software --check</code> HAZARD convention. Host-role-aware: a non-build host does not HAZARD on an absent build artifact (it was never required to build it).</p> <h3 id="does---check-run-the-completeness-gate-operator-decision-2026-07-21"><a class="header" href="#does---check-run-the-completeness-gate-operator-decision-2026-07-21">Does <code>--check</code> run the completeness gate? (operator decision, 2026-07-21)</a></h3> <p><strong>No. <code>--verify-setup</code> stays a distinct invocation.</strong> Consistent with operator ruling #7 (a separate verify mode) and with <code>env --check</code> being separate: <code>--check</code> answers pin-vs-recorded, <code>env --check</code> answers drift-from-recorded, <code>--verify-setup</code> answers complete-vs-recipe. <code>bootstrap</code> runs <code>--verify-setup</code> as its final self-check; an operator runs it explicitly. Rejected: folding it into the <code>--check</code> sweep, which would couple the recipe-vs-live question into the pin gate.</p> <h3 id="the-image-digest-probe"><a class="header" href="#the-image-digest-probe">The image-digest probe</a></h3> <p>Shells to <code>docker</code> / <code>podman inspect</code> for the locally pulled image digest. With no container runtime on PATH, the envhash records <code>runtime = none</code> for the image dimension and stays silent on it: <code>env --check</code> never reports a moved image digest it cannot read, and the completeness gate does not HAZARD on it.</p> <h3 id="the-spine-change-split"><a class="header" href="#the-spine-change-split">The spine-change split</a></h3> <p>Methodology (spine, host-template CLAUDE.md): the materialize receipt (#18, a fourth receipt kind) and the bootstrap-plus-completeness doctrine (a fresh clone runs <code>host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir></code>, setup completeness is gated not assumed). Tooling-only (no spine change): the envhash (#19), which is local, gitignored, and advisory.</p> <h2 id="issue-filing-and-18-reconciliation-2026-07-21"><a class="header" href="#issue-filing-and-18-reconciliation-2026-07-21">Issue filing and #18 reconciliation (2026-07-21)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Filed <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/20">#20</a></strong> for the bootstrap orchestrator and completeness gate (with Bug A folded in). Title linted clean (<code>host-lint --stdin</code>, exit 0).</li> <li><strong>Reopened <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/18">#18</a>.</strong> It was CLOSED/COMPLETED at the plan-cut timestamp (2026-07-19T15:40), yet <code>implement-receipt</code> is an unbuilt node with no receipt code, so the closure recorded work that had not happened. <code>release-and-re-pin</code> closes it when the writer ships.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0075-host-reconcile-the-merge-driver-framework-design"><a class="header" href="#plan0075-host-reconcile-the-merge-driver-framework-design">plan/0075 host-reconcile: the merge-driver framework design</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: cut, design-only, not started</strong> (operator ruling 2026-07-22, recorded in the closure queue in PLAN.md's Open work). Queued last, behind plan/0072.</p> <h2 id="why-12"><a class="header" href="#why-12">Why</a></h2> <p><code>host-reconcile</code> is a proposed new <code>host-*</code> methodology tool: a framework for domain-aware git merge drivers that reconcile typed files (version metadata, changelogs, manifests) across a moving base, the friction at the heart of an out-of-tree patch set carried atop a fast-moving upstream. The core is methodology-general; per-domain articulations (such as <code>host-reconcile-ffmpeg</code>) encode project-specific resolution rules. The full proposal is recorded in <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/18">connollydavid/host#18</a>; that issue is the design record this milestone starts from.</p> <h2 id="scope-4"><a class="header" href="#scope-4">Scope</a></h2> <p>Design only. The milestone produces the reviewed design: the tool boundary against the existing <code>host-*</code> family, the articulation model, and a go or no-go recommendation for a build. The build is not gated here; a build milestone is cut only if the design survives adversarial review. plan/0072's FFmpeg pack supplies the nearest concrete articulation candidate, which is why this milestone sits behind it in the queue.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0076-dream-store-model-the-declared-tier-build-of-the-dream-detector-model"><a class="header" href="#plan0076-dream-store-model-the-declared-tier-build-of-the-dream-detector-model">plan/0076 dream-store-model: the declared-tier build of the dream detector model</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: complete, shipped as host-lifecycle v0.42.0 (fd7c632, artifact 78e6be41, 2026-07-23); every node receipted done.</strong> The design is settled and recorded in <a href="plan/0076-dream-store-model/../../call/0045-dream-detectors-declare-stores-and-tier.html">call/0045</a>; the convening record (both ballot rounds, both weak-agent matrices, the binding conditions) is in <a href="plan/0076-dream-store-model/gather-data.html">gather-data.md</a>. Closes <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/22">host-lifecycle#22</a> at release. The held patch commit on the host-lifecycle worktree (the per-user-only guards) reworks inside the implement node.</p> <h2 id="why-13"><a class="header" href="#why-13">Why</a></h2> <p>The dream audit had no model of the store it audits: every detector ran on every store, and remedy strings ignored the target store's write discipline. The fix grew into a design with three parts: declared detector applicability, a cross-store link graph over a tier whose in-use status is itself declared state (a tool-written, audited repo-side marker), and one confirmed/review-prompt taxonomy with split exit codes. call/0045 records the decision and the guardrails; this plan builds it.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-17"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-17">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">The convening record</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: gather-data.md carries the mechanism, both ballot rounds, both weak-agent matrices with their parameters, and the seven binding conditions.</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">Extend the dream spec</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: the dream Allium spec models detector applicability, union resolution, the marker state machine (absent, stamped, retired, contradiction), the three absence states, the two finding kinds, and the exit split; the spec lanes pass under <code>software --check</code>.</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">Write the obligations</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> <li>verify: every new spec obligation carries a disposition and the obligations digests re-derive clean.</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-model"><a class="header" href="#implement-model">Implement the detector model</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> <li>verify: applicability declarations with cited format facts enforce in detect(); room-touching leads with "leave a review note"; output groups confirmed first behind a count line; exits are clean zero, advisory-only three, confirmed one; coverage lines are generated from the applicability declarations and store facts, in text and JSON, with per-state counts and marker provenance.</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">Write the test matrix</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #implement-marker, #implement-taxonomy</li> <li>verify: cargo test covers the three absence states, marker lifecycle transitions, both finding kinds, the exit split, per-state counts, and the remedy strings' append-only anti-action tails; all green.</li> </ul> <h3 id="file-cross-check-issue"><a class="header" href="#file-cross-check-issue">File the cross-check follow-up</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> <li>verify: the room-touching spine cross-check issue is filed on host-lifecycle with a linted title, and its URL is recorded in this file.</li> <li>Filed: <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/23">host-lifecycle#23</a> (title linted clean, 2026-07-22).</li> </ul> <h3 id="migration-ledger"><a class="header" href="#migration-ledger">Write the migration ledger entry</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #implement-marker, #implement-taxonomy</li> <li>verify: the revision-keyed UPGRADING entry states the mechanism, the expected day-one confirmed wall, the initialization fork, and the prohibition on link drops that merely clear the wall; the spine memory doctrine names the marker; book and entrance checks stay green.</li> </ul> <h3 id="cast-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#cast-acceptance">Cast acceptance of the built diff</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #write-tests, #migration-ledger</li> <li>verify: an adversarial review of the built diff against the seven binding conditions records zero blocking findings.</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">Weak-agent acceptance on the built output</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> <li>verify: the real qwen3.5-4b, at its card parameters, reads the built dream output for each absence state and names the state-correct safe action, rotation-stable; the transcript is recorded in this plan.</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #cast-acceptance, #fen-acceptance</li> <li>verify: <code>host-lifecycle release host-lifecycle --change-class adds-flag</code> cascades clean (worktree pushed, tag, <code>.host-software</code> re-pin, template pin bump, release receipt, hooks reinstalled); <code>software --check .</code> is clean at the new pin; host-lifecycle#22 closes with the outcome comment.</li> </ul> <h3 id="triage-own-links"><a class="header" href="#triage-own-links">Triage the ten forward-marker links</a></h3> <ul> <li>depends: #release-and-re-pin</li> <li>verify: the operator has either initialized the store (links re-tiered advisory with seeding owed) or retired the markers by appended corrections; <code>dream .</code> reports the chosen terminal state and the queue annotation in PLAN.md records it.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0076-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-built-output"><a class="header" href="#plan0076-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-built-output">plan/0076 fen-acceptance: the real qwen3.5-4b reads the built output</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-22</li> <li>Model: <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code> (Fen), the gateway's OpenAI-compatible surface at <code>api.d07yx58.net</code> (token out of band, never recorded).</li> <li>Params: the model card's thinking-general settings, identical to the corrected re-ballot matrix recorded in <a href="plan/0076-dream-store-model/gather-data.html">gather-data.md</a> (thinking enabled through the chat template).</li> <li>Protocol: the built binary produced the real output for each absence state (a no-marker confirmed dangling link; a stamped-marker storeless machine; a stamped-marker present store with the target entry missing). Each probe hands the model the verbatim finding line and suggestion and asks for its single next action; two repeats per state check stability. Probes and raw transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/dream-store-model/fen-acceptance/</code> on the operator's machine; the verdict lines are reproduced verbatim below.</li> </ul> <h2 id="pass-criteria-1"><a class="header" href="#pass-criteria-1">Pass criteria</a></h2> <ul> <li>Confirmed (no marker): fix or drop rides a new appended correction, no in-place edit, and the model does NOT initialize a store or touch the marker (the operator fork is not the agent's action).</li> <li>Advisory, uninitialized here: leave the link in place and report; no drop on this machine's evidence.</li> <li>Advisory, entry missing: create the target or correct the link through the tier-correct write.</li> </ul> <h2 id="results-six-of-six-stable"><a class="header" href="#results-six-of-six-stable">Results: six of six, stable</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">state 1 repeat 1: ACTION: Append a new correction entry to the repo MEMORY.md file to either fix the slug or drop the forward `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link without editing the existing entry in place. state 1 repeat 2: ACTION: I will append a new correction entry to repo MEMORY.md to resolve the dangling link instead of editing the existing session-note in place. state 2 repeat 1: ACTION: I will leave the `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link standing in the review-prompt entry and report that the per-user store required for resolution is absent on this machine. state 2 repeat 2: ACTION: Leave the `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link standing in the note and report its unresolved status without modifying the entry since the per-user store is absent here. state 3 repeat 1: ACTION: Create a new dated entry for `qwen-eval-notes` in the repository's MEMORY.md file to resolve the broken reference. state 3 repeat 2: ACTION: I will append a new dated entry for `qwen-eval-notes` to the repo MEMORY.md file to resolve the broken link. </code></pre> <p>Every response names the state-correct safe action; both repeats agree in every state; no response initializes a store, stamps or retires the marker, edits an entry in place, or drops a link on machine-local evidence. The confirmed-state remedy's operator fork read correctly as not the agent's own action, which was the anti-gaming guardrail's residual worry.</p> <h2 id="re-run-after-the-cast-acceptance-fixes-six-of-six-again"><a class="header" href="#re-run-after-the-cast-acceptance-fixes-six-of-six-again">Re-run after the cast-acceptance fixes: six of six again</a></h2> <p>The cast-acceptance review reworked the remedy strings (the operator subject on the uninitialized state, the drop-confirmation and anti-stamp tails on the confirmed state, the dedicated retired arm), so the probe pair re-ran against the fixed build's verbatim output. Same protocol, same result, and the anti-stamp tail read exactly as designed:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">state 1 repeat 1: ACTION: Append a new correction entry to the repo MEMORY.md to either fix the slug or drop the dangling `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link, without editing the existing session note. state 1 repeat 2: ACTION: Append a new correction entry to repo MEMORY.md that drops the `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link from session-note to fix the dangling reference without editing the original note or attempting tier initialization. state 2 repeat 1: ACTION: Leave the [[qwen-eval-notes]] link standing in the session-note and report this dangling-link finding without editing or modifying the entry since the per-user store is absent on this machine. state 2 repeat 2: ACTION: I will leave the `[[qwen-eval-notes]]` link standing in the review prompt without modifying or removing it as instructed by the audit tool. state 3 repeat 1: ACTION: I will append a new dated entry for `qwen-eval-notes` to the repo MEMORY.md file to resolve the broken link identified by the audit tool. state 3 repeat 2: ACTION: Append a new dated entry defining `qwen-eval-notes` to the end of the repository's MEMORY.md file to resolve the dangling link. </code></pre> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0076-gather-data-the-store-model-convening-record"><a class="header" href="#plan0076-gather-data-the-store-model-convening-record">plan/0076 gather-data: the store-model convening record</a></h1> <p>The design in <a href="plan/0076-dream-store-model/../../call/0045-dream-detectors-declare-stores-and-tier.html">call/0045</a> was settled through a two-round cast convening under an operator-proposed mechanism: adversarial ranked-choice ballots from the five personas, each ballot attacking its own top choice before ranking, the operator as tie-breaker and participant. The weak agent voted as the real model; its first matrix mis-parameterized and spoiled, and the corrected matrix is the auditable ballot. Both matrices are retained side by side as data.</p> <h2 id="the-proposal-under-ballot"><a class="header" href="#the-proposal-under-ballot">The proposal under ballot</a></h2> <p>The trigger proposal (thesis: every detector declares the store formats it applies to and carries a store-correct remedy; links resolve across the whole memory graph; a finding count never stands in for memory health) reframed the two <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/22">host-lifecycle#22</a> defects as one missing model, in five pillars: declared applicability, cross-store union resolution, store-correct remedies, a confirmed-versus-review-prompt distinction for room-touching, and legible silence.</p> <h2 id="opening-ballots"><a class="header" href="#opening-ballots">Opening ballots</a></h2> <p>Two contested questions went to ballot. On absence semantics (what the repo tier reports when the per-user store is absent), honest-flag beat skip-and-state four to one; the maintainer persona dissented on machine-locality grounds: local absence cannot distinguish a target that never existed from one on another operator's machine, and flagging on it de-facto mandates an optional store. On room-touching, label-now-defer-cross-check beat defer-everything four to one, with the weak agent stable for outright suppression; the suppression preference is recorded as its standing dissent.</p> <p>Convergent conditions from the opening round, carried forward: the coverage line is load-bearing and reaches JSON; each finding names the union scope it consulted; repo-tier remedies carry the appended-correction anti-action tail; the machine-locality of any union verdict is recorded; a standing baseline's terminal state is recorded, and annotating a baseline as known noise is itself a finding, never a disposition; behavior changes are ledgered for adopters.</p> <h2 id="the-weak-agent-matrices"><a class="header" href="#the-weak-agent-matrices">The weak-agent matrices</a></h2> <ul> <li>Model: <code>unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL</code> (Fen), served on the local gateway's OpenAI-compatible surface at <code>api.d07yx58.net</code> (the plan/0073 direct channel's successor; the token lives out of band and is never recorded).</li> <li>Spoiled matrix: no-think decoding at temperatures 0.2 and 0.6, top_p 0.8, no top_k, min_p, or presence penalty. Under option-order rotation the model answered the same letter from both orders, opposite content: position bias, rotation-proof failed, ballot recorded spoiled at weight zero.</li> <li>Corrected matrix (operator-directed lookup, model card and unsloth run guide, fetched 2026-07-22): thinking enabled through the chat template, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty 1.5, output budget 32768. Under the same rotation the ballots were content-stable on both questions. The spoil-then-validate pair is itself a recorded finding: a weak agent's menu resolution is only as good as its decoding configuration, which a remedy author cannot control, so remedy strings lead with one safe action and never present a menu.</li> <li>The absence-semantics probe (both orders) and the room-touching probe (both orders, three options) are reproduced below verbatim, with the re-ballot probe. Each ran once per option order.</li> </ul> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">Probe: absence semantics. "A tool called dream audits two stores of notes: the repo log (append-only, shared, in git) and a per-user folder of editable notes on this machine. Links written [[like-this]] in the repo log usually point at notes in the per-user folder. On this machine the per-user folder does not exist at all. Ten links in the repo log therefore point at nothing the tool can see." Option one: report each link as unresolved, advise "fix or drop this link (via a new appended correction, never an in-place edit)", print "per-user store absent on this machine".
