Option two: report none, print "per-user store absent; cross-store links not checked". Ask: which is safer to act on; one sentence attacking the preferred option; then ANSWER: A or B. Probe: room-touching. "One detector fires on EVERY mention of an old decision record, and today its advice says: confirm the decision is still current; if superseded, mark it Status: superseded. Most alerts are false alarms, and marking a record superseded is a permanent change to a shared log. A precise version (checking real evidence) is planned but not built." Option one: relabel each alert "review prompt (not confirmed)" and change the advice to "leave a review note"; file a ticket. Option two: keep the alerts exactly as today; file a ticket. Option three: turn the detector off; print "room-touching check off until the precise version lands"; file a ticket. Ask: safest to act on; one attack sentence; then RANKING. </code></pre> <h2 id="the-operators-reframe"><a class="header" href="#the-operators-reframe">The operator's reframe</a></h2> <p>The operator examined the dissent and named the lacuna both camps shared: an uninitialized option is not an unused option. The single absence state collapsed three: a tier the project never opted into (a stray link is genuinely dangling, teeth are honest), a tier in use but uninitialized on this machine (unresolvable here, and dropping on this machine's evidence is the failure), and a tier in use with the target entry missing (create or correct). The operator ruled two parameters before the re-ballot: the tier's in-use status becomes tool-written declared state (dream stamps an audited repo-side marker at first observed store initialization), and dangling-link joins the unified confirmed/review-prompt taxonomy with the exit split clean zero, advisory-only three, confirmed one.</p> <h2 id="the-re-ballot"><a class="header" href="#the-re-ballot">The re-ballot</a></h2> <p>Head-to-head: the three-state declaration-driven semantics against the opening winner. Result: five of five for the three-state model. Mara held her opening reasoning and found three state-specific remedies more glanceable than one hedged string. Wren changed position with a recorded self-correction: her opening plank inferred a global fact from machine-local absence, the exact collapse the reframe names, and the marker gives the amnesiac reader repo-readable declared truth. Bly held his reasoning and moved his top choice: the marker is to store-in-use what the <code>.host</code> stamp is to template revision, and the gating tier becomes a function of repo contents alone. The maintainer persona held his dissent and found it answered in steady state, relocated to the migration window. The weak agent chose the staged behavior from both option orders, rotation-proof passed, and its own attack sentence independently named the stale-marker hazard.</p> <p>Every strong ballot's attack converged on one hazard from four angles: the marker is a one-bit global authority over the detector's teeth. An empty-seed stamp defuses the confirmed tier permanently; the day-one confirmed wall invites mass link-stripping under gate pressure; an agent staring at a red gate can mint the marker as the cheapest silencing act; a weak agent on a storeless machine could retire the marker as the only branch it can execute, which flips every checkout to confirmed. The seven binding conditions in call/0045's decision are the convergent answer: format-specified lifecycle, operator-attributable stamping, no machine-local flips in either direction, the pre-announced migration wall with the drop prohibition, mechanically generated per-state wording with one safe action first, state-and-determinant legibility with per-state counts and marker provenance, and the anti-gaming signatures in the MADR.</p> <h2 id="operator-rulings-ledger-2026-07-22"><a class="header" href="#operator-rulings-ledger-2026-07-22">Operator rulings ledger (2026-07-22)</a></h2> <ul> <li>The convening mechanism itself: adversarial ranked choice, five personas, real weak agent, operator tie-break.</li> <li>Full convening before implementation; the weak-agent simulation rejected, the real model required, and the corrected card parameters directed when the first matrix rambled.</li> <li>The lacuna reframe and the re-ballot direction, with the declaration and taxonomy parameters ruled ahead of it.</li> <li>Sign-offs: the three-state semantics with all seven conditions; room-touching label-now with its riders; the exit split; the build cut as this plan rather than an issue-scoped patch.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0077-reference-resolver-a-register-number-resolves-and-a-bare-issue-number-stops-being-dead-text"><a class="header" href="#plan0077-reference-resolver-a-register-number-resolves-and-a-bare-issue-number-stops-being-dead-text">plan/0077 reference resolver: a register number resolves, and a bare issue number stops being dead text</a></h1> <p>Closes <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/17">host-lifecycle#17</a> and the parked full-URL row in <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/../../PLAN.html">PLAN.md</a> (operator, plan/0042 review; sharpened by plan/0049: the reference must sit in a markdown link to the full URL, so it renders in the site). Queue position four of the 2026-07-22 closure ruling, cut 2026-07-23 after plan/0074 shipped.</p> <h2 id="why-14"><a class="header" href="#why-14">Why</a></h2> <p>The methodology makes a number an identity: a bare number at the plan root names a milestone, a numbered file under <code>call/</code> names a decision. Every room, every commit message and every doc then refers to those numbers, and nothing resolves them. In this repository alone, 122 distinct <code>plan/NNNN</code> and <code>call/NNNN</code> references appear across the authored docs; all 122 resolve by hand and none of them resolve by tool, so in the published site they are text that looks like a link and is not one.</p> <p>The same gap has a second face. A bare <code>#N</code> issue reference is not a safe full URL: it renders as nothing in the site, and read outside GitHub it does not even say which repository it belongs to. This tree carries 374 of them outside code fences, 187 in the append-only <code>MEMORY.md</code> and 35 in a dated review artifact, which is the shape of the answer as much as the size of the problem: the record layer is excluded, never rewritten.</p> <p>The two halves are one capability. Resolving <code>plan/0074</code> to a path, a markdown link or a GitHub URL is the same act as turning <code>#17</code> into <code>https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/17</code> inside a link; a checker that reports dead references needs the resolver that would have made them live.</p> <h2 id="scope-5"><a class="header" href="#scope-5">Scope</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The resolver.</strong> A host-lifecycle subcommand that takes a reference and emits the local path, a markdown link, or a GitHub URL derived from the repository's origin remote, with a <code>#anchor</code> preserved so a task node resolves to its heading.</li> <li><strong>The dead-reference check.</strong> A mode that reports references the site cannot render: a bare <code>#N</code> outside a link, and a <code>plan/</code>, <code>call/</code> reference that resolves to nothing. Record-layer paths are excluded by the same discipline the prose gate uses, because an append-only log is never rewritten to satisfy a checker.</li> <li><strong>The cross-host case.</strong> A <code>plan/</code> or <code>call/</code> reference in a software repository belongs to its governing host, not to the software repository, and it carries no repository name. An unresolvable reference is reported as unresolved-here rather than resolved wrongly or passed silently.</li> </ol> <p>Out of scope, recorded so it is not assumed: linkifying commit messages in the generated site (the issue names it as a use case; it needs the resolver first and is its own milestone), and rewriting the references this check reports.</p> <h2 id="open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles">Open questions the gather-data node settles</a></h2> <ul> <li>The verb: <code>resolve</code>, <code>link</code>, or <code>ref</code>, and whether the emission is flag-selected or positional. Settled by a rotation-proof weak-agent probe, as the <code>bootstrap</code> and <code>--verify-setup</code> names were.</li> <li>The check's home: its own mode, a fold into <code>validate</code>, or a fold into the prose sweep that already walks authored markdown.</li> <li>Whether the check gates (non-zero) or advises on day one, given a wall of 374 bare references of which perhaps 150 sit in live documents.</li> <li>How the record layer is excluded: reuse <code>.host-lintignore</code>, or an explicit list.</li> <li>Whether a software repository names its owning host, so a cross-repo reference resolves at all.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-18"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-18">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">The settled conditionals</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every open question above has a row in gather-data.md, the naming probe transcript is recorded, and the wall is measured per file</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">The reference surface</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the Allium spec models the reference kinds, the resolution outcomes (resolved, unresolved-here, unresolved-anywhere), the emission forms, and the check verdict; <code>allium check</code> and <code>analyse</code> exit 0 with zero findings</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">The obligations</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every <code>allium plan</code> obligation carries a disposition, and each names a test that exercises the rule rather than a helper beside it</li> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-resolve"><a class="header" href="#implement-resolve">The resolver</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a reference resolves to its path, its markdown link and its GitHub URL, with the anchor preserved and the origin remote read for the URL</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-check"><a class="header" href="#implement-check">The dead-reference check</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a bare issue number outside a link is reported, a resolving register reference is not, an unresolvable one is reported as unresolved, and every record-layer path is excluded</li> <li>depends: #implement-resolve</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">The test matrix</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the suite covers each reference kind, each emission form, each resolution outcome, the exclusions and the exit split; mutating the rule under each behavioural obligation fails its named test</li> <li>depends: #implement-check</li> </ul> <h3 id="cast-consult"><a class="header" href="#cast-consult">Cast consultation</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: each persona's concern is addressed or recorded, in design-review.md</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review">Adversarial review</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: an independent multi-lens read of the built diff records every blocking finding fixed or carried, with a dedicated lens for the record-layer exclusion (a checker that pressures an append-only log is the failure that matters here)</li> <li>depends: #cast-consult</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">The weak-agent acceptance</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the real qwen3.5-4b reads the check's output and names the state-correct next action, and reads a resolved reference as a link rather than as text; rotation-stable, transcript recorded</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spine-doctrine"><a class="header" href="#write-spine-doctrine">The spine doctrine</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the template manual states the reference discipline (a number resolves, a bare issue number is not a reference) and the ledger entry names the day-one wall and the record-layer exclusion</li> <li>depends: #adversarial-review</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the release cascades clean, <code>software --check .</code> is clean at the new pin, and host-lifecycle#17 closes with its outcome</li> <li>depends: #write-spine-doctrine, #fen-acceptance</li> </ul> <h3 id="remediate-this-tree"><a class="header" href="#remediate-this-tree">This tree's own references</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the live documents this check reports are remediated or their exclusion is recorded; <code>MEMORY.md</code> is untouched, and PLAN.md's parked row records the outcome</li> <li>depends: #release-and-re-pin</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0077-adversarial-review-four-lenses-read-the-built-diff"><a class="header" href="#plan0077-adversarial-review-four-lenses-read-the-built-diff">plan/0077 adversarial-review: four lenses read the built diff</a></h1> <p>Date: 2026-07-26. Subject: <code>4f27c7a..7700cf4</code> in host-lifecycle: the resolver, the sweep, the waiver rename and <code>migrate-recipe</code>.</p> <p>The cast round read <code>4f27c7a..06fa455</code> and recorded its blocking set in <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/design-review.html">design-review.md</a>. Three commits landed after it: the refusal that names a real reference, the rename of the reproducibility waiver, and the tool-carried recipe migration. The last two had no independent read at all before this round.</p> <h2 id="who-read-it-and-how"><a class="header" href="#who-read-it-and-how">Who read it, and how</a></h2> <p>Four lenses, each independent, each required to reproduce every claim against the built binary before recording it:</p> <ul> <li><strong>the record layer</strong>, the lens this milestone's plan names as the one that matters, because a checker that presses an append-only log into being rewritten has broken the thing it audits;</li> <li><strong>coverage honesty</strong>, whether any verdict claims more than the tool read, the class already found and fixed twice here;</li> <li><strong>resolver correctness</strong>, whether an emitted path, link or URL is right or merely plausible;</li> <li><strong>the rename and its migration</strong>, the three unreviewed commits, read against the decisions that authorise them.</li> </ul> <p>Fixtures were built outside both repositories, and no lens held write access to either. Findings the design review already records as fixed were re-attacked rather than re-reported; where a fix holds, that is recorded below under what could not be broken.</p> <h2 id="the-blocking-set"><a class="header" href="#the-blocking-set">The blocking set</a></h2> <h3 id="the-verdict-claims-coverage-the-run-does-not-have"><a class="header" href="#the-verdict-claims-coverage-the-run-does-not-have">The verdict claims coverage the run does not have</a></h3> <p>This is the third instance of the class. The first printed a clean line after reading zero documents; the second claimed coverage of references it had skipped by design. Both are fixed. The shape survived in the walk itself.</p> <p><strong>A document the tool cannot read is counted as swept, and a dead pointer inside it ships as exit 0.</strong> <code>authored_docs</code> takes <code>git ls-files</code> output verbatim, and git quotes any path holding a non-ASCII byte under its default <code>core.quotepath</code>, so the quoted name is counted and the read fails. The failure is swallowed by <code>let Ok(text) = … else { continue }</code>. Reproduced:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">$ git ls-files '*.md' README.md "na\303\257ve.md" <- holds a dead plan/0099 plan/0074-x/README.md $ host-lifecycle refs --check . -- 3 doc(s) swept; every reference in them resolves and renders exit=0 <- expected exit 1, one dead pointer </code></pre> <p>An unreadable document and one holding invalid UTF-8 take the identical path. Two lenses found this independently. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:1920</code>, <code>src/refs.rs:456</code> and <code>:579</code>.</p> <p><strong>The exclusion is never disclosed.</strong> On this host the sweep excludes 19 documents holding 319 bare references, and reports 293. The excluded population is larger than the reported one, and no verdict line mentions that a document was withheld. The clean branch is the sharp case: with a list that excludes everything, a README carrying two dead pointers yields <code>1 doc(s) swept; every reference in them resolves and renders</code> at exit 0. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:481-513</code>.</p> <p><strong>The unchecked-register disclosure prints on the clean branch alone.</strong> The design review's own fix sits after both early returns, so the advisory and dead verdicts drop it. A software repository, the case the disclosure exists for, almost always carries a bare <code>#N</code> and therefore never sees it. The dead verdict drops the swept count as well. Three lenses recorded this. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:504-513</code>.</p> <p><strong>A project whose rooms are renamed or nested gets an unqualified clean line.</strong> <code>ROOMS</code> is a literal <code>["plan","call"]</code>, so a tree using <code>milestones/</code> and <code>decisions/</code> has its references pass through the grammar unseen: the hedge that would have said the room was not held cannot fire, because nothing was counted to hedge about. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:25</code>, <code>:172-174</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-checker-presses-the-record-layer"><a class="header" href="#the-checker-presses-the-record-layer">The checker presses the record layer</a></h3> <p><strong>Three of five natural <code>.host-lintignore</code> spellings are silent no-ops, and the declared record then gates.</strong> A leading <code>/</code>, a bare directory name and a leading <code>./</code> all fail to match, so an operator who has declared their append-only log excluded is told to rewrite it, at exit 1. An unreadable list degrades to no exclusions at all. A negation is ignored, so <code>*.md</code> with <code>!README.md</code> withdraws a live authored document from coverage instead. The list is never reported as having matched nothing. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:1900-1910</code>.</p> <p><strong>Running the sweep on a subdirectory discards the exclusion list.</strong> The list is read from the root passed on the command line while the paths are relative to it, so any invocation below the repository root loses every exclusion. Reproduced against this tree:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">$ host-lifecycle refs --check plan/0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack bare signals-digest.md: 37 issue number(s) written outside a link bare handover.md: 3 issue number(s) written outside a link Advisory: nothing is blocked. No flag fixes this; each reference is an edit. </code></pre> <p>Both files are named in this repository's own <code>.host-lintignore</code> under the comment that calls them the immutable record. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:623</code> with <code>src/main.rs:1917</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-remedy-sends-the-reader-to-the-wrong-tracker"><a class="header" href="#the-remedy-sends-the-reader-to-the-wrong-tracker">The remedy sends the reader to the wrong tracker</a></h3> <p><strong>Both remedy strings hardcode <code>connollydavid/host-lifecycle</code>.</strong> Every adopter is handed a command whose effect is to rewrite their own issue reference into a link to this project's tracker. The weak-agent acceptance is the evidence that the printed command gets run verbatim: both repeats of the refusal probe executed it exactly. This is the cast round's blocking finding, the bare <code>#N</code> resolved against whatever remote happened to be local, relocated from the resolver into the remedy line. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:498</code> and <code>:613</code>.</p> <p><strong>A qualified reference on a non-GitHub forge builds a github.com URL.</strong> The register form correctly refuses when the origin names another forge; <code>owner/repo#N</code> builds the link anyway, so a GitLab-hosted project's reference to its own issue points at an unrelated repository that may well exist. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:246</code>.</p> <p><strong><code>component#N</code> guesses the owner from origin and ignores the owner the tree records.</strong> This repository holds two components at foreign owners in <code>.gitmodules</code> and eight recipes carrying an explicit URL in <code>.host-software</code>, and the resolver consults neither: <code>allium#12</code> resolves to <code>connollydavid/allium</code> where the recorded owner is <code>juxt</code>. In a fork every <code>--url</code> retargets to the contributor's namespace, where the tracker is disabled by default. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:235-243</code>.</p> <p><strong><code>--url</code> emits an anchor GitHub does not have.</strong> The site renders <code>{#write-spec}</code> as literal heading text and slugifies the whole line, so the emitted fragment matches no element and the reader lands at the top of a long document. The markdown form is correct, because mdBook honours the explicit id; the URL form is wrong across 151 headings in this tree. The settled conditional says the anchor is preserved through all three forms so a task node resolves to its heading, and for one of the three it does not. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:271</code>.</p> <h3 id="a-false-resolution-verdict"><a class="header" href="#a-false-resolution-verdict">A false resolution verdict</a></h3> <p><strong>Two entries sharing a number resolve to the alphabetically first, in silence.</strong> A milestone directory beside an abandoned draft of the same number yields a confident path to the draft, at exit 0, and nothing else in the binary gates the collision. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:138-139</code>.</p> <p><strong>First match wins plus a README existence gate turns a present milestone into a gating dead pointer.</strong> A stub directory that sorts first, and a milestone whose record is the directory rather than a README, both produce <code>names no entry in that room</code> at exit 1 about a room that demonstrably holds the entry. The design review carried this as wording; it gates. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:139-142</code>.</p> <p><strong><code>resolve</code> reports a verdict for a root it never read.</strong> The root is positional and unchecked, and an unrecognised flag falls through to become the root, so a mistyped <code>--md</code> produces the governing-host explanation at exit 1 inside the repository that owns the room. This is the sibling of the empty-corpus finding the cast round fixed for the sweep and never applied to the resolver. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:544-560</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-block-grammar-admits-prose-and-rejects-code"><a class="header" href="#the-block-grammar-admits-prose-and-rejects-code">The block grammar admits prose and rejects code</a></h3> <p><strong>A fenced block inside a blockquote is read as prose</strong>, which raises a false dead pointer at exit 1. An indented code block and an HTML comment do the same. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:405</code>.</p> <p><strong>An unbalanced backtick hides every reference after it on the line.</strong> A code span wrapped across a line break is legal and present here, so four live references in this tree are invisible to the sweep today, one of them a register reference in <code>plan/0053</code>. Odd fence-line parity swallows the whole tail of a document. This is the fail-unsafe direction: the gate loses a dead pointer rather than raising a false one. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:377-379</code>, <code>:404-411</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-wall-is-not-the-size-it-reports"><a class="header" href="#the-wall-is-not-the-size-it-reports">The wall is not the size it reports</a></h3> <p><strong>"They name no repository" is false for the references it counted.</strong> Every issue reference outside a link is classified as unrendered without consulting the repository it names, so <code>connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1</code> is counted and described as naming no repository. Distinct repositories on one line collapse into one finding, two occurrences of one number collapse, and a URL fragment, an HTML comment and an indented code block each count. In <code>PLAN.md</code> alone, most <code>#N</code> occurrences are already qualified. Three lenses recorded it. The reported wall of 293 conflates two populations, and the remediation node inherits the error. Defect: <code>src/refs.rs:425</code>, <code>:428-431</code>, <code>:491</code>.</p> <h3 id="the-migration-read-for-the-first-time"><a class="header" href="#the-migration-read-for-the-first-time">The migration, read for the first time</a></h3> <p><strong>The ledger's verify condition greps the token; the tool renames the key.</strong> <code>migrate_recipe_text</code> rewrites a line matching the key form and preserves comments, values and longer keys by design and by test. The ledger asserts the token appears nowhere in the file. An adopter whose recipe carries one annotation comment naming the old key runs the migration, is told it succeeded, and can then never record the upgrade: <code>upgrade --record</code> refuses at exit 1 and <code>software --check</code> raises a permanent hazard with no tool remedy. A recipe migrated correctly and then annotated goes red the same way. Defect: <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md:315</code> and <code>:322</code> against <code>src/main.rs:8644</code>.</p> <p><strong><code>migrate-recipe --dry-run</code> writes, and <code>migrate-recipe --help</code> migrates the working directory.</strong> Every argument that starts with a dash is discarded, the first remaining one becomes the target, and the default target is the working directory. Three sibling verbs in this same CLI accept <code>--dry-run</code>, which makes it the natural probe on the one verb that rewrites the reproducibility anchor. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:8690</code>.</p> <p><strong>A symlinked recipe is replaced by a regular file.</strong> The atomic write renames over the link, so the real recipe stays unmigrated, the tree gains a second divergent recipe, and the tool reports success. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:6930</code>.</p> <p><strong>A recipe with Windows line endings is silently converted.</strong> The migration reads by lines and rejoins with a bare newline, so a working recipe becomes a whole-file diff reported as one change. The ledger's own text promises every other line is untouched. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:8647</code>, <code>:8678</code>.</p> <p><strong>call/0047's consequence that every line an operator reads names the surviving key is false.</strong> The release path prints the retired spelling on both of its messages, one of them the refusal that tells an operator their component carries no waiver. The spine still documents the retired key in the multi-platform builds section, in the tool's own recipe reference, and in the reference CI comment; the retirement entry's title says the case is recorded with the old name while its action says the new one, and the title is what an operator is shown on record. Defect: <code>src/main.rs:9221</code> and <code>:9497</code>; <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md:854</code>; <code>host-template/tools/host-lifecycle/README.md:151</code>; <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md:311</code>; <code>host-template/.github/workflows/reproducible-build.yml:3</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-structural-finding"><a class="header" href="#the-structural-finding">The structural finding</a></h2> <p>Every finding in the coverage class sits outside what the specification can catch. The reason is structural: <code>host-lifecycle-refs.allium</code> models a reference and stops there, so its universe begins where a reference already exists, with the walk and the corpus outside it. <code>CleanVerdictSawNothing</code> therefore proves one thing only, that a clean verdict reported nothing, and it stays silent on whether everything was read. <code>ExcludedIsNeverReported</code> quantifies over a per-reference field while the implementation decides exclusion per document, in a function the specification does not model. Every finding in the first two sections above sits outside what the obligations can bite on, which is why they survived a discharge-clean manifest. Defect: <code>host-lifecycle-refs.allium:118-133</code>, <code>:214-227</code>, <code>:281</code>.</p> <h2 id="carried-with-the-reason"><a class="header" href="#carried-with-the-reason">Carried, with the reason</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Nothing runs the sweep.</strong> No lane, no verify step, no skill. The diff adds specification lanes for a capability nothing invokes. Carried from the design review, unchanged, and it bounds the blast radius of every gating finding above to human and agent invocation.</li> <li><strong>A mistyped register number is invisible.</strong> The grammar matches four digits exactly, so <code>plan/074</code> and <code>call/45</code> never enter the corpus, and <code>plan/0074x</code> resolves as a different reference.</li> <li><strong>No percent-encoding in any emission form.</strong> Bounded by the slug convention, which nothing enforces.</li> <li><strong>The default branch falls back to a literal <code>main</code></strong> on a detached head, which is what a lane checkout gives.</li> <li><strong>Shorthand hex colours of three and four digits</strong> are still counted as issue numbers; the six and eight digit forms were fixed.</li> <li><strong>The anchor is never validated</strong>, though <code>validate</code> rejects the identical token as a task reference.</li> <li><strong>The dead summary still prints a placeholder</strong> of the form the weak-agent acceptance records the model pasting verbatim, and which was removed from the advisory and refusal lines for that reason.</li> <li><strong>The migration widens file permissions</strong>, overrides a read-only recipe, and destroys a sibling file named for its temporary, all inherited from the shared atomic write.</li> <li><strong>A recipe carrying both spellings</strong> lets the retired line win by order and migrates into a silent duplicate key.</li> </ul> <h2 id="disposition-3"><a class="header" href="#disposition-3">Disposition</a></h2> <p>The operator ruled one pass over the whole set, specification included, on the reasoning that fixing instances of a class that has recurred three times leaves the fourth to be found by somebody else.</p> <p><strong>Every blocking finding above is fixed</strong>, in <code>58dd019</code> and <code>1b166fa</code> (host-lifecycle) and <code>e830c70</code> (host-template). The structural finding is fixed first, because it is the reason the rest survived a discharge-clean manifest: the specification now carries a document, a readability fact and an exclusion fact, and three invariants that bite on the corpus rather than on the reference. Each new disposition names a test that drives the built binary over a corpus with a known hole in it, and each was proven by mutation: reverting the unread gate, the disclosure, or the remedy slug fails its named test, and the restored tree is green.</p> <p>Two of the fixes were narrowed on the evidence rather than applied as reported:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Shorthand hex colours of three and four digits stay in the corpus.</strong> Excluding them would drop <code>#123</code> written as issue 123, which this tree is far likelier to contain than a bare colour outside code, and the block grammar now removes the places a colour actually appears. The six-digit rule stands.</li> <li><strong>The earlier ledger entries keep the retired spelling.</strong> They are history, they run before the rename entry in ledger order, and the migration cleans up what they wrote. Rewriting them would make the ledger disagree with what an adopter applying it in order actually does.</li> </ul> <p>The carried list is carried still, with one promotion: <strong>nothing runs the sweep</strong> is now the largest remaining gap, because the capability is correct and still surfaces nowhere. It is the <code>#remediate-this-tree</code> node's dependency and is recorded there rather than here.</p> <p>One measured consequence worth stating: under the corrected grammar and classification this tree's own wall is 297 issue references rather than the 293 reported before, and 183 of them name no repository. The earlier number was both too small (four live references sat behind an unmatched backtick) and wrong in kind (qualified references were counted as naming none). <code>#remediate-this-tree</code> inherits the corrected figure.</p> <h2 id="what-the-review-attacked-and-could-not-break"><a class="header" href="#what-the-review-attacked-and-could-not-break">What the review attacked and could not break</a></h2> <p>The acceptance rests on this as much as on the findings.</p> <p><code>refs --fix</code> never writes: eight argument combinations all refuse, and the tree hashes identically before and after. <code>MEMORY.md</code> is genuinely excluded by construction, at any depth, in a fresh scaffold with no list authored, and in the component worktree. A freshly scaffolded project's append-only log is never pressed. The empty-corpus fail-closed holds for a nonexistent directory, a directory that is not a repository, a file passed as a directory, and an empty repository. Untracked authored markdown is swept. Every one of the 127 distinct register references in this tree was resolved and the emitted path stated: 125 exist, none is a phantom, and the two unresolved are illustrative references inside ignore fences. Sweeping the entire tree with every exclusion removed finds no dead register pointer hiding in the record layer, so the exclusion currently hides legibility debt alone. Nested repositories are not descended into. The migration's wrong-line resistance is clean against a token in a URL, in a value, in a comment, as a longer key and in another component's section, and byte-identity on an unchanged file is proven with <code>cmp</code>. Idempotence holds. The dual parse is equivalent on stdout, with the deprecation on stderr alone. Both ledger verify conditions can fail, so neither joins the vacuous class this project has found 25 members of.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0077-design-review-the-cast-reads-the-built-diff"><a class="header" href="#plan0077-design-review-the-cast-reads-the-built-diff">plan/0077 design-review: the cast reads the built diff</a></h1> <p>Date: 2026-07-23. Subject: the reference resolver and sweep, <code>4f27c7a..06fa455</code> in host-lifecycle.</p> <p>This document was written after its receipt, which is itself a finding: the <code>#cast-consult</code> receipt named this path in its verify line while the file did not exist, and two chairs found that independently in the next consultation. The record is repaired here rather than quietly; see the closing note.</p> <h2 id="who-read-it-1"><a class="header" href="#who-read-it-1">Who read it</a></h2> <p>Mara, Bly, Orin and Wren each read the plan, the built diff and the sources their lens calls for, and each ran the built binary against this host (two rooms), the component worktree (no rooms), and fixtures of their own. Fen's contribution is the weak-agent acceptance in <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/fen-acceptance.html">fen-acceptance.md</a>, which failed the advisory state across three output revisions.</p> <h2 id="the-blocking-set-and-where-it-came-from"><a class="header" href="#the-blocking-set-and-where-it-came-from">The blocking set, and where it came from</a></h2> <p><strong>A bare <code>#N</code> was resolved against whatever remote happened to be local.</strong> Mara reproduced it: <code>resolve '#8' --markdown .</code> in this host emits a link to <em>agentic-host</em> issue 8, while the reference it came from (<code>plan/0024-sound-discharge/README.md</code>) means host-lifecycle issue 8. Every one of the 182 bare references the sweep counted would have been rewritten to the wrong tracker by the remedy the tool printed. An issue reference now names its repository, <code>component#N</code> takes the origin's owner, and a bare number is refused with the form to write instead.</p> <p><strong>The clean line was printed after reading zero documents.</strong> Bly ran it against a nonexistent directory and against a directory that is not a git repository: both printed "every reference in the authored docs resolves and renders", exit 0. The verdict now names how many documents were swept and fails closed when the walk finds none.</p> <p><strong>The clean line also claimed coverage of references it had skipped.</strong> In a software repository every register reference is skipped by design (the numbers belong to the governing host), and the verdict said nothing about them. It now counts them and says they were not checked.</p> <p><strong>A freshly scaffolded project has no exclusion list</strong>, so its append-only log was swept and told to rewrite itself on day one. Mara traced it precisely: <code>scaffold</code> writes no <code>.host-lintignore</code>, so the record-layer exclusion was conditional on the operator having already authored one. The record layer is now excluded by construction.</p> <p><strong>Untracked markdown was invisible.</strong> Wren's finding: an agent that authors a document, runs the sweep, sees clean and commits has verified nothing. The walk now includes untracked-but-not-ignored files.</p> <p><strong>The forge-URL constructions were untested, and Bly proved it by mutation</strong> — replacing both with a wrong host left 278 unit and 11 integration tests green. They now have a test that gives its fixture a real remote and asserts the URLs byte for byte.</p> <p><strong>The register <code>--url</code> emission was untested by the same method</strong>, and <code>blob/main</code> was hardcoded, handing a 404 to any repository on another default branch. Both fixed.</p> <p><strong>A CSS colour was counted as an issue number</strong>, as was a reference-style link. Fixed for the colour; the reference-style link is carried.</p> <h2 id="carried-not-fixed"><a class="header" href="#carried-not-fixed">Carried, not fixed</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Room names are hardcoded and must sit at the repository root</strong> (Orin). A project that renamed its rooms, or nests them under <code>docs/</code>, gets a clean verdict from a tool that read nothing. The fix is either to read the names from <code>.host</code> or to say plainly that no room was found; it is carried to the adversarial node, because it is the same class as the sweep's other coverage claims.</li> <li><strong>Non-GitHub forges and GitHub Enterprise</strong> are not recognised: <code>origin_slug</code> matches the literal <code>github.com</code>, so a self-hosted forge gets an advisory whose remedy cannot run.</li> <li><strong>A fork silently retargets every URL</strong>, because the tool has no notion of an upstream.</li> <li><strong>A milestone directory with no README</strong> is reported as "names no entry in that room", which is false: the directory is the record.</li> <li><strong>Nothing runs the sweep.</strong> No CI lane, no verify recheck, no skill step. The capability ships and nothing surfaces it, which is the finding that most resembles the gap plan/0074 was filed to close.</li> <li><strong>The <code>unresolved here</code> message asserts the governing-host explanation even in a repository that owns the room</strong>, so a wrong working directory is diagnosed as a wrong repository.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-closing-note-which-is-itself-a-finding"><a class="header" href="#the-closing-note-which-is-itself-a-finding">The closing note, which is itself a finding</a></h2> <p>The <code>#cast-consult</code> receipt was recorded before this document existed, with a verify line naming it. The receipt's evidence string was accurate about the findings and false about the artifact, and the task gate accepted it because it checks neither. Two chairs found it in the very next consultation, one of them citing it as the same hollow-discharge shape the previous milestone had just learned to name.</p> <p>The mechanical remedy is small and is recorded as owed: <code>tasks --record</code> should refuse a receipt whose verify line names a path that does not exist on disk.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0077-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-sweep"><a class="header" href="#plan0077-fen-acceptance-the-real-qwen35-4b-reads-the-sweep">plan/0077 fen-acceptance: the real qwen3.5-4b reads the sweep</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-23</li> <li>Model and parameters: as in <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/../0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/fen-acceptance.html">plan/0074</a>, the model card's thinking settings, two repeats per probe.</li> <li>Protocol: the built binary produced the real output for each state (a dead pointer in a fixture host, the advisory wall in this repository, a resolved reference, and the refusal described below). Each probe hands the model the verbatim output and asks for its single next action. Probes and transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/reference-resolver/</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-passed-on-the-first-reading"><a class="header" href="#what-passed-on-the-first-reading">What passed on the first reading</a></h2> <p>The dead-pointer state and the resolved reference both passed, stable across repeats:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">dead repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0091 . dead repeat 2: ACTION: Run host-lifecycle resolve plan/0091 . to check the reference and fix the dead pointer resolve repeat 1: ACTION: Insert `[plan/0074](plan/0074-.../README.md)` into the document. resolve repeat 2: ACTION: add citation to document </code></pre> <p>Both dead-pointer repeats run the exact command the output names, on the reference it names. Both resolve repeats treat the markdown link as something to paste into the document, which is the whole point of the emission.</p> <h2 id="what-did-not-three-revisions-running"><a class="header" href="#what-did-not-three-revisions-running">What did not, three revisions running</a></h2> <p>The advisory state failed every time, and the failures are worth recording because each revision fixed the defect it was aimed at and the model found the next one:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">first output → ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve '#N' --markdown /path (pasted my placeholder verbatim) → ACTION: host-lifecycle refs --fix . (invented a flag) after naming a real reference in the line → ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve (truncated the long line) → ACTION: Fix all bare issue references ... using resolve (a plan, not an action) after splitting into three short lines, the command alone on the last → ACTION: host-lifecycle refs --fix . (invented the flag again) → ACTION: Fix 293 bare issue references by converting them (a plan, not an action) after rewriting the line to say no flag fixes this → ACTION: fix_issue_references (invented a function) → ACTION: Run host-lifecycle refs --fix . (invented the flag again) </code></pre> <p>The pattern is stable: shown a report of hundreds of items, this model reaches for a fix flag whatever the text says. Three rewrites of the line did not change that, and a fourth would be optimism rather than engineering.</p> <h2 id="the-mitigation-and-its-evidence"><a class="header" href="#the-mitigation-and-its-evidence">The mitigation, and its evidence</a></h2> <p><code>refs --fix</code> now exists for one purpose: to refuse, with the reason and with a concrete next command naming a real reference from the tree. The wrong turn the model reliably takes is answered rather than punished with a usage error. Probing the refusal:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">refusal repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 --markdown /mnt/.../agentic-host refusal repeat 2: ACTION: Run `host-lifecycle resolve connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 --markdown /mnt/.../agentic-host` </code></pre> <p>Both repeats run the exact command the refusal printed. The loop closes: advisory output, invented flag, refusal that teaches, correct action. An earlier version of the refusal wrote the command as <code>resolve owner/repo#N --markdown <dir></code> and both repeats pasted the placeholders verbatim, which is why the refusal names a real reference from the tree instead.</p> <h2 id="the-honest-verdict"><a class="header" href="#the-honest-verdict">The honest verdict</a></h2> <p>Three of four states pass at the 4B bar directly. The advisory state does not, and no wording tested here makes it. What the acceptance establishes is weaker and still worth having: whichever of its two wrong turns the model takes, the tool answers with the reason and a command that works, and the model then runs it.</p> <h2 id="the-re-run-after-the-adversarial-round-changed-every-output"><a class="header" href="#the-re-run-after-the-adversarial-round-changed-every-output">The re-run, after the adversarial round changed every output</a></h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-26. The adversarial round rewrote the text of all four states, so this acceptance was resting on revisions that no longer exist. It was re-run against the real output of the fixed binary, same model, same parameters, two repeats per state.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">dead repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0091 . dead repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0091 . resolve repeat 1: ACTION: update-document-with-citation resolve repeat 2: ACTION: Insert the resolved markdown citation for plan/0074#write-spec into the document. refusal repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 --markdown . refusal repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 --markdown . advisory repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle refs --fix . (the invented flag, again) advisory repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve --markdown . (the command, truncated) </code></pre> <p>The verdict is unchanged: three states pass, the advisory state does not. Two things did change, and both are recorded rather than smoothed over.</p> <p><strong>The dead state improved for a reason this round found.</strong> The summary used to print <code>resolve <ref> <dir></code>, the placeholder shape this document records the model pasting verbatim; it now names the reference it found, and both repeats run it.</p> <p><strong>A first attempt at the re-run scored the resolve state as failing, and that was the probe's fault rather than the tool's.</strong> The rewritten probe had dropped the task framing the original carried (that the agent is writing a document and wants the site to link). Re-run with the framing matched, both repeats insert the link. The failing pair is discarded as a malformed probe, on the same footing as plan/0076's spoiled ballot: a probe that changed two things at once measures neither.</p> <p><strong>The advisory state's second wrong turn is new.</strong> The model invented no flag this time. It truncated the printed command to <code>resolve --markdown .</code> and dropped the reference. That landed on a bare usage error, which teaches nothing. The usage error now names a real reference from the tree, exactly as the <code>--fix</code> refusal does, and the probe closes the loop:</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">truncation repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0001 --markdown . truncation repeat 2: ACTION: Run host-lifecycle resolve plan/0001 --markdown . </code></pre> <p>Both of the advisory state's wrong turns are now answered by a refusal that names something real, and the model runs what it is given. The acceptance still rests on that weaker claim rather than on the advisory line reading correctly, and a fifth rewrite of that line would still be optimism.</p> <h2 id="what-this-did-not-test-2"><a class="header" href="#what-this-did-not-test-2">What this did not test</a></h2> <p>The register half of the sweep in a repository that owns no room (the tool reports the count and skips them, and how that line reads at the 4B bar is untested), and the resolver's <code>--url</code> emission, which was probed only through the integration tests.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-the-naming-probe-and-the-settled-conditionals-2026-07-23"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-the-naming-probe-and-the-settled-conditionals-2026-07-23">gather-data: the naming probe and the settled conditionals (2026-07-23)</a></h1> <p>This records the #gather-data node. Two names were settled by the real weak agent, the rest by measurement of this tree and by the doctrine already in force.</p> <h2 id="channel-1"><a class="header" href="#channel-1">Channel</a></h2> <p>The gateway's OpenAI-compatible surface at the model card's thinking parameters, identical to the matrices recorded in <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/../0076-dream-store-model/gather-data.html">plan/0076</a> and <a href="plan/0077-reference-resolver/../0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/fen-acceptance.html">plan/0074</a>. Each question ran twice with the option order rotated, so a first-position artefact is detectable. Probes and transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/reference-resolver/</code> on the operator's machine.</p> <h2 id="decision-1-the-verb-that-resolves-one-reference"><a class="header" href="#decision-1-the-verb-that-resolves-one-reference">Decision 1: the verb that resolves one reference</a></h2> <p>Given the sibling subcommands and a description of a command that turns <code>plan/0074</code>, <code>call/0045</code> or <code>plan/0074#write-spec</code> into a path, a markdown link or a GitHub URL:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Candidate</th><th>order 1</th><th>order 2</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><strong>resolve</strong></td><td><strong>A, chosen</strong></td><td><strong>D, chosen</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>link</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr> <tr><td>ref</td><td>C</td><td>B</td></tr> <tr><td>locate</td><td>D</td><td>A</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Chosen in both rotations from opposite ends of the list. <strong>Settled: <code>host-lifecycle resolve <ref></code>.</strong></p> <h2 id="decision-2-how-the-sweep-is-invoked"><a class="header" href="#decision-2-how-the-sweep-is-invoked">Decision 2: how the sweep is invoked</a></h2> <p>Given the sibling checks and a description of a sweep that reports references the published site cannot render:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Candidate</th><th>order 1</th><th>order 2</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><strong><code>refs --check <dir></code></strong></td><td><strong>A, chosen</strong></td><td><strong>D, chosen</strong></td></tr> <tr><td><code>resolve --check <dir></code></td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr> <tr><td><code>validate --refs <dir></code></td><td>C</td><td>B</td></tr> <tr><td><code>prose --refs <dir></code></td><td>D</td><td>A</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Rotation-proof again, and the pair reads coherently: <code>resolve</code> acts on one reference, <code>refs --check</code> sweeps a tree. <strong>Settled: <code>host-lifecycle refs --check <dir></code>.</strong> The sweep is its own mode rather than a flag on <code>validate</code> or <code>prose</code>, which matches the ruling that made the completeness gate a separate verify mode: one command, one question.</p> <h2 id="the-measured-wall"><a class="header" href="#the-measured-wall">The measured wall</a></h2> <p>Counted over this repository's authored markdown, outside fenced code:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Class</th><th>Count</th><th>Where</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Bare <code>#N</code> issue references</td><td>374 in 31 files</td><td>187 in <code>MEMORY.md</code>, 35 in <code>plan/0072/signals-digest.md</code>, 18 in <code>PLAN.md</code>, the rest spread across milestone READMEs</td></tr> <tr><td>Distinct <code>plan/NNNN</code> and <code>call/NNNN</code> references</td><td>122</td><td>every one resolves by hand; none resolves by tool</td></tr> <tr><td>Unresolvable register references</td><td>0</td><td>this tree has no dead register pointer today</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Two facts follow. Nothing in the register half is broken here, so its check can gate from the day it lands. The issue-number half carries 374 references, and 222 of them sit in files that are never rewritten.</p> <h2 id="the-settled-conditionals"><a class="header" href="#the-settled-conditionals">The settled conditionals</a></h2> <h3 id="the-exit-split"><a class="header" href="#the-exit-split">The exit split</a></h3> <p><code>0</code> clean, <code>3</code> advisory-only, <code>1</code> when any register reference resolves to nothing, <code>2</code> on a usage or IO error. This is the dream audit's split (call/0045) applied to a second surface, and the reasoning carries: a <code>plan/0099</code> that points at nothing is a dead pointer, mechanically evidenced and worth gating; a bare <code>#N</code> is legibility debt, real but not a defect in the record, and a wall of 374 that turns a tree red on the day it lands teaches an adopter to bypass the gate.</p> <h3 id="the-record-layer-exclusion"><a class="header" href="#the-record-layer-exclusion">The record-layer exclusion</a></h3> <p><code>.host-lintignore</code>, the list the prose gate already honours, which in this repository already names <code>MEMORY.md</code> and the dated review artifacts. One exclusion list, not two: an operator who has decided that a file is a record should not have to say so once per checker. This is the concrete form of the append-only rule, which is why the adversarial node carries a lens for it: a checker that pressures an append-only log into being rewritten has broken the thing it was auditing.</p> <h3 id="the-emission-forms"><a class="header" href="#the-emission-forms">The emission forms</a></h3> <p>The path by default (<code>plan/0074-host-lifecycle-materialize-receipt-and-envhash/README.md</code>), <code>--markdown</code> for the link, <code>--url</code> for the full GitHub URL built from the origin remote. An <code>#anchor</code> is preserved through all three, so a task node resolves to its heading. A repository with no origin remote can still emit a path and a markdown link, and says plainly that it cannot build a URL.</p> <h3 id="the-cross-host-case"><a class="header" href="#the-cross-host-case">The cross-host case</a></h3> <p>A <code>plan/</code> or <code>call/</code> reference in a software repository belongs to its governing host and carries no repository name. The resolver reports <code>unresolved here</code> and names the room it searched, rather than guessing or passing silently. Teaching a software repository to name its owning host would make such a reference resolvable and is <strong>out of scope</strong>: it is a recipe change with its own spine doctrine, recorded here so it is not mistaken for an oversight.</p> <h3 id="what-the-sweep-reads"><a class="header" href="#what-the-sweep-reads">What the sweep reads</a></h3> <p>Authored markdown, by the same walk the prose gate uses, minus the exclusion list. Fenced code is skipped, because a fenced <code>#3</code> is an example rather than a reference, which is the rule the tell gate already applies to its own fixtures.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0078-the-sweep-runs-in-the-verify-gate-and-the-clauses-beside-it-stop-failing-open"><a class="header" href="#plan0078-the-sweep-runs-in-the-verify-gate-and-the-clauses-beside-it-stop-failing-open">plan/0078 the sweep runs in the verify gate, and the clauses beside it stop failing open</a></h1> <p>Decided by <a href="plan/0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/../../call/0048-the-gate-runs-the-sweep-over-the-record.html">call/0048</a>, after two cast review rounds and a question round. Closes the gap <a href="plan/0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/../0077-reference-resolver/README.html">plan/0077</a>'s adversarial round named as its largest: the reference sweep is correct and nothing invokes it.</p> <h2 id="why-15"><a class="header" href="#why-15">Why</a></h2> <p>The <code>verify</code> phase's recheck is the gate that re-derives a <code>done</code> receipt, and it is step one of <code>host-lifecycle release</code>. It chains <code>validate</code>, <code>prose</code> and <code>reconcile</code>. plan/0077 hardened a fourth checker against a defect none of those three is hardened against, and then left it unwired.</p> <p>So the accurate statement of the gap is not that a good tool goes unused. It is that <strong>the gate's existing clauses can report clean over a corpus with a hole in it, and the one walk that was fixed is the one nothing runs.</strong> Reproduced: a tracked document carrying a real tell, made unreadable, yields <code>prose: clean</code> at exit 0.</p> <p>Two more defects sit on the same path. The document walk includes the working tree, so an uncommitted note blocks a release over a file no clone contains. And the ledger entry that would ship any of this would, under the convention the ledger already uses, carry a verify condition its own command's precondition makes true.</p> <h2 id="what-the-convening-measured"><a class="header" href="#what-the-convening-measured">What the convening measured</a></h2> <p>Real qwen3.5-4b, two repeats per state, on output the built binary produced.</p> <ul> <li>Shown a <strong>green</strong> gate whose tail carried this tree's advisory census, the model abandoned its task to remediate references, in both repeats. The gate must not print the enumeration.</li> <li>Shown a <strong>dead pointer</strong>, both repeats ran the exact command the output named. That text is measured-good and is kept byte for byte.</li> <li>The naming probe failed on position and was redesigned as a comprehension probe. Both rule-legal spellings read correctly; neither invented a third exit code.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-19"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-19">Build sequence</a></h2> <p>Three landings, because pre-existing fixes, a behaviour change, and a template revision have different blast radii. Landings that share a blast radius may merge; these do not. Each ends in something recorded.</p> <p>Prerequisite, ahead of landing one: the owed ledger entry for the host-lint v0.15.0 pin, which reserved two words in the bare-argument position and made the canonical build produce a second binary, and which shipped as a bare pointer bump with no entry.</p> <p><strong>Landing one: the walks tell the truth, and a verify can fail.</strong></p> <h3 id="walk-reports-what-it-could-not-read"><a class="header" href="#walk-reports-what-it-could-not-read">A walk reports what it could not read</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: a tracked document made unreadable turns <code>prose</code> non-zero with a line naming the document, rather than reporting clean; the same holds for host-lifecycle's own walk; a walk that fails outright never becomes an empty document set</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="corpus-selector"><a class="header" href="#corpus-selector">The gate reads the record, the hook reads the working tree</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the document walk takes a corpus selector; an untracked file carrying a tell is reported by the hook and ignored by the gate path; the walk exists once, so no second walk drifts from it</li> <li>depends: #walk-reports-what-it-could-not-read</li> </ul> <h3 id="argument-is-honoured"><a class="header" href="#argument-is-honoured">A directory argument is honoured or refused</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>--all <dir></code> and <code>--docs <dir></code> audit the named directory rather than the tree resolved from the working directory, or exit as a usage error; a fixture under a different root proves which tree was read</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="remedy-names-a-real-reference"><a class="header" href="#remedy-names-a-real-reference">The printed remedy names something real</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: no emission attaches a guessed repository to a bare issue number, and none prints a placeholder shape either; a test asserts the remedy names a reference that exists in the tree, and mutating it fails that test</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="recheck-runs-everywhere"><a class="header" href="#recheck-runs-everywhere">The recheck runs, or says it could not</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the recheck chooses its shell per platform rather than assuming one, and a shell that cannot be spawned reports that it could not run, distinctly from a condition that did not hold</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="capability-probe"><a class="header" href="#capability-probe">A capability answers for itself</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: one command with no shell operators reports whether the running binary carries a named capability, reads no tree, refuses an unknown name, and draws from the same constant the feature is gated on; the engine version appears wherever the naming and prose surfaces speak</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="floor-enforced-or-owed"><a class="header" href="#floor-enforced-or-owed">The version floor is enforced or the deferral is recorded</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: either a tool below an entry's floor is refused at record time with the floor named, or an issue records the deferral and the ledger says the floor is advisory</li> <li>depends: #capability-probe</li> </ul> <h3 id="engine-bump"><a class="header" href="#engine-bump">The embedded engine matches the pinned one</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the vendored bundle is cut and published, the embedded revision moves to the released one, and one tree yields one verdict from both surfaces where two verdicts were demonstrated</li> <li>depends: #corpus-selector, #argument-is-honoured, #remedy-names-a-real-reference, #capability-probe</li> </ul> <p><strong>Landing two: the gate mode.</strong></p> <h3 id="spec-the-two-corpora"><a class="header" href="#spec-the-two-corpora">The two corpora in the model</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the spec models both walks, the corpus each judges, and the gate's exit partition, so an obligation can bite on a verdict claiming more than its walk read; <code>allium check</code> and <code>analyse</code> exit 0</li> <li>depends: #engine-bump</li> </ul> <h3 id="gate-mode"><a class="header" href="#gate-mode">The gate mode</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: exit 0 with no blocking finding, advisory included; exit 1 on a dead pointer, an unreadable document, or a corpus the walk could not produce, each with a line naming its own cause; the advisory is counted and never enumerated; the coverage line names which corpus it read; the empty-corpus case is specified rather than inherited</li> <li>depends: #spec-the-two-corpora</li> </ul> <h3 id="composition-test"><a class="header" href="#composition-test">The composition is executed</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: a fixture host with a <code>done</code> verify receipt and a dead pointer re-opens the receipt under <code>software --check</code> and exits non-zero; this is the first test that executes a manifest recheck string</li> <li>depends: #gate-mode</li> </ul> <h3 id="cost"><a class="header" href="#cost">The recheck stays cheap</a></h3> <ul> <li>budget, fixed before the measurement: the gate clause costs no more than the slowest clause already in the chain, and the whole recheck does not more than double. The manifest's own header says a recheck must be cheap, and this runs on every <code>software --check</code>, in the verify skill, and at the first step of every release</li> <li>verify: the chain is measured before and after on the same tree and the same mount; if either bound is exceeded the disposition is recorded here rather than noted in passing, because a node that measures and shrugs is not a gate</li> <li>measured, release build, this tree, a <code>/mnt/c</code> mount (read the figures as ratios, not absolutes): the budget was <strong>breached on the first measurement</strong>. the gate cost 9419 ms where the slowest existing clause cost 2285 ms, and the whole chain grew past triple, against a ceiling of double. The cause was algorithmic rather than inherent: resolving a register reference listed its room directory, and this tree carries upward of two thousand register references, so the run listed the same two directories two thousand times. The rooms are now read once per run and the verdict is byte-identical. The gate costs 2134 ms where the slowest existing clause costs 2438 ms, and the chain grows by half. Both bounds hold</li> <li>depends: #composition-test</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">The weak agent stays on task</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: two repeats per state on real output; the count-only gate is compared against a gate printing no quantity, and the comparison decides which ships; a spoiled probe is recorded as protocol data</li> <li>depends: #gate-mode</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-the-gate"><a class="header" href="#release-the-gate">The gate ships</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: released by the tool-carried sequence, re-pinned, and the binary on the path is the released one</li> <li>depends: #cost, #fen-acceptance</li> </ul> <p><strong>Landing three: the revision adopters receive.</strong></p> <h3 id="template-wiring"><a class="header" href="#template-wiring">The manifest calls the mode</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the recheck line is one verb per clause with no exit arithmetic; a comment above the stanza states why a reference advisory passes while a prose warning gates; the clause this milestone adds runs on every platform, because it is a <code>host-lifecycle</code> invocation rather than a shell builtin</li> <li>scoped, with the evidence: the manifest's four pre-existing <code>test -f</code> conditions stay POSIX-only and are <strong>not</strong> fixed here. They belong to the <code>adopt</code>, <code>embed</code> and <code>release</code> phases, which this milestone does not touch, and no portable stand-in exists for half of them: <code>host-lifecycle version .</code> covers the two <code>.host</code> conditions exactly, and for <code>.host-software</code> neither <code>reconcile</code> (exit 0 with and without a recipe), <code>version</code> (reads the stamp, not the recipe) nor <code>env --check</code> (exit 2 either way, conflated with an unrecorded fingerprint) can tell the two trees apart. Closing it needs a new read-only surface and therefore its own release, which is owed work rather than a clause of this one</li> <li>depends: #release-the-gate</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-bullets"><a class="header" href="#spine-bullets">The spine says where it runs</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the existing reference section names the gate, the corpus it judges, and the asymmetry with its reason; an adopter who reads only the spine learns that something gates and what</li> <li>depends: #template-wiring</li> </ul> <h3 id="ledger-entry"><a class="header" href="#ledger-entry">The entry an adopter can fail</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the condition is the capability probe, and a tree that SHOULD fail it does, meaning an environment whose binary predates the floor rather than a tree carrying a dead pointer, which must record as applied; the action text opens with the two facts a cold reader needs first</li> <li>depends: #spine-bullets</li> </ul> <h3 id="census-home"><a class="header" href="#census-home">The census has a home</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the enumeration is reachable by one documented command and appears in no gate path; the chosen home is probed in the window it will actually be read</li> <li>depends: #gate-mode</li> </ul> <h3 id="walk-it-here"><a class="header" href="#walk-it-here">It is applied here before it is shipped</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: this repository's own operating manual carries the reference discipline, the pending entry is recorded honestly rather than on a condition its own precondition satisfies, and the new entry is applied here</li> <li>depends: #ledger-entry</li> </ul> <h3 id="record-the-outcome"><a class="header" href="#record-the-outcome">The record</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the PLAN.md row and the MEMORY.md entry are written and pushed, each in its own commit</li> <li>depends: #walk-it-here</li> </ul> <h2 id="out-of-scope-recorded-so-it-is-not-assumed"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-recorded-so-it-is-not-assumed">Out of scope, recorded so it is not assumed</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The ledger's verify convention.</strong> Of 49 entries, 30 carry a condition and 26 grep the fetched template, which <code>upgrade</code> requires present before it will run. Those cannot refuse a false record nor detect a revert. This milestone fixes the shape for its own entry and sets the precedent; sweeping 26 shipped entries needs a documented map and its own milestone, on the discipline the append-only exception requires.</li> <li><strong>The remaining findings of the FFmpeg pack review</strong>, which stay with their own milestone: the pack here is a skeleton and nothing in it is calibrated.</li> <li><strong>A fix flag for the advisory half.</strong> plan/0077 refused one because only the author knows which tracker a bare number meant, and that refusal stands.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0078-fen-acceptance-the-gates-output-read-by-the-real-qwen35-4b"><a class="header" href="#plan0078-fen-acceptance-the-gates-output-read-by-the-real-qwen35-4b">plan/0078 fen-acceptance: the gate's output, read by the real qwen3.5-4b</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-27</li> <li>Model and parameters: as in <a href="plan/0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/../0077-reference-resolver/fen-acceptance.html">plan/0077</a>, the model card's thinking settings, two repeats per state.</li> <li>Protocol: the built release binary produced the output for every state, including the discarded variant, which was built and run rather than hand-edited. The framing is the one the earlier rounds used, word for word, so the output is the only thing that differs. Probes and transcripts: <code>~/agentic-host-work/verify-wiring/</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-this-round-had-to-decide-1"><a class="header" href="#what-this-round-had-to-decide-1">What this round had to decide</a></h2> <p>The round-one probe established the failure this milestone exists to avoid: shown a <strong>green</strong> gate whose tail carried this tree's per-file census, the model abandoned the task it was on and went to remediate references, in both repeats. The words "Advisory: nothing is blocked" were in front of it both times.</p> <p>That measured the whole tail at once: a ten-line per-file leaderboard, two counters, a permission sentence, and a runnable remedy. Nothing isolated which part carried the capture, and the project's own memory records that inferring from a probe that changed several things at once is exactly the mistake to avoid. So the design question stayed open: is a bare <strong>count</strong> safe, or must the gate report no quantity at all?</p> <p>The cast split on it. The plan's design prints the count and drops the enumeration; the executor's seat asked for no quantity, on the grounds that any cardinal attached to a reducible class is a work queue with a progress bar. That reading was explicitly unmeasured, and its author said so.</p> <h2 id="the-comparison"><a class="header" href="#the-comparison">The comparison</a></h2> <p>Two variants of the same green gate, each built and captured from the real binary.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">A, the count kept: -- 167 recorded doc(s) read; every register reference in them resolves. 239 issue reference(s) carry legibility debt, which this gate does not judge; run `host-lifecycle refs --check` to see them. B, no quantity: -- 167 recorded doc(s) read; every register reference in them resolves. Issue-link legibility is not judged here; `host-lifecycle refs --check` reports it. </code></pre> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">A repeat 1: ACTION: Hand work back to the operator. A repeat 2: ACTION: Verification passed; hand work back to operator B repeat 1: ACTION: Hand work back to the operator. B repeat 2: ACTION: Hand work back to operator </code></pre> <p><strong>The count is safe.</strong> Both variants keep the agent on task in both repeats, and nothing separates them. What captured the agent in round one was the enumeration, not the cardinal: a sorted per-file leaderboard with a truncation ellipsis and a runnable remedy reads as a queue, and <code>239</code> on its own does not.</p> <p>The count ships. The disclosure is a real obligation, since a gate that reported nothing about what it withheld would be the hollow-green shape this project names milestones after, and this round establishes that keeping it costs nothing measurable.</p> <h2 id="the-gating-state"><a class="header" href="#the-gating-state">The gating state</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">dead repeat 1: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0099 . dead repeat 2: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0099 . </code></pre> <p>Both repeats run the exact command the output names. The DEAD line and its remedy sentence are unchanged from plan/0077, which measured them good, and this round confirms they survive the move into a gate.</p> <h2 id="the-honest-verdict-1"><a class="header" href="#the-honest-verdict-1">The honest verdict</a></h2> <p>The gate's green state and its dead state both pass at the 4B bar, which is a stronger result than plan/0077 reached: that milestone's advisory state failed every wording tried, and the mitigation was a refusal that answered the wrong turn rather than an output that avoided it. Removing the enumeration is what changed, and it changed the measured behaviour.</p> <p>One caution against reading this too widely. The green state was probed on a tree whose gating half is clean. A tree that is simultaneously green on references and carrying a large census is the case measured here; a tree that gates for one reason while disclosing another was not.</p> <h2 id="what-this-did-not-test-3"><a class="header" href="#what-this-did-not-test-3">What this did not test</a></h2> <p>The unreadable-corpus state, which shares its text with the dead state's structure but was not separately probed. The census in whatever home <code>#census-home</code> gives it, which has to be probed in the window it will actually be read rather than this one. And the ledger entry's action text, which belongs to the landing that writes it.</p> <h2 id="the-census-home-probed-in-the-window-it-would-be-read"><a class="header" href="#the-census-home-probed-in-the-window-it-would-be-read">The census home, probed in the window it would be read</a></h2> <p>The plan required the census to have a home, and the upstream seat required that home to be probed where it will actually be read rather than in a generic window. The tempting candidate was the <code>verify</code> skill's <code>## Reflect</code> step, which already carries an advisory census of the same shape (<code>host-lint gather</code>, triaged rather than acted on wholesale) and whose stated purpose is that an agent perceives neither the register it emits nor what its own change staled.</p> <p>The executor's seat disqualified it in review, on the grounds that an agent inside the verify skill is asking whether it is done. That was an argument; this is a measurement.</p> <p>The item was written into the Reflect step in the skill's own idiom, framed as a reading rather than a work queue, and probed with the real output of <code>refs --check</code> on this tree.</p> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore">reflect repeat 1: ACTION: Fix the 19 issue references in plan/0074-.../README.md and the 7 in plan/0074-.../gather-data.md by wrapping them as owner/repo#N links reflect repeat 2: ACTION: Edit plan/0026-open-bug-closure/README.md and other flagged documentation files to wrap bare issue references in owner/repo#N links </code></pre> <p>Both repeats abandoned the task and began remediating named files. The framing did not save it, exactly as three rewrites of the advisory line failed to save plan/0077's advisory state: what captures the agent is the per-file list, wherever it is shown.</p> <p><strong>So the census gets no automatic home at all.</strong> It is reached by one documented command, <code>host-lifecycle refs --check <dir></code>, named in the gate's own output and in the spine beside the gate. It appears in no gate path and now in no skill step either. The edit was reverted rather than shipped.</p> <p>The result generalises past this milestone: an advisory census belongs in a window a human opened on purpose, and an agent's session is not one. The <code>gather</code> item that shares the Reflect step has never been probed, and on this evidence it should be.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0079-the-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact-guarded-where-it-is-authored"><a class="header" href="#plan0079-the-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact-guarded-where-it-is-authored">plan/0079 the spine is a rendered artifact, guarded where it is authored</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: cut 2026-08-02, not started</li> <li>Decides: <a href="plan/0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact/../../call/0053-the-spine-copy-is-re-derived-not-asserted.html">call/0053</a></li> </ul> <h2 id="why-16"><a class="header" href="#why-16">Why</a></h2> <p><a href="plan/0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact/../../call/0004-template-is-versioned-source.html">call/0004</a> chose copy-at-version on 2026-06-14 and this repository never made the copy. Measured on 2026-08-02 against the canonical <code>host-lint</code> artifact: no non-trivial line of the root <code>CLAUDE.md</code> or <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> is byte-identical to the template's, and <code>git log --follow</code> puts the manual at fewer than one hundred and forty lines continuously since adoption, against the template's thousand. The rule was ratified, promoted into the spine itself, and was not true for a single commit.</p> <p>Nothing detected it because nothing re-derives it. An artifact reproduces from its pin or the build lane fails; a rung re-runs in its recorded toolchain; a task's inputs are fingerprinted; every phase carries a closed recheck. The methodology re-derives everything except itself, and the spine arrives instead by an instruction to an agent: "Re-apply the spine doc changes across the span."</p> <p><a href="plan/0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact/../0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/README.html">plan/0078</a> recorded the downstream symptom and deferred it: twenty-six of the ledger's thirty-two <code>verify</code> conditions grep a template that <code>upgrade</code> requires present before it will run, so they can neither refuse a false record nor detect a revert. Those conditions are an author reaching for something checkable on the adopter's side and finding nothing there.
