This milestone builds the thing that was missing.</p> <h2 id="what-the-measurement-showed"><a class="header" href="#what-the-measurement-showed">What the measurement showed</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>this repo</th><th>template</th><th>byte-identical</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>CLAUDE.md</code>, non-trivial lines</td><td>77</td><td>814</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td><code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, non-trivial lines</td><td>15</td><td>84</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Three further readings, each taken rather than assumed:</p> <ul> <li>The spine as adopter root content already measures clean: naming and prose both exit zero, references exit zero. The bar this milestone must hold is met by the text as it stands.</li> <li>This repository's own manual exits three, on a paragraph the render deletes as subsumed doctrine. The single failing text is duplicated doctrine.</li> <li>The template's hooks directory is empty, so its commits pass ungated. Every line it holds ships verbatim to every adopter. <code>--install-hooks</code> covers the host and its materialized worktrees; a template held as a submodule falls outside that set.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-20"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-20">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="guard-the-source"><a class="header" href="#guard-the-source">Guard the source</a></h3> <ul> <li>band</li> </ul> <h3 id="template-hooks"><a class="header" href="#template-hooks">The template is guarded at its own commits</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the template repository carries the same commit hooks every other repository under this methodology carries; a commit staging spine text that flags is refused there rather than reported later; the installer reaches a template held as a submodule rather than only the host and its materialized worktrees</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="template-naming-ci"><a class="header" href="#template-naming-ci">The naming lane runs in the template's continuous integration</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the template's own workflow runs the naming audit beside the prose audit over its tracked files, and a planted spine tell reddens it; the second line holds when the first is bypassed</li> <li>depends: #template-hooks</li> </ul> <h3 id="address-the-reader"><a class="header" href="#address-the-reader">Address the reader</a></h3> <ul> <li>band</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-addresses-adopter"><a class="header" href="#spine-addresses-adopter">The spine addresses the project that holds it</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every sentence in the spine addresses the project holding it, so the text reads correctly once rendered into an adopter; the orientation a template reader needs moves to a file outside the render</li> <li>depends: #template-hooks</li> </ul> <h3 id="the-mechanism"><a class="header" href="#the-mechanism">The mechanism</a></h3> <ul> <li>band</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-render"><a class="header" href="#spine-render">A project's manual is rendered</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>spine --render</code> writes the root manual and structure map from the template at the stamped revision followed by the project's own fragment; a second run yields identical bytes; a project carrying no fragment renders the spine alone</li> <li>depends: #spine-addresses-adopter</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-check"><a class="header" href="#spine-check">The render is re-derived, not asserted</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>spine --check</code> re-renders and compares byte for byte, exits non-zero on any drift, prints the resolved executable path and version so the deriving binary is named rather than inferred, and fails closed when the template is absent or unreadable rather than reporting clean</li> <li>depends: #spine-render</li> </ul> <h3 id="stamp-spine-hash"><a class="header" href="#stamp-spine-hash">The stamp names bytes</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the stamp carries the rendered file's digest, written by the tool and never by hand, so a cold read establishes what text the project holds; a stamp lacking the field is migrated once rather than refused</li> <li>depends: #spine-render</li> </ul> <h3 id="verify-recheck-clause"><a class="header" href="#verify-recheck-clause">The check is protected core</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the clause runs in the verify phase's recheck, refuses a skip receipt outright, and carries no waiver key and no advisory tier; a hand-edited manual re-opens the verify receipt and stops a release at its first step, proven on a tree rather than only in a fixture</li> <li>depends: #spine-check, #stamp-spine-hash</li> </ul> <h3 id="reconcile-fragment"><a class="header" href="#reconcile-fragment">The fragment cannot become a second source</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: reconcile reads the fragment and reports a restatement of any concept that has a spine home, so the paraphrase that produced zero shared lines here is caught rather than silently accepted</li> <li>depends: #spine-render</li> </ul> <h3 id="acceptance"><a class="header" href="#acceptance">The loop survives a weak reader</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the render and check outputs are put in front of a materially weaker model together with the exit code, and one correct next action comes back; where the local model cannot be driven the substitution is recorded and the claim is left unproven rather than asserted</li> <li>depends: #spine-check</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-host-lifecycle"><a class="header" href="#release-host-lifecycle">The mechanism ships</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: released through the tool-carried sequence authorized by call/0053, the artifact re-derived in its recorded toolchain, the pin and the release receipt recorded, and the component pushed before the host commit that pins it</li> <li>depends: #verify-recheck-clause, #reconcile-fragment, #template-naming-ci, #acceptance</li> </ul> <h3 id="the-migration"><a class="header" href="#the-migration">The migration</a></h3> <ul> <li>band</li> </ul> <h3 id="migrate-this-repo"><a class="header" href="#migrate-this-repo">This repository holds the spine</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the root manual is the render; this project's own text lives in its fragment and restates no spine rule; <code>spine --check</code> is clean here; the rendered files carry zero findings at the flagging and the warning tier both</li> <li>depends: #release-host-lifecycle</li> </ul> <h3 id="ledger-entry"><a class="header" href="#ledger-entry">Adopters are told once, structurally</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: one ledger entry whose action is structural rather than prose, whose condition tests the adopter's own tree, and which can actually fail; proven against a binary built before the change</li> <li>depends: #migrate-this-repo</li> </ul> <h2 id="out-of-scope-and-recorded"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-and-recorded">Out of scope, and recorded</a></h2> <ul> <li>The disposition of the fifty-one existing ledger entries once regeneration carries the prose half. They are append-only and stay. Whether a later entry supersedes a class of them is a separate decision.</li> <li>Whether the structure map takes a fragment slot of its own or stays spine-only. It is rendered either way.</li> <li>The ledger's own <code>verify</code> convention, where a condition resolves its tool from the environment rather than from the binary running the gate. Found on 2026-08-02 beside this work, it belongs to the ledger rather than to the spine, and it is left for the decision that settles what a ledger entry claims.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0080-commit-message-faults"><a class="header" href="#plan0080-commit-message-faults">plan/0080: commit-message faults</a></h1> <p>Mechanize what calibration supports. Trigger: <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/28">connollydavid/host-lint#28</a>, operator-filed. Four faults recur in commit messages and pass the prose lane. Decided by <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/../../call/0054-one-commit-message-fault-earns-a-detector.html">call/0054</a>; bundles the <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/24">connollydavid/host-lint#24</a> carve-out remainder, closure-queue position five. Single-component: the hook dispatch script is host-lint's own file, which host-lifecycle only copies at install.</p> <h2 id="calibration"><a class="header" href="#calibration">Calibration</a></h2> <p>Run before design, over 922 accepted commits across seven repositories (<a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/calibrate-28.py">calibrate-28.py</a>, raw readings in <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/calibration-28.txt">calibration-28.txt</a>).</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>measurement</th><th>result</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>restated comment sentences, eight-word bar</td><td>19</td></tr> <tr><td>the same at bars of five and twelve</td><td>22 and 7</td></tr> <tr><td>subject matches that are the record-title convention</td><td>12 of 12</td></tr> <tr><td>precedent-as-defence patterns, widened</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The heading sweep for the carve-out (<a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/calibrate-24.py">calibrate-24.py</a>): 240 tracked markdown files across ten stores, 2036 headings, zero ordinal-scaffold shapes, so the tier demotion changes no current verdict.</p> <h2 id="landed"><a class="header" href="#landed">Landed</a></h2> <p>Two commits on host-lint main, folded to one per issue by operator direction:</p> <ul> <li><code>3a6af0a</code>: the <code>commit</code> verb with the message and staged diff as named files, the calibrated advisory that names the safe direction, and a no-diff run that discloses the unrun check as a note; the commit-msg hook dispatch (usage-banner detection, staged-diff capture, <code>--stdin</code> fallbacks that name the unrun check); SKILL.md guidance for the unenforced faults. Mutation-proved: subject inclusion and the eight-word bar each redden exactly one test.</li> <li><code>550aa87</code>: the ordinal-scaffold heading demoted to the advisory tier, the LEXICON carve-out for declared designators with strict escalation naming the declaration command, and the VOCABULARY entry the original rule shipped without.</li> </ul> <h2 id="compatibility-surface"><a class="header" href="#compatibility-surface">Compatibility surface</a></h2> <p>The hook detects the verb by the usage banner's <code>host-lint commit --message</code> line. Rewording that line in a later release degrades every installed hook to <code>--stdin</code> until a reinstall (disclosed, but easy to miss), so the banner's commit line is part of the hook contract. The contract is test-backed: the integration case asserting the <code>re-run:</code> line reddens if the dispatch stops reaching the verb.</p> <h2 id="acceptance-1"><a class="header" href="#acceptance-1">Acceptance</a></h2> <p>The convening record is <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/convening.html">convening.md</a> (input: <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/briefing.html">briefing.md</a>); ballots, tally and the settled design live there, summarized in call/0054. Fen was simulated: every probe channel refused connection. The probe kit is preserved here: <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-p1.txt">fen-p1.txt</a>, <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-p1-worded.txt">fen-p1-worded.txt</a>, <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-p2.txt">fen-p2.txt</a>, the no-think runner <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-program.py">fen-program.py</a>, and the thinking-protocol runner <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-program-think.py">fen-program-think.py</a>. The operator sign-off of 2026-08-07 (call/0054) shipped the release on the labeled simulation, with the probes owed.</p> <p>The owed probes ran 2026-08-08 on the real model and the obligation is discharged; the release was never contingent on this run. Channel: the gateway behind TLS at api.d07yx58.net, served model <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> confirmed from the response body (quantization as served is unstated; the cast card names Q8_0). Protocol: thinking on at the Qwen3.5-4B card's thinking-general sampling, the plan/0076 corrected protocol, by operator direction, because a probe that suppresses the model's reasoning channel tests an artificially weakened agent. A first attempt with the no-think kit truncated all sixteen cells at its 500-token cap (this deployment reasons regardless of the request's <code>enable_thinking</code> key) and is preserved unedited in <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-results-spoiled-truncated.html">fen-results-spoiled-truncated.md</a>, whose header's "direct unsloth endpoint" label is the discovery branch's name for the same gateway. The transcripts are <a href="plan/0080-commit-message-faults/fen-results.html">fen-results.md</a>.</p> <p>Measured against the recorded tally, which the discharge does not rewrite: Q3, Q4 and Q5 are stable across both option orders and match the simulated ballot's first preference and the settled outcome. Q2 is a stable divergence, real Fen preferring the option that also checks documentation files; had that ballot stood in the convening, the settled option still carries 4 to 1. Q1 returned no usable signal, both orders ranking by presentation position with contradictory reasons, which the order rotation exists to catch; a model that ranks by position is itself a case for the ergonomic accommodation the simulated dissent bought: the hook prints the exact re-run line. Neither behavioral prediction reproduced (0 of 2 draws each): P1-bare chose the safe direction, trim the message and keep the comment, without the worded hint, and P2's revision carries no precedent residue. The floor requirements ship unchanged as guards; two draws on one deployment do not retire a tail risk. Every settled decision stands.</p> <h2 id="release"><a class="header" href="#release">Release</a></h2> <p>host-lint, change class <code>changes-output</code>: a heading verdict that blocked yesterday is advisory today, and one class covers the release with the severest honest reading. Released 2026-08-07 as v0.18.0 (<code>ba3cf1e</code>, canonical hash <code>ab720b3e</code>), then 2026-08-08 as v0.18.1 (<code>966259f</code>, <code>fd65cad2</code>), a lockfile patch: the v0.18.0 tag run failed before publishing assets because <code>cargo install</code> re-resolved an unpinned transitive (allium-parser v3.5.3, incompatible with the pinned allium-cli), so every tool install now passes <code>--locked</code>. host-lifecycle v0.50.0 (<code>66c24d6</code>, <code>5914a633</code>) shipped alongside, authorized by <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/26">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#26</a>: its held stack plus the v0.18.1 embed via the vendor-v6 bundle, which restores the manifest-equality invariant. The entrance manifest regenerated to the released toolset. Both issues closed at the release.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="briefing-the-commit-message-fault-detectors-host-lint28-plus-host-lint24s-remainder"><a class="header" href="#briefing-the-commit-message-fault-detectors-host-lint28-plus-host-lint24s-remainder">Briefing: the commit-message fault detectors (host-lint#28, plus host-lint#24's remainder)</a></h1> <h2 id="the-issue-operator-filed-2026-08-06-condensed-faithful"><a class="header" href="#the-issue-operator-filed-2026-08-06-condensed-faithful">The issue (operator-filed 2026-08-06, condensed, faithful)</a></h2> <p><code>host-lint --prose</code> catches trope shapes. Four faults recur in commit messages and PR bodies and pass it:</p> <ol> <li><strong>The message restates what the file already says.</strong> One message repeated the header comment of the file it added, diagram included; deleting the duplication cost 116 words and no facts. Mechanically checkable: compare the comment lines a commit adds against the message body, flag sentences appearing in both. Needs the diff and the message, no model.</li> <li><strong>The message answers a point nobody made</strong> (rebuts an alternative no reviewer proposed).</li> <li><strong>Precedent stands in as defence</strong> ("N other packages already do this"). Surface forms worth trying: <code>N <plural> already</code>, <code>others do</code>, <code>is what ... do</code>.</li> <li><strong>Paragraphs argue for a change instead of describing it.</strong></li> </ol> <p>Operator's suggested scope: fault 1 as a warning on the commit-msg path; fault 3 as an advisory; faults 2 and 4 as written guidance ("a more honest outcome than a check that mostly misses").</p> <h2 id="calibration-2026-08-06-922-accepted-commits-across-all-seven-repos"><a class="header" href="#calibration-2026-08-06-922-accepted-commits-across-all-seven-repos">Calibration (2026-08-06, 922 accepted commits across all seven repos)</a></h2> <p>Sentence-level, comment runs joined and markers stripped, normalized substring against the message body with the subject line excluded:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>repo</th><th>commits</th><th>dup W>=5</th><th>W>=8</th><th>W>=12</th><th>subject-matches</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>agentic-host</td><td>300</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>5</td></tr> <tr><td>host-lifecycle</td><td>209</td><td>12</td><td>10</td><td>2</td><td>1</td></tr> <tr><td>host-lint</td><td>146</td><td>9</td><td>8</td><td>4</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>host-grammar</td><td>20</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>host-prove</td><td>21</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>host-template</td><td>203</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>6</td></tr> <tr><td>host</td><td>23</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>total</strong></td><td><strong>922</strong></td><td><strong>22</strong></td><td><strong>19</strong></td><td><strong>7</strong></td><td><strong>12</strong></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Readings:</p> <ul> <li>The fault is real and current: one hit is a commit made TODAY during this session ("An upstream already set, by hand or by an earlier run, is kept as found" — in both the doc comment and the body). The corpus is the offender corpus, so hits are mostly true instances, with a minority of judgment-call quotes (a message quoting a factual claim like "--dry-run is not a flag of receipt --record").</li> <li>The subject line MUST be excluded: 12 hits are the house convention that a record commit's subject IS the added record's title (call/0053 etc.).</li> <li>Threshold: W>=8 keeps 19 of 22 while dropping short generic sentences; W>=12 loses most true instances.</li> <li><strong>Fault 3 scored ZERO in 922 commits</strong>, even with widened patterns (spelled numbers, "already do this", "others do", "is what X do", "standard practice"). An advisory would cost nothing and, on this corpus, catch nothing.</li> </ul> <h2 id="standing-constraints-and-precedent"><a class="header" href="#standing-constraints-and-precedent">Standing constraints and precedent</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Tiers</strong>: flag=1 blocks, warn=3 advisory at the commit hook. Commit-msg warns are hook-only (the release gate's prose regression reads docs, not messages), so a new commit-msg warn cannot re-open the verify receipt.</li> <li><strong>VOCABULARY.md is host-lint's rule source.</strong> An entry there that no code enforces breaks the property that VOCABULARY states what the tool enforces (the shape call/0046 retired <code>hermetic-exempt</code> for). Written-guidance-only content belongs in skill text, explicitly labeled unenforced — or nowhere.</li> <li><strong>The --stdin path already runs body prose advisory</strong> through the shared host-grammar engine, so a new host-grammar trope reaches commit bodies with no new plumbing — but a grammar change costs the full grammar -> host-lint -> host-lifecycle vendored cascade. A host-lint-side rule costs one release.</li> <li><strong>Fault 1 needs the staged diff</strong>, which host-lint's --stdin path does not receive today. The pure predicate (added-comment sentences x body sentences) is trivially unit-testable either way; the question is who observes the diff.</li> <li><strong>plan/0072's lesson</strong>: calibration against accepted history rewrote four designed decisions two reviews had passed. <strong>plan/0070's lesson</strong>: precision at the warn tier is what keeps the advisory tier trusted.</li> <li><strong>host-lint#24 remainder</strong>: the generic <code><noun> <cardinal></code> heading rule shipped (94cfb35); still open is the LEXICON carve-out for genuine heading designators ("Windows 11") paired with a recall-biased warn tier. Same detector-precision territory, same release vehicle candidate.</li> <li><strong>Push hold</strong>: all work lands as local held commits; a milestone cut or call/ record waits for the lift. Design now, land the record then.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-questions"><a class="header" href="#the-questions">The questions</a></h2> <p><strong>Q1 — who observes the diff for fault 1?</strong></p> <ul> <li>(a) host-lint runs <code>git diff --cached</code> itself when linting a commit message in a repo.</li> <li>(b) the commit-msg hook pipes the staged diff to host-lint alongside the message (explicit input, no git inside host-lint's stdin path).</li> <li>(c) a dedicated <code>host-lint commit</code> verb taking message file + diff, called by the hook.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Q2 — fault 1 tier and threshold?</strong></p> <ul> <li>(a) warn (exit 3) at sentence threshold W>=8, subject excluded, commit-msg path only.</li> <li>(b) warn at W>=5 (higher recall, admits short generic sentences).</li> <li>(c) warn at W>=8 but also surfaced in --prose/PR-body contexts, not only commit-msg.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Q3 — fault 3 (precedent), given zero corpus hits?</strong></p> <ul> <li>(a) do not build it; record the shape in guidance only; revisit if it ever appears.</li> <li>(b) build as a host-lint-side advisory on the commit-msg path (one release, no cascade).</li> <li>(c) build as a host-grammar trope (reaches all prose surfaces; full cascade).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Q4 — faults 2 and 4 guidance placement?</strong></p> <ul> <li>(a) the commit-message section of the relevant skill text, explicitly labeled as not mechanized.</li> <li>(b) VOCABULARY.md alongside the enforced rules, labeled advisory-prose.</li> <li>(c) nowhere: unenforceable guidance is noise (honest silence).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Q5 — packaging?</strong></p> <ul> <li>(a) one host-lint milestone bundling fault 1 + the #24 LEXICON-carve-out remainder, one release when the hold lifts.</li> <li>(b) fault 1 as an issue-scoped fix now (held commit), #24 remainder separate later.</li> <li>(c) wait: no detector work until the hold lifts and the milestone can be cut properly.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-each-persona-returns"><a class="header" href="#what-each-persona-returns">What each persona returns</a></h2> <p>For each question: your position (2-4 sentences, grounded in your lens), then the strongest objection to your own position, then a final ranked ordering of the options. End with the single most important overall note. Under 500 words total.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="convening-record-commit-message-fault-detectors-host-lint28--24-remainder"><a class="header" href="#convening-record-commit-message-fault-detectors-host-lint28--24-remainder">Convening record: commit-message fault detectors (host-lint#28 + #24 remainder)</a></h1> <p>Date 2026-08-06. Input: briefing-28.md (issue text, 922-commit calibration, five questions). Five personas; Fen SIMULATED — the recorded probe channel refused connection, so the weak-agent-trap lens stands in and the real probe is owed (prompts preserved: fen-p1.txt, fen-p2.txt).</p> <h2 id="ballots"><a class="header" href="#ballots">Ballots</a></h2> <h3 id="mara-human-operator-1"><a class="header" href="#mara-human-operator-1">Mara (human operator)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Q1: c > b > a — a <code>host-lint commit</code> verb with explicit inputs is reproducible by hand weeks later; git hidden inside the stdin path surprises in a worktree or bare store. Self-objection: new CLI surface for a single caller.</li> <li>Q2: a > c > b — W>=8, commit-msg only; the warn tier spends her attention and plan/0070's precision lesson is about exactly that. Self-objection: her own issue named PR bodies as an offender surface.</li> <li>Q3: a > b > c — the corpus overruled the advisory she herself filed; zero in 922 means no detector, guidance with pre-drafted patterns instead. Self-objection: survivor bias — zero may measure review vigilance, not absence.</li> <li>Q4: a > c > b — VOCABULARY stays enforcement-true (call/0046 paid for it); skill text labeled unenforced. Self-objection: unverifiable guidance cannot be trusted to be followed.</li> <li>Q5: a > b > c — one milestone, one release, batch-before-pushing standing rule. Self-objection: bundling holds a calibrated fix hostage to an open design; split if the LEXICON half stalls.</li> <li>Note: the day she stops reading exit 3, the advisory tier is dead; calibration overruled her own request — keep measuring before building.</li> </ul> <h3 id="wren-agentic-llm-operator"><a class="header" href="#wren-agentic-llm-operator">Wren (agentic LLM operator)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Q1: c > b > a — explicit inputs are the only inputs she can replay; shelling to git makes the stdin path impure and the verdict ambient. The verb's contract lives in --help, where a memoryless future session will look. Self-objection: a verb is surface every later session must rediscover.</li> <li>Q2: a > c > b — a warn she learns to dismiss trains her to dismiss the tier; (c) names no diff source for PR bodies, and an ambiguous input contract is where she stalls or guesses. Self-objection: PR bodies stay unguarded.</li> <li>Q3: a > b > c — zero hits means no red to loop against: an unverifiable detector with unknowable precision, spending warn-tier trust. Self-objection: the corpus is survivors; the fault may live in rejected drafts and unsampled PR bodies.</li> <li>Q4: a > c > b — skill text loads into her window, the only channel that reaches an amnesiac; one aspirational VOCABULARY entry teaches future-her the file can lie. Self-objection: skill coverage is probabilistic.</li> <li>Q5: a > b > c — the design and calibration are in-window now; deferring means a future session reconstructs with drift. Self-objection: if the lift comes first, the bundle delays what was ready.</li> <li>Note: the offender this corpus measures is her — one fault-1 hit was committed today by a session like hers. Mechanize exactly what calibration supports; keep warns believed; loadable skill text for the rest; nothing in between.</li> </ul> <h3 id="bly"><a class="header" href="#bly">Bly</a></h3> <ul> <li>Q1: c > b > a — explicit input or nothing; a tool shelling to git itself breaks on the irregular runtime (WSL, bare stores) and leaves no replayable record. The verb handles version skew cleanly. Self-objection: a fresh hook against an old binary must fail loudly naming the fix.</li> <li>Q2: a > c > b — warn that cries wolf dies, and real warns die with it; subject exclusion spares twelve false hits. Self-objection: PR bodies stay uncovered.</li> <li>Q3: a > b > c — zero hits, yet the dead detector rides every vendored cascade; record the shape AND the zero so a cold read knows it was considered. Self-objection: adopters beyond the seven repos may exhibit it.</li> <li>Q4: a > c > b — an unenforced VOCABULARY entry makes the record overstate completeness (the call/0046 shape); silence buries debt where the next session cannot see it. Self-objection: guidance never pointed-at may never be read.</li> <li>Q5: b > a > c — the operator's bug bit today; issue-scoped held commit now, the #24 remainder separately. Self-objection: under the hold both ship at the same lift anyway.</li> <li>Note (load-bearing): design the degraded path first — when hook and binary are version-skewed and no diff arrives, host-lint must say "fault-1 not checked", never exit clean as if it was. A record must over-report owed work, never hide it.</li> </ul> <h3 id="orin"><a class="header" href="#orin">Orin</a></h3> <ul> <li>Q1: c > b > a — the diff is a declared input, never ambient state; (a) makes the stdin path behave differently by where it runs, failing unsafe for a literal adopter. A verb gives a stable signature a ledger entry can reference. Self-objection: a verb with one caller is speculative API.</li> <li>Q2: a > b > c — the calibrated configuration is the only one executed against the population; a rule promised where its second input cannot exist (PR bodies via --prose) is a broken contract. Self-objection: judgment-call quotes still fire at W>=8.</li> <li>Q3: a > b > c — a detector shipped against zero corpus hits is an example written but never executed, his named recurring defect. Self-objection: the corpus is his own seat; unseen adopters get nothing.</li> <li>Q4: a > c > b — VOCABULARY's whole value is stating exactly what the tool enforces; the unenforced label is what lets guidance read honestly out of context. Self-objection: unenforced text rots silently; silence never rots.</li> <li>Q5: a > b > c — same detector-precision territory, same tool; under the hold bundling costs no latency and halves re-pins and ledger entries downstream. Self-objection: couples fault 1's ship date to the LEXICON judgment work.</li> <li>Note: all five questions are one — will the written contract still read true to someone applying it literally, months on, with no access to this calibration? Ship only what was executed against the population; label the rest unenforced.</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-simulated--substitution-noted-real-probe-owed-prompts-preserved"><a class="header" href="#fen-simulated--substitution-noted-real-probe-owed-prompts-preserved">Fen (SIMULATED — substitution noted; real probe owed, prompts preserved)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Q1: a > c > b — the DISSENT: he wants one command that reproduces the verdict in the repo; two-input plumbing he will garble. Self-objection: (a) makes the same stdin warn inside a repo and pass outside one, the non-reproducibility that confuses him most.</li> <li>Q2: a > c > b — he over-obeys; every printed line is an instruction, so precision is safety. Self-objection: tiers do not exist for him; only the wording protects.</li> <li>Q3: a > b > c — a zero-hit rule would fire mostly on his clumsy phrasing and he would contort messages to dodge it. Self-objection: guidance-only is invisible to him; (a) protects by omission, not instruction.</li> <li>Q4: a > c > b — "everything in VOCABULARY is enforced" is an invariant he can hold; break it and he hand-enforces advisory prose, destructively. Self-objection: he drops qualifiers; "not mechanized" is the nuance a quantized read loses.</li> <li>Q5: a > b > c — one release sequence is one chance to mis-sequence, not two. Self-objection: a longer held-work window is more in-flight state to lose.</li> <li>PROBE 1 (simulated): the 4B "fixes" the advisory by DELETING THE DOC COMMENT (the durable copy) and flattening the body — the warn text must state which side to keep.</li> <li>PROBE 2 (simulated): guidance strips the loudest advocacy but the precedent residue survives verbatim — the machine-matchable surface form is exactly what a weak agent leaves behind; keep the patterns recorded ready.</li> <li>Note: any printed warning is a command; every detector line must name the safe direction ("trim the message; keep the comment") or the advisory tier becomes a destructive-edit generator for weak agents.</li> </ul> <h2 id="tally-first-preferences-instant-runoff-not-needed"><a class="header" href="#tally-first-preferences-instant-runoff-not-needed">Tally (first preferences, instant-runoff not needed)</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Q</th><th>Mara</th><th>Wren</th><th>Bly</th><th>Orin</th><th>Fen(sim)</th><th>settled</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Q1 input surface</td><td>c</td><td>c</td><td>c</td><td>c</td><td>a</td><td><strong>c</strong> (4-1)</td></tr> <tr><td>Q2 tier/threshold</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td><strong>a</strong> (unanimous)</td></tr> <tr><td>Q3 precedent</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td><strong>a</strong> (unanimous)</td></tr> <tr><td>Q4 guidance home</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td><strong>a</strong> (unanimous; b disqualified by four)</td></tr> <tr><td>Q5 packaging</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td>b</td><td>a</td><td>a</td><td><strong>a</strong> (4-1)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="settled-design"><a class="header" href="#settled-design">Settled design</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>A <code>host-lint commit</code> verb</strong> with explicit inputs: <code>--message <file></code>, <code>--diff <file></code>. The hook stages the diff to a file and calls the verb. The verb runs the existing message checks (subject escalation, body prose advisory) plus the duplication check. Fen's dissent is honored in ergonomics: the verb's help documents the exact re-run line, and the hook prints it on a warn.</li> <li><strong>Duplication check, exactly as calibrated</strong>: comment runs from added lines, markers stripped, sentence-split, normalized; a sentence of 8+ words appearing in the BODY (subject excluded) warns (exit 3). The warn wording names the safe direction: trim the message; keep the comment (Fen probe 1).</li> <li><strong>Degraded path discloses (Bly)</strong>: no <code>--diff</code> supplied -> the verb still runs the message-only checks and prints "duplication not checked (no diff provided)" beside the verdict — the refs-gate disclosure pattern; never a silent clean-as- if-checked.</li> <li><strong>No precedent detector (unanimous, corpus-driven)</strong>: the shape, the widened patterns, the measured zero, and the survivor-bias caveat are recorded in guidance, ready to cut a rule the day a real instance appears.</li> <li><strong>Faults 2 and 4</strong>: skill text, explicitly labeled not mechanized. Never VOCABULARY.md (the call/0046 property). Wording must survive a quantized read (Fen: qualifiers get dropped — lead with the imperative, not the caveat).</li> <li><strong>Packaging</strong>: one detector-precision milestone bundling fault 1 with the host-lint#24 LEXICON-carve-out remainder; one host-lint release at the hold lift. If the carve-out stalls at lift time, split (Mara's fallback, honoring Bly). Implementation proceeds now as held commits in the host-lint worktree.</li> <li><strong>Owed before release</strong>: the REAL Fen probes (prompts in fen-p1.txt / fen-p1-worded.txt / fen-p2.txt; runner fen-program.py) as the acceptance gate, replacing today's simulation; the milestone cut, the call/ record (with the substitution noted), and the ledger entry land at the hold lift.</li> </ol> <h2 id="implementation-state-2026-08-06"><a class="header" href="#implementation-state-2026-08-06">Implementation state (2026-08-06)</a></h2> <p>Fault 1 SHIPPED as held commit 6574f90 in software/host-lint/main (amended from a53ee88: the operator flagged trope material and irrelevant counts in the added text; VOCABULARY section 7, the lib comments, and the message were rewritten to terse rule statements with the study numbers left to the milestone record, and a tricolon the prose lane itself caught in the reworded message was removed) (second deliberate DRIFT): <code>host-lint commit --message <file> [--diff <file>] [--json]</code>, pure predicates in lib (added_comment_text / normalize_for_restate / split_sentences / restated_comment_sentences), stdin checks unchanged, warn wording carries the safe direction, no-diff runs disclose as a Note. 4 unit tests + 8 integration cases; mutation-proved both calibrated boundaries (subject inclusion and word-bar drop each redden exactly one test). VOCABULARY section 7 documents the rule, the calibration, and the measured-zero scope boundary for precedent.</p> <p>Remaining after 2026-08-06: the hook side; the faults-2/4 guidance; the #24 LEXICON-carve-out half; the real Fen probes.</p> <h2 id="implementation-state-2026-08-07-the-settled-design-is-fully-implemented"><a class="header" href="#implementation-state-2026-08-07-the-settled-design-is-fully-implemented">Implementation state (2026-08-07): the settled design is fully implemented</a></h2> <p>All three implementable remainders landed as held commits on host-lint main (tip fa6f5d2): 71b27a5 the hook's commit-msg dispatch — one correction to the paragraph above: the dispatch script is host-lint's own <code>pre-commit</code> file (host-lifecycle only copies it), so no host-lifecycle change existed to make; afc3fb0 the #24 carve-out (scaffold heading Flag→Warn, LEXICON mask + strict escalation with the lexicon-add remedy, plus the VOCABULARY entry 94cfb35 never wrote; a fresh sweep of 2036 tracked headings across ten stores matched the shape zero times, so no current verdict changes); 5105fb5 the faults-2/4 guidance in SKILL.md, imperative-first per the Fen requirement. Still owed: the real Fen probes (all channels down 2026-08-07; the persistent monitor is <code>bvgf3ks3w</code> after two predecessors died with session continuations), the milestone cut, the call/ record, the releases — all staged in REVIEW-PACKET.md, executed at the hold lift. The 2026-08-07 advisor review of the full ten-commit held set found no blocking defects.</p> <p>Fold (2026-08-07, operator-directed, after the review above): the four #28 commits named in this file now live as one bug-closing commit, and the #24 commit rides above it — after the same day's terse-message pass the live pair is <code>3a6af0a</code> (#28) + <code>550aa87</code> (#24). Tree-identical rebuilds proven by empty diffs at each step; the pre-fold stack survives on branch <code>safety-fold-20260807</code> and the fold shape on <code>safety-reword-20260807</code>. Shas above this paragraph are the pre-fold history and stay as written.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="real-fen-results-direct-unsloth-endpoint-card-params-temp-06-for-ballots"><a class="header" href="#real-fen-results-direct-unsloth-endpoint-card-params-temp-06-for-ballots">Real Fen results (direct unsloth endpoint, card params temp 0.6 for ballots)</a></h1> <h2 id="q1-order-xyz-rc0"><a class="header" href="#q1-order-xyz-rc0">Q1 order-XYZ (rc=0)</a></h2> <think> Thinking Process: <ol> <li> <p><strong>Analyze the Request:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Goal:</strong> Rank three options (X, Y, Z) for a linter that warns when a commit message repeats a sentence from a comment the commit adds.</li> <li><strong>Inputs:</strong> Linter needs commit message and staged diff.</li> <li><strong>Options:</strong> <ul> <li>X) <code>git</code> runs the linter itself to read the staged diff.</li> <li>Y) Commit hook saves diff to file, passes as extra flag to existing lint command.</li> <li>Z) New command <code>host-lint commit</code> takes two named files (message, diff).</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Context:</strong> I am a small agent using this tool, re-running it after editing the message.</li> <li><strong>Task:</strong> Rank best to worst (e.g., 'Z, X, Y') and give one short reason.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><strong>Evaluate Option X (Git runs the linter):</strong></p> <ul> <li><em>Mechanism:</em> The linter is invoked as a subprocess within <code>git commit</code>. <code>git</code> needs to know how to pass the staged diff.</li> <li><em>Pros:</em> Integrated, no extra files, works automatically when <code>git commit</code> is run.</li> <li><em>Cons:</em> Requires modifying <code>git</code> behavior or hooking into it in a way that might be tricky. <code>git</code> itself doesn't easily pass stdin/stdout for diffs in a way that's easy to intercept for a custom linter without a hook. However, <code>git</code> can be told to run commands via hooks. But the option says "the linter runs git itself". That implies the linter is the one invoking <code>git</code>. This is backwards. If the linter runs <code>git</code>, it's checking the repo state. But the prompt says "the linter runs git itself to read the staged diff".</li> <li><em>Correction/Refinement:</em> Usually, a linter runs on the <em>output</em> of git. (Also good)</li> <li>Constraint Check: One or two sentences.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><strong>Refining for Conciseness and Clarity:</strong></p> <ul> <li>"This change adds a linting check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap."</li> <li>Does this describe the change? Yes.</li> <li>One or two sentences? Yes.</li> <li>Follows guidance (describe change, no advocacy)? Yes.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><strong>Output Generation.</strong> (Wait, I need to make sure I don't include any extra text like "Here is the revision:" etc.)</p> <p>Revised Body: This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap.</p> <p>Let's try to capture the essence slightly better if possible while keeping it neutral. Or: "This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body to warn on overlap."</p> <p>Let's go with: This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap.</p> <p>Wait, looking at the original draft: "The check compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap." "This change adds a linting check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap."</p> <p>Final Polish: This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap.</p> <p>Actually, looking at the draft again, it mentions "added comment line". The revision should reflect that accurately. Okay, ready to output.cw </think></p> </li> </ol> <p>This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap.</p> <h3 id="answer-tail-15"><a class="header" href="#answer-tail-15">answer tail</a></h3> <p>This change adds a check that compares each added comment line against the message body and warns on overlap.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0081-openwrt-style-pack-the-openwrt-package-style-rules-as-a-second-external-pack"><a class="header" href="#plan0081-openwrt-style-pack-the-openwrt-package-style-rules-as-a-second-external-pack">plan/0081 openwrt-style-pack: the OpenWrt package style rules as a second external pack</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Status: DRAFT.</strong> The <code>vendor-manuals</code> task is done: the four manuals are vendored and digest-pinned, and the crate is a workspace member whose corpus tests pass. The lane checkers (<code>meta</code>, <code>comment</code>, <code>msg</code>, <code>pr</code>) and the docs-and-calibration task are not. This line is parked while the suite-zero run (plan/0082) completes; it is not part of that run's close.</p> </blockquote> <p>This milestone delivers <code>host-lint-openwrt</code>, the second external pack in the host-lint workspace, built to the shape <a href="plan/0081-openwrt-style-pack/../0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack/README.html">plan/0072</a> established for <code>host-lint-ffmpeg</code>. Where the FFmpeg pack encodes one upstream project's commit and patch rules, this one encodes the four style manuals that govern a package contributed to <code>openwrt/packages</code>, and it checks all four of them.</p> <p>The rules are not upstream policy. <code>.github/llm-review-rules.md:100</code> states that the description block is free-form prose with no enforced convention, so there is no document to cite in review. The three manuals are <strong>measured practice</strong>: each rule rests on a counted share of the live tree, and each carries that share into the registry as its measured rate. This is a stronger footing than the FFmpeg pack started from, where every <code>measured_rate</code> was <code>None</code> until the calibration node ran, and the pack should not throw that away by re-deriving the rates from scratch.</p> <h2 id="scope-6"><a class="header" href="#scope-6">Scope</a></h2> <p>Delivered by this milestone, all in the host-lint repository except the final re-pin:</p> <ul> <li><code>host-lint-openwrt</code>, a workspace member beside <code>host-lint-ffmpeg</code>, sharing the lockfile and the vendored bundle, listed in <code>default-members</code> so a bare <code>cargo build</code> produces it.</li> <li>The three vendored style manuals, pinned by whole-file digest, as the pack's sources.</li> <li>A rule registry carrying the same <code>Source</code> / <code>Section</code> / <code>Rule</code> / <code>Tier</code> structs the FFmpeg pack uses, with completeness-as-a-test over the vendored manuals.</li> <li>Four lanes, one per manual, each with its own checker and its own fixtures.</li> <li><code>RULES.md</code> generated from the registry, and <code>CALIBRATION.md</code> recording where each measured rate comes from.</li> </ul> <p>Not delivered here, and deliberately:</p> <ul> <li>The mail, series, maintainers, forge and cosmetic lanes the FFmpeg pack carries. Those encode a mailing-list submission workflow that <code>openwrt/packages</code> does not have; it takes pull requests. Cloning a lane nothing reads would put dead code behind a tier.</li> <li>Any check that needs a build. The OpenWrt manuals state no build-time rule, so there is no <code>build</code> lane and no attested tier drawn from one.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-four-lanes"><a class="header" href="#the-four-lanes">The four lanes</a></h2> <p>Each lane is one manual, and the manual's own Checklist section is the lane's rule list.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Lane</th><th>Reads</th><th>Manual</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>meta</code></td><td><code>TITLE:=</code> and <code>define Package/<name>/description</code> in a package Makefile</td><td>Writing TITLE and description for an OpenWrt package</td></tr> <tr><td><code>comment</code></td><td>comments in the files OpenWrt writes, never a patch body</td><td>Writing comments in an OpenWrt package</td></tr> <tr><td><code>msg</code></td><td>one commit message</td><td>Writing a commit for an OpenWrt package</td></tr> <tr><td><code>pr</code></td><td>the body of a pull request, handed in</td><td>Writing a pull request for openwrt/packages</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The <code>pr</code> lane differs from the other three in where its subject lives. A Makefile, a comment and a commit message are all in the clone; a pull request body is on GitHub and nothing in a clone records it. That lane therefore reads an argument or standard input and can never run as a repository sweep, which is a shape the pack has to carry deliberately rather than discover when someone points it at a directory and gets silence.</p> <p>It is also the one lane with a real upstream artefact behind it. <code>.github/pull_request_template.md</code> is a file the project ships and GitHub prefills, so the rules keyed to its headings cite something rather than measure it. That artefact is <strong>referenced and resolved at check time, never embedded</strong>, by <a href="plan/0081-openwrt-style-pack/../../call/0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded.html">call/0055</a>: a vendored copy would be wrong the moment upstream edited it, and wrong silently. A short-lived gitignored cache is permitted so a sweep does not refetch, but it may only hold what the canonical location returned and may never change a verdict. When the template cannot be resolved, the rules keyed to it do not run and say so; they never fall back to the copy quoted inside <code>openwrt-pr-style.md</code>, which is illustration and not the artefact.</p> <p>The rules about <em>filling</em> those headings stay measured and stay offline, and that is where the finding is: a template body keeps the testing lines about 95% of the time and gives them a value only about two thirds of the time.</p> <p>The <code>comment</code> lane carries a provenance guard the other two do not need. A package directory mixes OpenWrt's own files with upstream's source, and every line a patch adds is upstream's in upstream's style. The lane must read a patch header before it treats a patch as carrying local prose: a file opening <code>From <40-hex-sha></code>, or carrying <code>From:</code> and <code>Subject:</code>, is a cherry-picked upstream commit and is exempt. Two thirds of the tree's patches were written locally and one third were not, so directory alone cannot decide it. Getting this wrong restyles an upstream author's words, which is the one failure in these three manuals that damages something outside the repository.</p> <h2 id="sources-and-pinning"><a class="header" href="#sources-and-pinning">Sources and pinning</a></h2> <p>The manuals are Claude artifacts, not files in a tree the pack can fetch, so the pack vendors them under <code>fixtures/manuals/</code> and pins the vendored copies by digest. A <code>PROVENANCE.md</code> beside them records, for each: the artifact identifier, the date read, and the upstream state the figures were measured against. The four rest on three different bases, which the provenance file keeps apart because their shares are not interchangeable: the description and comment manuals were measured at <code>1d40ad929a</code> on <code>master</code> dated 2026-06-07; the commit manual against the full history, 27197 non-merge commits; and the pull request manual against 5039 merged pull requests read from the GitHub API, with a targeted sample of 683 behind its new-package figures.</p> <p>The commit manual's Exemplars are fenced <code>host-lint:ignore</code>. Vendor them intact: they quote real commit subjects, and the prose audit would otherwise fire on the quoted text.</p> <h2 id="tiers"><a class="header" href="#tiers">Tiers</a></h2> <p>The tier says how much a finding is worth, and it is a claim about detectability, not about importance. The same three the FFmpeg pack uses:</p> <ul> <li><strong>mechanical</strong>, decidable from the artefact with no judgement. A trailing full stop, a tab indent, a missing sign-off, a line past 80 columns.</li> <li><strong>heuristic</strong>, decidable with a false-positive rate. Whether a description lists features, whether a comment says what rather than why.</li> <li><strong>attested</strong>, not mechanically decidable. Whether the comment explains something the line could not show; whether the commit holds one concern.</li> </ul> <p>A rule whose manual reports a share becomes that rule's <code>measured_rate</code>, and the recent column is the honest one where a convention has moved: two-space indent is 52.5% across the tree and 87.8% among 2025-2026 additions, and the rule follows the newer figure.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-21"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-21">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="vendor-manuals"><a class="header" href="#vendor-manuals">vendor-manuals</a></h3> <p><strong>DONE (2026-08-10).</strong> Created the crate, vendored the four manuals under <code>fixtures/manuals/</code> with <code>PROVENANCE.md</code>, and added it to <code>members</code> (being a member but not a default member, so the canonical artifact hash is unchanged until a lane lands). The digest-pinning test hashes every manual and passes, as does the distinct-files and exemplar-fences test. Verify by: <code>cargo test -p host-lint-openwrt</code> passes, and a manual edited without its digest re-recorded reddens.</p> <h3 id="rule-registry"><a class="header" href="#rule-registry">rule-registry</a></h3> <p>Encode the corpus: <code>Source</code> per manual, <code>Section</code> per manual heading, <code>Rule</code> per checklist line, each naming its section and carrying its tier, lane and measured rate. Carry the completeness test across, so a manual heading that states rules and has no rule encoded against it reddens. Verify by: the completeness test passes, and deleting a rule fails it.</p> <h3 id="meta-lane"><a class="header" href="#meta-lane">meta-lane</a></h3> <p>Check <code>TITLE:=</code> and the description block: noun phrase, capitalised, no full stop, three to seven words, does not name OpenWrt; description two-space indent, one or two lines, under 80 columns, present tense, ends with a full stop, and none of the five prohibitions. Verify by: the seven Exemplars pass clean and each cited counter-example flags its own rule.</p> <h3 id="comment-lane"><a class="header" href="#comment-lane">comment-lane</a></h3> <p>Implement the provenance guard first, then the form rules: own line, column 0, lowercase opening, no closing full stop, one line, no trailing inline comment, no commented-out code. Exempt the licence header. Verify by: the six Exemplars pass, a patch body carrying an upstream comment is skipped, and a locally-written patch is read.</p> <h3 id="msg-lane"><a class="header" href="#msg-lane">msg-lane</a></h3> <p>Check subject shape <code><package>: <what you did></code>, lowercase after the colon, no full stop, under 72 columns, bare package name rather than a path; body present and wrapped; sign-off present and matching the author. Verify by: the four Exemplars pass and each "Do not" case flags.</p> <h3 id="pr-template-resolver"><a class="header" href="#pr-template-resolver">pr-template-resolver</a></h3> <p>Implement <a href="plan/0081-openwrt-style-pack/../../call/0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded.html">call/0055</a> before the lane that depends on it: resolve <code>.github/pull_request_template.md</code> from a given <code>openwrt/packages</code> checkout or from the published raw file, cache it briefly under a gitignored path, and record the last-seen digest so a moved template reports as drift. Verify by four readings. A resolved template yields its headings. A second run inside the cache lifetime skips the fetch. An expired cache with no reachable source returns unresolved, never a stale hit. No code path reads the fence inside <code>openwrt-pr-style.md</code>.</p> <h3 id="pr-lane"><a class="header" href="#pr-lane">pr-lane</a></h3> <p>Check a pull request body handed in on standard input or as a file argument: template headings kept, maintainer a GitHub handle, description one or two lines, version and target and device each named rather than left blank behind a kept label, the CONTRIBUTING box ticked, and the patch section either deleted or ticked truthfully. Refuse a directory argument rather than sweeping, because the subject is not in the clone. Split the rules by what they need: the heading-matching rules consume the resolver and do not run without it, while the filling rules are measured and stay offline. Verify by: the quoted exemplar passes clean, a body with kept-but-empty testing labels flags, a directory argument exits with the refusal rather than silence, and an unresolved template leaves the heading rules unrun and named in the output while the filling rules still report.</p> <h3 id="docs-and-calibration"><a class="header" href="#docs-and-calibration">docs-and-calibration</a></h3> <p>Generate <code>RULES.md</code> from the registry with a <code>make-rules-doc.sh</code>, and write <code>CALIBRATION.md</code> recording each measured rate and the table it came from. Verify by: a drift test regenerates the doc and fails if it differs from the committed one.</p> <h3 id="release-and-repin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-repin">release-and-repin</a></h3> <p>Run the tool-carried release for host-lint, push the worktree, tag, then re-pin <code>.host-software</code> and record the receipt. Verify by: <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> returns to green with every component at its pin.</p> <h2 id="the-delivery-boundary"><a class="header" href="#the-delivery-boundary">The delivery boundary</a></h2> <p>Committing in the worktree moves its HEAD past the recorded pin, so <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> goes red from the first commit until the re-pin in the final task. That red is expected and is not drift. A session that stops before the release cascade must say so, because a clean <code>--check</code> is the signal the rest of the tooling trusts.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0082-suite-zero-open-bugs-every-open-issue-across-the-suite-closed-or-deferred-with-a-reason"><a class="header" href="#plan0082-suite-zero-open-bugs-every-open-issue-across-the-suite-closed-or-deferred-with-a-reason">plan/0082 suite-zero-open-bugs: every open issue across the suite closed or deferred with a reason</a></h1> <p>This milestone drives the whole <code>connollydavid/host-*</code> suite to zero open bugs. It is a closing milestone rather than a building one: nothing new is designed here except where an open issue's remedy has no design yet, and the deliverable is an empty tracker across nine repositories plus one recorded deferral for each thing that is not a bug.</p> <p>The census below was taken on 2026-08-10 and is the whole population. <code>host-template</code> has issues disabled, so its defects are carried on <code>connollydavid/host</code>; that is a standing condition of the suite and not something this milestone changes.</p> <h2 id="the-census"><a class="header" href="#the-census">The census</a></h2> <p>Six issues are open. Two of them are already fixed and were confirmed so by measurement, not by reading the fix direction and assuming it landed.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Issue</th><th>State on 2026-08-10</th><th>Disposition</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/24">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#24</a></td><td>resolved</td><td>verify and close</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/27">connollydavid/host-lint#27</a></td><td>resolved</td><td>verify and close</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/19">connollydavid/host#19</a></td><td>live defect</td><td>fix in the template</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/26">connollydavid/host-lint#26</a></td><td>live defect</td><td><strong>Done 2026-09-06</strong> (plan/0086): the grammar decides block structure before the mask, shipped in host-lint v0.19.0, verified against the pinned binary and closed with the transcript</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/23">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#23</a></td><td>owed work, not a defect</td><td>defer with a recorded reason</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/18">connollydavid/host#18</a></td><td>design handover, not a defect</td><td>defer to plan/0075</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Four further defects have no issue and will not get one. The operator directed that these findings fold into the work rather than the tracker, so they are carried here. Three were found while fixing <code>host-lint#26</code> and none was on the census when it was taken.</p> <ul> <li><strong>The LEXICON remedy publishes.</strong> The identifier tier's sanctioned fix mints a cross-reference on an upstream thread. Settled by <a href="plan/0082-suite-zero-open-bugs/../../call/0057-a-remedy-must-know-whether-its-artefact-publishes.html">call/0057</a>.</li> <li><strong>A released version shipped a red test suite.</strong> <code>allcaps_designator_before_decimal_does_not_warn</code> fails at the v0.18.1 pin with no local change, confirmed by stashing. The generator draws <code>[A-Z]{2,5}</code> but assumes out only <code>WARN_NOUNS</code>, while <code>FLAG_TERMS</code> holds <code>BOX</code>, <code>LEG</code>, <code>LAP</code>, <code>WAVE</code> and <code>WARN_ORDINAL_TERMS</code> holds <code>ERA</code>, <code>EPOCH</code>, <code>BATCH</code>. Proptest drew <code>ERA</code>. The property asserted that real vocabulary is silent; the tool was right and the test was wrong. A failure that only appears on the draw is a failure that ships.</li> <li><strong>A worktree hook lost its ignore list.</strong> <code>software --materialize</code> writes the <code>gitdir</code> link relatively, so a bare store stays portable. <code>repo_root()</code> took that target's parent and resolved it against the process working directory. That path lands outside the tree, so <code>.host-lintignore</code> and the LEXICON went missing without a word. Only git sets <code>GIT_DIR</code>, so the fault was reachable only from inside a hook, and only after the worktree hooks were installed at all. The fix for <code>host-lint#25</code> had assumed an absolute gitdir.</li> <li><strong>A failed release poisons the next attempt.</strong> Staging the deps-bundle appends the vendor source block to the tracked <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> and never removes it, so a second run duplicates <code>[source.crates-io]</code> and cargo refuses the manifest. The first release attempt here timed out mid-build and the second failed on the residue rather than on anything it did.</li> </ul> <p>The last of these is a <code>host-lifecycle</code> defect rather than a <code>host-lint</code> one, and it is recorded without a remedy task: this milestone works around it by restoring the file, and the fix belongs to whoever next opens the release path.</p> <h3 id="the-two-that-are-already-fixed"><a class="header" href="#the-two-that-are-already-fixed">The two that are already fixed</a></h3> <p><code>host-lifecycle#24</code> asked for two things: a queryable version, and the generator recorded as a proven component symmetrically with the checker. Both are present. <code>host-lifecycle --version</code> returns <code>host-lifecycle 0.50.0</code>, and <code>.host-software</code> carries a <code>host-lifecycle</code> stanza with a pinned toolchain, a canonical artifact hash and a deps-bundle, which is the same shape <code>host-lint</code> has. The issue predates both.</p> <p><code>host-lint#27</code> reported the <code>harness</code> ai-diction trope firing twice on the verbatim template spine and re-opening the verify receipt. It does not reproduce: <code>host-lifecycle prose host-template</code> returns <code>prose: clean … [host-lint 0.18.1]</code> at exit 0. One of the two cited lines is gone from the spine entirely; <code>kani:<harness></code> remains at <code>CLAUDE.md:476</code> and no longer fires. The fault was never in host-lint's rule set but in the template pinning a host-lint too old to accept its own spine, which is the skew <a href="plan/0082-suite-zero-open-bugs/../../call/0056-a-tool-dependency-is-a-floor-checked-in-the-lane.html">call/0056</a> addresses at the root.</p> <p>Neither may be closed on this reading alone. Each closing task below re-runs the repro from the issue body and quotes the output, because an issue closed against a claim rather than a transcript is how a fixed-looking defect returns.</p> <h2 id="what-is-not-in-scope"><a class="header" href="#what-is-not-in-scope">What is not in scope</a></h2> <p><code>host#18</code> is a complete design handover for a fourth methodology tool, and <a href="plan/0082-suite-zero-open-bugs/../0075-host-reconcile/README.html">plan/0075</a> already holds it as a cut, design-only milestone. <code>host-lifecycle#23</code> is the owed mechanical half of the room-touching detector, recorded so that "labelled" could not quietly become the fix; it is enhancement work with its own recorded stakes. Neither is a bug, and closing them here would be a category error. Both are deferred by name, with the deferral written into the issue so the tracker states the reason rather than going quiet.</p> <p>Zero open bugs is the goal. Zero open issues is not, and a milestone that conflates the two buys a clean tracker by discarding the record of what is owed.</p> <h2 id="closing-is-the-last-act"><a class="header" href="#closing-is-the-last-act">Closing is the last act</a></h2> <p>Operator ruling, 2026-08-10: <strong>no issue is closed until the session's final push has landed.</strong> Verification and the drafting of each closing comment happen whenever the work is done, but the <code>gh issue close</code> calls are held to the end and run only after every repository the work touched is pushed.</p> <p>The reason is the failure this milestone exists to prevent, applied to itself. An issue closed against a working tree is closed against something no one else can see, and if the push then fails on auth or the session ends first, the tracker says fixed while the fix exists on one machine. Closure is a claim made to everyone with access to the repository, and it must not outrun the evidence for it. The same rule already governs pushes here: never push a host commit whose software pin is unpushed.</p> <p>This inverts the natural order of the sequence below. <code>close-resolved</code> is written first because it is the smallest task, but it <em>executes</em> last, after <code>sweep-and-confirm</code> and after the final push.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-22"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-22">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="close-resolved"><a class="header" href="#close-resolved">close-resolved</a></h3> <p>Re-run each issue's own repro under the current toolchain and close the two that pass. Quote the transcript in the closing comment. Held to the end of the session by the ruling above: the verification may run at any point, the close may not. Verify by: <code>host-lifecycle --version</code> and the <code>.host-software</code> stanza answer <code>host-lifecycle#24</code>; <code>host-lifecycle prose host-template</code> at exit 0 answers <code>host-lint#27</code>; both issues are closed with the output pasted, not paraphrased, and both closes happen after the final push.</p> <h3 id="adopter-citation"><a class="header" href="#adopter-citation">adopter-citation</a></h3> <p>Fix <code>connollydavid/host#19</code>. <code>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</code> cites <code>call/0039</code>, a record that lives in agentic-host and that no adopter ever receives, so <code>refs --check</code> gates every fresh host on its first sweep with nothing the adopter did wrong to point at. The citation has to stop being a register reference in the copied file. Verify by: a clone of the template at the fixed revision passes <code>host-lifecycle refs --check</code> with zero dead pointers.</p> <h3 id="lexicon-line-masking"><a class="header" href="#lexicon-line-masking">lexicon-line-masking</a></h3> <p>Fix <code>connollydavid/host-lint#26</code>. <strong>Landed 2026-09-05 and verified closed 2026-09-06 (plan/0086)</strong>: the grammar decides block structure before the mask (<code>e5ac04cb</code>), shipped in v0.19.0 with two regression tests citing the issue; the repro transcript is plan/0086's. <code>mask_allowed</code> blanks a declared phrase with spaces, and on the markdown path a phrase declared at column one leaves four or more leading spaces, which <code>scan_prose_markdown</code> reads as an indented code block and skips the whole line. Every tell on that line clears silently. Mask with a filler that is neither alphanumeric nor whitespace so the blast radius is the phrase rather than the line. Verify by: the issue's own reproduction, where a declared <code>apache tapestry</code> at column one still leaves the standalone <code>tapestry</code> flagging, and a test asserts the surviving match.</p> <h3 id="lexicon-remedy-publishes"><a class="header" href="#lexicon-remedy-publishes">lexicon-remedy-publishes</a></h3> <p>The identifier tier's remedy asks for a tracker reference declared with a backing URL. In a commit message on a public repository both <code>owner/repo#N</code> and the URL mint a cross-reference on the target, so the hygiene lane's sanctioned fix is what pulls the governance repository into an upstream thread. host-lint has no notion that a commit message publishes in a way a file does not. Decide the remedy split before writing code, because this is a design gap rather than a coding error, and record it. Verify by: a <code>call/</code> records the decision, and the remedy text no longer directs an author toward a form that publishes when the artefact is a commit message.</p> <h3 id="defer-with-reason"><a class="header" href="#defer-with-reason">defer-with-reason</a></h3> <p>Write the deferral into <code>host#18</code> and <code>host-lifecycle#23</code> naming the milestone that holds each and why it is not a bug. These are comments rather than closes, but they are outward-facing writes on a public tracker and are held to the end under the same ruling. Verify by: both issues carry a comment naming plan/0075 and the owed cross-check respectively, and the suite's open-bug count is zero while the open-issue count is two by intent.</p> <h3 id="sweep-and-confirm"><a class="header" href="#sweep-and-confirm">sweep-and-confirm</a></h3> <p>Re-take the census across all nine repositories and confirm it against this document. Verify by: every open issue is one of the two deferred, and <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> and <code>--verify-setup .</code> are both green.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0083-lem-memory-recall-long-term-memory-as-vector-lookup-with-a-short-map-of-its-territory"><a class="header" href="#plan0083-lem-memory-recall-long-term-memory-as-vector-lookup-with-a-short-map-of-its-territory">plan/0083 lem-memory-recall: long-term memory as vector lookup, with a short map of its territory</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: cut 2026-08-21, not started</li> <li>Design: <a href="plan/0083-lem-memory-recall/../../DESIGN-LEM-MEMORY.html">DESIGN-LEM-MEMORY.md</a>, the living design document, cast consulted 2026-08-21</li> <li>Rulings: the operator adjudications of 2026-08-21: a new in-tree host-* component; LanceDB embedded; semantic before episodic namespaces; one living design doc; root CLAUDE.md compression descoped to plan/0079</li> </ul> <h2 id="why-17"><a class="header" href="#why-17">Why</a></h2> <p>MEMORY.md has outgrown its founding purpose: the record is past any single read, and a new session can no longer load it to avoid past mistakes. The record is read wholesale or not at all, and the load assumes a strong model and offers no order for the first hour. The design replaces whole-file reading with vector lookup over an embedded store, a knapped territory map as the load order, and Fen-gated acceptance. The append-only log stays the only write authority; every derived surface re-derives from it.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-23"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-23">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="exclusion-surface"><a class="header" href="#exclusion-surface">The exclusion surface is repaired first</a></h3> <p>The scoping task walks through host-lint's exclusion mechanism, and two defects planned in plan/0082 sit on that path. Both land as standalone patches before it: the host-lint#26 fix, where a column-one LEXICON phrase blanks to leading spaces and clears the whole line, and the worktree-hook ignore-list defect, where a relative gitdir strands <code>.host-lintignore</code> and the LEXICON outside the tree.</p> <ul> <li>verify: host-lint#26's own reproduction leaves the surviving match flagging; a worktree hook finds <code>.host-lintignore</code> and the LEXICON after <code>software --materialize</code></li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="vendor-calx-knap"><a class="header" href="#vendor-calx-knap">Vendor calx-knap</a></h3> <p>calx-knap enters as a submodule under tools/, external by source after the allium/specula precedent, used as-is and read-only: it is never maintained in this repo, and a change it needs goes upstream, never into the submodule. link-skills.sh gains the shape for its two skill directories; the spec copies to the repo root per the plugin's install contract; the register instruction block lands in CLAUDE.md with this repo's bindings; the calx-knap-gate binary builds in the recorded toolchain.</p> <ul> <li>verify: both skills link; <code>calx-knap.md</code> reads at the root; the gate binary honours the exit contract on the shipped example</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="component-scaffold"><a class="header" href="#component-scaffold">Component scaffold</a></h3> <p>The new component, named <code>host-memory</code> by operator ruling of 2026-08-21, lands under the <code>.host-software</code> recipe: bare store, worktree, deps-bundle pin, hermetic musl artifact in the recorded toolchain. The name names the content it serves, not the mechanism. LanceDB's dependency tree is audited against the deps-bundle doctrine before any release.</p> <ul> <li>verify: <code>software --check</code> reads the stanza clean; the artifact re-derives under <code>software --verify-build</code></li> <li>depends: #vendor-calx-knap</li> </ul> <h3 id="embedder-boundary"><a class="header" href="#embedder-boundary">Embedder boundary</a></h3> <p>Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B INT8 ONNX ships pinned behind an arm's-length boundary after the host-reference-ocr pattern, license checked and receipted; last-token pooling runs under the ort crate. Qwen lineage is deliberate: Fen is Qwen-lineage, so the canary and the embedder share a tokenizer family.</p> <ul> <li>verify: a receipt records the pinned weights and the license check; a fixed probe embeds byte-stable across re-runs</li> <li>depends: #component-scaffold</li> </ul> <h3 id="indexer-and-query"><a class="header" href="#indexer-and-query">Indexer and query</a></h3> <p><code>index</code>, <code>query</code>, and <code>map</code> commands in the single-command, tool-carried shape Fen demands; hash-gated re-embedding of changed units only; staleness advises, never gates; every hit carries exact pointers back into the log.</p> <ul> <li>verify: re-indexing an unchanged log embeds nothing; a stale index re-lists rather than falls silent; a garbled query degrades to best-effort hits plus the map</li> <li>depends: #embedder-boundary</li> </ul> <h3 id="semantic-pass"><a class="header" href="#semantic-pass">Semantic pass</a></h3> <p>MEMORY.md as the first namespace, one unit per entry: the entry format parses cleanly into date, lead, body, line range. Retrieval probes are frozen before compression work, and Fen completes the retrieval loop on the built artifact.</p> <ul> <li>verify: the frozen probe set passes; Fen finishes a query-to-deep-read loop, single command at a time</li> <li>depends: #indexer-and-query</li> </ul> <h3 id="episodic-pass"><a class="header" href="#episodic-pass">Episodic pass</a></h3> <p>call/ and plan/ as the second namespace, distinct collection or metadata filter: how the project solved what it solved, so retrieval answers past method alongside static fact.</p> <ul> <li>verify: a query about a past method returns the milestone record beside the static facts</li> <li>depends: #semantic-pass</li> </ul> <h3 id="territory-map"><a class="header" href="#territory-map">Territory map</a></h3> <p>Generated from the index, longhand first, knapped through the calx-knap corpus loop, gated on Fen, deployed to the session load. The map is the load order and the trigger that says there is something to ask.</p> <ul> <li>verify: the knapped map passes its probes on Fen; every region slug resolves against the index</li> <li>depends: #semantic-pass, #vendor-calx-knap</li> </ul> <h3 id="scope-prose-lane"><a class="header" href="#scope-prose-lane">Scope the prose lane</a></h3> <p>host-lint and the prose lane scope off the register, the map, and the index surfaces; the scoping uses host-lint's own exclusion mechanism, and nothing in the register names or configures the tool.</p> <ul> <li>verify: the prose lane exits zero over the tracked machine-audience surfaces; no human-audience document loses coverage</li> <li>depends: #exclusion-surface</li> </ul> <h3 id="knap-skills"><a class="header" href="#knap-skills">Knap the skills</a></h3> <p>The on-demand loaded skills compress into the register, one document at a time, probes frozen first, acceptance measured. Root CLAUDE.md waits on plan/0079's render, where its compression belongs.</p> <ul> <li>verify: each accepted skill passes its probes on Fen; LOW-YIELD skills keep their originals</li> <li>depends: #vendor-calx-knap, #scope-prose-lane</li> </ul> <h2 id="open-questions-5"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-5">Open questions</a></h2> <p>The map's generation (grown lexicon or index clustering) and its deployed path; distinct collections versus a metadata filter; dream's integration, with index freshness as an audited finding and the per-user tier as a third namespace candidate; the tokenizer lens, since the pinned tiktoken reference over-counts CJK and the embedder and the canary are Qwen-lineage.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0084-foreign-register-citation-form-a-citation-of-another-projects-register-names-its-repository-in-a-link"><a class="header" href="#plan0084-foreign-register-citation-form-a-citation-of-another-projects-register-names-its-repository-in-a-link">plan/0084 foreign-register citation form: a citation of another project's register names its repository in a link</a></h1> <p>Closes the open half of <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/19">connollydavid/host#19</a>, the limitation <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/../0078-sweep-in-the-verify-gate/README.html">plan/0078</a> carried as "carried, not closed" and the template's <code>GATE-refs-in-verify</code> ledger entry records as a known limit. Both reported halves were fixed in host-template <code>79c0b71</code>; what stayed open is that no form the sweep accepts exists for citing a record that lives in another project's register.</p> <h2 id="why-18"><a class="header" href="#why-18">Why</a></h2> <p>The sweep reads <code>plan/NNNN</code> and <code>call/NNNN</code> as references into the local rooms wherever the token appears, link text and link target included. The issue's four-form table is the measured statement: bare prose, a prose qualifier (<code>agentic-host call/0039</code>), and a markdown link to the other repository's blob URL all report DEAD; the one non-gating form is a code span, which marks an example rather than a reference and renders as literal text. The methodology's own attribution convention ("Recorded as agentic-host plan/0077", six times in the template's upgrade ledger) is flagged by the rule it documents whenever the ledger is swept, which is why the ledger sits outside the sweep and, one list serving both checkers, outside the prose gate with it.</p> <p>Measured 2026-09-05 against the pinned v0.50.0 source: the six ledger citations are the live population and all are prose form inside the excluded record layer; zero link-form citations exist in any tracked document. The accepted form therefore lands with no remediation wall: it is new capacity, not debt collection, the shape plan/0077's issue half faced with its 374 bare numbers.</p> <p>Sequencing, operator-approved: this lands before <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/../0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact/README.html">plan/0079</a> starts its build.
