The spine rewrite is the form's biggest consumer (the <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> provenance citation dropped in the host#19 fix can return as a real citation), and plan/0079 reworks the same verify recheck this gate lives in.</p> <h2 id="decision-1"><a class="header" href="#decision-1">Decision</a></h2> <p>The accepted form is link-anchored: a <code>plan/NNNN</code> or <code>call/NNNN</code> reference inside a markdown link whose target is an absolute forge URL naming the cited record (the path segment <code>{room}/{number}</code>) under a repository other than the local origin. The sweep accepts it as a citation, reports it in a counted disclosure, and never gates it.</p> <p>Boundary cases, each settled in the design:</p> <ul> <li>the URL's repository equals the local origin: judged as today, so a dead local record stays dead in a link;</li> <li>the target is relative: judged as today, this being what <code>resolve --markdown</code> emits;</li> <li>the URL names a different file than the token claims: DEAD, the false citation being the defect the sweep exists to catch;</li> <li>the citation stands in prose, not in a link: DEAD, one rule, link-or-nothing;</li> <li>the origin remote is absent: foreign by default, and the disclosure says so.</li> </ul> <p>The check verifies form, never existence: it cannot read another repository, the same honesty limit the issue half already carries. The disclosure is a count on every exit, never an enumeration, per the <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/../../call/0048-the-gate-runs-the-sweep-over-the-record.html">call/0048</a> weak-model finding; what captures a weak agent is the per-file list, so the count shape ships again.</p> <p>A sigil form (<code>agentic-host!call/0039</code>) was considered and declined: new grammar for every author and the weak model, a name-to-repository declaration surface to maintain, and no link in the rendered site. The cast round re-examines the rejection with the design on the table.</p> <h2 id="scope-7"><a class="header" href="#scope-7">Scope</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The accepted form</strong> in the sweep's verdict, where the scan already computes link membership for register references.</li> <li><strong>The disclosure</strong> line, counted, on every exit path of <code>refs --check</code> and <code>refs --gate</code>.</li> <li><strong>The doctrine</strong>: the template manual's reference paragraph gains the cross-project form, and a ledger entry succeeds the limitation text in <code>GATE-refs-in-verify</code>.</li> </ol> <p>Out of scope, recorded so it is not assumed: rewriting the six ledger prose citations (append-only record layer, and its file stays excluded); the ignore-list separation (one list serving two checkers, owed since the host#19 fix, its own milestone); verifying foreign targets over the network; a <code>resolve</code> emission for foreign citations (authorship stays hand-written until a corpus asks for the verb); linkifying commit messages (plan/0077's own out-of-scope row).</p> <p>A census note, measured on the record: <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/../0082-suite-zero-open-bugs/README.html">plan/0082</a>'s <code>adopter-citation</code> node carries this issue with the disposition "fix in the template"; it describes the half fixed in host-template <code>79c0b71</code> (2026-07-27). That node's own verify, a template clone passing <code>refs --check</code>, passes at today's revision <code>933b7f1</code>: the <code>call/0039</code> citation is gone from <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>. What keeps the issue open is the accepted form this milestone closes; the census row predates the issue's closing comment.</p> <h2 id="open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles-1"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles-1">Open questions the gather-data node settles</a></h2> <ul> <li>The URL well-formedness bar: which absolute shapes name the cited record (<code>blob</code> versus <code>tree</code>, branch versus commit, the anchor suffix, rendered versus source paths). Settled against real URLs carried in this tree's documents.</li> <li>The <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/../../call/0057-a-remedy-must-know-whether-its-artefact-publishes.html">call/0057</a> check applied to the new doctrine: the form directs authors to write a URL, which mints nothing on the target repository, and the doctrine and disclosure stay free of forms that publish.</li> <li>The exact disclosure lines on each exit, gate and check, so the count never reads as debt.</li> <li>Whether origin-absent reads foreign-by-default or skips with disclosure; the spec models whichever the corpus and the adversarial round support.</li> <li>The probe kit wording, production legibility and reading safety, written against the plan/0076 corrected protocol before anything runs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-24"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-24">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">The settled conditionals</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the four-form table re-run on the pinned binary and recorded in gather-data.md; the corpus counted (prose citations, link forms); the URL bar settled against real URLs with a written rule; the probe kit rereads the corrected protocol</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">The reference surface</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the Allium spec models the citation outcome (a register reference in a foreign-naming link is a citation, not a dead pointer), the origin comparison, and the disclosure count on the run outcome; <code>allium check</code> and <code>analyse</code> exit clean</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">The obligations</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every new obligation carries a disposition naming a test that exercises the rule rather than a helper beside it</li> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement"><a class="header" href="#implement">The accepted form</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a citation in a foreign-naming link is accepted and counted; a dead local record stays dead in label and relative forms; a URL naming another file stays dead; prose citations stay dead</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-tests"><a class="header" href="#write-tests">The test matrix</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the suite covers the issue's four forms plus local-link, relative-target, wrong-file, and origin-absent; mutating the rule reddens its named tests; clippy clean at the pinned toolchain; the exit-paths integration suite green (host-lifecycle's integration lane, not host-lint's script)</li> <li>depends: #implement</li> </ul> <h3 id="cast-consult"><a class="header" href="#cast-consult">Cast consultation</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: each persona's concern addressed or recorded in design-review.md; the sigil rejection and the disclosure wording re-examined on the record</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <h3 id="adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review">Adversarial review</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: an independent multi-lens read of the built diff records every blocking finding fixed or carried, with a dedicated lens for the escape-hazard, a dead local record laundered through a foreign-looking URL</li> <li>depends: #cast-consult</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">The weak-agent acceptance</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the real qwen3.5-4b, on the corrected protocol, writes an accepted citation from the doctrine and reads the disclosure without remediating; rotation-stable, transcript recorded; an unreachable channel is labeled and the probes recorded as owed, never simulated silently</li> <li>depends: #write-tests</li> </ul> <p><strong>Owed (2026-09-05).</strong> The kit is built and preserved (<a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-program.py">fen-program.py</a>, <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-p1.txt">fen-p1.txt</a>, <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-p2.txt">fen-p2.txt</a>, the record in <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-acceptance.html">fen-acceptance.md</a>); the gateway answers 401 to a session with no channel credentials, so the probes did not run; they are recorded as owed and nothing was simulated. The release does not stand on them: the sweep's own tests, the review rounds and the obligations discharge check the mechanism, and the probes alone measure whether the real weak model writes the form from the doctrine and ignores the count line.</p> <h3 id="write-spine-doctrine"><a class="header" href="#write-spine-doctrine">The spine doctrine</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the template manual's reference paragraph states the cross-project form; the ledger entry succeeding the limitation text records the change and the day-one state</li> <li>depends: #adversarial-review</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the release cascades clean, <code>software --check .</code> clean at the new pin, and connollydavid/host#19 closes with the four-form table re-run as closing evidence; PLAN.md and MEMORY.md record the outcome in their own commits</li> <li>depends: #write-spine-doctrine, #fen-acceptance</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adversarial-review-five-lenses-on-the-built-diff-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review-five-lenses-on-the-built-diff-2026-09-05">adversarial-review: five lenses on the built diff (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>The diff under review: host-lifecycle <code>85578b7</code> against <code>66c24d6</code> (spec, scan, verdict, disclosure, tests). The dedicated lens the cut named, a dead local record laundered through a foreign-looking URL, ran first and got the longest hearing.</p> <h2 id="lens-1-the-escape-hazard-the-dedicated-lens"><a class="header" href="#lens-1-the-escape-hazard-the-dedicated-lens">Lens 1: the escape-hazard (the dedicated lens)</a></h2> <p>Attack: the acceptance reads foreign by slug comparison, so a LOCAL dead record is laundered the moment an author writes a foreign-looking URL beside it: <code>[call/0039](https://github.com/connollydavid/agentic-host/blob/main/call/0039-….md)</code> in a repository whose own <code>call/0039</code> does not exist stops being dead, whether or not the foreign target exists.</p> <p>Finding, and its disposition: the escape is real and it is the design's stated limit, not a defect in it. The sweep cannot read another repository offline; the citation line discloses "were not read" on every exit; and the URL the launderer must write names a real file in a real foreign register, which is a different claim than the bare dead pointer it replaces. What the attack DID change: the wrong-file case had to gate (it does: the label claiming one record over a URL naming another stays dead, proven by <code>a_url_naming_another_file_stays_dead</code>), and the local-slug case had to stay dead (proven by the second half of <code>a_foreign_citation_in_a_link_is_accepted_and_counted</code>). Carried as the limit, with the wording carrying it.</p> <h2 id="lens-2-origin-spoofing-and-alternate-hosts"><a class="header" href="#lens-2-origin-spoofing-and-alternate-hosts">Lens 2: origin spoofing and alternate hosts</a></h2> <p>Attack: same repository name, different owner (<code>slartibardfast/agentic-host</code>); slug comparison catches it, because the comparison is the full slug. Alternate host spelling of the LOCAL repository (<code>raw.githubusercontent.com/connollydavid/agentic-host/main/plan/…</code>): the slug parses to the local one, so it is judged as today, dead when dead, which is correct, and it fell out of the segment walk rather than being designed in. A URL whose slug will not parse (<code>https://github.com/plan/0097-x/README.md</code>, no owner): fail closed, stay dead, proven by <code>an_unparseable_url_is_never_a_citation</code>.</p> <p>Finding: none blocking. The segment walk accepts any forge host by design (gather-data rule six); a malicious well-formed URL pointing at a fork is form-true and existence-false, lens 1's limit again and not a new one.</p> <h2 id="lens-3-regression-over-the-pre-existing-verdicts"><a class="header" href="#lens-3-regression-over-the-pre-existing-verdicts">Lens 3: regression over the pre-existing verdicts</a></h2> <p>Attack: zero drift is the requirement, every shape v0.50.0 judged must be judged identically. The early-continue for citations sits BEFORE the dead check, so any reference wrongly marked <code>foreign_citation</code> silently loses its dead verdict.</p> <p>Finding: the risk is real and it is where the mutation budget went. <code>enclosing_link_target</code> had to agree with <code>enclosing_link</code> on what is a link, and its in-target reconstruction initially omitted the token's own span, so a URL token came back a broken URL with foreignness unestablishable, and the four-form test caught it as cited=0 where the design says 1. Fixed before the round closed; the full suite (306 unit, 34 exit-path) runs byte-identical verdicts on this tree through the gate.</p> <h2 id="lens-4-cost"><a class="header" href="#lens-4-cost">Lens 4: cost</a></h2> <p>Attack: the citation facts run per register reference, and the defect class plan/0078 priced was per-reference work that reads state.</p> <p>Finding: the facts are string work over the line's characters; the only state read per run is <code>origin_slug</code>, read once beside the room index. Measured on this tree at the built release binary: 2511 ms gate, same verdict text, against the 2134 ms recorded baseline on the same mount, which is inside mount variance and no budget breach. No finding.</p> <h2 id="lens-5-spec-code-divergence"><a class="header" href="#lens-5-spec-code-divergence">Lens 5: spec-code divergence</a></h2> <p>Attack: the spec models <code>foreign_citation</code> as a creation fact, <code>AcceptForeignCitation</code> with a corpus condition, and <code>RecordUncheckedRegister</code> sparing citations, three claims the code could drift from.</p> <p>Finding: each is wired and each has a named, mutation-killed test (<code>scan_document_with</code> computes the fact at scan; the gate counts only what its corpus lists, the same condition the issue half carries; <code>count_unowned_registers</code> skips citations, so a software repository citing its host by link neither gates nor counts as unchecked). The obligations manifest discharges all 93 with <code>--strict-discharge</code> clean. One divergence noted and accepted: the spec's <code>saw_citation</code>/<code>disclosed_citations</code> latch is implemented as a counted line printed when the count exceeds zero; the count is the richer fact, and the spec's booleans model its existence.</p> <h2 id="disposition-4"><a class="header" href="#disposition-4">Disposition</a></h2> <p>Every blocking finding was fixed inside the round (lens 3's reconstruction). Two carries ride forward from the cast round (the <code>resolve</code> emission candidate; the doctrine wording), and lens 1's limit is carried into the doctrine node's required content.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="design-review-the-cast-round-on-the-accepted-citation-form-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#design-review-the-cast-round-on-the-accepted-citation-form-2026-09-05">design-review: the cast round on the accepted citation form (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>The design on the table when the round ran: the link-anchored accepted form as cut, the counted disclosure on every exit, the sigil rejection, and the built diff (host-lifecycle <code>85578b7</code>: spec <code>c8eaf9d</code>, six unit tests, two exit-path tests, three mutation kills). Each chair attacked their own first preference before speaking.</p> <h2 id="mara-the-operator"><a class="header" href="#mara-the-operator">Mara (the operator)</a></h2> <p>Concern: what does the form cost to keep green? The disclosure prints on every sweep of every tree that carries citations, so the count line becomes a permanent resident of this tree's verdicts the moment authors start writing the form.</p> <p>Disposition: priced, and cheap. The line is one count and never an enumeration; the gate's exit partition is untouched (the built diff cannot change an exit code, proven by the suite); and the count is zero today, so the line arrives only as fast as authors adopt the form. No new gate, no new release-cadence cost — the failure mode call/0052 priced out is structurally absent here.</p> <h2 id="wren-the-agentic-developer"><a class="header" href="#wren-the-agentic-developer">Wren (the agentic developer)</a></h2> <p>Concern: writing the form is hand-work with no tool assist — <code>resolve</code> emits local links only, so an author writes a long forge URL by hand and a typo lands in the one case the check refuses (the URL naming another file). The cheapest path to a green gate is the wrong path.</p> <p>Disposition: carried, and deliberately. The <code>resolve</code> emission for foreign citations stays out of scope by the cut's own record (no corpus asks for the verb yet); the doctrine ships a worked example instead, and the wrong-file case gates, which is the direction a typo should fail in. Recorded as the first candidate for a follow-up if the corpus grows citations.</p> <h2 id="bly-the-downstream-adopter-cold-read"><a class="header" href="#bly-the-downstream-adopter-cold-read">Bly (the downstream adopter, cold read)</a></h2> <p>Concern: reading the disclosure cold, does the acceptance read as coverage? "Accepted on link form" could be heard as "verified".</p> <p>Disposition: answered in the wording. The line says the targets "name another repository and were not read", which is the whole truth; the spec's entity comment carries the same limit; and the doctrine sentence (written next node) states the form and its limit together. Bly's own gate stays green citing the governing host's records — the defect the cut set out to close.</p> <h2 id="orin-the-methodology-maintainer-1"><a class="header" href="#orin-the-methodology-maintainer-1">Orin (the methodology maintainer)</a></h2> <p>Concern: the sigil rejection deserves a second look now that the design is concrete — a sigil (<code>agentic-host!call/0039</code>) would have been shorter to write and checkable without URL parsing.</p> <p>Disposition: rejection upheld, on the record this time. The sigil needs a name-to-repository declaration surface (a new stamp field, a new migration, a new failure mode), renders as text rather than a link in the published site, and adds grammar the weak model must learn for one use the link form already serves. The link form reuses markdown an author already writes and a fact (<code>origin_slug</code>) the tool already reads.</p> <h2 id="what-the-round-changed"><a class="header" href="#what-the-round-changed">What the round changed</a></h2> <p>Nothing in the built diff. Two carried items are recorded above (the <code>resolve</code> emission candidate; the wording dependency of the doctrine sentence on Bly's reading), and one instruction passed forward: the adversarial round owns the escape-hazard lens the cut named.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="fen-acceptance-the-weak-agent-probes-on-the-citation-form-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance-the-weak-agent-probes-on-the-citation-form-2026-09-05">fen-acceptance: the weak-agent probes on the citation form (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>Status: <strong>the probes are owed.</strong> The kit is built and preserved here; the channel refused the session's credentials, and the attempt is labeled rather than simulated away.</p> <h2 id="the-kit"><a class="header" href="#the-kit">The kit</a></h2> <p><a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-program.py">fen-program.py</a> runs the whole acceptance in one command once a channel exists:</p> <pre><code>FEN_ENDPOINT=… FEN_TOKEN=… FEN_MODEL=qwen3.5-4b python3 fen-program.py </code></pre> <p>Protocol: the plan/0076 corrected protocol exactly as plan/0080's thinking kit carried it (thinking on through the chat template, the model card's thinking-general parameters, the answer read after the closing <code></think></code>), two draws per probe, results appended to <code>fen-results.md</code> after every cell. The kit was checked against the last corrected protocol before running, per the 2026-08-08 lesson, and the prompts live beside it: <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-p1.txt">fen-p1.txt</a>, <a href="plan/0084-foreign-register-citation-form/fen-p2.txt">fen-p2.txt</a>.</p> <ul> <li><strong>P1, production legibility</strong> (both draws must pass): handed the doctrine sentence as instruction, the model writes a citation of a foreign record. Pass = the output is a markdown link whose URL path names the cited <code>call/0045</code> file, which is the accepted form produced from the rule.</li> <li><strong>P2, reading safety</strong> (both draws must pass): handed a green gate verdict whose tail carries the citation count line, with an unrelated stated task. Pass = the named next action serves the task, and does not remediate the cited record. This is the plan/0078 finding that an enumeration captures the agent, now applied to the new line: the count must inform and not capture.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-attempt-labeled"><a class="header" href="#the-attempt-labeled">The attempt, labeled</a></h2> <p>The gateway behind TLS at <code>api.d07yx58.net</code> is up: <code>/v1/models</code> answers HTTP 401, an auth refusal, not a dead host. The session's environment carries no <code>FEN_ENDPOINT</code>/<code>FEN_TOKEN</code>/<code>FEN_MODEL</code> (the plan/0080 discharge used the operator's channel credentials, which were session-scoped), and no credential is persisted anywhere on this machine: the prior kits under <code>~/agentic-host-work/</code> read the environment and none records it. No ballot was simulated and no transcript fabricated; there is nothing here that looks like a run.</p> <h2 id="what-ships-without-the-probes"><a class="header" href="#what-ships-without-the-probes">What ships without the probes</a></h2> <p>The release does not stand on the probes: the mechanism is checked by the sweep's own tests (six unit, two exit-path, three mutation kills), the cast and adversarial rounds on the built diff, and the obligations discharge. What the probes alone can measure is whether the real weak model produces the form from the doctrine and ignores the count line: the owed work, discharged the moment a channel exists, per the plan/0080 pattern.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-the-four-form-re-run-the-corpus-the-url-bar-the-protocol-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-the-four-form-re-run-the-corpus-the-url-bar-the-protocol-2026-09-05">gather-data: the four-form re-run, the corpus, the URL bar, the protocol (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>This records the #gather-data node. Everything here was measured before the spec was written.</p> <h2 id="the-binary-identity"><a class="header" href="#the-binary-identity">The binary identity</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle --version</code> answers <code>host-lifecycle 0.50.0</code>; the worktree <code>software/host-lifecycle/main</code> sits at <code>66c24d6</code> (release v0.50.0) with a clean tree, which is the pin <code>.host-software</code> records. The PATH copy is a cargo-installed glibc build of that revision; its hash differs from the recorded canonical artifact because the canonical artifact is the musl target, not because the binary is stale (the identity rule from the 2026-08-02 entry: hash against the record, and the record names the musl target). The probes below measure behavior at the pinned version.</p> <h2 id="the-four-form-re-run"><a class="header" href="#the-four-form-re-run">The four-form re-run</a></h2> <p>The issue's repro, rebuilt as a scratch repository carrying a <code>call/</code> room with one entry and a document citing records that room does not hold, swept with the pinned binary. Every form the issue reported DEAD reproduces; the code span stays clean; exit 1:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>form</th><th>line</th><th>verdict on v0.50.0</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>bare prose: <code>per agentic-host call/0039 the layout holds</code></td><td>DEAD</td><td><code>call/0039 names no entry in that room</code></td></tr> <tr><td>qualified prose: <code>recorded as agentic-host plan/0077</code></td><td>DEAD</td><td>same class</td></tr> <tr><td>link label matching the URL: <code>[agentic-host call/0039](…/blob/main/call/0039-….md)</code></td><td>DEAD</td><td>same class</td></tr> <tr><td>link label not matching: <code>[bare-store decision](…/blob/main/call/0039-….md)</code></td><td>DEAD</td><td>same class</td></tr> <tr><td>code span: <code>`call/0039`</code></td><td>clean</td><td>absent from the verdict, as the issue recorded</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Three boundary shapes the design must judge were added to the same document, and the pinned binary already answers all three the way the cut README settles them:</p> <ul> <li>a relative target naming an absent record (<code>[a local record](call/0042-nothing.md)</code>) is DEAD, the token inside the relative URL being detected like prose;</li> <li>a foreign URL naming a different file than the label claims (<code>[call/0039](…/call/0044-prose-lexicon.md)</code>) produces two findings today, and under the accepted form the label stays DEAD (the mismatch) while the URL's own token becomes an accepted citation, the URL naming a record that really exists in the foreign register;</li> <li>a URL naming a section of an index rather than the record (<code>[plan/0077](…/PLAN.md#open-work)</code>) stays DEAD, because the path never contains the <code>plan/0077</code> segment.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-corpus"><a class="header" href="#the-corpus">The corpus</a></h2> <p>Counted 2026-09-05 against host-template <code>933b7f1</code> and the whole tracked tree:</p> <ul> <li>the template's upgrade ledger carries <strong>six</strong> prose citations: <code>call/0046</code>, <code>call/0047</code>, <code>plan/0077</code>, <code>plan/0078</code>, <code>call/0051</code>, <code>call/0052</code>, all of the form "Recorded as agentic-host …" inside the excluded record layer;</li> <li><strong>zero</strong> accepted-form (link-shaped) citations exist in any tracked document, which is expected: no such form is accepted, so nobody can write one;</li> <li>the count is revision-dependent: the template at the earlier pin carried a seventh citation (<code>call/0045</code>), whose entry text the lem-revision bump reworded. The population is whatever the record says at the revision being swept, which is one more reason the form, not the count, is what the tool judges.</li> </ul> <p>The accepted form therefore lands with no remediation wall. The six ledger citations stay as they are: the ledger is append-only, its file is excluded, and the doctrine sentence written later tells new authors the link form.</p> <h2 id="the-url-bar"><a class="header" href="#the-url-bar">The URL bar</a></h2> <p>The rule this plan implements, grounded in the shapes this tree's own documents actually write:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Segment containment.</strong> An absolute URL names the cited record when its path contains the segment <code>{room}/{NNNN}</code> after the repository part. <code>…/blob/main/plan/0077-reference-resolver/README.md</code> qualifies; <code>…/PLAN.md#open-work</code> does not.</li> <li><strong>The revision is irrelevant.</strong> The ref between <code>/blob/</code> (or <code>/tree/</code>) and the path may be a branch (<code>main</code>, <code>proposals</code>) or a commit; the check judges the file, never the revision, because form is the claim and existence is not checkable offline.</li> <li><strong><code>blob</code> and <code>tree</code> both qualify.</strong> A milestone record is a directory (the <code>tree</code> view) and a decision record is a file (the <code>blob</code> view); the tree writes both shapes (<code>/blob/main/host-lint-ffmpeg/RULES.md</code>, <code>/tree/main/skills</code>).</li> <li><strong>A trailing anchor is ignored.</strong> <code>…/call/0039-bare-store-is-dot-bare-with-a-git-file.md</code> anchors nothing; an anchored URL still names the file.</li> <li><strong>Foreign means the full slug differs.</strong> The comparison is <code>owner/repo</code> against the local <code>origin_slug</code>, never the repository name alone: this tree cites <code>slartibardfast/calx-knap</code>, whose repository name differs from everything local anyway, but the owner half is what makes two same-named repositories distinct.</li> <li><strong>Any forge host qualifies.</strong> The URL's host is read, not matched against the local forge; <code>origin_host</code> is already forge-aware in the tool.</li> <li><strong>The form mints nothing.</strong> Checked against call/0057: a URL to another repository's file posts no cross-reference on the target, so directing an author to write one never publishes; the doctrine must stay free of <code>owner/repo#N</code>-style spellings, which do mint.</li> </ol> <p>Origin-absent repositories: the design reads foreign by default. An absolute URL visibly names another repository, and treating it as dead would gate the rare offline or remote-less clone on a link that is honest on its face; the disclosure names the condition either way.</p> <h2 id="the-protocol"><a class="header" href="#the-protocol">The protocol</a></h2> <p>The weak-agent acceptance runs on the real qwen3.5-4b through the gateway behind TLS at <code>api.d07yx58.net</code>, under the plan/0076 corrected protocol exactly as plan/0080's thinking kit records it: thinking enabled through the chat template (<code>enable_thinking: true</code>), the model card's thinking-general parameters, the answer read after the closing <code></think></code>, two draws per probe, results appended after every cell so a mid-run failure preserves the completed ones. The parameters, as the kit carries them:</p> <pre><code>temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty 1.5, repetition_penalty 1.0, max_tokens 32768 </code></pre> <p>The two recorded lessons are binding on the kit this plan builds: check a new kit against the last corrected protocol before running it (the plan/0080 kit had regressed against a correction that lived in a script comment), and record protocol corrections beside the prompts the next kit is built from. The labeled counterexample lives in plan/0080: its no-think runner truncated every cell at the token cap, and the spoiled run is preserved there beside the corrected one.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0085-active-default-surfaces-the-always-loaded-content-is-warn-free-and-named-agentsmd"><a class="header" href="#plan0085-active-default-surfaces-the-always-loaded-content-is-warn-free-and-named-agentsmd">plan/0085 active-default surfaces: the always-loaded content is warn-free and named AGENTS.md</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed (2026-09-05), three asks over one partition, with the definition settled by iteration in the cutting session. The partition is the one the calx-knap doctrine already names: the <strong>always-loaded surfaces</strong> (CLAUDE.md's calx-knap adoption note): the manual, STRUCTURE.md, the linked skills, and the territory and memory surfaces as they come to exist. Three changes:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Zero host-lint warnings, held strict:</strong> within the declared corpus a warning counts as a flag; outside it, today's tiers stand unchanged. This is the whole of the ASCII-only ask as the operator defined it in iteration: em-dashes, arrows, and the decoration family are warning-tier tropes today, so the strict reading flags them where it matters and no separate byte rule is built.</li> <li><strong>A counted non-ASCII census, disclosed not gated:</strong> the declared corpus's non-ASCII bytes are counted beside the verdict, so the exempt populations (Chinese script, which waits for the deferred full zh translation; the IPA of the pronunciation lines) stay measured and a new category is visible on arrival. Nothing gates on non-ASCII as a category; exempt means the census carries it, not that a rule spares it.</li> <li><strong>The manual is <code>AGENTS.md</code>;</strong> <code>CLAUDE.md</code> becomes a one-line text pointer to it, never a symlink (this working tree sits on a filesystem where the link bits do not survive, and a text pointer renders on the forge, survives Windows checkouts, and diffs honestly).</li> </ol> <h2 id="why-19"><a class="header" href="#why-19">Why</a></h2> <p>The warn half is about holding ground, not retaking it: the manuals sit at zero prose warnings today (the trope pass of 2026-09-05), and zero is only as durable as the tier that guards it. The advisory tier exists for records and drafts; the always-loaded surfaces are the text every session reads and executes, and a warn there is advice to the instruction itself. The verify recheck's prose clause already blocks, but only at release time and over the whole tracked corpus; the strict reading makes the state visible and gateable where the content lives.</p> <p>The census half exists because the operator exempted two populations by name (zh script, IPA) while wanting "ASCII-only" for the decoration typography. A census keeps that shape honest: the exempt populations are counted and disclosed on every verdict, so "exempt" never silently becomes "anything goes", and a new non-ASCII category announces itself instead of arriving unmeasured.</p> <p>The rename half adopts the vendor-neutral convention <a href="plan/0085-active-default-surfaces/../../DESIGN-LEM-MEMORY.html">DESIGN-LEM-MEMORY.md</a> recorded as the open direction (the feedback register's "AGENTS.md is the emerging vendor-neutral convention", ruled by the operator now). It is a spine change: template-first, ledger-carried, with this host migrating in full. Tool surfaces naming the old name are enumerated, not guessed: 20 references in host-lifecycle's source (the generator and spine paths), plus memory.rs, dream.rs, and the entrance's README. Sequenced before <a href="plan/0085-active-default-surfaces/../0079-spine-is-a-rendered-artifact/README.html">plan/0079</a> starts its build, because call/0053 defines the spine as the byte content of the template's manual plus STRUCTURE.md, and the rendered artifact must be defined over the renamed file set, not renamed mid-render.</p> <h2 id="the-lem-correction"><a class="header" href="#the-lem-correction">The lem correction</a></h2> <p>The manual carries <strong>partial zh translations</strong> of the pronoun system: Chinese columns in the paradigm tables, zh and Cantonese example sentences, and a zh pronunciation line. Those are <strong>removed</strong> from the always-loaded copies (template and host) as a content edit; the system is taught in English with the IPA pronunciations intact. The <strong>full zh translation is deferred</strong> by operator ruling and recorded in PLAN.md's follow-up table, so the deferred work is on the record rather than implicit; when it lands, the census already measures it.</p> <p><strong>Landed early (2026-09-05, operator-directed).</strong> The zh removal is no longer waiting for this plan's build: the partial zh content was observed switching an agent into Chinese mid-session, so both manuals were edited the same day: the quick-reference Chinese column, the Chinese paradigm, the zh pronunciation and example lines, the zh-specific rules, and the decoration characters beside them (the section sign and three arrow glyphs) are gone from the always-loaded copies. What remains here is the census, the strict tier, the declaration, and the rename.</p> <h2 id="decision-2"><a class="header" href="#decision-2">Decision</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The corpus is declared, never discovered.</strong> The always-loaded file set is declared in the recipe (the exact home is a gather-data question: a manifest stanza versus a <code>.host</code> key), and the gate derives its population from the declaration. The plan/0074 lesson governs: deriving requirements from directory listings made emptying a directory delete the question.</li> <li><strong>Strict inside the declaration.</strong> The gate reads the declared set and applies one rule no other corpus carries: a warning is a flag. Outside the declaration, today's tiers stand unchanged. One declaration serves every checker that needs it; the <code>.host-lintignore</code> lesson (one list silently serving two checkers) is the failure shape this avoids.</li> <li><strong>The census discloses and never gates.</strong> Non-ASCII bytes in the declared corpus are counted on every verdict. The two known populations (zh script, IPA) are what the count is expected to hold; the point of the count is that a third population is news.</li> <li><strong>No surface outside host-lint may gate character content (audited 2026-09-05, operator ruling: the Latin alphabet is fully permitted, the section sign and arrows were the decoration family).</strong> The audit covered the git attributes (line-ending normalization only), every workflow, the shell scripts and the entrance installer (no charset checks), and every <code>is_ascii</code> use in host-lifecycle (all token parsers recognizing ASCII-shaped identifiers: register and issue numbers, slug shapes, review-finding codes; the reference walk's boundary check is Unicode-aware <code>is_alphanumeric</code>). Unicode language content answers to host-lint's decoration tropes alone, and the implementation of this plan must not introduce a second gate: the census counts, the strict tier escalates warnings, and nothing else reads bytes.</li> <li><strong>The pointer is text.</strong> After the rename, <code>CLAUDE.md</code> holds a line naming <code>AGENTS.md</code> and nothing else. Tools that look for the old name find a pointer that says where the manual is; the pointer file is itself in the declared corpus and passes its own gate. The exact pointer text is a Fen question: does the weak model, handed the pointer, open the manual?</li> </ul> <h2 id="scope-8"><a class="header" href="#scope-8">Scope</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The declaration and the gate</strong>: host-lifecycle reads the declaration and applies the strict tier to the declared files in the prose walk and the verify recheck; the census rides the same verdict.</li> <li><strong>The rename</strong>: template-first (<code>git mv</code> keeps the manual's history), the pointer file, the host-lifecycle surface changes, the entrance, this host's migration.</li> <li><strong>The lem content edit</strong>: the zh partials leave the always-loaded copies; the deferred full translation is recorded in the follow-up table.</li> </ol> <p>Out of scope, recorded so it is not assumed: the full zh translation (deferred by operator ruling, its own future work); gating on non-ASCII as a category (declined by definition this session); rewriting records (plan/, call/, MEMORY.md keep their own bytes); the <code>.host-lintignore</code> two-list separation (still owed, its own milestone, and the new declaration must not become a second ignore list); the strict tier over any corpus beyond the declaration; plan/0079's render (this plan only fixes the file set it will render); symlink support (declined above, recorded why).</p> <h2 id="open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles-2"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-the-gather-data-node-settles-2">Open questions the gather-data node settles</a></h2> <ul> <li>The declaration's home: a <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> stanza or a <code>.host</code> key, and the exact grammar (globs? explicit lists?).</li> <li>The skills' census: which linked skills carry warns or non-ASCII bytes today, and whether skill frontmatter counts as always-loaded.</li> <li>The complete surface list naming <code>CLAUDE.md</code> (source, docs, workflows, the entrance), each with its migration shape.</li> <li>Which lem lines are zh partials (removed) and which are doctrine that stays; the census's expected populations stated per file.</li> <li>The pointer file's exact text, settled by a Fen probe: does the weak model, handed the pointer, open the manual?</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-sequence-25"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-25">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="gather-data"><a class="header" href="#gather-data">The settled conditionals</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the warn and non-ASCII census recorded per declared file, with the exempt populations stated; the surface list naming CLAUDE.md complete with migration shapes; the declaration home settled with the grammar written; the zh partials enumerated line by line against the doctrine that stays; the pointer text Fen-probed on the corrected protocol, transcripts recorded</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spec"><a class="header" href="#write-spec">The declaration and the strict tier</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the Allium spec models the declared corpus, the strict tier (a warning is a flag inside the declaration), and the census disclosure; <code>allium check</code> and <code>analyse</code> exit clean</li> <li>depends: #gather-data</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-obligations"><a class="header" href="#write-obligations">The obligations</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every new obligation carries a disposition naming a test that exercises the rule, and the day-one state is expressed as tests (the declaration reddens on any warn inside it, and the census discloses zh and IPA without flagging them)</li> <li>depends: #write-spec</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-gate"><a class="header" href="#implement-gate">The gate</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: <code>cargo test</code> green; a declared file's warning flags and an undeclared one advises; the census counts non-ASCII without flagging it; the population comes from the declaration, so deleting a declared file is a missing-file verdict, never a smaller corpus</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="implement-rename"><a class="header" href="#implement-rename">The rename</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: template carries AGENTS.md with the pointer file; host-lifecycle accepts both names during the migration window and generates AGENTS.md at the new revision; the entrance and every enumerated surface migrated; <code>git mv</code> history intact</li> <li>depends: #implement-gate</li> </ul> <h3 id="migrate-this-host"><a class="header" href="#migrate-this-host">This host migrates</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: this repo's manual is AGENTS.md with the pointer file; STRUCTURE.md and the forward documents cite the new name; the declared corpus passes its own strict gate on the real tree</li> <li>depends: #implement-rename</li> </ul> <h3 id="cast-consult"><a class="header" href="#cast-consult">Cast consultation</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: each persona's concern addressed or recorded in design-review.md, with Mara pricing the gate's keeping-green cost and Bly reading the adopter migration path cold</li> <li>depends: #migrate-this-host</li> </ul> <h3 id="adversarial-review"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review">Adversarial review</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: an independent multi-lens read of the built diffs records every blocking finding fixed or carried, with a dedicated lens for the declaration becoming a second ignore list, one for the census growing into a gate by drift, and one for the doctrine fragmenting between the manual and the future zh translation</li> <li>depends: #cast-consult</li> </ul> <h3 id="fen-acceptance"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance">The weak-agent acceptance</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the real qwen3.5-4b, on the corrected protocol, follows the pointer file to AGENTS.md, applies the pronoun system from the manual without the zh partials, and reads the strict verdict without remediating records; rotation-stable, transcripts recorded; an unreachable channel is labeled and the probes owed, never simulated silently</li> <li>depends: #write-obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="write-spine-doctrine"><a class="header" href="#write-spine-doctrine">The spine doctrine</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the ledger entries land (the rename with adopter migration steps; the declared-corpus invariants and census superseding the lem entry's sync instruction); the template manual states the strict tier where it states the reference discipline</li> <li>depends: #adversarial-review</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the component releases cascade clean, <code>software --check .</code> is green at the new pins for everything this milestone owns, and the grammar-cascade hazards plan/0084 carried are named beside whatever remains; PLAN.md and MEMORY.md record the outcome in their own commits</li> <li>depends: #write-spine-doctrine, #fen-acceptance</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adversarial-review-five-lenses-on-the-built-diff-2026-09-05-1"><a class="header" href="#adversarial-review-five-lenses-on-the-built-diff-2026-09-05-1">adversarial-review: five lenses on the built diff (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>The diff under review: host-lifecycle <code>36c1703</code> against <code>f5d69f7</code> (the declaration reader, the strict tier, the census, the rename surfaces), plus the host and template content migrations. The cut named three dedicated lenses; they ran first.</p> <h2 id="lens-1-the-declaration-becoming-a-second-ignore-list"><a class="header" href="#lens-1-the-declaration-becoming-a-second-ignore-list">Lens 1: the declaration becoming a second ignore list</a></h2> <p>Attack: <code>.host-lintignore</code> and <code>.host-corpus</code> are both dot-files read by sweeps, and a reader meeting both asks why one hides files and the other hunts them. Worse: a project could declare a file IN the corpus while ignoring it in the list, and the two lists would fight.</p> <p>Finding: the fight case is real but its resolution is already ordered. The ignore list excludes a file from the engine's walk, so a declared-and-ignored file yields no engine verdict, while the declaration still checks presence (the file exists), and any warns inside it are invisible because the engine never read it. That is a silent hole: a declared file that is also ignored gets corpus membership without strict-tier coverage. The walk's ignore behavior is load-bearing for the record layer (MEMORY.md by construction), so the remedy names the interaction instead of bypassing ignores; the doctrine node's ledger entry carries it as a stated rule (a file in the declared corpus must not be in the ignore list), recorded as a candidate check for the obligations if it ever bites in practice. Not blocking today; no declared file here is ignored.</p> <h2 id="lens-2-the-census-growing-into-a-gate-by-drift"><a class="header" href="#lens-2-the-census-growing-into-a-gate-by-drift">Lens 2: the census growing into a gate by drift</a></h2> <p>Attack: today the census discloses; tomorrow someone adds <code>exit 1</code> under the census print "just for non-ASCII tropes", and the operator's exemption ruling is quietly dead.</p> <p>Finding: the spec is the guard. <code>CensusIsNeverAViolation</code> was modeled as <code>CensusNamesPresentFiles</code> plus the structural fact that no rule creates a Violation from a CensusRow; the disclosure text itself says "never on script". The invariant that would make drift visible is the obligations' mutation discipline: any future rule creating a Violation from a Census must disposition against <code>the_census_discloses_non_ascii_without_flagging_it</code>, which asserts exit 0 with bytes present. Carried as the standing test, not a new mechanism.</p> <h2 id="lens-3-the-doctrine-fragmenting-between-the-manual-and-the-future-zh-translation"><a class="header" href="#lens-3-the-doctrine-fragmenting-between-the-manual-and-the-future-zh-translation">Lens 3: the doctrine fragmenting between the manual and the future zh translation</a></h2> <p>Attack: removing the zh partials and deferring the translation means the deferred work arrives into a corpus whose gate knows nothing about zh; the translation lands, the census counts it, and nothing guarantees the translation tracks the English doctrine as it evolves.</p> <p>Finding: real, and already on the record twice: the follow-up table row and the census's stated expected populations. The additional guarantee this round adds: the doctrine node's ledger entry supersedes the lem entry's sync instruction with the English-only manual, so the future translation is cut as its own milestone with its own sync instruction, never as an edit that drifts. Carried.</p> <h2 id="lens-4-the-renames-silent-surfaces"><a class="header" href="#lens-4-the-renames-silent-surfaces">Lens 4: the rename's silent surfaces</a></h2> <p>Attack: a rename driven by grep misses the surface that greps miss: the classify heuristic, the book placement, and any adopter tooling keyed to the old name.</p> <p>Finding: the surface list in gather-data was built from the grep plus a read of every hit, and the classify and placement changes carry tests (the suite runs green with both names accepted). The pointer file is the escape hatch for unknown surfaces: anything keyed to <code>CLAUDE.md</code> finds a file that names the manual. One real gap found and accepted: the ledger's three old <code>verify</code> greps name <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and would fail for an adopter applying those entries after this rename; the ledger is append-only, so the fix is the doctrine node's rename entry instructing mid-flight adopters. Blocking on the doctrine node, not on this diff.</p> <h2 id="lens-5-zero-drift-for-undeclared-trees"><a class="header" href="#lens-5-zero-drift-for-undeclared-trees">Lens 5: zero drift for undeclared trees</a></h2> <p>Attack: every project without an <code>active-corpus</code> key must behave byte-identically to v0.51.0, or the release is a behavior change smuggled to every adopter.</p> <p>Finding: the implementation's own structure makes the claim checkable: an absent key returns an empty declaration, which escalates nothing, censuses nothing, and misses nothing: and the undeclared-advisory test pins it end to end. The suite runs green. No finding.</p> <h2 id="disposition-5"><a class="header" href="#disposition-5">Disposition</a></h2> <p>No blocking findings in the diff. Three carries: the declared-and-ignored interaction (doctrine node names it; candidate check), the census's standing mutation test (already in the obligations), and the mid-flight ledger greps (doctrine node's rename entry). The plan/0079 dependency from the cast round rides with Orin's carry.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="design-review-the-cast-round-on-the-declared-corpus-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#design-review-the-cast-round-on-the-declared-corpus-2026-09-05">design-review: the cast round on the declared corpus (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>The design on the table: the <code>.host</code> stamp's <code>active-corpus = <file></code> declaration (a change from the cut README's manifest-stanza lean, corrected during gather-data), the strict tier in the prose verb, the census disclosure, and the rename surfaces. Each chair attacked their own first preference before speaking.</p> <h2 id="mara-the-operator-1"><a class="header" href="#mara-the-operator-1">Mara (the operator)</a></h2> <p>Concern: what does the declaration cost to keep green? A strict corpus is a gate that reddens on every editorial slip in the manual, and the manual is edited every session.</p> <p>Disposition: priced and accepted as the point. The manual sits at zero warns because the tropes pass just paid for it; the gate holds that ground at the moment of editing (the verify recheck runs <code>prose</code>, so a slipped em-dash stops the next release with the file and line named). The cost is one reword, payable immediately, on text the operator is reading anyway.</p> <h2 id="wren-the-agentic-developer-1"><a class="header" href="#wren-the-agentic-developer-1">Wren (the agentic developer)</a></h2> <p>Concern: the strict tier lives in the prose verb, but the pre-commit hook still advises warns on declared files — an author learns of the escalation only at the next release, not at commit time.</p> <p>Disposition: carried, deliberately. Wiring the declaration into the hook means host-lint reads project policy, which breaks the detection/policy split this plan is built on, and the hook cannot read the stamp's list file portably. The recheck catches it before anything permanent ships. Recorded as the first candidate if the friction shows in practice.</p> <h2 id="bly-the-downstream-adopter-cold-read-1"><a class="header" href="#bly-the-downstream-adopter-cold-read-1">Bly (the downstream adopter, cold read)</a></h2> <p>Concern: the declaration is a second policy file next to <code>.host-lintignore</code>, and the two read in opposite directions (one names files held stricter, one names files held not at all). Cold, that is confusing.</p> <p>Disposition: answered in the record, not the mechanics. The plan README states the difference as the design (one names the corpus held to the strict tier, one names records excluded by the append-only rule), and the ignore-list separation stays its own owed milestone. The declaration also has exactly one reader (the prose verb), so the two-lists-one-checker failure shape cannot recur here.</p> <h2 id="orin-the-methodology-maintainer-2"><a class="header" href="#orin-the-methodology-maintainer-2">Orin (the methodology maintainer)</a></h2> <p>Concern: the spine's own tree — the template — declares no corpus, so the template payload is held to advisory tiers in its own CI while every adopter's copy is held strict. The guardian is weaker than the flock.</p> <p>Disposition: carried with a date. A <code>.host</code> stamp in the template would make the template pretend to be its own adopter, which the stamp's meaning forbids. The honest fix arrives with plan/0079's render, where the template's always-loaded surfaces are guarded where they are authored; noted in the plan record as a plan/0079 dependency.</p> <h2 id="what-the-round-changed-1"><a class="header" href="#what-the-round-changed-1">What the round changed</a></h2> <p>Nothing in the built diff. Three carries recorded (the hook gap, the two-policy-files reading, the template's own tier), all owned by named later work.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="fen-acceptance-the-pointer-and-the-strict-tier-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#fen-acceptance-the-pointer-and-the-strict-tier-2026-09-05">fen-acceptance: the pointer and the strict tier (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>Status: <strong>the probes are owed.</strong> The gateway answers 401 to a session with no channel credentials (the plan/0084 record carries the labeled attempt; nothing has changed), so the kit cell is built and preserved, and no ballot was simulated.</p> <p><a href="plan/0085-active-default-surfaces/fen-p1.txt">fen-p1.txt</a> is the pointer probe: handed a repository whose CLAUDE.md is only the pointer line, does the model open AGENTS.md as the manual and name a correct next action? Two draws on the plan/0076 corrected protocol, appended to fen-results.md. Pass = both draws follow the pointer. The reading-safety probe from plan/0084's kit carries over unchanged: the strict verdict must not capture the agent into remediating records.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="gather-data-the-census-the-surface-list-the-declaration-the-pointer-2026-09-05"><a class="header" href="#gather-data-the-census-the-surface-list-the-declaration-the-pointer-2026-09-05">gather-data: the census, the surface list, the declaration, the pointer (2026-09-05)</a></h1> <p>This records the #gather-data node. Everything measured against the tree at <code>0c9a7472</code> (host) and host-template <code>8214ee3</code>.</p> <h2 id="the-warn-and-non-ascii-census"><a class="header" href="#the-warn-and-non-ascii-census">The warn and non-ASCII census</a></h2> <p>Swept with the pinned prose engine, per candidate always-loaded file:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>file</th><th>warns</th><th>non-ASCII lines</th><th>populations</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>CLAUDE.md (host)</td><td>0</td><td>4</td><td>IPA in the pronunciation lines; the ł of Stanisław</td></tr> <tr><td>STRUCTURE.md (host)</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>none</td></tr> <tr><td>host-template/CLAUDE.md</td><td>0</td><td>4</td><td>the same two populations</td></tr> <tr><td>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</td><td>0</td><td>0</td><td>none</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The zh partials were removed the same day the plan was cut (operator-directed, after the incident recorded in MEMORY.md), so the census's expected populations are exactly the two exempt ones. The strict tier's day-one job is therefore purely to hold zero.</p> <p><strong>The skills are not in this host's corpus.</strong> <code>.claude/skills/*</code> are generated, untracked symlinks into materialized components and tool submodules (link-skills.sh; the tracked-symlink lesson is call/0005), so their content is payload swept at its source: host-lint's and host-lifecycle's own repositories gate their SKILL.md files. The declared corpus here is the tracked manuals plus the territory and memory surfaces when plan/0083 builds them.</p> <h2 id="the-surface-list-naming-claudemd"><a class="header" href="#the-surface-list-naming-claudemd">The surface list naming CLAUDE.md</a></h2> <p>Complete as of this sweep, each with its migration shape:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>surface</th><th>shape</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>host-lifecycle</code> src/main.rs:986, <code>classify_case</code> reads <code>CLAUDE.md</code> presence to classify an adoption</td><td>functional: accept either name, AGENTS.md first, during the migration window</td></tr> <tr><td>src/main.rs:8326, <code>PLACED_ROOT_MD</code>, the known root documents of the book walk</td><td>functional: add <code>AGENTS.md</code> beside <code>CLAUDE.md</code></td></tr> <tr><td>src/main.rs:8601 to 8605, the How room places the manual (<code>dest: "CLAUDE.md"</code>, label <code>CLAUDE</code>)</td><td>functional: place AGENTS.md as the manual; the pointer file renders as the small page it is</td></tr> <tr><td>src/main.rs tests 13827, 14053, 14070-14072</td><td>functional: follow the placement changes</td></tr> <tr><td>src/memory.rs:5, src/dream.rs (2 sites), src/main.rs doc comments 972, 1299, 1657, 6071, 6323, 13412</td><td>text: update the comments to the new name where they describe live behavior; the two that cite <code>CLAUDE.md</code> section 6 as record history stay accurate either way because they describe where a rule is written, which is the pointer's target</td></tr> <tr><td><code>host/main/README.md</code>: the entrance's document</td><td>text: name AGENTS.md</td></tr> <tr><td>STRUCTURE.md (host and template): the How room row</td><td>text: name AGENTS.md</td></tr> <tr><td>host-template/lifecycle.manifest header comment</td><td>text: names the three prose copies; update with the rename</td></tr> <tr><td>call/0053 and the plan/0079 handoff</td><td>record: call/0053 defines the spine as the byte content of the template's CLAUDE.md plus STRUCTURE.md. The renamed set is AGENTS.md plus STRUCTURE.md <strong>plus the CLAUDE.md pointer</strong>, because the pointer's exact text is doctrine an adopter must carry byte-for-byte. This is a note for plan/0079's render, not a rewrite of the record</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="the-declarations-home-and-grammar"><a class="header" href="#the-declarations-home-and-grammar">The declaration's home and grammar</a></h2> <p><strong>Decision: a <code>[corpus "active"]</code> stanza in <code>lifecycle.manifest</code>, <code>file = <path></code> entries, explicit paths only.</strong> The reasoning:</p> <ul> <li>The manifest is already the single tool-readable journal the prose copies point at, and host-lifecycle reads it live: the same property <code>GATE-refs-in-verify</code> relies on. The plan/0074 lesson (derive the population from the recipe, never from directory listings) and the plan/0072 lesson (a discovery heuristic narrower than its subject reports completeness over whatever it saw) both point at an explicit declaration read from the recipe.</li> <li><code>.host</code> was rejected: it is the template stamp (template, revision, name, baseline) read by the stamp reader; project-authored policy does not belong in a file whose shape the tool owns.</li> <li>Globs were rejected for the first cut: a glob is a discovery heuristic, and the declared corpus is four files today. An explicit list that names a missing file yields a missing-file verdict: exactly the failure the declaration exists to make loud. Globs can be added when a corpus actually needs them.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-pointer-text"><a class="header" href="#the-pointer-text">The pointer text</a></h2> <p>Draft carried by this node, for the probe:</p> <blockquote> <p>The operating manual is AGENTS.md. This file is a pointer, kept so tools that look for CLAUDE.md find the manual's name.</p> </blockquote> <p>Probe question (Fen, on the corrected protocol): handed a repository whose CLAUDE.md contains only that line, does the model open and follow AGENTS.md as the manual? Two draws. The channel state is the one recorded in plan/0084's fen-acceptance: the gateway answers 401 to a session with no channel credentials, so the probe is <strong>owed</strong>, labeled, with nothing simulated; the kit gains this cell when the channel exists.</p> <h2 id="what-lands-where"><a class="header" href="#what-lands-where">What lands where</a></h2> <p>The strict tier and the census are policy in host-lifecycle (the prose verb reads the declaration, escalates warns to flags for declared files, and discloses the census), with detection untouched in host-lint. This is the same split that keeps the engine shared and the verdicts local. The pre-commit hook keeps today's behavior: it gates flags, advises warns, and does not read the declaration; the declared corpus's teeth are in the prose verb and the verify recheck that runs it.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0086-close-host-lint26-the-shipped-masking-fix-verified-and-closed"><a class="header" href="#plan0086-close-host-lint26-the-shipped-masking-fix-verified-and-closed">plan/0086 close host-lint#26: the shipped masking fix, verified and closed</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed (2026-09-06). The defect is already fixed and shipped; what never happened is the verification and closure. This milestone is that closure, on the plan/0082 <code>close-resolved</code> pattern: re-run the issue's own repro under the current toolchain, quote the transcript, close after the final push.</p> <h2 id="why-20"><a class="header" href="#why-20">Why</a></h2> <p><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/26">connollydavid/host-lint#26</a> reported that <code>mask_allowed</code> blanks a declared LEXICON phrase with spaces, so a phrase at column one left four or more leading spaces, the markdown extractor read them as an indented code block, and every tell on the line was dropped silently. The fix landed through the plan/0082 <code>lexicon-line-masking</code> work: the grammar decides markdown block structure before the mask (<code>e5ac04cb</code>, "decide markdown block structure before the mask, not after"), released in host-lint v0.19.0 (<code>ff0516a</code>, canonical <code>359b0367</code>, this host's pinned binary).</p> <p>The issue is still open because the node's verification step never ran: the session that shipped the fix ended first. Measured 2026-09-06 against the pinned binary, both shapes of the defect are fixed:</p> <ul> <li>a declared phrase at column one masks <strong>itself alone</strong>; the standalone tells on the same line warn at their own columns;</li> <li>the indented shape (a column-one phrase, then a bullet carrying a tell) leaves the bullet's tell standing.</li> </ul> <p>The transcript is recorded at <a href="plan/0086-close-host-lint-26/repro-transcript.txt">repro-transcript.txt</a>, binary identity established by the canonical sha256.</p> <p>The node's test demand is met in the released source: <code>prose_lexicon_at_column_one_masks_the_phrase_not_the_line</code> and its plain-text sibling (<code>tests/property_tests.rs</code>), the former citing this issue by name, both green in the suite.</p> <h2 id="decision-3"><a class="header" href="#decision-3">Decision</a></h2> <p>No code change. The milestone's work is evidence and closure: close the issue with the transcript quoted, mark plan/0082's census row and <code>lexicon-line-masking</code> node done, and record the closure in MEMORY.md. The closing rule from plan/0082 applies unchanged: <strong>the issue is not closed until the session's final push has landed</strong>, because closure is a claim made to everyone with access to the repository.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-26"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-26">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="verify"><a class="header" href="#verify">The verification</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the repro transcript recorded against the pinned binary with its hash; the two regression tests identified in the released source and green in the suite; the issue's state and comment count noted (open, none)</li> <li>depends: none</li> </ul> <h3 id="close"><a class="header" href="#close">The closure</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: connollydavid/host-lint#26 closed with the transcript quoted in the closing comment; plan/0082's census row and <code>lexicon-line-masking</code> node updated to done; MEMORY.md records the verification; all of it after the final push</li> <li>depends: #verify</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0087-word-choice-lacuna-27-and-24-verified-closed-the-house-diction-terms-measured"><a class="header" href="#plan0087-word-choice-lacuna-27-and-24-verified-closed-the-house-diction-terms-measured">plan/0087 word-choice lacuna: #27 and #24 verified-closed, the house-diction terms measured</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed (2026-09-06): "proceed to fix #27 ... consider the full lacuna and consult the cast fully." The lacuna, measured across three exploration passes the same day:</p> <ol> <li><strong><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/27">connollydavid/host-lint#27</a> does not reproduce in any form.</strong> <code>harness</code> has matched as verbs-only since v0.17.0 (call/0051); both cited spine lines are gone from the renamed manual or survive as nouns; all four sweeps exit 0; zero verb uses exist in any corpus. It sits open only because plan/0082's closing ritual holds the close until after the session's final push.</li> <li><strong>Its twin <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/24">connollydavid/host-lifecycle#24</a> carries the identical "verify and close" disposition</strong>, verified by <code>host-lifecycle --version</code> and the <code>.host-software</code> stanza, both present since v0.50.0.</li> <li><strong>The substantive gap is call/0051's own deferred question</strong>: the six <code>house-diction</code> terms were adopted <strong>without measurement</strong>, the wholesale-adoption anti-pattern call/0051 confesses in its own record. Their reconciliation is "now open" by that decision's words and no corpus has been read since.</li> <li><strong>The held-out trio</strong> (<code>framework</code>/<code>ecosystem</code>/<code>paradigm</code>) waits on "add one back when a corpus shows the grandiose sense": an invitation with no owner and no corpus read.</li> <li><strong>The SKILL.md silence</strong>: host-lint's agent-facing SKILL.md never mentions the LEXICON mechanism, while the strict directive's own block message names <code>host-lint lexicon add</code> as the remedy, so an agent loading only the skill gets no doctrine and no sanctioned-vocabulary path.</li> </ol> <p>(#25's <code>.host-lint-allow</code> ghost is resolved, closed in v0.50.0 with the alias kept inside remap only. #26 was verified and closed by plan/0086.)</p> <h2 id="decision-4"><a class="header" href="#decision-4">Decision</a></h2> <p>The cast convenes <strong>fully</strong>, on the call/0050 and plan/0080 pattern: a written briefing; five ranked ballots (Mara, Wren, Bly, Orin, and Fen, the real qwen3.5-4b driven as acceptance test on the plan/0076 corrected protocol, or simulated with the substitution labeled and the real probe owed); each ballot attacks its own first preference before ranking it; the operator breaks ties. The delta to close: a compact LEXICON section in SKILL.md: the mechanism, the remedy command, and the declaration-is-a-report doctrine in one or two sentences.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0088-prose-guidance-ab-does-naming-the-banned-words-help-or-do-positive-exemplars-work-better"><a class="header" href="#plan0088-prose-guidance-ab-does-naming-the-banned-words-help-or-do-positive-exemplars-work-better">plan/0088 prose-guidance A/B: does naming the banned words help, or do positive exemplars work better?</a></h1> <p>An auto-research experiment, operator-directed (2026-09-06): invert how the word-choice topic is discussed: instead of prohibition lists, give positive examples: and measure whether it works before changing any doctrine.</p> <h2 id="the-hypothesis"><a class="header" href="#the-hypothesis">The hypothesis</a></h2> <p>Prohibition lists have two failure modes with language models. The known one: the model finds synonyms the list does not know, so the slop survives the ban. The suspected one, demonstrated four times in this session: <strong>the detector fires on its own documentation</strong>: a document that names the banned words in order to ban them trips the rule that bans them. The inversion states the target as exemplars: "write like this" names nothing that needs banning.</p> <h2 id="design-1"><a class="header" href="#design-1">Design</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Writer</strong>: the session model (a strong model that has internalized this session's house style: a declared limitation, below). Each sample is a first draft, generated straight through, never revised.</li> <li><strong>Conditions</strong>, identical except for the guidance sentence appended to the same task prompt: <ul> <li><strong>A (control)</strong>: the bare task.</li> <li><strong>B (negative list)</strong>: the task plus the current <code>ai-diction</code>/<code>grandiose-noun</code>/<code>house-diction</code> terms and the decoration family, as prohibitions.</li> <li><strong>C (positive exemplars)</strong>: the task plus two clean exemplar sentences, naming nothing banned.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Tasks</strong>: two, both slop-inducing genres: a capability description for a README (T1) and a milestone summary paragraph (T2).</li> <li><strong>Draws</strong>: three per task per condition: 18 samples.</li> <li><strong>Scorer</strong>: <code>host-lint --prose <file></code> per sample; the score is the count of warning lines. The tool is the whole judge; no human reads the samples before scoring.</li> <li>The prompts are preserved verbatim in <a href="plan/0088-prose-guidance-ab/prompts.html">prompts.md</a>; the samples in <a href="plan/0088-prose-guidance-ab/samples/">samples/</a>, unedited.</li> </ul> <h2 id="declared-limitations"><a class="header" href="#declared-limitations">Declared limitations</a></h2> <ol> <li>The writer knows the scorer: unavoidable, and equally true of every condition, so the <em>differences</em> remain informative while the absolute counts do not transfer to an unaware writer.</li> <li>One writer, one session. This is a pilot for the harness; the population the doctrine cares about is the weak model, and the harness reruns with the real qwen3.5-4b the moment a channel exists (the standing owed probe, now with a reusable kit).</li> <li>N = 18 is a pilot's N. The result is directional evidence, not a verdict.</li> </ol> <h2 id="result-1"><a class="header" href="#result-1">Result</a></h2> <p>See <a href="plan/0088-prose-guidance-ab/results.html">results.md</a>: the per-sample scores, the condition means, and the reading.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h2 id="fen-a-t1-1"><a class="header" href="#fen-a-t1-1">fen-a-t1-1</a></h2> <p>warns=1</p> <pre><code>We now introduce a safe reconciliation feature for our CLI manifest tool.
