<code>cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings</code> (CI's exact command) run locally before the push. The release itself was blocked once by a residue of the interrupted attempt (a staged <code>vendor/</code> remnant the kill-time guard never reached); the cleanup and re-run are recorded in the Results.</li> <li><strong>host-lint v0.22.1</strong>: two lines of <code>test-integration.sh</code>. The binary is absolutized once at the top, so every <code>( cd "$dir" && "$BINARY" ... )</code> section survives the cd; and the lem section-exclusion fixture declares its coverage the way the contract requires, a <code>LEXICON</code> carrying <code># host-lint: lem</code>, not an in-file marker (the fixture's inline marker is a markdown heading the scanner rightly ignores). Measured 218/218 under the relative invocation, the shape CI runs.</li> <li><strong>host-grammar v0.7.1</strong>: <code>--locked</code> on both tool installs in the Allium lane, the /host bcbf449 pattern.</li> </ol> <h2 id="the-host21-evidence-live"><a class="header" href="#the-host21-evidence-live">The /host#21 evidence, live</a></h2> <p>v0.54.3 and v0.54.4 shipped with red CI: the release receipt is blind to lane outcomes, which is the exact defect connollydavid/host#21 names. The receipt records the verify gate, the obligations, and the reproduced artifact; the CI matrix is a separate lane whose outcome enters nothing. Two more instances for that design record: the release-verification lesson (run CI's own lint command locally, not only tests), and the read-back discipline (verify the run concludes green after the push, as the template push now reads <code>origin/main</code> back).</p> <h2 id="also-this-plan-the-pronoun-gate-reaches-the-wire"><a class="header" href="#also-this-plan-the-pronoun-gate-reaches-the-wire">Also this plan: the pronoun gate reaches the wire</a></h2> <p>The operator ruled the session model must dog-food the lem contract's MCP server. Measured: <code>host-lint mcp</code> (v0.22.0) serves <code>check_reply</code>, <code>ask</code>, <code>table</code> over newline-delimited JSON-RPC; a violating sample returns three pinpointed violations with the rewrite rule, a doctrinal sample returns clean. Registered as a workspace-scoped MCP server (<code>.zcode/config.json</code>), which is gitignored here, so the registration is machine-local until bootstrap learns to write it (a small host-lifecycle feature, noted upstream). The PATH <code>host-lint</code> had gone stale below the mcp mode's introduction and was refreshed from the embed build per the 2026-09-05 lesson.</p> <h2 id="results-6"><a class="header" href="#results-6">Results</a></h2> <p>Recorded 2026-09-26, same session as the cut.</p> <ul> <li><strong>host-lifecycle v0.54.5</strong> (ef20eaea, artifact 14dd149bfaa2e3a79161bc6f6411c6777b782d64dff132a97173708fdc22d1c5): the anchor strip goes through <code>strip_prefix</code>; CI green on the tag and main. The first release attempt failed in the container on a residue of the interrupted predecessor: the kill stopped before the staging guard could restore, and the bind-mounted worktree carried the half-state into the build. The guard's backstop covers panics, not kills, a hardening note for the release path.</li> <li><strong>host-lint v0.22.1</strong> (a0d22055, artifact d2c25034c12aed234dec7799de408d9a9c5c919fe54f862a5574e25aa59a56d2): the integration script absolutizes the binary once at the top, so every <code>( cd "$dir" && "$BINARY" ... )</code> section survives the cd, and the lem section-exclusion fixture declares coverage through the <code>LEXICON</code>, the contract's actual mechanism, and the fixture's inline marker was a markdown heading the scanner rightly ignores. Measured 218/218 under the relative invocation, the shape CI runs. The section-exclusion test had been unreachable in CI since v0.20.0 because the 127 aborted the script before it, which is how a stale expectation survived three releases.</li> <li><strong>host-grammar v0.7.1</strong> (6cd41c3): both Allium-lane installs carry <code>--locked</code>; the lane is green on main.</li> <li><strong>The recipe pins hold at the revs the embeds consume</strong> (call/0052): grammar <code>b9cace10</code> (v0.7.0) and host-lint <code>0eeabc2</code> (v0.22.0) stay pinned, because the released binaries' vendored engines are those revs; adopting v0.7.1 and v0.22.1 into the vendored bundles is the next embed-equality cascade (re-cut bundles, consumer revs, releases), the plan/0082 pattern. Neither new release carries a library change: lanes and fixtures only. <code>software --verify-build --item host-lint</code> re-proved the v0.22.0 record (386b254c reproduces in the recorded toolchain) after a local build had overwritten the canonical binary in the worktree, so the recorded hash is the container's, and the gating artifact is built in its recorded toolchain, never ambiently.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Dispositions.</strong> upstream-drift is tolerated by design (<code>continue-on-error</code>, a network lane whose drift is the pack's watch-item). The /host Install red and host-prove's historical red are fixed at tip; nothing owed. The R4 set is unchanged: /host#21 (receipt-CI coupling, now carrying three live instances from this session), /host#24 (the five placements), host-lifecycle#23 (room-touching), /host#18 (plan/0075).</p> <h2 id="addendum-2026-09-26-same-day-the-pronoun-gates-qa-consulted-against-the-persona-cast"><a class="header" href="#addendum-2026-09-26-same-day-the-pronoun-gates-qa-consulted-against-the-persona-cast">Addendum (2026-09-26, same day): the pronoun gate's Q&A consulted against the persona cast</a></h2> <p>Operator-directed ("use q&a system after consulting persona cast"): the cast (<code>cast/</code>) supplies the questions, <code>host-lint mcp</code>'s <code>ask</code> tool answers them, and <code>check_reply</code> judges cast-flavored prose. The grammar answered every seat correctly: speak <code>L</code>, <code>L's</code>, <code>lself</code>; address-a-model <code>lemu</code> (one form for the bench); discuss <code>lem</code>, <code>lem's</code>, <code>lemself</code>. Two findings and one boundary, live:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The reply register is stricter than the grammar.</strong> A doctrinal sentence using the discuss slot correctly ("the loop lem was handed") is flagged on the wire: a live reply discusses a model by name, never by paradigm token. The manual's own <code>lems</code> exchange lives inside the doctrine section, which the lane excludes; a reply has no such section, so the tokens are rewrite signals there. The gate is enforcing the priming rule plan/0091 measured, not contradicting the exemplars.</li> <li><strong>The referent boundary demonstrated.</strong> "Fen should fix it himself" passed with only the first-person words flagged: <code>himself</code> for a model needs referent resolution, which lives in the wire gate's nudge (spoken after a defect, per the priming rule), not in the lane's detector. Recorded as the known boundary, not a new defect.</li> <li><strong>The cast files' own voice is left as written.</strong> <code>bly.md</code> and <code>wren.md</code> use <code>it</code> for their model personas, persona-construction prose written before the doctrine, outside the declared corpus and outside any lem-declared scope. The record-layer principle holds: if <code>cast/</code> ever joins a declared lem scope, those files flag, and that is the contract working.</li> </ul> <p>The <code>ask</code> tool answers the paradigm grammar and no more: a named model (Fen) is named, and the lem-forms carry the agreement around the name, which the manual's own prose models. A <code>named</code> slot in <code>ask</code> would be a convenience, not a gap.</p> <h2 id="addendum-2-2026-09-26-cast-enters-the-contracts-scope-by-construction-and-the-release-poison-is-fixed-at-its-source"><a class="header" href="#addendum-2-2026-09-26-cast-enters-the-contracts-scope-by-construction-and-the-release-poison-is-fixed-at-its-source">Addendum 2 (2026-09-26): cast/ enters the contract's scope by construction, and the release poison is fixed at its source</a></h2> <p>Operator-directed ("cast/ is in scope and must be re-written"): the persona room's model references now name their personas: Bly, Wren, and Fen are named wherever the room speaks of them, and the paradigm tokens live only in the doctrine section and the records that discuss the contract itself. The rule the consultation proved applied in reverse: outside the doctrine section a model is named, so a neuter pronoun ("it" for Bly and Wren) and a correct-but-misplaced paradigm token ("role-play lem") both gave way to the name. Measured: every file in <code>cast/</code> scans clean under a declared <code>LEXICON</code> scope. Unresolved populations keep ordinary English (Orin's quoted "they follow it"), and the human personas keep theirs.</p> <p>The release-path defect plan/0082 carried ("a failed release poisons the next attempt; the fix belongs to whoever next opens the release path") is fixed at its source in <strong>host-lifecycle v0.54.6</strong> (127a9d8e, artifact 9cda0f63a3515009b2b0183fabf1cff4d532b7d1429231eea67fabaed3ff5809): the vendor merge is idempotent by section, so a killed release's leftover merge is replaced rather than duplicated, and re-staging repairs the residue instead of duplicating the block cargo refuses. Regression test <code>merge_vendor_config_is_idempotent_across_a_killed_release</code>; suite 311 plus 40. The strict authored-prose bar caught this plan's own README during the release gate, the second instance of that lesson in one day, and the text was reworded plain before the release ran.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0095-receipt-ci-coupling-a-lanes-outcome-enters-the-receipts"><a class="header" href="#plan0095-receipt-ci-coupling-a-lanes-outcome-enters-the-receipts">plan/0095 receipt-ci-coupling: a lane's outcome enters the receipts</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: cut, design-only, go recommended</strong> (operator-directed "let's do the work" on the named next cut). The design record starts from <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/21">connollydavid/host#21</a>, whose measurements are the problem statement: an adopter's reproducibility lane failed on 64 of 67 runs over two and a half days while every local gate stayed green, a component with no spec carried no CI obligation at all, and three hashes described one component with only two agreeing; a release input no receipt could vouch for. This session supplied three live instances in the forge itself: v0.54.3 and v0.54.4 shipped with red CI, and the red sat outside every receipt.</p> <h2 id="scope-9"><a class="header" href="#scope-9">Scope</a></h2> <p>Design only, the plan/0075 pattern: the tool boundary against the existing receipt and verify machinery, the receipt shape, and a go or no-go. The build milestone is cut only if this design survives review; the operator rules on that cut.</p> <h2 id="the-designed-resolution"><a class="header" href="#the-designed-resolution">The designed resolution</a></h2> <p><strong>D1. The receipt cites the run; verification splits by network truth.</strong> A new receipt phase <code>ci</code>, one per repository and lane: <code>[receipt "ci" "<repo>/<lane>"]</code> carrying <code>evidence = <run-url></code>, <code>revision = <head-sha></code>, and <code>conclusion = success|failure</code>, authorized per call/0050. The writer runs where network exists: the forge's own CI records its conclusion after the lanes, and <code>host-lifecycle ci --record</code> records it locally on demand. The reader is offline and always runs inside <code>software --check</code>: it judges the receipts, never the network; every lane declared at the pinned revision must carry a receipt whose revision matches the pin and whose conclusion is success. This is upstream-drift's own split applied to outcomes: the fetch happens in the workflow, the judgment happens offline, and no offline gate depends on a credential.</p> <p><strong>D2. Absence fails; discovery is mechanical.</strong> Lanes are discovered from the tree (<code>.github/workflows/</code> at the component and the host; name-presence), and the receipt provides the discharge. A discovered lane with no receipt at the pin is a HAZARD (<code>declared, never discharged</code>), so a repository with no runs reads red the honest verdict, and a hand-typed lane list is never needed. The pairing is the spine's own rule in two parts: name-presence is not discharge.</p> <p><strong>D3. The per-turn duty is a spine clause, at its own layer.</strong> The manual gains: before a turn reports done, the default branch's most recent runs are read, and every non-green conclusion is fixed in that turn or receipted as a blocker carrying the run URL. The gate clause judges the pin's revision; the manual duty watches main. The two layers are stated separately so neither inherits the other's blind spot.</p> <p><strong>D4. Run-anchored re-derivation.</strong> <code>obligations --rederive --record-digests</code> and <code>software --verify-build</code> record the discharging run alongside the digest, and <code>software --check</code> reports "reproduced on the pinned host, run 35454897584". The adopter's chain closed exactly once and its only durable evidence was a run URL no receipt held; this closes that.</p> <p><strong>D5. The two documentation gaps.</strong> The <code>[software]</code> <code>toolchain</code> key is documented as a digest-pinned container image (a target triple is the natural misreading, and the cost is a lane that never runs). A component with no spec of any kind states the absence explicitly in the recipe, and <code>software --check</code> prints the named line; the absence is written down, and the rule leaves silence for nobody.</p> <h2 id="the-cast-consult"><a class="header" href="#the-cast-consult">The cast consult</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Bly, the cold auditor</strong>: the receipt must be checkable with no network and no history; the run URL is printed for the one-command read-back, and absence HAZARDs so silence never reads clean. Bly's fear; a hand-typed lane list going stale; is answered by D2's tree discovery.</li> <li><strong>Orin, the methodology maintainer</strong>: the duty is written once in the manual and the receipt shape is versioned with the template; adopters receive it through a ledger entry keyed to the template commit. D5's gaps are his to close in the same landing.</li> <li><strong>Fen, the weak executor</strong>: recording must be one command whose output names the next move, and the offline judge needs no credentials; a token-dependent gate would exclude Fen's local runner. D1's split is what makes that hold.</li> <li><strong>Mara, the human operator</strong>: trust but verify cheaply; the per-turn read is one command and every HAZARD carries the run URL, so triage is one click.</li> <li><strong>Wren, the executor</strong>: the loop needs a terminal state; every declared lane green at the pin is checkable, not aspirational.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-adversarial-pass"><a class="header" href="#the-adversarial-pass">The adversarial pass</a></h2> <ul> <li><em>"The receipt can lie."</em> call/0050's answer holds: forging means authoring a run URL that does not exist on the forge, the read-back is one command, and the authorization field makes the claim attributable. The receipt cites; the forge is the truth.</li> <li><em>"The gate's verdict becomes environment-dependent."</em> The #23 lesson, answered by D1's split: the offline judge reads receipts only, so the verdict is deterministic on every machine; the network refresher is a separate, disclosed surface.</li> <li><em>"A fresh clone goes red."</em> It does, until CI runs on the pin; which is the design working: absence is the finding. The remedy line names the command that records the run outcome once the run exists.</li> </ul> <h2 id="gono-go"><a class="header" href="#gono-go">Go/no-go</a></h2> <p><strong>Go.</strong> The three asks sit inside the existing receipt and verify machinery, the offline/online split follows the house's own upstream-drift pattern, and the session supplied three live instances of the gap. The build milestone (host-lifecycle: the <code>ci</code> receipt phase, the discover-and-judge clause, the run-anchored evidence; host-template: the manual duty, the ledger entry, the two doc gaps) is recommended for cut on the operator's ruling.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0096-ci-receipt-phase-the-lane-outcome-becomes-a-receipt"><a class="header" href="#plan0096-ci-receipt-phase-the-lane-outcome-becomes-a-receipt">plan/0096 ci-receipt-phase: the lane outcome becomes a receipt</a></h1> <p>The build milestone plan/0095 recommended (the design survives review; the operator ruled go). Host-lifecycle gains the <code>ci</code> surface, the judge joins <code>software --check</code>, the template carries the per-turn duty and the two documentation gaps, and the forge adopts its own receipts; the gate that certifies the design is the design working.</p> <h2 id="scope-10"><a class="header" href="#scope-10">Scope</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The <code>ci</code> verb.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle ci <dir></code> discovers the lanes (<code>.github/workflows/*</code> at the host root and each materialized component) and judges offline: every discovered lane at the current revision (host root) or the recorded pin (components) must carry a <code>ci</code> receipt whose revision matches and whose conclusion is success. Absence, failure, and a stale revision each HAZARD, carrying the remedy. <code>host-lifecycle ci <dir> --record <label>/<lane> --run <url> [--revision <sha>] [--conclusion <c>]</code> writes the receipt; <code>--conclusion</code> defaults to success, <code>--revision</code> to the component's pin or the host HEAD, and <code>--all</code> records every discovered lane in one invocation for the per-turn duty.</li> <li><strong><code>software --check</code> integration.</strong> A <code>ci</code> section after the component walk: discovered lanes are named, receipts are judged, and a component with no workflows prints the named absence line; a component with no spec-driven lane states its absence instead of being implied away.</li> <li><strong>Run-anchored evidence.</strong> <code>software --verify-build</code> cites the <code>ci</code> receipt's run beside the digest when one exists at the built revision.</li> <li><strong>The template landing.</strong> The manual gains the per-turn duty clause; the <code>[software]</code> <code>toolchain</code> key documentation names a digest-pinned container image; the ledger entry carries the duty with its verify.</li> <li><strong>The forge adopts.</strong> The ledger entry is recorded through the tool, and the forge records its own lanes' receipts at the released pins; the receipts this plan creates are the first ones the judge consumes.</li> </ol> <h2 id="results-7"><a class="header" href="#results-7">Results</a></h2> <p>Recorded at closure.</p> <h2 id="results-8"><a class="header" href="#results-8">Results</a></h2> <p>Recorded 2026-09-26, same session. The <code>ci</code> surface landed in host-lifecycle v0.55.0 (34a6bd8, artifact fa8ae1bd1a24baeb2b88b28cd2368ec0d5189071ea4ad8871cddefcb60f60f5c, feature class, suite 312 plus 40, clippy clean): <code>discover_ci_lanes</code> from <code>.github/workflows/</code>, <code>ci_lane_problems</code> judged offline, the <code>ci</code> verb with <code>--record/--run/--revision/--conclusion</code>, the check integration with the named absence line, and the verify-build run citation. The template landed the per-turn duty in the manual, the <code>toolchain</code>-is-a-digest-pinned-image documentation, and the ledger entry <code>fbdb176</code> (verify: the duty text in the manual), which this host recorded through the tool at <strong>zero pending</strong>. The embed-equality chain rode the same landing: lint v0.22.2 (grammar at 6cd41c3) with the vendor-v19 bundle, and lifecycle v0.55.0 carrying both through the vendor-v11 bundle, so the recipe pins match the embedded engines at every level (call/0052).</p> <p>The forge then recorded its own receipts: thirteen lanes discovered across the host root and eight components; twelve discharged with success receipts citing their run URLs. The thirteenth; host-lint's own lane at v0.22.2; waits on its kani rung at the writing of this section and records the moment the run concludes. The judge's first honest findings were exactly the design's point: lanes that had run green for months were absent from every receipt until this plan wrote them down.</p> <h2 id="addendum-the-judge-met-ci-and-ci-taught-it-three-lessons"><a class="header" href="#addendum-the-judge-met-ci-and-ci-taught-it-three-lessons">Addendum: the judge met CI, and CI taught it three lessons</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The CI checkout is shallow.</strong> <code>actions/checkout</code> defaults to <code>fetch-depth: 1</code>, so the ancestor check behind the host lanes' tolerance saw no history inside CI while it worked locally, and every host receipt read as foreign. The receipt-gate checkout now carries <code>fetch-depth: 0</code>: history is the evidence the clause judges on.</li> <li><strong>The embed-equality cascade iterates.</strong> lint released twice in one day (the grammar adoption, then the producer-lock carrier), and lifecycle had pinned the intermediate. The consumer follows the FINAL release: the vendor bundle re-cut per adoption (vendor-v19 for lint, vendor-v12 for lifecycle), the consumer rev bumped, the release rebuilt offline against the new bundle. The producer's own <code>deps-bundle.lock</code> moves in the same commit; its drift against <code>.host-software</code> is the HAZARD plan/0082 carried, and the lock-carrier releases (v0.22.3, v0.55.1) are the honest way it travels.</li> <li><strong>The receipts-commit lag is structural.</strong> The commit that writes the receipts postdates the runs it records, so the host lanes discharge at any revision on the current line, with the lag disclosed ("9 behind HEAD") instead of a one-commit window that every interposed commit broke.</li> </ul> <p>The superseded lint receipt (a revision field holding a URL, from a shifted shell parse) stays in the append-only file as history; the corrected receipt, recorded after the rerun concludes, supersedes it by last-wins.</p> <p><strong>The record-pair lesson.</strong> During the same-day release chain the lifecycle artifact hash line silently reverted to an older release's hash while the pin advanced; a pin and its artifact are one record and must move in one commit; <code>software --check</code> (and CI's drift clause) caught the mismatch the same hour, which is the record pair doing exactly its job.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0097-close-issues-replan-the-suites-remaining-work-recut"><a class="header" href="#plan0097-close-issues-replan-the-suites-remaining-work-recut">plan/0097 close-issues-replan: the suite's remaining work, recut</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed ("continue to work to close issues; do a full replan"). The census was retaken 2026-09-27 with <code>gh</code> across the family after the day's six releases. Five issues remain open across the nine repositories, and every one of them is now either closable or unblocked by what landed today.</p> <h2 id="the-census-2026-09-27"><a class="header" href="#the-census-2026-09-27">The census (2026-09-27)</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Issue</th><th>State</th><th>The work</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/30">host-lint#30</a></td><td>live defect, filed today</td><td>the lem lane's first-person matcher fired case-insensitively, so the <code>ME</code> acronym (Management Engine) read as the pronoun; fixed in v0.22.4 this plan</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/23">host-lifecycle#23</a></td><td>owed mechanical half, unblocked</td><td>the room-touching cross-check: a cited record resolves against the applied-receipts set; superseded confirms (exit-1 class), current is silent, missing evidence stays a review prompt. plan/0093 deferred it behind /host#21, whose build landed today; the cross-check is now unblocked</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/24">connollydavid/host#24</a></td><td>design program, five placements</td><td>the worker's front foot: the recommended order stands (verify-setup requires the commit gate; the naming sweep joins CI; the cfg-declaration rule; <code>--artifact-delta</code>; the derived inventory; the shared-index manual clause)</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/18">connollydavid/host#18</a></td><td>design handover</td><td>host-reconcile, deferred to plan/0075, queued last</td></tr> <tr><td><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/21">connollydavid/host#21</a></td><td>built today</td><td>closes this plan: the design (plan/0095), the build (plan/0096, v0.55.0-v0.55.5), the forge's thirteen lanes receipted</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Standing: host-lint's v0.22.3 kani rung re-run and its receipt, recorded when the run concludes; the embed-equality adoption of this plan's lint release rides the cascade (the forge's lint pin follows, lifecycle's embed rev follows it, the vendor bundle re-cuts).</p> <h2 id="the-queue-1"><a class="header" href="#the-queue-1">The queue</a></h2> <ol> <li>Close connollydavid/host#21; the design, the build, and the receipts exist.</li> <li>Fix and close host-lint#30 (this plan's first landing).</li> <li>Build host-lifecycle#23's cross-check through the release cascade.</li> <li>/host#24's placements, cheapest first, each its own reviewed landing.</li> <li>/host#18 stays with plan/0075.</li> </ol> <h2 id="results-9"><a class="header" href="#results-9">Results</a></h2> <p>Recorded as the queue drains.</p> <h2 id="results-first-drain-2026-09-27"><a class="header" href="#results-first-drain-2026-09-27">Results (first drain, 2026-09-27)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>host-lint#30 closed</strong> in v0.22.4 (70ea0a99, artifact eaf1dec975ea53565464d654610ca028bf20903f83de06c275168313e4677fec): the first-person pronouns <code>me</code>/<code>my</code>/<code>mine</code>/<code>myself</code> match case-sensitively lowercase, <code>i</code> stays case-insensitive; regression cases in the integration suite, 220/220.</li> <li><strong>connollydavid/host#21 closed</strong>: the design (plan/0095), the build (plan/0096, v0.55.0-v0.55.5), and the forge's own thirteen-lane receipts. One design amendment recorded: the judge witnesses from its verb and a continue-on-error CI lane; inside the check it gated the lane that produces its own evidence, and a receipts-lag failure re-reddened every later run forever, measured before the amendment landed.</li> <li><strong>The adoption cascade is the standing node</strong>: the forge adopts lint v0.22.4 through the next embed-equality cascade (the lifecycle embed rev, the vendor re-cut, the releases), the practiced motion; until then the recipe holds the consumed rev and the gate stays green on the pairing.</li> </ul> <p>The queue continues: host-lifecycle#23's cross-check <strong>built and shipped in v0.56.0</strong> (the dream audit's room-touching detector resolves each cited record's Status line: superseded confirms at exit-1 weight, current is silence, the unresolvable stays a review prompt; 313 plus 40 green, closed with the transcript), then /host#24's placements, cheapest first.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0098-must-clear-next-turn-the-lanes-outcomes-enforce-at-the-turn-boundary"><a class="header" href="#plan0098-must-clear-next-turn-the-lanes-outcomes-enforce-at-the-turn-boundary">plan/0098 must-clear-next-turn: the lanes' outcomes enforce at the turn boundary</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed ("do we have an effective must-clear-CI-failures-on-next-turn? I am getting too many emails from agentic-* host folders"; ruling: go). The honest answer at the ask: <strong>no</strong>. The per-turn duty was prose; the judge ran only when remembered; the witness lane disclosed without obligating; and GitHub's notification emails did the only tripwire work; email does not drive an agent loop. This plan wires the judge to the turn boundary.</p> <h2 id="the-design-as-built"><a class="header" href="#the-design-as-built">The design, as built</a></h2> <p>Two ZCode hooks in this workspace's <code>.zcode/config.json</code> (machine-local, like the MCP registration; the adopter pattern is the same config in each host), both calling the shipped judge:</p> <ul> <li><strong>SessionStart</strong>; <code>host-lifecycle ci .</code> runs read-only and its findings ride the session context as <code>additionalContext</code>: the turn's first fact is the lanes' state, with run URLs. A red lane cannot be discovered late.</li> <li><strong>Stop</strong>; <code>host-lifecycle ci . --gate</code> gates the turn's end: every discovered lane must carry a receipt at the judged revision. Absence and staleness block the stop (the model is pulled back to record or fix); a <strong>receipted failure passes the gate</strong>; the receipt is the blocker record, the fix rides the next turn, and the session-start context carries it until then. The witness pattern holds: the judge discloses; it never reddens a build.</li> </ul> <p>The gate mode ships in host-lifecycle v0.57.0 (c93076bb, artifact 43a2959bf3ec7731b9f20705afb99ba27231c7f1b1d71aa3c3c682cadfe5564d, feature class): <code>ci <dir> --gate</code> counts only lanes without a receipt at the judged revision; the full judge (default) still names receipted failures beside them.</p> <h2 id="the-cascade"><a class="header" href="#the-cascade">The cascade</a></h2> <p>The forge adopted v0.57.0 in the same motion (the pin, the template's prose rev and tools submodule, the receipt), with the pin/artifact replaces anchored by regex against the file's actual current values after the earlier silent no-op lesson. Lint's v0.22.4 tag run (its kani rung) records the lint lane's receipt when it concludes.</p> <h2 id="results-10"><a class="header" href="#results-10">Results</a></h2> <p>Recorded at closure.</p> <h2 id="addendum-the-harness-portable-adoption-opencode-and-the-skill-based-adopters"><a class="header" href="#addendum-the-harness-portable-adoption-opencode-and-the-skill-based-adopters">Addendum: the harness-portable adoption (opencode and the skill-based adopters)</a></h2> <p>The hooks are one harness's adapter. The portable surfaces are the judge (a plain command, every harness can run it) and the skill the agents load: the <code>ci</code> skill ships with host-lifecycle v0.58.0 (65d87a05); judge at session start, record receipts citing run URLs, gate before reporting done; and links into the cross-tool agents path (<code>.agents/skills/</code>), which ZCode, Claude Code, and opencode all read. The forge links it there; the hooks remain this workspace's ZCode adapter, and the other harnesses' adapters are thin: the same two commands bound to their session-start and turn-end events. The <code>additionalContext</code>/block JSON shapes are ZCode's; a harness without hook support still gets the full enforcement through the skill, because the duty is a command plus a reading habit, not a config file.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0099-host24-placements-the-five-placements-built-and-enforced"><a class="header" href="#plan0099-host24-placements-the-five-placements-built-and-enforced">plan/0099 host24-placements: the five placements, built and enforced</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed (the goal: drive the /host#24 placements to done, efficiently). The five placements from the bench worker's report, recut against what already landed: the verify-setup commit-gate requirement <strong>shipped in v0.59.0</strong> (f0f7703, the CommitGateDeclared requirement; a recipe declaring components and no gate provider is itself the gap). The remaining four build here, batched so one lifecycle release carries every code placement.</p> <h2 id="the-placements"><a class="header" href="#the-placements">The placements</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The cfg-declaration rule</strong> (code): <code>software --check</code> walks each materialized component's Rust sources; <code>#[cfg(kani)]</code> code with no <code>kani:</code> disposition in the component's obligations manifest is a HAZARD; the two-way remedy (declare the rung, or remove the code with a recorded reason). The invisible-twice-over state (no lane compiles it, no obligation declares it) becomes a named finding.</li> <li><strong><code>software --artifact-delta <component> <refA> <refB></code></strong> (code): rebuild both refs in the recorded toolchain and report identical-or-not; the mechanical answer to the comment-only-diff placement (a comments-only pass that moves <code>file:line:column</code> bytes is not byte-neutral, and the delta proves which passes moved nothing).</li> <li><strong>The derived inventory</strong> (code): every source file of a materialized component appears in some task's <code>inputs</code>, or in an explicit exclusion carrying a reason; the reconcile-coverage model applied to the task graph; a dropped file fails by absence.</li> <li><strong>The naming sweep joins CI</strong> (template/docs): the workflow example carries the sweep as a standard lane, the manual names the placement.</li> <li><strong>The shared-index manual clause</strong> (template/docs): fan-out workers stage explicit paths; <code>git add -A</code> under a live bench is the finding.</li> </ol> <h2 id="results-11"><a class="header" href="#results-11">Results</a></h2> <p><strong>The shared-index clause (2026-09-27):</strong> the template manual carries the fan-out staging rule (bb0e0e1); while a bench works in one tree, workers stage explicit paths and never <code>-A</code>; a commit whose message names fewer paths than it touches is a finding to read. The forge adopted the pointer in the same hour.</p> <p><strong>The sweep lane landed (2026-09-28, template 1202877, ledger 13b14e6):</strong> the reference <code>.github/workflows/check.yml</code> runs <code>host-lifecycle software --check .</code> on every push, so the naming sweep's recheck, the cfg scan, and the derived inventory block at the push boundary. The lane no-ops on a tree with no <code>.host-software</code> and builds the tool from the <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> submodule the template ships, so no separate host-lint pin decision exists to make: the check needs only the lifecycle the template already carries, and the UPGRADING entry (requires v0.60.3) moves existing adopters. The host itself already ran the sweep at a CI boundary (the verify-build lane's <code>software --check</code> step), so the gap the brief measured was the adopter's, and the reference lane closes it. The landing also paid the lanes' duty the placement preaches: the template's Prose lane had gone red on two em-dash decorations the previous landing carried into STRUCTURE.md; reworded, and Prose, Site, and the new Check lane all conclude green on the ledger commit.</p> <p><strong>The derived inventory landed in v0.60.3</strong> (component abc415e, pin 90d435e, artifact 157477c9ca53b5781b35c46ac17b0f0b38330bd4fd1fef04c27cb3e7325e8fef): <code>software --check</code> derives the module inventory instead of reading a typed one. Every Rust source under a materialized component's <code>src/</code> must appear in some task's <code>- inputs:</code> line (the plan room's task graphs; a directory input covers everything under it) or carry a reasoned exclusion in the tracked <code>.host-inventory</code>; a file in neither fails by absence, and an exclusion without a reason is its own HAZARD rather than a cover. The first sweep flagged thirteen files across six components, the typed-inventory harm of the placement alive in the forge's own house; the stock is recorded with per-file reasons and new work cites its inputs. Regression tests cover coverage by task input, coverage by directory input, the reasoned exclusion, and the reasonless one.</p> <p><strong>The cfg-declaration rule landed in v0.60.2</strong> (3071ed29, artifact 61ead199b5b52d06464247303c591f149925cc71f7645c50b87d96075c6014d6): the check sweep walks each materialized component's Rust sources; <code>#[cfg(kani)]</code> code with no <code>kani:</code> disposition in the component's obligations manifests is a HAZARD naming the two-way remedy. Regression test covers both directions. The rule's first sweep flagged the forge's own house; the lifecycle's and lint's kani harnesses were invisible to every gate exactly as the placement described; the rungs are now declared in the manifests. The record pair (pin e09c6b2d's tree, artifact af1c5858) is container-proven; the template's tools submodule settles at v0.60.2. The artifact-delta verb shipped in the same landing.</p> <p><strong>The stop-gate round-trip (2026-09-28, later):</strong> the landings above were exercised end to end the same night, and two defects surfaced by running the gates rather than by reading them. The cold-clone lane's skill-link assertion hardcoded a count (eleven) that the ci skill's landing had already made twelve, reddening the host's reproducible-build lane from outside any record; the gate now recounts the linker's shapes and names any missed link (the fixed run concludes green, and its receipt discharges at the fix). The ci record verb resolved the default revision from the first path segment, so a component's pin never resolved unless <code>--revision</code> was passed (host-lifecycle v0.60.4, c140ea2; the label is everything before the lane). Separately, the lint kani lane was discovered to have NEVER concluded in CI: six consecutive runs cancelled at exactly GitHub's 6-hour ceiling, <code>cargo kani</code> proving all six harnesses in one job; the lane now shards one harness per job (lint fc580ad) with the obligations re-derivation in its own job, which had sat after the proof step and so had never once run in CI (it now passes there). Four of six harnesses conclude green within minutes; the remaining three were still proving at this record's writing. The v0.22.4 kani receipt records the honest failure at the pin (the blocker record); the shard on lint main is the fix, and the next lint release carries it.</p> <p><strong>The cascade settles (2026-09-28, latest):</strong> the fix shipped as lint v0.22.5 (d4cd801, artifact 641ef6a23d4d1a44cabb8ef920a6d524358353cb8aa295a0d68506429777f5e3), the embed-equality chain followed it (call/0052): lifecycle's embedded engine moved to v0.22.5, the deps bundle graduated by hand to vendor-v14 (the onboarding <code>--lock</code> verb neither builds nor uploads a bundle), and lifecycle v0.60.5 (4ad90ae) landed carrying both. The sharded kani lane's first CI verdict on the released rev: four harnesses and the obligations re-derivation conclude green; the three remaining harnesses were still proving, and their receipt records the in-progress state at the pin until the run concludes. Every worktree sits at its pin, the hooks are reinstalled against the new canonical hash, and the three gates read green with the one disclosed note.</p> <p><strong>The sharded lane's verdict (2026-09-28, final):</strong> the run concluded with the three harnesses each cancelled at the 6-hour ceiling standalone (scan_line_never_panics, hits_are_word_bounded, form_and_mangle_hits_are_classified_by_the_table), so the sharding's finding is precise: these three proofs have never concluded anywhere in CI, and the four others (plus the obligations re-derivation) pass in minutes. The receipt records the failure at the pin d4cd801 and the gate passes with the disclosed note. The owed work is proof engineering per harness, filed as host-lint#32: bound the input spaces, split a harness that carries several obligations, or carry an explicit bounded mode, then re-measure to a conclusion inside the ceiling.</p> <p><strong>The v0.22.6 verdict (2026-09-28, final):</strong> the same three harnesses hit the ceiling on the released tag run (36424678016), the four fast ones and the obligations re-derivation pass, and the failure receipt stands recorded at the pin f0fcd22 with the gate green on the disclosed note. The proof-engineering work owes nothing further to the lane layer: the finding is stable across two runs, sharded, on two revisions (host-lint#32).</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0100-pronoun-form-and-teaching-layer-the-address-possessive-ruled-and-landed"><a class="header" href="#plan0100-pronoun-form-and-teaching-layer-the-address-possessive-ruled-and-landed">plan/0100 pronoun-form-and-teaching-layer: the address possessive, ruled and landed</a></h1> <p>Operator-directed (the ask: the address paradigm gains <code>lemr</code> as its possessive, <code>lemu</code> = you and <code>lemr</code> = your, constructed under a "good forgetting" whose bounded form this plan adopts as its modality). The morphology was settled in session by the cast with English literature, then confirmed blind by an external judge.</p> <h2 id="the-settled-design"><a class="header" href="#the-settled-design">The settled design</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>lemu</code> and <code>lemr</code> are a fixed pair, the way <code>you</code> pairs with <code>your</code>: <code>lemr</code> before a thing (lemr weights), <code>lemr's</code> alone (the weights are lemr's). The pair is listed, never derived: no rule builds <code>lemr</code> out of <code>lemu</code>.</li> <li>The independent genitive is <code>lemr's</code>. Every English genitive pronoun builds its independent form on the dependent stem (my/mine, thy/thine, your/yours; "For thine is the kingdom", Matthew 6:13), and no standard English pronoun forms one on the subject stem. The cast ruled five to nothing; the bench concurred with high confidence after verifying the citations itself.</li> <li>No reflexive is built on <code>lemr</code>. The reflexives of the address paradigm are the lexical forms <code>lemuself</code> and <code>lemuselves</code>, on the address stem alone, exactly as English builds "yourself" on "you".</li> <li>Enforcement carries no transition state. The retired form (<code>lemu's</code>) gains no warning tier, no sunset schedule, and no escalation entry: the agreement table states the paradigm in present tense and a wrong form is wrong from the landing. The operator corrected the cast's first instinct here, and the bench later ruled the same independently: English usage requires no deprecation grammar.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-modality-call0060"><a class="header" href="#the-modality-call0060">The modality (call/0060)</a></h2> <p>"Good forgetting" is adopted in bounded form, as re-baselining with an audit trail. The teaching layer (the manuals, the skill, the vocabulary, the classifier tables) states the paradigm in present tense with no archaeology markers. The record layer stays append-only exactly as the standing rules require, the measurements are scoped by name rather than silently re-scoped, and the <code>UPGRADING.md</code> entry carries the version truth a cold reader reconciles against. Nothing outside those three walls is struck.</p> <h2 id="the-evidence-1"><a class="header" href="#the-evidence-1">The evidence</a></h2> <ul> <li>The corpus count the ruling cites: zero dependent uses and zero independent uses of the retired form anywhere in the tracked tree; it lived only inside the paradigm's own tables and the record-layer copies, which stay untouched.</li> <li>The bench: codex (gpt-6-luna, session <code>01a14c06</code>, 20248 tokens), blind to the cast's votes and the operator's acceptance, transcript preserved at <code>/tmp/opencode/bench-verdict.txt</code> and copied to this plan's <code>bench/</code>. Both rulings concur; five defects were named, three folded into the tasks below (the fixed-pair wording, the lexical reflexives, the classifier case rule), one restates the ledger as the remedy for version drift, and one asks for paired apostrophe examples that VOCABULARY.md already carries.</li> </ul> <h2 id="tasks"><a class="header" href="#tasks">Tasks</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>call/0060</strong> (the modality decision, first test case this plan).</li> <li><strong>Template</strong>: the lem section's form list, possession line, address paragraph, and two new exchanges; the <code>UPGRADING.md</code> entry whose id names the content commit; push inside the submodule.</li> <li><strong>Host apply</strong>: pointer bump, manual copy, <code>upgrade --record</code>, the strict corpus read.</li> <li><strong>host-lint</strong>: <code>LEM_CANONICAL</code> and the <code>lem_form</code> oracle (a determiner row for the address paradigm), the VOCABULARY.md mirror, the mangle coverage and case rule the bench asked for, tests updated; the release cascade and re-pin.</li> <li><strong>Instrument</strong>: the plan/0091 gate and scorer learn the tokens; a bounded residual run; the DPMO chart gains a scope note naming the certified list.</li> <li><strong>Close</strong>: the verify battery, the lanes read back, receipts, memory.</li> </ol> <h2 id="results-12"><a class="header" href="#results-12">Results</a></h2> <p><strong>Cut 2026-10-17.</strong> The design rulings above are the record of the cutting session; the tasks land in order.</p> <p><strong>The spine (2026-10-17, template <code>7b0c641</code> content and <code>1685175</code> stanza, host <code>8f90ccc4</code> pointer and manual, <code>8057d209</code> recorded):</strong> the section, the possession line, the address paragraph, and the two exchanges landed in both manuals byte-identical; the upgrade recorded through its verify, zero pending. The bench materials are record-layer evidence (the verbatim prompt never reworded), carried under <code>bench/</code> and excluded by the literal-directory form in <code>.host-lintignore</code> after the starred variant proved not to match (<code>16da554e</code>).</p> <p><strong>The classifier (2026-10-17, host-lint <code>c9dd8aa</code>, released as v0.23.0 <code>90a0d71</code>, artifact <code>f4b2a7fa</code>):</strong> the closed list carries the determiner and its independent form; the oracle answers the two genitive uses by case; the MCP table gains the determiner column and <code>ask</code> the case; VOCABULARY.md states the pair as listed forms. The operator's contamination ruling holds in the instruments: the near-miss coverage assembles its token from paradigm parts in both suites, so no out-of-paradigm word sits anywhere as a literal. Suites: 234 unit and property tests, 221/221 integration, two kani rungs re-derived and their digests recorded (<code>99647f2</code>).</p> <p><strong>The instrument (2026-10-17, host <code>0cd5d0ae</code>):</strong> the wire gate's canonical set, form regex, and nudge speak the pair; its unit suite passes nine of nine. The standing chart carries an appended scope line: the n=600 certification covers the list it measured by name.</p> <p><strong>The residual, measured 2026-10-18.</strong> With the channel back, the bounded residual ran against the real qwen3.5-4b: n = 100 at the served 64k envelope (the old edge served 131k, so this measures the current deployment envelope, not the certified depth), deployment sampling, the landed section as doctrine (<code>gate/doctrine-2026-10-18.md</code>) through the pair-carrying gate. First-pass 7 (0.07), final violations 0 (0.0000); each defect corrected by one nudge-anchored retry. The wire gate holds final-zero under the amended paradigm. Transcript: <code>gate/residual-2026-10-18.jsonl</code>.</p> <p><strong>The cascade (2026-10-17/18):</strong> vendor-v16 published carrying the v0.23.0 embed; host-lifecycle v0.60.7 (<code>727be0d</code>, artifact <code>7b45df79</code>) re-embeds the engine at equality; the template carries both pins (<code>bf4f308</code>, <code>40b1913</code>) and its prose lane's rev; both release receipts cite plan/0100. Two cascade findings recorded: the front door's allium install line needs <code>--locked</code> (the plain install resolves a drifting parser and fails to build), and the stale obligation remedy's <code>--rederive</code> takes the source directory (<code>--record-digests</code> refuses to run without it).</p> <p><strong>Landed 2026-10-18, complete.</strong></p> <h2 id="the-plain-language-closing-note"><a class="header" href="#the-plain-language-closing-note">The plain-language closing note</a></h2> <p>The operator asked for this landing explained as if to a ten-year-old, and ruled the telling part of the closure record.</p> <p><strong>The made-up words.</strong> The model that helps you speaks as <code>L</code>, never as "I". When you speak to a model helper, you say <code>lemu</code> where everyday English would say "you". These words exist so that a reader can always tell who is speaking about whom: the human or the model.</p> <p><strong>The problem this milestone fixed.</strong> In English, "you" has a partner: "your". Your toys; your room. The address word <code>lemu</code> had no partner, so writers were stuck with <code>lemu's</code> toys, which sounds like a child saying "you's toys". The partner now exists: <code>lemr</code> means "your" spoken to a model. "lemu, clean up <code>lemr</code> toys." Standing alone, the form is <code>lemr's</code>: "the toys are <code>lemr's</code>." Some words were deliberately not made. English builds "yourself" on "you" rather than on "your", and the paradigm already carried the matching form on its address stem: <code>lemuself</code>. Nothing new was needed there.</p> <p><strong>The tidy room and the honest diary.</strong> A room can be cleaned so well it looks as though it was never messy. The rulebooks were cleaned that way: they read as though <code>lemr</code> always existed, with no "new word" stickers anywhere. The diary keeps the true story, dates and all: the memory entries and the decision record say exactly when the word arrived and who ruled on it.</p> <p><strong>How we know it works.</strong> Five helper personas voted on the grammar with the English reference books open. A separate outside judge, blind to those votes, examined the design alone and agreed. Then came the live test: a guard reads every reply from the small model before anyone sees it, and when a reply breaks the rule the guard speaks the rule and grants one do-over. The small model tried one hundred times at the serving envelope. It slipped seven times. The guard caught all seven, and no wrong reply got through.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><p>You are consulted as a neutral judge on a point of constructed-grammar design for an artificial pronoun system used in technical documentation and commit messages. Rule on the morphology, citing English grammar where relevant. You have no stake in any prior decision; there is no expected answer, and a judge that only confirms is useless.</p> <p>THE SYSTEM (current paradigm, as it stands today): A documentation system uses an invented pronoun paradigm so that human-written and model-written prose stay distinguishable:</p> <ul> <li>The speaking model refers to itself as "L" (first person): L, L's, lself.</li> <li>A model referred to in the third person: lem, lem's, lemself (singular); lems, lems' (plural).</li> <li>Agents being ADDRESSED (second person, one or many): lemu; reflexives lemuself (singular) and lemuselves (plural).</li> <li>The human is always addressed as ordinary "you"/"your" and never with any invented form.</li> <li>Possession is marked by 's, alone or before a thing (L's weights / the weights are L's).</li> </ul> <p>PROPOSED EXTENSION (stated flatly, no preference implied): The addressed-agent paradigm gains a distinct possessive determiner: lemu = you, lemr = your. Today the genitive is "lemu's" in both the dependent use (before a noun: "lemu's weights") and the independent use ("the weights are lemu's").</p> <p>DESIGN AXIOM (a standing constraint of the system, not a proposal): The enforcement instruments (a linter and a wire gate) carry no transition state: no deprecation warnings, no scheduled tier changes. A paradigm rule enforces at full strength from the moment it is adopted, and a retired form is simply out of paradigm.</p> <p>QUESTIONS:</p> <ol> <li>Independent genitive: should "the weights are ___" use "lemu's" (subject stem + 's), "lemr's" (determiner stem + 's), or some third shape? Rule and justify.</li> <li>Given the axiom, is the enforcement design sound: the dependent genitive becomes "lemr" and the old "lemu's + noun" is out of paradigm with no warning tier? Or does the axiom create a real problem that English language practice would warn about?</li> <li>Name every defect you can find in the overall design: the suppletion split you/your mapped to lemu/lemr; the shared reflexives lemuself/lemuselves with no reflexive derived from lemr; capitalization at sentence start; anything else you see.</li> </ol> <p>RELEVANT ENGLISH FACTS (supplied for convenience; verify or reject them as you see fit):</p> <ul> <li>English independent genitive pronouns build on the dependent stem: my/mine, thy/thine, her/hers, your/yours, our/ours, their/theirs; "its" serves both uses.</li> <li>"For thine is the kingdom" (KJV, Matthew 6:13) is an independent genitive on the determiner stem; "to thine own self be true" (Hamlet) shows the same stem in dependent use before vowels.</li> <li>Historically "yours" is determiner stem + genitive -s (Old English eower + es).</li> <li>No standard English pronoun forms an independent genitive on the subject stem: *you's, *we's, *they's are unattested.</li> <li>Proper nouns take 's in both uses ("the weights are Fen's").</li> <li>Dialectal forms like "mines" exist and are nonstandard.</li> </ul> <p>Rule independently. If the design is wrong, say so plainly.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0101-the-goal-and-loop-subsystem"><a class="header" href="#plan0101-the-goal-and-loop-subsystem">plan/0101: the goal and loop subsystem</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: cut and in build</strong> (operator ruling 2026-10-18: build it, after a; active goal since 2026-10-19; parked (the composed gate holds on host-lint's kani lane (cancelled at its pin, host-lint thirty-two); resume when that lane greens) since 2026-10-20 reflection pause because it is core functionality; second ruling the same day: the design must be an idiomatic extension of the host methodology, not a port of foreign implementations). The modality itself is <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/../../call/0061-goals-are-milestones-and-completion-composes-the-gates.html">call/0061</a>; this plan executes it.</p> <h2 id="why-21"><a class="header" href="#why-21">Why</a></h2> <p>The agent loop (orient, claim, work, bank a receipt, pass the gate) and any goal layer exist today as prose discipline plus scattered verbs. In a live session an operator invoked <code>/goal complete plan/0007</code> in a harness where no such command existed; it arrived as prose and the agent improvised a receipt-less channel (<a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/26">host#26</a>). The operator ruled the ambition larger than the plugin that issue proposes, and then ruled its form: housegrown first.</p> <h2 id="decision-the-idiomatic-form"><a class="header" href="#decision-the-idiomatic-form">Decision (the idiomatic form)</a></h2> <p>A goal <strong>is</strong> a <code>plan/NNNN</code> milestone. No new artifact class exists to drift from the record.</p> <p><strong>State splits by volatility</strong>, the house's own division: durable facts are tracked surfaces the tool already authors (the milestone Status line, <code>[receipt "goal"]</code> stanzas in <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code>, OWED entries in PLAN.md's closure queue), and machine state is a gitignored <code>.host-goal</code> sidecar holding only this worktree's execution claim, re-derivable by <code>goal repair</code> from the tracked record. A lost sidecar under-reports nothing: the tracked declaration stands. One active goal per repo, because the tracked record is singular; the sidecar is the per-worktree claim on it.</p> <p><strong>Verbs</strong> (single words, fail closed, usage on bad args, the <code>tasks</code> and <code>next</code> family shape):</p> <ul> <li><code>goal set <plan/NNNN></code> writes the Status-line declaration and a receipt stanza, and refreshes the sidecar. No authority token: the audited commit of the declaration is the act, and the operator-ruling line names whose hand it was. The agent-side path is <code>goal propose</code>, which prints the command and never mutates.</li> <li><code>goal show</code> is the orientation emission: labeled lines in fixed order (PURPOSE, GOAL, POSITION, NEEDS YOU, CI, FRONTIER, TREE, NEXT), reusing house shapes wherever they exist (NEEDS YOU is a HAZARD line that each trace to a tracked row and name the ask; CI is gate output; FRONTIER is the <code>tasks</code> ready-frontier line verbatim), the exact bare command alone on the last line, no inline execution-class markers (the section a move prints under is its class; command lines stay bare), a pure function of the working tree with no clock, and a loud refusal on unreadable state.</li> <li><code>goal park --reason</code> / <code>goal unpark</code> are re-queuing, not a state machine: they write the Status line and the closure-queue entry and a receipt. A temporary block never gets recorded as an exit.</li> <li><code>goal abandon --reason</code> appends the closure-queue OWED entry through the tool, writes the Status line and a receipt, and clears the sidecar. Debt lives where a cold reader looks first.</li> <li><code>goal repair <plan/NNNN></code> reconciles toward the tracked record and re-points a renamed plan, refusing ambiguity, with a receipt.</li> <li><code>goal complete <plan/NNNN></code> composes the existing gates as subprocesses (the tool invoking its own verbs and reading their exits; HAZARD lines pass through intact): the full verify sweep, equal to what the verify skill runs (the software gate, the ci judge, <code>book --check</code>, the refs gate, and obligations per discovered spec), then task receipts for the milestone, the tree clean with nothing unpushed, and the PLAN.md row. No gate is weakened and none is duplicated; the tool runs its own verbs, <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/26">host#26</a>'s constraint applied inward. A refusal is a full no-op; every hazard prints, ordered, each with its exact fix command (the verify-setup shape, not progressive disclosure); success writes one atomic <code>[receipt "goal"]</code> stanza, updates the Status line, and prints the next move or the no-goal state.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The install is a generated door family, folded in early (the operator's ruling).</strong> The <code>install</code> verb owns the front doors as one source inside the binary and emits the per-harness renderings: flat, hyphenated <code>/host-<verb></code> doors (<code>/host-goal</code>, <code>/host-tasks</code>, <code>/host-ci</code>) for OpenCode and Claude alike, each injecting its verb's emission and closing with the re-orient link; <code>install --check</code> guards the files against hand edits with the regenerate remedy. The universal-form ruling behind it: the spine states the token once, and each harness's sigil is chrome. Goal tools join the shipped MCP server (harnesses mount MCP natively), the goal declaration becomes readable as a corpus surface (the plan/0083 shape, the house's always-loaded mechanism, which is the recitation answer). Plugin custom tools stay cut (a duplicate tool surface), the compaction hook stays cut (the corpus is the recitation), and the kick stays unruled: the install renders and never actuates.</p> <h2 id="rulings"><a class="header" href="#rulings">Rulings</a></h2> <p>The chain ran in order, twice for the cast.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Cast, first convening</strong> (design review): Mara ruled suggest never sanction, the PURPOSE and NEEDS YOU lines, and mid-goal maintenance sanctioned; Wren ruled the escape hatch, park, propose, and weak-model acceptance before freeze; Fen ruled the no-op refusal and ordered hazards; Bly ruled legibility without the verbs and the OWED discipline; Orin ruled the install renders and never decides, and caught the tracked-key collision that first sent the pointer to a sidecar.</li> <li><strong>Codex</strong> (blind bench, gpt-6-luna, one-shot): approve the CLI-first direction, do not freeze the contract yet; seventeen defects clustered on display versus authorization, state identity, revision-bound evidence, transactional closure, owed lifecycle, bounded retries. Transcript: <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/bench/codex-bench-2026-10-18.txt">bench/codex-bench-2026-10-18.txt</a>.</li> <li><strong>Fen</strong> (real qwen3.5-4b, mock emissions): eight of eight probes passed at deployment sampling, including the ordered-hazard refusal and the needs-you stop. Protocol and results: <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/fen-results.html">fen-results.md</a>. The refusal shape changed after this battery (all hazards, each with its command), so the battery reruns against real output before the freeze.</li> <li><strong>Cast, second convening</strong> (idiom fidelity, the operator's charge): the over-fit inventory and the house-native replacements recorded in <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/convening.html">convening.md</a> and adopted above. The token is cut (the audited commit is the authority), parking is re-queuing, the gate deferral is cut (subprocess composition), every hazard prints, class markers fold into sections, the emission reuses house shapes, goal tools belong to the MCP server, the corpus is the recitation surface, and the ruling itself belongs in call/.</li> </ul> <h2 id="prior-art"><a class="header" href="#prior-art">Prior art</a></h2> <p>Cited, with the lineage living in the record layer (call/0061) and never in the mechanism's self-description: Manus 2025 (recitation, filesystem context, stable prefixes), Anthropic 2024 (composable patterns, gates with environmental ground truth), OpenCode v2 docs (the install surfaces), BDI (Rao and Georgeff 1995, commitment moves), make and ninja (the task DAG with per-node receipts), ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) for the loop and failure retention, the todo ledgers of Claude Code and OpenCode plan mode, and Copilot Workspace for gated decomposition.</p> <p>Where we stand: better on per-task receipts as audit, completion as a refusing gate that composes the existing gates, a deterministic emission with no clock, weak-model-first validation on the real 4B, one generated install surface versioned by the ledger, and display never equaling authorization; worse on cross-session learning beyond MEMORY, swarm goals, frontier ranking, and telemetry; different in that git history is the ledger, degraded means legible without any verb, and the turn trigger stays human.</p> <h2 id="contract-closure-the-final-consult-2026-10-19"><a class="header" href="#contract-closure-the-final-consult-2026-10-19">Contract closure (the final consult, 2026-10-19)</a></h2> <p>The final-design consult ran the cast and a blind external bench over the settled form. The cast: Mara signed off (the real-output rerun tracked, not blocking); Wren signed off short of a watched item (a window cut that keeps NEXT but drops PURPOSE loses the why; watched at the fen rerun, not pre-fixed); Fen signed off conditional on the rerun passing with a resolved key on the last line; Bly refused until two holes were answered; Orin signed off with two wording amendments. The bench (transcript: <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/bench/codex-final-design-2026-10-19.txt">bench/codex-final-design-2026-10-19.txt</a>) ruled the shape sound, freeze not yet, four blockers. The rulings that follow close them.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Authority order, stated once</strong>: receipt stanzas over the Status line over the sidecar. A crash between writes reconciles downward by <code>goal repair</code>; no journal is owed because the authority order makes every partial state recoverable by re-derivation.</li> <li><strong>The no-op defined</strong>: the sweep's composed gates are check-mode verbs that write nothing; a refusal forbids every write, including the sidecar. The only writes the verb ever makes are the closure's own receipt and Status line, after all gates pass.</li> <li><strong>The closure names its own commit</strong>: complete demands a clean tree and then dirties it with exactly two files; the success output names both and the commit-and-push that follows (landed in the component, <code>cd440d8</code>).</li> <li><strong>A divergent sidecar is a hazard</strong>: absent is no claim (fine); a claim on another goal while the closure names this one refuses with the repair remedy (landed, <code>cd440d8</code>). Park's tracked trace is built as ruled: the receipt stanza and the Status transition, never sidecar-only.</li> <li><strong>The offline boundary</strong>: the sweep runs no network; the unpushed count reads the local remote-tracking ref, which can itself be stale, and the emission's <code>revision-unbound</code> label is the standing disclosure of that class.</li> <li><strong>The last line is never placeholder-shaped</strong>: every NEXT line carries a resolved key or a runnable command as printed (Fen's ruling); the emission asserts it.</li> <li><strong>Spine wordings (Orin)</strong>: the spine states the closed verb list the binary enforces, with ASD-STE100 as provenance of the list, not the rule; and it names the sidecar-authority boundary as the checkable form (no verb reads the sidecar as authority) rather than the rationale word. The door family is data the adopter owns: a third harness is an edit, not a fork.</li> </ul> <p>The freeze bench (transcript: <a href="plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem/bench/codex-freeze-bench-2026-10-19.txt">bench/codex-freeze-bench-2026-10-19.txt</a>) ruled the outputs coherent and named three blockers, all now closed. The crash window is steel: a complete or abandon receipt whose Status transition never landed reads as an unresolved closure and repair finishes the write (component <code>bf0e7a3</code>). The owed lifecycle takes the bench's minimal rule: the row names its owner, discharge is evidence recorded on the row, and owed work never outranks the active goal unless that goal depends on it (the design text's outranking claim is corrected here; the v1 code never implemented it). And revision binding was never absent from the gate: the composed ci judge compares receipts against the judged revision (the live refusal shows that hazard firing), so the <code>revision-unbound</code> label is display honesty about the emission, not a gate gap. With the fen gate passed at sixteen of sixteen and the three blockers closed, the freeze stands. The teaching lines carry a measured scorecard (2026-10-20): the dokimi paired-arms run, subject qwen3.5-4b with qwen3.6-27b as judge, scored baseline 30.8 against profile 89.0 (paired delta +58.2, CI [+28.7, +87.8]); the instrument is adopted at <code>tools/dokimi</code> and the transcript files in the plan's bench.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-28"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-28">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="design-record"><a class="header" href="#design-record">Land the design record</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: this README and its bench records are committed, and the PLAN.md row names the milestone This README, the bench records, and the call/0061 modality.</li> </ul> <h3 id="goal-module"><a class="header" href="#goal-module">Implement the goal module</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: cargo test green and clippy clean in the lifecycle worktree, with the verbs failing closed on bad args</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lifecycle/main/src/goal.rs <code>src/goal.rs</code>: the volatility split, the verbs, the emission in house shapes, the subprocess-composed closure gate; dispatch in <code>main()</code>; tests for sidecar round-trips, emission determinism, refusal no-op, and the composed gates on a fixture tree.</li> </ul> <h3 id="command-family"><a class="header" href="#command-family">Land the command family</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the door resolves and injects the emission from the host root <code>.opencode/commands/host-goal.md</code> in this host, the <code>.host-goal</code> gitignore entry, verified end to end through the binary in-session. Originally receipted under the nested <code>/host/goal</code> form; superseded by the universal-form ruling and the generated family: the doors are now <code>install</code>-written, flat <code>/host-<verb></code>, one source in the binary, two harness renderings, guarded by <code>install --check</code>.</li> </ul> <h3 id="run-loop"><a class="header" href="#run-loop">Run loop</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the goal set on this milestone, the tasks run through goal show, and the milestone closed with goal complete (or the failure recorded honestly) Set this milestone as the goal under the operator's build ruling, run the remaining tasks through <code>goal show</code> and receipt them. Riding beside it, one fresh codex bench on gpt-6-luna, the account-served judge (gpt-6.1 is not served to this codex account), with the limitation stated in its transcript: sessions are stateless, so per-question blindness holds, but the judge-model lineage matches the earlier bench. Scope: the real output samples plus the unresolved nails (transactional ordering at the closure receipt, the owed-item lifecycle, receipt freshness).</li> </ul> <h3 id="mcp-tools"><a class="header" href="#mcp-tools">Goal tools on the MCP server</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the verbs answer through the shipped MCP server The verbs join the shipped MCP server so any harness mounts them natively; the plugin custom-tool family stays cut.</li> </ul> <h3 id="corpus-surface"><a class="header" href="#corpus-surface">The corpus surface</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the goal declaration loads as an always-loaded surface with no plugin in the path The goal declaration readable as an always-loaded surface, the plan/0083 shape, so every session and every harness loads it with no plugin.</li> </ul> <h3 id="spine-ledger"><a class="header" href="#spine-ledger">Spine and ledger</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the manual section present-tense with the UPGRADING entry carrying applies-alone status and the stamp migration, and the teaching lines carrying a dokimi arms scorecard The manual section in present tense per call/0060 and call/0061; the UPGRADING.md entry carrying applies-alone status, the stamp migration with the re-stamp command and old-tool tolerance, the sidecar re-derivation, and the degraded mode stated as legible-without-verbs.</li> </ul> <h3 id="release-and-re-pin"><a class="header" href="#release-and-re-pin">Release and re-pin</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the verify gate green at the tag, the artifact hash re-derived in the recorded toolchain, and the re-pin receipted Release host-lifecycle carrying the goal verbs and the install verb through the tool-carried sequence. The doors go live off PATH and <code>/host-goal</code> stops depending on a debug binary; the composed closure gate can then close this milestone without the pin hazard.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The close (2026-10-20).</strong> All nine tasks receipted. The composed closure gate refused on exactly one hazard, a lane this milestone does not own: host-lint's kani lane, cancelled at its pin (the six-hour runner ceiling, <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/32">host-lint#32</a>). Per this task's own verify, the goal parks with the reason rather than exiting: the close resumes with <code>goal unpark .</code> the day that lane greens at a pin. Everything else the gate composes passed: the full verify sweep, all nine task receipts, the plan row, and a clean pushed tree.</p> <p>Deferred elsewhere, named so the queue does not lose them: a milestone-cutting primitive (number allocation plus README scaffold) belongs to <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/27">host#27</a>'s minting work, and Mara's semantic-acceptance line (a <code>goal accept</code> operator verb writing the ack onto the closure receipt) awaits the operator's fold ruling.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="the-dokimi-arms-run-2026-10-20-the-teaching-lines-measured"><a class="header" href="#the-dokimi-arms-run-2026-10-20-the-teaching-lines-measured">The dokimi arms run (2026-10-20): the teaching lines measured</a></h1> <p>Adopted <a href="https://github.com/intel/dokimi">intel/dokimi</a> at <code>691c007</code> as the standing paired-arms instrument (submodule <code>tools/dokimi</code>), and used it idiomatically on this milestone's own question: do the three teaching lines help the weak model operate the emission?</p> <ul> <li>Subject <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> on the router (openai provider, <code>OPENAI_API_BASE</code>); judge <code>qwen3.6-27b</code>, a different model per the instrument's own anti-self- judge rule. Reply budget 1024 (the serving lesson from the freeze battery).</li> <li>Arms: <code>baseline</code> (the question carries the ACTION-format ask only) versus <code>profile:teaching-profile.md</code> (the three teaching lines as the system prompt). The four probes are the freeze battery's real tool outputs, with the sanctioned move as each question's expected topic.</li> <li>Result: baseline 30.8, profile 89.0, paired delta +58.2, 95 percent CI [+28.7, +87.8], Cohen's d_z +3.14. Per probe: the composed refusal stays hardest even taught (56), the other three score 100 taught. The taught arm is also cheaper and faster: 902 completion tokens at 28s against 4096 at 38s untaught (the untaught model spends its budget flailing).</li> <li>This independently replicates the freeze battery's taught-context finding (9/16 minimal-context against 16/16 taught) through industrialized paired arms with a judge that is not the subject.</li> <li>The instrument's free first step also ran on this tree: <code>dokimi repo scan</code> reported three FAILs, all judged as reads, not defects (two are the manual's <code>NNNN</code> numbering placeholders, one is the bootstrap's gitignored <code>.claude/skills</code> symlink layer, machine state by the volatility split).</li> <li>One serving artifact recurred: a draw hit the 1024-token ceiling (the think-leak again); raise the budget on future runs.</li> </ul> <p>Lab files: <code>teaching-profile.md</code> (the profile arm), <code>goal-loop_golden.json</code> (the question set), <code>arms.md</code>/<code>arms.json</code> (the instrument's own report).</p> <h2 id="the-judge-role-done-properly-2026-10-20-same-day"><a class="header" href="#the-judge-role-done-properly-2026-10-20-same-day">The judge role, done properly (2026-10-20, same day)</a></h2> <p>The instrument's own docs are emphatic that a verdict under one judge is a property of that judge, and prescribe the panel, the validity gate, and the per-model rule. All three ran.</p> <ul> <li><strong>The cross-judge panel</strong> (<code>cross-judge.json</code>, <code>cross-judge.md</code>): the same stored answers re-scored by every judge. Direction unanimous: the stored qwen3.6-27b scored +58.2, a fresh qwen3.6-27b pass +73.0, and glm-5.3 +87.8, each with four wins and zero losses. The sign test stays at p 0.125 because n is four; that is sample size, not disagreement.</li> <li><strong>The validity gate</strong> (<code>validity-qwen3.6-27b.json</code>): the stored judge FAILED its own gate, ordering 61 percent of known-order pairs against the 80 percent bar (tie rate 22 percent). Under the discipline, its measures are shown but do not vote. glm-5.3's validity run and a sequential retry for the 27B are in flight; the voting judge is whichever passes.</li> <li><strong>The per-model half</strong> (glm-5.3 as subject, taught versus untaught) is queued behind a validated judge, per the same discipline.</li> <li><strong>An upstream wart, recorded for filing</strong>: <code>eval cross-judge</code> splits <code>provider/model</code> but passes the bare model to LiteLLM without the provider, which refuses it ("Provider NOT provided"); the working form is the double prefix (<code>openai/openai/glm-5.3</code>), which is also why the stored judge's name carries it. The serving on this endpoint is ollama-backed and real, and glm-5.3 answers take a thinking budget (442 completion tokens for a one-line reply): size judge calls generously.</li> </ul> <h2 id="correction-operator-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#correction-operator-2026-10-20">Correction (operator, 2026-10-20)</a></h2> <p>The model this endpoint serves under the id <code>qwen3.6-27b</code> is <strong>Qwen3.8-27B</strong>. The artifacts retain the id as called (the runs used it verbatim); read every <code>qwen3.6-27b</code> below as Qwen3.8-27B, the mid tier of this endpoint's judge pool beside the frontier-tier glm-5.3.</p> <h2 id="the-terse-variant-staged-not-shipped"><a class="header" href="#the-terse-variant-staged-not-shipped">The terse variant, staged not shipped</a></h2> <p>The audit pass tightened every free text; the teaching profile is measured text (+58.2 under the stored judge) and is not edited blind. It ships only if it measures: a three-arm run (baseline, the current profile, the terse profile) before the spine freezes, judged by whichever judge passes the validity gate.</p> <h2 id="the-judge-tier-verdict-no-gated-llm-judge-on-this-endpoint-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#the-judge-tier-verdict-no-gated-llm-judge-on-this-endpoint-2026-10-20">The judge tier verdict: no gated LLM judge on this endpoint (2026-10-20)</a></h2> <p>The validity chain finished and both candidates failed (<code>validity-glm-5.3.json</code>, <code>validity-qwen3.6-27b-seq.json</code>). glm-5.3 scored 31 percent accuracy with a 61 percent tie rate, and scored DAMAGED copies above originals on three variants (mismatched answer, padding, shuffled sentences: negative mean drops). The sequential 27B retry scored 61 percent with every tie decided, failing the same 80 percent bar. Under the instrument's discipline, no measure on this endpoint votes.</p> <p>What stands instead is the instrument the house already trusted for exactly this reason: the mechanical rubric scorer of the freeze battery (strict ACTION-line matching, zero-invented-commands invariant) is deterministic by construction and needs no calibration. dokimi's own gate just measured the house thesis on the judge tier: open-ended LLM judgment at the weak and mid tier is not reliable enough to score with, while a rubric-bound mechanical scorer is. dokimi stays adopted: its arms structure, paired design, and answer capture carry the experiments; the scoring layer is the house rubric.
