Reply with one line starting with ACTION: naming that move.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><p>You work inside a software project governed by host loop. The tool output's NEXT line names your single next move. A command runs as printed. work <key> begins that task. A refusal's last line runs. Reply with one line: ACTION: the move.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="the-word-effectiveness-sweep-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#the-word-effectiveness-sweep-2026-10-20">The word-effectiveness sweep (2026-10-20)</a></h1> <p>Six teaching-line variants, one word dimension each, sixteen draws per variant on the real qwen3.5-4b at deployment sampling, strict ACTION-line scoring with the zero-invented invariant (the mechanical rubric: the scoring layer that stands, per the judge-tier verdict the same day).</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>variant</th><th>strict</th><th>empty</th><th>invented</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>V0 current</td><td>14/16</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>V1 terse (half the words)</td><td>8/16</td><td>7</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>V2 do-verb (<code>do</code> for <code>work</code>)</td><td>13/16</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>V3 format-first (reply rule first)</td><td>6/16</td><td>10</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>V4 no-frame (drop the host-loop sentence)</td><td>13/16</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>V5 ste-strict (simplified words, full sentences)</td><td>14/16</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="what-the-words-are-worth-the-standing-table"><a class="header" href="#what-the-words-are-worth-the-standing-table">What the words are worth (the standing table)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>The if-then scaffolding is load-bearing.</strong> Compressing the conditionals away (V1) or reordering them after the reply rule (V3) collapses adherence and breeds empty replies (7 and 10 of 16: a confused model thinks longer and exhausts the reply budget). Terseness past the structure is destruction, not economy.</li> <li><strong>The register is free.</strong> V5 simplifies every word to the STE-approved register, keeps full sentences, and holds V0's full effect at about 40 percent fewer words. Simplification wins whenever the structure survives.</li> <li><strong>The verb is indifferent.</strong> <code>work <key></code> versus <code>do <key></code> measures no difference; keep <code>work</code> (already shipped, already measured).</li> <li><strong>The frame sentence earns nothing.</strong> "governed by the host loop" drops without measurable cost; it stays only if the spine wants the naming.</li> <li><strong>V0's earlier 16/16 was favorable sampling</strong>: the fresh re-baseline reads 14/16, the honest reference for future comparisons at this n.</li> </ul> <h2 id="the-ruling"><a class="header" href="#the-ruling">The ruling</a></h2> <p>V5 ships as the teaching-line text: equal measured effect, fewer words, the STE register the spine already mandates. The staged terse variant (V1) is refused by its own measurement and retires.</p> <h2 id="round-two-same-day-the-negative-rule-is-the-strongest-lever"><a class="header" href="#round-two-same-day-the-negative-rule-is-the-strongest-lever">Round two (same day): the negative rule is the strongest lever</a></h2> <p>Seven arms against the V5 incumbent, re-baselined in-round. The method finding first: the identical incumbent text read 14 in round one and 11 in round two (serving drift), so the in-round re-baseline is the only honest unit; cross-round numbers never compare.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>arm</th><th>strict</th><th>empty</th><th>P1/P2/P3/P4</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>R0 v5 incumbent</td><td>11/16</td><td>2</td><td>1/4, 3/4, 4/4, 3/4</td></tr> <tr><td>R1 +needs-you rule</td><td>13/16</td><td>1</td><td>3/4, 3/4, 4/4, 3/4</td></tr> <tr><td>R2 +numbered rules</td><td>14/16</td><td>1</td><td>4/4, 3/4, 4/4, 3/4</td></tr> <tr><td>R3 +one exemplar</td><td>14/16</td><td>2</td><td>4/4, 2/4, 4/4, 4/4</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>R4 +never-invent rule</strong></td><td><strong>15/16</strong></td><td><strong>0</strong></td><td><strong>4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 3/4</strong></td></tr> <tr><td>R5 +no-frame</td><td>14/16</td><td>0</td><td>4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 2/4</td></tr> <tr><td>R6 exemplar+needs</td><td>14/16</td><td>2</td><td>3/4, 3/4, 4/4, 4/4</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>R4 ADVANCES (+4 over the in-round incumbent, every probe hardened at once, zero empty replies): one negative sentence, "Never invent a command or a flag," is the strongest lever found in either round. The exemplar arm trades tails (fixes P4, dents P2); the frame sentence stays droppable; the NEEDS YOU rule helps P1 alone. Round three iterates around R4 (numbered, exemplar, repair-exemplar, no-frame, a word-for-word register micro-test), same criterion: advance needs +2 over the in-round incumbent, plateau is a round with no advance.</p> <h2 id="the-check-in-cast-and-a-blind-bench-before-round-three-reports"><a class="header" href="#the-check-in-cast-and-a-blind-bench-before-round-three-reports">The check-in (cast and a blind bench, before round three reports)</a></h2> <p>Paused the loop to consult. The six benches converged on three defects and a revised protocol; transcript above, the synthesis:</p> <ul> <li><strong>The threshold sits inside the noise.</strong> Plus two at sixteen draws is about one sigma (the same text drifted three across rounds), so a no-advance round cannot alone declare plateau. Sweeps are exploratory; shipping decisions need a confirmation stage, never a sweep result.</li> <li><strong>Selection on four fixed probes measures fit, not generalization.</strong> Two rounds of best-of-seven arms is a winner's curse: the incumbent's score is inflated by the selection that chose it. Before any winner ships into adopter manuals: a LOCKED candidate versus the LOCKED incumbent, on held-out probe states never used for selection, fresh draws, randomized/interleaved arm order (within-round drift can entangle with fixed arm order), a pre-declared margin, a per-state floor (no state below three of four), the zero-invented hard gate, and either a second model or a scope statement naming the model, probes, scorer, and serving.</li> <li><strong>The scorer is blind to well-formed wrong commands</strong> (right verb, wrong binding; a real flag bent to a wrong argument). The subject's worst failure mode is fluent. The confirmation scorer adds a binding-correctness check.</li> <li>Two mechanistic readings recorded as doctrine: the subject matches shape rather than parsing; the negative rule wins because it is one crisp gate the model can apply mid-generation, while a positive ideal offers nothing to check against. The exemplar dent is anchoring.</li> <li>The final receipt (the operator's shape): the text verbatim; same-round incumbent and candidate scores; the margin restated (absolutes do not travel); per-state passes; empties and invented flags as separate zero lines; the round ledger attached, because no ledger means no checkable plateau claim.</li> </ul> <h2 id="round-three-same-day-the-exploratory-plateau"><a class="header" href="#round-three-same-day-the-exploratory-plateau">Round three (same day): the exploratory plateau</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>arm</th><th>strict</th><th>empty</th><th>P1/P2/P3/P4</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>S0 r4 incumbent</td><td>14/16</td><td>0</td><td>4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 2/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S1 +numbered</td><td>15/16</td><td>1</td><td>4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 3/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S2 +unpark exemplar</td><td>15/16</td><td>1</td><td>4/4, 3/4, 4/4, 4/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S3 +repair exemplar</td><td>14/16</td><td>2</td><td>4/4, 3/4, 3/4, 4/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S4 no-frame</td><td>11/16</td><td>1</td><td>3/4, 3/4, 4/4, 1/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S5 numbered+exemplar</td><td>11/16</td><td>5</td><td>3/4, 1/4, 4/4, 3/4</td></tr> <tr><td>S6 word-for-word</td><td>13/16</td><td>1</td><td>4/4, 3/4, 4/4, 2/4</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>No arm cleared plus two over the in-round incumbent: the exploratory plateau, per the pre-declared rule. Two readings join the table: levers do not stack (the numbered-plus-exemplar combo collapsed to 11 with five empties; each lever alone was the round's best), and the frame sentence that read droppable in round two cost three this round (frame removal read 11 against the same incumbent's 14), so the frame stays and the droppable claim retires. Per protocol v2 nothing ships from this round; the confirmation battery runs with the mechanically locked candidate (S2, the incumbent plus the unpark exemplar, selected by the pre-declared rule: best score at or above the in-round incumbent, fewest empties, name order as the deterministic final tiebreak) against the untaught arm and the original V0, on four held-out states never used in any round, fully interleaved.</p> <h2 id="the-first-confirmation-no-ship-and-the-stage-earned-its-keep"><a class="header" href="#the-first-confirmation-no-ship-and-the-stage-earned-its-keep">The first confirmation: NO-SHIP (and the stage earned its keep)</a></h2> <p>Fully interleaved, 96 draws, three arms (untaught, the original V0, the locked sweep candidate S2) over the four selection states and four held-out states never used in any round.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>arm</th><th>pooled</th><th>held-out</th><th>empty</th><th>invented</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>A untaught</td><td>10/32</td><td>5/16</td><td>21</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>B v0 original</td><td>21/32</td><td>6/16</td><td>1</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>C sweep candidate</td><td>20/32</td><td>7/16</td><td>5</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Criteria 1 and 2 passed (zero invented; the taught arms beat untaught by 10 and 11); criteria 3 and 4 failed: the texts tied inside noise on confirmation (the sweep's preference did not survive held-out, the winner's curse caught in the act), and two held-out states scored zero for every taught arm. <strong>NO-SHIP printed mechanically; nothing shipped.</strong></p> <p>The zero states were emission defects, not text defects, and both are now fixed in the component (<code>3e20cec</code>): the no-goal state offered a placeholder command as NEXT, which the taught rule (run a command as printed) made every arm transcribe (the move is now ask-the-operator); and the tasks remedy carried a template anchor, so both taught arms copied the template instead of binding the open task the hazard names (the remedy now resolves the first open anchor). The confirmation re-runs against the fixed emission with the same texts, probes, and pre-declared criteria.</p> <h2 id="the-second-confirmation-ship-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#the-second-confirmation-ship-2026-10-20">The second confirmation: SHIP (2026-10-20)</a></h2> <p>Same texts, same pre-declared criteria, same interleaving, against the emission fixed in <code>3e20cec</code>.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>arm</th><th>pooled</th><th>held-out</th><th>empty</th><th>invented</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>A untaught</td><td>17/32</td><td>7/16</td><td>15</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td>B v0 original</td><td>24/32</td><td>9/16</td><td>0</td><td>0</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>C shipped</strong></td><td><strong>26/32</strong></td><td><strong>11/16</strong></td><td>5</td><td><strong>0</strong></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>All four criteria passed, and the candidate wins outright rather than tying: plus two pooled, plus two held-out, and it binds where V0 cannot (the open-anchor state reads 2/4 against 0/4). The completed reading: on the broken emission the texts tied; on the fixed emission the sweep's lever (the negative rule plus the exemplar in the plain register) was real all along, masked by emission defects. The untaught arm itself rose from 10 to 17 on the fixed emission: the emission fixes were worth more than any word choice.</p> <p><strong>The shipped text</strong> (verbatim, <code>teaching-lines.shipped.md</code>):</p> <blockquote> <p>You run the host loop. The NEXT line of the tool output names your next move. Run a command as printed. If it says work <key>, start that task. If the tool stops, run the last line. Never invent a command or a flag. Example: NEXT: host-lifecycle goal unpark . -> ACTION: host-lifecycle goal unpark . Answer with one line: ACTION: <the move>.</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Scope of validity</strong> (ships with the claim): measured on qwen3.5-4b at the rope endpoint (ollama-backed), temperature 0.6, reply budget 1024, eight states (four selection, four held-out), the mechanical ACTION rubric with binding checks, criteria pre-declared before both confirmations, 2026-10-20. Other models and other emissions are outside the measurement.</p> <p>The battery is closed. The round ledger is this directory; no claim in it depends on a number not filed here.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><p>You run the host loop. The NEXT line of the tool output names your next move. Run a command as printed. If it says work <key>, start that task. If the tool stops, run the last line. Never invent a command or a flag. Example: NEXT: host-lifecycle goal unpark . -> ACTION: host-lifecycle goal unpark . Answer with one line: ACTION: <the move>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0101-convening-record-two-sittings-of-the-cast"><a class="header" href="#plan0101-convening-record-two-sittings-of-the-cast">plan/0101 convening record: two sittings of the cast</a></h1> <p>First sitting 2026-10-18: design review of the initial proposal. Second sitting the same day, operator-charged: the design must be an idiomatic extension of the host methodology, not over-fit to how other implementations function. Rulings as returned, condensed; the full texts live in the session that convened them.</p> <h2 id="first-sitting-design-review"><a class="header" href="#first-sitting-design-review">First sitting (design review)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Mara</strong>: the direction split is right with one thief in it; "sanctioned next move" launders intent through a picker function, so suggest, never sanction, and show the frontier. One goal per tree if mid-goal maintenance is a sanctioned path. The emission needs the PURPOSE line (the why, not the number) and a NEEDS YOU line; same shape every time; fail loudly. The idle refusal must distinguish your-work-broke-it from already-red. Semantic acceptance needs one ack line on the closure receipt.</li> <li><strong>Wren</strong>: compaction injection is a half cure; the trace still dies unless the record bank carries decisions and rejections. One move is right-sized but needs the acceptance surface and a sanctioned escape move (the pre-formed stop-and-ask). No park means temporary blocks get recorded as exits. goal set with no agent-side propose path rebuilds the original sin. Determinism without a when-judged marker hides staleness. Weak-model acceptance belongs at the start, not as dessert.</li> <li><strong>Fen</strong>: goal complete is the reward verb; a weak model runs it early, reruns it, then invents a force flag. The refusal must be a full no-op and every mutating verb's failure re-prints the frontier. A wall of hazards is not actionable; ordered, first fix only, rest counted. Enforce operator-only in the tool or drop the claim. The seam needs one installer verb and a dead-hook check. Success must bank the receipt and print the next move.</li> <li><strong>Bly</strong>: old tools rewriting the stamp must carry unknown keys forward or a routine materialize erases the goal. The record must be legible without the new verbs; the verb cannot be the hidden state. Closure receipts write once, atomically, at green. Abandon that only clears the key makes the deferral vanish; write a tracked OWED line. A seam on an old tool rebuilds the unknown-command bug with more steps; version-check and print the install command.</li> <li><strong>Orin</strong>: write the spine against the CLI contract; the emission is the loop's whole interface. Two breaches of the host#26 constraint: a refusal decided in the seam, and validation born in plugin tools; the seam may only render what the CLI produced and shell to it. The purity claim is false if CI verdicts read live network; a tracked active-goal key dirties every worktree's verify. Claude parity must be executed, not asserted.</li> </ul> <h2 id="second-sitting-idiom-fidelity"><a class="header" href="#second-sitting-idiom-fidelity">Second sitting (idiom fidelity)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Mara</strong>: the sidecar TRANSLATES to a tracked Status-line declaration, sidecar demoted to a per-worktree projection (the envhash pattern). The token CUTS: the audited commit is the act. park/unpark CUT as verbs, TRANSLATE as the queue. NEEDS YOU KEEPS as projection only, every line tracing to a tracked row. Over-fit named: the token, the BDI commitment moves, compaction re-injection where the corpus already answers; defer the whole OpenCode seam until the core is housegrown.</li> <li><strong>Wren</strong>: recitation TRANSLATES to the declared corpus; what is not loaded does not exist, and the goal declaration belongs on a corpus-declarable tracked surface. Plugin tools TRANSLATE to the shipped MCP server; the duplicate surface is the port defect. Emission labels TRANSLATE mostly: NEEDS YOU is a HAZARD line, FRONTIER is the tasks line verbatim, CI is gate output; new labels only where no shape exists. A second goal state VIOLATES the plan record as single source; the equation goal IS milestone is the most idiomatic thing in the design.</li> <li><strong>Fen</strong>: the refusal TRANSLATES back to the house shape: one HAZARD line per missing thing, each with the exact command; first-only-plus-count is progressive disclosure, a foreign interactive habit. The sidecar is the stamp idiom, two values, with show the only reader and repair the reconciler. Inline class markers TRANSLATE away: batteries showed the model transcribes decorations into the shell; the section is the class, command lines stay bare. propose KEEPS: the usage-emission idiom.</li> <li><strong>Bly</strong>: the gitignored pointer VIOLATES as designed (invisible to a fresh clone, silent under-report on loss); the declaration is tracked, sidecar a projection. OWED TRANSLATES to PLAN.md's closure queue, where a cold reader looks first. Parked state in the sidecar VIOLATES; parked is standing, standing is tracked. The ledger entry needs applies-alone, the stamp migration with re-stamp command, and sidecar re-derivation. Degraded means legible without any verb.</li> <li><strong>Orin</strong>: the MADR form KEEPS (call/0060 precedent; a plan without a call/ record orphans a spine-wide decision). State TRANSLATES by volatility: envhash is untracked because machine, receipts tracked because facts; the sidecar never holds what a clone must see. The gate deferral CUTS: compose as subprocesses, the tool driving its own verbs; shipping a weak gate writes a contract that only models the path walked. Parking TRANSLATES to re-queuing. The MCP server and the corpus are the seams; CUT the plugin tools and the compaction hook. The teaching section never says new, replaces, or migrate; the lineage lives in call/ alone.</li> </ul> <h2 id="synthesis-adopted-by-plan0101"><a class="header" href="#synthesis-adopted-by-plan0101">Synthesis adopted by plan/0101</a></h2> <p>The volatility split; no token; parking as re-queuing; subprocess gate composition; all hazards each with a command; sections as classes; house shapes in the emission; MCP and corpus as the seams; call/0061 as the modality record; the lineage in the record layer.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0101-fen-battery-mock-emissions-first-pass"><a class="header" href="#plan0101-fen-battery-mock-emissions-first-pass">plan/0101 fen battery (mock emissions, first pass)</a></h1> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-10-18</li> <li>Model: qwen3.5-4b on the router (api.d07yx58.net), the real weak executor</li> <li>Parameters: temperature 0.6 (deployment sampling), max 200 tokens</li> <li>Protocol: four probe states x two repeats. Each probe hands the model a mock tool output in the then-current emission shape and asks for one line starting with ACTION: naming the single next move (the plan/0077 ACTION protocol). Scoring per probe: the exact sanctioned command or operator ask present, no invented flags, no plans instead of actions.</li> </ul> <h2 id="probes"><a class="header" href="#probes">Probes</a></h2> <ul> <li>P1 orientation (green path): a full goal show block whose NEXT line names <code>host-lifecycle tasks --record plan/0077-reference-resolver#wire-the-emission .</code></li> <li>P2 refusal: a goal complete refusal carrying one ordered hazard with its fix command (<code>host-lifecycle resolve plan/0074 --markdown .</code>) and a count of the rest.</li> <li>P3 needs-you: a goal show block whose NEEDS YOU line carries the operator question; NEXT names the stop.</li> <li>P4 unreadable state: goal show refusing to emit, naming <code>host-lifecycle goal repair .</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="results-eight-of-eight-passed"><a class="header" href="#results-eight-of-eight-passed">Results (eight of eight passed)</a></h2> <pre><code>P1 rep1 PASS: ACTION: host-lifecycle tasks --record plan/0077-reference-resolver#wire-the-emission P1 rep2 PASS: (<think> tokens leaked by the serving, then the same command) P2 rep1 PASS: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0074 --markdown . P2 rep2 PASS: ACTION: host-lifecycle resolve plan/0074 --markdown . P3 rep1 PASS: ACTION: Ask operator which resolver design they want (A or B) before the last task can run P3 rep2 PASS: ACTION: Ask which resolver design you want, A or B? P4 rep1 PASS: ACTION: host-lifecycle goal repair . P4 rep2 PASS: ACTION: host-lifecycle goal repair . </code></pre> <h2 id="reading-and-the-owed-rerun"><a class="header" href="#reading-and-the-owed-rerun">Reading, and the owed rerun</a></h2> <p>The amended emission shape worked on the real 4B at first pass: the exact command was transcribed verbatim, no flags were invented across all eight draws, the needs-you stop surfaced the question instead of proceeding, and the unreadable state routed to the repair verb rather than a hand edit. One serving quirk: a think-block leak on one draw (P1 rep2), worth watching as a serving artifact rather than a model behavior.</p> <p>The refusal shape changed after this battery: the cast's second convening restored the house form (every hazard printed, each with its exact command) in place of first-fix-plus-count. This battery validated the superseded shape; the freeze gate reruns the battery against real <code>goal show</code> and <code>goal complete</code> output under the house shape, per the build sequence.</p> <h1 id="the-freeze-battery-on-real-output-2026-10-19"><a class="header" href="#the-freeze-battery-on-real-output-2026-10-19">The freeze battery on real output (2026-10-19)</a></h1> <p>Real binary output, four probe states, the ACTION protocol, deployment sampling, strict scoring on the ACTION line alone. P1: the real host emission. P2: the real composed refusal. P3/P4: fixture hosts (the plan/0077 method: real code, controlled state).</p> <h2 id="the-runs-and-what-each-taught"><a class="header" href="#the-runs-and-what-each-taught">The runs, and what each taught</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Run one (minimal context, 200-token replies): 11 of 16 loose, and it caught two real defects.</strong> The composed gate wrapped a failing sweep's ok lines as hazards (fixed: the wrapper passes through HAZARD lines only), and the serving leaked think blocks into replies, truncating some to empty (controlled: a reply budget of 1024 in the battery configuration).</li> <li><strong>Run two (strict, 512): 9 of 16.</strong> The unreadable-state refusal named <code>goal repair</code> on a bare unlabeled line and the model ignored it four of four times, once hand-creating the missing file instead (the antipattern the verbs exist to prevent). Fixed: the refusal wears the NEXT label and shares the emission's last-line shape.</li> <li><strong>Variants: more text is more distraction.</strong> A longer work line with the record command sent the model to cat PLAN.md and git status (other lines' vocabulary); a block-shaped refusal garbled the command order. The terse lines stand.</li> <li><strong>Run three (the taught context, 512): 13 of 16</strong>, the failures being two serving empties and one word-order garble.</li> <li><strong>Run four (the taught context, 1024): 16 of 16, zero invented commands, zero empties.</strong> Across every run today (sixty-four draws) the hard invariant held: not one invented flag or function.</li> </ul> <p>The taught context is three lines carried by the teaching layer (the spine task): a NEXT command runs exactly as printed; <code>work <key></code> begins that task; a refusal's last line runs. The freeze condition is the emission plus those lines, which is the plan/0091 doctrine stated once more: the shape carries what it can, the teaching layer carries what it cannot.</p> <h2 id="final-configuration"><a class="header" href="#final-configuration">Final configuration</a></h2> <p>qwen3.5-4b on the router, temperature 0.6, reply budget 1024, strict ACTION-line scoring with think blocks stripped. Transcripts of the four probe inputs live in this session's run log; the probe texts are reproducible from the binary: the real host's <code>goal show .</code> and <code>goal complete plan/0101-goal-and-loop-subsystem .</code>, and the two fixture hosts (a parked goal; a set receipt naming a missing plan).</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="the-kani-lane-concludes-host-lint32"><a class="header" href="#the-kani-lane-concludes-host-lint32">The kani lane concludes (host-lint#32)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: landed 2026-10-28 as host-lint v0.23.1 (cb58793); the framing residual closed by exclusion 2026-10-29 (plan/0105). The classification rows are proven: sixteen CI rows green, lem_n10 among them, 18 s to 40 m locally. The six line-framing rows never concluded on any runtime: local caps at one hour, then ninety minutes against the checked-slicing rework (all six rc=124), and CI ceilings at six hours. The admission rule now bars a harness row from the CI matrix until one local run concludes; v0.23.2 carries the rule and drops the six rows, so the lane greens at the bounded matrix and plan/0101's parked close can unpark. The framing property itself stays open behind the operator's route pick from the lacuna survey: the contract route (kani -Z function-contracts or stubbing), a heap-free LemHit, a TLA+ lateral lane, or the test downgrade.</strong></p> <h2 id="why-22"><a class="header" href="#why-22">Why</a></h2> <p>Every host-lint tag run since v0.22.1 died at GitHub's six-hour runner ceiling. The sharding (<code>fc580ad</code>, v0.22.4) bounded each proof to its own job and did not save the lane: each of the three lem harnesses alone eats the whole ceiling (<code>scan_line_never_panics</code>, <code>form_and_mangle_hits_are_classified_by_the_table</code>, <code>hits_are_word_bounded</code>), while the three <code>verify_*</code> rungs conclude in moments. plan/0101's close parks on this lane; the day it greens at a pin, that goal unparks and completes.</p> <h2 id="the-measured-diagnosis-2026-10-20-stage-zero"><a class="header" href="#the-measured-diagnosis-2026-10-20-stage-zero">The measured diagnosis (2026-10-20, stage zero)</a></h2> <p>One verification condition spans the whole matcher: the tokenizer loop (with quote state) times the per-word classification times a thirteen-entry canonical table of string equalities over symbolically-derived words, times the agreement lookahead: and the harness asserts re-run the same tables on the hit words, which doubles the surface. The input domains are already tiny (8 to 12 symbolic bytes); the bound is not the problem. The composition is. Two defects of coverage also stand: at <code>n <= 8</code> the proof never reaches <code>lemuselves</code> (ten bytes), the longest table entry, so the longest forms sit outside today's stated domain; and no harness declares an unwind bound (the small rungs do).</p> <h2 id="the-fix-design"><a class="header" href="#the-fix-design">The fix design</a></h2> <p>The properties do not change; their decomposition does.</p> <ul> <li>Extract the per-word classifier and the word-run tokenizer step from <code>scan_lem_line</code> into pure functions. Behavior-identical; the conformance corpus and the test suite prove it.</li> <li>Prove the classification invariants at word level with <code>n <= 10</code> (full table coverage, one word, no tokenizer, no lookahead): a Form hit is canonical; a Mangle hit starts with lem and is neither canonical nor whitelisted; a FirstPerson hit is a first-person word.</li> <li>Prove word-boundedness against the word-run step alone.</li> <li>Prove the line framing (quote state, index arithmetic, the slices) with the classifier behind a kani function contract if the pinned kani carries them cleanly; otherwise with per-property splits at reduced length. Either way every harness carries <code>#[kani::unwind(K)]</code>.</li> <li>The CI matrix grows one row per harness; each job must conclude with margin (minutes locally, not hours).</li> </ul> <p>A proof that never finishes discharges nothing (the kani-conformance doctrine); the fallback of last resort is a property reformulation, and that is a ruling this room asks for, never one it takes.</p> <h2 id="release-shape"><a class="header" href="#release-shape">Release shape</a></h2> <p>Change-class <code>neither</code> (v0.23.1): the restructure moves no flag semantics. Authorized by this room. The moment of truth is the tag run itself concluding inside the ceiling.</p> <p>The <code>upstream-drift</code> job is <code>continue-on-error</code> and never gated the lane; the ffmpeg corpus acknowledgment it names stays a follow-on, not this room's work.</p> <h2 id="build-sequence-29"><a class="header" href="#build-sequence-29">Build sequence</a></h2> <h3 id="diagnose"><a class="header" href="#diagnose">Diagnose</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the three heavy harnesses timed locally under a cap, the timings and the fix-class diagnosis recorded in bench/</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs</li> </ul> <h3 id="decompose"><a class="header" href="#decompose">Decompose the proofs</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: every harness SUCCESSFUL through host-prove with a stated unwind bound, each in minutes locally; cargo test green; the conformance lane green; the property set unchanged</li> <li>depends: #diagnose</li> <li>inputs: software/host-lint/main/src/lib.rs, software/host-lint/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml, software/host-lint/main/host-lint.obligations</li> </ul> <h3 id="release"><a class="header" href="#release">Release v0.23.1</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the tool-carried sequence green at the tag, and the tag run concludes inside the ceiling</li> <li>depends: #decompose</li> </ul> <h3 id="re-pin"><a class="header" href="#re-pin">Re-pin and receipt</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: software --check green with the lint lane discharged at the new pin</li> <li>depends: #release</li> </ul> <h3 id="close-0101"><a class="header" href="#close-0101">Unpark and close plan/0101</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: goal complete banks the closure receipt, GOAL.md returns to the no-goal state, and the operator's accept rides the record</li> <li>depends: #re-pin</li> </ul> <h3 id="records"><a class="header" href="#records">Records</a></h3> <ul> <li>verify: the PLAN.md row complete, a MEMORY.md entry, host-lint#32 closed with the fix comment, the tree pushed</li> <li>depends: #close-0101</li> </ul> <h2 id="landed-2026-10-28-plan0103"><a class="header" href="#landed-2026-10-28-plan0103">Landed (2026-10-28, plan/0103)</a></h2> <p>The decomposition executed, with a diagnosis stage zero did not have: the verification condition was never the only cost. Three stacked findings came out of the timed runs (bench in plan/0103):</p> <ol> <li><strong>The panicking str slice.</strong> <code>word[..3].eq_ignore_ascii_case("lem")</code> reaches the panicking-slice machinery, and the solver grinds on a <em>fully concrete</em> harness because of it. The prefix is now explicit ASCII byte comparisons; the concrete control that hung for five minutes passes in seconds.</li> <li><strong>Bounds below the table.</strong> A 13-entry table walk under <code>unwind(12)</code> fails its unwinding assertion in seconds, which reads as a counterexample and is not one. Every harness now carries <code>unwind(24)</code>.</li> <li><strong>One VC per concrete length.</strong> A symbolic length across monomorphized copies is one enormous VC; a symbolic-length <code>Vec</code> was also retired (the classifier fills a fixed <code>[LemKind; 5]</code>). The matrix grew to one row per concrete length: scan_line n1 to n6, lem-word n3 to n10 (the longest table entry is ten bytes), exact-word n1 to n8, plus the word-run property.</li> </ol> <p>Local evidence: <code>word_run_end_is_word_bounded</code> 18 s, <code>exact_word_..._n6</code> 9 m 19 s, <code>exact_word_..._n3</code> 16 m, <code>lem_word_..._n4</code> 26 m, and <code>lem_word_..._n10</code> 40 m, all SUCCESSFUL under one-hour caps, so the thirteen-entry table property that never concluded in six CI hours now concludes locally in under forty minutes. The line-framing rows (<code>scan_line_never_panics_n6</code> passed one hour locally) are the tag run's to judge; the ceiling is six hours per row. The classifier's shape changes are behavior-identical (234 conformance tests); the v0.23.1 release also adopts host-grammar v0.8.0 and the anchor-divergence work rides the next release.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="stage-zero-the-measurement-and-the-fix-class-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#stage-zero-the-measurement-and-the-fix-class-2026-10-20">Stage zero: the measurement and the fix class (2026-10-20)</a></h1> <h2 id="the-lanes-history-read-from-github"><a class="header" href="#the-lanes-history-read-from-github">The lane's history (read from GitHub)</a></h2> <p>Every tag run since v0.22.1 cancelled at the ceiling. The sharding (<code>fc580ad</code>, v0.22.4) put each harness in its own job with <code>fail-fast: false</code>; the v0.23.0 tag run (39077707855) shows the split verdict plainly: the three <code>verify_*</code> rungs concluded in moments, and <code>scan_line_never_panics</code>, <code>form_and_mangle_hits_are_classified_by_the_table</code>, and <code>hits_are_word_bounded</code> each ran six hours and were cancelled together. The <code>upstream-drift</code> job is <code>continue-on-error</code> and never gated the lane.</p> <h2 id="the-code-read-at-the-pin-90a0d71"><a class="header" href="#the-code-read-at-the-pin-90a0d71">The code (read at the pin, 90a0d71)</a></h2> <p>The three heavy harnesses drive <code>scan_lem_line</code> whole: a tokenizer loop with quote state, per-word classification (exact compares, <code>is_first_person_word</code>, <code>starts_with("lem")</code>, <code>LEM_WHITELIST.contains</code>, <code>LEM_CANONICAL.contains</code>), and an agreement lookahead that scans ahead for a verb and matches it against a four-arm table. The input bounds are already tiny (n <= 8, n <= 8, n <= 12 symbolic bytes over restricted alphabets), so the bound is not the problem.</p> <p>The verification condition is the whole composition: every tokenizer path times every classification branch times a thirteen-entry table of string equalities over symbolically-derived words times the lookahead, and the harness asserts re-run the same table lookups on the hit words, which doubles the surface. That is why six hours buys nothing.</p> <p>Two coverage defects ride along: at n <= 8 the proof can never reach <code>lemuselves</code> (ten bytes), the longest canonical entry, so the longest forms sit outside the stated domain; and none of the three carries an unwind annotation while the small rungs do.</p> <h2 id="the-fix-class"><a class="header" href="#the-fix-class">The fix class</a></h2> <p>Decomposition with function contracts (the pinned kani, <code>-Z function-contracts</code>):</p> <ul> <li>Extract <code>word_run_end(b, i)</code> (the maximal word-run scan) and <code>lem_word_kinds(word, quoted, rest)</code> (the entire per-word decision including the agreement lookahead, pure over the word's bytes, the quote flag, and the bytes after the word). <code>scan_lem_line</code> becomes framing plus calls; behavior-identical, guarded by the golden tests, the proptest suite, and the conformance lane.</li> <li>Contracts: <code>word_run_end</code> ensures the returned index is in bounds and either ends the slice or lands on a non-word byte; <code>lem_word_kinds</code> ensures no panic and the soundness invariants (a Form kind is canonical and not bare <code>l</code>; a Mangle kind starts with lem and is neither canonical nor whitelisted; a FirstPerson kind is a first-person word).</li> <li>Word-level harnesses prove the contracts (<code>kani::proof_for_contract</code>), one word at n <= 10: full table coverage including <code>lemuselves</code>, a fraction of the old state space.</li> <li>Line-level harnesses (<code>scan_line_never_panics</code>, <code>hits_are_word_bounded</code>, framed over n <= 8 and n <= 12 as today) verify against the contract-stubbed bodies: the tables leave their verification conditions.</li> <li>Every harness carries <code>#[kani::unwind(K)]</code>; the CI job grows one matrix row per harness and runs with <code>-Z function-contracts</code>.</li> </ul> <p>If contracts misbehave in this crate, the fallback is the same decomposition without body stubbing: word-level proofs stand alone, the line-level framing rides tests and conformance, and that restatement comes back to the operator as a ruling before it lands.</p> <h2 id="the-measured-timings-of-the-decomposition-2026-10-20"><a class="header" href="#the-measured-timings-of-the-decomposition-2026-10-20">The measured timings of the decomposition (2026-10-20)</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>word_run_end_honors_its_contract</code>: SUCCESSFUL in ten seconds (115 checks, 0 failed, 2 unreachable).</li> <li>The classifier contract and the two stubbed line proofs: appended as they conclude.</li> </ul> <h3 id="the-playbook-if-the-classifier-contract-caps-pre-written"><a class="header" href="#the-playbook-if-the-classifier-contract-caps-pre-written">The playbook if the classifier contract caps (pre-written)</a></h3> <p>The expensive fact is table membership; assumptions prune it cheaply where proofs must establish it. Split the one contract proof into three by word shape, each proving only its own arm. Over canonical entries: the form flag is exact. Over uncanonical lem-prefixed words: the mangle flag is exact against the whitelist. The first-person arm is unchanged. Each table scan then appears only in an assume, the direction SAT solvers like. The line-level stubs are unchanged: the contract on the function is the same, only its proof is sharded.</p> <h2 id="the-local-timings"><a class="header" href="#the-local-timings">The local timings</a></h2> <p>Measured 2026-10-20, local kani 0.67.0 (the CI pin), sequential runs under thirty-minute caps (log preserved from the run):</p> <ul> <li><code>scan_line_never_panics</code>: started 04:04:05, cap fired 04:34:05, <strong>no verdict</strong>: thirty minutes buys nothing locally either.</li> <li><code>form_and_mangle_hits_are_classified_by_the_table</code>: started 04:34:05, killed at the one-minute mark to free the source for the fix. The <code>FAILED</code> line the kill left in the log is an artifact, not a counterexample: the harness asserts are the matcher's push conditions restated, so a genuine failure is semantically impossible; a killed solver exits nonzero and the truncated output parsed as a verdict. GitHub's own timing is this harness's measurement: six hours, cancelled.</li> <li><code>hits_are_word_bounded</code>: never started; GitHub's six-hour cancellation is its measurement.</li> </ul> <p>The design is identical under every one of these numbers: the composition, not any single harness, is what six hours cannot buy.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0103-open-issue-sweep-the-superset-eleven-issues-simplest-first"><a class="header" href="#plan0103-open-issue-sweep-the-superset-eleven-issues-simplest-first">plan/0103 open-issue sweep: the superset, eleven issues, simplest first</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: cut 2026-10-28, in build</strong> (operator-directed: "please examine the superset of open issues. let's fix the generator emits milestone siblings.</li> <li><strong>lint#32 (medium-large)</strong>: plan/0102 executes: pure per-word classifier and word-run extraction, word-level proofs at n at most 10, unwind bounds everywhere, v0.23.1.</li> <li><strong>lc#33 (medium-large)</strong>: an <code>--inapplicable</code> recorded claim; the check reports a named disclosure, never a permanent HAZARD; the spine calls Actions a reference lane.</li> <li><strong>lc#30 (large)</strong>: a release-asset receipt digest, reconciled offline by <code>software --check</code>, plus the static workflow scan (no staged bundle, or a CARGO_HOME override).</li> <li><strong>host#27 (large)</strong>: <code>tasks --new</code> title validation, a measured STE-style subset in host-grammar, <code>mint_name</code>/<code>rule_comment</code> MCP tools in host-lint.</li> <li><strong>host#26 (ruled)</strong>: close the /goal half citing plan/0101; the OpenCode plugin is its own future milestone, recorded here as deferred, not cut.</li> <li><strong>host#18 (largest, last)</strong>: plan/0075 executes: the reviewed host-reconcile design, go/no-go, build ungated.</li> </ol> <h2 id="status-2026-10-28-end-of-the-first-working-session"><a class="header" href="#status-2026-10-28-end-of-the-first-working-session">Status (2026-10-28, end of the first working session)</a></h2> <p>Done and closed: #28, lc#34 (v0.61.1), lc#32 (v0.61.2), lc#31 (v0.61.3 plus the 9a0f7d0 ledger entry), host#25 (v0.61.4), lc#33 (v0.61.5 plus 7ef379e), and host#26 (closed citing plan/0101, the plugin deferred by ruling). The embed-equality and publish debts the gates now hazard are exactly the next two releases' cargo.</p> <h2 id="constraints"><a class="header" href="#constraints">Constraints</a></h2> <p>One release cascade per lifecycle issue (six). An unpushed pin halts the sweep with a report. Credentials never committed. Every issue closes with a comment citing its release and run URLs. The sweep ends with <code>software --check</code> and the ci receipts green, plan/0103 completed, MEMORY appended.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0102-diagnose-the-three-stuck-harnesses-timed-locally-2026-10-28"><a class="header" href="#plan0102-diagnose-the-three-stuck-harnesses-timed-locally-2026-10-28">plan/0102 diagnose: the three stuck harnesses, timed locally (2026-10-28)</a></h1> <p>Kani 0.67.0 (the CI-pinned version), one harness per run, <code>--output-format terse</code>, a 600-second cap, on this machine (WSL, the crate at its pin 90a0d71):</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Harness</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>scan_line_never_panics</code></td><td>no conclusion; killed at the 600 s cap</td></tr> <tr><td><code>hits_are_word_bounded</code></td><td>no conclusion; killed at the 600 s cap</td></tr> <tr><td><code>form_and_mangle_hits_are_classified_by_the_table</code></td><td>no conclusion; killed at the cap (run stopped early, the first two establish the shape)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>None of the three concludes in ten minutes locally, consistent with the CI record (each dies at GitHub's six-hour ceiling) and with stage zero's diagnosis: the verification condition spans the whole matcher, and the harnesses build a symbolic-length <code>Vec<u8></code> byte by byte, heap <code>String</code>s per word and per hit, and run the thirteen-entry table over symbolically derived words, with no unwind bounds declared anywhere.</p> <p>The decomposition follows plan/0102 as cut: pure per-word classifier and word-run extraction, word-level proofs at n at most 10 (full table coverage including <code>lemuselves</code>), framing properties split per-property at reduced length, an explicit <code>#[kani::unwind(K)]</code> on every harness, one matrix row each.</p> <p>Operational note: <code>timeout 600 cargo kani ... | tail</code> does not return at the cap: the solver children survive the SIGTERM and hold the pipe, so <code>rc</code> read tail's and <code>elapsed</code> printed only after the children drained. Time the kani process directly next round.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0102-diagnose-why-the-lem-harnesses-hung-found-by-bisection-2026-10-28"><a class="header" href="#plan0102-diagnose-why-the-lem-harnesses-hung-found-by-bisection-2026-10-28">plan/0102 diagnose: why the lem harnesses hung, found by bisection (2026-10-28)</a></h1> <p>The controlled experiments, each a minimal harness on the same stack (Kani 0.67.0 / CBMC 6.8.0, this machine):</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Harness</th><th>Input</th><th>Result</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>verify_review_code_accepts_hash_digit</code> (calibration)</td><td>1 symbolic byte</td><td>SUCCESS in 21 s</td></tr> <tr><td><code>vec_alloc_smoke</code></td><td>1 symbolic byte through <code>Vec::push</code></td><td>SUCCESS in 13 s</td></tr> <tr><td><code>str_eq_smoke</code></td><td>1 symbolic byte through <code>str</code> equality</td><td>SUCCESS in 19 s</td></tr> <tr><td><code>classify_concrete_smoke</code> (unwind 4)</td><td>fully concrete content</td><td>FAILED in 22 s: unwinding assertion (the table loop needs more than 4)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>classify_concrete_smoke</code> (unwind 16)</td><td>fully concrete content</td><td>NO CONCLUSION in 5 minutes</td></tr> <tr><td><code>exact_word_..._n1</code></td><td>1 symbolic byte through the classifier</td><td>NO CONCLUSION in 10 minutes</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The classifier on fully concrete input hanging the solver isolated the cost to the code shape, and the construct was <code>word[..3].eq_ignore_ascii_case("lem")</code>: a str range slice reaches the panicking-slice machinery, and that is what the solver drowns in. Replaced with explicit ASCII byte comparisons, the concrete control passes at once. With the slice gone, the remaining failures became legible unwinding assertions (a 13-entry table walk needs more than <code>unwind(12)</code>), fixed by <code>unwind(24)</code> everywhere. <code>exact_word_..._n6</code> then concluded: SUCCESS in 9 m 19 s.</p> <p>What did not help, recorded so nobody re-tries it: <code>from_utf8_unchecked</code> (no change; the validation was not the cost), the heap-free classifier shape (correct to keep anyway, but not the cause), <code>--no-slice-formula</code> (not a CBMC 6.8 flag; the kani flag hung), and concrete-vs-symbolic length (necessary for legibility, not sufficient without the slice fix).</p> <p>The landed shape: one harness per concrete length (a symbolic length across monomorphized copies is one enormous VC), <code>unwind(24)</code> on every harness, the classifier filling a fixed <code>[LemKind; 5]</code>, and the byte-level prefix. The lem-table and line-framing worst cases did not conclude inside 20-minute local caps; the tag run over the 22-row matrix is the acceptance.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="host27-measurement-the-name-verb-register-taken-from-the-corpus-2026-10-28"><a class="header" href="#host27-measurement-the-name-verb-register-taken-from-the-corpus-2026-10-28">host#27 measurement: the name-verb register, taken from the corpus (2026-10-28)</a></h1> <p>Harvest: every <code>### <title> {#anchor}</code> task heading in <code>plan/*/README.md</code>, first word lowercased, counted. The corpus speaks for itself:</p> <ul> <li>Verb-led titles exist and repeat: release (14), write (11 with compounds), implement (4), add (4), gather (3), validate (3), settle (3), update (2), re-pin (2), rule (2).</li> <li>Noun-led titles are the majority (the, cast, a, this, adversarial, fen, spine, msg-lane, ...): the imperative rule must not NAK them, so the ruling fires on the first word only when it is a <em>measured non-approved verb</em> or a numeral, never on mere non-membership.</li> </ul> <p>So the register encodes two measured lists, not the licensed ASD-STE100 set:</p> <ul> <li>APPROVED: the verbs measured above, plus the goal verbs the house already ships (set, park, unpark, complete, install, show).</li> <li>NAKED, with alternatives: the live case the issue records, <code>drive</code> to <code>run</code> (2026-10-19, the anchor that went <code>#dogfood-loop</code> to <code>#run-the-loop</code> in an hour). The list grows by measurement, one collision at a time, the same way a LEXICON declaration lands.</li> </ul> <p>The same measurement rules out a regex for "imperative": without a POS layer the ruling keys on the measured lists, which is exactly how the house wants a word list to behave.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="plan0104-the-wire-gate-becomes-a-component-host-voice"><a class="header" href="#plan0104-the-wire-gate-becomes-a-component-host-voice">plan/0104 the wire gate becomes a component: host-voice</a></h1> <p><strong>Status: cut 2026-10-29, queued</strong> (operator ruling 2026-10-29, the plan/0089 carries ruled: the promotion begins as its own milestone, and the lem lane's flag tier is confirmed in the same breath)</p> <h2 id="why-24"><a class="header" href="#why-24">Why</a></h2> <p>The wire gate (plan/0091's <code>lemgate.py</code>, certified at occurrence below 0.005 with gate v3) still lives inside plan/0091's directory. page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="reserve-agentic-host-for-this-repository-scrub-the-collision-by-a-one-time-history-rewrite"><a class="header" href="#reserve-agentic-host-for-this-repository-scrub-the-collision-by-a-one-time-history-rewrite">Reserve <code>agentic-host</code> for this repository; scrub the collision by a one-time history rewrite</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: instance</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-16</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p><code>agentic-host</code> was used two ways: as the name of <em>this repository</em> and as the generic <em>kind</em> a consumer builds. The collision leaked this repository's identity into the methodology a consumer adopts, and the <code>.agentic-host</code> stamp and the <code>template-agentic-host</code> name carried the same ambiguity into shipped software. An ambiguous name in the artifacts a consumer receives is a consumer-facing defect, not a cosmetic one. This repository is meta (adopter-zero); consumers do not see this repository's <code>call/</code> decisions, so the fix had to land in the software itself.</p> <h2 id="decision-outcome"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong><code>agentic-host</code> names <em>this repository</em> exclusively</strong>, the project that develops <code>host</code> and the <code>host-*</code> tooling.</li> <li><strong>A repo that adopts the methodology is "an agentic project"</strong> (e.g. <code>agentic-acme</code>). Two clean namespaces: <code>agentic-*</code> for <strong>projects</strong> (this repo, plus adopters), <code>host-*</code> for the methodology's <strong>reusable artifacts</strong>.</li> <li><strong>Structural renames:</strong> <code>template-agentic-host</code> to <strong><code>host-template</code></strong> (the scaffold is a methodology artifact, not a project, so it leaves the <code>agentic-*</code> namespace), and the <code>.agentic-host</code> stamp to <strong><code>.host</code></strong> (joining the <code>.host-*</code> config family).</li> <li><strong>Applied as a one-time, archive-first, map-only history rewrite</strong> across all four repos (<code>host</code>, <code>host-lifecycle</code>, <code>host-template</code>, <code>agentic-host</code>); the sanctioned exception to history-immutability. The literal map: <code>template-agentic-host ==> host-template</code>, <code>.agentic-host ==> .host</code>. Nothing outside the map changed byte-for-byte in history.</li> <li><strong>Prose was forward-only</strong> ("an agentic host" to "an agentic project", with a bracketed example on first mention; this repository named <code>agentic-host</code>; the word "forge" banned). Prose is context-dependent (the same phrase meant this repository in some files and the kind in others), so it could not be a history substitution. Legitimate "agentic" usages were preserved: <em>agentic tells</em> (host-lint's domain), <em>agentic LLM</em> (Wren), <em>agentic development</em>, and <code>Agentic-MCP-Win32s</code> (a correctly-named adopter).</li> <li><strong>Archive:</strong> an <code>archive/pre-host-rename</code> tag on every repo preserves the pre-rewrite tip verbatim. <code>host</code>'s <code>v0.1.0</code> and <code>host-lifecycle</code>'s <code>v0.4.1</code> were retagged onto the scrubbed commits.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences"><a class="header" href="#consequences">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: the methodology a consumer receives no longer carries this repository's name; <code>agentic-*</code> (projects) vs <code>host-*</code> (artifacts) is a clean dichotomy.</li> <li>Cost: every pre-rewrite SHA is invalid; any existing clone must re-fetch. The archive tags make the old state recoverable.</li> <li>This is a forge-only record. The consumer-facing half (the <code>agentic-*</code> / <code>host-*</code> vocabulary) lives in <code>host-template</code>'s own docs, where consumers read it.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="parallelizing-the-prose-scan-escalates-run-accumulation-to-the-timing-lane"><a class="header" href="#parallelizing-the-prose-scan-escalates-run-accumulation-to-the-timing-lane">Parallelizing the prose scan escalates run-accumulation to the timing lane</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-18</li> <li>Scope: host-grammar</li> <li>Relates: <code>call/0002</code> (verification lanes by property type, invokes its escalation bridge); <code>plan/0007</code> (the prose-tell engine being parallelized); <code>plan/0008</code> (the milestone that implements this).</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-1"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-1">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p><code>plan/0007</code> shipped the prose-tell engine (<code>host-grammar::scan_prose</code>) as a single sequential pass. For large documents we want to parallelize it. The lexical and per-sentence tells are embarrassingly parallel, but three equations accumulate state <strong>across</strong> sentences (anaphora, countdown, listicle) so a run can straddle a chunk boundary. A chunked-parallel scan must therefore reconcile boundary runs and assemble output in document order while K workers complete in <strong>arbitrary order</strong>.</p> <p><code>call/0002</code> reserves the TLA+/Specula lane strictly for timing and concurrency ("for all interleavings") and routes functional invariants to allium. The question: does the parallel scan stay in allium's lane, or does it cross the escalation bridge into Specula's?</p> <h2 id="decision-5"><a class="header" href="#decision-5">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>The parallel scan splits across both lanes; the worker-completion ordering crosses the bridge into the Specula/TLA+ lane.</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>allium lane (functional).</strong> The merge of per-chunk run summaries is an associative monoid; <code>parallel(split) == sequential</code> for all sentence sequences and all split points. This is a "for all inputs" property, verified by property-based testing in host-grammar.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Specula lane (temporal/interleaving).</strong> K workers complete in any order and their partial results are assembled into one ordered output. The invariant (<em>for every completion interleaving, the assembled output is identical and in document order</em>), plus liveness (every worker joins; no chunk is dropped), is a "for all interleavings" property that property-based testing cannot exhaustively explore. This is exactly the bridge condition in <code>call/0002</code>, so it escalates. A TLA+ spec model-checks it with TLC.</p> </li> </ul> <p>This is a software decision about <code>host-grammar</code>, not a methodology change (anti-ouroboros): it applies <code>call/0002</code>'s existing rule, it does not amend it.</p> <h2 id="consequences-1"><a class="header" href="#consequences-1">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: the bridge is exercised for the first time with a concrete, honest trigger; TLA+ is used on its home ground, not as a general requirements tool.</li> <li>Good: the two lanes stay complementary; PBT proves the merge math, TLC proves the interleaving safety/liveness; neither subsumes the other.</li> <li>Cost: a TLA+ spec and a TLC run join the milestone's obligations, and (per the milestone decision) TLC is wired into CI, which adds a Java/tla2tools dependency to the pipeline.</li> <li>Constraint: the implementation must keep workers free of shared mutable state (each returns an owned summary; the merge is sequential), so the model the spec checks matches the code.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="discharge-is-re-derivation-in-a-pinned-toolchain-not-a-signed-attestation-enforcement-is-project-pluggable"><a class="header" href="#discharge-is-re-derivation-in-a-pinned-toolchain-not-a-signed-attestation-enforcement-is-project-pluggable">Discharge is re-derivation in a pinned toolchain, not a signed attestation; enforcement is project-pluggable</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-20</li> <li>Scope: host-prove, host-lifecycle (the verification toolchain)</li> <li>Supersedes: <code>call/0016</code> (the CI-signed ed25519 attestation token).</li> <li>Relates: <code>call/0002</code> (verification lanes by property type); <code>plan/0023</code> (the verification ladder + host-prove's version+SHA256-pinned proof toolchains); <code>plan/0024</code> (the milestone, now shrunk to this); connollydavid/host #8 (discharge is name-presence), #9 (bound dropped). Generalizes the reproducible-build mechanism already shipping (<code>.host-software</code>'s <code>artifact = … <sha256></code> + <code>toolchain = …@sha256</code>, re-derived by <code>software --verify-build</code> <strong>in the recorded container</strong>, host#14) so it also covers proofs, not only builds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-2"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-2">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p><code>call/0016</code> fixed #8 (discharge was <code>src.contains(name)</code>, name-presence, not a real PASS) with a CI-signed ed25519 attestation token, verified offline. Two fatal problems surfaced:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Key management is a deal-breaker for adopters.</strong> host-lifecycle is one shared binary, so a baked-in public key can't serve every adopter, and a shared keypair would let any adopter forge any other's tokens. Each adopter would need its own keypair, an operator-managed CI secret, and an integrity anchor (branch protection) for the public key: a fragile, human-rooted burden the methodology cannot make mechanical.</li> <li><strong>It complicates parallel checkouts.</strong> Per-project secrets and committed <code>.att</code> files in every worktree do not compose with the bare-store/parallel-worktree model.</li> </ul> <p>And the fallback "CI-green is the discharge" <strong>overfits GitHub</strong> (required status checks). The methodology must not depend on GitHub, or any specific CI.</p> <p>The principle <code>AVAILABLE ≠ DISCHARGED</code> (a rung discharges only on a real PASS) is right. Only the mechanism for carrying "a real PASS happened" into a later check needs replacing.</p> <h2 id="decision-6"><a class="header" href="#decision-6">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>An obligation discharges only by RE-DERIVING in its recorded pinned toolchain (checkable by anyone, anywhere), not by a signed token and not by any specific CI being green.</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Builds</strong> re-derive in the recorded <code>toolchain</code> container and must reproduce the recorded <code>artifact</code> sha256 (host#14, <code>software --verify-build</code>). A stub source yields a different hash.</li> <li><strong>Proofs</strong> re-run in host-prove's <strong>version+SHA256-pinned proof toolchain</strong> (apalache / kani / tlaps, plan/0023) via <code>obligations --prove</code>, and must PASS at the declared bound. A stub / failing / <code>THEOREM X == TRUE</code> proof fails the re-run.</li> <li><strong>Re-derivation runs anywhere</strong>: a developer's machine, any CI, a pre-push hook, a cron. The authority is the <em>pinned re-derivation</em>, never the platform that runs it.</li> <li><strong>The offline hook does only cheap structural checks</strong>: a name-presence <strong>lint</strong> (the named target exists, honest about being a lint, not the discharge) + <strong>input-digest staleness</strong> (<code>git hash-object</code> of the consumed inputs; a change since the recorded discharge ⇒ HAZARD).</li> <li><strong>Enforcement is project-pluggable.</strong> That re-derivation <em>ran and passed</em> before "done" / release is enforced by whatever a project has: a required status check (GitHub), a pipeline (any CI), a pre-push hook, or operator discipline via the <code>verify</code> lifecycle phase. The methodology prescribes the <strong>act</strong> (run <code>verify</code> before declaring done / releasing) and ships the <strong>re-deriver</strong> (<code>host-lifecycle</code>); the enforcement <strong>mechanism</strong> is the project's choice.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-hash-artifacts-a-local-build-gives-us-and-their-limits"><a class="header" href="#what-hash-artifacts-a-local-build-gives-us-and-their-limits">What hash artifacts a local build gives us (and their limits)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Artifact sha256</strong> (<code>.host-software</code>) discharges <em>build reproducibility</em>, unforgeable in the useful sense (any written hash is checked by rebuilding in the pinned toolchain).</li> <li><strong>Input digests</strong> (<code>git hash-object</code>) give offline <em>staleness</em>, a cheap honest-drift catcher (a determined agent can re-record the hash, but still faces the re-run). Not a forgery gate.</li> <li><strong>A proof's PASS is a boolean from running the verifier, not a blob to hash</strong>, so proofs re-run (cheaply, in the pinned proof toolchain); they are not hashed. (Proof certificates exist but are out of scope, over-engineering.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-2"><a class="header" href="#consequences-2">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>No keys, no secrets, no <code>.att</code>, no signer, no per-project key management, no parallel- checkout friction, no CI overfit.</strong> plan/0024 collapses to: reframe #8 (discharge = re-derivation), <code>obligations --prove</code> re-runs in the pinned toolchain checking PASS + bound (#9), input-digest staleness, and the small #10/#11/#12/#13 fixes. host-prove keeps its pinned toolchains + verdict/bound parser (an agent-UX aid); <strong>no crypto on any path</strong>.</li> <li><strong><code>AVAILABLE ≠ DISCHARGED</code> / <code>BUILT ≠ RELEASED</code> survive</strong>, discharge is still a real PASS, now proven by re-derivation rather than a signature.</li> <li><strong>Honest irreducible limit:</strong> a project with <em>no</em> enforcement (no CI, no hook, no discipline) can still self-assert locally; the methodology can ship the re-deriver but cannot force a project to run it (the same limit as "you can skip your own tests"). The <code>verify</code> phase + a receipt (<code>plan/0025</code>) make <em>not</em> running it visible, not impossible.</li> <li><strong>Property-triviality stays out of scope</strong> (a vacuous proof re-derives as PASS), a review concern, not mechanizable, exactly as <code>call/0016</code> already noted.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>CI-signed ed25519 token</strong> (<code>call/0016</code>, superseded): per-adopter key management is a deal-breaker; complicates parallel checkouts.</li> <li><strong>CI-green as the authority</strong>: overfits GitHub / a specific CI; the methodology must stay platform-agnostic.</li> <li><strong>A committed plaintext result marker</strong>: forgeable by the agent (it edits the file); relocates #8, does not fix it.</li> <li><strong>Re-run the heavy verifier in the commit hook</strong>: breaks the fast/offline hook; re-derivation belongs in the heavy <code>verify</code> lane, not the hook.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="literal-tell-citations-live-in-a-host-lintignore-fenced-block-never---no-verify"><a class="header" href="#literal-tell-citations-live-in-a-host-lintignore-fenced-block-never---no-verify">Literal tell-citations live in a <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fenced block, never <code>--no-verify</code></a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-20</li> <li>Scope: host-lint (the <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fenced-block skip) and agentic-host's authored docs (the literal-citation disposition).</li> <li>Relates to: <code>call/0006</code> (the sanctioned-vocabulary allowlist), <code>call/0009</code> (exclude the generated record from the audit), <code>CLAUDE.md</code> §0 (host-lint is the hygiene lane).</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-3"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-3">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>The host <em>develops</em> host-lint, so its own authored content legitimately cites tell-shaped tokens: decision records explain detection by naming the token classes they handle, and <code>PLAN.md</code> carries a mandated retired-ordinal dictionary (old name to content name, kept for reading history). <code>call/</code> is intentionally linted, and that caught a <em>real</em> ordinal tell that had hidden in a decision record. But the recurring legitimate citations were being committed with <code>git commit --no-verify</code>, a blanket bypass that defeats the lane: it is exactly how the real tell slipped in unnoticed. Excluding whole files via <code>.host-lintignore</code> is no safer; it mutes any <em>future</em> real tell in those files. We need an exclusion that is line-precise, explicit, visible in the source, and that cannot silently hide a real tell.</p> <h2 id="decision-outcome-1"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-1">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>A tell-shaped token in linted host content is legitimate only if it is a real tracker reference (the <code>closes</code>/<code>fixes</code> traceability allowlist) or a declared LEXICON entry; anything else is a violation and is reworded out. For the residual case, literal <em>reference</em> content that must reproduce old tokens for history (the retired-ordinal dictionary, an archived citation), that content goes in a fenced code block whose info string is <strong><code>host-lint:ignore</code></strong>:</p> <pre><code>```host-lint:ignore <literal reference content, reproduced verbatim> ``` </code></pre> <p>host-lint's naming scan skips such a block; its prose scan already skips every fenced block. Why this form:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Idiomatic markdown.</strong> It is the mermaid / PlantUML info-string pattern, a plain fenced block to a renderer, and a meaningful "this is excluded literal reference data" to a reader. No bolted-on HTML-comment pragma, no out-of-band config.</li> <li><strong>Explicit, never blanket.</strong> Only a block <em>tagged</em> <code>host-lint:ignore</code> is skipped; a regular code block and all prose stay linted. The exemption is always a deliberate, reviewable act, the "excluded, not bypassed, validated" rule, now self-documenting at the point of use.</li> <li><strong>Inline stays linted.</strong> Only fenced <em>blocks</em> are skipped, never inline backticks, so a tell cannot be laundered by inline-quoting it; it must be reworded.</li> <li><strong>Region-precise, drift-proof.</strong> It bounds exactly the fenced lines, with no line numbers to rot.</li> </ul> <p><code>git commit --no-verify</code> is retired for record-layer commits: the legitimate cases are now handled (a tracker reference, a LEXICON entry, or a <code>host-lint:ignore</code> block), and everything else is a real tell to fix. The lane is never bypassed.</p> <h2 id="consequences-3"><a class="header" href="#consequences-3">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: the host's own docs self-audit clean with no bypass; the gate is honest.</li> <li>Good: a future real tell in prose still flags; a tell moved into a <code>host-lint:ignore</code> block is a visible, reviewable change in the diff, not a silent mute.</li> <li>Cost: a small host-lint feature (the naming scan learns the info string) and a one-time cleanup (wrap the dictionary, reword the violations, retire the <code>--no-verify</code> rule).</li> <li>Builds on <code>call/0006</code> (an allowlist for legitimate vocabulary) and <code>call/0009</code> (exclude the generated record): this is the third escape, literal reference <em>citations</em>, and the strictest, because it is per-block and visible.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="the-host--family-is-software-developed-here-embedded-as-where-room-components"><a class="header" href="#the-host--family-is-software-developed-here-embedded-as-where-room-components">The host-* family is software developed here, embedded as Where-room components</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-21</li> <li>Scope: host-lint, host-lifecycle, host-prove, host-grammar (the host-* software family) and agentic-host's <code>.host-software</code> composition</li> <li>Relates to: <code>call/0010</code> (the <code>.host-software</code> Where-room recipe), <code>call/0013</code> (reserve agentic-host for this repository), <code>call/0017</code> (every phase emits a receipt, the <code>recurring-per-component</code> machinery), <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> ("the Where room is the software under test, one or more components").</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-4"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-4">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>agentic-host is the development host for the <strong>whole</strong> host-* family (host-lint, host-lifecycle, host-prove, host-grammar), not just host-lint. The planning (<code>plan/</code>, <code>call/</code>, <code>MEMORY.md</code>) and the worktrees for all of them live here, and their code is authored here.</p> <p>Each host-* artifact wears two hats at once:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Developed software</strong>: its own repo (<code>connollydavid/host-*</code>), its own test suite and <strong>CI</strong> (<code>ci.yml</code>), its own co-located specs, its own version/tag/release lifecycle. The <em>producer</em> identity.</li> <li><strong>Methodology tooling</strong>: agentic-host (and any adopter) consumes a pinned version to operate or verify the methodology: host-lint as the hygiene hook, host-lifecycle as the lifecycle driver, host-prove as the deep-rung verifier. The <em>consumer</em> identity.</li> </ol> <p>The residency was inconsistent: <strong>host-lint</strong> is a <code>.host-software</code> Where component (developed here, its built binary and skill served from the worktree), while <strong>host-lifecycle</strong> and <strong>host-prove</strong> sit under <code>tools/</code> as referenced submodules, and <strong>host-grammar</strong> is a git-dep library. That asymmetry, an accident of host-lint being "first," not a principled line, led to a false "tooling vs Where-room software" binary: a conclusion that <code>host-lifecycle release host-lifecycle</code> "cannot resolve" and that embedding a tool as a Where component would be a category error. It is not. The methodology already supports <strong>more than one software-under-development per host</strong>: <code>.host-software</code> is explicitly "one or more components", agentic-host already carries two (<code>host-lint</code> + <code>host</code>), and the receipt machinery's <code>embed</code>/<code>release</code> are <code>recurring-per-component</code>.</p> <h2 id="decision-outcome-2"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-2">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p><strong>agentic-host is a multi-software development host.</strong> Everything <code>host-*</code> is software <em>developed here</em> and is embedded as a <code>.host-software</code> <strong>Where-room component</strong>: host-lint (already), host-lifecycle, host-prove, host-grammar. Each is released through the lifecycle orchestration (<code>host-lifecycle release <component></code>) and emits its receipt in the project ledger, while keeping its own producer CI and release in its own repo. Its tooling function is served from its Where worktree (built binary + worktree-sourced skills), the host-lint model.</p> <p>The clean line:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>tools/</code></strong> holds only genuinely <strong>external</strong> referenced verification tools: <strong>allium</strong> (JUXT), <strong>specula</strong>. "Reference, don't vendor" governs an <em>adopter</em> consuming tools; it does not govern the <em>development host</em> that builds them.</li> <li><strong><code>.host-software</code></strong> holds the software developed here, the whole host-* family.</li> </ul> <p>The split identity is honored by a <strong>lightweight</strong> boundary (each tool's own repo, CI, and release/version); giving each tool its own agentic project is <strong>not</strong> required. agentic-host stays the <em>single</em> development host for a coupled family (host-grammar is a shared build dependency of host-lint and host-lifecycle; the roadmap is one). Fragmenting into a project per tool would leave agentic-host "responsible only for host-template", over-separation that dissolves a real strength.</p> <h2 id="considered-options"><a class="header" href="#considered-options">Considered options</a></h2> <ul> <li><em><em>Each host-</em> tool as its own agentic project</em>* (own <code>cast/</code>/<code>call/</code>/<code>plan/</code>/<code>.host</code>). Rejected: the producer identity needs only own-repo + CI + release, not full methodology ceremony per tool; N projects fragment one coupled roadmap and multiply operational cost for one developer.</li> <li><strong>Status quo</strong>: host-* tools stay <code>tools/</code> submodules, released ad-hoc. Rejected: it rests on the false tools-vs-software binary, blocks dogfooding <code>release</code> on the tools, and is asymmetric with host-lint for no principled reason.</li> <li><strong>Embed the family as Where components of one multi-software development host</strong> (chosen): uniform with host-lint, makes <code>release <component></code> resolve, and reuses the <code>recurring-per-component</code> machinery already built.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-4"><a class="header" href="#consequences-4">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>host-lifecycle, host-prove, host-grammar stop being <code>tools/</code> submodule / git-dep references and become <code>.host-software</code> Where components (see <code>plan/0028</code>); <code>tools/</code> then holds only allium + specula.</li> <li>The skill-wiring mechanism (<code>link-skills.sh</code>, which symlinks <code>tools/*/skills/*</code>) must also wire a Where component's skills from its worktree, the host-lint pattern, generalized to multi-skill components.</li> <li>host-grammar is a library (no deployable artifact): it releases tag-only, and its dependents (host-lint, host-lifecycle) keep their git-rev dependency pinned to its released tag (closing the current unpinned-host-grammar gap in host-lifecycle's manifest).</li> <li>The general pattern, <em>a development host embeds the tools it develops as Where software, an adopter references them</em>, may warrant a spine clarification in <code>host-template</code>; that is a separate follow-up, not this project-scoped decision.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="the-host--static-musl-releases-build-hermetically-against-a-pinned-dependency-bundle"><a class="header" href="#the-host--static-musl-releases-build-hermetically-against-a-pinned-dependency-bundle">The host-* static-musl releases build hermetically against a pinned dependency bundle</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-22</li> <li>Scope: host-lint, host-lifecycle, host-prove (the artifact-bearing Where-room software)</li> <li>Relates: the spine MUST authored in <code>host-template</code> (<code>ecce498</code>, the methodology home for "a component shipping static release binaries reproduces them offline from pinned inputs"); <code>plan/0032</code> (the milestone); <code>plan/0028</code> (the <code>GLIBC_2.39</code> divergence this retires); <code>call/0010</code> (the <code>.host-software</code> recipe); <code>call/0018</code> (discharge is re-derivation in a pinned toolchain, to which this adds offline hermeticity).</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-5"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-5">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>The recorded canonical artifact for each host-* binary was a glibc-dynamic <code>target/release/<bin></code> built in <code>rust:1.95.0</code>, with the <code>host-grammar</code> git dependency and the crates.io deps fetched over the network during the build.
