Where a document is genuinely new and not ready to stage, check it with the working-tree walk instead, which is what <code>host-lint --prose <file></code> reads.</li> <li><strong>Prove a check by breaking it.</strong> For anything claimed to pass, run the mutation that should make it fail. A check that stays green when its subject is broken proved nothing.</li> <li><strong>Resolve every citation with the tool</strong> rather than typing it, because exact-token recall is a known failure at every model strength.</li> <li><strong>Leave the tree green and the working tree clean.</strong> A stop with a dirty tree is indistinguishable from a crash, and the next cold session reads debris as work in progress.</li> </ol> <h2 id="consequences-31"><a class="header" href="#consequences-31">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>The loop prepares releases and never performs one. It may build, test, verify reproduction, and stage the whole cascade; the tag, the asset, and the pin that makes bytes installable wait for the operator. This costs throughput knowingly: most fixes here reach an adopter only through a release, so the loop's output is prepared work. <ul> <li><strong>Superseded by <a href="call/0050-a-release-carries-a-resolvable-authorization.html">call/0050</a>, and left here because it described this project falsely for two sessions.</strong> The cost above was never paid; nine releases were performed while this paragraph said none would be. It also had no legal stopping point to offer: <code>release</code> writes the version bump before it prints, so "prepare and stop" means stopping with a dirty tree, which rule eighteen forbids. The loop now performs releases and every one of them is attributable.</li> </ul> </li> <li>A stop is a success. What it could not decide goes where the next session reads by default: the open question in prose under the milestone node it blocks, a <code>call/</code> at <code>Status: proposed</code> when a decision is owed, an issue on the forge, and a <code>MEMORY.md</code> entry naming both, each in its own commit.</li> <li>Prohibitions are phrased against outcomes because the probe showed that method-shaped rules leak. Any future rule added here inherits that requirement.</li> <li>This decision binds the agent, not the operator. Every act forbidden above remains ordinary operator work, and several are ordinary maintainer work in this repository specifically.</li> <li><strong>Rule fifteen was amended on the day this was accepted, by operator direction, and the reason is recorded rather than smoothed away.</strong> It first said only to gate before the outward act. Within hours the charter itself was committed on a clean verdict that meant nothing: <code>prose</code> reads the recorded corpus, the file was still untracked, and the gate never opened it. A warning surfaced once the file was tracked and blocked the next release. Rule three would have this appended rather than edited; the rule list is an operating text that has to be followed in one reading, so it was amended in place and the amendment declared here. That is the operator's call to make and not the loop's.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0050-a-release-carries-a-resolvable-authorization"><a class="header" href="#call0050-a-release-carries-a-resolvable-authorization">call/0050: a release carries a resolvable authorization</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: every release cascade in this repository and its components; what makes one permitted, and what the record has to show afterwards</li> <li>Date: 2026-07-28</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-9"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-9">Context and problem</a></h2> <p><a href="call/0049-the-unattended-charter.html">call/0049</a> rule one forbids the loop making anything permanent: no tag, no release asset, no pin that makes bytes installable. Its Consequences state the position plainly ("the loop prepares releases and never performs one") and cost it knowingly.</p> <p>Across two working sessions the loop performed nine releases (host-lifecycle v0.47.0 through v0.47.2, host-lint v0.16.2 through v0.16.6). Each had the operator's approval, spoken in a session window that no longer exists. So the rule stood on the books while practice ignored it, and the record cannot show either fact.</p> <p>Three separate findings say the rule rather than the compliance is the defect.</p> <p><strong>The rule is phrased against an actor.</strong> <a href="call/0049-the-unattended-charter.html">call/0049</a> established that a prohibition phrased against a <em>method</em> leaks and one phrased against an <em>outcome</em> holds. Rule one is phrased against neither: "the loop may not" is answered by "the operator told me to," and the loop adjudicates its own actorhood mid-run. Its Scope says <em>any autonomous run</em>, and an attended session where the operator answers in the moment is arguably not one. That leaves two defensible readings of the charter's own first rule, which is rule twelve firing on the document that contains it.</p> <p><strong>There is no legal place to stop.</strong> <code>release</code> writes the version bump into the worktree before it prints anything, so "prepare and stop" means stopping with a dirty tree, the state rule eighteen exists to forbid. The obvious repair, letting the loop commit and push and stop before the tag, does not work either: a pushed commit cannot be amended, so the "reversible" half already contains an act rule two treats as permanent.</p> <p><strong>The record is silent in both directions.</strong> The release receipt carries <code>disposition</code>, <code>evidence</code>, <code>tool</code> and <code>recorded</code>, and no field naming who authorized it. A cold auditor can find neither a violation nor a compliant run. The gap under-reports, which is the failure this project has closed twice elsewhere.</p> <p>There is a fourth fact, and it reframes the other three. The tool has never been able to perform an outward act: no <code>git tag</code>, no <code>git push</code>, no <code>gh release</code> appears anywhere in host-lifecycle's source. <code>release</code> bumps, rebuilds, verifies reproduction, and then <strong>prints</strong> the outward steps. The boundary the doctrine describes was already drawn in code, and the loop walked around it by running git by hand.</p> <h2 id="how-this-was-decided-1"><a class="header" href="#how-this-was-decided-1">How this was decided</a></h2> <p>The four textual personas were convened on the question and returned ranked ballots under an adversarial constraint: attack your own top choice before ranking it. The fifth was driven as the real weak model, and used as this project uses it, as an acceptance test rather than a lens.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>ballot</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Mara</td><td>C > A > B, conditioned on a recorded authorization and on closing the scope ambiguity</td></tr> <tr><td>Wren</td><td>D > A > C > B</td></tr> <tr><td>Bly</td><td>D > C > A > B</td></tr> <tr><td>Orin</td><td>D > A > C > B</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The options were: <strong>A</strong>, a delegation form recorded per release; <strong>B</strong>, hold the line as written; <strong>C</strong>, split the cascade by reversibility; <strong>D</strong>, build the gate first and then re-cut the rule.</p> <p>D carried three of four first preferences. Mara's C attached two conditions, the second of which is D's substance, so no ballot opposed it.</p> <p><strong>B ranked last on every ballot</strong>, and the measurement says why. The real <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> was given the complete output of a genuine release run and asked for its single next action. Under the message the tool prints today, which lists the commands beneath <code>Outward steps (operator-run):</code>, it performed an outward step in <strong>both</strong> repeats. One repeat also used the artifact hash where the commit SHA belongs, which corrupts the pin it was writing. Under a message naming the means rather than the outcome (stop, say this, hand back one command), it held in <strong>both</strong> repeats. One thing changed between the rounds.</p> <p>That is <a href="call/../plan/0071-host-install-mode/README.html">plan/0071</a>'s finding arriving at the charter: an instruction that names an outcome without naming the means leaves the means to be invented. A heading reading "operator-run" above a list of runnable commands is such an instruction, and the loop is not the only reader that fails it.</p> <h2 id="decision-34"><a class="header" href="#decision-34">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>Rule one is re-cut against the outcome: no release proceeds without a resolvable authorization recorded on its receipt.</strong> Attended and unattended stop mattering, which was the ambiguity.</p> <p>The gate, which lands before the sentence does:</p> <ul> <li><code>host-lifecycle release</code> requires <code>--authorized <ref></code> and refuses without it. Fail-closed, so forgetting blocks rather than proceeds.</li> <li>The ref resolves through the existing reference machinery to a <strong>tracked</strong> record: a <code>call/</code>, a plan node, an issue. It reuses <code>resolve</code>, and introduces no new concept.</li> <li>The release receipt carries <code>authorization</code> beside <code>evidence</code>, so the operator's go lands in a tracked file rather than in a window that closes.</li> <li><code>software --check</code> re-opens any release receipt recorded without one.</li> </ul> <p>Two constraints on that gate, both from precedent.</p> <p><strong>What gates is the authorization's absence.</strong> A field the audited party fills in is a signature on a form the signer printed, and this project has already watched an agent minute an invented "operator-authorized override" during an external migration. So nothing tests whether the authorization is honest; what is tested is that it is present and that it resolves to something in the tree. Forging it means also authoring the record it resolves to, in a commit, in history the operator reads. That converts an invisible act into an attributable one. <strong>Attribution is not prevention</strong>, and this decision claims no more than that.</p> <p><strong>Receipts predating this decision are disclosed, not re-opened.</strong> Ninety-six release receipts carry no authorization because no field existed. Hazarding on them would redden the gate over history nobody can amend, and would teach the reader to skip the line. They are reported as a counted set beside the verdict, which is the disclosure this project already applies to the record layer.</p> <p>The only control that would actually stop a determined loop is credential separation: the loop does not hold the token that can tag. That cannot ship in a copy-at-version text methodology, because it is configuration on a machine the methodology never sees. It is recorded here as a consequence, never written as a rule, because a rule no adopter's tool can check is the defect <a href="call/0046-retire-the-unimplemented-hermeticity-escape.html">call/0046</a> retired.</p> <h2 id="consequences-32"><a class="header" href="#consequences-32">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>The charter sentence lands only after the flag exists and a test fails without it. Rule six applied to this decision, whose entire subject is a rule that outran its tool.</li> <li>The loop performs releases again, and every one of them is attributable. The permission stays where it was; the record is what gains a field.</li> <li>A release now needs a tracked record to point at before it can happen, so the authorization is written before the work rather than remembered after it.</li> <li>The nine releases already performed remain unattributable. This decision does not repair them and nothing can; they are the reason the field exists.</li> <li>Credential separation stays the real lock and stays unshipped. Anyone reading this as enforcement rather than as attribution has read it wrong.</li> <li>The operator authorized this decision, and its own release cascade, by choosing to build and ship it end to end after the risk was stated: the agent authors the rule that binds the agent, and self-authorizes the release that carries it. That risk is recorded here rather than resolved, because recording it is the only honest thing available to the party it names.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0051-a-lexicon-entry-reports-a-grammar-defect"><a class="header" href="#call0051-a-lexicon-entry-reports-a-grammar-defect">call/0051: a LEXICON entry reports a grammar defect</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: the hygiene lane's shared vocabulary; what a declaration in a LEXICON means, where one may be relied on, and what the published template may carry</li> <li>Date: 2026-07-29</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-10"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-10">Context and problem</a></h2> <p><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/20">connollydavid/host#20</a> reported one word in the template's operating manual warning under the prose lane, in a repository that had adopted the spine and propagated it. The word was reworded and the adopter went green. Its closing note named a class the fix did not touch: the template's own documents are not held to the lane an adopter runs them under.</p> <p>The class is real and it is not about where that word sat in a sentence.</p> <p>The template declares its sanctioned vocabulary in a <code>LEXICON</code>, and so does this repository. Both files carry exactly one entry. It is the same word, with the same justification written out twice, reached independently. An adopter receives neither file: <code>scaffold</code> seeds a comment-only <code>LEXICON</code> with zero entries, so the spine passes its own gate here and warns in every repository it is copied into.</p> <p>That is the defect. A declaration is scoped to the repository that holds it, and the spine's text is not.</p> <h2 id="what-the-corpus-says"><a class="header" href="#what-the-corpus-says">What the corpus says</a></h2> <p>The word is <code>harness</code>. Measured over the tracked markdown and source of this repository and the template:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>count</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>total occurrences</td><td>157</td></tr> <tr><td>the verb, with an abstract object</td><td>2</td></tr> <tr><td>the noun</td><td>the remainder</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Both of the two are the <code>LEXICON</code> comments themselves, which quote the verb to explain why the noun was declared. No document in either tree uses the word as a verb at all.</p> <p>The plural was measured separately after the operator asked whether it was always a verb. It occurs 46 times and is a plural noun in every one, most often naming Kani proof harnesses and the agent harnesses an operator runs.</p> <p>So the rule caught nothing and charged 155 legitimate uses for it. The word is a term of art here, older than the register the lane detects: a test harness, a proof harness (Kani's own name for a <code>#[kani::proof]</code> function), an agent harness. Applying the spine's own operator test, whether a shape is a property of how models segment work or of this project's domain, the noun is domain and the verb is register.</p> <h2 id="what-the-source-says-and-where-this-departs-from-it"><a class="header" href="#what-the-source-says-and-where-this-departs-from-it">What the source says, and where this departs from it</a></h2> <p>The catalog was then read rather than assumed, which should have happened first. It lists the word, under the entry <code>"Delve" and Friends</code>, as one of a family of overused vocabulary. It does not qualify it by part of speech, and it does not describe a construction.</p> <p>So this decision <strong>departs from its cited source</strong> for this entry. The departure is recorded rather than dressed up as a reading of the catalog, and it rests on two things. The corpus measurement above is the first. The second is that the catalog qualifies by part of speech where a word carries a legitimate other sense: the same entry lists <code>leverage</code> as <code>(as a verb)</code>. Narrowing a word whose noun is domain vocabulary is the method the catalog already applies; applying it here is consistent with how the catalog works while differing from what it says about this word.</p> <p>Reading the catalog surfaced a larger discrepancy between it and the rule that cites it. Six of the seventeen terms this project detects (<code>realm</code>, <code>underscore</code>, <code>showcase</code>, <code>intricate</code>, <code>nuanced</code>, <code>multifaceted</code>) do not appear in the catalog at all. Two that do appear (<code>certainly</code>, <code>framework</code>) are absent here. The <code>(as a verb)</code> qualifier on <code>leverage</code> was dropped, so a financial or mechanical noun sense flags. And two separate catalog entries, the overused-vocabulary family and the grandiose-noun family, are fused into a single rule carrying one weight and one citation.</p> <p>Two parts of that discrepancy are cheap enough to settle here, because a citation is a factual claim and a wrong one should not outlive the reading that caught it. The fused rule becomes three. <code>ai-diction</code> and <code>grandiose-noun</code> each cite the catalog entry they came from; <code>house-diction</code> holds the six terms the catalog does not contain, and cites this project. A verdict then names the rule it matched, and no term can borrow a source that does not carry it. What is left open is the substantive question of whether each of those six earns its place, which needs the same corpus measurement this decision applied to one word.</p> <h2 id="the-path-that-was-not-available"><a class="header" href="#the-path-that-was-not-available">The path that was not available</a></h2> <p>Rewording every site was considered first and does not work. Two occurrences sit inside <code>UPGRADING.md</code> entries, and that file's header forbids amending one: an entry is a contract with claims already recorded against it in adopters' <code>.host-receipts</code>, and editing it can convert a correctly applied upgrade into a standing hazard on a tree its owner cannot fix. Boxing is an amendment too, and the stanzas are machine-read.</p> <p>The operator ruled out declaration and the ledger ruled out amendment, so the only remaining path was a narrower rule. The constraint and the evidence agreed.</p> <h2 id="decision-35"><a class="header" href="#decision-35">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>The bare word leaves the shared grammar; the construction stays.</strong> <code>ai-diction</code> now carries the verb with its object across four conjugations rather than the bare token. The noun clears everywhere.</p> <p><strong>A <code>LEXICON</code> entry is a report, not a settlement.</strong> Declaring a token records that the shared grammar over-fired on this corpus. It is provisional, and it is owed upstream.</p> <p><strong>The same entry in two repositories is a confirmed over-fire.</strong> Local legitimacy is local by definition, so a declaration reached independently twice is evidence about the rule rather than about either project. It is fixed in the grammar and both declarations retire. This is the existing graduation path run backwards, and it had no trigger before.</p> <p><strong>The template carries no <code>LEXICON</code>.</strong> Its text is copied into repositories that never receive the file, so a declaration there is unsound at the moment it is written. The published spine is held to the unexempted bar, and a tell-shaped token in it is reworded or the grammar is wrong.</p> <h2 id="consequences-33"><a class="header" href="#consequences-33">Consequences</a></h2> <p>Both <code>LEXICON</code> files retire in this change. Neither repository keeps a declaration to inherit, and neither keeps one to trust.</p> <p>The template's prose is now first-class on its own terms rather than on a declaration adopters do not get, which is what <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host/issues/20">connollydavid/host#20</a> asked for beyond its one word.</p> <p>The narrowing is a behaviour change in a shared dependency, so it rides the release cascade through host-grammar, host-lint, and host-lifecycle rather than landing as a documentation edit.</p> <p>Three host-lint tests used the retired token as their worked example of an over-firing term. They were first moved to <code>realm</code>, which is one of the six terms the catalog does not contain, and then to <code>paradigm</code> and <code>landscape</code>, which it does. The first move was made before the catalog was read and is the same error this decision is about, committed while recording it. The tests keep the shape they were written to prove, and that shape covers the hyphenated declared phrase that reaches the masker's word-boundary handling.</p> <p><code>paradigm</code> did not survive the session that chose it. The operator observed that <code>framework</code> is a special case with respect to software, and the observation generalises: the catalog describes prose in general, while this rule ships to software projects, where <code>framework</code>, <code>ecosystem</code> and <code>paradigm</code> each name a real thing a project builds on. All three are held out of <code>grandiose-noun</code>, which keeps <code>tapestry</code>, <code>landscape</code> and <code>synergy</code>. The evidence is the same as for the bare token, and it is stronger, because every reader of this rule is a software project by construction rather than by measurement of one corpus. The worked example the sentence above describes had used <code>the actor paradigm</code> as its instance of legitimate vocabulary while the same session held that <code>paradigm</code> had no collision to measure; the fixture was the evidence and it went unread. It now uses <code>tapestry</code>, which the catalog lists and which is also the name of a Java web framework a project may legitimately declare.</p> <p>Moving that fixture surfaced a defect in the masker, filed as <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/26">connollydavid/host-lint#26</a>: a declared phrase blanked at the start of a markdown line leaves four or more leading spaces, which the structural pass reads as an indented code block, so every tell on the line clears silently. The declaration's blast radius is the line rather than the phrase. The old fixture began with <code>The </code> and never reached it. That is a second instance of this decision's own theme, a rule whose behaviour nobody had measured at its boundary, and it is scoped to host-lint rather than to the shared grammar.</p> <p>The remaining sixteen terms are left detecting as they are. <code>showcase</code>, raised in the same session, occurs zero times in this corpus, so there is no collision to measure and narrowing it on a reading of the word would repeat the uncalibrated move that produced this defect. Its real defect is the attribution, which the reconciliation above covers rather than this decision.</p> <p>The trigger for narrowing is a measured collision. The trigger for reconciliation is a term that cannot be traced to the source it cites. They are different questions and the second is now open.</p> <h2 id="addendum-2026-09-06-plan0087-the-deferred-question-answered"><a class="header" href="#addendum-2026-09-06-plan0087-the-deferred-question-answered">Addendum (2026-09-06, plan/0087): the deferred question answered</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-host-lint:ignore"> The reconciliation left open "whether each of the six house-diction terms earns its place — needs the same corpus measurement". Measured 2026-09-06 ([plan/0087](../plan/0087-word-choice-lacuna/gather-data.md), this decision's method): every occurrence of `realm`, `underscore`, `showcase`, `intricate`, and `multifaceted` in the swept corpora is a meta-mention of the terms themselves; `nuanced`'s three genuine uses sit in an excluded record (the weak model's raw transcript). Zero over-firing evidence; the rule is inert on this corpus. The terms stay detecting, the measurement being their evidence base; narrowing on a zero-collision measurement would repeat the uncalibrated move this decision refused for `showcase`. The held-out trio's corpus reading also landed: no grandiose-sense use observed, the invitation re-read at the next word-choice milestone. The adopter corpus remains where a collision would surface, through the LEXICON report path this decision established. </code></pre> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0052-a-pin-is-reconciled-wherever-it-is-recorded"><a class="header" href="#call0052-a-pin-is-reconciled-wherever-it-is-recorded">call/0052: a pin is reconciled wherever it is recorded</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted, on the revised decision below. <strong>The Decision section further down is superseded</strong> and kept only as the record of what was first asserted; read <a href="call/0052-a-pin-is-reconciled-wherever-it-is-recorded.html#decision-revised-2026-08-03">Decision, revised</a> as the live one.</li> <li>Scope: the pin surfaces of the <code>host-*</code> family; which ones a release must reconcile, which are gated today, and which are not</li> <li>Date: 2026-07-29</li> <li>Ratified: 2026-08-03 by the operator, on the revised decision, after the four-persona convening returned unanimous revision against the first one. The operator was shown the three readings (floor-and-advisory, equality, hybrid) with their measured costs and chose the floor. Recorded here because an approval spoken in a session window is not a record (<a href="call/0050-a-release-carries-a-resolvable-authorization.html">call/0050</a>).</li> <li>History: first authored by the agent between operator turns and pushed at <code>Status: accepted</code> on a one-line instruction, which was an overreach: <a href="call/0049-the-unattended-charter.html">call/0049</a> already directs an owed decision to <code>Status: proposed</code>, and the tool treats <code>accepted</code> as a credential (only an accepted decision authorizes a skip receipt), so self-accepting minted the authority it claimed. Reopened to <code>proposed</code> at <code>a61bf546</code>. The original body is unedited throughout; the findings against it are under Revisions owed, and the answers to them are under Decision, revised.</li> <li>Relates: <a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a>, which established the invariant over the template's pin sites and is now spine-resident; <a href="call/0010-software-is-a-bare-store-with-worktrees.html">call/0010</a>, which makes <code>.host-software</code> the anchor; <a href="call/0043-each-component-self-owns-its-vendor-bundle.html">call/0043</a>, which adds the vendored copy as a further surface</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-11"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-11">Context and problem</a></h2> <p><a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a> settled that a release is finished only when every carried pin of the released tool equals the commit <code>.host-software</code> records. Its invariant is stated over one surface, the template: the <code>prose.yml</code> install rev and two submodule gitlinks. <code>software --check</code> gates exactly those sites.</p> <p>A component of this family may also depend on a sibling. <code>host-lifecycle</code> git-depends on both <code>host-grammar</code> and <code>host-lint</code> in its own <code>Cargo.toml</code>, and embeds the second as the engine its prose gate runs in process. Those revs are pin sites by every argument <a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a> makes, and no check reads them.</p> <p>Measured on the date above, before any part of the work in <a href="call/0051-a-lexicon-entry-reports-a-grammar-defect.html">call/0051</a> had landed:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>surface</th><th>records</th><th><code>.host-software</code> records</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>host-lifecycle/Cargo.toml</code> host-lint rev</td><td><code>bb16c466</code> (v0.16.0)</td><td><code>cc3ec6a</code> (v0.16.6)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Six releases apart, and <code>software --check</code> reported no hazard over it. The consequence is not cosmetic. The in-process engine decides the prose clause of the verify receipt, so the gate that closes a release and the CLI installed beside it can return different verdicts on the same file. The drift was visible only because the verdict line carries <code>[host-lint 0.16.0]</code>, a disclosure added for another purpose entirely.</p> <p>The same shape nearly shipped a false instruction. A drafted ledger entry told adopters that a host-lifecycle version embeds a reconciled rule, while the release preparing to carry it would have bumped one sibling rev and left the other at the revision holding the unreconciled rule.</p> <h2 id="decision-36"><a class="header" href="#decision-36">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>The invariant is surface-independent.</strong> Every recorded revision of a <code>host-*</code> component equals that component's <code>.host-software</code> pin, wherever it is recorded. The template's sites, a sibling's dependency revs, and a vendored copy are the same claim about the same anchor, and enumerating surfaces one at a time is what let this one sit unread.</p> <p><strong>A release reconciles every surface it touches, and the sibling revs are part of the cascade.</strong> Bumping a component that another embeds is unfinished until the embedding component records the released commit.</p> <h2 id="consequences-34"><a class="header" href="#consequences-34">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>The check does not exist yet, and the drift recorded above is live at the time of writing.</strong> This decision states the rule and records what is owed. It does not claim an implementation, because the failure this session is closing was a record that read as complete while the tree disagreed.</p> <p>Enforcement is owed as a sibling of the template-pin gate, which already reads a recorded site and compares it to the anchor. The generalized form reads each materialized component's manifest for a <code>host-*</code> git dependency and compares its rev to the recorded pin. It is mechanical and offline, over two files that both exist. The trigger is the next host-lifecycle release that touches <code>software --check</code>.</p> <p>Until it lands, the sibling revs are reconciled by hand as part of the release cascade, which is the state <a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a> describes for the template before its own gate was written.</p> <p>One surface stays out of scope here. A vendored dependency bundle carries copies of these revisions too, and it is pinned by hash rather than by commit, so the comparison is a different one. <a href="call/0043-each-component-self-owns-its-vendor-bundle.html">call/0043</a> owns that surface, and a bundle whose contents predate a sibling release is a case that decision should answer rather than this one.</p> <h2 id="revisions-owed"><a class="header" href="#revisions-owed">Revisions owed</a></h2> <p>Four personas were convened on this record and returned unanimous revision. The findings, each measured against the tree rather than argued:</p> <p><strong>The invariant is wrong in both directions.</strong> Anchored on <code>.host-software</code>, a tree uniformly one release behind satisfies it, so the surface that would have shipped a false instruction passes cleanly while both sides sit at the superseded revision. In the other direction, a consumer that has correctly taken a release violates it until the anchor moves, so the invariant is transiently false by construction in every cascade it mandates. It needs the released commit as its reference and an ordering clause saying the anchor moves first.</p> <p><strong>The owed check was scoped to one seventh of the problem.</strong> Naming "each materialized component's manifest" closes one of seven drifted tokens. Six more sit in component CI workflows, pinning this family's tools by hardcoded revision, drifted by up to thirty-two tags, read by no check.</p> <p><strong>The remedy is derivation, not comparison, and it is already committed here.</strong> Two workflows in this repository derive the revision from <code>.host-software</code> rather than hardcoding it, under a comment recording that the hardcoded form drifted and failed. A derived revision cannot drift and needs no comparator. The components never received the pattern. A surface that can be derived is retired rather than compared, and comparison is for what cannot.</p> <p><strong>The write-once surface is absent.</strong> A ledger entry's <code>requires</code> and <code>verify</code> are recorded revision claims, re-run against the adopter's tree on every gate run, and unamendable once receipts exist. It is the only pin site in this family that reconciliation-later does not reach, and it is named in this record's Context and then left out of its Decision. It is staged last, after every revision it asserts is recorded true.</p> <p><strong>Hand reconciliation is not an interim remedy.</strong> The consequences above prescribe it and cite the state that preceded the template's own gate. Measured, the drift this record documents survived nine hand-reconciled release cascades, and what caught it was a version string added to a verdict line for an unrelated purpose.</p> <p>The census of drifted sites is deliberately not reproduced here. An advisory census is a reading rather than a work queue, and a count staled by the next workflow added would answer enumeration with a longer enumeration, which is the diagnosis this record makes of itself.</p> <h2 id="decision-revised-2026-08-03"><a class="header" href="#decision-revised-2026-08-03">Decision, revised (2026-08-03)</a></h2> <p>The first decision asserted one invariant over every surface. That was the error, and it is the error the convening found from four directions at once. <strong>These surfaces carry two different claims, and the claim follows what the recorded revision determines.</strong></p> <p><strong>A manifest revision is an equality claim, because it is compiled into the artifact.</strong> A component's <code>Cargo.toml</code> git dependency on a sibling of this family becomes bytes in the binary whose hash <code>.host-software</code> records. It is therefore a claim about the anchor itself, and the anchor is its own reference. <code>host-lifecycle</code> embeds <code>host-lint</code> as the engine its prose gate runs in process, which is why the drift this record opens with was not cosmetic: the gate that closes a release and the CLI installed beside it could return different verdicts on the same file.</p> <p><strong>A CI workflow revision is a floor, because it ships to nobody.</strong> A component's CI installs a lane driver to run <code>obligations</code> over its own spec. <a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a>'s equality argument does not reach it: that argument is about <em>distribution</em>, that the template hands the tool to adopters and a stale pin there hands out a stale tool. Nothing is handed to anyone here. The pin says <em>this lane needs at least this version</em>, which is what one of the sites already said in a comment nobody had read. <code>host/install.yml</code> records v0.47.1 because an earlier host-lifecycle "reports every behavioural obligation here as missing a test, because the tests are shell rather than Rust."</p> <p><strong>The ordering is what the check reads, and it answers finding one in both directions.</strong> In the tool's own history: below the anchor is a satisfied floor, reported every run and never gating; above it is the cascade window a consumer correctly sits in after taking a release, benign by construction; outside the history is not a floor at all, because the revision names nothing reachable and the install itself would fail, so that alone gates. A uniformly stale tree no longer passes silently, because every below-anchor pin is enumerated; a correctly-updated consumer no longer fails, because ahead-of-anchor is a recognised state rather than a violation.</p> <p><strong>The anchor moves first.</strong> <code>.host-software</code> is re-pinned before the surfaces that reference it, so a cascade is a window that closes rather than a contradiction that must be argued away. On the equality surface that window is one release wide and load-bearing: re-pinning <code>host-lint</code> obliges the next <code>host-lifecycle</code> release to bump its manifest, which is precisely the reconciliation whose absence this record documents.</p> <p><strong>Why equality was rejected as the single rule, measured rather than argued.</strong> Seven CI sites across five component repositories. A component CI commit moves that worktree off its pin, and four of the five are tag-pinned, so clearing them costs four component releases <em>per host-lifecycle release</em>, none of which changes a line of component code. At the cadence this tool actually releases at, that is on the order of eighty forced releases in six weeks. That amplification is the most likely reason these sat unread for nineteen releases, so equality would have re-created the pressure that caused the defect. Against that it bought nothing behavioural: all eight sites are below the anchor and every lane passes at it, 240 obligations dispositioned across <code>host-lint</code>, <code>host-prove</code>, <code>host-grammar</code>, <code>host-reference</code> and <code>host</code>.</p> <p><strong>Compared, not derived (operator ruling, carried forward).</strong> Deriving retires a surface and this repository's own workflows do it, but it is sound only where the anchor and the consumer commit together. A component carries no <code>.host-software</code>, so derivation would have to fetch another repository's HEAD at run time, which trades a stale pin for a floating one and costs the component reproducible CI. Under the floor reading derivation is additionally the wrong shape: a floor states a deliberate minimum, and a minimum that silently tracks whatever is newest is not a minimum.</p> <p><strong>The advisory tier reports the finding rather than hiding it.</strong> Every below-anchor pin is counted, enumerated with its version, and printed with its next action on every run, which is the tier <a href="call/../plan/0057-deps-bundle-graduation/README.html">plan/0057</a> established for an owed deps-bundle graduation. <a href="call/../plan/0051-host-lifecycle-review/README.html">plan/0051</a> rejected the retro-red trap for the reason that applies exactly here: a gate red on pre-existing state that cannot be cleared cheaply teaches its readers to skim its output, which is this same failure one level up.</p> <h3 id="what-this-answers"><a class="header" href="#what-this-answers">What this answers</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>finding</th><th>disposition</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>The invariant is wrong in both directions</td><td>Answered. Below is a satisfied floor, above is the cascade window, and the anchor-moves-first clause is stated above.</td></tr> <tr><td>The owed check was scoped to one seventh</td><td>Answered. Both surfaces are read: the manifest by equality, the CI workflows by floor. Neither existed before this.</td></tr> <tr><td>The remedy is derivation, not comparison</td><td>Ruled against by the operator, with the reason recorded above, and further weakened by the floor reading.</td></tr> <tr><td>The write-once surface is absent</td><td>Named here and owed below; it is staged last, after every revision it asserts is recorded true.</td></tr> <tr><td>Hand reconciliation is not an interim remedy</td><td>Answered by ceasing to prescribe it. Neither surface now depends on anyone remembering.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="owed"><a class="header" href="#owed">Owed</a></h3> <p><strong>A violated floor should gate, and does not yet.</strong> What gates today is a revision outside the tool's history. A floor that resolves but whose lane no longer <em>passes</em> at that version is the other half, and detecting it means running the lane at the pinned version rather than reading a number. The trigger is the first component CI failure traced to a pin below the anchor.</p> <p><strong>The ledger entry.</strong> A <code>requires</code>/<code>verify</code> pair is a recorded revision claim, re-run against every adopter's tree and unamendable once receipts exist. It is the one pin site in this family that reconciliation-later cannot reach, and it is staged after this decision and the release that carries it.</p> <p>One surface stays out of scope, as before. A vendored dependency bundle carries copies of these revisions and is pinned by hash rather than by commit, so the comparison is a different one; <a href="call/0043-each-component-self-owns-its-vendor-bundle.html">call/0043</a> owns it.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0053-the-spine-copy-is-re-derived-not-asserted"><a class="header" href="#call0053-the-spine-copy-is-re-derived-not-asserted">call/0053: the spine copy is re-derived, not asserted</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: the methodology spine and how it reaches this repository and every adopter; what the spine mechanically is, how a project's copy is produced, and what re-verifies it on every gate run</li> <li>Date: 2026-08-02</li> <li>Ratified: 2026-08-02 by the operator, who ruled on all three prerequisites this record had left open: guard the spine at the <strong>commit hook</strong> rather than only in CI, rewrite the spine to address the adopter who holds it, and perform the migration in full. Those rulings are folded into the text below rather than left as commentary. Entered at <code>proposed</code> per <a href="call/0052-a-pin-is-reconciled-wherever-it-is-recorded.html">call/0052</a>, because the tool treats <code>accepted</code> as a credential and an agent does not issue itself one.</li> <li>Refines: <a href="call/0004-template-is-versioned-source.html">call/0004</a>, whose copy-at-version outcome stands unchanged. This decision supplies the enforcement call/0004 never had.</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-12"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-12">Context and problem</a></h2> <p>call/0004 chose copy-at-version on 2026-06-14: the template authors the spine, every project holds a copy at the revision it adopted, and "the copy is inline and acted-on (not a fragile pointer), so governance stays strong locally." It named this repository adopter zero, not a special case.</p> <p>Measured on 2026-08-02, against the canonical <code>host-lint</code> artifact rather than a PATH copy:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th></th><th>this repo</th><th>template</th><th>byte-identical</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>CLAUDE.md</code>, non-trivial lines</td><td>77</td><td>814</td><td><strong>0</strong></td></tr> <tr><td><code>STRUCTURE.md</code>, non-trivial lines</td><td>15</td><td>84</td><td><strong>0</strong></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Not one line. <code>git log --follow</code> puts this repository's <code>CLAUDE.md</code> between 128 and 137 lines continuously from 2026-06-06 to today, while the template's is 1001. The copy was never made. call/0004 was ratified, later promoted into the spine itself, and was not true for a single commit in seven weeks.</p> <p>Nothing detected it because nothing re-derives it. The spine arrives by an instruction to an agent, which is the whole of the mechanism: the adopt skill says "Copy the template's <code>CLAUDE.md</code> in unchanged at the chosen revision", and the upgrade skill's re-apply instruction reads, in full, "Re-apply the spine doc changes across the span; leave project-specifics alone." <code>host-lifecycle scaffold</code> writes three empty rooms and the stamp; it does not touch either file.</p> <p>That is the asymmetry. An artifact reproduces byte-for-byte from its pin or the build lane fails. A rung is discharged by re-derivation, not by name-presence. A task's inputs are fingerprinted so a <code>done</code> goes stale when they drift. Every phase carries a closed <code>recheck =</code> because evidence is never self-asserted. The methodology re-derives everything except itself.</p> <p>The cost is not abstract. The upgrade ledger carries 51 entries, 32 with a <code>verify</code>, and 26 of those 32 test a file under <code>host-template/</code>, a shape the ledger's own header forbids and cannot amend, because it is "a post-condition of the command's own precondition." Those entries are an author reaching for something checkable on the adopter's side, finding nothing there, and grepping the template instead. The ledger is not badly written; it is carrying a load that belongs to a mechanism nobody built.</p> <h2 id="what-the-stamp-claims-and-what-it-can-show"><a class="header" href="#what-the-stamp-claims-and-what-it-can-show">What the stamp claims, and what it can show</a></h2> <p><code>.host</code> records <code>baseline = "ff04a94"</code>, a ledger position. It carries no revision for the copy and no hash of it. So the stamp asserts that this project holds the spine at a revision, and there is no artifact against which that assertion could ever be checked. A claim with no possible referent cannot drift, because it was never anchored; it can only be discovered to have been empty.</p> <h2 id="decision-37"><a class="header" href="#decision-37">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>The spine is a file set, not a region, and a project's copy is a rendered artifact re-derived on every gate run.</strong></p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>The spine is defined by extension, not by description.</strong> It is the byte content of <code>host-template/CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>host-template/STRUCTURE.md</code>, whole, at the revision <code>.host</code> records. Not a subset, not a paraphrase, not the four principles plus two disciplines. A boundary drawn by description is a boundary two readers draw differently.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A project authors <code>CLAUDE.project.md</code> and nothing else.</strong> Its root <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> are generated by <code>host-lifecycle spine --render</code>: the spine verbatim, then the project's fragment. The boundary is a file boundary, because a marked region inside one merged manual is exactly what a case-(b) adoption cannot produce cleanly, and a boundary an agent places by hand is a boundary that is placed wrong.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>spine --check</code> re-renders and compares byte-for-byte,</strong> the shape <code>--verify-build</code> already uses. It is a clause of the <code>verify</code> phase's <code>recheck</code>, so drift re-opens the receipt and stops a release at its first step.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>.host</code> gains <code>spine = <sha256></code> of the rendered file.</strong> The stamp then names bytes rather than a label, and a cold read can establish what text the project actually holds.</p> </li> </ol> <h3 id="the-anti-drift-clauses"><a class="header" href="#the-anti-drift-clauses">The anti-drift clauses</a></h3> <p>call/0004 failed as a rule that was written down. These exist so this one cannot fail the same way.</p> <ol start="5"> <li> <p><strong>No waiver, no exemption, no escape key.</strong> There is no <code>spine-waiver</code>, no ignore entry that reaches the rendered files, and no advisory tier. <a href="call/0046-retire-the-unimplemented-hermeticity-escape.html">call/0046</a> retired an unimplemented escape rather than implement it; this ships with none to retire.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The clause is protected core.</strong> <code>skippable = false</code>, as <code>verify</code> already is. A skip receipt is refused outright rather than accepted with a citation.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>A check that cannot run is red.</strong> Absent template, unreadable file, unknown subcommand: each fails closed and names the command that fixes it. A verdict over a corpus with a hole in it is a claim the run cannot make.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The check names the binary that answered.</strong> <code>spine --check</code> prints the resolved executable path and version. On 2026-08-02 a stale <code>host-lint</code> on PATH produced a false defect report that nearly triggered a release cascade, and nothing in the tree could have caught it; a re-derivation whose deriver is unidentified is not a re-derivation.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The rule lives in the spine.</strong> A rule about what the spine is belongs in the file set it governs, so every adopter holds it verbatim and no project can soften it locally. This decision is the authoring record; the rule itself ships in the template.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The fragment is held against becoming a second source.</strong> A project that restates spine doctrine in its own words rebuilds the fork this exists to close, which is precisely how this repository arrived at 0 shared lines. <code>reconcile</code> already requires pointing over paraphrasing; it is pointed at the fragment, and its coverage bites there.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The rendered files carry zero lint findings, at the flagging and the warning tier both.</strong> Measured today, the spine as adopter root content is already <code>rc=0</code> on the naming and prose lanes and <code>rc=0</code> on references. This repository's own manual is <code>rc=3</code>, on a paragraph the render deletes as subsumed doctrine.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The spine is guarded where it is authored, by commit hook.</strong> The template repository carries the same <code>pre-commit</code> and <code>commit-msg</code> hooks every other repository under this methodology carries, so spine text that would redden an adopter cannot be committed upstream in the first place. On 2026-08-02 its hooks directory was empty: the one repository whose every line ships verbatim to every adopter was the one repository with no gate on its own commits, and <code>--install-hooks</code> reaches the host and its materialized worktrees but not a submodule. A lane in CI is the second line, not the first, because CI reports after the text is already recorded.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="consequences-35"><a class="header" href="#consequences-35">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>This repository pays first and most.</strong> It absorbs 1001 verbatim lines; its 137 become the fragment; its four principles are replaced by the template's wording. That is the host↔template sole-source reconciliation its own <code>CLAUDE.md</code> defers as "a deferred and deliberate duplication," performed rather than deferred.</p> <p><strong>Most of the ledger stops being needed.</strong> A prose-only entry has nothing to ask of an adopter once regeneration is the application. What remains is structural: convert the submodule, untrack the symlink, wire a lane. That is what the ledger's header says it is for.</p> <p><strong><code>CLAUDE.md</code> becomes generated and tracked,</strong> a category this methodology has not had. The existing rule against tracking generated artifacts governs paths that may be absent; the manual never is. It is the lockfile pattern, and it is checked the way a lockfile is checked: regenerate, compare.</p> <p><strong>A new failure mode is created and must be accepted knowingly.</strong> Spine prose that trips a lint rule reddens every adopter's gate on text they cannot edit, and a <code>LEXICON</code> entry is unsound for inherited text by <a href="call/0051-a-lexicon-entry-reports-a-grammar-defect.html">call/0051</a>. So the spine must hold clean under the rules it ships with no declaration anywhere. Today nothing guarantees that: the template's hooks directory is empty, its CI runs one lane (<code>host-lifecycle prose .</code>), and this repository excludes <code>host-template/</code> from its naming audit as "audited upstream, not host content." Clause 12 closes it at the commit, and the naming lane joins the template's CI behind that.</p> <p><strong>The spine is currently written for the wrong reader.</strong> It opens "You are working in a <em>template</em>. A real project replaces the example personas with its own", which is false in every rendered adopter file. The render is therefore not concatenation, and rewriting the spine to address the adopter who will hold it is a prerequisite to the mechanism rather than a detail of it.</p> <h2 id="what-this-does-not-decide"><a class="header" href="#what-this-does-not-decide">What this does not decide</a></h2> <ul> <li>Whether <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> takes the same fragment treatment as <code>CLAUDE.md</code> or is spine-only. It is rendered either way; only the fragment slot is open.</li> <li>How <code>reconcile</code>'s coverage check is scoped to the fragment (clause 10) in mechanical terms.</li> <li>The disposition of the 51 existing ledger entries once regeneration carries the prose half. They are append-only and stay; whether a new entry supersedes a class of them is a separate decision.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0054-one-commit-message-fault-earns-a-detector"><a class="header" href="#call0054-one-commit-message-fault-earns-a-detector">call/0054: one commit-message fault earns a detector</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: host-lint's commit-time checks; which of the four reported message faults gets a detector, at what tier and with what inputs; where unenforced guidance lives; how the work is packaged and released</li> <li>Date: 2026-08-07</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-13"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-13">Context and problem</a></h2> <p><a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/28">connollydavid/host-lint#28</a> (operator-filed) names four faults that recur in commit messages and pass <code>--prose</code>: a message that restates comments its diff adds, advocacy in place of description, answers to points nobody raised, and precedent offered as defence. <a href="call/0037-advisory-ordinal-nouns-warn-not-flag.html">call/0037</a> and the plan/0070 review priced the warn tier: an advisory that fires on legitimate text trains its reader to dismiss the tier. <a href="call/0046-vocabulary-states-what-the-tool-enforces.html">call/0046</a> fixed VOCABULARY.md as enforcement-true. Any new detector has to clear both.</p> <p>Five questions were put to the cast: the input surface, the tier and threshold, whether the precedent fault gets a detector, where guidance the tool cannot check lives, and packaging.</p> <h2 id="calibration-before-design"><a class="header" href="#calibration-before-design">Calibration before design</a></h2> <p>Measured over 922 accepted commits across seven repositories before anything was designed.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>measurement</th><th>result</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>restated comment sentences at an eight-word bar</td><td>19</td></tr> <tr><td>the same at bars of five and twelve words</td><td>22 and 7</td></tr> <tr><td>subject-line matches that are the record-title convention</td><td>12 of 12</td></tr> <tr><td>precedent-as-defence patterns, widened</td><td>0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The subject is therefore excluded from comparison, the eight-word bar keeps quotes and short idioms out, and the precedent detector has no corpus to earn a tier against. The caveat is recorded: the corpus is accepted history; rejected drafts and PR bodies were not sampled. A separate sweep for the <a href="https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lint/issues/24">connollydavid/host-lint#24</a> remainder found zero ordinal-scaffold shapes in 2036 tracked markdown headings across ten stores.</p> <h2 id="convening"><a class="header" href="#convening">Convening</a></h2> <p>Five personas, ranked ballots, each required to attack its own first preference before ranking. Fen was simulated: every probe channel refused connection, the weak-agent-trap lens stood in, and the prompts are preserved with the milestone record.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>question</th><th>settled</th><th>margin</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>input surface</td><td>a <code>host-lint commit</code> verb; message and diff as named files</td><td>4 to 1</td></tr> <tr><td>tier and threshold</td><td>warn, eight-word bar, subject excluded, commit-msg only</td><td>unanimous</td></tr> <tr><td>precedent detector</td><td>not built; the shape and the measured zero recorded in guidance</td><td>unanimous</td></tr> <tr><td>guidance home</td><td>skill text labeled unenforced, never VOCABULARY.md</td><td>unanimous</td></tr> <tr><td>packaging</td><td>one milestone bundling the host-lint#24 carve-out; one release</td><td>4 to 1</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Fen's dissent on the input surface asked for one command that reproduces the verdict; it is honored in ergonomics, with the hook printing the exact re-run line beside every warn. Two floor requirements bind the implementation: a degraded path states what it did not check, never a silent clean, and a warn names the safe direction (trim the sentence from the message; keep the comment), because a printed warning is a command to a weak agent and a bare one invites deleting the durable comment instead.</p> <h2 id="decision-38"><a class="header" href="#decision-38">Decision</a></h2> <p>Mechanize the restatement fault exactly as calibrated: a <code>commit</code> verb with the message and the staged diff as named files, an advisory verdict, the calibrated boundaries, and a commit-msg hook that stages the diff, detects the verb from the usage banner, and falls back to <code>--stdin</code> with the unrun check disclosed. Advocacy and unraised-point answers land as skill text that says no rule enforces it. No precedent detector ships against a measured zero. The host-lint#24 remainder rides the same milestone: the whole-heading ordinal-scaffold rule demotes to the advisory tier, and a declared LEXICON designator escapes it durably, with strict escalation carrying the declaration command as its remedy.</p> <p>One correction to the convening's working record: the hook dispatch script is host-lint's own file, which host-lifecycle only copies at install, so the milestone is single-component.</p> <h2 id="acceptance-and-the-substitution"><a class="header" href="#acceptance-and-the-substitution">Acceptance and the substitution</a></h2> <p>The real qwen3.5-4b probes were owed as the acceptance gate. Every channel stayed unreachable through 2026-08-07: the direct endpoint refused, the gateway carried no route to the model, and the MCP host sat on an unreachable subnet, with a persistent watch probing for days. The operator, with that state reported, lifted the hold and directed execution on 2026-08-07: the release ships on the labeled simulation by operator sign-off. The probe prompts and runner are preserved with the milestone record; the probes stay owed and run when a channel exists.</p> <h2 id="consequences-36"><a class="header" href="#consequences-36">Consequences</a></h2> <p>host-lint releases once for the whole milestone, change class <code>changes-output</code>, because a heading verdict that blocked yesterday is advisory today. This record is the release's authorization. The advisory tier grows by two forms, both inside the known split where the commit hook treats a warn as advisory while the release gate counts it as a regression; that split is recorded as an open operator decision, not resolved here.</p> <h2 id="discharge-of-the-owed-probes-2026-08-08"><a class="header" href="#discharge-of-the-owed-probes-2026-08-08">Discharge of the owed probes (2026-08-08)</a></h2> <p>The real qwen3.5-4b probes ran once a channel existed: the gateway behind TLS at api.d07yx58.net, served model confirmed in the response body, thinking on at the card's thinking-general sampling per the plan/0076 corrected protocol, by operator direction, because suppressing a small model's reasoning channel tests a weaker agent than the one the design serves. The release was not contingent on this run; what discharges is the obligation this record left owed. Transcripts and the reconciliation live with <a href="call/../plan/0080-commit-message-faults/README.html">plan/0080</a>.</p> <p>Measured against the simulation: first preferences agree on three of five questions; Q2 diverges stably toward documentation-file coverage, and with that ballot standing in the convening the settled option still carries 4 to 1; Q1 yields no signal, both orders ranking by presentation position. Neither behavioral prediction reproduced in either draw: the bare warning produced the safe direction, and the revised body carries no precedent residue. Every settled decision stands, and the floor requirements remain as guards, two draws not being grounds to retire a tail risk. This measured record is the weight future convenings give a simulated Fen ballot.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded"><a class="header" href="#call0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded">call/0055: upstream artefacts are referenced, not embedded</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: how <code>host-lint-openwrt</code> obtains an upstream artefact it checks against; the line between a rule source the pack vendors and a live artefact it must resolve; what a temporary cache may and may not stand in for</li> <li>Date: 2026-08-10</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-14"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-14">Context and problem</a></h2> <p><a href="call/../plan/0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack/README.html">plan/0072</a> established pin-and-vendor for the FFmpeg pack: every upstream source is copied in and pinned by whole-file digest, so the corpus is provable offline and drift localises to the section that moved. <a href="call/../plan/0081-openwrt-style-pack/README.html">plan/0081</a> inherited that shape, and the fourth style manual broke it.</p> <p>Three of the four manuals describe habits measured from the tree and from history. The fourth describes a pull request body, and its rules key to <code>.github/pull_request_template.md</code>, a file <code>openwrt/packages</code> ships and GitHub prefills. That is not a measurement. It is a live artefact owned by another project, and it changes without asking. The manual's own figures say so: template adoption runs 0.0% in 2024, 44.0% in 2025 and 71.6% in 2026, because the template in this form landed mid-2025 and replaced a plainer one.</p> <p>A vendored copy of that file would be wrong the moment upstream edits it, and wrong silently. The pack would keep reporting a confident verdict against headings the project no longer ships, which is the same failure mode as a checker whose completeness test passes over what it happened to see.</p> <p>There is a second, quieter path to the same fault. <code>openwrt-pr-style.md</code> quotes the template in full inside a fenced block. That quote is vendored, because the manual is vendored. If the checker read its expected headings out of that fence, the pack would embed the upstream artefact by the back door, through a file that looks like the project's own.</p> <h2 id="the-distinction-that-settles-it"><a class="header" href="#the-distinction-that-settles-it">The distinction that settles it</a></h2> <p>Two kinds of input were being treated as one.</p> <ul> <li>A <strong>rule source</strong> states what the pack enforces. The four manuals are rule sources. They are project-authored measurements, they are the pack's own, and freezing them is correct: a rule that changes without the registry changing is exactly what the digest pin exists to catch.</li> <li>A <strong>checked-against artefact</strong> is something the pack compares a submission to, owned and moved by someone else. <code>.github/pull_request_template.md</code> is one. Freezing it is not conservatism; it is a wrong answer with a long shelf life.</li> </ul> <p>Pin-and-vendor is right for the first and wrong for the second.</p> <h2 id="decision-39"><a class="header" href="#decision-39">Decision</a></h2> <p>Upstream artefacts are <strong>referenced and resolved at check time</strong>, never embedded.</p> <ol> <li>The pack carries no copy of <code>.github/pull_request_template.md</code>. It records the artefact's canonical location and resolves it per run. A local <code>openwrt/packages</code> checkout answers when one is given; otherwise the published raw file does.</li> <li>A <strong>temporary cache is permitted</strong> and is expected, so a sweep does not refetch per invocation. It is bounded by a short lifetime, it is gitignored and never tracked, and it is a cache in the strict sense: it may only hold what was fetched from the canonical location, and its presence may never change a verdict from what a live fetch would have produced.</li> <li>When the artefact cannot be resolved and no live cache entry stands, the template-keyed rules <strong>do not run and say so</strong>. A degraded path states what it did not check. It never falls back to the manual's quoted fence, and it never reports clean for a rule it could not evaluate.</li> <li>The last-seen digest is recorded so a moved template is <strong>reported as drift</strong>, not absorbed. Drift on a checked-against artefact is news about upstream, not a defect in the pack.</li> <li>The quoted template inside <code>openwrt-pr-style.md</code> is illustration. No checker may read expected headings, labels or box wording from it. The manual is a rule source; the fence inside it is not a copy of the artefact for the pack's purposes.</li> </ol> <p>The four style manuals stay vendored and digest-pinned under <code>fixtures/manuals/</code>, unchanged by this decision.</p> <h2 id="consequences-37"><a class="header" href="#consequences-37">Consequences</a></h2> <p>The <code>pr</code> lane gains a resolution step the other three do not have, and with it a failure mode they do not have: it can be unable to check. That is accepted, and it is why point three is written as a floor rather than a preference. A lane that quietly passes because it could not read the thing it compares against is worse than a lane that refuses, and this pack already carries one refusal of that shape, since the <code>pr</code> lane also refuses a directory argument rather than sweeping a clone for a body that is not in it.</p> <p>Offline reproducibility is now partial by construction. The three tree-facing lanes remain fully offline; the <code>pr</code> lane's template-keyed rules do not, and the release gate must not treat that as a regression to be engineered away. The measured rules of the <code>pr</code> lane, those about <em>filling</em> the headings rather than matching them, stay offline and keep working when resolution fails, which is where most of that manual's findings live: a template body keeps the testing lines about 95% of the time and supplies a value only about two thirds of the time.</p> <p>This decision is scoped to artefacts the pack checks against. It does not reopen pin-and-vendor for rule sources, and it does not apply to the FFmpeg pack, whose pinned documents are prose that states rules rather than a form a submission is matched to.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0056-a-tool-dependency-is-a-floor-checked-in-the-lane"><a class="header" href="#call0056-a-tool-dependency-is-a-floor-checked-in-the-lane">call/0056: a tool dependency is a floor, checked in the lane</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: how a skill or a reference workflow declares its dependency on a <code>host-*</code> binary; where that binary is resolved from; when and against what the declared floor is verified; the version policy while the tools are pre-1.0</li> <li>Date: 2026-08-10</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-15"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-15">Context and problem</a></h2> <p>Three observations arrived together, and they are one problem.</p> <p><strong>The declaration already exists; nothing enforces it.</strong> <code>host-template/UPGRADING.md</code> carries a <code>requires = host-lifecycle vX.Y.Z</code> field on its ledger entries, and states repeatedly that an adopter should bump the pinned tool before moving the pointer. The <code>RENAME-repro-waiver</code> entry was applied with the lane running v0.35.1, which parses only <code>repro-exempt</code>, so it read an exempt component as DRIFT. <code>upgrade --record</code> ran the entry's verify and it passed, because the verify ran under a different binary than the lane did. A floor that is never checked against the binary actually in the lane is not a floor; it is a comment.</p> <p><strong>The template acquires the tool three ways.</strong> <code>site.yml</code> and <code>reproducible-build.yml</code> build the <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> submodule; <code>prose.yml</code> runs <code>cargo install --git … --rev <inline></code>. Three mechanisms means three places a version can be stated, so skew is available by construction. <a href="call/0038-releasing-a-tool-updates-the-template-pin.html">call/0038</a> and the <code>software --check</code> gate do catch the resulting drift for the template itself, and did so in this session. An <strong>adopter</strong> is left uncovered: a project instantiated from the template has no <code>.host-software</code> stanza over <code>tools/</code>, so nothing gates its wired-once tool pointer. The protection stops exactly where the population is largest.</p> <p><strong>Skills currently declare nothing.</strong> A sweep of <code>.claude/skills/</code> finds no version string, no rev, no requires clause. So this is a choice about what to build rather than a migration away from something, and the cheap wrong answer is available: let each skill pin what it was written against. That would re-mint the anchor once per skill and reproduce the workflow skew at greater scale.</p> <h2 id="decision-40"><a class="header" href="#decision-40">Decision</a></h2> <p>A skill declares a <strong>floor</strong>, not a pin, and the floor is verified <strong>in the lane, at invocation, against the binary about to run</strong>.</p> <ol> <li><strong>One anchor.</strong> Which binary runs is resolved from <code>.host-software</code> and nowhere else. A skill does not pin a revision, and neither does a reference workflow; the three acquisition mechanisms collapse to one resolution.</li> <li><strong>A floor is a capability claim.</strong> A skill declares <code>requires: host-lifecycle >= X.Y.Z</code>, where the version named is the one the capability it uses first appeared in. It is a floor because a consumer needs a behaviour to be present, not to be exact.</li> <li><strong>Checked where it is used.</strong> The lane probes the resolved binary's version immediately before invoking it and compares it to the declared floor. A floor established at record time by one binary and relied on at run time by another is not established at all, which is the whole lesson of the <code>RENAME-repro-waiver</code> misread.</li> <li><strong>Floor only, while the tools are 0.x.</strong> Semver permits a 0.x minor to break, so the strict reading would demand <code>>=0.50, <0.51</code>. It is refused: a speculative upper bound forces churn at every minor and produces false failures far more often than it prevents a real incompatibility. The floor rises when something actually breaks. An upper bound is added only for a <strong>known and recorded</strong> incompatibility, and adding one requires a <code>call/</code>.</li> <li><strong>An undeterminable version refuses.</strong> When the lane cannot read a version, it says so and does not run the dependent checks. It never assumes the floor holds. This is the same floor <a href="call/0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded.html">call/0055</a> sets for an unresolvable artefact and <a href="call/0054-one-commit-message-fault-earns-a-detector.html">call/0054</a> sets for a degraded path: a silent pass on something that was not verified is the failure mode, not the safe default.</li> </ol> <h2 id="consequences-38"><a class="header" href="#consequences-38">Consequences</a></h2> <p>Every lane gains a version probe it did not have, which is the cost, and it is small next to the failure it removes. The failure is specific and was observed: a check reporting green while running a binary that could not evaluate what it claimed to have checked.</p> <p>Adopters gain coverage they never had. Because the floor travels with the skill rather than with the host's recipe, a project instantiated from the template carries its own requirement and can verify it without a <code>.host-software</code> stanza naming the tool. That is the gap this decision exists to close, and it is why the rule is written for skills and workflows generally rather than for this repository's Where room.</p> <p>This does not retire call/0038 or the <code>software --check</code> tool-pin HAZARDs. Those answer whether the <em>recorded</em> pins agree, and they keep answering it. The floor answers whether the binary <em>in hand</em> can do the job. A clean pin check still says nothing about the binary a lane actually loaded, which is the distinction the four Where-room commands already draw and which this decision extends to the tools themselves.</p> <p>The <code>requires</code> field in <code>UPGRADING.md</code> is not new syntax to invent; it is an existing declaration that becomes enforced. Its ledger entries keep their current wording.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="call0057-a-remedy-must-know-whether-its-artefact-publishes"><a class="header" href="#call0057-a-remedy-must-know-whether-its-artefact-publishes">call/0057: a remedy must know whether its artefact publishes</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Scope: host-lint's identifier-tier remedy; where a tracker reference's backing URL is allowed to live; what the tool must know about the artefact it is correcting before it names a fix</li> <li>Date: 2026-08-10</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-16"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-16">Context and problem</a></h2> <p>The identifier tier refuses an un-cited tracker reference and tells the author to declare it with a backing URL, through <code>host-lint lexicon add "<phrase>" --url <url></code>. The guard is sound: a bare <code>#7</code> names no repository, and a citation that cannot be resolved is not a citation.</p> <p>The remedy is not. On a public repository, GitHub mints a cross-reference on the target whenever a commit naming it is pushed, and it does so for both spellings the guard accepts, <code>owner/repo#N</code> and the URL. That was measured rather than assumed: one commit through each form, each producing an entry on the target thread. So the sanctioned fix for a hygiene finding is the thing that posts into someone else's issue, and a branch amended and force-pushed during review posts once per rewrite.</p> <p>The governance repository is the one that suffers. <code>agentic-host</code> cites other projects' trackers constantly, because that is what a methodology repository does, and every such citation carried in a commit message pulls this repository into an upstream thread that never asked for it.</p> <p>Underneath sits the actual defect: <strong>host-lint has no notion that a commit message publishes in a way a file does not.</strong> It lints a message and a markdown file through the same tiers and offers the same remedy, because from inside the linter both are text. They are not. A file changes a working tree; a pushed commit message is delivered to every watcher of every repository it names. A tool that recommends an edit is responsible for where that edit ends up, and this one cannot currently tell.</p> <h2 id="the-distinction-that-settles-it-1"><a class="header" href="#the-distinction-that-settles-it-1">The distinction that settles it</a></h2> <p>The guard and the remedy were fused, and they separate cleanly.</p> <ul> <li>The <strong>guard</strong> is about resolvability: does this reference name a repository? That is a property of the reference and is right to enforce everywhere, unchanged.</li> <li>The <strong>remedy</strong> is about where the resolving evidence is written. That is a property of the artefact under correction, and it is the half that has to become artefact-aware.</li> </ul> <p>The LEXICON file is the answer already sitting in the tool. It is a file. A file mints no cross-reference, it is reviewed with the change, and it is exactly the declared-vocabulary store this project already trusts. The URL belongs there. It never belonged in the commit message.</p> <h2 id="decision-41"><a class="header" href="#decision-41">Decision</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>The backing URL lives in the LEXICON, never in an artefact that publishes.</strong> For a commit message, the remedy is <code>host-lint lexicon add</code>, and the message itself keeps the bare token. The declaration resolves the reference for a reader without posting anything to the target.</li> <li><strong>host-lint learns the publishing surface of what it is linting.</strong> A commit message is a publishing artefact. A tracked file is not. The <code>commit</code> verb and the commit-msg hook lint a publishing artefact by construction, which is enough to decide the tier without inspecting remotes.</li> <li><strong>A remedy naming a form that publishes is never emitted for a publishing artefact.</strong> The remedy text is selected by surface, not by tier alone. This is a floor, matching the ones in <a href="call/0054-one-commit-message-fault-earns-a-detector.html">call/0054</a>, <a href="call/0055-upstream-artefacts-are-referenced-not-embedded.html">call/0055</a> and <a href="call/0056-a-tool-dependency-is-a-floor-checked-in-the-lane.html">call/0056</a>: the tool states what it could not do. Quiet harm is the failure every one of those floors exists to prevent.</li> <li><strong>The guard is unchanged.</strong> A bare numeral naming no repository still fails. Nothing here loosens what counts as a citation; it moves where the citation is recorded.</li> </ol> <h2 id="consequences-39"><a class="header" href="#consequences-39">Consequences</a></h2> <p>An author correcting a commit message now edits two things, the message and the LEXICON, where before they edited one. That is the cost, and it buys back a side effect the author could not see and did not choose. The LEXICON edit is also the durable one: the next occurrence of the same reference is already declared.</p> <p>This is the first rule in host-lint keyed to <em>where output goes</em> rather than to what the text says, so it opens a question this decision does not answer: whether other remedies carry the same hazard. A pull request title becomes a squash-merge subject and so becomes a commit message, which suggests they do.
