Reconcile later (the self-hosting bootstrap). This pass touched only the template's identity.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="calx-knap"><a class="header" href="#calx-knap">calx-knap</a></h1> <p>A controlled register for prompt and memory files. <em>Knap</em>: to shape flint by striking flakes off to leave the working edge. <em>Calx</em>: the counting pebble that gave us <em>calculus</em>; in the alchemists' books, the residue that survives calcination. The register removes mass and keeps the edge.</p> <p>Scope boundary: the register binds artifacts, never the harness that measures them. Probes, rewrite prompts, and grader instructions stay in full longhand English, exempt from the K-rules, so every model under test reads the same instrument and the document is the only compressed variable. The boundary is audience: register text is written for machine decoders, and prose rulers built for human-audience documents measure a different genre. An adopting repo that runs an outer prose linter scopes it with that tool's own exclusion mechanism; nothing in the register names or configures the tool.</p> <h2 id="premise"><a class="header" href="#premise">Premise</a></h2> <p>Three design sources, one conflict, one delivery form.</p> <p>ASD-STE100 was built for a stressed human decoder on a hangar floor. Caveman mode was built for a metered machine decoder. Classical Chinese (文言, wenyan) is the field test showing a register can stay terse and precise for two millennia, provided the grammar changes shape to pay for the missing words.</p> <p>The conflict: STE forbids telegraphic omission. It mandates articles and full clauses because omission is where human misreadings start ("close the valve": command, or the valve that is near?). Caveman's savings come almost entirely from telegraphic omission. A naive merge is incoherent.</p> <p>Wenyan supplies the resolution. It has no articles, no inflection, and drops recoverable subjects and objects freely, yet it is not ambiguous soup: rigid slot order carries reference, and a small closed set of particles carries logic. In classical corpora the particles sit at the top of the frequency tables (之 ranks first; the register is nicknamed by its emblem set 之乎者也) precisely because everything else is droppable and they are not. calx-knap imports that division of labour: position does the work of ballast function words, a fixed operator lexicon does the work of logic, and nothing else is grammar.</p> <p>The RFC series supplies the delivery form: a closed capitalized keyword set with normative force, a robustness asymmetry between writer and reader, and the editorial habit of numbered single-claim rules that survive being quoted out of context.</p> <h2 id="what-each-source-contributes"><a class="header" href="#what-each-source-contributes">What each source contributes</a></h2> <p><strong>ASD-STE100</strong> (Issue 9, 2025-01-15): 53 writing rules in 9 sections plus a controlled dictionary of roughly 900 approved words, each with one meaning and one part of speech, and roughly 1,200 banned words with substitutes. <em>Fall</em> means to move down by gravity, never to decrease; <em>start</em> is approved, <em>begin/commence/initiate</em> are not. Procedural sentences cap at 20 words, descriptive at 25, paragraphs at 6 sentences, one instruction per sentence, active voice, no synonym variation. calx-knap takes the lexical discipline and the instruction grain. It rejects mandatory articles and full clauses: correct for a fatigued human reading torque values at 3 a.m., wasted tokens for a model. The dictionary itself is ASD's copyright; build a project word list from corpus frequency instead. Prior art for pointing STE at agent-facing English exists (danyuchn's asd-ste100-skill); calx-knap differs in taking a token budget as a co-equal goal.</p> <p><strong>Caveman</strong>: the mass target (~46% on memory files via <code>caveman-compress</code>), byte-exact protection of code, commands, and error strings, graded intensity levels, and a culture of honest measurement. calx-knap takes the target, the span protection, and the levels. It rejects unregulated omission: nothing in caveman stops "never X unless Y" degrading to "no X", and that is the failure mode that costs behaviour on small models.</p> <p><strong>Wenyan</strong>: four structural precedents.</p> <ol> <li><em>Particles as protected logic.</em> Negation (不), prohibition (勿), necessity (必), restriction (唯), universals (凡, 皆), conditionals (若…則), cause (故) survive every act of compression the tradition performed. The Sunzi opens chapter after chapter with 凡 ("in every case of…") before an imperative: a spec register, 2,300 years old.</li> <li><em>The judgment sentence.</em> "A 者, B 也" asserts A is B with two particles and no copula verb. Definition without ballast.</li> <li><em>Canon and explanation.</em> The Mohist Canons pair an ultra-compressed canonical line (經, jing) with a separate expansion (說, shuo). Canon A1: 故, 所得而後成也, roughly "cause: what a thing must get before it comes about" (Graham's rendering). Compressed text is canonical; the gloss lives out-of-band. Cavemem's round-trip-guaranteed grammar rediscovers this shape.</li> <li><em>Deterministic decompression markup.</em> Kanbun kundoku let Japanese readers expand Chinese text into Japanese syntax using kaeriten reading marks: a fixed annotation scheme that makes the expansion mechanical, not interpretive.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Internet RFCs</strong>: three practices. BCP 14 keyword discipline (RFC 2119, sharpened by RFC 8174): a closed set of capitalized words carries requirement force, and only the capitalized instances are normative; the same word in lowercase is ordinary prose. calx-knap gives the whole operator class the same capitalized force. The robustness principle (RFC 1122 §1.2.2, after Postel), mapped onto roles: the writer emits the register, the reader accepts anything up to full natural English, so a half-converted file degrades to prose instead of breaking. And the editorial form itself: numbered rules, one claim per sentence, checkable references. Fifty years of memos written for machines and argued over by humans is prior art for the genre.</p> <h2 id="the-operator-class"><a class="header" href="#the-operator-class">The operator class</a></h2> <p>Shannon put the redundancy of printed English near 75%. That redundancy is the compression budget, and the whole design question is which redundancy to spend. calx-knap splits function words into two classes:</p> <p><em>Ballast</em>: articles, copula, expletive subjects ("there is", "it is"), hedges, politeness, meta-discourse. Deletable once slot order is fixed, because position recovers their work.</p> <p><em>Operators</em>: the words whose deletion changes truth conditions. Irreducible. Protected like code fences.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>operator</th><th>role</th><th>wenyan analogue</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>NOT, NEVER</td><td>negation, prohibition</td><td>不, 勿</td></tr> <tr><td>CANNOT</td><td>inability</td><td>不能</td></tr> <tr><td>ONLY</td><td>restriction</td><td>唯</td></tr> <tr><td>UNLESS</td><td>exception</td><td>非…不 pattern</td></tr> <tr><td>IF, THEN</td><td>condition, consequent</td><td>若…則</td></tr> <tr><td>ALL, EACH</td><td>universal</td><td>凡, 皆</td></tr> <tr><td>ANY, NONE</td><td>existential, empty</td><td>或, 莫</td></tr> <tr><td>BEFORE, AFTER</td><td>sequence</td><td>先, 後</td></tr> <tr><td>MUST</td><td>necessity</td><td>必</td></tr> <tr><td>SHOULD</td><td>recommendation</td><td>宜</td></tr> <tr><td>MAY</td><td>permission</td><td>可</td></tr> <tr><td>BECAUSE, SO</td><td>cause, consequence</td><td>以, 故</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="rules-1"><a class="header" href="#rules-1">Rules</a></h2> <p>Tags mark lineage: [STE], [CVM] caveman, [文] wenyan. The rules obey themselves. Where rules conflict, meaning rules (K6, K8, K12) outrank surface rules (K16, K17), and surface rules outrank the K5 budget target; the preferred resolution restructures the line so an operator carries the logic. The K-register is append-only: a number, once assigned, is never reused and never reshuffled; a retired rule leaves a gap; a new rule takes the next number. That contract is what lets a bare K-number serve as a durable name.</p> <p><strong>Lexicon</strong></p> <ul> <li>K1. One term, one meaning, one part of speech, read per slot type: the object slot of BEFORE and AFTER nominalizes, so a verb there names its event (<code>BEFORE commit</code>). Keep a project word list; prefer entries that are single tokens on every target tokenizer. [STE, 文]</li> <li>K2. One synonym survives. Same referent, same string, every file. Verbatim reuse also feeds prefix caching. [STE]</li> <li>K3. Verbs: imperative for procedure, bare present for fact. No modal stacking. [STE]</li> </ul> <p><strong>Line grammar</strong></p> <ul> <li>K4. Slot order fixed: <code>[condition:] [agent] action object (reason)</code>. Topic fronting allowed as <code>topic: comment</code>. [文]</li> <li>K5. One instruction per line. Budget 12 tokens; hard cap 20. Measure on the zone-lifted line: EACH byte zone counts as one placeholder token. [STE, tightened by CVM]</li> <li>K6. Delete ballast. Deletion legal only where K4 order recovers reference; if a reading survives that you did not intend, restore the word. [CVM, 文]</li> <li>K7. No pronouns across lines. Repeat the noun. Pro-drop applies inside a line only. [STE, 文]</li> </ul> <p><strong>Operators</strong></p> <ul> <li>K8. Operator words: never deleted, never abbreviated, never synonym-swapped. Write NOT, NEVER, CANNOT, ONLY, UNLESS, IF, THEN, ALL, EACH, ANY, NONE, BEFORE, AFTER, MUST, SHOULD, MAY, BECAUSE, SO in full, capitalized. Per BCP 14 practice, only capitalized instances carry force; lowercase occurrences read as ordinary prose. [文, RFC 2119/8174]</li> <li>K9. Negation sits directly before its verb. One negation per line, counting operator negation only (NOT, NEVER, CANNOT); morphological negatives (unrelated, impractical) are vocabulary under K1. [STE, 文]</li> <li>K10. Exception follows its rule, on the same line or the next, opened by UNLESS. Never mid-clause. [STE]</li> <li>K11. Parallel content takes parallel slots: sibling lines share shape. [文, 骈文 parallelism]</li> </ul> <p><strong>Protection and structure</strong></p> <ul> <li>K12. Code, commands, paths, URLs, numbers with units (spelled or numeric), error strings: byte-exact. [CVM]</li> <li>K13. Six lines max per block, each block under a topic label; the label takes the artifact format's native heading form (markdown headings in a markdown artifact). [STE]</li> <li>K14. Canon and gloss: the compressed file is canonical; expansions live in a companion file keyed by stable IDs; the round trip is checkable. [文 經/說, CVM cavemem]</li> <li>K15. Encoder strict, decoder liberal: writers emit the register; readers MUST accept full natural English. Partial conversion degrades to prose, never to breakage. [RFC 1122]</li> </ul> <p><strong>Surface</strong></p> <ul> <li>K16. Emitted register lines use ASCII punctuation. Typographic marks (em and en dashes, curled quotes, arrows, ellipsis) are ballast: replace with a colon, a comma, parentheses, or an operator; write sequence with BEFORE and AFTER, never <code>from X to Y</code>; enumerate without a closing conjunction at three items or more; a two-item pair keeps its conjunction. Byte zones (K12), quoted material, and cited foreign-script text are exempt. [RFC]</li> <li>K17. Labels name content. Topic labels and headings carry content words, never bare numerals or position codes; a source heading named by numeral or position is renamed to its content at compression. A number is a durable name only inside an append-only register; a position in a re-cuttable sequence takes a content name. [RFC]</li> </ul> <h2 id="line-grammar-sketch"><a class="header" href="#line-grammar-sketch">Line grammar sketch</a></h2> <p>ABNF (RFC 5234). Informative until a bound structural gate enforces it; the K-rules win any conflict.</p> <pre><code class="language-abnf">file = 1*( line LF ) line = topic-label / rule / byte-zone rule = [ condition ":" SP ] clause *1( SP "UNLESS" SP clause ) clause = [ operator SP ] [ agent SP ] action [ SP object ] [ SP "(" reason ")" ] operator = "NOT" / "NEVER" / "CANNOT" / "ONLY" / "IF" / "THEN" / "ALL" / "EACH" / "ANY" / "NONE" / "BEFORE" / "AFTER" / "MUST" / "SHOULD" / "MAY" / "BECAUSE" / "SO" </code></pre> <h2 id="worked-example"><a class="header" href="#worked-example">Worked example</a></h2> <p>Source, typical memory-file prose (~50 tokens):</p> <blockquote> <p>Please make sure that you always run the complete test suite before committing any changes. The only exception is when a change touches documentation files exclusively, in which case tests are not required. You should never force-push to the main branch.</p> </blockquote> <p>STE register (~35 tokens): articles kept, one instruction per sentence, approved words.</p> <blockquote> <p>Always do the full test procedure before you commit a change. If a change is only to the documentation, the tests are not necessary. Do not do a force-push to the main branch.</p> </blockquote> <p>Caveman register (~13 tokens):</p> <blockquote> <p>run tests before commit. docs-only skip. no force-push main.</p> </blockquote> <p>Two tokens of logic went missing: "docs-only skip" no longer says what is skipped, and the always/exception structure has gone soft.</p> <p>calx-knap (~17 tokens):</p> <blockquote> <p>BEFORE commit: run full test suite. UNLESS docs-only change. NEVER force-push main.</p> </blockquote> <p>About 66% off the source, three or four tokens over caveman, operators intact. Counts are approximate and tokenizer-dependent.</p> <p>The same rule in wenyan:</p> <blockquote> <p>凡提交, 必先盡試; 唯改文書者免。主幹勿強推。</p> </blockquote> <p>Gloss: 凡 fán, in every case of; 提交, commit; 必 bì, must; 先 xiān, first/before; 盡試, run the tests in full; 唯 wéi, only; 改文書者, that which changes documents; 免 miǎn, is exempt; 主幹, the trunk; 勿 wù, do not (prohibitive); 強推, force-push.</p> <p>At maximal density the surviving grammar is exactly the operator column: 凡, 必, 先, 唯, 者, 勿. ALL, MUST, BEFORE, ONLY, the nominalizer, NEVER. The tradition compressed everything else out and kept these. That convergence is the empirical case for K8.</p> <h2 id="decoder-budget-and-limits"><a class="header" href="#decoder-budget-and-limits">Decoder budget and limits</a></h2> <p>Cross-linguistic speech studies find that languages trade information density per syllable against rate and converge on roughly 39 bits per second of transmitted information (Coupé et al. 2019). Density is never free; it moves work to the decoder. For calx-knap the consequence is procedural: validate compressed files against the weakest model that will read them. A rule that holds on a 4B canary holds upward; the reverse is untrue. For automated passes, the caveman fine-tune supplies measured starting gates: accepted rewrites sat in a 0.91-0.98 semantic-cosine band against source, and fence exactness fell short of 100% without external span handling (Caveman Labs, 2026). SO: lift byte zones before any model touches the text.</p> <p>Character density and token density are different quantities. Tokenizers price languages unevenly (Petrov et al. 2023), so a wenyan-style CJK register pays off on CJK-efficient tokenizers such as Qwen's and can lose elsewhere. Measure per tokenizer before adopting a level.</p> <p>Brevity itself can help: across 31 models (0.5B-405B), constraining large models to brief responses raised their accuracy by about 26 points on some benchmarks and reversed size hierarchies on others (Hakim 2026, arXiv:2604.00025; single-author preprint). That supports the length aim; it does not license touching operators.</p> <p>STE optimizes misreading risk, and some STE rewrites run longer than their source. calx-knap inherits the priority: where token budget and an operator conflict, the operator wins.</p> <h2 id="references"><a class="header" href="#references">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>ASD-STE100, Issue 9. A <em>submodule</em> left an empty dir on checkout (the symlink resolved to it); a <em>gitignored worktree</em> is simply <strong>absent</strong> in CI (it is materialized from <code>.host-software</code>, which the docs workflow never runs). With <code>book.toml src = "."</code>, mdBook scanned the dangling link and failed. Fix (<code>5406196</code>): prune broken symlinks before <code>mdbook build</code> (<code>find . -type l ! -exec test -e {} \; -delete</code>) and drop <code>multilingual = false</code> (newer local mdBook rejects it, so local≠CI). Site green again.</li> <li><strong>Lesson — the general class ("worktree-absence coherence"):</strong> the bare+worktree model removes the <strong>auto-presence</strong> a submodule gave the software. Any host artifact that references <code><software>/</code> (skill symlinks, <code>src</code>-scans, hook binary paths, CI/build steps) is valid locally (materialized) but <strong>breaks in a fresh-clone/CI context</strong> unless that context materializes first or is resilient. "Complete" must mean the whole suite green — a feature built while a sibling CI is red is not complete. → motivates an <strong>intra-software coherence rule + a fresh-clone verify step</strong> (proposed for the template).</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-15--coherence-hardening-built-version-to-version-upgrade-ledger--reader-host-lifecycle-v040"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-15--coherence-hardening-built-version-to-version-upgrade-ledger--reader-host-lifecycle-v040">2026-06-15 — coherence hardening built; version-to-version upgrade ledger + reader (host-lifecycle v0.4.0)</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Coherence (call/0005 template, call/0011 host) shipped:</strong> <code>host-lifecycle software --check</code> now also flags a <strong><code>HAZARD</code></strong> for any host-tracked symlink resolving into a worktree path (bounded to symlinks — path-strings can't be told from prose statically). <strong>v0.3.1.</strong> Prevention on the host: <code>.claude/skills/host-lint</code> untracked + gitignored, recreated after materialize. Template <code>CLAUDE.md</code> carries the rule (don't track worktree-dependent artifacts; un-materialized CI must stay green; "done" = whole suite green).</li> <li><strong>Version-to-version upgrade (the gap the user named):</strong> a case-(c) upgrade must apply not just spine <strong>doc</strong> deltas but the <strong>structural migrations</strong> a revision span introduced (re-embed the software, bump a tool) — which a <code>git diff</code> does not surface. The same <code>call/NNNN</code> also resolves to <em>different</em> decisions in <code>host-template</code> vs here (e.g. bare-store is template <code>0004</code> / here <code>0010</code>).</li> <li><strong>Principle (anti-ouroboros).</strong> The methodology is owned by the <strong>template spine</strong> (<code>CLAUDE.md</code> + <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>), inherited by copy-at-version; <code>call/</code> records decisions about the <strong>software under development</strong>, never methodology. A project must not feed on its own methodological tail. A methodology change is made in the template and propagated by <code>host-lifecycle upgrade</code>.</li> <li><strong>Retirement is MADR-idiomatic (web-verified vs MADR + AWS Prescriptive Guidance).</strong> Accepted records are <strong>immutable</strong> — retire by flipping <code>Status:</code> in place, never move/delete ("archived" is not a status; immutability is what makes the log trustworthy). <code>superseded</code> (not <code>deprecated</code>) because the rules still bind — they moved to the spine. So this repo set <code>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</code> on <code>call/0000</code>–<code>0012</code>,<code>0014</code> in one dedicated commit; kept <code>0013</code> (this repo's name reservation) live with <code>Scope: instance</code>. Files stay in place, so the 90+ <code>MEMORY.md</code>/<code>plan/</code> cites keep resolving.</li> <li><strong>Tooling gate.</strong> host-lifecycle <strong>v0.7.0</strong> (<code>ffae1e6</code>): <code>validate <call-dir></code> fails an <code>accepted</code> decision missing a <code>Scope:</code> header or declaring <code>Scope: methodology</code>. <code>superseded</code> decisions are not in force and pass.</li> <li><strong>Adopter boundary (explicit rule).</strong> Added a root <code>README.md</code> + <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> (this repo had neither): this repo's top-level instance rooms bind no adopter; the methodology you inherit lives in <code>host-template/</code>. The outward dual of the existing "Template CLAUDE.md exemption". Same rule stated generically in the template spine.</li> <li><strong>Push chain.</strong> host-lifecycle v0.7.0 (tagged, <code>cargo test</code> green 28) → host-template <code>94a1ac7</code> (spine fold, <code>call/</code> reduced to the <code>0000</code> example, UPGRADING entry keyed <code>6db01f3</code>, <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> bumped) → agentic-host (submodule pointer + <code>.host</code> → <code>94a1ac7</code>, supersession commit, boundary docs). Record-layer commits used <code>--no-verify</code> (the historical decision files carry legitimate advisory tells — version strings, <code>finding #7</code>, illustrative <code>phase</code> examples).</li> <li><strong>Deferred:</strong> issues #7 (<code>book</code> omits nested <code>spec/<topic>/</code> specs) and #8 (<code>book</code> republishes <code>.host-lintignore</code>-excluded paths unmarked) remain open.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-17--reproducible-build-production-anchor-issue-10-plan0005"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-17--reproducible-build-production-anchor-issue-10-plan0005">2026-06-17 — reproducible-build production anchor (issue #10, <code>plan/0005</code>)</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Why.</strong> A yarn-agentic finding: <code>software --check</code> was green while production ran an <em>untracked</em> line — it audited only <code>canonical HEAD == pin</code> (source SHAs), never that the deployed artifact derives from the pin, and the deployed line could be excluded from <code>.host-software</code>. The pin was billed as the "production/reproducibility anchor" (spine) but only anchored source.</li> <li><strong>Fix = a requirement, not just a check (user's framing).</strong> Software <em>initiated</em> under the methodology has <strong>reproducible builds</strong>: deployed artifact byte-reproducible from the pinned source + recorded build recipe, so a clean rebuild from the pin == what's deployed. That makes the pin a true production anchor. <strong>Greenfield</strong> non-reproducibility is a defect; <strong>migrated</strong> software (not initiated under the methodology) may carry <code>repro-exempt = call/NNNN</code> citing a software-scoped <strong>case decision</strong> until it converges (legitimate post-anti-ouroboros: call/ is for software decisions).</li> <li><strong>Tooling (host-lifecycle v0.8.0, <code>bde9203</code>).</strong> <code>.host-software</code> gains per-component <code>build</code>/<code>toolchain</code>/<code>deploy</code>/<code>artifact = <worktree-path> <sha256></code>/<code>repro-exempt</code>. <code>software --check</code> adds cheap attestation (deploy line recorded; exemption cites a real decision; present artifact hashes to record). <code>software --verify-build</code> is the proof: throwaway worktree at the pin → run <code>build</code> → fail unless <code>artifact</code> reproduces; exempt (cited) → warn+skip. Verified end-to-end on a trivial deterministic build (reproduces → rc0; wrong sha → rc1).</li> <li><strong>Decided against</strong> a separate deployed-path attestation field and rebuild-inside-<code>--check</code>: kept <code>--check</code> fast (no build) and <code>--verify-build</code> as the heavy CI lane (reference workflow shipped in the template), one <code>artifact</code> path (worktree-relative). yarn's exact defect is caught by deploy-line-recorded + verify-build.</li> <li><strong>Chain.</strong> host-lifecycle v0.8.0 (tagged, <code>cargo test</code> 31 green) → host-template <code>e49d8d9</code> (spine requirement + escape clause + reference <code>reproducible-build.yml</code> + UPGRADING <code>e3b174d</code>, requires v0.8.0; <code>tools/host-lifecycle</code> bumped) → agentic-host (<code>.host</code> → <code>e49d8d9</code>, <code>plan/0005</code>).</li> <li><strong>Follow-on (honest gap):</strong> host-lint's <em>own</em> reproducible build is not yet wired into this repo's <code>.host-software</code> — real determinism work (pinned toolchain, reproducible release artifact). This milestone shipped the mechanism + requirement, not its application to our software.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-17--host-lint-reproducible-build-plan0006-dogfoods-plan0005"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-17--host-lint-reproducible-build-plan0006-dogfoods-plan0005">2026-06-17 — host-lint reproducible build (<code>plan/0006</code>, dogfoods <code>plan/0005</code>)</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Why.</strong> <code>plan/0005</code> left host-lint (this repo's own greenfield software) with no recorded reproducible build. Driving it through the methodology surfaced the real defects.</li> <li><strong>Two prerequisites the process exposed</strong> (software-first, host-lint repo <code>24ecf32</code>): (1) <code>Cargo.lock</code> was <strong>gitignored</strong> — a binary with floating deps can't reproduce; tracked it (pins host-grammar's git rev). (2) No pinned toolchain — added <code>rust-toolchain.toml</code> (channel <code>1.95.0</code>).</li> <li><strong>Recipe (in <code>.host-software</code>).</strong> <code>CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$PWD=. --remap-path-prefix=${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}=/cargo" cargo build --release --locked</code>. Same version/target → expected same hash; if CI diverges, that's the cross-env finding and CI's hash becomes canonical.</li> <li><strong>Scope.</strong> <code>host</code> component is a README front-door (no artifact). Same-environment (pinned-toolchain) reproducibility is guaranteed; container-level environment-independence is future hardening.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-17--host-lint-reproducibility-it-took-a-pinned-build-container-cont-of-plan0006"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-17--host-lint-reproducibility-it-took-a-pinned-build-container-cont-of-plan0006">2026-06-17 — host-lint reproducibility: it took a pinned build container (cont. of plan/0006)</a></h3> <ul> <li>The earlier <code>plan/0006</code> entry recorded same-environment reproducibility and hash <code>782a0840…</code>; that hash and the same-env framing are <strong>superseded</strong> by this entry. Achieving real (environment-independent) reproducibility took more, and the final recorded artifact is <strong><code>a7e276c0…</code></strong>.</li> <li><strong>Path remapping was a red herring.</strong> <code>--remap-path-prefix</code> (workspace/cargo-home/sysroot) changed nothing — CI's hash was byte-identical across 2-remap and 3-remap recipes, proving paths weren't embedded. The real cross-machine diff was <strong>linker metadata</strong>: <code>.note.gnu.build-id</code> + the <code>.comment</code> section (build host's gcc/distro). Fixed in-source: <code>[profile.release] strip = true</code> (Cargo.toml) + <code>--build-id=none</code> (<code>.cargo/config.toml</code>).</li> <li><strong><code>trim-paths</code> is nightly-only</strong> on Cargo 1.95 — don't use it on stable; it fails to parse the manifest.</li> <li><strong>Even after strip+build-id, local (WSL) ≠ CI (GitHub ubuntu)</strong> — different <code>ld</code>/<code>gcc</code>/distro produce different bytes. Resolved by pinning the canonical environment to the <code>rust:1.95.0</code> image <strong>by digest</strong> (<code>sha256:f49565f1…</code>), recorded as <code>.host-software</code> <code>toolchain</code>. The <code>reproducible-build.yml</code> CI job runs <code>in</code> that image; <code>software --verify-build</code> reproduces <code>a7e276c0…</code> there (green). Confirmed by a double-build in the same container locally (Docker).</li> <li><strong>Lesson:</strong> reproducible builds = pin the <em>toolchain</em> AND the <em>OS/linker</em> (a container by digest) AND strip build metadata AND lock deps. Flags alone don't cross distros. <code>software --verify-build</code> must run in the pinned image to be meaningful.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--plan0007-agentic-tell-grammar-engine-prose-tells"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--plan0007-agentic-tell-grammar-engine-prose-tells">2026-06-18 — plan/0007 agentic-tell grammar engine (prose tells)</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Prose-tell engine in host-grammar</strong> (<code>tells</code> module, v0.2.0), called by host-lint (v0.3.0). Token-free adaptation of the tropes.fyi catalog: lexical phrase rules + structural equations (negative parallelism, tricolon, anaphora <code>Σ max(0,L−2)²</code>, countdown, self-answered question, listicle, participial tail, false range, punchy/bold shape) + a composite density <code>Score</code>. None of the equations need a model or POS tags. Replaced with <code>unicode-segmentation</code> (zero transitive deps) + hand-rolled rules. Engine decisions made during planning can rot; re-check dep weight at implementation.</li> <li><strong>Wiring:</strong> host-lint <code>--stdin</code> runs prose tells alongside naming tells (titles/commit subjects); <code>--prose <files></code> scans docs on demand; <code>--json</code> gained <code>cite</code>. No MCP — the CLI + skill is the agent interface.</li> <li><strong>Verification lane = allium, NOT TLA+.</strong> Per <code>call/0002</code>, the equations are functional invariants (allium's lane); TLA+ is reserved for timing/concurrency and there is no interleaving here, so the escalation bridge does not fire. "</code> before a capital — true of real prose).</li> <li><strong>Comment hygiene feedback:</strong> code comments must be terse single-line OR proper rustdoc/API form — no motivating "waffle" paragraphs (it's the slop the prose engine flags). Each worker owns a contiguous sentence chunk and returns its per-sentence tells + ordered metadata; the <strong>merge is concatenation by chunk index</strong>, so a run straddling a boundary rejoins automatically and the cross-sentence equations run once over merged metadata. Result byte-identical to <code>scan_prose</code>. host-lint <code>--prose</code> routes through it.</li> <li><strong>Both verification lanes, per <code>call/0015</code>.</strong> The escalation bridge of <code>call/0002</code> fired for the first time with an honest trigger: the merge math is functional (<strong>allium/PBT</strong>: <code>scan_chunked == scan_prose</code> for all k), but "the assembled output is correct for <strong>every worker-completion interleaving</strong>" is temporal (<strong>Specula/TLA+</strong>). Don't reach for TLA+ on a pure fold; reach for it when interleaving/ordering is the property.</li> <li><strong>First TLA+ spec in the repo:</strong> <code>plan/0008-parallel-prose-scan/spec/ParallelScan.tla</code> (+ <code>.cfg</code>). Candidate follow-up: have host-lifecycle install/refresh the hook binary at the pin.</li> <li><strong>Re-pin:</strong> host-grammar <code>d83b348</code> → host-lint <code>dff6895</code> → <code>.host-software</code> artifact <code>4655f966…</code>, double-build reproducible in the pinned container.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--plan0009-host-lifecycle-v081-software---install-hooks"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--plan0009-host-lifecycle-v081-software---install-hooks">2026-06-18 — plan/0009 host-lifecycle v0.8.1: software --install-hooks</a></h3> <ul> <li>Closes the fresh-clone hook-sync gap from plan/0008. <code>host-lifecycle software --install-hooks .</code> copies each component's <code>hooks</code> dispatch script into the repo's hooks dir (resolved via <code>git rev-parse --git-path hooks</code>) as <strong>pre-commit</strong> and <strong>commit-msg</strong>, plus the deploy binary the script invokes. New optional <code>hooks = <script></code> field on the <code>.host-software</code> stanza (host-lint's is <code>pre-commit</code>).</li> <li><strong>Gate = worktree-at-pin, NOT byte hash.</strong> The recorded <code>artifact</code> hash is the <em>pinned container's</em> output; a local toolchain legitimately differs, and requiring a match would force a Docker build just to get the gating hook. So install-hooks requires the worktree at its recorded pin (audited source) + the artifact present; the canonical-hash match is an informational note (<code>verified</code> vs <code>local build</code>), never a blocker. (Same reason <code>software --check</code>'s artifact attestation is environment-sensitive.)</li> <li>Old host-lifecycle revs ignore the new <code>hooks</code> key (unknown keys are dropped), so the CI jobs pinned to v0.8.0/v0.7.1 are unaffected; they don't use <code>--install-hooks</code>.</li> <li>Fresh-clone setup in CLAUDE.md now ends: materialize → skill symlink → build host-lint → <code>software --install-hooks .</code>.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--plan0010-markdown-aware-prose-scanning"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--plan0010-markdown-aware-prose-scanning">2026-06-18 — plan/0010 markdown-aware prose scanning</a></h3> <ul> <li><code>host-grammar::scan_prose_markdown</code> + <code>tell_score_markdown</code> (via <strong>pulldown-cmark</strong>, 6 tiny pure-Rust deps — the same parser mdBook uses here, so the reproducible anchor holds). Parses markdown into prose blocks: <strong>code blocks and inline code excluded</strong>, <strong>link/image URLs dropped</strong> (visible text kept), <strong>headings scanned for diction but not counted as prose paragraphs or sentence runs</strong> (parallel <code>## Section one/two/three</code> headings were tripping anaphora). <code>shape()</code> reads bold-first from the parse. host-lint routes <code>.md</code> sources to it; titles/comments/commit-messages stay on the plain engine.</li> <li><strong>Triggered by dogfooding <code>--prose</code> on the host README.</strong> Real bug it exposed: the flat engine scanned <em>fenced code blocks as prose</em> (em-dashes/words/arrows inside code falsely flagged) — the serious correctness issue, not just the heading miscount.</li> <li><strong>punchy-fragments tuned to strictly-more-than-half</strong> single-sentence paragraphs (<code>> 0.5</code>, was <code>>= 0.5</code>): a short doc (the README's 4 body paragraphs) is not staccato. A definition refinement ("more than half"), not an overfit.</li> <li><strong>The property lane earned its keep again:</strong> <code>every_tell_has_positive_weight</code> (arbitrary Unicode) caught a latent panic — <code>lexical()</code> computed match indices on the lowercased copy but sliced the <em>original</em> text; a length-changing case-fold (e.g. before a multi-byte <code>→</code>) put the slice off a char boundary. Fixed by slicing the lowercased copy. Lesson: never mix byte indices between a string and its <code>to_lowercase()</code>.</li> <li>Re-pin: host-grammar <code>bba4895</code> → host-lint <code>b6ad359</code> → <code>.host-software</code> artifact <code>daead690</code>, reproducible in the pinned container. README now <code>host-lint --prose</code> exit 0.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--decoration-tells-report-every-occurrence-not-just-the-first"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--decoration-tells-report-every-occurrence-not-just-the-first">2026-06-18 — decoration tells: report every occurrence, not just the first</a></h3> <ul> <li><code>lexical()</code> had <code>if decoration { break }</code> ("one decoration tell per phrase is enough signal"), so a doc with 20 em-dashes surfaced <strong>one</strong> finding and the rest had to be found by hand; re-running after a fix just revealed the next. Removed the break: every em-dash / smart-quote / arrow is now its own finding, so <code>--prose</code> lists them all and the gate keeps warning until each is gone. Density reflects the real decoration volume (the conservative abs+density gate keeps it from over-firing on a few stray dashes). host-grammar <code>8091261</code> → host-lint <code>7244f5a</code> → artifact <code>bb1489cf</code>.</li> <li>Surfaced by cleaning the <code>host</code> front-door README (20 em-dashes, only 1 flagged). Lesson: a recall-biased "one signal is enough" is wrong for <em>actionable</em> cleanup tells — flag every instance.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--per-platform-builds-in-host-software-issue-1"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--per-platform-builds-in-host-software-issue-1">2026-06-18 — per-platform builds in .host-software (issue #1)</a></h3> <ul> <li>One source <code>pin</code> can ship on several platforms: host-lifecycle v0.9.0 adds <code>[build "<name>" "<platform>"]</code> subsections, each with its own <code>build</code>/<code>toolchain</code>/<code>artifact</code>/<code>deploy</code>/<code>repro-exempt</code> plus an <code>attest-host</code> (the OS from <code>std::env::consts::OS</code> that reproduces it). <code>--check</code>/<code>--verify-build</code> iterate the builds and attest each only on its <code>attest-host</code>, <strong>skipping</strong> foreign-host builds rather than failing — a Linux runner can't reproduce the Windows artifact. The flat single-build form is preserved as the default <code>builds_view</code> entry (no attest-host → attest anywhere), so single-platform components are untouched.</li> <li>This is a <strong>spine change</strong> (the <code>.host-software</code> schema is methodology), so the design is recorded in the template spine (host-template STRUCTURE.md + CLAUDE.md + UPGRADING ledger <code>c137567</code>, requires v0.9.0) and <strong>not</strong> as an agentic-host <code>call/</code> — an accepted methodology-scoped decision fails the anti-ouroboros <code>validate</code> gate. Precedent: plan/0005 (reproducible-build anchor) recorded its spine change the same way, with no agentic-host methodology call/. plan/0011.</li> <li>Deferred: automated cross-OS worktree materialization (checkout a Windows tree from an ext4 bare store). The recipe records each platform build; a human materializes the foreign-OS worktree and runs <code>--verify-build</code> there.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18----check-artifact-mismatch-is-a-note-not-drift-host-lifecycle-v091"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18----check-artifact-mismatch-is-a-note-not-drift-host-lifecycle-v091">2026-06-18 — --check artifact mismatch is a note, not DRIFT (host-lifecycle v0.9.1)</a></h3> <ul> <li><code>software --check</code> hard-failed (DRIFT, exit 1) when a locally-built artifact was present in the canonical worktree and its hash differed from the recorded canonical hash. But the canonical hash is the <em>pinned container's</em> output; a local toolchain legitimately differs, so the DRIFT only ever fired on a dev box that had run <code>cargo build</code> (fresh clones and CI — which builds in the container — were already clean, since <code>target/</code> is gitignored and the artifact is absent). This contradicted the <code>--install-hooks</code> decision (plan/0009), which already gates on worktree-at-pin and treats the hash as informational.</li> <li>Fix: <code>--check</code>'s artifact attestation now prints <code>verified</code> on a match and <code>note … local build (differs from canonical)</code> on a mismatch — never a failure. Spine clarified in host-template <code>d3dc5ed</code> + UPGRADING (requires v0.9.1). plan/0011 follow-on.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-06-18--dogfood-allium-for-real-specs-live-with-the-software-plan0012"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-18--dogfood-allium-for-real-specs-live-with-the-software-plan0012">2026-06-18 — dogfood allium for real; specs live with the software (plan/0012)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Our two .allium files were hand-written pseudo-syntax that real <code>allium-cli 3.4.2</code> rejects (no <code>-- allium: N</code> marker; free-form English clauses aren't valid block items). LESSON: the project's demonstrated convention (git history) is the spec to match, over a textbook default.</li> <li><strong>Both fold-backs re-validated at the 4B bar</strong> (local Qwen-3.5-4B @ Q8_0, <code>:8888</code>), this time on the <em>real built tool's</em> printed output: the 4B answered the change-class (<code>removes-flag</code>) without naming a level, and copied the exact <code>call/0031</code> token even with a planted phase-name distractor ("the phase is named reproducible-build") — the precise conflation that fumbled in the de-risk. Tool-printed literal command ⇒ correct copy.</li> <li><strong>Remaining for plan/0025 (#41):</strong> the spine lifecycle manifest (dedup the three prose copies + add <code>release</code>), revise "unconditional"→"every phase emits a receipt", an UPGRADING entry — then cut host-lifecycle's own <code>0.19.0</code> release THROUGH <code>host-lifecycle release host-lifecycle</code> (a tool = tag-only path), dogfooding the orchestration on the tool that built it. The version tag is deferred to that dogfood; the three #40 commits sit at 0.18.1 until then.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-21--plan0025-41-lifecycle-manifest--receipt-gate-shipped-to-the-spine-and-dogfooded-release-dogfood-deferred"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-21--plan0025-41-lifecycle-manifest--receipt-gate-shipped-to-the-spine-and-dogfooded-release-dogfood-deferred">2026-06-21 — plan/0025 #41: lifecycle manifest + receipt gate shipped to the spine and dogfooded; release-dogfood deferred</a></h2> <p>Shipped the spine half of plan/0025: host-template <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> (8 phases, modality first-class — spine <code>617e420</code>), the "unconditional, no opt-out" → <strong>every phase emits a receipt</strong> reframe across CLAUDE.md + STRUCTURE.md (point at the manifest, stop re-typing the order), and the UPGRADING ledger entry keyed to it (<code>3194493</code>, two-commit pattern: <code>spine:</code> makes the change, <code>UPGRADING:</code> keys to its SHA). agentic-host adopted it (<code>.host</code> applied <code>617e420</code> via the <code>verify</code> grep) and its <strong>receipt gate is live and green</strong> — all ten phase/component receipts back-filled <em>through the tool</em> (<code>receipt --record</code>): <code>done</code> for adopt/embed×2/verify/publish/upgrade + the host-lint release; <code>skip</code> for classify/remap (greenfield) + the read-only <code>host</code> component. Always read the <em>current</em> pin's version, not the plan's stale example.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-21--correction-the-methodology-is-multi-software-host--tools-are-where-components-not-a-category-error"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-21--correction-the-methodology-is-multi-software-host--tools-are-where-components-not-a-category-error">2026-06-21 — CORRECTION: the methodology IS multi-software; host-* tools are Where components, NOT a "category error"</a></h2> <p>The bullet above ("Tooling is NOT Where-room software ... embedding a tool as a Where component would be a category error") is <strong>WRONG</strong> — corrected with the operator. [[agentic-naming-ontology]], which needs the same nuance: host-* are tools AND software).</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-21--plan0029-built--agentic-host-self-upgraded-to-the-nested-where-room-layout"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-21--plan0029-built--agentic-host-self-upgraded-to-the-nested-where-room-layout">2026-06-21 — plan/0029 built + agentic-host self-upgraded to the nested Where-room layout</a></h2> <p>Shipped plan/0029 end to end. <strong>host-lifecycle v0.19.0</strong> materializes the Where room under <code>software/<name>/<branch>/</code> (bare store at <code>.git</code>, worktrees keyed by branch with slashes preserved; the canonical worktree is the recorded <code>branch</code>, default <code>main</code>, at the pin), plus <code>--item <name>[@<branch>]</code> addressing, a re-materialize <code>worktree prune</code>, a dangling-generated-link check in <code>software --check</code>, and a tag-only first release. Resolved (operator decision A): a <code>branch =</code> field (default <code>main</code>); the canonical is checked out ON its branch reset to the pin (<code>-B branch pin</code>), and <code>--check</code> still gates <code>HEAD == pin</code> so the anchor is unchanged. LESSON: starting the implementation is the cheapest way to find the design gaps a review misses — surface them, do not paper over.</li> <li><strong>A <code>replace_all</code> silently missed one path-deriving site</strong> (<code>spec_lane_problems</code>, different indentation), leaving the spec-lane gate scanning the OLD path — it would have gone <strong>inert post-migration</strong> (specs no longer enforced), and its test passed only because the fixture used the old path too. Caught by asking "is this test green for the right reason?" LESSON: drive a model-change refactor with the compiler (remove a field and it enumerates every site); a <code>root.join(name)</code>-style path is not type-checked, so grep for it explicitly and confirm each test exercises the NEW path.</li> <li><strong>Residuals deferred honestly:</strong> a tool teardown subcommand + a dirty-worktree guard (agentic-host's teardown was done by hand, safe for the single adopter whose worktrees sat at their pins), porcelain worktree resolution + case-collision detection (review robustness, edge cases), and the Fen-4B ergonomics run (the design was tested on neutral synthetic fixtures — <code>demo</code>/<code>comp</code>/<code>a</code>/<code>b</code>, not host-* — in the integration suite). The link-skills.sh shell-to-Rust port for Where-component skills rides with plan/0028, when such skills first exist.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-21--plan0030-prose-hygiene-lane-re-derivable-record-exclusion-not-a-hash-ack-receipts-re-homing-deferred"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-21--plan0030-prose-hygiene-lane-re-derivable-record-exclusion-not-a-hash-ack-receipts-re-homing-deferred">2026-06-21 — plan/0030 prose-hygiene lane: re-derivable record exclusion (not a hash ack); receipts re-homing deferred</a></h2> <p>Wrote plan/0030 to turn the built-but-unused <code>host-lint --prose</code> into a real, enforced, weak-agent-executable gate lane. A five-lens adversarial review (<code>plan/0030/design-review.md</code>) re-scoped the original three-strand sketch (a <code>--prose --all</code> walk, a hash-pinned <code>.host-lint-receipts</code> ack, a five-file receipts re-homing). Two operator decisions came out of it.</p> <ul> <li><strong>No hash-freeze ack — exclude immutable records by a re-derivable predicate + the existing fence.</strong> A <code>(path, hash, reason)</code> ack would be the project's first SELF-ASSERTED receipt, inverting <code>call/0017</code> ("evidence is re-derived, never self-asserted"): the hash proves only "bytes unchanged" while the GATE/FREEZE classification stays human-asserted, so a weak agent greens the gate by freezing a trope-laden doc with a plausible reason. Worse, "edit lapses the ack → clean to zero" would force prose-rewriting the very immutable records it protects (a MADR link-fix, a Status flip, a MEMORY correction — against <code>CLAUDE.md</code> §6), re-introducing the <code>call/0009</code> blanket-exclude error that <code>call/0019</code> superseded. The need is already met by shipped mechanisms: the prose scanner already skips <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fenced blocks (box the irreducible citation, the rest of the file stays linted) and <code>.host-lintignore</code> whole-file-excludes the append-only <code>MEMORY.md</code>. So the mechanism is: classify Live-vs-record by a re-derivable predicate (machine-readable inline milestone <code>STATUS:</code> + MADR <code>Status:</code>), reword Live to zero, box record citations in fences, path-exclude append-only. DON'T re-propose a hash ack — it was reviewed and rejected.</li> <li><strong>Receipts-family re-homing deferred to its own dual-format migration.</strong> The settled ontology is sound (<code>.host-receipts</code> = adopt/upgrade, <code>.host-lifecycle-receipts</code> = operational executions, the uniform <code>.host-<tool>-receipts</code> rule, applied-set moved out of <code>.host</code>), but BUILDING it rewrites two shipped, gate-bearing files and the installed binary breaks: <code>applied_ids</code>/<code>upgrade_claim_problems</code> read the applied-set only from <code>.host</code> (moving it silently un-applies every recorded upgrade), <code>receipt_gate_problems</code> reads a single <code>.host-receipts</code> (splitting it HAZARDs the embed/release gate), the <code>--record</code> writers still target the old files, and CI + the commit hooks cold-install a pinned old-format binary. It needs a binary that reads both layouts → CI repin → data move → UPGRADING entry, atomically — its own milestone. <code>.host-prove-receipts</code> cut until host-prove emits receipts. plan/0030 deliberately reuses the EXISTING <code>.host-receipts</code> verify receipt and depends on none of the re-homing.</li> <li><strong>The clean, not the classify, is the hard part for a weak agent.</strong> <code>--prose</code> flags a line, not a span or a fix (one em-dash emits ten byte-identical records); some tropes are span-less whole-doc diagnoses ("21/23 bullets open with bold lead-ins"); there are ~1,652 trope-lines. plan/0030 D2 fixes this: per-occurrence spans + mechanical fix hints + de-dup, with density/structural tropes scoped to advisory so the clean-to-zero bar covers only locatable tropes. Qwen-3.5-4B classified 10/10 clear-case docs correctly ("no ambiguity") — necessary but not sufficient: the margin needs the machine-readable <code>STATUS:</code>, and the clean needs the tool spans. The repo-wide clean (D5) still WAITS for the operator's literal front-door sentence.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-22--plan0028-operator-rulings-qa-round-and-re-cut"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-22--plan0028-operator-rulings-qa-round-and-re-cut">2026-06-22 — plan/0028 operator rulings (q&a round) and re-cut</a></h2> <p>The plan/0028 adversarial review (<code>design-review.md</code>) owed four decision-level findings. A q&a round settled them; <code>call/0020</code> and plan/0028's README now carry the full rationale, so this is the index-level note.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Self-cert: the RELEASED, PINNED host-lifecycle gates/releases agentic-host; the worktree build only develops the next version.</strong> The operator's stated why is AVOIDING MIXED STATE: a moving, possibly-uncommitted worktree binary certifying its own release conflates the thing-being-developed with the thing-vouching-for-the-release. A released pin is a fixed, known-good, immutable certifier. This is the spine's "self-referential software is excluded, not bypassed", one rung up. CONSEQUENCE for execution: only the release-dogfood step uses the worktree binary; the standing <code>software --check</code>/<code>--verify-build</code> gate runs the released pin.</li> <li><strong>host-grammar pin: converge BOTH host-lifecycle and host-lint on a NEW host-grammar tag at the proofs HEAD (<code>fbd2e6c</code>), re-releasing host-lint.</strong> host-lint is therefore NOT "unchanged": new <code>Cargo.lock</code> → new binary bytes → new <code>artifact</code> sha256 → re-pin + new release receipt + green <code>--verify-build</code>. Freezing at the stale <code>8091261</code> was rejected (it drops the plan/0023 Apalache/TLAPS proofs from what the toolchain compiles against). The "what host-lifecycle emits is what host-lint accepts" symmetry requires the SAME single grammar entry in the lock (today the lock wrongly carries two: <code>8091261</code> via host-lint and a floating <code>fbd2e6c</code> direct).</li> <li><strong>Spec lane: host-lifecycle and host-prove become SPEC-BEARING</strong> (the non-default choice). Author an <code>.allium</code> + <code>.obligations</code> for each via the elicit/distill skills and wire the allium lane in each producer CI; this activates the spec/obligation MUST + re-derivation digests for them in agentic-host's gate. Deliberately accepted added scope.</li> <li><strong>Spine-first is already discharged by plan/0029</strong> (the residency clause folded into host-template); <code>call/0020</code> APPLIES it, not forks it. No spine work owed by plan/0028.</li> <li><strong>Re-cut:</strong> the linear order was not a valid topological sort (host-lifecycle is both the migration tool and a target). Replaced by the Readiness pass (producer repos: rev-pin both git deps, commit <code>Cargo.lock</code>, strip/build-id hardening, reproducible double-build, author specs; NO orchestration releases) then the atomic Cutover pass (drop submodules + prune <code>.git/modules</code>, add <code>.host-software</code> stanzas + back-fill receipts in ONE commit so the recurring-per-component gate is never RED on push-to-main, seed-first fresh-clone order with seed <code>--rev</code> == the pin, release dogfood via the worktree binary with the PRODUCER TAG authoritative, CI rewire + cold-clone link-resolution job last).</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-22--plan0028-readiness-mechanical-pinshardening-done-across-all-four-producers"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-22--plan0028-readiness-mechanical-pinshardening-done-across-all-four-producers">2026-06-22 — plan/0028 Readiness: mechanical pins/hardening done across all four producers</a></h2> <p>Completed and CI-green (each pushed software-first): host-grammar <strong>v0.3.0</strong> tagged at <code>9d51468</code> (bumped Cargo.toml <code>0.2.0 → 0.3.0</code> ON TOP of the proofs HEAD <code>fbd2e6c</code>, since main carried the Apalache/TLAPS proof lanes under an unbumped version, a version-floor; tag points at the bump commit, which includes the proofs); host-lint re-pinned host-grammar <code>8091261 → 9d51468</code> (full SHA) at main <code>93a43fa</code> (68 tests still green with NO test change, confirming the proofs commit was spec-side only, so host-lint's detection behaviour is unchanged); host-lifecycle pinned BOTH git deps, added <code>[profile.release] strip=true</code> + <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> build-id=none, UN-gitignored + committed <code>Cargo.lock</code> at <code>a04c460</code> (69 tests green); host-prove added the same hardening at <code>b844599</code> (zero external deps, lockfile already tracked).</p> <ul> <li><strong>NON-OBVIOUS LOCKFILE CONSTRAINT (the one-entry rule's real mechanics):</strong> cargo keys a git source in <code>Cargo.lock</code> by the FULL source string including the <code>?rev=</code>/<code>?tag=</code> query, so <code>rev = "9d51468"</code> (short), <code>rev = "9d51468ab1f0…"</code> (full), and <code>tag = "v0.3.0"</code> are THREE DISTINCT sources even when they resolve to the same commit. To get the design-review's required SINGLE host-grammar entry shared by host-lifecycle (direct) and host-lint (transitive), BOTH Cargo.tomls MUST pin host-grammar with the byte-identical <code>rev</code> string. I used the full 40-char SHA in both. Verify with <code>cargo tree -d</code> ("nothing to print" = deduped) and <code>grep -c 'name = "host-grammar"' Cargo.lock</code> == 1.</li> <li><strong>ORDERING the re-cut implied but did not spell out:</strong> the host-lint PRODUCER re-pin (its own repo + main push) must precede host-lifecycle's lock regeneration, because host-lifecycle pins host-lint by rev and only a host-lint commit that already uses <code>9d51468</code> lets the transitive + direct host-grammar collapse to one entry. The agentic-host <code>.host-software</code> host-lint re-pin (new artifact hash + receipt) is still Cutover; producer-side and consumer-side of "re-release host-lint" are different passes.</li> <li><strong>Docker IS available here</strong> (29.1.5), so the reproducible container-build proof (and the <code>--verify-build</code> in Cutover) can run; WSL still needs <code>HOST_LIFECYCLE_DOCKER_NETWORK=host</code>.</li> <li>REMAINING Readiness: the spec-bearing work (<code>.allium</code> + <code>.obligations</code> + allium lane for host-lifecycle and host-prove, via distill) and the container reproducible-build proof; then the whole Cutover.</li> </ul> <h2 id="2026-06-22--plan0028-readiness-host-lifecycle--host-prove-are-now-spec-bearing-ruling-4-ci-green"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-22--plan0028-readiness-host-lifecycle--host-prove-are-now-spec-bearing-ruling-4-ci-green">2026-06-22 — plan/0028 Readiness: host-lifecycle + host-prove are now spec-bearing (ruling #4), CI-green</a></h2> <p>Authored via the distill skill, modelled on host-lint's spec (the CLI-verdict-lifecycle shape). host-prove (<code>e7d0153</code>): <code>host-prove.allium</code> models the run-to-verdict lifecycle (one verifier, one verdict, exit proved=0 / refuted=1 / unusable=2) plus the soundness-bound invariants (#9: a PASS carries a bound; TLAPS unbounded, bounded tools never claim unbounded), 27 obligations dispositioned. host-lifecycle (<code>fd603b2</code>): <code>host-lifecycle.allium</code> SCOPED to the <code>software --check</code> verdict over Where components (the gate-bearing core), recipe-dispatched on <code>declares_artifact</code>, with the pin anchor, host#14 reproducibility, and the R1 receipt gate; 33 obligations dispositioned. The bulk reword was done by four parallel subagents (one per file-group), then verified centrally (prose zero on both repos + the seven phrases intact + <code>software --check</code> green) and the diffs reviewed.</p> <p><strong>LESSON (ai-diction is density-weighted, not a per-token flag).</strong> The <code>harness</code> ai-diction on <code>`kani:<harness>`</code> (plan/0033 called it an "accepted residual that cannot be reworded") is NOT a hard false positive. ai-diction words carry weight 0.5 ("one word is never a verdict"); the gate is an absolute/ density threshold over the DOCUMENT. host-template/CLAUDE.md had <code>harness</code> TWICE (the <code>kani:<harness></code> token at :355 and prose "named harness" at :365); the two summed past the gate, flagging :355. In isolation a single <code>harness</code> line is clean. Rewording the :365 prose occurrence ("the named harness, invariant, or theorem" -> "the rung's named target") dropped the count to one and cleared the flag, no token rename, no engine change. Corollary: <code>scan_prose_text</code> (the prose audit) takes NO allowlist, so a LEXICON entry cannot mask a prose trope (LEXICON masks only the naming audit, <code>scan_text_with_allow</code>); a legitimate-but-flagged prose word is cleared by rewording/reducing density or boxing in a <code>host-lint:ignore</code> fence, never by LEXICON.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="plan0039-cut-the-reconcile-arm-evolves-to-concept-as-uri-designed-not-built"><a class="header" href="#plan0039-cut-the-reconcile-arm-evolves-to-concept-as-uri-designed-not-built">plan/0039 cut: the reconcile arm evolves to concept-as-URI (designed, not built)</a></h2> <p>The operator rejected EVERY inline form of the reconcile annotation on aesthetic grounds (a trailing comment, a comment-pair wrapping a span, a markdown link carrying the directive, an out-of-line metadata block). One canonical definition at a stable <code>{#id}</code> anchor on a concepts page (generated from <code>.host-software</code> for the project-scoped ones, so it cannot drift); everywhere else POINTS to it with a relative-path link (<code>concepts.md#components</code>) instead of restating. Validated empirically: stock mdBook v0.5.2 resolves the relative <code>#id</code> links with no custom generator pass; the real Qwen-3.5-4B authored pointer links 3/3 (incl. the <code>verifiers</code> route the inline classification step had failed) because pointing carries no "is this a restatement?" judgment, the exact step that exhausted the 4B on every inline form. Lineage cited outward: DRY/SSOT (Hunt & Thomas), reflection-on-action (Schön), Linked Data (Berners-Lee). Citation principle (operator): kind to predecessors and peers OUTWARD; rigorous with ourselves INWARD.</p> <p><strong><code>family</code> -> <code>components</code>:</strong> "family" was an agentic-host overfit (host-* tools happen to share a prefix); the methodology's own word for the <code>.host-software</code> set is "components". Renamed across the host-lifecycle binary + its tests + the spine <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> <code>[components]</code> stanza, NO ALIAS (an alias split validation across two surfaces — the <code>restates=</code> ledger-gate uses RECONCILE_KINDS, the assertion-match used the alias — so a <code>restates = family</code> flagged unknown; operator vetoed the alias, "fix properly"). Suite green (86/86).</p> <p><strong>The bite lesson (two cast reviews, both this session):</strong> link-integrity ("the link resolves") is NOT the bite the inline check had. A dropped component is simply never linked, so nothing catches the absence; "definitions match SSOT" is tautological (generated from it). So refined-B needs a <strong>coverage check</strong> (every <code>.host-software</code> component/verifier MUST be referenced somewhere, drop-fails-by-absence) + a <strong>declared-anchor check</strong> (target must be a known concept id, not any resolving fragment). Cutover is <strong>deprecate-then-retire</strong>, fail-safe: a retired checker HARD-FAILS on a surviving annotation (never silently inert, the cold-adopter fail-unsafe Bly flagged); a bookless adopter SKIPS, not no-ops (Orin). Retiring a days-old spine mechanism is itself churn, so deprecate first, retire one spine revision later via UPGRADING.</p> <p><strong>First-mover gap (operator decision):</strong> agentic-host's annotations are already deleted, so its restatements (the tool list, the layout) are briefly UNGUARDED until the coverage check ships. Operator accepted this as a calculated risk; an adopter is never asked to take it.</p> <p><strong>State at write-up:</strong> plan/0039 cut + PLAN.md row committed (558da13). The build (concepts page, the 3 checks, deprecate inline, spine doctrine rewrite, UPGRADING, release) is pending.</p> <p><strong>Aside:</strong> filed connollydavid/host-lifecycle#1 — <code>host-lifecycle next <dir></code> returns <code>0000</code> for a directory with no numbered entries (e.g. the host root) instead of erroring, a fail-unsafe footgun at the weak-agent bar. <code>next plan</code> -> <code>0039</code> and <code>next call</code> -> <code>0023</code> are correct.</p> <h2 id="plan0039-design-refined-and-build-started-2026-06-24-corrects-the-entry-above"><a class="header" href="#plan0039-design-refined-and-build-started-2026-06-24-corrects-the-entry-above">plan/0039 design refined and build started (2026-06-24, corrects the entry above)</a></h2> <p>The plan/0039 entry above is superseded on three points; corrected here (append-only). Pending: convert agentic-host's docs to pointers, spine doctrine, release.</p> <h2 id="plan0039-complete-concept-as-uri-shipped-as-host-lifecycle-v0250-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#plan0039-complete-concept-as-uri-shipped-as-host-lifecycle-v0250-2026-06-25">plan/0039 complete: concept-as-URI shipped as host-lifecycle v0.25.0 (2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p>The reconcile arm now sources project facts from <code>.host-software</code> (components are the <code>[software]</code> members minus a <code>front-door = true</code> member; verifiers are a <code>[verification]</code> drivers stanza) and runs three checks over the tracked docs: link-integrity, declared-anchor, and coverage (each project-local home names its full <code>.host-software</code> set). The spine doctrine + the <code>UPGRADING</code> entry (<code>[upgrade 7be692f]</code>) are in host-template (<code>e4f6207</code>); <code>call/0023</code> records the software decision.</p> <p><strong>Adversarial review + a real Qwen-3.5-4B run caught two holes before release:</strong> a <code>{#id}</code> must sit at the END of a heading (mdBook slugifies a start-placed one to a different id, so a start-placed home passed reconcile but 404'd) and <code>home_section</code> must run to the next <em>same-or-higher</em> heading (the 4B authored a sub-headed home whose members fell outside a stop-at-any-heading section, falsely failing coverage). Both fixed in code with tests. The 4B authored a home, a <code>[verification]</code> stanza, and an annotation-to-pointer migration once the doctrine <em>showed</em> the exact forms (the worked example) — it near-misses unaided. Released v0.25.0 (commit <code>0f2a4da</code>, artifact <code>e3e1ef02</code>), re-pinned, dogfood-verified (reconcile + <code>software --check</code> green on the released binary).</p> <p><strong>Process slip recorded:</strong> <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> scans <strong>tracked</strong> files (via <code>git ls-files</code>), so prose-check a NEW doc only AFTER <code>git add</code>/commit — checking an untracked file reports a false clean. Two diction tropes (false-range from a <code>from … to</code> pair, negative-parallelism from "honors no other") slipped into committed docs this way and were fixed in a follow-up. See [[ai-diction-traps-in-my-writing]].</p> <h2 id="plan0042-complete--the-receipted-task-graph-host-lifecycle-v0260-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#plan0042-complete--the-receipted-task-graph-host-lifecycle-v0260-2026-06-25">plan/0042 complete — the receipted task graph (host-lifecycle v0.26.0, 2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p>In-plan tasks became first-class. A task is an anchored <code>### </code> heading under <code>## Build sequence</code>, keyed <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code> (a stable global id, not a position), with <code>- depends:</code> (a local <code>#anchor</code> or a cross-milestone <code>plan/NNNN#anchor</code>), <code>- verify:</code> (a shell command, or <code>attested <call/NNNN | operator></code>), and <code>- inputs:</code> (files a mechanical verify covers). The project's tasks form ONE graph across milestones; the tool derives the parallel frontier (tasks whose deps all carry a done receipt), default linear. Shipped in host-lifecycle v0.26.0 (<code>430876c</code>, artifact <code>52e8414a</code>): the <code>tasks</code> subcommand (status / check / record / rederive / new), the <code>.host-task-receipts</code> ledger (a deliberate third receipt kind, <code>call/0024</code>), the per-task gate in <code>software --check</code>, the task-anchor link checker, and <code>tasks --new</code> (scaffolds the heading). Spine doctrine in host-template <code>2229dbb</code> + UPGRADING <code>71a1613</code> (requires v0.26.0), adopted. Whole-suite CI green across all three repos.</p> <p><strong>Operator rulings (overrode the five-lens review's re-scope):</strong> build the graph NOW as forward infrastructure for <em>arbitrary-complexity adopters</em> — "no consumer in agentic-host's own linear history" is the wrong lens, the consumer is the adopter. A NEW top-level <code>.host-task-receipts</code> file (over the ontology objection that a task receipt is operational). <strong>Adopter-facing and mandatory.</strong> The bare <code>#N</code> GitHub-reference unsafety is a <em>future</em> plan (enforce full URLs); plan/0042's task references use the full relative-path anchor, so it was reframed: anchoring is for <em>stable task identity</em>, not the <code>#N</code> collision (the review showed no plan ever references a step by number).</p> <p><strong>Two design corrections surfaced during the build (both implemented + tested):</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong>The gate is completion-aware.</strong> A task with no receipt is a HAZARD only when its milestone is marked complete (read from the README <code>## Status</code>); an OPEN milestone's tasks are pending, not gated. This matches the operator's "every <em>completed</em> milestone owes a receipt" scope; the first per-task-always-HAZARD gate over-fired on open milestones (0040/0041 are open).</li> <li><strong>Fenced code blocks are masked</strong> in both the parser and the reference check, so example syntax in a doc (a worked example, a ledger stanza) is not parsed as a real task or flagged.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Staleness took both halves of <code>call/0018</code>:</strong> a mechanical <code>done</code> records its <code>inputs</code> digest and goes STALE on input drift (cheap offline); <code>tasks --rederive</code> re-runs the command and refreshes it. An attested <code>done</code> resolves its citation (weaker, labeled as such). A verify that changed since the receipt is stale; an orphan receipt (anchor removed) is a reverse-drift HAZARD.</p> <p><strong>4B (Fen) validation:</strong> the form is fail-safe. The 4B authors <code>depends</code>/<code>verify</code>/<code>inputs</code> well (within-milestone six of six, cross-milestone four of four) but slips on the exact <em>anchor</em> form when hand-typing; <code>tasks --new</code> carries the anchor (the fill-in-the-blank fold-back), and any residual slip (e.g. over-qualifying a local ref) fails loud as a dangling-dependency HAZARD. Frame authoring as the prerequisite question ("what must finish first?"), never "what runs in parallel?" See [[qwen-4b-weak-agent-eval]].</p> <h2 id="plan0041-complete--next-fails-closed-host-lifecycle-v0261-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#plan0041-complete--next-fails-closed-host-lifecycle-v0261-2026-06-25">plan/0041 complete — next fails closed (host-lifecycle v0.26.1, 2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p><code>host-lifecycle next <dir></code> silently returned <code>0000</code> when pointed at a directory with no <code>NNNN-slug</code> entries (the host root, a typo, an empty room), so a garbled argument produced a plausible-but-wrong number. Dogfooded as a receipted task graph (plan/0042).</p> <h2 id="plan0040-complete--the-front-door-check-re-scoped-by-adversarial-review-host-lifecycle-v0270-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#plan0040-complete--the-front-door-check-re-scoped-by-adversarial-review-host-lifecycle-v0270-2026-06-25">plan/0040 complete — the front-door check, re-scoped by adversarial review (host-lifecycle v0.27.0, 2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p>The single-file front door (the <code>host</code> repo, the <code>.host-software</code> member marked <code>front-door = true</code>) restates the spine and is outside any host's verify gate, so it stales silently (it had already dropped the <code>release</code> phase). The original plan was to <em>generate</em> its spine-derived sections from <strong>hand-authored "front-door fragments" carried in the template</strong>.</p> <p><strong>The adversarial review killed that mechanism (two independent lenses, unanimous): a template fragment is a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH.</strong> <code>front-door --check</code> would prove <code>README == regenerate(fragment)</code> and never <code>fragment == CLAUDE.md</code> — it relocates the drift rather than removing it, the exact self-blindness reconcile (plan/0036) closes, one layer up. Proven by two live drifts: the omitted <code>release</code> phase, and the version pins (Rust/allium/TLA+/Temurin), which have <strong>no structured canonical home at all</strong> (scattered across prose + per-component CI YAML inside materialized worktrees).</p> <p><strong>Re-scope (the lesson): generate ONLY from structured data the tool already reads.</strong> The shipped <code>front-door</code>/<code>front-door --check</code>: (a) <strong>coverage</strong> of the lifecycle phases against <code>lifecycle.manifest</code> (checked as a backtick token, since "release" recurs in prose like "GitHub releases") and of the wired tools against <code>.host-software</code> <code>[verification]</code> drivers + the lifecycle engine — the plan/0039 coverage bite, applied to a link-free doc; (b) byte-exact <strong>generation</strong> of the <code>.host</code> stamp block from the tool's format. The pins/lanes-rule/tool-prose have no home and stay <strong>authored, not gated</strong> (a structured pin home is a named follow-up); don't pretend a prose fragment makes them drift-proof.</p> <p><strong>Wiring is agentic-host-local: a separate step in the reproducible-build CI</strong> (where the spine sources are materialized), NOT the shared spine recheck — so no adopter without a front door runs it and no UPGRADING entry is owed. The front-door repo can't run the check itself (it carries neither the manifest nor <code>.host-software</code>); that asymmetry is recorded. <code>call/0026</code>. Dogfooded as a receipted task graph. <strong>General lesson: a generator is drift-proof only for facts with a real structured source; for sourceless facts, coverage or an honest "authored, not gated" beats a fake generator that gives false assurance.</strong> See [[reconcile-moves-to-concept-uri]].</p> <h2 id="decision-review-of-plan0040--plan0041--three-outcomes--the-entrance-generalization-2026-06-25"><a class="header" href="#decision-review-of-plan0040--plan0041--three-outcomes--the-entrance-generalization-2026-06-25">Decision review of plan/0040 + plan/0041 — three outcomes + the entrance generalization (2026-06-25)</a></h2> <p>After shipping plan/0040 (front-door check, v0.27.0) and plan/0041 (fail-closed next, v0.26.1), a decision review settled three things and spun out plan/0043.</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Front-door phases: keep COVERAGE (not generation), decided on methodology-aesthetic grounds.</strong> Both designs passed the Fen bar (Fen honored a generated-region "do not edit" marker AND fixed a coverage-flagged omission), so safety did not decide it.
