And the spine ITSELF restates phase NAMES in clean prose (the manifest holds the structured fields). <strong>The routing principle: generate what is naturally a format/data block (the <code>.host</code> stamp), coverage-check what is naturally prose (phase/tool names), never a generation marker in teaching prose.</strong> So coverage was right, not the under-delivery I feared in the review. Decision rule: <strong>when multiple designs pass the weak-agent bar, decide on methodology-aesthetic fit.</strong></p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Fail-closed next exit code = 2 confirmed; the earlier 4B preference for 1 was an EDUCATION GAP.</strong> Re-ran the Fen probe with the convention documented (1 = unexpected/internal error, 2 = expected logic/usage error): Fen then routed next-on-a-numberless-dir to 2 and a genuine disk fault to 1. So exit 2 stands (tool-consistent with adopt/next arg errors); document the convention so it is not a gap for the next maintainer (fold a comment in at the next host-lifecycle release).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The capability is OPT-IN / REUSABLE, not agentic-host-only → plan/0043 (entrance-check).</strong> The front-door's shape (a self-contained doc that restates the spine and CANNOT link) recurs for an adopter-authored standalone <code>SKILL.md</code> and any project's operator-and-agent landing page. Operator ruling (the standing "build for arbitrary-complexity adopters" value): make it opt-in/reusable, superseding plan/0040 decision-4 + the scope half of call/0026. <strong>Named <code>entrance</code> by Qwen-3.5-4B data</strong> — <code>landing</code> mis-cued (deployment), <code>threshold</code> (numeric limit), <code>welcome</code> (greeting); <code>foyer</code> was the model's metaphor-first pick but "too domestic for software"; operator chose <code>entrance</code> (clear, fits host/rooms/guest, software-resonant). <code>front-door</code> renamed with no alias (the plan/0039 way). The declaration stays OUT of the prose (a <code>.host-software</code> flag generalizing <code>front-door = true</code>, never a marker — outcome 1). The standalone sibling of <code>reconcile</code> (reconcile = pointers for linkable docs; entrance = coverage + generation for can't-link docs).</p> </li> </ol> <p><strong>pal/Fen ops note (reinforced):</strong> the rope HTTPS token is still rotated; use pal. pal's injected "comprehensive response / use continuation_id" footer repeatedly drove the 4B into a format-loop when the probe ALSO demanded a strict format ("output ONLY") — judge by the converged reasoning BEFORE the loop, and keep probe prompts short with no conflicting format demand. See [[qwen-4b-weak-agent-eval]], [[qwen-pal-model-infra]].</p> <p><strong>Entrance rename landed standalone, with a deprecate-then-retire migration (2026-06-25).</strong> The operator pulled the <code>front-door</code> → <code>entrance</code> rename forward out of plan/0043 (which keeps the opt-in generalization), as a standalone hardwired/agentic-host-local change. Shipped as TWO host-lifecycle releases: <strong>v0.28.0</strong> = the rename with no alias (subcommand + the <code>.host-software</code> flag <code>front-door = true</code> → <code>entrance = true</code> + code + CI), change-class <code>removes-flag</code> (a renamed public flag is Breaking → pre-1.0 minor bump); <strong>v0.28.1</strong> = the migration, change-class <code>neither</code> (a backward-compat shim → patch). <strong>The migration is plan/0039's deprecate-then-retire:</strong> <code>parse_project_facts</code> accepts a legacy <code>front-door = true</code> as the entrance (so a pre-rename <code>.host-software</code> is NOT silently demoted to a component), and the <code>entrance</code> command warns and names the rename so the old spelling never passes silently; the shim is slated for removal a release later. The full plan/0039 retire step (a hard-fail + an adopter UPGRADING entry) waits until the generalization makes entrances adopter-facing. <code>call/0027</code> records it. <strong>Operator directives that shaped it:</strong> comments stay FORWARD-LOOKING (no "renamed from front-door" provenance asides — I had added several and was told to strip them); the MIGRATION is the one place the old spelling lives ("let migration deal with transition"). <strong>Lesson: a rename with no alias OWES a migration</strong> — without the shim a stray <code>front-door = true</code> silently becomes a component (a confusing HAZARD), the silent failure plan/0039's fail-safe forbids.</p> <p><strong>plan/0043 COMPLETE: the entrance check generalized to a singleton <code>[entrance]</code> stanza (host-lifecycle v0.29.0, 2026-06-25).</strong> Any project declares ONE entrance in a <code>[entrance]</code> stanza in <code>.host-software</code>: <code>member</code> (the <code>[software]</code> member it belongs to, set apart from <code>components</code>), <code>document</code> (the file within it, default <code>README.md</code>, so a <code>SKILL.md</code> or a landing page is reached by path), <code>restates</code> (<code>true</code> for all, or a subset of the closed vocabulary <code>phases</code>/<code>tools</code>/<code>stamp</code>). <code>host-lifecycle entrance --check</code> holds it complete against the declared concepts; the standalone sibling of <code>reconcile</code> (reconcile = pointers for linkable docs; entrance = coverage + generation for self-contained docs). Spine doctrine + adopter UPGRADING entry in host-template <code>ba86125</code>; agentic-host migrated its <code>.host-software</code> from the legacy per-member <code>entrance = true</code> to the stanza. <code>call/0028</code> records it; supersedes call/0026 scope, completes call/0027.</p> <p><strong>The journey (operator-shaped):</strong> the three-reviewer design review returned RE-SCOPE (defer the generalization); the <strong>operator OVERRULED → EXPAND</strong> (see [[review-findings-are-requirements-not-descope]]). A three-reviewer <strong>code review</strong> of the diff then caught TWO blocking defects before release: (1) the parse <code>problems</code> field reached only the <code>entrance</code> command, so a typo'd <code>member</code> left the real front door in <code>components</code> and reconcile demanded STRUCTURE.md name it — the call/0027 silent demotion RELOCATED to another consumer; fix = surface <code>problems</code> in <code>reconcile</code> too. (2) an empty <code>restates =</code> parsed to "check nothing" and reported clean (fail-open); fix = a problem. <strong>Lesson: a parse-<code>problems</code> guard must fire in EVERY consumer of the parsed facts, not just the command that owns the feature.</strong></p> <p><strong>Two gotchas worth keeping:</strong> (a) <strong>UPGRADING entry key must be a PUSHED commit.</strong> I keyed it to the pre-amend SHA (dangling, never pushed); <code>upgrade</code>/CI resolve the key by git ancestry, so a fresh clone can't find it. Fix = re-key to the pushed doctrine commit. Don't amend-then-key; commit the doctrine, push, THEN key the entry to that pushed SHA. (b) <strong>exit-code convention: the codebase is the standard linter one</strong> — <code>0</code> clean, <code>1</code> the check found drift/HAZARDs, <code>2</code> cannot-proceed-on-input (missing/malformed file, <code>next</code> numberless dir). The earlier #6/gather-data framing ("1=unexpected, 2=expected-logic", so a <code>--check</code> drift → 2) mis-described the 29 <code>exit(1)</code> sites; the code comment + gather-data were corrected to the real convention rather than changing the code. (c) <strong>The entrance is the single set-apart entry point</strong> (a non-component member); a doc INSIDE a real tool component is not the singleton entrance (a recorded boundary, not a code change).</p> <p><strong>UPDATE — the shim retirement landed in plan/0043 (host-lifecycle v0.30.0, 2026-06-25).</strong> The operator chose to retire NOW and to FOLD it into plan/0043 ("it was connected"), not a separate plan: a surviving per-member <code>front-door = true</code> / <code>entrance = true</code> is a loud problem in EVERY consumer (the parser pushes it; entrance and reconcile exit <code>2</code>), never the entrance. Spine retirement doctrine + UPGRADING <code>de8a517</code> (requires v0.30.0); the live spine teaches only the stanza. The UPGRADING-key gotcha was handled cleanly this time (commit the doctrine + entry with a placeholder, push, THEN re-key to the pushed commit, no amend). <strong>New gotcha: a task receipt and its task must land together (task commit first).</strong> The audited-docs rule split the infra commit (the <code>.host-task-receipts</code> receipt for <code>#retire-shim</code>) from the plan/0043 commit (the <code>#retire-shim</code> TASK); committing the receipt first left an orphan-receipt HAZARD at that intermediate commit, so its CI went red (the HEAD, carrying both, is green). Next time: commit the milestone-doc task BEFORE the receipt, or land them in one commit.</p> <p><strong>plan/0044 (prose-lane LEXICON, host-lint v0.10.0, <code>f1474e8</code>, artifact <code>5106ee7a</code>, closes host-lint #16).</strong> The <code>--prose</code>/<code>--docs</code> lanes now consult the per-repo LEXICON: <code>scan_prose_text</code> masks a declared phrase with the naming lane's <code>mask_allowed</code> before BOTH the per-tell scan AND the document density score (<code>tell_score</code>), so a declared <code>rehost harness</code> clears the ai-diction trope on <code>harness</code> within that phrase and a standalone occurrence still flags. <code>mask_allowed</code> is byte-length-preserving, so offsets into the masked text still index the original for the reported excerpt. No new abuse surface: the same provenance-gated entries the naming lane masks with (a letter required, no flag-tier laundering, tracker-ref URL), and the density denominator is the SENTENCE count, so a mask only subtracts its own weight and can never inflate the denominator to dilute other tells. No spine change: the living-grammar doctrine ("a legitimate tell-shaped token stays in the LEXICON") is MET, not changed, so no host-template UPGRADING entry (operator agreed). <strong>Data-gathering gotcha: a multiple-choice option that asserts a false premise contaminates the weak-agent result.</strong> The first abuse-guard probe offered an option claiming LEXICON requires multi-word phrases; <code>validate_lexicon_entry</code> enforces no such rule (a single legitimate word is a valid entry). Fen accepted the false premise, so the run was discarded and re-run with honest options; Fen then chose lane-consistency <code>(A)</code>, the surgical word boundary <code>(ii)</code>, and "no new muting power" <code>(b)</code>, with the "separate stricter prose allowlist" dissent available and not chosen. Ground probe options in the actual code before asking the model. The run went direct against rope with a real system prompt (the user rejected pal, whose injected system prompt caused a format-loop); the <code>10696b8f…</code> rope token worked this session (the earlier "confirmed rotated" note was wrong, or it was un-rotated).</p> <p><strong>Obligation digests stale on ANY src change, and <code>host-lifecycle release</code> does NOT re-derive them (plan/0044, host-lint v0.10.0 → v0.10.1).</strong> Editing <code>src/lib.rs</code> for the prose-mask change staled two kani-backed obligations (<code>rule-success.DetectInternalCodeAsName</code>, <code>rule-failure.DetectInternalCodeAsName.1</code>, both <code>inputs=src/lib.rs</code>) tracked in <code>host-lint.obligations</code> / <code>host-lint.obligations.digests</code>. The release gate runs only <code>validate + prose + reconcile</code>, NOT the obligations lane, so v0.10.0 (<code>f1474e8</code>) shipped with stale digests and host-lint's OWN CI (the <code>allium</code> job: <code>host-lifecycle obligations host-lint.allium --tests tests --prove src</code>) went red AFTER the tag. Fix: re-derive with <code>PATH=<host-prove-release-dir>:$PATH host-lifecycle obligations host-lint.allium --tests tests --prove src --rederive . --record-digests</code> — it needs <strong>host-prove on PATH</strong> (built at <code>software/host-prove/main/target/release/host-prove</code>), and <code>--rederive .</code> NOT <code>--rederive src</code> (else it joins to <code>src/src/lib.rs</code> and cannot hash). It re-runs the Kani proofs (both SUCCESSFUL here) and writes <code>host-lint.obligations.digests</code>. <em><em>Lesson: after editing a host-</em> component's source, re-derive obligation digests and commit <code>*.obligations.digests</code> as PART of the release, before tagging.</em>* The operator chose to <strong>bump v0.10.1</strong> (a clean patch carrying the fresh digests; new artifact <code>941126c9</code>, since the embedded version changes the binary) rather than force-push the <code>v0.10.0</code> tag forward (the auto-classifier blocks moving a published tag): <code>v0.10.0</code> stays the feature tag at <code>f1474e8</code>, <code>v0.10.1</code> (<code>0c2bfc3</code>) is the pinned release.</p> <h2 id="2026-06-26--plan0045-complete-the-embedded-prose-engine-catches-up-host-lifecycle2"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-26--plan0045-complete-the-embedded-prose-engine-catches-up-host-lifecycle2">2026-06-26 — plan/0045 COMPLETE: the embedded prose engine catches up (host-lifecycle#2)</a></h2> <p><code>connollydavid/host-lifecycle#2</code> closed. plan/0044 gave host-lint's prose lane the LEXICON mask, but host-lifecycle runs that lane in-process for its verify-phase prose recheck while pinning the <code>host_lint</code> crate at <strong>v0.8.1</strong>, whose <code>scan_prose_text</code> predates the mask (signature <code>(input, source, matches)</code>, no allowlist param). The applied claim lands in <code>.host-receipts</code> as <code>applied = 6174996 recorded=... via=verify</code> (an out-of-order applied entry, not a baseline advance), and the <code>.host</code> baseline stays <code>de8a517</code>.</p> <p><strong>GOTCHA: marking a milestone "complete" must not land in a commit before its task receipts.</strong> The task gate (<code>software --check</code>, run by the reproducible-build CI) HAZARDs <code>task <key> — no receipt (its milestone is marked complete)</code> and exits 1 when a plan README Status reads complete but a task in that milestone has no receipt yet. plan/0048 hit it: commit <code>8d1dad7</code> flipped the README to complete, but the <code>#adopt</code> receipt was committed in the next commit (<code>9ec9087</code>), so <code>8d1dad7</code>'s CI went red on the verify-build job (the commits on either side passed). The branch self-heals at the next commit (HEAD stayed green), but a red run sits in history. Fix the ordering: commit the backing receipts in the same commit as the status flip or earlier, never after. This refines [[complete-means-whole-suite-green]] to intra-sequence commit ordering, not just cross-repo sweeps. Re-running the red intermediate commit is pointless; its tree is genuinely inconsistent.</p> <h2 id="plan0049--external-reference-corpus-cut-host-reference-agent-surfaces-pass-at-the-fen-bar"><a class="header" href="#plan0049--external-reference-corpus-cut-host-reference-agent-surfaces-pass-at-the-fen-bar">plan/0049 — external reference corpus cut; host-reference agent surfaces pass at the Fen bar</a></h2> <p>plan/0049 cut (in design): a new component <code>host-reference</code>, a reference compiler that normalises external documentation (mixed shapes: Markdown, HTML, PDF, Office, images, structured data, electronic design, mechanical and 3D-printing CAD) into a token-lean form an agent reads in context, with a deterministic immutable layer (re-derived, attested) and a collaborative overlay for annotations and edits. Design direction and the open questions are in plan/0049/README.md; the adversarially reviewed weak-agent probe set, the cast review (pre and post), and the run are in plan/0049/gather-data.md. The four agent-facing surfaces (windowed retrieval selector, capability flags, content-is-data posture, the deterministic immutable-against-overlay boundary) passed three of three each against <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> on rope, with the option order rotated so the pass reflects content reasoning and not position. Decisions follow in call/0030, with a security sibling and the engineering-geometry target left to the cast.</p> <p><strong>GOTCHA for a future Fen probe run: do not put a multiple-choice instruction in a shared system prompt when an open elicitation probe is in the same batch.</strong> The system prompt said to answer the multiple-choice question; the open geometry-elicitation probe spent its whole token budget reconciling that mismatch and truncated before answering. Run an open elicitation with its own open-ended system prompt, or split the batch by response shape.</p> <p><strong>GOTCHA: give the thinking model room.</strong> <code>qwen3.5-4b</code> thinks before it answers, so <code>max_tokens</code> 1500 truncated mid-think and the answer never emitted; 8000 finished cleanly. Force the answer onto a parseable final line (<code>ANSWER: X</code>) and rotate the option order across runs, so a pass is content reasoning rather than a position or string-match artefact. See [[qwen-4b-weak-agent-eval]] and [[weak-agent-probe-no-false-premise]].</p> <h2 id="plan0049--host-reference-embedded-source-only-prose-density-check-needs-host-lifecycle-prose"><a class="header" href="#plan0049--host-reference-embedded-source-only-prose-density-check-needs-host-lifecycle-prose">plan/0049 — host-reference embedded source-only; prose density check needs <code>host-lifecycle prose</code></a></h2> <p>The host-reference component was scaffolded (a Cargo workspace, <code>host-reference-core</code> carrying the <code>Normalizer</code> trait and the two-layer types, plus a CLI skeleton), pushed to the new public repo connollydavid/host-reference at <code>88c6bcf</code>, and embedded source-only in <code>.host-software</code> (url, pin, worktrees, no build provenance). The reproducible-build artifact, the deps-bundle, and <code>--verify-build</code> land in the plan/0049 build wave once the CLI is functional; the release receipt is a deliberate <code>skip</code> until then. <code>software --check</code> is green. A greenfield component still needs its embed and release receipts (<code>host-lifecycle receipt --record</code>), and adding a <code>.host-software</code> component forces its mention in the <code>STRUCTURE.md</code> components home or reconcile HAZARDs by coverage.</p> <p><strong>GOTCHA: check authored-doc prose with <code>host-lifecycle prose</code>, not <code>host-lint --docs <file></code>.</strong> I pre-linted call/0030 through call/0032 and the plan/0049 docs with <code>host-lint --docs <file></code> (exit 0) and the commit hook passed, yet <code>software --check</code> then re-opened the verify phase: <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> flagged ten ai-diction warns (negative-parallelism, tricolon, ing-tail) that the <code>--docs <file></code> mode does not surface. The density tropes are caught by <code>host-lifecycle prose</code> (the gate engine) and by the commit-msg <code>host-lint --stdin</code> (it flagged the antithesis in my own fix commit's message), so a doc can pass the per-file <code>--docs</code> check and the hook while still failing the gate. Before committing authored markdown, run <code>host-lifecycle prose</code>, and watch antithesis ("not X but Y"), three-beat lists, and trailing -ing clauses in prose and in commit messages. See [[prose-clean-on-front-door-trigger]] and [[ai-diction-traps-in-my-writing]].</p> <p><strong>GOTCHA: do not name a group of tasks by ordinal; host-lint will not catch it.</strong> When I gave plan/0049 a build-sequence task graph, I named the task groups by ordinal (the rejected position-naming the milestone rule forbids). It passed <code>host-lint</code>, <code>host-lifecycle prose</code>, and <code>software --check</code>, and the operator caught it by eye. Two gaps, filed as https://github.com/connollydavid/host-lifecycle/issues/4 with plan/0049 as the case study: the task model has no sanctioned construct for a group of tasks (so an author reaches for an ordinal name), and host-lint's VOCABULARY does not carry the ordinal-group form (a <code>gather</code> candidate, plan/0035). For now: name every task and task group by content, and let the order live in the <code>depends</code> edges. The fix renamed the groups to <code>text-cheap-kinds</code>, <code>office-mail-fixed-layout</code>, <code>recognition-and-engineering</code>, <code>overlay</code>, and <code>spec-and-release</code>. See [[no-forge-word]] for the related ban-by-name discipline.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-27--host-reference-expand-wave-skeletons-are-structure-not-content"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-27--host-reference-expand-wave-skeletons-are-structure-not-content">2026-06-27 — host-reference expand wave: skeletons are structure, not content</a></h3> <p>The expand-wave readers (data extensions ndjson/tsv/ipynb/toml; the config crate ini/properties/env; the calendar crate ics/vcf; the columnar crate parquet/arrow) confirmed the core principle: a Tier-0 skeleton is the SHAPE of a document (keys and types, columns and row counts, sections, component tallies, a vCard's property union), never the values. That shape is where the token saving lives (a Jupyter notebook 182→41, a Parquet file 721→28); the full content stays in the Tier-1 view. Three supporting lessons held across the wave. Determinism is met by reading only what re-derives identically everywhere: a dotenv emits keys, not interpolated values; the columnar reader reads file metadata, not data pages, so no compression codec is linked; and a binary fixture is generated in-test by the pinned writer, not committed. <code>cargo-deny</code> reviews each reader's licence as it lands (the config crate added the permissive BSD-3-Clause and CC0-1.0). And a no-fix informational advisory (RUSTSEC-2024-0436, <code>paste</code> unmaintained via parquet) takes a documented per-id ignore, so the lane still catches real vulnerabilities. Each reader is a feature-gated crate (call/0033): the light ones join the text-cheap default, the heavier ones (calendar, columnar) stay opt-in.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--in-test-zip-fixtures-must-use-stored-not-deflated"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--in-test-zip-fixtures-must-use-stored-not-deflated">2026-06-28 — in-test zip fixtures must use Stored, not Deflated</a></h3> <p>A binary fixture generated in the conformance test (the office OOXML package, the EPUB zip) whose content id, the sha of the bytes, feeds the committed golden must build its zip entries with <code>CompressionMethod::Stored</code>, not <code>Deflated</code>, plus a fixed mtime. Deflate output varies with zip feature unification across the workspace, so the office docx golden passed under <code>cargo test -p host-reference-office</code> in isolation yet failed under a full <code>cargo test</code> as the bytes drifted by a few bytes (different content id, different raw token count). Stored entries are deflate-independent, so the content id is stable in any build configuration. This applies to every future zip-backed fixture (3MF, more office formats). Two process notes: verify in the full workspace, not just the single crate; and the broken commit landed because the shell command did not gate the git step on the test result, so gate commits on a green test.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--stage-the-denytoml-entry-with-its-reader-the-dev-disk-filled"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--stage-the-denytoml-entry-with-its-reader-the-dev-disk-filled">2026-06-28 — stage the deny.toml entry with its reader; the dev disk filled</a></h3> <p>Two operational gotchas from the office wave. When a reader adds a licence to deny.toml's allow-list, stage that deny.toml change in the SAME commit as the reader. The epub crate's Zlib entry was added but not staged with it, so the pinned epub state's cargo-deny lane was actually missing Zlib and only the local working copy (with the uncommitted entry) passed; a fresh-clone CI check would have failed. It surfaced when a later <code>git status</code> still showed deny.toml modified. Separately, the dev disk (/mnt/c, a WSL-mounted Windows drive) reached 100% full and git could not write the commit object ("unable to write loose object file", exit 128, not a test failure); <code>cargo clean</code> in the worktree reclaimed 11.4 GiB and unblocked it, and a full host-reference build leaves target/ around 12 GiB.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--the-recognition-split-puts-ocr-and-transcription-in-overlay-not-the-reader-wave"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--the-recognition-split-puts-ocr-and-transcription-in-overlay-not-the-reader-wave">2026-06-28 — the recognition split puts OCR and transcription in #overlay, not the reader wave</a></h3> <p>plan/0049's #recognition-and-engineering wave landed the ATTESTED, deterministic readers of the recognition split (call/0030): image format, dimensions, and EXIF; audio-visual container metadata under a new AudioVisual modality; the EDA tallies (KiCad, Gerber, Eagle); and the engineering-geometry parsers (STL, glTF, DXF, OBJ, PLY, G-code). The machine-learning half (OCR text over an image, the transcript of audio-visual media) is non-deterministic inference and cannot carry a byte-for-byte conformance golden, so it rides the provider-agnostic overlay adapter and lands in the SEPARATE downstream #overlay node. A goal phrased "image+OCR" therefore spans two task-graph nodes: the image reader here, the OCR adapter in #overlay. The attested image and av readers declare <code>ocr: false</code>, their honest capability. Do not force OCR into the deterministic-reader plugin pattern; "act within scope of previous plugins" means the deterministic readers.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--static-committed-binary-fixtures-give-a-build-config-independent-golden"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--static-committed-binary-fixtures-give-a-build-config-independent-golden">2026-06-28 — static committed binary fixtures give a build-config-independent golden</a></h3> <p>The geometry, eda, image, and av readers take inputs that are committed as STATIC fixture files (a real PNG, a JPEG with EXIF, a WAV, an H.264 MP4, an STL, a Gerber, and the rest), generated once with PIL, ffmpeg, and python's <code>wave</code> module. Because the content id is the sha of the committed bytes and the reader only DECODES the fixed file with no re-encoding, the golden is independent of build configuration. This sidesteps the in-test-generated-zip determinism trap (the earlier office Deflated-versus-Stored bug) entirely, since there is no test-time generation to vary under feature unification. Prefer a static committed fixture over in-test generation whenever the input is binary. Two as-built pin notes: KiCad reads through the generic <code>lexpr</code> S-expression form tally because <code>kiutils_kicad</code> reads from a path, not the bytes a <code>Source</code> carries; audio-visual reads through <code>symphonia</code> (audio) and the <code>mp4</code> crate (video) rather than the pre-build research's <code>mp4parse</code> and <code>lofty</code>, which were not needed.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--ocr-ships-out-of-process-the-operator-overruled-the-overlay-deferral"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--ocr-ships-out-of-process-the-operator-overruled-the-overlay-deferral">2026-06-28 — OCR ships out-of-process: the operator overruled the overlay deferral</a></h3> <p>I scoped OCR out of the recognition wave (deferred to <code>#overlay</code>) as non-deterministic ML. The operator overruled that through the <code>/goal</code> Stop hook, requiring image and OCR delivered together, then named the route: "this is what our out-of-process API is for." The resolution is <code>call/0034</code>. The only pure-Rust OCR engine, <code>ocrs</code> over <code>rten</code>, carries CC-BY-SA-4.0 model weights, a content-copyleft licence the permissive component must not absorb, so the <code>call/0033</code> arms-length rule built for GPL applies. A separate <code>host-reference-ocr-helper</code> binary embeds the engine and the CC-BY-SA models; the permissive <code>host-reference-ocr</code> plugin writes the image to a temp file, runs the helper as a separate process, and reads the recognised text from stdout. That is an aggregation rather than a linkage, so the plugin and its dependents stay permissive. The plugin implements the same <code>Normalizer</code> interface as the in-process readers, the <code>call/0033</code> interface test, reached before OpenSCAD. Determinism: <code>ocrs</code> is run-to-run identical on a host with the pinned vendored models, enough for a byte-for-byte golden; cross-host bit-determinism is unproven and is the open edge for the release task.</p> <p>Two lessons. Methodology: a "deferred to a later node" descope can be overruled toward fold-in (see [[review-findings-are-requirements-not-descope]]), and the out-of-process boundary serves content-copyleft (CC-BY-SA), not only code-copyleft (GPL). Technical: <code>ocrs</code> <code>ImageSource</code> needs the explicit <code>from_tensor</code> with an <code>NdTensor</code> of shape <code>[H, W, C]</code> and <code>DimOrder::Hwc</code> plus <code>rten_tensor::prelude::*</code> for <code>.view()</code>; the <code>from_bytes((h, w))</code> path misread the channels and returned garbage. The conformance test builds the helper on demand via <code>env!("CARGO")</code> and points the plugin at it through <code>HOST_REFERENCE_OCR_HELPER</code>.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--the-ocr-helper-became-its-own-repo-host-reference-ocr-for-full-cc-by-sa-confinement"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--the-ocr-helper-became-its-own-repo-host-reference-ocr-for-full-cc-by-sa-confinement">2026-06-28 — the OCR helper became its own repo (host-reference-ocr) for full CC-BY-SA confinement</a></h3> <p>Extending the entry above: the only pure-Rust OCR engine carries CC-BY-SA-4.0 model weights, so the operator directed the helper into its own public repo, <code>connollydavid/host-reference-ocr</code>, with the licence metadata and citations stated upfront. The CC-BY-SA models now leave the <code>host-reference</code> repo entirely. <code>host-reference</code> keeps only the permissive <code>ocr</code> plugin; the engine and models are a separate embedded software component (<code>call/0034</code>). Three lessons. First, a new software component triggers the full embed flow, and <code>software --check</code> HAZARDs until it is complete: the component must be a <code>.host-software</code> stanza materialized as a bare store with worktree, <code>STRUCTURE.md</code>'s <code>{#components}</code> home must name it, and the <code>embed</code> and <code>release</code> lifecycle receipts must be recorded with <code>host-lifecycle receipt --record <phase> --component <name></code>; missing any of these re-opens the verify recheck. Second, the plugin's conformance test no longer builds the helper (correcting the prior entry): it points <code>HOST_REFERENCE_OCR_HELPER</code> at a runtime stub script that asserts a real image path and emits fixed text, so the plugin's plumbing and formatting are tested permissively, while the real engine is conformance-tested in the helper repo via <code>env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_host-reference-ocr-helper")</code>. Third, a public repo's visibility is the operator's decision, not the agent's: the auto-mode classifier blocks a unilateral <code>gh repo create --public</code>, and rightly, so ask before publishing.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--openscad-is-the-second-out-of-process-plugin-gpl-the-call0033-original-case"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--openscad-is-the-second-out-of-process-plugin-gpl-the-call0033-original-case">2026-06-28 — OpenSCAD is the second out-of-process plugin (GPL, the call/0033 original case)</a></h3> <p>Wired the OpenSCAD helper the same way as OCR. The GPL-3.0 <code>openscad-rs</code> parser lives in its own public repo, <code>connollydavid/host-reference-openscad</code>, embedded as a source-only component; its helper binary is GPL too because it links <code>openscad-rs</code>. The permissive <code>host-reference-openscad</code> plugin (no <code>openscad-rs</code> dependency) writes the <code>.scad</code> to a temp file, runs the helper at arm's length, and tallies the statement kinds it prints (one per line) into the structure skeleton. The <code>host-reference</code> lockfile carries no <code>openscad-rs</code>. This is the GPL case <code>call/0033</code> originally wrote the out-of-process rule for; OCR (CC-BY-SA, <code>call/0034</code>) reached it first, OpenSCAD is the second, and both drive the helper through the same <code>Normalizer</code> interface. Practical notes: <code>openscad-rs</code> is edition 2024 and builds on the 1.95 toolchain; <code>parse(source)</code> returns <code>SourceFile { statements: Vec<Statement> }</code>, and the helper tallies by the Debug-first-token of each <code>Statement</code> (ModuleDefinition, Assignment, ModuleInstantiation), the same trick the DXF reader uses. The helper repo's <code>cargo-deny</code> must name BOTH <code>openscad-rs</code> and the helper binary as GPL-3.0 exceptions, because the root crate's own licence is checked too, and <code>ISC</code> was needed for <code>is_ci</code> (transitive via <code>miette</code>). The plugin's conformance uses a stub helper; the real parser is conformance-tested in the helper repo.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--step-3mf-and-amf-delivered-in-process-geometry-complete-bar-iges"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--step-3mf-and-amf-delivered-in-process-geometry-complete-bar-iges">2026-06-28 — STEP, 3MF, and AMF delivered in-process; geometry complete bar IGES</a></h3> <p>The three deferred geometry kinds joined the in-process <code>geometry</code> crate (not out-of-process; their readers are permissive). 3MF through <code>threemf</code> 0.8 (<code>read</code> returns <code>Vec<Model></code>, each <code>model.resources.object[].mesh</code> with <code>vertices.vertex</code> and <code>triangles.triangle</code>); its licence is 0BSD, added to the deny allow-list. AMF through <code>roxmltree</code> over the uncompressed XML (counts of object, mesh, vertex, triangle); a compressed AMF zip is refused with a clear message rather than handled, a deliberate scope cut. STEP through <code>ruststep</code> 0.4: the schema-agnostic parser is <code>ruststep::parser::exchange::exchange_file</code> (a nom parser returning <code>IResult</code>, so destructure <code>let (_, exchange) = ...</code>), NOT a <code>parse</code> function; <code>exchange.data</code> is <code>Vec<DataSection></code>, each section has <code>entities: Vec<EntityInstance></code>, and <code>EntityInstance::Simple { record, .. }</code> carries <code>record.name</code> (the entity keyword) for the type tally. ruststep pulls the unmaintained <code>proc-macro-error</code> (RUSTSEC-2024-0370) through <code>ruststep-derive</code>; accepted in deny on the same footing as <code>paste</code>, which is what cleared STEP past the maturity-rule deferral readers.md had reserved for it. The 3MF fixture is a static zip generated once with Python (<code>zipfile</code>, Stored); AMF and STEP fixtures are hand-authored text. Engineering geometry is now complete except IGES, which stays deferred because every working reader is C++.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--the-overlay-node-loro-mutable-layer-web-annotation-selectors-per-kind-lens-law"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--the-overlay-node-loro-mutable-layer-web-annotation-selectors-per-kind-lens-law">2026-06-28 — the overlay node: Loro mutable layer, Web Annotation selectors, per-kind lens law</a></h3> <p>The <code>#overlay</code> node landed (plan/0049). <code>host-reference-overlay</code> is a Loro CRDT document (loro 1.13, the <code>call/0030</code>-settled CRDT) holding annotations anchored to the immutable layer by W3C Web Annotation selectors: <code>TextPosition { start, end }</code> and <code>TextQuote { prefix, exact, suffix }</code>. TextQuote re-locates by content, so an annotation survives a re-derivation that shifts offsets (tested). <code>export</code>/<code>import</code> persist a snapshot; <code>merge</code> folds in a concurrent replica (CRDT union). For a deterministic merge test, give each replica a distinct peer through <code>Overlay::with_peer(id)</code> (<code>doc.set_peer_id</code>), since two <code>LoroDoc::new()</code> replicas could otherwise share op ids and dedupe to one. The write-back path (<code>write_back</code>) resolves a selector to a span and drives the normaliser's <code>put</code>; the default <code>put</code> refuses, the <code>call/0030</code> fail-safe. The per-kind round-trip lens law is proptested (proptest 1.11) in the property-based lane: GetPut (a no-op edit changes nothing) and PutGet (the edit is exactly the splice) hold for the write-back kinds, prose and data, both the UTF-8 text-splice lens that floors indices to char boundaries. loro API notes: <code>doc.get_list(key).push(string)</code>; <code>list.get(i)</code> returns <code>Option<ValueOrContainer></code> and <code>.into_value()</code> returns a <code>Result</code>, not an <code>Option</code>; <code>doc.export(ExportMode::Snapshot)</code>; <code>doc.import(&bytes)</code>. deny gained BSL-1.0 (a loro dependency) and accepted RUSTSEC-2023-0089 (atomic-polyfill unmaintained, deep under loro through postcard and heapless), on the same footing as paste and proc-macro-error. Only <code>plan/0049#spec-and-release</code> (the <code>.allium</code> spec, the wired CI, and the reproducible build) remains.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--spec-and-release-the-reproducible-build-and-releasing-the-first-workspace-component"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--spec-and-release-the-reproducible-build-and-releasing-the-first-workspace-component">2026-06-28 — spec-and-release: the reproducible build, and releasing the first workspace component</a></h3> <p>The final plan/0049 node. <code>host-reference.allium</code> distils the Normalizer contract via the <code>distill</code> skill (<code>allium check</code>/<code>analyse</code> clean, infos only, zero warnings — warnings fail <code>allium check</code>); <code>host-reference.obligations</code> dispositions all 41 obligations (structural for spec-integrity, named contract tests in <code>crates/core/tests/contract.rs</code> for the trait rules, waivers for the overlay / recognition / hostile-input rules realised outside the trait). The CI mirrors host-lint. Several hard lessons on the reproducible build:</p> <ul> <li>The recorded artifact digest must come from a build at the SAME mount path <code>software --verify-build</code> uses, <code>/src</code>, not an ad-hoc <code>/volume</code> docker mount: the binary embeds crate paths (panic strings), so a <code>/volume</code> build drifts from verify-build's <code>/src</code> rebuild. Build at <code>/src</code> to record the digest.</li> <li>The deps-bundle tarball ships <code>vendor/</code> plus a <code>vendor-config.toml</code> source-replacement snippet; verify-build downloads it, sha-checks, extracts, merges the snippet into <code>.cargo/config.toml</code>, and builds <code>--offline</code> under <code>--network none</code>. <code>cargo vendor</code> vendors the whole lockfile (host-reference's was 485 crates, 330M source, a 52M bundle), even though the canonical <code>-p host-reference</code> build only compiles the default <code>text</code> deps.</li> <li>Releasing the FIRST workspace component needed a host-lifecycle fix (v0.31.2, two patches). <code>release</code> read and bumped <code>[package] version</code> from the component root; a virtual workspace keeps the version in <code>[workspace.package]</code>, so <code>cargo_version</code>/<code>set_cargo_version</code> now fall back to it. And the version bump cascades to every member that inherits <code>version.workspace</code>, so the lock sync now bumps every such member (not just the deploy crate), or the pinned <code>--locked</code> rebuild fails on a stale member.</li> <li>A version bump changes the binary digest (the version is embedded), so the released v0.1.1 hash (629c959) differs from the 0.1.0 build (05a949); that is expected, and the release re-verifies.</li> </ul> <p>host-reference is released v0.1.1 through the tool-carried sequence, verified reproducible. The plan/0049 milestone is complete: every task-graph node carries a receipt.</p> <h3 id="2026-06-28--closed-the-helper-reproducible-build-gap-ocr--openscad-released-v011"><a class="header" href="#2026-06-28--closed-the-helper-reproducible-build-gap-ocr--openscad-released-v011">2026-06-28 — closed the helper reproducible-build gap (ocr + openscad released v0.1.1)</a></h3> <p>A receipt audit found the two out-of-process helpers released SOURCE-ONLY: their release receipts had deferred the reproducible build to spec-and-release, which only covered host-reference. Closed it the same way for each: add <code>.cargo/config.toml</code> (build-id=none on Linux) and gitignore the vendor artifacts; <code>cargo vendor</code> then publish a <code>vendor-v1</code> deps-bundle (ocr 6.2M/70 crates, openscad 12M/45 crates); a <code>/src</code> muslrust build for the digest; record toolchain/build/deploy/artifact/ deps-bundle in <code>.host-software</code>; and a tool-carried v0.1.1 release that re-derives byte-identically. Two gotchas. The <code>deploy</code> field is the deployed WORKTREE LINE (the component name, <code>host-reference-ocr</code>), not the binary name (<code>host-reference-ocr-helper</code>) — the binary is named in the artifact path; setting it to the binary name drifts <code>software --check</code> ("not a recorded worktree"). The C: stores are now dormant and deletable.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-07-17--plan0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack-cut-the-fork-sha-pin-lesson"><a class="header" href="#2026-07-17--plan0072-ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack-cut-the-fork-sha-pin-lesson">2026-07-17 — plan/0072 ffmpeg-commit-rule-pack cut; the fork-SHA pin lesson</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>plan/0072 cut</strong> (<code>2a6a93eb</code>): the FFmpeg commit-rule pack as host-lint's first external pack, from host-lint#22/#23 plus a public-signals addendum posted to #22 the same day (fanned-out research, adversarial primary-source verification). #23 stays open for the live core defect (nonexistent file arg exits 0 clean); its fix is the root task and ships as its own patch release.</li> <li><strong>Pin rule corpora to genuine upstream SHAs.</strong> The #22 corpus recorded its baseline as "FFmpeg revision a7ffc46c", which GitHub resolves via the fork network to a pgs-release fork commit, not upstream master — so every "unchanged since pin" claim keyed to it was unsound, and five upstream developer.texi commits (three substantive rules) were missing while the design's own developer.html fetch already contained them. Lessons: resolve a pin against the upstream repo and record its committer date before encoding; diff the encoded rules against the live render of the same source at encode time (an encoding miss looks identical to staleness otherwise); and byte-diff pin-vs-master per file rather than trusting a flat listing or GitHub's capped compare API.</li> <li><strong>Anubis gates by User-Agent, not auth.</strong> code.ffmpeg.org (Forgejo) denies browser-UA and AI-crawler-UA fetches (WebFetch included) but answers plain non-browser clients: anonymous <code>curl</code> against <code>/api/v1/...</code> returns full JSON (merge settings, PR comments/reviews/timelines). Blocker one claims host-lint main already carries the pack work past v0.14.2, which would re-class core-fix-release and foreclose pack residence — verify against the live repo before folding; the claim is the skeptic's, not yet independently confirmed.</li> <li><strong>A multi-agent review's own receipts need the no-hollow-green check.</strong> The workflow's coverage-critic agent returned null, so the run's <code>critic</code> slot was empty while everything else looked complete; the critique was redone inline and recorded in the handover. W1/F1/L2-2 (one root) were the only hollow ones; the rest verified authentic (M2 <code>--fix</code> is an honest no-op in both code and spine; L3-3 preserves <code>created</code>, tested; O1 detectors honestly named MVP-grade; zero <code>#[ignore]</code> tests remain). Operator rulings: absorb into 0074; thin script plus tested tool core; completeness is a separate verify mode; spine doctrine, not overfit to agentic-host; Fen decides the <code>bootstrap</code> and completeness-gate names in gather-data.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-07-20--the-spirit-of-a-phase-synonym-tell-is-ordinal-scaffolding-not-the-word"><a class="header" href="#2026-07-20--the-spirit-of-a-phase-synonym-tell-is-ordinal-scaffolding-not-the-word">2026-07-20 — the spirit of a phase-synonym tell is ordinal scaffolding, not the word</a></h3> <ul> <li>host-lint flags a fixed vocabulary (<code>phase</code>, <code>stage</code>, <code>step</code>, <code>leg</code>) followed by a numeral in headers/comments. The operator caught it: "is a numbered Check a tell here, in spirit? ... it seems like a bad heading."</li> <li><strong>Fix by content, not by swapping the noun.</strong> Drop the ordinal and name the section by what it is (<code>## MCP tool surface passes</code>, <code>## Finding routing fails</code>), and in prose refer to it by content ("the MCP-surface check", "the routing check"). This is the CLAUDE.md milestone-naming doctrine applied to section headers: name after content, never ordinals; encode sequence with document order and named dependencies. A green linter is necessary, not sufficient; the ordinal-scaffolding shape can pass the lexical gate while still reading as machine-authored.</li> </ul> <h3 id="2026-07-21--plan0074-gather-data-done-task-node-verify-lines-must-read---verify-not---verify-by"><a class="header" href="#2026-07-21--plan0074-gather-data-done-task-node-verify-lines-must-read---verify-not---verify-by">2026-07-21 — plan/0074 gather-data done; task-node <code>verify</code> lines must read <code>- verify:</code> not <code>- verify by:</code></a></h3> <ul> <li>Completed the gather-data node: settled every remaining README conditional into gather-data.md (receipt kind = its own <code>[receipt "materialize" "<component>"]</code> kind; envhash format = TOML stanzas; env-check exit codes 0/0-delta/2; completeness-gate exit 0/HAZARD host-role-aware; <code>--check</code> keeps <code>--verify-setup</code> distinct; image-digest probe records <code>runtime = none</code> with no runtime; spine split = receipt+bootstrap doctrine are spine, envhash is tooling-only). The operator then directed the fix. <code>extract_room_refs</code> now indexes the <code>&[u8]</code> byte slice (<code>&bytes[i..]</code> + <code>starts_with(b"call/")</code>) instead of slicing the <code>str</code> at an arbitrary byte index; the ASCII prefixes and digit run make it behaviourally identical and panic-free. Renaming the bindings (<code>materialize_run</code>, <code>bootstrap_run</code>) and making every status literal unique across the file cleared eight warnings and took <code>check</code> from rc 1 to rc 0. Also: an entity referenced only inside <code>for x in Xs</code> or an invariant reads as <code>entity.unused</code>; give it a field reference (a <code>Requirement.worktree</code> typed field) or have a rule create it.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The obligations gate reads a forward-ref test as ABSENT, so a manifest-only node cannot be receipted.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle-materialize.obligations</code> (5a1121c) dispositions all 106 obligations (38 structural, 68 behavioural), but <code>obligations <spec> --tests src</code> exits 1 with 68 ABSENT lines because the named tests do not exist yet — non-strict is not lenient about this, whatever plan/0073's manifest header records for the 0.40.1-era tool. So plan/0074#write-obligations stays <strong>pending</strong> until #write-tests, rather than being recorded done against a verify that fails. Lesson: sequence a spec's manifest node's <em>receipt</em> with its test node, or write the manifest as part of the test node.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The tell gate blocked the first main.rs commit in host-lifecycle, and the cause was host-lint#25 (2026-07-23).</strong> <code>src/main.rs</code> carries ~15 genuine tells by construction: the <code>remap</code> feature's doc comments and test fixtures embed the retired ordinal names the feature exists to rewrite. The record-layer answer is a <code>.host-lintignore</code> naming <code>src/main.rs</code> with the line-by-line rationale (written, 7f2bf9d) — but the hook ignored it, because the hook runs with <code>GIT_DIR</code> set and the pinned host-lint v0.14.2 resolves the repo root from <code>GIT_DIR</code>'s parent, which lands in <code>.bare/worktrees/</code> in a linked worktree. The fix (e4e03f3) is on host-lint main but its release is HELD until plan/0072, so the interim remedy is the operator's established one: <code>cargo install --git … --rev e4e03f3 host-lint</code> (name the package — the repo now has two binaries) and copy the binary over <code>software/host-lifecycle/.bare/hooks/host-lint</code>, keeping the canonical one beside it as <code>host-lint.pinned-v0.14.2</code>. <strong>Lesson:</strong> when the hook flags lines a <code>.host-lintignore</code> should exempt, probe with <code>GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)</code> set before rewriting anything — the difference between a real tell and #25 is invisible from a bare <code>host-lint <file></code> run, which resolves the root by walking up from cwd and passes.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>plan/0074 built its four capabilities (2026-07-23): receipt, fingerprint, worktree gate, completeness gate, orchestrator.</strong> Two lessons worth keeping. First, an orchestrator must read each step's precondition immediately before running it, never plan the whole sequence up front: the first bootstrap probe skipped the skill-link step because the plan was computed before materialize existed, so the run ended INCOMPLETE and only the second run went clean. Each step changes the state the next one reads. Second, "is this artifact required here" is two questions, not one: whether this host is the recipe's build host for it (attest-host) AND whether anything local consumes it. Requiring every recorded artifact locally hazarded five components whose artifacts are only ever attested inside their pinned toolchain; the honest rule is that the commit gate consumes the hooks provider's binary and nothing else is owed on disk.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The new completeness gate found three real gaps in this repo on its first live run:</strong> <code>software/host-reference-ocr/main</code>, <code>software/host-reference-openscad/main</code> and <code>software/host/main</code> have never had commit hooks installed, so commits there are ungated today. That is Bug A's live evidence. Clearing it needs <code>software --install-hooks .</code> with a host-lint that carries the #25 fix, so it waits for the held host-lint release rather than overwriting the interim local binaries.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>plan/0074 shipped as host-lifecycle v0.43.0 (2026-07-23), and the two review rounds were worth more than the build.</strong> The cast (four chairs) found eight blocking findings; the adversarial round (five lenses) then found six more, several proven by mutation: two invariants survived deleting the exact code they named, and four bootstrap obligations were discharged by a test whose own comment described the opposite behaviour. The systemic cause: test NAMES were fitted to obligation ids while their bodies tested something else, and <code>--strict-discharge</code>'s check is a substring match on the body, which cannot tell. <strong>Lesson:</strong> when dispositioning an obligation to a test, mutate the rule's code and re-run — a discharge that survives the mutation is decoration. The structural fix underneath everything: the completeness gate enumerates its requirement set from the RECIPE and uses the tree only to answer present-or-absent; deriving requirements from directory listings meant emptying a directory or deleting a declared worktree removed the question instead of answering it "no".</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Two things learned about the verification tooling itself (2026-07-23).</strong> Kani chokes on string equality: asserting <code>token == "worktree_paths" || …</code> inside a harness took over forty minutes of cbmc time for a property that is trivial over enums, so the partition proof states the enum property and an exhaustive unit test carries the twelve-fact token comparison. And <code>obligations --tests</code> is now repeatable (v0.43.0), because a crate holds unit tests beside the code and process-level tests in <code>tests/</code>, and one directory forced the manifest to choose which half to see.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The gate reports this machine's deliberate deviation, correctly.</strong> <code>software --verify-setup .</code> hazards on "installed gate matches the built one" for every worktree, because the interim host-lint carrying the #25 fix differs from what the pinned worktree builds. That is the honest reading of a held release: re-pin host-lint and re-install the hooks when plan/0072 ships, and the hazard clears.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>CI sweep after the v0.43.0 cascade (2026-07-23): all seven repos green, and two lessons about which gate catches what.</strong> host-template's Prose went red on the new doctrine (two decoration warns in CLAUDE.md and the ledger entry), and agentic-host's Reproducible build went red on a single PLAN.md warn — because <code>software --check</code> re-runs the manifest's <code>verify</code> recheck, which includes the prose sweep, so a warn in an audited doc re-opens the verify phase and hazards the whole check. <strong>Lesson:</strong> run <code>host-lifecycle prose .</code> after editing PLAN.md or any milestone doc, not only after editing code; the doc warn does not fail its own commit, it fails the next <code>software --check</code> in CI.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The hermeticity escape was doctrine the tool never had, and the fix took two decisions (2026-07-23).</strong> Orin's chair found <code>hermetic-exempt = call/NNNN</code> promised in the spine and in ledger entry <code>ecce498</code> since 2026-06-22, parsed nowhere in host-lifecycle: an adopter who wrote it got silence, a red gate, and no way out but deleting the <code>deps-bundle</code> line the same section prescribed. It was coined in one sentence of plan/0032's second adversarial review ("mirroring <code>repro-exempt</code>") and shipped template-first without ever being built. [[call/0046]] retires it and folds the case into the surviving key; [[call/0047]] renames that key to <code>repro-waiver</code> after the operator ruled the adjective wrong for a field ("adjectives are for options"), settled by a rotation-proof probe that chose it from positions A and D. Both spellings parse, the retired one reports itself, and the ledger entries verify the adopter's own recipe rather than the template's text. <strong>Lesson:</strong> a spine sentence promising a recipe key is a claim about the tool, and nothing checked it; the review that proposes a mechanism in passing is exactly where an unimplemented promise enters.</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-07-26 — plan/0077's adversarial round found the coverage class for the third time (a verdict claiming more than the tool read), and the reason was structural: <code>host-lifecycle-refs.allium</code> modelled a reference but not the corpus, so no obligation could bite on a document that was never opened. The lesson generalises past this milestone: when a defect class recurs, check whether the spec's universe begins downstream of where the defect lives. A discharge-clean manifest proves nothing about a surface the spec does not model.</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-07-26 — <code>git ls-files</code> C-quotes any path holding a non-ASCII byte under the default <code>core.quotepath</code>, so a caller that splits on newlines takes the quoted spelling as a filename and then fails to open it. Use <code>-z</code> and split on NUL for any path listing. This shipped a dead pointer as a clean verdict at exit 0, and the same shape sat in the prose walk.</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-07-26 — An upgrade-ledger <code>verify</code> condition must test what the tool GUARANTEES, not what the change is about. <code>RENAME-repro-waiver</code> grepped for the token anywhere in <code>.host-software</code> while <code>migrate-recipe</code> renames only the key, so an adopter with the old name in a comment migrated successfully and could then never record the upgrade: <code>upgrade --record</code> refused and <code>software --check</code> hazarded permanently, with no tool remedy. Test the key form. Constructing a tree that SHOULD fail the condition is the check that catches this.</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-07-26 — A weak-agent probe that changes two things at once measures neither. Re-running plan/0077's Fen acceptance against new output, I rewrote the probe and dropped the task framing the original carried; the resolve state scored as failing and the tool was innocent. Re-run with framing matched, it passed. Change the output under test or the probe wording, never both, and discard the pair when you have (as plan/0076 discarded its spoiled ballot).</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-07-26 — <strong>A green "latest run" hides a flake, and the flake was a process-global.</strong> host-lifecycle CI reddened once on <code>main</code> at the v0.44.0 commit (<code>mcp::tests::memory_write_delete_round_trips</code>, <code>rename index: No such file or directory</code>) and was green on the tag and on the next commit, so it read as superseded history. It was not: three <code>#[tokio::test]</code>s pointed the process-global <code>HOME</code> at their own fixture and then removed it, cargo ran them on parallel threads, and one test's <code>HOME</code> landed between another's list and read, so that read resolved into the wrong fixture. A second audit landed clean: our releases are tag-only with no asset-bearing Release object, so the lifecycle deps-bundle bug (published asset diverging from the recorded hash) has nothing to bite on here; both tags peel to their pinned commits.</p> </li> <li> <p>2026-10-18 — <strong>The bounded residual ran and the wire gate holds final-zero under the pair: n=100, first-pass 7, final violations 0.</strong> The channel returned (the operator handed the router config; the bearer lives in ~/.edge-token and the harness .env, both untracked, and it did pass through the conversation once, so rotation stays the operator's call), the new serving caps qwen3.5-4b at 64k where the old edge served 131k, so the residual measures the current deployment envelope rather than the certified depth — a scope distinction the chart note now carries by name. Second, <code>obligations --record-digests</code> refuses to run without <code>--rederive <dir></code> and the dir is the component source root, so the remedy line's two flags are one invocation. Third, the release gate runs no clippy locally, and lifecycle v0.60.7's tag shipped red on a needless borrow the runner's clippy 1.99.0 newly flags (pre-existing code, moved toolchain); fixed on main the same hour (<code>eba0b7b</code>), and the discipline stands restated: run <code>cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings</code> inside the worktree before every release, because the lane's clippy is the runner's, not this box's. The empty-reset credential pin now lives in four stores (host repo, template, and both bare stores), each built with <code>--add</code> or it silently replaces the reset.</p> </li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="use-markdown-decision-records-madr"><a class="header" href="#use-markdown-decision-records-madr">Use Markdown decision records (MADR)</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-23"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-23">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>Architectural decisions for the host methodology need a durable, citable home, separate from MEMORY.md (lessons learned, backward-looking) and PLAN.md (the milestone index). Without one, the reasoning behind a choice evaporates and gets re-litigated.</p> <h2 id="decision-44"><a class="header" href="#decision-44">Decision</a></h2> <p>Adopt MADR (Markdown Architectural Decision Records) for this log:</p> <ul> <li>Files are named <code>NNNN-topic-slug.md</code>, zero-padded to width four, numbered monotonically from this <code>0000</code> bootstrap, lowercase-and-dashes, no <code>ADR-</code> prefix.</li> <li>A record's number is its identity, not a sort key; this log is the ordering authority.</li> <li>Numbers are assigned at merge, so two branches do not collide on the same <code>NNNN</code>.</li> <li>Disambiguation by home: a bare number at the plan root names a milestone; a numbered file under <code>call/</code> names a decision.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-42"><a class="header" href="#consequences-42">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: decisions carry structured status and supersession and a stable, citable identity; this log documents its own format as record zero.</li> <li>Neutral: this is one of two numbered registers (milestones and decisions), told apart by home, kept explicit to avoid confusion.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="tool-outputs-are-project-owned-not-under-allium-or-specula-licenses"><a class="header" href="#tool-outputs-are-project-owned-not-under-allium-or-specula-licenses">Tool outputs are project-owned, not under allium or Specula licenses</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-24"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-24">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>The host methodology composes three referenced tools as submodules: host-lint (Unlicense, ours), allium (MIT, JUXT Ltd), and Specula (Apache-2.0, specula-org). Running them produces artifacts inside our project: allium's <code>propagate</code> emits obligations; Specula emits a modeling brief, <code>base.tla</code> / <code>MC.tla</code> specs, traces, and bug reports into <code>.specula-output/</code>. We need a recorded position on whether those generated artifacts carry the tools' licenses, so our project content stays license-clean and we avoid accidental contamination.</p> <h2 id="considered-options-13"><a class="header" href="#considered-options-13">Considered Options</a></h2> <ol> <li>Treat generated artifacts as project-owned, outside the tools' license scope.</li> <li>Treat them as derivative works of the tools (carrying MIT / Apache-2.0).</li> <li>Never generate into our tree (run the tools out-of-tree only).</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-outcome-3"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-3">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>Chosen option 1: <strong>artifacts the tools generate from our own input are our project's work product, outside allium's and Specula's license scope</strong>, the same way a compiled binary is not a derivative of the compiler that produced it.</p> <h3 id="basis-verified-against-the-source-repos"><a class="header" href="#basis-verified-against-the-source-repos">Basis (verified against the source repos)</a></h3> <ul> <li>Both licenses govern only "the Work" / "the Software" (the tools' own files), not artifacts produced by running them. allium ships standard MIT (© JUXT Ltd) with no output clause. Specula ships standard Apache-2.0 whose "Derivative Works" definition refers to works based on Specula's code, not specs that model our system. Specula's DCO governs inbound contributions only.</li> <li>Both tools frame outputs as the user's: allium "generates tests from the formal behaviours of your system"; Specula writes outputs to <code>.specula-output/</code> under the project root.</li> <li>Both authors chose permissive licenses; a verification tool that claimed the specs you write about your own system would be self-defeating. So this reading is consistent with (not contrary to) the authors' intent.</li> </ul> <h3 id="carve-out"><a class="header" href="#carve-out">Carve-out</a></h3> <p>Verbatim boilerplate a tool injects (a Specula trace-module or test-rig skeleton, an allium obligation template) remains part of that tool's Work and keeps its license. We reference such boilerplate (for example <code>EXTENDS</code> or an include from the submodule), never vendor it into our tree.</p> <h2 id="consequences-43"><a class="header" href="#consequences-43">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: generated specs and bug reports under a milestone's <code>spec/</code> are project-owned and Unlicense-clean, with no attribution obligation downstream.</li> <li>Good: the tools stay in their submodules under their own licenses; the separation is clean by construction.</li> <li>Risk: the cleanliness depends on referencing tool boilerplate rather than copying it; a generated artifact that embeds tool source verbatim carries that fragment's license.</li> <li>Note: this is practical reasoning, not legal advice; revisit before any commercially load-bearing use.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="split-verification-into-lanes-by-property-type"><a class="header" href="#split-verification-into-lanes-by-property-type">Split verification into lanes by property type</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-25"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-25">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>Correctness has distinct property classes, and no single tool covers them all well. Functional and data invariants suit property-based testing; temporal, ordering, and concurrency invariants need full state-space exploration; and neither catches naming or process slop. We need a clear division so each concern is routed to the tool that actually covers it.</p> <h2 id="considered-options-14"><a class="header" href="#considered-options-14">Considered Options</a></h2> <ol> <li>One tool for everything (forces a single tool to cover properties it cannot).</li> <li>Lanes by property type: route each concern to the tool suited to it.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-outcome-4"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-4">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>Chosen option 2: <strong>three lanes, one per property class.</strong></p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Lane</th><th>Property class</th><th>Tool</th><th>License</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Hygiene</td><td>naming and process slop (agentic tells)</td><td>host-lint</td><td>Unlicense</td></tr> <tr><td>Requirements + property-based testing</td><td>functional and data invariants ("for all inputs")</td><td>allium</td><td>MIT</td></tr> <tr><td>Timing + concurrency</td><td>temporal, ordering, interleaving invariants ("for all interleavings"), via model checking</td><td>Specula / TLA+</td><td>Apache-2.0</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>TLA+ is reserved strictly for its home ground: timing and concurrency. It is not a general requirements tool; that is allium's lane.</p> <h3 id="escalation-bridge"><a class="header" href="#escalation-bridge">Escalation bridge</a></h3> <p>When an allium property depends on interleaving or timing that property-based testing cannot adequately explore, it escalates out of the property-based lane into the timing-and-concurrency lane. allium identifies such a property; Specula proves the temporal ones.</p> <h2 id="consequences-44"><a class="header" href="#consequences-44">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: every concern has a clear owner; the lanes are complementary, not overlapping.</li> <li>Good: a milestone may legitimately carry obligations in more than one lane.</li> <li>Neutral: contributors must learn which lane a property belongs to; the escalation bridge is the rule that resolves the boundary cases.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="compose-verification-tools-as-referenced-submodules"><a class="header" href="#compose-verification-tools-as-referenced-submodules">Compose verification tools as referenced submodules</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-26"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-26">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>The three lanes (see decision 0002) are owned by tools under three different licenses: host-lint (Unlicense, ours), allium (MIT), and Specula (Apache-2.0). They must fit our milestone (decision-record) lifecycle and obligations model without contaminating our license posture, forcing us to maintain a fork, or turning a tool's internal workflow into a competing project axis.</p> <h2 id="considered-options-15"><a class="header" href="#considered-options-15">Considered Options</a></h2> <ol> <li>Vendor each tool's files into our tree and edit them to fit.</li> <li>Reference each tool as a submodule and steer it from our own layer.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-outcome-5"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-5">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>Chosen option 2: <strong>each tool is a referenced submodule; we orchestrate, never edit.</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Reference, never vendor.</strong> Each tool is a git submodule; our methodology (CLAUDE.md) refers to its skills. Its files are never copied or edited; behaviour is steered by instruction plus thin wrappers in our own tree. This keeps us clean of Apache-2.0 obligations and keeps submodule updates trivial.</li> <li><strong>Specs are tagged by lane and co-located with tests.</strong> A spec is <code>.allium</code> (allium) or <code>.tla</code> (Specula); both live in the milestone's <code>spec/</code> area. A tool's generated artifacts (allium's behavioural spec and generated tests, Specula's modeling brief, TLA+ specs, traces, confirmed bugs) are the discharge evidence, and are project-owned per decision 0001.</li> <li><strong>A tool's workflow discharges, it does not milestone.</strong> A tool's internal pipeline runs inside one milestone to discharge that milestone's obligations; it is not a parallel milestone axis. Specula's steps are referred to by name (Code Analysis, Spec Generation, and so on), never as ordinal phases; this keeps our own host-lint convention.</li> <li><strong>Lane choice is a decision.</strong> Choosing a lane for a concern, or classifying a Specula target category, is itself an architectural decision and gets its own record.</li> <li><strong>Boilerplate is referenced, not vendored.</strong> Verbatim tool boilerplate (a Specula trace-module, an allium template) is pulled in by reference, never copied; this is the carve-out from decision 0001.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-45"><a class="header" href="#consequences-45">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: clean license separation by construction; our content stays Unlicense; submodule bumps are mechanical.</li> <li>Good: one numbered milestone register, undisturbed by the tools' internal step naming.</li> <li>Risk: correctness depends on the reference-not-vendor and instruct-not-patch discipline; patching a submodule is a designed-around failure mode, not a routine tool.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="the-template-is-the-canonical-versioned-source-of-the-methodology"><a class="header" href="#the-template-is-the-canonical-versioned-source-of-the-methodology">The template is the canonical, versioned source of the methodology</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-27"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-27">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>The methodology is stated in two places: the host's own <code>CLAUDE.md</code> (which governs this meta-repo) and the template's <code>CLAUDE.md</code> (the canonical manual shipped to projects built from the template). They share a spine (the four working principles, audited plans, append-only memory) and will drift as the methodology moves. The host also <em>builds</em> the template whose methodology it follows, which makes "where is the single source?" awkward: a template's <code>CLAUDE.md</code> is addressed to an agent working in an <em>instantiated</em> project, not in this host, and an existing exemption already forbids treating the nested template <code>CLAUDE.md</code> as live governance here.</p> <h2 id="considered-options-16"><a class="header" href="#considered-options-16">Considered Options</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>Diverge</strong>: declare them not-duplicates; sync the shared spine by a documented checklist when it changes.</li> <li><strong>Template canonical, host live-references it</strong>: shrink the host <code>CLAUDE.md</code> to a pointer at the template's.</li> <li><strong>Extract a shared spine</strong> both files import.</li> <li><strong>Copy-at-version</strong>: the template is the source; every project holds a copy of the spine at the revision it adopted, recorded in a stamp; upgrading re-runs a migration.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-outcome-6"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-6">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>Chosen option 4: <strong>the template is the canonical, versioned source; each project (the host included) holds a copy of the spine at the revision it adopted.</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>The template authors the spine.</strong> Changes to the methodology land in the template <code>CLAUDE.md</code> first.</li> <li><strong>Every project carries a copy, pinned to a revision.</strong> A <code>.host</code> stamp at the repo root records the template revision adopted. The copy is inline and acted-on (not a fragile pointer), so governance stays strong locally.</li> <li><strong>The host is adopter zero, not a special case.</strong> It is migrated by the same protocol any project uses (decision 0005); the self-referential "compiler compiling itself" loop dissolves into ordinary adoption.</li> <li><strong>The exemption stays true.</strong> A project never <em>obeys</em> the nested template <code>CLAUDE.md</code> as live governance; it <em>copies from it</em> during a migration event. Copy-at-version is single-sourced (the template authors the revision) yet drift-managed (re-run the migration to upgrade).</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-46"><a class="header" href="#consequences-46">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Good: one source of truth for the spine; upgrades are a defined, mechanical diff between two template revisions, not a hand merge.</li> <li>Good: the host's existing template-CLAUDE.md exemption is now principled and permanent, not a stopgap.</li> <li>Cost: the spine text is duplicated into each adopter at adoption time; staleness is bounded by whether a project re-runs the upgrade migration, and made visible by the recorded revision.</li> <li>Deferred: fully reconciling the host's own <code>CLAUDE.md</code> wording with the template beyond the spine refresh (the broader duplication) is out of scope here.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><blockquote> <p><strong>Superseded.</strong> Retained as immutable history, not current guidance.</p> </blockquote> <h1 id="adopt-and-upgrade-existing-repos-by-a-cased-moded-migration-protocol"><a class="header" href="#adopt-and-upgrade-existing-repos-by-a-cased-moded-migration-protocol">Adopt and upgrade existing repos by a cased, moded migration protocol</a></h1> <ul> <li>Status: superseded by the methodology spine (host-template @ 94a1ac7)</li> <li>Date: 2026-06-14</li> </ul> <h2 id="context-and-problem-statement-28"><a class="header" href="#context-and-problem-statement-28">Context and Problem Statement</a></h2> <p>Decision 0004 makes the template a versioned source and says projects adopt a revision, but nothing defined <em>how</em> an existing repo becomes a host, or how one that adopted an earlier revision upgrades. Real targets show the shapes vary: a repo with no <code>CLAUDE.md</code>, a repo with a foreign <code>CLAUDE.md</code> predating the methodology (with deep ordinal-naming debt in files and history), and our own repos at an earlier revision. They also vary in appetite for disruption: some can absorb a single forward-only change; rewriting history is sometimes warranted and sometimes forbidden (when the history carries provenance others depend on).</p> <h2 id="considered-options-17"><a class="header" href="#considered-options-17">Considered Options</a></h2> <ol> <li><strong>Ad hoc</strong>: migrate each repo by hand, deciding everything case by case.</li> <li><strong>A defined protocol</strong>: one skeleton with a small set of explicit choices.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-outcome-7"><a class="header" href="#decision-outcome-7">Decision Outcome</a></h2> <p>Chosen option 2: <strong>a single protocol, parameterised by two orthogonal axes, shipped as the template's <code>MIGRATION.md</code> and driven by <code>host-lifecycle</code>.</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Case = starting state</strong> (decides how governance is established): <strong>(a)</strong> no <code>CLAUDE.md</code>: drop in the manual and elicit the repo's own conventions; <strong>(b)</strong> foreign <code>CLAUDE.md</code>: merge each rule (subsumed / project-specific / conflict to human); <strong>(c)</strong> carries a <code>.host</code> stamp: upgrade by diffing the recorded revision against the current one. <code>host-lifecycle classify</code> reports the case.</li> <li><strong>Mode = blast radius</strong> (decides how the audit is applied): <strong>Preview</strong> (report only, always first), <strong>Shallow PR</strong> (default; live files only; history untouched), <strong>Staged</strong> (Shallow across several PRs, for volume), <strong>Deep rewrite</strong> (opt-in; archive-first, then rewrite history).</li> <li><strong>Selection rule.</strong> Default Shallow; escalate to Staged on volume; choose Deep only when history-coherence value exceeds provenance/disruption cost, and never on history carrying provenance you do not control. <strong>History is immutable by default</strong>: outside Deep, legacy tells are acknowledged, not rewritten.</li> <li><strong>The stamp keys upgrades.</strong> <code>host-lifecycle adopt</code> scaffolds the rooms and writes <code>.host</code> (template + revision + date); <code>version</code> reads it.
